L0:PGI 201.170 Peer reviews.
L1:(a) Defense Pricing, Contracting, and Acquisition Policy peer reviews.
L1:(1) The Office of the Principal Director, Defense Pricing, Contracting, and
L0:Acquisition Policy (DPCAP), using the procedures in this section, will organize teams of
L0:reviewers and facilitate peer reviews for solicitations and contracts as follows:
L1:(i) DPCAP will conduct the preaward peer reviews for competitive procurements
L0:prior to the three phases of the acquisition (see PGI 201.170-2(a)) for all procurements with
L0:an estimated value of $1 billion or more under major defense acquisition programs for which
L0:USD(A&S) is the milestone decision authority or USD(A&S) designates as requiring a peer
L0:review regardless of value. DoD components may request DPCAP-led peer reviews for
L0:acquisitions valued below the $1 billion threshold. DPCAP will conduct these reviews upon
L0:approval by the Director, DPCAP (Contract Policy).
L1:(ii) DPCAP will conduct the preaward peer reviews for noncompetitive
L0:procurements prior to the two phases of the acquisition (see PGI 201.170-2(b)) for contract
L0:actions, e.g., new contracts, modifications to existing contracts, requests for equitable
L0:adjustment, claims valued at $1 billion or more, or for any other contract action USD(A&S)
L0:designates as requiring a peer review regardless of value. DoD components may request
L0:DPCAP-led peer reviews for contract actions valued below the $1 billion threshold. DPCAP
L0:will conduct these reviews upon approval by the Director, DPCAP (Price, Cost and Finance).
L1:(iii) Use the following criteria to identify actions that are subject to peer review:
L1:(A) If the not-to-exceed amount for an undefinitized contract action or an
L0:unpriced change order exceeds the peer review threshold, then the resulting definitization
L0:modification(s) will be subject to peer review regardless of actual performance up to the
L0:point of definitization.
L1:(B) For indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contracts that will
L0:establish pricing terms that apply to orders, use the total maximum dollar value for purposes
L0:of the peer review threshold. IDIQ contracts that will not establish pricing terms in the basic
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 1
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 201
L0:contract are not subject to peer review, but individual orders that exceed the threshold are
L0:subject to peer review.
L0:when considering the firm requirement for all supplies or services:
L1:(C) For noncompetitive contract actions, use the greater of the following
L1:(1) The approved Government objective amount.
L1:(2) The contractor proposed amount.
L1:(2) To facilitate planning for peer reviews, the military departments and defense
L0:agencies must provide a rolling annual forecast of acquisitions that will be subject to DPCAP
L0:peer reviews at the end of each quarter (i.e., March 31; June 30; September 30; December
L0:31).
L1:(i) Military departments and defense agencies must submit quarterly forecasts
L0:for competitive peer reviews to the Director, DPCAP (Contract Policy), at
L1:(ii) Military departments and defense agencies must submit quarterly forecasts
L0:for noncompetitive peer reviews to the Director, DPCAP (Price, Cost and Finance), at
L1:(b) Component peer reviews. The military departments and defense agencies must
L0:establish procedures for—
L1:(1) Preaward peer reviews of solicitations for competitive procurements not subject
L0:to paragraph (a)(1)(i) of this section; and
L1:(2) Preaward peer reviews of noncompetitive procurements not subject to
L0:paragraph (a)(1)(ii) of this section.
L1:(c) DoD components may request a DPCAP-led peer review for procurements that
L0:would not otherwise require a DPCAP-led peer review.
L1:(d) Military departments and defense agencies must, on or about June 30 and
L0:December 31 of each year, submit recommended best practices and lessons learned from
L0:competitive acquisition peer reviews under major defense acquisition programs to
L0:may be selected for posting at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/cp/policy/competitive-
L0:source-selection.html.
L0:PGI 201.170-1 Objectives of peer reviews.
L0:The objectives of peer reviews are to—
L1:(a) Ensure that DoD contracting officers are implementing policy and regulations in a
L0:consistent and appropriate manner;
L1:(b) Continue to improve the quality of contracting processes throughout DoD; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 1
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 201
L1:(c) Facilitate cross-sharing of best practices and lessons learned throughout DoD.
L0:DPCAP maintains a compilation of peer review lessons learned and best practices that
L0:is available at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/cp/policy/peer-reviews.html for
L0:competitive peer reviews and at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/pcf/ss-peer-
L0:reviews.html for noncompetitive peer reviews.
L0:PGI 201.170-2 Preaward peer reviews.
L1:(a) Preaward peer reviews for competitive acquisitions must be conducted prior to each
L0:of the following three phases of the acquisition:
L1:(1) Issuance of the solicitation.
L1:(2) Request for final proposal revisions (if applicable).
L1:(3) Contract award.
L1:(b) Preaward peer reviews for noncompetitive acquisitions must be conducted prior to
L0:each of the following two phases of the acquisition:
L1:(1) Negotiation.
L1:(2) Contract award.
L0:PGI 201.170-3 Administration of peer reviews.
L1:(a) The results and recommendations that are products of peer reviews are intended to
L0:be advisory in nature; however, in the event the peer review report includes a
L0:recommendation that is identified as “significant” and the contracting officer does not intend
L0:to follow that recommendation, the senior procurement official of the contracting activity for
L0:the reviewed organization must be made aware of this fact before action is taken (or
L0:inaction, as applicable) that is contrary to the recommendation. Reviews will be conducted
L0:in a manner that preserves the authority, judgment, and discretion of the contracting officer
L0:and the senior officials of the requiring activity.
L1:(b) Peer review teams should be comprised of senior contracting officials and attorneys
L0:as appropriate. Teams may include civilian employees or military personnel external to the
L0:department, agency, or component that is the subject of the peer review.
L1:(c) Reviews are generally conducted remotely. However, a peer review may be
L0:conducted at the location of the executing contracting organization when appropriate.
L1:(d) See paragraph (g) of this section for a list of the documents that must be made
L0:available to the competitive peer review team, along with the specific elements the team will
L0:examine. See paragraph (h) of this section for a list of the documents that must be made
L0:available to the noncompetitive peer review team, along with a link to the noncompetitive
L0:peer review preparation resource.
L1:(e) The review team observations and recommendations will be communicated to the
L0:contracting officer and the senior procurement official immediately upon completion of a
L0:review.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 1
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 201

L0:PGI 201.404-70 Roles and responsibilities.
L0:Contracting officers must inform all individuals performing on their behalf of their delegated

L1:(a) When designating Department of State personnel as a contracting officer’s
L0:representative (COR for contracts executed by DoD in support of Department of State in

L1:(b) DoD COR certification standards define minimum COR competencies, experience,
L0:and training requirements according to the nature and complexity of the requirement and
L0:contract performance risk. These COR certification standards should be considered when
L0:developing service requirements, soliciting proposals, and performing surveillance during
L0:contract performance. The DoD standards and policy are provided in DoD Instruction
L0:5000.72, DoD Standard for Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) Certification.
L1:(c) Guidance on the appointment and duties of CORs is provided in the DoD COR
L0:Guidebook.
L1:(d) DoD components must use the Joint Appointment Module (JAM), within the
L0:Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), to electronically track COR
L0:nominations, appointments, terminations, and training certifications for contracts

L1:(SPM) Module, located in the PIEE, for all other contract surveillance actions. Further
L0:guidance on the use of JAM and SPM Module is available at https://piee.eb.mil/piee-
L0:landing/.
L1:(e) A COR assists in the technical monitoring or administration of a contract.
L1:(1) Unless an exemption applies, contracting officers must designate a COR for
L0:all service contracts, including both firm-fixed-price and other than firm-fixed-price
L0:contracts, and supply contracts with cost-reimbursable line items awarded by a DoD
L0:component or by any other Federal agency on behalf of DoD within 3 business days of

L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 201
L0:dollar value and complexity of the specific contract for which they are designated. For
L0:geographically dispersed large contracts with multiple task orders, contracting officers
L0:should consider appointing multiple or alternate CORs to assist with surveillance duties.
L0:These CORs should have specific duties based on criteria, such as geographic region
L0:or distinct task areas, to avoid conflicting or duplicative direction. Contracting officers
L0:may exempt service contracts from this requirement when—
L1:(i) The contract will be awarded using simplified acquisition procedures;
L1:(ii) The requirement is not complex; and
L1:(iii) The contracting officer documents the file, in writing, with the specific

L1:(2) For supply contracts with cost-reimbursement contracts line items, contracting

L0:and DCMA.
L1:(3) The contracting officer must ensure the written designation required by FAR
L0:1.404(a)(1) is maintained in JAM or the SPM Module.

L1:(h) Within 30 days of completing the COR file review, contracting officers must-

title: 203.170 Business practices
content:
L0:203.170 Business practices.
L0:To ensure the separation of functions for oversight, source selection, contract
L0:negotiation, and contract award, departments and agencies must adhere to the
L0:following best practice policies:
L1:(a) Senior leaders must not perform multiple roles in source selection for a major
L0:weapon system or major service acquisition.
L1:(b) Vacant acquisition positions must be filled on an “acting” basis from below until
L0:a permanent appointment is made. To provide promising professionals an opportunity
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 3
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 203
L0:to gain experience by temporarily filling higher positions, these oversight duties must
L0:not accrue at the top.
L1:(c) Acquisition process reviews of the military departments must be conducted to
L0:assess and improve acquisition and management processes, roles, and structures. The
L0:scope of the reviews should include—
L1:(1) Distribution of acquisition roles and responsibilities among personnel;
L1:(2) Processes for reporting concerns about unusual or inappropriate actions; and
L1:(3) Application of DoD Instruction 5000.2, Operation of the Defense Acquisition
L0:System, and the disciplines in the Defense Acquisition Guidebook.
L1:(d) Source selection processes must be—
L1:(1) Reviewed and approved by cognizant organizations responsible for
L0:oversight;
L1:(2) Documented by the head of the contracting activity or at the agency level;
L0:and
L1:(3) Periodically reviewed by outside officials independent of that office or
L0:agency.
L1:(e) Legal review of documentation of major acquisition system source selection must
L0:be conducted prior to contract award, including the supporting documentation of the
L0:source selection evaluation board, source selection advisory council, and source selection
L0:authority.
L1:(f) Procurement management reviews must determine whether clearance threshold
L0:authorities are clear and must provide independent review for acquisitions exceeding
L0:the simplified acquisition threshold.

title: 3.702 Definition
content:
3.702 Definition

L0:Final conviction means a conviction, whether entered on a verdict or plea, including a plea of nolo contendere, for which sentence has been imposed.

title: 3.703 Authority
content:
3.703 Authority

L1:(a) Section 1(e) of Pub. L. 87-849, 18 U.S.C. 218 ( the Act ), gives the President or the heads of executive agencies acting under regulations prescribed by the President, the power to declare void and rescind contracts and other transactions listed in the Act. This applies when there has been a final conviction for bribery, conflict of interest, or any other violation of Chapter 11 of Title 18 of the United States Code (18 U.S.C. 201-224). Executive Order 12448, November 4, 1983, delegates the President's authority under the Act to the heads of the executive agencies and military departments.
L1:(b) 41 U.S.C. 2105(c) requires Federal agencies, upon receiving information that a contractor or person has violated 41 U.S.C. 2102, to consider rescinding a contract when-
L2:(1) The contractor or someone acting for the contractor has been convicted of an offense punishable under 41 U.S.C. 2105(a); or
L2:(2) The agency head, or designee, has determined, based on a preponderance of the evidence, that the contractor or someone acting for the contractor has engaged in conduct constituting such an offense.

title: 3.704 Policy
content:
3.704 Policy

L1:(a) In cases with a final conviction for any violation of 18 U.S.C. 201-224 involving or relating to agency-awarded contracts, the agency head or designee must consider the available facts. If appropriate, they must declare contracts void and rescind them, and recover the amounts spent and property transferred by the agency according to the policies and procedures in this subpart.
L1:(b) A final conviction under 18 U.S.C. 201-224 relating to a contract may also indicate the party is not presently responsible. The agency should consider starting debarment proceedings according to part 9, if debarment has not already begun or is not in effect when the final conviction occurs.
L1:(c) If there is a final conviction for an offense punishable under 41 U.S.C. 2105, or if the agency head or designee has determined, based on a preponderance of the evidence, that the contractor or someone acting for the contractor has engaged in such conduct, then the head of the contracting activity must consider, in addition to any other penalty prescribed by law or regulation—
L2:(1) Declaring contracts void and rescinding them, as appropriate, and recovering the amounts spent under the contracts by using the procedures at 3.705 (see 3.104-7); and
L2:(2) Recommending the initiation of suspension or debarment proceedings according to part 9.

title: 3.705 Procedures
Subpart 3.8 Limitations on the Payment of Funds to Influence Federal Transactions

Subpart 3.8 Limitations on the Payment of Funds to Influence Federal Transactions

title: 3.800 Scope of subpart
content:
3.800 Scope of subpart

L0:This subpart prescribes policies and procedures implementing 31 U.S.C. 1352, “Limitation on use of appropriated funds to influence certain Federal contracting and financial transactions.”

title: 3.801 Definitions
content:
3.801 Definitions

L0:As used in this subpart-
L0:Agency means executive agency as defined in 2.101.
L0:Covered Federal action means any of the following actions:
L2:(1) Awarding any Federal contract.
L2:(2) Making any Federal grant.
L2:(3) Making any Federal loan.
L2:(4) Entering into any cooperative agreement.
L2:(5) Extending, continuing, renewing, amending, or modifying any Federal contract, grant, loan, or cooperative agreement.
L0:Indian tribe and "tribal organization" have the meaning provided in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act ( 25 U.S.C. 450b ) and include Alaskan Natives.
L0:Influencing or attempting to influence means making, with the intent to influence, any communication to or appearance before an officer or employee of any agency, a Member of Congress, an officer or employee of Congress, or an employee of a Member of Congress in connection with any covered Federal action.
L0:Local government means a unit of government in a State and, if chartered, established, or otherwise recognized by a State for the performance of a governmental duty, including a local public authority, a special district, an intrastate district, a council of governments, a sponsor group representative organization, and any other instrumentality of a local government.
L0:Officer or employee of an agency includes the following individuals who are employed by an agency:
L2:(1) An individual who is appointed to a position in the Government under Title 5, United States Code, including a position under a temporary appointment.
L2:(2) A member of the uniformed services, as defined in subsection 101(3), Title 37, United States Code.
L2:(3) A special Government employee, as defined in section 202, Title 18, United States Code.
L2:(4) An individual who is a member of a Federal advisory committee, as defined by the Federal Advisory Committee Act, Title 5, United States Code, appendix 2.
L0:Person means an individual, corporation, company, association, authority, firm, partnership, society, State, and local government, regardless of whether such entity is operated for profit or not for profit. This term excludes an Indian tribe, tribal organization, or any other Indian organization eligible to receive Federal contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, or loans from an agency, but only with respect to expenditures by such tribe or organization that are made for purposes specified in paragraph 3.802(a) and are permitted by other Federal law.
L0:Reasonable compensation means, with respect to a regularly employed officer or employee of any person, compensation that is consistent with the normal compensation for such officer or employee for work that is not furnished to, not funded by, or not furnished in cooperation with the Federal Government.
L0:Reasonable payment means, with respect to professional and other technical services, a payment in an amount that is consistent with the amount normally paid for such services in the private sector.
L0:Recipient includes the contractor and all subcontractors. This term excludes an Indian tribe, tribal organization, or any other Indian organization eligible to receive Federal contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, or loans from an agency, but only with respect to expenditures by such tribe or organization that are made for purposes specified in paragraph 3.802(a) and are permitted by other Federal law.
L0:Regularly employed means, with respect to an officer or employee of a person requesting or receiving a Federal contract, an officer or employee who is employed by such person for at least 130 working days within 1 year immediately preceding the date of the submission that initiates agency consideration of such person for receipt of such contract. An officer or employee who is employed by such person for less than 130 working days within 1 year immediately preceding the date of the submission that initiates agency consideration of such person shall be considered to be regularly employed as soon as he or she is employed by such person for 130 working days.
L0:State means a State of the United States, the District of Columbia, an outlying area of the United States, an agency or instrumentality of a State, and multi-State, regional, or interstate entity having governmental duties and powers.

title: 3.802 Statutory prohibition and requirement
content:
3.802 Statutory prohibition and requirement

L1:(a) 31 U.S.C. 1352 prohibits recipients of Federal contracts, grants, loans, or cooperative agreements from using appropriated funds to pay any person for influencing or attempting to influence an officer or employee of an agency, a Member of Congress, an officer or employee of Congress, or an employee of a Member of Congress regarding covered Federal actions.
L2:(1) For purposes of this subpart the term "appropriated funds" does not include profit or fee from a covered Federal action.
L2:(2) If a person shows they have enough non-Federal appropriated funds, the Government must assume these other funds were used for any influencing activities that would be unallowable if paid for with Federal appropriated funds.
L1:(b) 31 U.S.C. 1352 also requires offerors to submit a declaration that includes both certification and disclosure, with regular updates of the disclosure after contract award. These requirements appear in the provision at 52.203-11, Certification and Disclosure Regarding Payments to Influence Certain Federal Transactions, and the clause at 52.203-12, Limitation on Payments to Influence Certain Federal Transactions.

title: 3.803 Exceptions
content:
3.803 Exceptions

L1:(a) The prohibition of paragraph 3.802(a) does not apply under the following conditions:
L2:(1) Agency and legislative liaison by own employees.
L3:(i) Payment of reasonable compensation made to an officer or employee of a person requesting or receiving a covered Federal action is permitted when the payment is for agency and legislative liaison activities not directly related to a covered Federal action. Providing any information specifically requested by an agency or Congress is permitted at any time.
L3:(ii) Participating with an agency in discussions unrelated to a specific solicitation for any covered Federal action, is permitted when discussions concern-
L4:(A) The qualities and characteristics (including demonstrations) of the person's products or services, sales terms, and service capabilities; or
L4:(B) How the person's products or services might be adapted for agency use.
L3:(iii) Providing information not specifically requested but necessary for an agency to make an informed decision about starting a covered Federal action is permitted before formal solicitation.
L3:(iv) Participating in technical discussions about preparing an unsolicited proposal before its official submission is permitted.
L3:(v) Making capability presentations before formal solicitation when seeking an award under the Small Business Act, as amended by Public Law 95-507 and later amendments, is permitted.
L2:(2) Professional and technical services .
L3:(i) Reasonable compensation to an officer or employee of a person requesting or receiving a covered Federal action is permitted when payment is for professional or technical services directly related to preparing, submitting, or negotiating bids, proposals, or applications for that Federal action, or for meeting requirements imposed by or pursuant to law as a condition for receiving that Federal action.
L3:(ii) Reasonable payment to persons who are not officers or employees of a person requesting or receiving a covered Federal action is permitted when payment is for professional or technical services directly related to preparing, submitting, or negotiating bids, proposals, or applications for that Federal action, or for meeting requirements imposed by or pursuant to law as a condition for receiving that Federal Action. These persons may include consultants and trade associations.
L3:(iii) In this section, "professional and technical services" means advice and analysis directly applying professional or technical expertise. For example, drafting of a legal document accompanying a bid or proposal by a lawyer is allowable. Similarly, technical advice provided by an engineer on the performance or operational capability of a piece of equipment rendered directly in the negotiation of a contract is allowable. However, communications with the intent to influence made by a professional or a technical person are not allowable under this section unless they provide advice and analysis directly applying their professional or technical expertise and unless the advice or analysis is rendered directly and solely in the preparation, submission or negotiation of a covered Federal action. Thus, for example, communications with the intent to influence made by a lawyer that do not provide legal advice or analysis directly and solely related to the legal aspects of his or her client's proposal, but generally advocate one proposal over another, are not allowable under this section because the lawyer is not providing professional legal services. Similarly, communications with the intent to influence made by an engineer providing an engineering analysis prior to the preparation or submission of a bid or proposal are not allowable under this section since the engineer is providing technical services but not directly in the preparation, submission or negotiation of a covered Federal action.
L3:(iv) Requirements imposed by or pursuant to law as a condition for receiving a covered Federal action includes those in laws, regulations, and the actual award documents.
L1:(b) Only the communications and services specifically authorized in paragraph (a) are permitted.
L1:(c) The disclosure requirements in paragraph 3.802(b) do not apply to reasonable compensation paid to regularly employed officers of a person.

title: 3.903 Policy
content:
3.903 Policy

L1:(a)
L2:(1) Contractors and subcontractors are prohibited from discharging, demoting, or otherwise discriminating against an employee as a reprisal for disclosing, to any of the entities listed at paragraph (b) of this section, information that the employee reasonably believes is—
L3:(i) Evidence of gross mismanagement of a Federal contract;
L3:(ii) A gross waste of Federal funds;
L3:(iii) An abuse of authority relating to a Federal contract;
L3:(iv) A substantial and specific danger to public health or safety; or
L3:(v) A violation of law, rule, or regulation related to a Federal contract (including the competition for or negotiation of a contract).
L2:(2) A reprisal is prohibited even when requested by an executive branch official, unless the request takes the form of a non-discretionary directive and is within the authority of the executive branch official making the request.
L1:(b) Disclosure may be made to the following entities:
L2:(1) A Member of Congress or a representative of a committee of Congress.
L2:(2) An Inspector General.
L2:(3) The Government Accountability Office.
L2:(4) A Federal employee responsible for contract oversight or management at the relevant agency.
L2:(5) An authorized official of the Department of Justice or other law enforcement agency.
L2:(6) A court or grand jury.
L2:(7) A management official or other employee of the contractor or subcontractor who has the responsibility to investigate, discover, or address misconduct.
L1:(c) An employee who initiates or provides evidence of contractor or subcontractor misconduct in any judicial or administrative proceeding relating to waste, fraud, or abuse on a Federal contract must be deemed to have made a disclosure.

title: 3.904 Complaints
content:
3.904 Complaints

L0:A contractor or subcontractor employee who believes that he or she has been discharged, demoted, or otherwise discriminated against contrary to the policy in 3.903 may submit a complaint with the Inspector General of the agency concerned. Procedures for submitting fraud, waste, abuse, and whistleblower complaints are generally accessible on agency Office of Inspector General hotline or whistleblower internet sites or the complainant may directly contact the cognizant Office of the Inspector General for submission instructions. A complaint under 41 U.S.C. 4712 must be filed within three years from the date on which the alleged reprisal occurred.

title: 3.904-1 Procedures for filing complaints
content:
3.904-1 Procedures for filing complaints

L0:A contractor or subcontractor employee who believes that he or she has been discharged, demoted, or otherwise discriminated against contrary to the policy in 3.903 may submit a complaint with the Inspector General of the agency concerned. Procedures for submitting fraud, waste, abuse, and whistleblower complaints are generally accessible on agency Office of Inspector General hotline or whistleblower internet sites or the complainant may directly contact the cognizant Office of the Inspector General for submission instructions. A complaint under 41 U.S.C. 4712 must be filed within three years from the date on which the alleged reprisal occurred.

title: 3.904-2 Procedures for investigating complaints
content:
3.904-2 Procedures for investigating complaints

L1:(a) Investigation of complaints will be conducted according to 41 U.S.C. 4712(b).
L1:(b) After the investigation is complete, the head of the agency must ensure the Inspector General provides the report of findings to-
L2:(1) The head of the agency;
L2:(2) The complainant and any person acting on the complainant's behalf; and
L2:(3) The contractor and/or subcontractor alleged to have committed the violation.
L1:(c) The complainant, contractor, and/or subcontractor must have the opportunity to submit a written response to the report of findings. This response must be submitted to the head of the agency and the Office of Inspector General within a timeframe set by the agency that allows the agency head to take action within 30 days after receiving the report, as required by 3.905-1(a).

title: 3.905 Remedies and enforcement of orders
content:
3.905 Remedies and enforcement of orders

L1:(a) Agency response to Inspector General report. Not later than 30 days after receiving a report pursuant to 3.904-2, the head of the agency shall—
L2:(1) Determine whether sufficient basis exists to conclude that the contractor or subcontractor has subjected the employee who submitted the complaint to a reprisal as prohibited by 3.903; and
L2:(2) Either issue an order denying relief or take one or more of the following actions:
L3:(i) Order the contractor or subcontractor to take affirmative action to abate the reprisal.
L3:(ii) Order the contractor or subcontractor to reinstate the complainant employee to their previous position, with compensatory damages (including back pay), employment benefits, and other terms and conditions of employment that would apply if the reprisal had not occurred.
L3:(iii) Order the contractor or subcontractor to pay the complainant employee an amount equal to all costs and expenses (including attorneys' fees and expert witnesses' fees) reasonably incurred by the complainant for, or in connection with, bringing the complaint regarding the reprisal, as determined by the head of the agency.
L3:(iv) Consider disciplinary or corrective action against any executive agency official, if appropriate.
L1:(b) Complainant's right to go to court .
L2:(1) Paragraph (b)(2) of this section applies if-
L3:(i) The head of the agency issues an order denying relief; or
L3:(ii)
L4:(A) The head of the agency has not issued an order-
L5:( 1 ) Within 210 days after the submission of the complaint; or
L5:( 2 ) Within 30 days after the expiration of an extension of time granted in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 4712(b)(2)(B) for the submission of the report to those stated in 3.904-2(b); and
L4:(B) There is no showing that such delay is due to the bad faith of the complainant.
L2:(2) If the conditions in either paragraph (b)(1)(i) or (ii) of this section are met:
L3:(i) The complainant must be deemed to have exhausted all administrative remedies with respect to the complaint; and
L3:(ii) The complainant may bring a de novo action at law or equity against the contractor or subcontractor to seek compensatory damages and other relief available under 41 U.S.C. 4712 in the appropriate U.S. district court, which has jurisdiction regardless of the amount in controversy.
L4:(A) Such an action must, at the request of either party to the action, be tried by the court with a jury.
L4:(B) An action under this authority may not be brought more than 2 years after the date on which remedies are deemed to have been exhausted.
L1:(c) Admissibility in evidence . An Inspector General determination and an agency head order denying relief under this section must be admissible in evidence in any de novo action at law or equity brought pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 4712.
L1:(d) No waiver . The rights and remedies provided for in 41 U.S.C. 4712 may not be waived by any agreement, policy, form, or condition of employment.

title: 3.905-2 Enforcement of orders
content:
3.905-2 Enforcement of orders

L1:(a) When a contractor or subcontractor fails to comply with an order issued under 3.905-1(a)(2), the head of the agency concerned must file an action to enforce the order in the U.S. district court for the district where the reprisal occurred. In any action brought under this authority, the court may grant appropriate relief, including injunctive relief, compensatory and exemplary damages, and attorney fees and costs. The complainant employee upon whose behalf an order was issued may also file such an action or join an action filed by the head of the agency.
L1:(b) Any person adversely affected or aggrieved by an order issued under 3.905-1(a)(2) may seek review of the order's compliance with 41 U.S.C. 4712 and its implementing regulations in the U.S. court of appeals for the circuit where the reprisal is alleged to have occurred. The petition for review must be filed within 60 days after the head of the agency issues the order. Filing such an appeal does not stop enforcement of the agency head's order unless the court specifically grants a stay.

3.1002 Policy

L1:(a) Government contractors must conduct themselves with the highest degree of integrity and honesty.
L1:(b) Contractors should have a written code of business ethics and conduct. To promote compliance with such code of business ethics and conduct, contractors should have an employee business ethics and compliance training program and an internal control system that—
L2:(1) Are suitable to the size of the company and extent of its involvement in Government contracting;
L2:(2) Facilitate timely discovery and disclosure of improper conduct in connection with Government contracts; and
L2:(3) Ensure corrective measures are promptly instituted and carried out.

title: 3.1003 Requirements
content:
3.1003 Requirements

L1:(a) Contractor requirements .
L2:(1) Although the policy at 3.1002 provides guidance for all Government contractors, the contract clauses at 52.203-13, Contractor Code of Business Ethics and Conduct, and 52.203-14, Display of Hotline Poster(s), become mandatory when contracts meet the conditions specified in 3.1004.
L2:(2) A contractor may be suspended and/or debarred if a principal knowingly fails to promptly disclose to the Government credible evidence of Federal criminal law violations involving fraud, conflict of interest, bribery, or gratuity violations found in Title 18 of the United States Code, or Civil False Claims Act violations. This disclosure requirement applies whether or not clause 52.203-13 is applicable. Failure to timely disclose credible evidence of such violations remains grounds for suspension and/or debarment until 3 years after final contract payment (see part 9).
L2:(3) The Payment clauses at FAR 52.212-4(i)(5), 52.232-25(d), 52.232-26(c), and 52.232-27(l) require contractors to return any contract financing or invoice overpayments they discover to the Government. A contractor may be suspended and/or debarred if a principal knowingly fails to timely disclose credible evidence of a significant overpayment, except for overpayments resulting from contract financing payments as defined in 32.001 (see part 9).
L1:(b) Notification of possible contractor violation . If the contracting officer learns of a possible contractor violation of Federal criminal law involving fraud, conflict of interest, bribery, or gratuity violations found in Title 18 U.S.C., or a violation of the civil False Claims Act, the contracting officer must:
L2:(1) Coordinate the matter with the agency Office of the Inspector General; or
L2:(2) Take action according to agency procedures.
L1:(c) Fraud Hotline Poster .
L2:(1) Agency Offices of Inspector General (OIGs) determine the need for and content of their respective agency OIG fraud hotline poster(s).
L2:(2) When requested by the Department of Homeland Security, agencies must ensure that contracts funded with disaster assistance funds require display of applicable fraud hotline posters. As established by the agency OIG, these posters may be displayed instead of, or in addition to, the agency's standard poster.

title: 3.1004 Contract clauses
content:
3.1004 Contract clauses

L1:(a) Insert the clause at FAR 52.203-13, Contractor Code of Business Ethics and Conduct, in solicitations and contracts if the value of the contract is expected to exceed $7.5 million and the performance period is 120 days or more.
L1:(b)
L2:(1) Unless the contract is for the acquisition of a commercial product or commercial service or will be performed entirely outside the United States, insert the clause at 52.203-14, Display of Hotline Poster(s), if—
L3:(i) The contract exceeds $7.5 million or a lesser amount established by the agency; and
L3:(ii)
L4:(A) The agency has a fraud hotline poster; or
L4:(B) The contract is funded with disaster assistance funds.
L2:(2) In paragraph (b)(3) of the clause, the contracting officer shall—
L3:(i) Identify the applicable posters; and
L3:(ii) Insert the website link(s) or other contact information for obtaining the agency and/or Department of Homeland Security poster.
L2:(3) In paragraph (d) of the clause, if the agency has established policies and procedures for display of the OIG fraud hotline poster at a lesser amount, the contracting officer shall replace “$7.5 million” with the lesser amount that the agency has established.

title: Subpart 3.11 Preventing Personal Conflicts of Interest for Contractor Employees Performing Acquisition Functions
content:
Subpart 3.11 Preventing Personal Conflicts of Interest for Contractor Employees Performing Acquisition Functions

L0:This subpart implements policy on personal conflicts of interest by employees of Government contractors as required by 41 U.S.C. 2303.

title: 3.1100 Scope of subpart
content:
3.1100 Scope of subpart

L0:This subpart implements policy on personal conflicts of interest by employees of Government contractors as required by 41 U.S.C. 2303.

title: 3.1101 Definitions
content:
3.1101 Definitions

L0:As used in this subpart-
L0:Acquisition function closely associated with inherently governmental functions means supporting or providing advice or recommendations with regard to the following activities of a Federal agency:
L2:(1) Planning acquisitions.
L2:(2) Determining what supplies or services are to be acquired by the Government, including developing statements of work.
L2:(3) Developing or approving any contractual documents, to include documents defining requirements, incentive plans, and evaluation criteria.
L2:(4) Evaluating contract proposals.
L2:(5) Awarding Government contracts.
L2:(6) Administering contracts (including ordering changes or giving technical direction in contract performance or contract quantities, evaluating contractor performance, and accepting or rejecting contractor products or services).
L2:(7) Terminating contracts.
L2:(8) Determining whether contract costs are reasonable, allocable, and allowable.
L0:Covered employee means an individual who performs an acquisition function closely associated with inherently governmental functions and is-
L2:(1) An employee of the contractor; or
L2:(2) A subcontractor that is a self-employed individual treated as a covered employee of the contractor because there is no employer to whom such an individual could submit the required disclosures.
L0:Personal conflict of interest means a situation in which a covered employee has a financial interest, personal activity, or relationship that could impair the employee’s ability to act impartially and in the best interest of the Government when performing under the contract. (A de minimis interest that would not "impair the employee’s ability to act impartially and in the best interest of the Government" is not covered under this definition.)
L2:(1) Among the sources of personal conflicts of interest are-
L3:(i) Financial interests of the covered employee, of close family members, or of other members of the covered employee's household;
L3:(ii) Other employment or financial relationships (including seeking or negotiating for prospective employment or business); and
L3:(iii) Gifts, including travel.
L2:(2) For example, financial interests referred to in paragraph (1) of this definition may arise from-
L3:(i) Compensation, including wages, salaries, commissions, professional fees, or fees for business referrals;
L3:(ii) Consulting relationships (including commercial and professional consulting and service arrangements, scientific and technical advisory board memberships, or serving as an expert witness in litigation);
L3:(iii) Services provided in exchange for honorariums or travel expense reimbursements;
L3:(iv) Research funding or other forms of research support;
L3:(v) Investment in the form of stock or bond ownership or partnership interest (excluding diversified mutual fund investments);
L3:(vi) Real estate investments;
L3:(vii) Patents, copyrights, and other intellectual property interests; or
L3:(viii) Business ownership and investment interests.

title: 3.1102 Policy
content:
3.1102 Policy

L0:The Government's policy is to require contractors to—
L1:(a) Identify and prevent personal conflicts of interest of their covered employees; and
L1:(b) Prohibit covered employees who have access to non-public information by reason of performance on a Government contract from using such information for personal gain.

title: 3.1103 Procedures
content:
3.1103 Procedures

L1:(a) By use of the contract clause at 52.203-16, as prescribed at 3.1106, the contracting officer must require each contractor whose employees perform acquisition functions closely associated with inherently Government functions to—
L2:(1) Have procedures in place to screen covered employees for potential personal conflicts of interest by—
L3:(i) Obtaining and maintaining from each covered employee, when the employee is initially assigned to the task under the contract, a disclosure of interests that might be affected by the task to which the employee has been assigned, as follows:
L4:(A) Financial interests of the covered employee, of close family members, or of other members of the covered employee's household.
L4:(B) Other employment or financial relationships of the covered employee (including seeking or negotiating for prospective employment or business).
L4:(C) Gifts, including travel; and
L3:(ii) Requiring each covered employee to update the disclosure statement whenever the employee's personal or financial circumstances change in such a way that a new personal conflict of interest might occur because of the task the covered employee is performing.
L2:(2) For each covered employee—
L3:(i) Prevent personal conflicts of interest, including not assigning or allowing a covered employee to perform any task under the contract for which the Contractor has identified a personal conflict of interest that cannot be satisfactorily prevented or reduced in consultation with the contracting agency;
L3:(ii) Prohibit use of non-public information (information not available to the public) accessed through Government contract work for personal gain; and
L3:(iii) Obtain a signed non-disclosure agreement to prohibit disclosure of non-public information accessed through performance of a Government contract.
L2:(3) Inform covered employees of their obligation—
L3:(i) To disclose and prevent personal conflicts of interest;
L3:(ii) Not to use non-public information accessed through performance of a Government contract for personal gain; and
L3:(iii) To avoid even the appearance of personal conflicts of interest;
L2:(4) Maintain effective oversight to verify compliance with personal conflict-of-interest safeguards;
L2:(5) Take appropriate disciplinary action when covered employees fail to comply with policies established pursuant to this section; and
L2:(6) Report any personal conflict-of-interest violation by a covered employee to the contracting officer as soon as identified. This report must include-
L3:(i) A description of the violation;
L3:(ii) The proposed actions the contractor will take in response to the violation; and
L3:(iii) Follow-up reports of corrective actions taken, as necessary.
L1:(b) If a contractor reports a personal conflict-of-interest violation by a covered employee to the contracting officer according to paragraph (b)(6) of clause 52.203-16, Preventing Personal Conflicts of Interest, the contracting officer must—
L2:(1) Review the actions taken by the contractor;
L2:(2) Determine whether the contractor's actions have resolved the violation satisfactorily; and
L2:(3) Take any appropriate action in consultation with agency legal counsel if the contracting officer determines that the contractor has not resolved the violation satisfactorily.

title: 3.1104 Mitigation or waiver
content:
3.1104 Mitigation or waiver

L1:(a) In exceptional circumstances, if the contractor cannot satisfactorily prevent a personal conflict of interest as required by paragraph (b)(2)(i) of the clause at 52.203-16, Preventing Personal Conflicts of Interest, the contractor may submit a request, through the contracting officer asking the head of the contracting activity to—
L2:(1) Agree to a plan to mitigate the personal conflict of interest; or
L2:(2) Waive the requirement to prevent personal conflicts of interest.
L1:(b) If the head of the contracting activity determines in writing that such action is in the best interest of the Government, the head of the contracting activity may impose conditions that provide mitigation of a personal conflict of interest or grant a waiver.
L1:(c) This authority shall not be redelegated.

title: 3.1105 Violations
content:
3.1105 Violations

L0:If the contracting officer suspects violation by the contractor of a requirement of paragraph (b), (c)(3), or (d) of the clause at 52.203-16, Preventing Personal Conflicts of Interest, the contracting officer must contact the agency legal counsel for advice and/or recommendations on a course of action.

title: 3.1106 Contract clause
content:
3.1106 Contract clause

L1:(a) Insert the clause at 52.203-16, Preventing Personal Conflicts of Interest, in solicitations and contracts that—
L2:(1) Exceed the simplified acquisition threshold; and
L2:(2) Include a requirement for services by contractor employee(s) that involve performance of acquisition functions closely associated with inherently governmental functions for, or on behalf of, a Federal agency or department.
L1:(b) If only a portion of a contract involves the performance of acquisition functions closely associated with inherently governmental functions, the contracting officer must still insert the clause but must limit the clause's applicability to only that portion of the contract that involves such services.
L1:(c) Do not insert the clause in solicitations or contracts with a self-employed individual if the acquisition functions closely associated with inherently governmental functions are to be performed entirely by the self-employed individual, rather than an employee of the contractor.

title: 4.000 Scope of part
content:
4.000 Scope of part

L0:This part prescribes policies and procedures relating to the administrative aspects of contract execution, contractor-submitted documents, reporting, retention, and files.

title: 4.001 Definitions
content:
4.001 Definitions

L0:As used in this part-
L0:Executive means officers, managing partners, or any other employees in management positions.
L0:First-tier subcontract means a subcontract awarded directly by the Contractor to acquire supplies or services (including construction) for performing a prime contract. It does not include the contractor’s supplier agreements with vendors, such as long-term arrangements for materials or supplies that benefit multiple contracts and/or the costs of which are normally applied to a contractor’s general and administrative expenses or indirect costs.
L0:Generic entity identifier means an identifier assigned to a category of vendors, not specific to any individual or entity.
L0:Total compensation means the cash and noncash dollar value earned by the executive during the contractor’s preceding fiscal year and includes the information described at 17 CFR 229.402(c)(2).

title: 4.002 Electronic commerce in contracting
content:
4.002 Electronic commerce in contracting

L0:Agencies must use electronic commerce to the maximum extent that is practicable and cost-effective, see 41 U.S.C. 2301.

title: Subpart 4.1 Presolicitation
content:
Subpart 4.1 Presolicitation

L1:(a) Each office performing contracting, contract administration, or paying functions must establish a file containing the records of each solicitation and contractual action.
L1:(b) The file documentation must comprehensively record the transaction history to ensure—
L2:(1) A complete background is available for making informed decisions at each step in the acquisition process;
L2:(2) There is clear support for all actions taken;
L2:(3) Necessary information is accessible for reviews and investigations; and
L2:(4) Essential facts are available in case litigation or congressional inquiries arise.

title: 4.101 Contract files
content:
4.101 Contract files

L1:(a) Each office performing contracting, contract administration, or paying functions must establish a file containing the records of each solicitation and contractual action.
L1:(b) The file documentation must comprehensively record the transaction history to ensure—
L2:(1) A complete background is available for making informed decisions at each step in the acquisition process;
L2:(2) There is clear support for all actions taken;
L2:(3) Necessary information is accessible for reviews and investigations; and
L2:(4) Essential facts are available in case litigation or congressional inquiries arise.

title: Subpart 4.2 Solicitation, Evaluation, and Award
content:
Subpart 4.2 Solicitation, Evaluation, and Award

L1:(a) Agencies must use a procurement instrument identifier (PIID) unique Governmentwide to identify each solicitation, contract, agreement, or order. The PIID must be used in all related procurement actions including forms and electronic generated formats.
L1:(b) The PIID consists of a combination of thirteen to seventeen alpha and/or numeric characters sequenced to convey certain information. Do not use special characters (such as hyphens, dashes, or spaces).
L2:(1) Positions 1 through 6 . Use the issuing office Activity Address Code to identify the department/agency and office issuing the instrument.
L2:(2) Positions 7 through 8 . Use the last two digits of the fiscal year in which the procurement instrument is issued or awarded (i.e., signed).
L2:(3) Position 9 . Use one of the upper-case letters according to Table 4-1. Departments and independent agencies may assign those letters identified for department use below according to agency policy; however, any use must be applied to the entire department or agency.
L2:(4) Positions 10 through 17 . Use the number assigned by the issuing agency in these positions. Agencies may choose between four and eight characters to be used, but the same number of characters must be used agencywide. Do not use leading or trailing zeroes to equal the maximum in any system or data transmission. A separate series of numbers may be used for any type of instrument listed in paragraph (b)(3) of this section. An agency may reserve blocks of numbers or alpha-numeric numbers for its various components to use.
L1:(c) Agencies must use a non-unique identifier for a procurement action (i.e., supplementary PIID) that is used with the PIID. The supplementary PIID is used to identify amendments to solicitations and modifications to contracts, orders, and agreements. The supplementary PIID is reported as a separate data element used with, but not appended to, the PIID.
L2:(1) Amendments to solicitations . Use a four-position numeric serial number in addition to the 13–17-character PIID beginning with 0001.
L2:(2) Modifications to contracts, orders, and agreements . Use a six-position alpha, numeric, or a combination of both, in addition to the 13–17-character PIID. For example, a modification could be numbered P00001.
L3:(i) Position 1 . Use the letter P if the modification is issued by the procuring contracting office. Use the letter A if the modification is issued by the contract administration office (if other than the procuring contracting office).
L3:(ii) Positions 2 through 6 . These positions may be alpha, numeric, or a combination of both, according to agency procedures.
L3:(iii) Each office authorized to issue modifications must assign the supplementary identification numbers in sequence (unless provided otherwise in agency procedures). Do not assign the numbers until the contracting officer determines that a modification is to be issued.
L1:(d)
L2:(1) Agencies must not change the PIID unless one of the following circumstances applies:
L3:(i) The PIID serial numbering system is exhausted.
L3:(ii) Continued use of a PIID is administratively burdensome (e.g., for implementing new agency contract writing systems).
L3:(iii) The contract is transferred between contracting departments.
L2:(2) If one of the circumstances described at 4.201(d)(1) applies, the contracting officer may assign a new PIID by issuing an administrative contract modification (see part 43). The modification must identify both the original and the newly assigned PIID.

title: 4.201 Unique procurement instrument identifiers
content:
4.201 Unique procurement instrument identifiers

L1:(a) Agencies must use a procurement instrument identifier (PIID) unique Governmentwide to identify each solicitation, contract, agreement, or order. The PIID must be used in all related procurement actions including forms and electronic generated formats.
L1:(b) The PIID consists of a combination of thirteen to seventeen alpha and/or numeric characters sequenced to convey certain information. Do not use special characters (such as hyphens, dashes, or spaces).
L2:(1) Positions 1 through 6 . Use the issuing office Activity Address Code to identify the department/agency and office issuing the instrument.
L2:(2) Positions 7 through 8 . Use the last two digits of the fiscal year in which the procurement instrument is issued or awarded (i.e., signed).
L2:(3) Position 9 . Use one of the upper-case letters according to Table 4-1. Departments and independent agencies may assign those letters identified for department use below according to agency policy; however, any use must be applied to the entire department or agency.
L2:(4) Positions 10 through 17 . Use the number assigned by the issuing agency in these positions. Agencies may choose between four and eight characters to be used, but the same number of characters must be used agencywide. Do not use leading or trailing zeroes to equal the maximum in any system or data transmission. A separate series of numbers may be used for any type of instrument listed in paragraph (b)(3) of this section. An agency may reserve blocks of numbers or alpha-numeric numbers for its various components to use.
L1:(c) Agencies must use a non-unique identifier for a procurement action (i.e., supplementary PIID) that is used with the PIID. The supplementary PIID is used to identify amendments to solicitations and modifications to contracts, orders, and agreements. The supplementary PIID is reported as a separate data element used with, but not appended to, the PIID.
L2:(1) Amendments to solicitations . Use a four-position numeric serial number in addition to the 13–17-character PIID beginning with 0001.
L2:(2) Modifications to contracts, orders, and agreements . Use a six-position alpha, numeric, or a combination of both, in addition to the 13–17-character PIID. For example, a modification could be numbered P00001.
L3:(i) Position 1 . Use the letter P if the modification is issued by the procuring contracting office. Use the letter A if the modification is issued by the contract administration office (if other than the procuring contracting office).
L3:(ii) Positions 2 through 6 . These positions may be alpha, numeric, or a combination of both, according to agency procedures.
L3:(iii) Each office authorized to issue modifications must assign the supplementary identification numbers in sequence (unless provided otherwise in agency procedures). Do not assign the numbers until the contracting officer determines that a modification is to be issued.
L1:(d)
L2:(1) Agencies must not change the PIID unless one of the following circumstances applies:
L3:(i) The PIID serial numbering system is exhausted.
L3:(ii) Continued use of a PIID is administratively burdensome (e.g., for implementing new agency contract writing systems).
L3:(iii) The contract is transferred between contracting departments.
L2:(2) If one of the circumstances described at 4.201(d)(1) applies, the contracting officer may assign a new PIID by issuing an administrative contract modification (see part 43). The modification must identify both the original and the newly assigned PIID.

title: 4.202 Uniform use of line items
content:
4.202 Uniform use of line items

L1:(a) Procurement instruments must identify the supplies or services to be acquired as separately identified line items and, as needed, subline items.
L1:(b) Line items—
L2:(1) Are established to define deliverables or organize information about deliverables;
L2:(2) Describe characteristics for the item purchased, e.g., pricing, delivery, and funding information; and
L2:(3) May be subdivided into separate unique subsets (called subline items) to ease administration. Subline items are established to define deliverables (deliverable subline items) or organize information about deliverables (informational subline items). If a line item has deliverable subline items, the line item itself is informational.

title: 4.202-1 Policy
content:
4.202-1 Policy

L1:(a) Procurement instruments must identify the supplies or services to be acquired as separately identified line items and, as needed, subline items.
L1:(b) Line items—
L2:(1) Are established to define deliverables or organize information about deliverables;
L2:(2) Describe characteristics for the item purchased, e.g., pricing, delivery, and funding information; and
L2:(3) May be subdivided into separate unique subsets (called subline items) to ease administration. Subline items are established to define deliverables (deliverable subline items) or organize information about deliverables (informational subline items). If a line item has deliverable subline items, the line item itself is informational.

title: 4.202-2 Establishing line items
content:
4.202-2 Establishing line items

L0:Establish separate line items for deliverables that have the following characteristics except as provided at 4.202-5:
L1:(a) Separately identifiable.
L2:(1) A supply is separately identifiable if it has its own identification (e.g., national stock number (NSN), item description, manufacturer's part number).
L2:(2) Services are separately identifiable if they have no more than one statement of work or performance work statement.
L2:(3) If the procurement instrument involves a first article (see part 9), establish a separate line item for each item requiring a separate approval. If the first article consists of a lot composed of a mixture of items that will be approved as a single lot, a single line item may be used.
L1:(b) Single unit price or total price.
L1:(c) Single accounting classification citation. A single deliverable may be funded by multiple accounting classifications when the deliverable effort cannot be otherwise subdivided.
L1:(d) Separate delivery schedule, destination, period of performance, or place of performance.
L1:(e) Single contract pricing type (e.g., fixed-price or cost-reimbursement).

title: 4.202-3 Establishing subline items
content:
4.202-3 Establishing subline items

L0:Subline items may be used to facilitate tracking of performance, deliverables, payment, and contract funds accounting or for other management purposes. The list of characteristics at 4.202-2 applies to deliverable subline items, but it is not applicable to informational subline items. A line item with subline items must contain only that information that is common to all subline items thereunder. All subline items under one line item must be the same contract type as the line item.
L1:(a) Deliverable subline items. Deliverable subline items may be used for several related items that require separate identification. For example, instead of establishing multiple separate line items, subline items may be established for—
L2:(1) Items that are basically the same, except for minor variations such as—
L3:(i) Size or color;
L3:(ii) Accounting classification, but see also 4.202-4(a)(4); or
L3:(iii) Date of delivery, destination, or period or place of performance;
L2:(2) Separately priced collateral functions that relate to the primary product, such as packaging and handling, or transportation; or
L2:(3) Items to be separately identified at the time of shipment or performance.
L1:(b) Informational subline items.
L2:(1) Informational subline items may be used by agencies for administrative purposes. This type of subline item identifies information that relates directly to the line item and is an integral part of it (e.g., parts of an assembly or parts of a kit).
L2:(2) Position informational subline items within the line item description, not in the quantity or price fields.

title: 4.202-4 Required data elements for line items and subline items
content:
4.202-4 Required data elements for line items and subline items

L1:(a) Except as provided in 4.202-5, each line item or subline item must include in the schedule (or in a comparable section of the procurement instrument), at a minimum, the following information as separate, distinct data elements:
L2:(1) Line item or subline item number established in accordance with agency procedures.
L2:(2) Description of what is being purchased.
L2:(3) Product or Service Code (PSC).
L2:(4) Accounting classification citation.
L3:(i) Line items or deliverable subline items. If multiple accounting classifications for a single deliverable apply, include the dollar amount for each accounting classification in the schedule (or a comparable section of the procurement instrument).
L3:(ii) Informational subline items. An accounting classification citation is not required. (See 4.202-3).
L2:(5)
L3:(i) For fixed-price line items:
L4:(A) Unit of measure.
L4:(B) Quantity.
L4:(C) Unit price.
L4:(D) Total price.
L3:(ii) For cost-reimbursement line items:
L4:(C) Estimated cost.
L4:(D) Fee (if any).
L4:(E) Total estimated cost plus any fee.
L1:(b) If a contract contains a combination of fixed-price, time-and-materials, labor-hour, or cost- reimbursement line items, identify the contract type for each line item in the schedule (or a comparable section of the procurement instrument) to facilitate payment.
L1:(c) Each deliverable line item or deliverable subline item must have its own delivery schedule, destination, period of performance, or place of performance expressly stated in the appropriate section of the procurement instrument (“as required” constitutes an expressly stated delivery term). When a line item has deliverable subline items, identify the delivery schedule, destination, period of performance, or place of performance at the subline item level, rather than the line item level.
L1:(d) Terms and conditions in other sections of the contract (such as contract clauses or payment instructions) must also specify applicability to individual line items if not applicable to the contract as a whole.

title: 4.202-5 Exceptions to required data elements
content:
4.202-5 Exceptions to required data elements

L1:(a) Indefinite-delivery contracts —
L2:(1) General. The following required data elements are not known at time of issuance of an indefinite-delivery contract, however each order must provide them at issuance: accounting classification, delivery date and destination, or period and place of performance.
L2:(2) Indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) and requirements contracts.
L3:(i) IDIQ and requirements contracts may omit the quantity at the line item level for the base award provided that the total contract minimum and maximum, or the estimate, respectively, is stated.
L3:(ii) Multiple-award IDIQ contracts awarded using the procedures at parts 13 or 15 may omit price or cost at the line item or subline item level for the contract award, provided that the total contract minimum and maximum is stated (see part 16).
L1:(b) Item description and PSC. These data elements are not required in the line item if there are associated deliverable subline items that include the actual detailed identification. When this exception applies, use a general narrative description for the line item.
L1:(c) Single unit price or single total price. The requirement for a single unit price or single total price at the line item level does not apply if any of the following conditions are present:
L2:(1) There are associated deliverable subline items that are priced.
L2:(2) The line item or subline item is not separately priced.
L2:(3) The supplies or services are being acquired on a cost-reimbursement, time-and-materials, or labor-hour basis.
L2:(4) The procurement instrument is for services and firm prices have been established for elements of the total price, but the actual number of the elements is not known until performance (e.g., a labor-hour contract for maintenance/repair). The contracting officer may structure these procurement instruments to reflect a firm or estimated total amount for each line item.

title: 4.203 System for Award Management
4.203-1 Policy
4.203-2 Procedures
content:
4.203-2 Procedures

L1:(a) At the time an offer or quotation is submitted—
L2:(1) Use the offeror or quoter’s UEI to verify that the entity has an active Federal Government contracts registration in SAM, and document the date of SAM verification in the contract file; or
L2:(2) If a solicitation does not require registration in SAM—
L3:(i) Review the information provided in response to the provision at 52.204-90, Offeror Identification, and validate the CAGE code using the CAGE code search feature at https://cage.dla.mil ; and
L3:(ii) Verify the offeror has included in its offer the entity-level representations and certifications normally collected in SAM.
L1:(b) Use the legal business name or “doing business as” name and physical address in SAM for the successful offeror’s UEI to identify the contractor in the award document and all corresponding forms and data exchanges. Do not change data retrieved from SAM.

title: 4.204 Taxpayer identification information
content:
4.204 Taxpayer identification information

L1:(a) Agencies must collect the taxpayer identification number (TIN) to comply with the following statutory requirements—
L2:(1) Debt collection . 31 U.S.C. 7701(c) requires each contractor doing business with a Government agency to furnish its TIN to that agency. 31 U.S.C. 3325(d) requires the Government to include the TIN of the contractor receiving payment with each certified voucher. The Government may use the TIN to collect and report on any delinquent amounts arising out of the contractor's relationship with the Government.
L2:(2) Information reporting to the IRS. The TIN is required for Government reporting of certain contract information and payment information to the IRS. 26 U.S.C. 6109 requires a contractor to provide its TIN if a Form 1099 is required. The payment office is responsible for submitting reports to the IRS.
L1:(b) Contracting officers will obtain the TIN from—
L2:(1) SAM if offerors are required to be registered in SAM, see 4.203-2(a)(1) and 52.204-7; or
L2:(2) Offers if offerors are not required to be registered in SAM, see 4.203-2(a)(2) and 52.204-90.

title: 4.205 Personal identity verification
content:
4.205 Personal identity verification

L1:(a) Agencies must include their implementation of Homeland Security Presidential Directive-12 and the Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) Number 201 in solicitations and contracts. For information on personal identity verification (PIV) products and services see http://www.idmanagement.gov .
L1:(b) When acquiring PIV products and services not using the General Services Administration Federal Supply Schedule for HSPD-12 Product and Service Components, agencies must ensure that the applicable products and services are approved as compliant with FIPS PUB 201 including—
L2:(1) Certifying the products and services procured meet all applicable Federal standards and requirements;
L2:(2) Ensuring interoperability and conformance to applicable Federal standards for the lifecycle of the components; and
L2:(3) Maintaining a written plan for ensuring ongoing conformance to applicable Federal standards for the lifecycle of the components.

title: 4.206 Contracting officer's signature
content:
4.206 Contracting officer's signature

L0:Only contracting officers can sign contracts on behalf of the United States. The contracting officer's name and official title must be typed, stamped, or printed on the contract. The contracting officer normally signs the contract after the contractor has signed it. A digital signature using a certificate from the PIV or Common Access Card (CAC) assigned to the contracting officer is considered acceptable as a written signature.

title: 4.207 Contractor's signature
content:
4.207 Contractor's signature

L1:(a) Individuals . A contract with an individual must be signed by that individual. A contract with an individual doing business as a firm must be signed by that individual, and the signature must be followed by the individual's typed, stamped, or printed name and the words “, an individual doing business as ______________________” [insert name of firm].
L1:(b) Partnerships . A contract with a partnership must be signed in the partnership name. Before signing for the Government, the contracting officer must obtain a list of all partners and ensure that the individual(s) signing for the partnership have authority to bind the partnership.
L1:(c) Corporations . A contract with a corporation must be signed in the corporate name, followed by the word “by” and the signature and title of the person authorized to sign. The contracting officer must ensure that the person signing for the corporation has authority to bind the corporation.
L1:(d) Joint venturers. A contract with joint venturers may involve any combination of individuals, partnerships, or corporations. The contract must be signed by each participant in the joint venture in the manner prescribed in paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section for each type of participant. When a corporation is participating, the contracting officer must verify that the corporation is authorized to participate in the joint venture.
L1:(e) Agents . When an agent is to sign the contract, other than as stated in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section, the agent's authorization to bind the principal must be established by evidence that satisfies the contracting officer.
L1:(f) Digital signatures . Contractor’s digital signatures are acceptable as a written signature when using authentication and/or signature certificates from a PIV or CAC obtained from a credentialed organization.

title: 4.208 Solicitation provisions and contract clauses
content:

L1:(c) When offerors are not required to be registered in SAM, insert—

title: Subpart 4.3 Post-award
content:
Subpart 4.3 Post-award

L1:(a) As required by 41 U.S.C. 1122 and 1712, the Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS), https://www.fpds.gov , provides a comprehensive web-based tool for agencies to report contract actions.
L2:(1) At a minimum, agencies must report—
L3:(i) The following contract actions over the micro-purchase threshold, regardless of solicitation process used:
L4:(A) Definitive contracts, including purchase orders and imprest fund buys awarded by a contracting officer.
L4:(B) Indefinite delivery vehicle (identified as an “IDV” in FPDS) and all calls and orders awarded under it; and
L3:(ii) Any modification to the contract actions in paragraph (a)(1)(i) that change previously reported contract action data, regardless of dollar value.
L2:(2) Agencies may submit actions other than those listed at paragraph (a)(1) of this section if approved in writing by the Office of Federal Procurement Policy (OFPP).
L2:(3) Agencies will not report the following types of contract actions in FPDS:
L3:(i) Imprest fund transactions below the micro-purchase threshold, including those made via the Government purchase card (unless specific agency procedures prescribe reporting these actions).
L3:(ii) Orders from the General Services Administration ( GSA) stock and the GSA Global Supply Program.
L3:(iii) Purchases made at GSA or AbilityOne service stores, as these items stocked for resale have already been reported by GSA.
L3:(iv) Purchases made using non-appropriated fund activity cards, chaplain fund cards, individual Government personnel training orders, and Defense Printing orders.
L3:(v) Actions that, according to other authority, will not be entered into FPDS ( e.g. , reporting of the information would compromise national security).
L3:(vi) Contract actions in which the required data would constitute classified information.
L3:(vii) Resale activity ( i.e., commissary or exchange activity).
L3:(viii) Revenue generating arrangements ( i.e., concessions).
L3:(ix) Training expenditures not issued as orders or contracts.
L3:(x) Interagency agreements other than interagency acquisitions required to be reported.
L3:(xi) Letters of obligation used in the A-76 process.
L1:(b) Agencies awarding assisted acquisitions or direct acquisitions must report these actions and identify the Program/Funding Agency and Office Codes from the applicable agency codes maintained by each agency at the System for Award Management (SAM). These codes represent the agency and office that has provided the predominant amount of funding for the contract action. For assisted acquisitions, the requesting agency will receive socioeconomic credit for meeting agency small business goals, where applicable. Requesting agencies must provide the appropriate agency/bureau component code as part of the written interagency agreement between the requesting and servicing agencies (see part 17).
L1:(c) Agencies awarding contract actions with a mix of appropriated and non-appropriated funding must only report the full appropriated portion of the contract action in FPDS.
L1:(d) Agencies may consolidate, at least monthly, multiple action reports for a vendor when it would be overly burdensome to report each action individually.
L1:(e)
L2:(1) Agencies m ay use a generic entity identifier , rather than an entity’s assigned unique entity identifier (UEI), for—
L3:(i) Contract actions valued at or below $40,000 that are awarded to a contractor that is—
L4:(A) A student;
L4:(B) A dependent of either a veteran, foreign Service officer, or military member assigned outside the United States and its outlying areas (as defined in 2.101); or
L4:(C) Located outside the United States and its outlying areas for work to be performed outside the United States and its outlying areas and the contractor does not otherwise have a UEI;
L3:(ii) Contracts valued above $40,000 awarded to individuals located outside the United States and its outlying areas for work to be performed outside the United States and its outlying areas; or
L3:(iii) Contracts when specific public identification of the contracted party could endanger the mission, contractor, or recipients of the acquired goods or services. The contracting officer must include a written determination in the contract file of a decision applicable to authority under this paragraph (g)(1)(iii).
L2:(2) The Integrated Award Environment program office will maintain the list of generic entity identifiers that agencies may use.
L1:(f) Responsibilities .
L2:(1) The Senior Procurement Executive in coordination with the head of the contracting activity is responsible for developing and monitoring a process to ensure timely and accurate reporting of contractual actions to FPDS.
L2:(2)
L3:(i) The contracting officer awarding the contract action is responsible for accurately completing the individual contract action report (CAR). Unpublished CARs in FPDS are not considered complete.
L3:(ii) Complete the CAR in FPDS within three business days after contract award.
L3:(iii) Complete the CAR for any action awarded without providing full and open competition due to unusual or compelling urgency or according to any of the emergency acquisition flexibilities (see part 18) within 30 days after contract award.
L2:(3) The chief acquisition officer of each agency required to report its contract actions must submit to OFPP within 120 days after the end of each fiscal year, an annual certification of whether, and to what degree, agency CAR data for the preceding fiscal year is complete and accurate.
