title: Subpart 12.3 Postaward
content:
Subpart 12.3 Postaward

L1:(a) Posting requirements .
L2:(1) Comply with the award notice posting requirements in subpart 5.3.
L2:(2) Make the justifications required by 12.102(b) for acquisitions valued over the SAT publicly available in accordance with 6.301.
L1:(b) Explanations for unsuccessful quoters. When using the simplified procedures at 12.201-1, upon request, provide a brief explanation of the award decision that explains why the unsuccessful quoter was not selected. If an award notice was not required to be posted to the GPE, also provide the information that would be included in an award notice (see 5.301(c)).
L1:(c) Notifications and debriefings of unsuccessful offerors. When using the procedures in 12.201-2, follow the procedures in part 15 or 14 for notification of unsuccessful offerors and debriefings, as appropriate. When providing a debriefing, include the information listed at 52.212-1(e).

title: 12.301 Notifications
content:
12.301 Notifications

L1:(a) Posting requirements .
L2:(1) Comply with the award notice posting requirements in subpart 5.3.
L2:(2) Make the justifications required by 12.102(b) for acquisitions valued over the SAT publicly available in accordance with 6.301.
L1:(b) Explanations for unsuccessful quoters. When using the simplified procedures at 12.201-1, upon request, provide a brief explanation of the award decision that explains why the unsuccessful quoter was not selected. If an award notice was not required to be posted to the GPE, also provide the information that would be included in an award notice (see 5.301(c)).
L1:(c) Notifications and debriefings of unsuccessful offerors. When using the procedures in 12.201-2, follow the procedures in part 15 or 14 for notification of unsuccessful offerors and debriefings, as appropriate. When providing a debriefing, include the information listed at 52.212-1(e).

title: 12.302 Subcontracts
content:
12.302 Subcontracts

L0:See requirements for subcontracts for commercial products and commercial services in part 44.

title: 12.303 Cancellations
content:
12.303 Cancellations

L1:(a) The Government may withdraw, amend, or cancel purchase orders by written notice to the supplier at any time before acceptance of the order occurs (see 12.201-1(b)).
L1:(b) If the supplier did not accept the purchase order in writing, request that the supplier provide written acceptance of the cancellation.
L1:(c) If the contractor does not accept the cancellation or claims that costs were incurred as a result of the contractor beginning performance under the purchase order, follow the procedures at 12.304 to terminate the purchase order.

title: 12.304 Terminations
content:
12.304 Terminations

L1:(a) General. Follow the procedures in this section and the termination paragraphs of the clause at 52.212-4, when terminating contracts for commercial products or commercial services. Do not use the procedures in part 49.
L1:(b) Termination for cause .
L2:(1) Before terminating a contract for cause, send a cure notice to the contractor, unless the reason for the termination is late delivery.
L2:(2) When a termination for cause is appropriate, send the contractor a written notification regarding the termination. At a minimum, this notification must include—
L3:(i) A statement that the contract is terminated for cause;
L3:(ii) The reasons for the termination;
L3:(iii) Which remedies the Government intends to seek or give a date by which the Government will inform the contractor of the remedy; and
L3:(iv) A statement that the notice constitutes a final decision of the contracting officer, and that the contractor has the right to appeal under the Disputes clause.
L2:(3) Follow the procedures in part 42 to report termination information to the Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System.
L1:(c) Termination for the Government’s convenience. When terminating for the Government’s convenience, the parties should mutually agree upon the requirements of the termination proposal. Balance the Government’s need to obtain sufficient documentation to support payment to the contractor against the goal of having a simple and expeditious settlement.

title: Subpart 12.4 Micro-purchases
content:
Subpart 12.4 Micro-purchases

L1:(a) Agency heads are encouraged to delegate micro-purchase authority (see part 1).
L1:(b) Micro-purchases do not require written provisions or clauses. This paragraph takes precedence over any other FAR requirement to the contrary but does not prohibit the use of any clause.
L1:(c) The security prohibitions and exclusions addressed at subpart 40.2 apply to micro-purchases, unless an exception applies or waiver is granted according to that subpart. However, the provisions and clauses in that subpart are not used for micro-purchases.
L1:(d) Paragraph (s) , Unauthorized Obligations, of the clause at 52.212-4, Terms and Conditions—Commercial Products and Commercial Services, automatically applies to any micro-purchase, including those made with the Governmentwide commercial purchase card. This clause prevents violations of the Anti-Deficiency Act (31 U.S.C. 1341).

title: 12.401 General
content:
12.401 General

L1:(a) Agency heads are encouraged to delegate micro-purchase authority (see part 1).
L1:(b) Micro-purchases do not require written provisions or clauses. This paragraph takes precedence over any other FAR requirement to the contrary but does not prohibit the use of any clause.
L1:(c) The security prohibitions and exclusions addressed at subpart 40.2 apply to micro-purchases, unless an exception applies or waiver is granted according to that subpart. However, the provisions and clauses in that subpart are not used for micro-purchases.
L1:(d) Paragraph (s) , Unauthorized Obligations, of the clause at 52.212-4, Terms and Conditions—Commercial Products and Commercial Services, automatically applies to any micro-purchase, including those made with the Governmentwide commercial purchase card. This clause prevents violations of the Anti-Deficiency Act (31 U.S.C. 1341).

title: 12.402 Purchase guidelines
content:
12.402 Purchase guidelines

L1:(a) To the extent practicable, distribute micro-purchases equitably among qualified suppliers.
L1:(b) Micro-purchases may be awarded without soliciting competitive quotations if the contracting officer or individual appointed in accordance with 1.403-2(b) considers the price to be reasonable.
L1:(c) The administrative cost of verifying the reasonableness of the price for purchases may more than offset potential savings from detecting instances of overpricing. Therefore, action to verify price reasonableness need only be taken if there is—
L2:(1) A lack of understanding of competitive pricing; or
L2:(2) Reason to suspect that a price is not reasonable.
L1:(d) If the contracting officer solicited competitive quotations and made award to a supplier that did not provide the lowest quote, documentation of the award must include identification of the suppliers solicited and a brief explanation of the award decision.

title: 12.403 Methods
content:
12.403 Methods

L1:(a) Use the following methods as the primary means of making micro-purchases:
L2:(1) The Governmentwide commercial purchase card . The Governmentwide commercial purchase card is authorized for use in making purchases of supplies, services, or construction. Contracting officers and other individuals designated according to part 1 may use the Governmentwide commercial purchase card. The card may be used only for purchases authorized by law or regulation.
L2:(2) Purchase orders . Purchase orders (including orders against blanket purchase agreements) may be used to make micro-purchases. See 12.203(d)(1).
L1:(b) The SF 44, Purchase Order-Invoice-Voucher, is a multipurpose pocket-size purchase order form designed primarily for on-the-spot, over-the-counter purchases of supplies and nonpersonal services while away from the purchasing office or at isolated activities. Contracting officers may use it in limited circumstances and only when advantageous to the Government if all of the following conditions are satisfied:
L2:(1) An agency authorizes use of the SF 44.
L2:(2) The amount of the purchase is at or below the micro-purchase threshold or higher dollar thresholds established by an agency for purchases made under unusual and compelling urgency or in support of contingency operations.
L2:(3) The supplies or services are immediately available, and one delivery and one payment will be made.
L2:(4) Its use is determined to be more economical and efficient than use of the Governmentwide commercial purchase card.
L1:(c) Imprest funds and third-party drafts may be used to acquire supplies or services if an agency receives authorization from the Department of Treasury to use these methods and the purchases are made in accordance with Part IV of the Treasury Financial Manual for Guidance of Departments and Agencies. An imprest fund transaction shall not exceed $500 or such other limits as have been approved by the agency head. A third-party draft transaction shall not exceed $2,500, unless authorized at a higher level in accordance with Treasury restrictions.

title: 13.000 Scope of part
content:
13.000 Scope of part

L0:This part implements simplified procedures for the acquisition of noncommercial products and services valued at or below the simplified acquisition threshold (SAT) in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 1901-1903, 1905, and 3305.

title: 13.001 Applicability
content:
13.001 Applicability

L1:(a) The procedures in this part may be used only if—
L2:(1) There are no commercial products or commercial services that can satisfy the agency’s needs (see part 12); and
L2:(2) The supplies or services are not available from a required source (see part 8).
L1:(b) Follow the procedures in this part when procuring noncommercial products and services valued at greater than the micro-purchase threshold (MPT) but at or below the SAT, except
L2:(1) When procuring architect-engineering services, follow the short selection process at 36.602-5;
L2:(2) When procuring construction as a noncommercial service, comply with the requirements in part 36 for construction contracts and subpart 22.4 on labor standards for contracts involving construction; and
L2:(3) When procuring research and development, use the procedures in this part in conjunction with the procedures in part 35, as appropriate.
L1:(c) Do not divide requirements, the aggregate value of which exceeds the SAT, merely to permit use of the procedures in this part.
L1:(d) Go to https://www.acquisition.gov/inapplicablelaws for the lists of laws that do not apply to acquisitions valued at or below the SAT (41 U.S.C. 1905).

title: Subpart 13.1 Presolicitation
content:
Subpart 13.1 Presolicitation

L1:(a) Agencies must promote competition to the maximum extent practicable when procuring noncommercial products and services valued at or below the SAT.
L1:(b) Contracting officers may solicit from a single source based on a determination and findings (see subpart 1.5) that only one source is reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand-name or industrial mobilization).

title: 13.101 Competition
content:
13.101 Competition

L1:(a) Agencies must promote competition to the maximum extent practicable when procuring noncommercial products and services valued at or below the SAT.
L1:(b) Contracting officers may solicit from a single source based on a determination and findings (see subpart 1.5) that only one source is reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand-name or industrial mobilization).

title: 13.102 Small business
content:
13.102 Small business

L0:Acquisitions of supplies or services that have an anticipated dollar value above the MPT, but at or below the SAT, must be set aside for small business concerns (see part 19).

title: 13.103 Quality assurance
content:
13.103 Quality assurance

L0:Generally, inspection and acceptance should be at destination. Inspection at the supplier’s location should be specified only if required by 46.404.

title: Subpart 13.2 Solicitation, Evaluation, and Award
content:
Subpart 13.2 Solicitation, Evaluation, and Award

L0:Follow the simplified procedures at 12.201-1 for issuing requests for quotations (RFQs). Agencies are encouraged to use additional innovative approaches and may leverage the other flexibilities identified in that section; however, if using blanket purchase agreements (BPAs), the maximum value of each individual purchase under a BPA may not exceed the SAT.

title: 13.201 Procedures
content:
13.201 Procedures

L0:Follow the simplified procedures at 12.201-1 for issuing requests for quotations (RFQs). Agencies are encouraged to use additional innovative approaches and may leverage the other flexibilities identified in that section; however, if using blanket purchase agreements (BPAs), the maximum value of each individual purchase under a BPA may not exceed the SAT.

title: 13.202 Evaluation
content:
13.202 Evaluation

L0:Follow the procedures in 12.203 when establishing evaluation factors and a process to evaluate quotations in an efficient and minimally burdensome manner. Notify potential quoters of the basis on which the agency will make the award decision. Exercise good business judgment in deciding whether or not to accept a quotation received after the due date or time.

title: 13.203 Award
content:
13.203 Award

L1:(a) Price reasonableness . The contracting officer must determine the price to be fair and reasonable. Whenever possible, base price reasonableness on competitive quotations.
L1:(b) Documentation . Include in the contract file a written description of the procedures used in awarding the purchase order and the number of quotations received.
L1:(c) Forms and format . Use the Optional Form (OF) 347, Order for Supplies or Services; the OF 336, Continuation Sheet, or OF 348, Order for Supplies and Services Schedule—Continuation; or similar agency forms or automated formats to the maximum extent practicable.

title: 13.204 Contract clauses
content:
13.204 Contract clauses

L1:(a) Include clauses prescribed elsewhere in the FAR in purchase orders for noncommercial supplies or services valued at or below the SAT as required or applicable based on the clause prescriptions.
L1:(b) Contracting officers may use the clause at 52.213-4, Terms and Conditions—Simplified Acquisitions (Noncommercial), to provide a streamlined set of terms and conditions for inspection/acceptance, excusable delays, terminations, and warranties. This clause is either used in lieu of similar clauses prescribed for these purposes or tailored to incorporate only some of the streamlined terms and conditions, as necessary.
L1:(c) Do not use part 12 clauses ( i.e. , 52.212-1, 52.212-2, or 52.212-4) in noncommercial acquisitions.

title: Subpart 13.3 Postaward
content:
Subpart 13.3 Postaward

L0:Comply with the award notice posting requirements in subpart 5.3. Upon request, provide a brief explanation of the award decision that explains why the unsuccessful quoter was not selected. If an award notice was not required to be posted to the Government point of entry, also provide the information that would be included in an award notice (see 5.301(c)).

title: 13.301 Notifications
content:
13.301 Notifications

L0:Comply with the award notice posting requirements in subpart 5.3. Upon request, provide a brief explanation of the award decision that explains why the unsuccessful quoter was not selected. If an award notice was not required to be posted to the Government point of entry, also provide the information that would be included in an award notice (see 5.301(c)).

title: 13.302 Cancellations and terminations
content:
13.302 Cancellations and terminations

L1:(a) The Government may withdraw, amend, or cancel purchase orders by written notice to the supplier at any time before acceptance of the order occurs (see 12.201-1(b)).
L1:(b) If the supplier did not accept the purchase order in writing, request that the supplier provide written acceptance of the cancellation.
L1:(c) If the contractor does not accept the cancellation or claims that costs were incurred as a result of the contractor beginning performance under the purchase order, follow the procedures in part 49 or 52.213-4 to terminate the purchase order.

title: 13.303 Contract financing and payments
content:
13.303 Contract financing and payments

L1:(a) Unless agency regulations permit otherwise, do not provide financing for purchases valued at or below the SAT.
L1:(b) See part 32 for payment procedures, including the option to use fast payment procedures.

title: Subpart 13.4 Micro-purchases
content:
Subpart 13.4 Micro-purchases

L1:(a) Follow the procedure in 12.4 when making purchases valued at or below the MPT.
L1:(b) While micro-purchases do not require written provision or clauses, the clause at 52.232-39, Unenforceability of Unauthorized Obligations, automatically applies to any micro-purchase, including those made with the Governmentwide commercial purchase card. This clause prevents violations of the Anti-Deficiency Act (31 U.S.C. 1341).

title: 13.401 General
content:
13.401 General

L1:(a) Follow the procedure in 12.4 when making purchases valued at or below the MPT.
L1:(b) While micro-purchases do not require written provision or clauses, the clause at 52.232-39, Unenforceability of Unauthorized Obligations, automatically applies to any micro-purchase, including those made with the Governmentwide commercial purchase card. This clause prevents violations of the Anti-Deficiency Act (31 U.S.C. 1341).

title: 14.000 Scope of part
content:
14.000 Scope of part

L0:This part prescribes (a) the basic requirements of contracting for supplies and services (including construction) by sealed bidding, (b) the information to be included in the invitation for bids (IFB), (c) procedures concerning the submission of bids, (d) requirements for opening, evaluating bids, awarding contracts, and (e) procedures for two-step sealed bidding.

title: Subpart 14.1 General
content:
Subpart 14.1 General

L1:(a) Sealed bidding is a method of contracting that employs competitive bids, public opening of bids, and awards.
L1:(b) Use sealed bidding whenever the conditions in 6.101(b) are met.
L1:(c) The contracting officer must use firm-fixed-price contracts when using sealed bidding or fixed-price contracts with economic price adjustment clauses when some flexibility is necessary and feasible.

title: Subpart 14.2 Presolicitation
content:
Subpart 14.2 Presolicitation

L1:(a) Contracting officers must prepare invitation for bids and contracts using parts I, II, III, and IV of the uniform contract format (see part 15) to the maximum practicable extent.
L1:(b) The uniform contract format is not required when contracting for—
L2:(1) Construction (see part 36);
L2:(2) Shipbuilding (including design, construction, and conversion), ship overhaul, and ship repair;
L2:(3) Subsistence items;
L2:(4) Supplies or services requiring special contract forms prescribed elsewhere in this regulation that are inconsistent with the uniform contract format; or
L2:(5) Firm-fixed-price or fixed-price with economic price adjustment acquisitions that use the simplified contract format.
L1:(c)
L2:(1) The contracting officer may use the simplified contract format in lieu of the uniform contract format.
L2:(2) The contracting officer has flexibility in preparation and organization of the simplified contract format. The following format should be used to the maximum extent practical:
L3:(i) Use Standard Form (SF) 1447, Solicitation/Contract, as the first page of the IFB.
L3:(ii) Include the following for each line item:
L4:(A) Line item number.
L4:(B) Description of supplies or services, or data sufficient to identify the requirement.
L4:(C) Quantity and unit of issue.
L4:(D) Unit price and amount.
L4:(E) Packaging and marking requirements.
L4:(F) Inspection and acceptance, quality assurance, and reliability requirements.
L4:(G) Place of delivery, performance and delivery dates, period of performance, and f.o.b. point.
L4:(H) Other item-peculiar information as necessary (e.g., individual fund citations).
L3:(iii) Include the clauses required by this regulation. Additional clauses must be incorporated only when necessary to the particular acquisition.
L3:(iv) List of documents and attachments (include if necessary).
L3:(v) Representations and instructions:
L4:(A) Insert the IFB provisions that require representations, certifications, or the submission of other information by offerors.
L4:(B) Insert the IFB provisions required by 14.207. Include any other information/instructions necessary to guide offerors.
L4:(C) Insert all price related evaluation factors and any significant price related subfactors for award.
L4:(D) Upon award, the contracting officer must retain the representations and instructions in the contract file.

title: 14.202 Uniform contract format
content:
14.202 Uniform contract format

L0:The contracting officer must prepare the Schedule as follows:
L1:(a) Section A, Solicitation/contract form .
L2:(1) For sealed bidding the SF 33 or the SF 1447 may be used. When the SF 1447 is used as the IFB document, insert the information in subdivisions (a)(2)(i) and (a)(2)(iv) of this section in block 9 of the SF 1447.
L2:(2) If the SF 33 or the SF 1447 are not used, include the following on the first page of the invitation for bids:
L3:(i) Name, address, and location of issuing activity, including room and building where bids must be submitted.
L3:(ii) Invitation for bids number.
L3:(iii) Date of issuance.
L3:(iv) Time specified for receipt of bids.
L3:(v) Number of pages.
L3:(vi) Requisition or other purchase authority.
L3:(vii) Requirement for a bidder to provide its name and complete address, including street, city, county, State, and ZIP code.
L3:(viii) A statement that bidders should include in the bid the address to which payment should be mailed, if that address is different from that of the bidder.
L1:(b) Section B, Supplies or services and prices .
L2:(1) See 15.108-1(b)
L2:(2) Optional Form 336 (OF 336), Continuation Sheet, may be used.
L1:(c) Section C, Description/specifications. (see 15.108-1(c)).
L1:(d) Section D, Packaging and marking (see 15.108-1(d)).
L1:(e) Section E, Inspection and acceptance (see 15.108-1(e)).
L1:(f) Section F, Deliveries or performance (see 15.108-1(f)).
L1:(g) Section G, Contract administration data (see 15.108-1(g)).
L1:(h) Section H, Special contract requirements (see 15.108-1(h)).

14.202-1 Part I Schedule

L1:(a) Section A, Solicitation/contract form .
L2:(1) For sealed bidding the SF 33 or the SF 1447 may be used. When the SF 1447 is used as the IFB document, insert the information in subdivisions (a)(2)(i) and (a)(2)(iv) of this section in block 9 of the SF 1447.
L2:(2) If the SF 33 or the SF 1447 are not used, include the following on the first page of the invitation for bids:

title: 14.202-2 Part II Contract clauses
content:
14.202-2 Part II Contract clauses

L0:Section I, Contract clauses (see 15.108-2).

title: 14.202-3 Part III Documents, exhibits, and other attachments
content:
14.202-3 Part III Documents, exhibits, and other attachments

L0:Section J, List of documents, exhibits, and other attachments (see 15.108-3).

title: 14.202-4 Part IV Representations and instructions
content:
14.202-4 Part IV Representations and instructions

L0:The contracting officer must prepare the representations and instructions as follows:
L1:(a) Section K, Representations, certifications, and other statements of bidders (see 15.108-4(a)).
L1:(b) Section L, Instructions, conditions, and notices to bidders (see 15.108-4(b)). The contracting officer must include the time and place for bid openings.
L1:(c) Section M, Evaluation factors for award (see 15.108-4(c)).

title: 14.203 Requirements
content:
14.203 Requirements

L1:(a) An IFB must clearly, accurately, and completely describe the Government requirements.
L1:(b) Restrictive specifications or requirements that might unduly limit the number of bidders are prohibited.
L1:(c) Include all documents and information (whether attached or incorporated by reference) prospective bidders will need for the purpose of bidding.
L1:(d) The contracting officer must state in the invitation for bids that bids will be evaluated without discussions (see 52.214-10 and, for construction contracts, 52.214-19).
L1:(e) When considering establishing qualification requirements, see and follow subpart 9.2.

title: 14.204 Economic purchase quantities (supplies)
content:
14.204 Economic purchase quantities (supplies)

L0:Contracting officers must comply with the economic purchase quantity planning requirements for supplies in part 7. See part 7 for instructions regarding use of the provision at 52.207-4, Economic Purchase Quantity—Supplies, and for guidance on handling responses to that provision.

title: 14.205 Bid samples
content:
14.205 Bid samples

L1:(a) The contracting officer must not require bidders to furnish bid samples unless—
L2:(1) Characteristics of the product cannot be described adequately in the specification or purchase description;
L2:(2) Necessary to determine the responsiveness of the bid. Do not use samples to determine a bidder's ability to produce the required items; and
L2:(3) Products must be suitable from the standpoint of balance, facility of use, general “feel”, color, pattern, or other characteristics that cannot be described adequately in the specification.
L1:(b) If the contracting officer requires bid samples, the IFB must state—
L2:(1) The number and, if appropriate, size, and description of the bid samples required; and
L2:(2) List all the characteristics for which the bid samples will be examined.
L1:(c)
L2:(1) Contracting officers may waive bid sample requirements when a bidder offers a product previously or currently contracted for or tested by the Government and found to comply with specification requirements conforming in every material respect with those in the current invitation for bids. (See 14.207(j)(2)).
L2:(2) Where samples required by a Federal, Military, or other formal specification are not considered necessary and a waiver of the sample requirements of the specification is, include a statement in the invitation that notwithstanding the requirements of the specification, samples are not required.
L1:(d) Bid samples furnished with a bid that are not required by the invitation generally will not be considered as qualifying the bid and will be disregarded. However, the bid sample will not be disregarded if it is clear from the bid or accompanying papers that the bidder's intention was to qualify the bid. If the qualification does not conform to the IFB, see 14.306-3(d).
L1:(e)
L2:(1) Return samples that are not destroyed in testing to bidders at their request and expense, unless otherwise specified in the invitation.
L2:(2) Request disposition instructions from bidders.
L2:(3) Samples are ordinarily returned collect to the address from which received if disposition instructions are not received within 30 days. Small items may be returned by mail, postage prepaid.
L2:(4) Transmit samples that are intended for inspection purposes in connection with deliveries to the inspecting activity concerned, with instructions to retain the sample until completion of the contract or until disposition instructions are furnished.
L2:(5) Where samples are consumed or their usefulness is impaired by tests, dispose as scrap unless the bidder requests their return.

title: 14.206 Descriptive literature
content:
14.206 Descriptive literature

L1:(a) Contracting officers must not require bidders to furnish descriptive literature unless it is needed before award to determine whether the products offered meet the specification and to establish exactly what the bidder proposes to furnish.
L1:(b) The contracting officer must document in the contract file the justification why product acceptability cannot be determined without the submission of descriptive literature, except when the contract specifications require submission.
L1:(c)
L2:(1) If the invitation will require descriptive literature, the IFB must clearly state—
L3:(i) What descriptive literature the bidders must furnish;
L3:(ii) The purpose for requiring the literature;
L3:(iii) The extent of its consideration in the evaluation of bids; and
L3:(iv) The rules that will apply if a bidder fails to furnish the literature before bid opening or if the literature provided does not comply with the requirements of the invitation.
L2:(2) If bidders must furnish descriptive literature, see 14.207(k).
L1:(d)
L2:(1) The contracting officer may waive the requirement for descriptive literature if—
L3:(i) The bidder states in the bid that the product being offered is the same as a product previously or currently being furnished to the contracting activity; and
L3:(ii) The contracting officer determines that the product offered complies with the specification requirements of the current invitation for bids. When the contracting officer waives the requirement, see 14.207(k)(2).
L2:(2) When descriptive literature is not necessary and a waiver of literature requirements of a specification has been authorized, the contracting officer must include a statement in the invitation that, despite the requirements of the specifications, descriptive literature is not required.
L2:(3) If the IFB provides for a waiver, a bidder may submit a bid on the basis of either the descriptive literature furnished with the bid or a previously furnished product. If the bid is submitted on one basis, the bidder may not have it considered on the other basis after bids are opened.
L1:(e) If descriptive literature is furnished when it is not required by the invitation for bids, follow the procedures at 14.205(d).

title: 14.207 Solicitation Provisions
content:
14.207 Solicitation Provisions

L1:(a) The provisions prescribed in this section apply to preparation and submission of bids in general. See other FAR parts for provisions and clauses related to specific acquisition requirements.
L1:(b) Insert in all invitations for bids the provisions at—
L2:(1) 52.214-3, Amendments to Invitations for Bids; and
L2:(2) 52.214-4, False Statements in Bids.
L2:(3) 52.214-5, Submission of Bids.
L2:(4) 52.214-6, Explanation to Prospective Bidders.
L2:(5) 52.214-7, Late Submissions, Modifications, and Withdrawals of Bids.
L1:(c) Insert in all invitations for bids, except those for construction, the provision at 52.214-10, Contract Award-Sealed Bidding.
L1:(d) Insert in invitations for bids to which the uniform contract format applies, the provision at 52.214-12, Preparation of Bids.
L1:(e) Insert the provision at 52.214-14, Place of Performance—Sealed Bidding, in invitations for bids except those in which the place of performance is specified by the Government.
L1:(f) Insert the provision at 52.214-15, Period for Acceptance of Bids, in invitations for bids (IFB's) that are not issued on SF 33 or SF 1447 except IFB's—
L2:(1) For construction work or
L2:(2) In which the Government specifies a minimum acceptance period.
L1:(g) Insert the provision at 52.214-16, Minimum Bid Acceptance Period, in invitations for bids, except for construction, if the contracting officer determines that a minimum acceptance period must be specified.
L1:(h) Insert the provision at 52.214-18, Preparation of Bids—Construction, in invitations for bids for construction work.
L1:(i) Insert the provision at 52.214-19, Contract Award—Sealed Bidding—Construction, in all invitations for bids for construction work.
L1:(j)
L2:(1) Insert the provision at 52.214-20, Bid Samples, in invitations for bids if bid samples are required.
L2:(2) If it appears that the conditions in 14.205(c)(1) will apply and the contracting officer anticipates granting waivers and—
L3:(i) If the nature of the required product does not necessitate limiting the grant of a waiver to a product produced at the same plant in which the product previously acquired or tested was produced, use the provision with its Alternate I; or
L3:(ii) If the nature of the required product necessitates limiting the grant of a waiver to a product produced at the same plant in which the product previously acquired or tested was produced, use the provision with its Alternate II.
L2:(3) See 14.205(c)(2) regarding waiving the requirement for all bidders.
L1:(k)
L2:(1) Insert the provision at 52.214-21, Descriptive Literature, in invitations for bids if—
L3:(i) Descriptive literature is required to evaluate the technical acceptability of an offered product and
L3:(ii) The required information will not be readily available unless it is submitted by bidders.
L2:(2) Use the basic clause with its Alternate I if the possibility exists that the contracting officer may waive the requirement for furnishing descriptive literature for a bidder offering a previously supplied product that meets specification requirements of the current IFB.
L2:(3) See 14.206(d)(2) regarding waiving the requirement for all bidders.
L1:(l) Insert the provision at 52.214-22, Evaluation of Bids for Multiple Awards, in invitations for bids if the contracting officer determines that multiple awards might be made if doing so is economically advantageous to the Government.
L1:(m) Insert the provision at 52.214-23, Late Submissions, Modifications, Revisions, and Withdrawals of Technical Proposals under Two-Step Sealed Bidding, in solicitations for technical proposals in step one of two-step sealed bidding.
L1:(n) Insert the provision at 52.214-24, Multiple Technical Proposals, in solicitations for technical proposals in step one of two-step sealed bidding if the contracting officer permits the submission of multiple technical proposals.
L1:(o) Insert the provision at 52.214-25, Step Two of Two-Step Sealed Bidding, in invitations for bids issued under step two of two-step sealed bidding.
L1:(p) Insert the provision at 52.214-34, Submission of Offers in the English Language, in solicitations that include any of the clauses prescribed in part 25. It may be included in other solicitations when the contracting officer decides that it is necessary.
L1:(q) Insert the provision at 52.214-35, Submission of Offers in U.S. Currency, in solicitations that include any of the clauses prescribed in part 25, unless the contracting officer includes the clause at 52.225-17, Evaluation of Foreign Currency Offers, as prescribed in part 25. It may be included in other solicitations when the contracting officer decides that it is necessary.

title: 14.208 Contract clauses
content:
14.208 Contract clauses

L1:(a) Insert the clause at 52.214-26, Audit and Records-Sealed Bidding, in solicitations and contracts if the contract amount is expected to exceed the threshold at part 15 for submission of certified cost or pricing data.
L1:(b)
L2:(1) Insert the clause at 52.214-27, Price Reduction for Defective Certified Cost or Pricing Data—Modifications—Sealed Bidding, in solicitations and contracts if the contract amount is expected to exceed the threshold for submission of certified cost or pricing data at part 15.
L2:(2) In exceptional cases, the head of the contracting activity may waive the requirement for inclusion of the clause in a contract with a foreign government or agency of that government. The authorizations for the waiver and the reasons for granting it must be in writing.
L1:(c) Insert the clause at 52.214-28, Subcontractor Certified Cost or Pricing Data—Modifications—Sealed Bidding, in solicitations and contracts if the contract amount is expected to exceed the threshold for submission of certified cost or pricing data at part 15; or
L2:(1) Upon request of a contractor in connection with a prime contract entered into before July 1, 2018, the contracting officer must modify the contract without requiring consideration to replace clause 52.214-28, Subcontractor Certified Cost or Pricing Data—Modifications—Sealed Bidding, with its Alternate I.
L1:(d) Insert the clause at 52.214-29, Order of Precedence—Sealed Bidding, in solicitations and contracts to which the uniform contract format applies.

title: 14.209 Soliciting bids
content:
14.209 Soliciting bids

L1:(a) See subpart 5.1 for presolicitation notices.
L1:(b) See subpart 5.2 for publicizing the IFB.
L1:(c) The contracting officer must specify in the IFB whether bids will be accepted by paper submission, or electronic transmission method, or both.
L1:(d) If the IFB has been issued and it becomes necessary to make changes in quantity, specifications, delivery schedules, opening dates, etc., or to make a correction, such changes must be accomplished by amendment of the IFB using Standard Form 30, Amendment of Solicitation/ Modification of Contract. Amendments must—
L2:(1) Be issued before the time set for bid opening;
L2:(2) If determined necessary by the contracting officer, consider the amount of time remaining until bid opening and the need for an extension to the bid opening date;
L2:(3) Be published in the GPE, if the IFB was published in the GPE, as a solicitation amendment ;
L2:(4) If applicable, be displayed in the bid room;
L2:(5) Provide all prospective bidders equal access to the amendment providing the information necessary to submit bids; and
L2:(6) Require acknowledgment of each amendment within each bidder’s bid.
L1:(e) When electronic bids are specified, the contracting officer must include in the IFB the acceptable methods and the necessary information that allows bidders to submit bids that are compatible with Government systems.
L1:(f) When a contracting office is located in the United States, any IFB sent to a prospective bidder located outside the United States must be sent by electronic data interchange or air mail if security classification permits.
L1:(g)
L2:(1) The master IFB is provided to potential sources who are requested to retain it for continued and repetitive use.
L2:(2) Subsequent individual IFB must reference the date of the current master IFB and identify any changes.
L2:(3) When using a master IFB the contracting officer must—
L3:(i) Make available copies of the master IFB on request; and
L3:(ii) Provide the cognizant contract administration activity a current copy of the master IFB.
L1:(h) Retain records of invitations for bids and records of bids as a record of each invitation a contracting office issues and each abstract or record of bids. The file for each invitation must show the—
L2:(1) Distribution that was made;
L2:(2) Date the invitation was issued; and
L2:(3) Names and addresses of prospective bidders who requested the invitation and were not included on the original IFB list must be added to the list and made a part of the record.
L1:(i) See 15.101 and 15.201 for policy on the release of acquisition information before and after the issuance of the IFB.
L1:(j) An IFB may be cancelled by the contracting officer when clearly in the public interest; e.g.,
L2:(1) Where there is no longer a requirement for the supplies or services; or
L2:(2) Where amendments to the IFB would be of such magnitude that a new IFB is desirable.
L1:(k) If an IFB is cancelled prior to the date and time specified in 14.301, the contracting officer must—
L2:(1) Identify the IFB number and short title or subject matter;
L2:(2) Briefly explain the reason for the cancellation; and
L2:(3) Where appropriate, assure prospective bidders that they will be given an opportunity to bid on any resolicitation of bids or any future requirements for the type of supplies or services involved. Cancellations must be recorded in accordance with 14.303(g).

title: 14.210 Submission of Bids
content:
14.210 Submission of Bids

L1:(a) Allow prospective bidders a reasonable time to prepare and submit bids in response to all invitations, consistent with the needs of the Government.
L1:(b) Provide at least 30 calendar days when a synopsis is required (see subpart 5.1).
L1:(c) Require bidders to submit sealed bids to be opened publicly at the time and place stated in the IFB.

title: 14.211 Two-step sealed bidding
content:
14.211 Two-step sealed bidding

L0:Two-step sealed bidding is a combination of competitive procedures designed to obtain the benefits of sealed bidding when adequate specifications are not available. An objective is to permit the development of a sufficiently descriptive and not unduly restrictive statement of the Government's requirements, including an adequate technical data package, so that subsequent acquisitions may use conventional sealed bidding methods. This two-step method is especially useful in acquisitions requiring technical proposals, particularly those for complex items.
L1:(a) Step one consists of the request for submission of technical proposals, evaluation, and (if necessary) discussion of a technical proposal. No pricing is submitted with step one. The objective is to determine the acceptability of the supplies or services offered. As used in this context, the word technical has a broad connotation and includes, among other things, the engineering approach, special manufacturing processes, and special testing techniques. It is the proper step for clarification of questions relating to technical requirements. Conformity to the technical requirements is resolved in this step, but not responsibility as defined in 9.
L1:(b) Step two involves the submission of sealed priced bids by those who submitted acceptable technical proposals in step one. Bids submitted in step two are evaluated and the awards made in accordance with subpart 14.3.

title: 14.211-1 General
content:
14.211-1 General

This two-step method is especially useful in acquisitions requiring technical proposals, particularly those for complex items.

It is the proper step for clarification of questions relating to technical requirements. Conformity to the technical requirements is resolved in this step, but not responsibility as defined in 9.
L1:(b) Step two involves the submission of sealed priced bids by those who submitted acceptable technical proposals in step one. Bids submitted in step two are evaluated and the awards made in accordance with subpart 14.3.

title: 14.211-2 Conditions for use
content:
14.211-2 Conditions for use

L1:(a) Unless other factors require the use of sealed bidding, the contracting officer may use two-step sealed bidding rather than negotiation when all of the following conditions are present:
L2:(1) Available specifications or purchase descriptions are not definite or complete or may be too restrictive without technical evaluation, and any necessary discussion, of the technical aspects of the requirement to ensure mutual understanding between each source and the Government.
L2:(2) Definite criteria exist for evaluating technical proposals.
L2:(3) More than one technically qualified source is expected to be available.
L2:(4) There is sufficient time to use the two-step method.
L2:(5) The contracting officer intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract or a fixed-price contract with economic price adjustment.
L1:(b) None of the following precludes the use of two-step sealed bidding:
L2:(1) Multi-year contracting.
L2:(2) Government property to be made available to the successful bidder.
L2:(3) A total small business set-aside (see part 19).
L2:(4) The use of a set-aside or price evaluation preference for HUBZone small business concerns (see part 19).
L2:(5) The use of a set-aside for service-disabled veteran-owned small business concerns (see part 19).
L2:(6) The use of a set-aside for economically disadvantaged women-owned small business concerns and women-owned small business concerns eligible under the Women-Owned Small Business Program (see part 19).
L2:(7) A first or subsequent production quantity is being acquired under a performance specification.

title: 14.211-3 Procedures
content:
14.211-3 Procedures

L1:(a) Step one .
L2:(1) Synopsize requests for technical proposals in accordance with Part 5. The request must include, as a minimum, the following:
L3:(i) A description of the supplies or services required.
L3:(ii) A statement of intent to use the two-step method.
L3:(iii) The requirements of the technical proposal.
L3:(iv) The evaluation criteria, to include all factors and any significant subfactors.
L3:(v) A statement that the technical proposals must not include prices or pricing information.
L3:(vi) The date, or date and hour, by which the technical proposal must be received (see 14.210).
L3:(vii) A statement that, in the second step—
L4:(A) The contracting officer will consider awards based upon bids that have acceptable technical proposals, either initially or as a result of discussions; and
L4:(B) Each technical proposal must be based on the bidder's own technical proposals.
L3:(viii) A statement that—
L4:(A) Bidders should submit technical proposals that are acceptable without additional explanation or information;
L4:(B) The Government may make a final determination regarding a technical proposal's acceptability solely on the basis as submitted; and
L4:(C) The Government may proceed with the second step without requesting further information from any bidder; however, the Government may request additional information from bidders of bids that it considers reasonably susceptible of being made acceptable and may discuss bids with their bidders.
L3:(ix) A statement that a notice of unacceptability will be forwarded to the bidder upon completion of the technical proposal evaluation and final determination of unacceptability.
L3:(x) A statement either that each bidder may only submit one technical proposal or, if authorized, multiple technical proposals. When specifications permit different technical approaches, it is generally in the Government's interest to authorize multiple technical proposals. If multiple technical proposals are authorized, see 14.207(n).
L2:(2) Include information on delivery or performance requirements that may assist bidders in determining whether or not to submit a technical proposal. Indicate that the information is not binding on the Government and that the invitation issued under step two will include actual delivery or performance requirements.
L2:(3) Upon receipt, the contracting officer must—
L3:(i) Safeguard technical proposals against disclosure to unauthorized persons;
L3:(ii) Accept and handle data marked in accordance with part 15 and 27; and
L3:(iii) Remove any reference to price or cost.
L2:(4) The contracting officer must establish a time period for evaluating technical proposals. The period may vary with the complexity and number of technical proposals involved. However, the evaluation should be completed quickly.
L2:(5)
L3:(i) Base evaluations on the criteria in the request for proposals but not consideration of responsibility as defined in part 9. Categorize technical proposals as—
L4:(A) Acceptable;
L4:(B) Reasonably susceptible of being made acceptable; or
L4:(C) Unacceptable.
L3:(ii) Categorize any proposal that modifies, or fails to conform to the essential requirements or specifications of, the request for technical proposals as unacceptable.
L2:(6)
L3:(i) The contracting officer may proceed directly with step two if there are sufficient acceptable proposals to ensure adequate price competition under step two, and if further time, effort and delay to make additional technical proposals acceptable and thereby increase competition would not be in Government's interest. If this is not the case, the contracting officer must request bidders whose technical proposals may be made acceptable to submit additional clarifying or supplementing information. The contracting officer must identify the nature of the deficiencies in the technical proposal or the nature of the additional information required. The contracting officer may also arrange discussions for this purpose. Do not discuss a technical proposal with any bidder other than the submitter.
L3:(ii) When requesting additional information, the contracting officer must establish an appropriate time for bidders to conclude discussions, if any, submit all additional information, and incorporate such additional information as part of their technical proposals. The contracting officer may extend the due date for such submissions at their discretion. If the additional information is incorporated into a technical proposal within the established time, and the contracting officer determines that the technical proposal is acceptable, the contracting officer will update its category to acceptable.
L2:(7) When a technical proposal is found unacceptable (either initially or after clarification), the contracting officer must promptly notify the bidder of the basis of the determination and that a revision of the technical proposal will not be considered. Upon written request, the contracting officer must debrief unsuccessful bidders (see part 15).
L2:(8) Late technical proposals are governed by part 15.
L2:(9) If it is necessary to discontinue two-step sealed bidding, the contracting officer must include a statement of the facts and circumstances in the contract file. The contracting officer must notify each bidder in writing. When step one results in no acceptable technical proposals or only one acceptable technical proposal, the acquisition may be continued by negotiation.
L1:(b) Step two.
L2:(1) Follow sealed bidding procedures except that invitations for bids in step two must—
L3:(i) Be issued only to those bidders that submitted acceptable technical proposals in step one;
L3:(ii) Include the provision prescribed in 14.207(o);
L3:(iii) Clearly state that the bidder must comply with the specifications and the bidder's technical proposal; and
L3:(iv) Not be synopsized through the Governmentwide point of entry (GPE) as an acquisition opportunity nor publicly posted.
L2:(2) List the names of firms that submitted acceptable proposals in step one through the GPE for the benefit of prospective subcontractors (see 5.201).

title: Subpart 14.3 Evaluation and award
content:
Subpart 14.3 Evaluation and award

L1:(a) Bidders are responsible for submitting bids, and any modifications or withdrawals not later than the exact time set for opening of bids. If no time is specified in the IFB, the time for receipt is 4:30 p.m., local time, for the designated Government office on the date that bids are due.
L1:(b) Bids may be modified or withdrawn by any method authorized by the IFB.
L1:(c) The receiving official receiving a paper bid submission, modification or withdrawal must—
L2:(1) Write on the envelope—
L3:(i) The date and time of receipt and by whom; and
L3:(ii) The invitation for bid number; and
L2:(2) Sign the envelope.
L2:(3) Not disclose bid information before the time set for bid opening. See part 3 for requirements for protecting information including access to and disclosure thereof.
L1:(d) A bidder or its authorized representative may withdraw a paper bid submission in person if, before the exact time set for opening of bids, the identity of the persons requesting withdrawal is established and that person signs a receipt for the bid.
L1:(e) A bidder may withdraw an electronically submitted bid if notice is received in the office designated in the IFB not later than the exact time set for opening of bids. Upon withdrawal of an electronically transmitted bid, the data received must not be viewed and, to the maximum extent practical, must be purged from primary and backup data storage systems.
L1:(f)
L2:(1) Any bid, modification, or withdrawal of a bid received at the Government office designated in the IFB after the exact time specified for receipt of bids is “late” and will not be considered unless—
L3:(i) It is received before award is made; and
L3:(ii) The contracting officer determines that accepting the late bid would not unduly delay the acquisition; and—
L4:(A) If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the IFB, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of bids; or
L4:(B) There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of bids and was under the Government's control prior to the time set for receipt of bids.
L2:(2) The contracting officer will consider and may accept, a late modification of an otherwise successful bid, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, at any time it is received.
L1:(g) Acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes the time/date stamp of that installation on the bid wrapper, other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.
L1:(h) If an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that bids cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of bids by the exact time specified in the IFB, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the bid opening date, the time specified for receipt of bids will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the IFB on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.
L1:(i) The contracting officer must promptly notify any bidder if its bid, modification, or withdrawal was received late, and must inform the bidder whether its bid will be considered, unless contract award is imminent, and the notices prescribed in 14.309 would suffice.
L1:(j) Late bids and modifications that are not considered must be held unopened, unless opened for identification, until after award and then retained with other unsuccessful bids. However, any bid bond or guarantee must be returned.
L1:(k) If available, the following must be included in the contract files for each late bid, modification, or withdrawal:
L2:(1) The date and hour of receipt.
L2:(2) A statement, with supporting rationale, regarding whether the bid was considered for award.
L2:(3) The envelope, wrapper, or other evidence of the date of receipt.
