L0:PGI 204.76—SUPPLIER PERFORMANCE RISK SYSTEM
L0:PGI 204.7603 Procedures.
L0:The Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) provides item risk, price risk, and
L0:supplier risk assessment on end products and price risk and supplier risk assessment
L0:on services. SPRS provides item and price risk for end products using the material
L0:identifiers listed in paragraphs (a)(1)(i) through (v). SPRS also provides a supplier risk
L0:score for the contractor that provided the product or services. The contracting officer
L0:may consider item risk, price risk, and supplier risk assessments to determine the
L0:performance risk of the offeror or product and to assess the risk of ongoing contractor
L0:performance.
L1:(a) Item risk.
L1:(1) SPRS provides the contracting officer warnings and mitigation strategies for
L0:end products identified by military departments or defense agencies as high risk (due to
L0:diminishing manufacturing sources and material shortages, history of counterfeiting,
L0:etc.). End products are identified by one or more of the following material identifiers:
L1:(i) National Stock Number (NSN).
L1:(ii) Internet Blog Serial Number (IBSN).
L1:(iii) Universal Product Code (UPC).
L1:(iv) Global Standards 1 (GS1).
L1:(v) Manufacturer Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) and part
L0:number.
L1:(2) Presolicitation. For items identified as high risk in SPRS or by the requiring
L0:activity in purchase requests, the contracting officer must mitigate this risk by including
L0:a clause that addresses first article approval or certificate of conformance in the
L0:solicitation or by applying other risk mitigation strategies.
L1:(b) Price risk. SPRS provides the contracting officer warning of possible over- or
L0:under-payment risks based on historical purchase data.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 4
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 204
L1:(c) Supplier risk. SPRS provides the contracting officer a score for the assessment
L0:of the contractor’s performance. The supplier risk score includes data associated with
L0:the contractor’s quality and delivery data.
L1:(d) Evaluation of quotations or offers for supplies. During the evaluation of the
L0:offers received for supplies or services that contain supplies, the contracting officer
L0:must consider the risk assessments available in SPRS.
L1:(e) Award and documentation.
L1:(1) In determining a price fair and reasonable, the contracting officer must
L0:review the price risk data provided in SPRS and follow the procedures at
L0:FAR 12.203 or 15.4 to make an award decision. In the event that price risk has been
L0:identified, the contracting officer must perform further price analysis.
L1:(2) In assessing offeror performance capabilities, the contracting officer must
L0:review the supplier risk data provided in SPRS and tailor the contract oversight for risk.
L0:Mitigate supplier risk by—
L1:(i) Including clauses to strengthen oversight (e.g., a clause that addresses
L0:first article testing or certificate of conformance); and
L1:(ii) Removing discretionary clauses to recognize successful performance
L0:(e.g., a clause that addresses first article testing).
L1:(3) The contracting officer must document the contract file on any action taken
L0:as a result of information obtained from SPRS.

title: 204.309-70 Handling of contract files

title: 204.705-70 Specific retention periods

title: 204.7200 Scope of subpart

L0:204.7200 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart provides policy and guidance related to antiterrorism awareness
L0:training for contractor personnel who require routine physical access to a Federally-
L0:controlled facility or military installation.

title: 204.7201 Definition
content:
L0:204.7201 Definition.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Military installation” means a base, camp, post, station, yard, center, or other
L0:activity under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of a military department or, in the
L0:case of an activity in a foreign country, under the operational control of the
L0:Secretary of a military department or the Secretary of Defense (see 10 U.S.C.
L0:2801(c)(4)).

title: 204.7202 Policy
content:
L0:204.7202 Policy.
L0:It is DoD policy that—
L1:(a) Contractor personnel who, as a condition of contract performance, require
L0:routine physical access to a Federally-controlled facility or military installation are
L0:required to complete Level I antiterrorism awareness training within 30 days of
L0:requiring access and annually thereafter; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 4
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 204
L1:(b) In accordance with Department of Defense Instruction O-2000.16, Volume 1,
L0:DoD Antiterrorism (AT) Program Implementation: DoD AT Standards, Level I
L0:antiterrorism awareness training may be completed—
L1:(1) Through a DoD-sponsored and certified computer or web-based distance
L0:learning instruction for Level I antiterrorism awareness; or
L1:(2) Under the instruction of a qualified Level I antiterrorism awareness
L0:instructor.

title: 204.7400 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:204.7400 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart prescribes policies and procedures for the release and safeguarding of
L0:information to litigation support contractors. It implements the requirements at 10
L0:U.S.C. 129d.
subpart: SUBPART 204.74 — DISCLOSURE OF INFORMATION TO LITIGATION

title: 204.7401 Definitions
content:
L0:204.7401 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Computer software” means computer programs, source code, source code
L0:listings, object code listings, design details, algorithms, processes, flow charts,
L0:formulae, and related material that would enable the software to be reproduced,
L0:recreated, or recompiled. Computer software does not include computer data bases
L0:or computer software documentation.
L0:“Litigation information” means any information, including sensitive information,
L0:that is furnished to the contractor by or on behalf of the Government, or that is
L0:generated or obtained by the contractor in the performance of litigation support
L0:under a contract. The term does not include information that is lawfully, publicly
L0:available without restriction, including information contained in a publicly
L0:available solicitation.
L0:“Litigation support” means administrative, technical, or professional services
L0:provided in support of the Government during or in anticipation of litigation.
L0:“Litigation support contractor” means a contractor (including its experts,
L0:technical consultants, subcontractors, and suppliers) providing litigation support
L0:under a contract that contains the clause at 252.204-7014, Limitations on the Use
L0:or Disclosure of Information by Litigation Support Contractors.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 4
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 204
L0:“Sensitive information” means controlled unclassified information of a
L0:commercial, financial, proprietary, or privileged nature. The term includes
L0:technical data and computer software, but does not include information that is
L0:lawfully, publicly available without restriction.
L0:“Technical data” means recorded information, regardless of the form or method
L0:of the recording, of a scientific or technical nature (including computer software
L0:documentation). The term does not include computer software or data incidental to
L0:contract administration, such as financial and/or management information.
subpart: SUBPART 204.74 — DISCLOSURE OF INFORMATION TO LITIGATION

title: 204.7402 Policy
content:
L0:204.7402 Policy.
L1:(a) Any release or disclosure of litigation information that includes sensitive
L0:information to a litigation support contractor, and the litigation support contractor's
L0:use and handling of such information, must comply with the requirements of 10
L0:U.S.C. 129d.
L1:(b) To the maximum extent practicable, DoD will provide notice to an offeror or
L0:contractor submitting, delivering, or otherwise providing information to DoD in
L0:connection with an offer or performance of a contract that such information may be
L0:released or disclosed to litigation support contractors.
L1:(c) Information that is publicly available without restriction, including publicly
L0:available solicitations for litigation support services, will not be protected from
L0:disclosure as litigation information.
L1:(d) When sharing sensitive information with a litigation support contractor,
L0:contracting officers must ensure that all other applicable requirements for handling
L0:and safeguarding the relevant types of sensitive information are included in the
L0:contract (e.g., FAR part 40 and subpart 24.1; DFARS part 240 and subpart 224.1).

title: 204.7600 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:204.7600 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart provides policies and procedures for use of the Supplier Performance
L0:Risk System (SPRS) risk assessments in the evaluation of a quotation or offer.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 4
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 204

title: 204.7601 Definitions
content:
L0:204.7601 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Item risk” means the probability that a product, based on intended use, will
L0:introduce performance risk resulting in safety issues, mission degradation, or
L0:monetary loss.
L0:“Price risk” means the measure of whether a proposed price for a product or
L0:service is consistent with historical prices paid for that item or service.
L0:“Supplier risk” means the probability that an award may subject the
L0:procurement to the risk of unsuccessful performance or to supply chain risk.

title: 204.7602 Applicability
content:
L0:204.7602 Applicability.
L0:Use of SPRS risk assessments is required for the evaluation of quotations or offers
L0:in response to solicitations for supplies and services, including solicitations using
L0:FAR part 12 procedures for the acquisition of commercial products and commercial
L0:services, excluding solicitations for the procurement of supplies or services
L0:exempted by the Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 5000.79, Defense-wide
L0:Sharing and Use of Supplier and Product Performance Information. SPRS retrieves
L0:item, price, quality, delivery, and contractor information from contracts in
L0:Government reporting systems in order to develop risk assessments of contractors.
L0:SPRS is available at https://piee.eb.mil/, and the SPRS user's guides are available
L0:at https://www.sprs.csd.disa.mil/reference.htm.

title: 204.7603 Procedures
content:
L0:204.7603 Procedures.
L0:The contracting officer must consider price risk and supplier risk, if available in
L0:SPRS, as a part of the award decision. For procurement of an end product
L0:identified by a material identifier that is available as described at PGI 204.7603,
L0:the contracting officer must also consider assessments of item risk, if available, as a
L0:part of the award decision. Offerors or quoters without a risk assessment in SPRS
L0:must not be considered favorably or unfavorably. Contracting officers must use
L0:their discretion in considering the information available in SPRS on item risk, price
L0:risk, and supplier risk as follows:
L1:(a) Item risk.
L1:(1) Consider item risk to determine whether the procurement of products
L0:represents a high performance risk to the Government. If an item has a high risk
L0:rating, then the SPRS item risk report will display the reason(s) an item is
L0:identified as high risk.
L1:(2) Before issuing a solicitation for the procurement of an end product
L0:identified by a material identifier that is available as described at PGI 204.7603,
L0:the contracting officer must ensure a SPRS item risk search has been performed
L0:and must consider any item risk warnings provided. When evaluating quotations or
L0:offers for an end product identified by a material identifier, a SPRS item risk search
L0:is required for any end product that did not have an item risk search performed
L0:prior to solicitation. If there are item risk warnings, the contracting officer must
L0:consider strategies to mitigate risk, such as the following:
L1:(i) Consulting with the program office.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 4
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 204
L1:(ii) Including mitigating requirements in the statement of work, as
L0:provided by the requiring activity.
L1:(iii) Including FAR and DFARS clauses identified in the SPRS
L0:application, as appropriate.
L1:(b) Price risk.
L1:(1) When procuring a service or an end product identified by a material
L0:identifier that is available as described at PGI 204.7603, the contracting officer
L0:must consider price risk assessment in determining if a proposed price is consistent
L0:with historical prices paid for an item or otherwise creates a risk to the
L0:Government. Contracting officers must not rely solely on the price risk assessment
L0:when determining prices to be fair and reasonable.
L1:(2) The contracting officer must consider strategies to mitigate price risk,
L0:such as the following:
L1:(i) Not awarding to offerors or quoters with high risk price ratings unless
L0:there is a way to justify the price through additional price or cost analysis.
L1:(ii) Utilizing appropriate price negotiation techniques and procedures.
L1:(iii) Using price reasonableness or price realism techniques at FAR

title: 13.203 or 15.4. See also 215.403-3 when making award decisions
content:
L0:13.203 or 15.4. See also 215.403-3 when making award decisions.
L1:(c) Supplier risk. The contracting officer must consider supplier risk, to assess
L0:the risk of unsuccessful performance and supply chain risk, in award decisions.
L0:Supplier risk assessments in SPRS include quality, delivery, and other contractor
L0:performance information.

title: 204.770 U.S.-International Atomic Energy Agency Additional Protocol
content: L0:204.770 U.S.-International Atomic Energy Agency Additional Protocol.
citation: R-DFARS 204.770 — U.S.-International Atomic Energy Agency Additional Protocol

title: 204.770-1 General
content:
L0:204.770-1 General.
L0:Under the U.S.-International Atomic Energy Agency Additional Protocol (U.S.-
L0:IAEA AP), the United States is required to declare a wide range of public and
L0:private nuclear-related activities to the IAEA and potentially provide access to
L0:IAEA inspectors for verification purposes.

title: 204.770-2 National security exclusion
content:
L0:204.770-2 National security exclusion.
L1:(a) The U.S.-IAEA AP permits the United States unilaterally to declare
L0:exclusions from inspection requirements for activities, or locations or information
L0:associated with such activities, with direct national security significance.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 4
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 204
L1:(b) In order to ensure that all relevant activities are reviewed for direct national
L0:security significance, both current and former activities, and associated locations or
L0:information, are to be considered for applicability for a national security exclusion.
L1:(c) If a DoD program manager receives notification from a contractor that the
L0:contractor is required to report any of its activities in accordance with the U.S.-
L0:IAEA AP, the program manager will—
L1:(1) Conduct a security assessment to determine if, and by what means,
L0:access may be granted to the IAEA; or
L1:(2) Provide written justification to the component or agency treaty office for
L0:application of the national security exclusion at that location to exclude access by
L0:the IAEA, in accordance with DoD Instruction 2060.03, Application of the National
L0:Security Exclusion to the Agreements Between the United States of America and
L0:the International Atomic Energy Agency for the Application of Safeguards in the
L0:United States of America.

L1:(a) Any fissionable materials (e.g., uranium, plutonium, neptunium, thorium,
L0:americium);
L1:(b) Other radiological source materials; or
L1:(c) Technologies directly related to nuclear power production, including nuclear
L0:or radiological waste materials.

L0:Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Information by Litigation Support
L0:Contractors (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Computer software means computer programs, source code, source code listings,
L0:object code listings, design details, algorithms, processes, flow charts, formulae, and
L0:related material that would enable the software to be reproduced, recreated, or
L0:recompiled. Computer software does not include computer data bases or computer
L0:software documentation.
L0:Litigation information means any information, including sensitive information,
L0:that is furnished to the contractor by or on behalf of the Government, or that is
L0:generated or obtained by the contractor in the performance of litigation support
L0:under a contract. The term does not include information that is lawfully, publicly
L0:available without restriction, including information contained in a publicly
L0:available solicitation.
L0:Litigation support means administrative, technical, or professional services
L0:provided in support of the Government during or in anticipation of litigation.
L0:Litigation support contractor means a contractor (including its experts, technical
L0:consultants, subcontractors, and suppliers) providing litigation support under a
L0:contract that contains this clause.
L0:Sensitive information means controlled unclassified information of a commercial,
L0:financial, proprietary, or privileged nature. The term includes technical data and
L0:computer software, but does not include information that is lawfully, publicly
L0:available without restriction.
L0:Technical data means recorded information, regardless of the form or method of
L0:the recording, of a scientific or technical nature (including computer software
L0:documentation). The term does not include computer software or data incidental to
L0:contract administration, such as financial and/or management information.
L1:(b) Limitations on use or disclosure of litigation information. Notwithstanding
L0:any other provision of this contract, the Contractor shall—

L0:litigation support under this contract;
L1:(2) Not disclose litigation information to any entity outside the Contractor's
L0:organization unless, prior to such disclosure the Contracting Officer has provided
L0:written consent to such disclosure;
L1:(3) Take all precautions necessary to prevent unauthorized disclosure of
L0:litigation information;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 4
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 204
L1:(4) Not use litigation information to compete against a third party for

L0:contract that contains the clause at 252.204-7014, Limitations on the Use or
L0:Disclosure of Information by Litigation Support Contractors.
L0:Sensitive information means controlled unclassified information of a commercial,
L0:financial, proprietary, or privileged nature. The term includes technical data and
L0:computer software, but does not include information that is lawfully, publicly
L0:available without restriction.
L0:Technical data means recorded information, regardless of the form or method of
L0:the recording, of a scientific or technical nature (including computer software
L0:documentation). The term does not include computer software or data incidental to
L0:contract administration, such as financial and/or management information.
L1:(b) Notice of authorized disclosures Notwithstanding any other provision of this
L0:solicitation or contract, the Government may disclose to a litigation support
L0:contractor, for the sole purpose of litigation support activities, any information,
L0:including sensitive information, received—
L1:(1) Within or in connection with a quotation or offer; or
L1:(2) In the performance of or in connection with a contract.
L1:(c) Subcontracts. Include the substance of this clause, including this paragraph
L1:(c), in all subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial products or
L0:commercial services.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.204-7022 Expediting Contract Closeout
content:
L0:252.204-7022 Expediting Contract Closeout.
L0:As prescribed in 204.308-70, insert the following clause:
L0:Expediting Contract Closeout
L1:(a) At the conclusion of all applicable closeout requirements of Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation 4.308, the Government and Contractor shall mutually agree
L0:on the residual dollar amount remaining on the contract. Both the Government and
L0:Contractor agree to waive payment of any residual dollar amount of $1,000 or less
L0:to which either party may be entitled at the time of contract closeout.
L1:(b) A residual dollar amount includes all money owed to either party at the end
L0:of the contract and as a result of the contract, excluding amounts connected in any
L0:way with taxation or a violation of law or regulation.
L1:(c) For purposes of determining residual dollar amounts, offsets (e.g., across
L0:multiple contracts or orders) may be considered only to the extent permitted by law.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.204-7023 Reporting Requirements for Contracted Services
content:
L0:252.204-7023 Reporting Requirements for Contracted Services.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 204.208-71(a)(1) and (2), insert the following clause:
L0:Reporting Requirements for Contracted Services—Basic (Jul 2021)
L1:(a) Definition. As used in this clause—
L0:First-tier subcontract means a subcontract awarded directly by the contractor for
L0:the purpose of acquiring services for performance of a prime contract. It does not
L0:include the contractor's supplier agreements with vendors, such as long-term
L0:arrangements for materials or supplies or services that benefit multiple contracts
L0:and/or the costs of which are normally applied to a contractor's general and
L0:administrative expenses or indirect costs.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall report annually, by October 31, at
L0:https://www.sam.gov, on the services performed under this contract or order,
L0:including any first-tier subcontracts, during the preceding Government fiscal year
L0:(October 1-September 30).
L1:(c) The Contractor shall report the following information for the contract or
L0:order:
L1:(1) The total dollar amount invoiced for services performed during the
L0:preceding Government fiscal year under the contract or order.
L1:(2) The number of Contractor direct labor hours, to include first-tier
L0:subcontractor direct labor hours, as applicable, expended on the services performed
L0:under the contract or order during the previous Government fiscal year.
L1:(d) The Government will review the Contractor's reported information for
L0:reasonableness and consistency with available contract information. In the event
L0:the Government believes that revisions to the Contractor's reported information are
L0:warranted, the Government will notify the Contractor. Upon notification, the
L0:Contractor shall revise the reported information or provide the Government with a
L0:supporting rationale for the information.
L0:(End of clause)

L0:As prescribed in 204.208-71(a)(3), use the following clause, which substitutes

L0:and “order” in lieu of “contract or order” in paragraphs (c) and (c)(1) and (2), and

L0:orders under the contract or agreement require service contract reporting.

L1:(a) Definition. As used in this clause—

title: 252.204-7024 Notice on the Use of the Supplier Performance Risk System
content:
L0:252.204-7024 Notice on the Use of the Supplier Performance Risk System.
L0:As prescribed in 204.7604, insert the following provision:
L0:Notice on the Use of the Supplier Performance Risk System
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this provision—
L0:Item risk means the probability that a product, based on intended use, will
L0:introduce performance risk resulting in safety issues, mission degradation, or
L0:monetary loss.
L0:Price risk means a measure of whether a proposed price for a product or service
L0:is consistent with historical prices paid for that item or service.
L0:Supplier risk means the probability that an award may subject the procurement
L0:to the risk of unsuccessful performance or to supply chain risk (see Defense Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation Supplement 240).
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 4
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 204
L1:(b) The Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS), available at
L0:https://piee.eb.mil/, will be used in the evaluation of the Quoter or Offeror's
L0:performance. SPRS retrieves item, price, quality, delivery, and contractor
L0:information on contracts from Government reporting systems in order to develop
L0:risk assessments.
L1:(c) The Contracting Officer will consider SPRS risk assessments during the
L0:evaluation of quotations or offers received in response to this solicitation as follows:
L1:(1) Item risk will be considered to determine whether the procurement
L0:represents a high performance risk to the Government.
L1:(2) Price risk will be considered in determining if a proposed price is
L0:consistent with historical prices paid for a product or a service or otherwise creates
L0:a risk to the Government.
L1:(3) Supplier risk, including but not limited to quality and delivery, will be
L0:considered to assess the risk of unsuccessful performance and supply chain risk.
L1:(d) SPRS risk assessments are generated daily. Quoters or Offerors are able to
L0:access their risk assessments by following the access instructions in the SPRS
L0:user's guide available at https://www.sprs.csd.disa.mil/reference.htm. Quoters and
L0:Offerors are granted access to SPRS for their own risk assessment classifications
L0:only. SPRS reporting procedures and risk assessment methodology are detailed in
L0:the SPRS user's guide. The method to challenge a rating generated by SPRS is also
L0:provided in the user's guide. SPRS evaluation criteria are available at
L0:https://www.sprs.csd.disa.mil/pdf/SPRS_DataEvaluationCriteria.pdf.
L1:(e) The Contracting Officer may consider any other available and relevant
L0:information when evaluating a quotation or an offer.
L0:(End of provision)

L1:(5) Inventory if applicable
L1:(C) Use manufacturer part numbers or similar identifiers when

L1:(i) Service line items:
L1:(A) Contracting officers must match the quantities with the frequency
L0:with which performance will be reviewed, and on fixed-price line items, payment made.
L0:If the quantity used is 1, then the contract only allows for 1 payment, 1 time, for that 1

L2:(a)(1) Line items. Line items must consist of four numeric digits from 0001 to 9999.
L1:(2) Subline items.
L1:(i) Subline items must consist of a “line item base” (four numeric digits derived
L0:from the separately identifiable or informational line item associated with one or more
L0:subline items) concatenated with an “extension” of either two numeric or two alpha
L0:characters, depending on the type of subline item.
L1:(ii) Types of subline items.
L1:(A) Deliverable subline items. The line item extension for deliverable
L0:subline items must only consist of two alpha characters from AA through ZZ. Use alpha
L0:characters for deliverable subline items, running AA through ZZ. For example, where line
L0:item 0005 is associated with three deliverable subline items, line item base 0005 would be
L0:concatenated with extensions AA, AB, and AC to form deliverable subline items 0005AA,
L0:0005AB, and 0005AC.
L1:(B) Informational subline items. The line item extension for informational
L0:subline items must only consist of two numeric characters from 01 through 99. For example,
L0:where line item 0001 has two informational subline items, line item base 0001 would be
L0:concatenated with extensions 01 and 02 to form info subline items 000101 and 000102.
L1:(3) Exhibit line items. Exhibit line items must be associated with informational line
L0:items or subline items using an exhibit identifier. Exhibit line items must consist of the exhibit
L0:identifier concatenated with a serial extension. For example, where informational line item
L0:0004 is associated with Exhibit C, associated ELINs would be C001, C002, C003, etc.
L0:Where exhibit Identifiers consist of two alpha characters, excluding I and O, the serial
L0:number following the exhibit identifier in an exhibit line item number would be two digits. For
L0:example, given Exhibit GG, exhibit line items could include GG01, GG02, GG03, GG04, etc.
L0:Serial numbers need not be consecutive, but they must be unique.

L2:(a)(1) Line item numbering. Do not use the letters I or O.
L1:(2) Do not use lowercase alpha characters
L1:(3) Do not use special characters (e.g. $, &) or spaces
L1:(4) Do not re-purpose a number that has been deleted, terminated, canceled, or
L0:otherwise removed from the contract.
L1:(5) Numbers must be sequential but do not need to be consecutive.
L1:(b) Subline item numbering. Number subline items by adding either two numeric
L0:characters or two alpha characters to the basic line item number.
L1:(1) Information subline item numbers. Use numeric characters only for
L0:information subline items, running 01 through 99. Do not use spaces or special
L0:characters to separate the subline item number from the line item number that is its
L0:root. For example, if the line item number is 0001, the first three subline items would be
L0:000101, 000102, and 000103. Do not use a designation more than once within a line
L0:item.
L1:(2) Separately identified subline items. Use alpha characters only for separately
L0:identified subline items, running AA through ZZ. Do not use spaces or special
L0:characters to separate the subline item number from the line item number that is its
L0:root. For example, if the line item number is 0001, the first three subline items would be
L0:0001AA, 0001AB, and 0001AC.
L1:(i) Do not use the letters I or O as alpha characters.
L1:(ii) Use all 24 available alpha characters in the second position before
L0:selecting a different alpha character for the first position. For example, AA, AB, AC,
L0:through AZ before beginning BA, BB, and BC.
L1:(c) Within a given line item, the subline item numbers must be sequential but need
L0:not be consecutive.

L0:PGI 204.203 System for Award Management.
L0:PGI 204.203-270 Procedures.
L1:(a) Assist offerors in obtaining the required Commercial and Government Entity
L1:(CAGE) codes. Note that if an offeror’s facility requires security clearance in
L0:accordance with a potential contract, the offeror is required to have a CAGE code
L0:assigned to that facility. If the facility is a location other than the offeror’s office
L0:submitting the proposal, that facility is not required to be separately registered in the
L0:System for Award Management (SAM) in order to have a CAGE code assigned.
L0:Offerors may be directed to the DLA CAGE Branch (see PGI 204.203-271 for contact
L0:information);
L1:(b) Do not deny a potential offeror a solicitation package because the offeror does
L0:not have a CAGE code, unique entity identifier, or TIN;
L1:(c) Do not require a contractor to register sections or locations of their organization
L0:in SAM for reasons not already required by clauses present in their contracts in order to
L0:obtain a CAGE code; and
L1:(d) Do not require a contractor to obtain new CAGE codes or change CAGE code
L0:records assigned to their locations solely for Government administration purposes (such
L0:as a result of a Government reorganization, change in Government contracting officer or
L0:office) or for distinction in Government systems beyond physical address and Electronic
L0:Funds Transfer (EFT) data.
L0:PGI 204.203-271 Maintenance of the CAGE file.
L0:The following information and procedures are provided to assist contracting officers.
L1:(a) Assignment of CAGE codes for entities located in the United States or its
L0:outlying areas.
L1:(1) CAGE codes are assigned per legal entity at individual physical addresses
L0:(i.e., the same entity at the same physical address will not be assigned two or more
L0:CAGE codes). The only exception to this rule is when an entity has a registration in the
L0:SAM with multiple EFT addresses identified by multiple EFT indicators. In this case,
L0:each EFT indicator record is assigned a separate CAGE code to assist in correct
L0:processing of payments.
L1:(2) CAGE codes are not assigned to mailing addresses; a physical address
L0:must be provided. Neither U.S. Post Office boxes nor addresses that can be identified
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 4
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 204
L0:as belonging to commercial mail and/or shipping provider locations will be accepted as
L0:physical addresses.
L1:(3) CAGE codes are not assigned to entities where the provided physical
L0:address is identified as a short-term virtual location, such as mobile offices, commercial
L0:packaging/mailing facilities (e.g., UPS stores, FedEx stores), mailbox rentals and
L0:certain business incubator locations if the majority of the operations are not performed
L0:from that incubator location. A sole proprietor, partnership, corporate entity, or other
L0:business organization must have a principal place of business, even if it is a home
L0:office, from where the business operates and record books are maintained. In that
L0:case, a home address of an officer of the company or board member would be required.
L1:(4) Individuals who register in SAM as sole proprietors are assigned CAGE
L0:codes. However, there may not be multiple CAGE codes assigned to the same location
L0:even if the entity names are differentiated by establishing a Limited Liability Corporation
L1:(LLC) (e.g., “John Smith” and “John Smith, LLC”). Additionally, the standard for the
L0:legal business name for sole proprietors, driven by Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
L0:standards, is the use of the individual’s personal name. Any additional name used for
L0:the sole proprietorship should be identified as a doing business as (DBA) name (e.g.,
L0:“John Smith” is the legal business name, “Smith Construction” is the DBA).
L1:(5) Authorized agents or brokers may be assigned CAGE codes for
L0:identification and processing purposes. A single CAGE code will be assigned to the
L0:agent or broker entity in addition to any codes assigned to the entities represented by
L0:the agent or broker (i.e., only one code will be assigned to a specific agent or broker
L0:entity regardless of the number of firms represented by that agent or broker). Codes
L0:will not be assigned to an agent or broker in care of the entity being represented or in
L0:any way infer that the agent or broker is a separate establishment bearing the name of
L0:the entity represented by the agent or broker.
L1:(6) There are some cases where both the owner of real property and a separate
L0:legal entity located at the same address as the real property each are required to have
L0:CAGE codes assigned. Examples are an office building owner and a tenant in the
L0:office building, or a landowner and a company using all or a portion of the land to farm.
L0:Additional cases exist where two separate entities may lease office space in the same
L0:building and both require CAGE codes. In both situations, the most specific physical
L0:address will be requested (i.e., specific additions of suites, floors, or room numbers) to
L0:distinguish between the two entities. If no more specific physical address is able to be
L0:identified, then documentation such as that listed in PGI 204.203-271(c)(3)(i)(A) will be

L1:(ii) If the entity indicates it does hold active Federal Government contracts,

L1:(A) If the entity indicates that the change in legal business name is not

title: 206.103-5 Authorized or required by statute
content:
L0:206.103-5 Authorized or required by statute.
L1:(c) Application. Agencies may use this authority to—
L1:(i) Acquire supplies and services from military exchange stores outside the
L0:United States for use by the armed forces outside the United States in accordance with
L0:10 U.S.C. 2424(a) and subject to the limitations of 10 U.S.C. 2424(b). The limitations of
L0:10 U.S.C. 2424(b)(1) and (2) do not apply to the purchase of soft drinks that are
L0:manufactured in the United States. For the purposes of 10 U.S.C. 2424, soft drinks
L0:manufactured in the United States are brand name carbonated sodas, manufactured in
L0:the United States, as evidenced by product markings.
L1:(ii) Acquire police, fire protection, airfield operation, or other community
L0:services from local governments at military installations to be closed under the
L0:circumstances in 237.7401 (section 2907 of Fiscal Year 1994 Defense Authorization Act
L0:(Pub. L. 103-160)).
L1:(iii) Acquire products and services under the Pilot Program to Incentivize
L0:Contracting with Employee-Owned Businesses (see subpart 270.1).
L1:(d) Limitations.
L1:(i) 10 U.S.C. 4141 precludes use of this exception for awards to colleges or
L0:universities for the performance of research and development, or for the construction of
L0:any research or other facility, unless—
L1:(A) The statute authorizing or requiring award specifically—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 6
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 206
L1:(1) States that the statute modifies or supersedes the provisions of 10
L1:(2) Identifies the particular college or university involved; and
L1:(3) States that award is being made in contravention of 10 U.S.C.
L0:U.S.C. 4141;
L0:4141(a); and
L1:(B) The Secretary of Defense provides Congress written notice of intent to
L0:award. The contract cannot be awarded until 180 days have elapsed since the date
L0:Congress received the notice of intent to award. Contracting activities must submit a

L0:Director, Defense Pricing, Contracting, and Acquisition Policy, Office of the Under

title: 207.103-70 Agency-head responsibilities
content:
L0:207.103-70 Agency-head responsibilities.
L1:(a) Prepare written acquisition plans for—
L1:(1) Acquisitions for development, as defined in FAR 35.001, when the total price
L0:of all contracts for the acquisition program is estimated at $10 million or more;
L1:(2) Acquisitions for production or services when the total price of all contracts
L0:for the acquisition program is estimated at $50 million or more for all fiscal years or $25
L0:million or more for any fiscal year; and
L1:(3) Any other acquisition considered appropriate by the department or agency.
L1:(b) Written plans are not required for final buy out or one-time buy acquisitions.
L0:The terms "final buy out" and "one-time buy" refer to a single contract that covers all
L0:known present and future requirements. This exception does not apply to a multiyear
L0:contract or a contract with options or phases.
L1:(c) Prepare written acquisition plans for acquisition programs meeting the
L0:thresholds of paragraphs (a) of this section on a program basis. Other acquisition plans
L0:may be written on either a program or an individual contract basis.
L1:(d) For procurement of conventional ammunition, as defined in DoDD 5160.65,
L0:Single Manager for Conventional Ammunition (SMCA), the SMCA will review the
L0:acquisition plan to determine if it is consistent with retaining national technology and
L0:industrial base capabilities in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(3) and section 806 of
L0:Public Law 105-261. The department or agency—
L1:(1) Must submit the acquisition plan to the address in PGI 207.103-70(d); and
L1:(2) Must not proceed with the procurement until the SMCA provides written
L0:concurrence with the acquisition plan. In the case of a non-concurrence, the SMCA will
L0:resolve issues with the Army Office of the Executive Director for Conventional
L0:Ammunition.

title: 207.106-70 Additional requirements for major systems
content:
L0:207.106-70 Additional requirements for major systems.
L1:(a) Contracting officers are prohibited by 10 U.S.C. 3208(d)(1) from requiring offers
L0:for development or production of major systems that would enable the Government to
L0:use technical data to competitively reprocure identical items or components of the
L0:system if the item or component were developed exclusively at private expense, unless
L0:the contracting officer determines that—
L1:(1) The original supplier of the item or component will be unable to satisfy
L0:program schedule or delivery requirements;
L1:(2) Proposals by the original supplier of the item or component to meet
L0:mobilization requirements are insufficient to meet the agency's mobilization needs; or
L1:(3) The Government is otherwise entitled to unlimited rights in technical data.
L1:(b) If the contracting officer makes a determination, under paragraphs (a)(1) and (2)
L0:of this section, for a competitive solicitation, 10 U.S.C. 3208(d)(2) requires that the
L0:evaluation of items developed at private expense be based on an analysis of the total
L0:value, in terms of innovative design, life-cycle costs, and other pertinent factors, of
L0:incorporating such items in the system.
L1:(c) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3774(a) and DoD policy requirements, acquisition
L0:plans for major weapon systems and subsystems of major weapon systems must—
L1:(1) Assess the long-term technical data and computer software needs of those
L0:systems and subsystems; and
L1:(2) Establish acquisition strategies that provide for the technical data
L0:deliverables and associated license rights needed to sustain those systems and
L0:subsystems over their life cycle. The strategy may include—
L1:(i) The development of maintenance capabilities within DoD; or
L1:(ii) Competition for contracts for sustainment of the systems or subsystems.
L1:(d) Assessments and corresponding acquisition strategies developed under
L0:paragraph (c) of this section must—
L1:(1) Be developed before issuance of a solicitation for the weapon system or
L0:subsystem;
L1:(2) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 4328, to emphasize reliability and
L0:maintainability in weapon system design, ensure that reliability and
L0:maintainability are included in the performance attributes of the key performance
L0:parameters on sustainment during the development of capabilities requirements.
L0:For additional guidance see PGI 207.104-70;
L1:(3) Address the merits of including a priced contract option for the future
L0:delivery of technical data and computer software, and associated license rights, that
L0:were not acquired upon initial contract award;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 7
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 207
L1:(4) Address the potential for changes in the sustainment plan over the life cycle
L0:of the weapon system or subsystem; and
L1:(5) Apply to weapon systems and subsystems that are to be supported by
L0:performance-based logistics arrangements as well as to weapon systems and
L0:subsystems that are to be supported by other sustainment approaches.
L1:(e) See part 209 for policy applicable to acquisition strategies that consider the use
L0:of lead system integrators.
L2:(f)(1) In accordance with section 202 of the Weapon Systems Acquisition Reform
L0:Act of 2009 (Pub. L. 111-23), acquisition plans for major defense acquisition
L0:programs as defined in 10 U.S.C. 4201, must include measures that—
L1:(i) Ensure competition, or the option of competition, at both the prime
L0:contract level and subcontract level (at such tier or tiers as are appropriate) throughout
L0:the program life cycle as a means to improve contractor performance; and
L1:(ii) Document the rationale for the selection of the appropriate subcontract
L0:tier or tiers under paragraph (f)(1)(i) of this section, and the measures which will be
L0:employed to ensure competition, or the option of competition.
L1:(2) Measures to ensure competition, or the option of competition, may include,
L0:but are not limited to, cost-effective measures intended to achieve the following:
L1:(i) Competitive prototyping.
L1:(ii) Dual-sourcing.
L1:(iii) Unbundling of contracts.
L1:(iv) Funding of next-generation prototype systems or subsystems.
L1:(v) Use of modular, open architectures to enable competition for upgrades.
L1:(vi) Use of build-to-print approaches to enable production through multiple
L0:sources.
L1:(vii) Acquisition of complete technical data packages.
L1:(viii) Periodic competitions for subsystem upgrades.
L1:(ix) Licensing of additional suppliers.
L1:(x) Periodic system or program reviews to address long-term competitive
L0:effects of program decisions.
L1:(3) In order to ensure fair and objective “make-or-buy” decisions by prime
L0:contractors, acquisition strategies and resultant solicitations and contracts must—
L1:(i) Require prime contractors to give full and fair consideration to qualified
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 7
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 207
L0:sources other than the prime contractor for the development or construction of major
L0:subsystems and components of major weapon systems;
L1:(ii) Provide for Government surveillance of the process by which prime
L0:contractors consider such sources and determine whether to conduct such development
L0:or construction in-house or through a subcontract; and
L1:(iii) Provide for the assessment of the extent to which the prime contractor
L0:has given full and fair consideration to qualified sources in sourcing decisions as a part
L0:of past performance evaluations.
L1:(4) Whenever a source-of-repair decision results in a plan to award a contract
L0:for the performance of maintenance and sustainment services on a major weapon
L0:system, to the maximum extent practicable and consistent with statutory requirements,
L0:the acquisition plan must prescribe that award will be made on a competitive basis
L0:after giving full consideration to all sources (including sources that partner or
L0:subcontract with public or private sector repair activities).
L1:(5) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 4328, acquisition plans for engineering
L0:manufacturing and development and production of major systems defined in
L0:10 U.S.C. 3041(a) and 4202 and for major defense acquisition programs, must
L0:include performance measures that are developed using best practices for
L0:responding to the positive or negative performance of a contractor for the
L0:engineering and manufacturing development or production of a weapon system,
L0:including embedded software. At a minimum the contracting officer must—
L1:(i) Encourage the use of incentive fees and penalties as appropriate; and
L1:(ii) Allow the program manager or comparable requiring activity official
L0:exercising program management responsibilities, to base determinations of a
L0:contractor’s performance on reliability and maintainability data collected during the
L0:program. Such data collection and associated evaluation metrics must be described in
L0:detail in the contract; and to the maximum extent practicable, the data must be shared
L0:with appropriate contractor and Government organizations.
L1:(g) In accordance with section 815 of the National Defense Authorization Act for
L0:Fiscal Year 2009 (Pub. L. 110-417) and DoD policy requirements, acquisition plans for
L0:major weapons systems must include a plan for the preservation and storage of special
L0:tooling associated with the production of hardware for major defense acquisition
L0:programs through the end of the service life of the related weapons system. The plan
L0:must include the identification of any contract clauses, facilities, and funding required
L0:for the preservation and storage of such tooling. The Under Secretary of Defense for
L0:Acquisition and Sustainment (USD(A&S)) may waive this requirement if USD(A&S)
L0:determines that it is in the best interest of DoD.
L1:(h) When selecting contract type, see 234.004 (section 811 of the National Defense
L0:Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (Pub. L. 112-239)).

title: 207.172 Human research
content:
L0:207.172 Human research.
L0:Any DoD component sponsoring research involving human subjects—

title: 207.470 Statutory requirements
content:
L0:207.470 Statutory requirements.
L1:(a) The contracting officer must not enter into any contract for the lease or charter
L0:of any vessel, aircraft, or combat vehicle, or any contract for services that would require
L0:the use of the contractor’s vessel, aircraft, or combat vehicle, unless the Secretary of the
L0:military department concerned has satisfied the requirements of
L0:10 U.S.C. 3671-3677, when—
L1:(1) The contract will be a long-term lease or charter as defined in 10 U.S.C.
L0:3674(a)(1); or
L1:(2) The terms of the contract provide for a substantial termination liability as
L0:defined in 10 U.S.C. 3674(b). Also see PGI 207.470.
L1:(b) As required by 10 U.S.C. 3678, the contracting officer must not enter into any
L0:contract for any vessel, aircraft, or vehicle, through a lease, charter, or similar
L0:agreement with a term of 18 months or more, or extend or renew any such contract for a
L0:term of 18 months or more, unless the head of the contracting activity has—
L1:(1) Considered all costs of such a contract (including estimated termination
L0:liability); and
L1:(2) Determined in writing that the contract is in the best interest of the
L0:Government.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 7

L0:officer may use leasing in the acquisition of commercial vehicles and associated
L0:equipment whenever the contracting officer determines that leasing of such vehicles is
L0:practicable and efficient (10 U.S.C. 3681).

title: 207.7001 Definition
content:
L0:207.7001 Definition.
L0:“End item,” as used in this subpart, means a production product assembled, completed,
L0:and ready for issue or deployment.

title: 207.7002 Authority to acquire additional quantities of end items
content:
L0:207.7002 Authority to acquire additional quantities of end items.
L0:10 U.S.C. 3069 authorizes DoD to use available funds for the acquisition of an end item
L0:at a higher quantity than the quantity specified in a law providing the funding for the
L0:specific end item, if the head of an agency determines that—
L1:(a) The agency has an established requirement for the end item that is expected to
L0:remain substantially unchanged throughout the period of the acquisition;
L1:(b) It is possible to acquire the higher quantity of the end item without additional
L0:funding because of production efficiencies or other cost reductions;
L1:(c) The amount of funds used for the acquisition of the higher quantity of the end
L0:item will not exceed the amount provided under that law for the acquisition of the end
L0:item; and
L1:(d) The amount provided under that law for the acquisition of the end item is
L0:sufficient to ensure that each unit of the end item acquired within the higher quantity is
L0:fully funded as a complete end item.

L0:PGI 207.171 Component breakout.
L0:DoD policy is to break out components of weapons systems or other major end items under
L0:certain circumstances.
L1:(a) When it is anticipated that a prime contract will be awarded without adequate price
L0:competition, and the prime contractor is expected to acquire any component without
L0:adequate price competition, the agency must break out that component if—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 7
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 207
L1:(1) Substantial net cost savings probably will be achieved; and
L1:(2) Breakout action will not jeopardize the quality, reliability, performance, or timely
L0:delivery of the end item.
L1:(b) Even when either or both the prime contract and the component will be acquired with
L0:adequate price competition, the agency must consider breakout of the component if
L0:substantial net cost savings will result from—
L1:(1) Greater quantity acquisitions; or
L1:(2) Such factors as improved logistics support (through reduction in varieties of
L0:spare parts) and economies in operations and training (through standardization of design).
L1:(c) Breakout normally is not justified for a component that is not expected to exceed $1
L0:million for the current year's requirement.
L0:PGI 207.171-1 Procedures.
L1:(1) Responsibility.
L1:(i) Agencies are responsible for ensuring that—
L1:(A) Breakout reviews are performed on components meeting the criteria in PGI
L0:207.171(a) and (b);
L1:(B) Components susceptible to breakout are earmarked for consideration in
L0:future acquisitions;
L1:(C) Components earmarked for breakout are considered during requirements
L0:determination and appropriate decisions are made; and
L1:(D) Components are broken out when required.
L1:(ii) The program manager or other official responsible for the material program
L0:concerned is responsible for breakout selection, review, and decision.
L1:(iii) The contracting officer or buyer and other specialists (e.g., small business
L0:specialist, engineering, production, logistics, and maintenance) support the program
L0:manager in implementing the breakout program.
L1:(2) Breakout review and decision.
L1:(i) A breakout review and decision includes—
L1:(A) An assessment of the potential risks to the end item from possibilities such
L0:as delayed delivery and reduced reliability of the component;
L1:(B) A calculation of estimated net cost savings (i.e., estimated acquisition
L0:savings less any offsetting costs); and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 7
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 207
L1:(C) An analysis of the technical, operational, logistics, and administrative factors
L0:involved.
L1:(ii) The decision must be supported by adequate explanatory information, including
L0:an assessment by the end item contractor when feasible.
L1:(iii) The following questions should be used in the decision process:
L1:(A) Is the end item contractor likely to do further design or engineering effort on
L0:the component?
L1:(B) Is a suitable data package available with rights to use it for Government
L0:acquisition? (Note that breakout may be warranted even though competitive acquisition is
L0:not possible.)
L1:(C) Can any quality control and reliability problems of the component be
L0:resolved without requiring effort by the end item contractor?
L1:(D) Will the component require further technical support (e.g., development of
L0:specifications, testing requirements, or quality assurance requirements)? If so, does the
L0:Government have the resources (manpower, technical competence, facilities, etc.) to
L0:provide such support? Or, can the support be obtained from the end item contractor (even
L0:though the component is broken out) or other source?
L1:(E) Will breakout impair logistics support (e.g., by jeopardizing standardization
L0:of components)?
L1:(F) Will breakout unduly fragment administration, management, or performance
L0:of the end item contract (e.g., by complicating production scheduling or preventing
L0:identification of responsibility for end item failure caused by a defective component)?
L1:(G) Can breakout be accomplished without jeopardizing delivery requirements
L0:of the end item?
L1:(H) If a decision is made to break out a component, can advance acquisition
L0:funds be made available to provide the new source any necessary additional lead time?
L1:(I) Is there a source other than the present manufacturer capable of supplying
L0:the component?
L1:(J) Has the component been (or is it going to be) acquired directly by the
L0:Government as a support item in the supply system or as Government-furnished equipment
L0:in other end items?
L1:(K) Will the financial risks and other responsibilities assumed by the
L0:Government after breakout be acceptable?
L1:(L) Will breakout result in substantial net cost savings? Develop estimates of
L0:probable savings in cost considering all offsetting costs such as increases in the cost of
L0:requirements determination and control, contracting, contract administration, data package
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 7
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 207
L0:purchase, material inspection, qualification or preproduction testing, ground support and test
L0:equipment, transportation, security, storage, distribution, and technical support.
L1:(iv) If answers to the questions reveal conditions unfavorable to breakout, the
L0:program manager should explore whether the unfavorable conditions can be eliminated.
L0:For example, where adequate technical support is not available from Government
L0:resources, consider contracting for the necessary services from the end item contractor or
L0:other qualified source.
L1:(3) Records.
L1:(i) The contracting activity shall maintain records on components reviewed for
L0:breakout. Records should evidence whether the components—
L1:(A) Have no potential for breakout;
L1:(B) Have been earmarked as potential breakout candidates; or
L1:(C) Have been, or will be, broken out.
L1:(ii) The program manager or other designated official must sign the records.
L1:(iii) Records must reflect the facts and conditions of the case, including any
L0:assessment by the contractor, and the basis for the decision. The records must contain the
L0:assessments, calculations, and analyses discussed in paragraph 2 of this section, including
L0:the trade-off analysis between savings and increased risk to the Government because of
L0:responsibility for Government-furnished equipment.

title: 208.7001 Definitions
content:
L0:208.7001 Definitions.
L0:For purposes of this subpart—

title: 208.7003-1 Assignments under integrated materiel management

L0:the requirement. This exception does not apply to items—

L1:(ii) With special security characteristics; or

title: 208.7003-2 Exceptions
content:
L0:208.7003-2 Exceptions.
L0:Requiring departments must submit to the acquiring department all contracting
L0:requirements for items assigned for IMM, except—
L1:(a) Items obtained through the sources in FAR 8.103;
L1:(b) Items obtained under 208.7003-1(a);
L1:(c) Requirements not in excess of the simplified acquisition threshold, when
L0:contracting by the requiring department is in the best interest of the Government;
L1:(d) In an emergency. When an emergency purchase is made, the requiring
L0:department must send one copy of the contract and a statement of the emergency to the
L0:contracting activity of the acquiring department;
L1:(e) Requirements for which the IMM delegates contracting authority to the
L0:requiring department;
L1:(f) Items in a research and development stage (as described in FAR Part 35). Under
L0:this exception, the military departments may contract for research and development
L0:requirements, including quantities for testing purposes and items undergoing in-service
L0:evaluation (not yet in actual production, but beyond prototype). Generally, this
L0:exception applies only when research and development funds are used.
L1:(g) Items peculiar to nuclear ordnance material where design characteristics or test-
L0:inspection requirements are controlled by the Department of Energy (DoE) or by DoD to
L0:ensure reliability of nuclear weapons.
L1:(1) This exception applies to all items designed for and peculiar to nuclear
L0:ordnance regardless of agency control, or to any item which requires test or inspection
L0:conducted or controlled by DoE or DoD.
L1:(2) This exception does not cover items used for both nuclear ordnance and
L0:other purposes if the items are not subject to the special testing procedures.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 8
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 208
L1:(h) Items to be acquired under FAR 6.103-6 (national security requires limitation of
L0:sources);
L1:(i) Items directly related to a major system and which are design controlled by and
L0:acquired from either the system manufacturer or a manufacturer of a major subsystem;
L1:(j) Items subject to rapid design changes, or to continuous redesign or modification
L0:during the production and/or operational use phases, which require continual contact
L0:between industry and the requiring department to ensure that the item meets the
L0:requirements:
L1:(1) This exception permits the requiring department to contract for items of
L0:highly unstable design. For use of this exception, it must be clearly impractical, both
L0:technically and contractually, to refer the acquisition to the acquiring department.
L0:Anticipation that contracting by negotiation will be appropriate, or that a number of
L0:design changes may occur during contract performance is not in itself sufficient reason
L0:for using this exception.
L1:(2) This exception also applies to items requiring compatibility testing, provided
L0:such testing requires continual contact between industry and the requiring department;
L1:(k) Containers acquired only with items for which they are designed;
L1:(l) One-time buy of a noncataloged item.
L1:(1) This exception permits the requiring departments to contract for a
L0:nonrecurring requirement for a noncataloged item. This exception could cover a part or
L0:component for a prototype which may be stock numbered at a later date.
L1:(2) This exception does not permit acquisitions of recurring requirements for an
L0:item, based solely on the fact that the item is not stock numbered, nor may it be used to
L0:acquire items which have only slightly different characteristics than previously
L0:cataloged items.

L0:contracts, issued by the General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Information

L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 8
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 208

L0:ordering from GSA Self-Service Stores;
L1:(3) Order only those items required in the performance of Government
L0:contracts; and
L1:(4) The Contractor shall pay invoices from Government supply sources
L0:promptly.
L1:(A) The Contractor shall pay purchases made from DoD supply sources
L0:within 30 days of the date of a proper invoice.
L1:(B) The Contractor shall annotate each invoice with the date of receipt.
L1:(C) For the purposes of computing interest for late Contractor payments,
L0:the Government’s invoice is deemed to be a demand for payment in accordance with the
L0:Interest clause of this contract.
L1:(D) If the Contractor fails to pay or pays late that may also result in the
L0:DoD supply source refusing to honor the requisition (see DFARS 208-105-2(a)(4)(ii)) or
L0:in the Contracting Officer terminating the Contractor’s authorization to use DoD supply
L0:sources.
L1:(1) In the event the Contracting Officer decides to terminate the
L0:authorization due to the Contractor’s failure to pay in a timely manner, the Contracting
L0:Officer will provide the Contractor with prompt written notice of the intent to terminate
L0:the authorization and the basis for such action.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall have 10 days after receipt of the Government’s
L0:notice in which to provide additional information as to why the authorization should not
L0:be terminated.
L1:(3) Any such termination does not provide the Contractor with an
L0:excusable delay for failure to perform or complete the contract in accordance with the
L0:terms of the contract, and the Contractor shall be solely responsible for any increased
L0:costs.
L1:(d) When placing orders for Government stock on a non-reimbursable basis, the
L0:Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Comply with the requirements of the Contracting Officer's authorization;
L0:and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 8
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 208
L1:(2) When using electronic transactions to submit requisitions on a

L0:Implementation Convention 511R, Requisition; and acknowledge receipts by

L1:(e) Only the Contractor may request authorization for subcontractor use of

L0:252.251-7001 Use of Interagency Fleet Management System (IFMS) Vehicles
L0:and Related Services.
L0:As prescribed in 208.7501(b), use the following clause:
L0:USE OF INTERAGENCY FLEET MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (IFMS) VEHICLES AND
L0:RELATED SERVICES (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Contractor, if authorized use of IFMS vehicles, shall submit requests for five
L0:or fewer vehicles and related services in writing to the appropriate General Services
L0:Administration (GSA) Regional Customer Service Bureau, Attention: Motor Equipment
L0:Activity. Submit requests for more than five vehicles to GSA headquarters: General
L0:Services Administration, FTM, Washington, DC 20406. Include the following in each
L0:request:
L1:(1) Two copies of the agency authorization to obtain vehicles and related
L0:services from GSA.
L1:(2) The number of vehicles and related services required and the period of use.
L1:(3) A list of the Contractor's employees authorized to request vehicles and
L0:related services.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 8
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 208
L1:(4) A list of the makes, models, and serial numbers of Contractor-owned or
L0:leased equipment authorized to be serviced.
L1:(5) Billing instructions and address.
L1:(b) The Contractor should make requests for any unusual quantities of vehicles as
L0:far in advance as possible.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall establish and enforce suitable penalties for employees who
L0:use or authorize the use of Government vehicles for other than performance of
L0:Government contracts.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall assume, without the right of reimbursement from the
L0:Government, the cost or expense of any use of IFMS vehicles and services not related to
L0:the performance of the contract.
L1:(e) Only the Contractor may request authorization for subcontractor use of IFMS
L0:vehicles. The Contracting Officer will not grant authorization for subcontractor use
L0:without approval of the Contractor.

L0:PGI 208.7002-1 Acquiring department responsibilities.
L0:The acquiring department generally is responsible under the integrated material
L0:management (IMM) program for—
L1:(1) Operational aspects of acquisition planning (phasing the submission of requirements
L0:to contracting, consolidating or dividing requirements, analyzing the market, and determining
L0:patterns for the phased placement of orders to avoid unnecessary production fluctuations
L0:and meet the needs of requiring departments at the lowest price);
L1:(2) Purchasing;
L1:(3) Performing or assigning contract administration, including follow-up and expediting of
L0:inspection and transportation; and
L1:(4) Obtaining licenses under patents and settling patent infringement claims arising out
L0:of the acquisition. (Acquiring departments must obtain approval from the department whose
L0:funds are to be charged for obtaining licenses or settling claims.)

L0:PGI 208.7002-2 Requiring department responsibilities.
L0:The requiring department is responsible for—

L0:PGI 208.7004 Procedures.
L0:PGI 208.7004-1 Purchase authorization from requiring department.
L1:(1) Requiring departments send their requirements to acquiring departments on either a
L0:DD Form 448, Military Interdepartmental Purchase Request (MIPR), or a DD Form 416,
L0:Requisition for Coal, Coke or Briquettes. A MIPR or a DD Form 416 is the acquiring
L0:department's authority to acquire the supplies or services on behalf of the requiring
L0:department.
L1:(2) The acquiring department is authorized to create obligations against the funds cited
L0:in a MIPR without further referral to the requiring department. The acquiring department has
L0:no responsibility to determine the validity of a stated requirement in an approved MIPR, but it
L0:should bring apparent errors in the requirement to the attention of the requiring department.
L1:(3) Changes that affect the contents of the MIPR must be processed as a MIPR
L0:amendment regardless of the status of the MIPR. The requiring department may initially
L0:transmit changes electronically or by some other expedited means, but must confirm
L0:changes by a MIPR amendment.
L1:(4) The requiring department must submit requirements for additional line items of
L0:supplies or services not provided for in the original MIPR as a new MIPR. The requiring
L0:department may use a MIPR amendment for increased quantities only if—
L1:(i) The original MIPR requirements have not been released for solicitation; and
L1:(ii) The acquiring department agrees.
L0:PGI 208.7004-2 Acceptance by acquiring department.
L1:(1) Acquiring departments formally accept a MIPR by DD Form 448-2, Acceptance of
L0:MIPR, as soon as practicable, but no later than 30 days after receipt of the MIPR. If the 30
L0:day time limit cannot be met, the acquiring department must inform the requiring department
L0:of the reason for the delay, and the anticipated date the MIPR will be accepted. The
L0:acquiring department must accept MIPRs in writing before expiration of the funds.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 8
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 208
L1:(2) The acquiring department in accepting a MIPR will determine whether to use
L0:Category I (reimbursable funds citation) or Category II (direct funds citation) methods of
L0:funding.
L1:(i) Category I method of funding is used under the following circumstances and
L0:results in citing the funds of the acquiring department in the contract:
L1:(A) Delivery is from existing inventories of the acquiring department;
L1:(B) Delivery is by diversion from existing contracts of the acquiring department;
L1:(C) Production or assembly is through Government work orders in Government-
L0:owned plants;
L1:(D) Production quantities are allocated among users from one or more
L0:contracts, and the identification of specific quantities of the end item to individual contracts is
L0:not feasible at the time of MIPR acceptance;
L1:(E) Acquisition of the end items involves separate acquisition of components to
L0:be assembled by the acquiring department;
L1:(F) Payments will be made without reference to deliveries of end items (e.g.,
L0:cost-reimbursement type contracts and fixed-price contracts with progress payment
L0:clauses); or
L1:(G) Category II method of funding is not feasible and economical.
L1:(ii) Category II method of funding is used in circumstances other than those in
L0:paragraph (2)(i) of this subsection. Category II funding results in citation of the requiring
L0:department's funds and MIPR number in the resultant contract.
L1:(3) When the acquiring departments accepts a MIPR for Category I funding—
L1:(i) The DD Form 448-2, Acceptance of MIPR, is the authority for the requiring
L0:department to record the obligation of funds;
L1:(ii) The acquiring department will annotate the DD Form 448-2 if contingencies,
L0:price revisions, or variations in quantities are anticipated. The acquiring department will
L0:periodically advise the requiring department, prior to submission of billings, of any changes
L0:in the acceptance figure so that the requiring department may issue an amendment to the
L0:MIPR, and the recorded obligation may be adjusted to reflect the current price;
L1:(iii) If the acquiring department does not qualify the acceptance of a MIPR for
L0:anticipated contingencies, the price on the acceptance will be final and will be billed at time
L0:of delivery; and
L1:(iv) Upon receipt of the final billing (SF 1080, Voucher for Transferring Funds), the
L0:requiring department may adjust the fiscal records accordingly without authorization from or
L0:notice to the acquiring department.
L1:(4) When the MIPR is accepted for Category II funding, a conformed copy of the
L0:contract (see DFARS 204.802(1)(ii)) is the authority to record the obligation. When all
L0:awards have been placed to satisfy the total MIPR requirement, any unused funds
L0:remaining on the MIPR become excess to the acquiring department. The acquiring
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 8
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 208
L0:department will immediately notify the requiring department of the excess funds by
L0:submitting an Acceptance of MIPR (DD Form 448-2). This amendment is authorization for
L0:the requiring department to withdraw the funds. The acquiring department is prohibited from
L0:further use of such excess funds.
L1:(5) When the acquiring department requires additional funds to complete the contracting
L0:action for the requiring department, the request for additional funds must identify the exact
L0:items involved, and the reason why additional funds are required. The requiring department
L0:must act quickly to—
L1:(i) Provide the funds by an amendment of the MIPR; or
L1:(ii) Reduce the requirements.
L1:(6) The accepting activity of the acquiring department must remain responsible for the
L0:MIPR even though that activity may split the MIPR into segments for action by other
L0:contracting activities.
L0:PGI 208.7004-3 Use of advance MIPRs.
L1:(1) An advance MIPR is an unfunded MIPR provided to the acquiring department in
L0:advance of the funded MIPR so that initial steps in planning the contract action can begin at
L0:an earlier date.
L1:(2) In order to use an advance MIPR, the acquiring department and the requiring
L0:department must agree that its use will be beneficial. The departments may execute a
L0:blanket agreement to use advance MIPRs.
L1:(3) The requiring department must not release an advance MIPR to the acquiring
L0:department without obtaining proper internal approval of the requirement.
L1:(4) When advance MIPRs are used, mark “ADVANCE MIPR” prominently on the DD
L0:Form 448.
L1:(5) For urgent requirements, the advance MIPR may be transmitted electronically.
L1:(6) On the basis of an advance MIPR, the acquiring department may take the initial
L0:steps toward awarding a contract, such as obtaining internal coordination and preparing an
L0:acquisition plan. Acquiring departments may determine the extent of these initial actions but
L0:must not award contracts on the basis of advance MIPRs.
L0:PGI 208.7004-4 Cutoff dates for submission of Category II MIPRs.
L1:(1) Unless otherwise agreed between the departments, May 31 is the cutoff date for the
L0:receipt of MIPRs citing expiring appropriations which must be obligated by September 30 of
L0:that fiscal year. If circumstances arise that require the submission of MIPRs citing expiring
L0:appropriations after the cutoff date, the requiring department will communicate with the
L0:acquiring department before submission to find out whether the acquiring department can
L0:execute a contract or otherwise obligate the funds by the end of the fiscal year. Acquiring
L0:departments will make every effort to obligate funds for all such MIPRs accepted after the
L0:cutoff date. However, acceptance of a late MIPR does not constitute assurance by the
L0:acquiring department that all such funds will be obligated.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 8
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 208
L1:(2) Nothing in these instructions is intended to restrict the processing of MIPRs when the
L0:acquiring department is capable of executing contracts or otherwise obligating funds before
L0:the end of the fiscal year.
L1:(3) The May 31 cutoff date does not apply to MIPRs citing continuing appropriations.
L0:PGI 208.7004-5 Notification of inability to obligate on Category II MIPRs.
L0:On August 1, the acquiring department will advise the requiring department of any Category
L0:II MIPRs on hand citing expiring appropriations it will be unable to obligate prior to the fund
L0:expiration date. If an unforeseen situation develops after August 1 that will prevent
L0:execution of a contract, the acquiring department will notify the requiring department as
L0:quickly as possible and will return the MIPR. The letter of transmittal returning the MIPR will
L0:authorize purchase by the requiring department and state the reason that the acquisition
L0:could not be accomplished.
L0:PGI 208.7004-6 Cancellation of requirements.
L1:(1) Category I MIPRs. The requiring department will notify the acquiring department by
L0:electronic or other immediate means when cancelling all or part of the supplies or services
L0:requested in the MIPR. Within 30 days, the acquiring department will notify the requiring
L0:department of the quantity of items available for termination and the amount of funds in
L0:excess of the estimated settlement costs. Upon receipt of this information, the requiring
L0:department will issue a MIPR amendment to reduce the quantities and funds accordingly.
L1:(2) Category II MIPRs. The requiring department will notify the acquiring department
L0:electronically or by other immediate means when cancelling all or any part of the supplies or
L0:services requested in the MIPR.
L1:(i) If the acquiring department has not entered into a contract for the supplies or
L0:services to be cancelled, the acquiring department will immediately notify the requiring
L0:department. Upon receipt of such notification, the requiring department must initiate a MIPR
L0:amendment to revoke the estimated amount shown on the original MIPR for the cancelled
L0:items.
L1:(ii) If the items to be cancelled have already been placed under contract—
L1:(A) As soon as practicable, but in no event more than 45 days after receipt of
L0:the cancellation notice from the requiring department, the contracting officer must issue a
L0:termination data letter to the requiring department (original and four copies) containing, as a
L0:minimum, the information in Table 8-1, Termination Data Letter.
L1:(B) The termination contracting officer (TCO) will review the proceedings at
L0:least every 60 days to reassess the Government's probable obligation. If any additional
L0:funds are excess to the probable settlement requirements, or if it appears that previous
L0:release of excess funds will result in a shortage of the amount that will be required for
L0:settlement, the TCO will promptly notify the contracting office which will amend the
L0:termination data letter. The requiring department will process a MIPR amendment to reflect
L0:the reinstatement of funds within 30 days after receiving the amended termination data
L0:letter.
L1:(C) Upon receipt of a copy of the termination settlement agreement, the
L0:requiring department will prepare a MIPR amendment, if required, to remove any remaining
L0:excess funds.

L0:a) Definitions.

L0:assigned commodity integrated material manager for refined precious metals and is
L0:responsible for the storage and issue of such material.
L0:“Dual pricing evaluation procedure” means a procedure where offerors submit two prices
L0:for precious metals bearing items--one based on Government-furnished precious metals
L0:and one based on contractor-furnished precious metals. The contracting officer evaluates
L0:the prices to determine which is in the Government's best interest.
L0:“Precious Metals Indicator Code (PMIC)” means a single-digit, alpha-numeric code
L0:assigned to national stock numbered items in the Defense Integrated Data System Total
L0:Item Record used to indicate the presence or absence of precious metals in the item.
L0:PMICs and the content value of corresponding items are listed in DoD 4100.39-M, Federal
L0:Logistics Information System (FLIS) Procedures Manual, Volume 10, Chapter 4, Table 160.
L0:“Refined precious metal” means recovered silver, gold, platinum, palladium, iridium,
L0:rhodium, or ruthenium, in bullion, granulation or sponge form, which has been purified to at
L0:least .999 percentage of fineness.
L0:b) Policy.
