L0:PGI 208.74—ENTERPRISE SOFTWARE AGREEMENTS
L0:PGI 208.7401 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Golden Disk” means a purchased license or entitlement to distribute an unlimited or bulk
L0:number of copies of software throughout DoD.
L0:“Software product manager” means the Government official who manages an enterprise
L0:software agreement.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 8
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 208
L0:PGI 208.7403 Acquisition procedures.
L1:(1) After requirements are determined, the requiring official must review the information
L0:at the ESI website to determine if the required commercial software or related services are
L0:available from DoD inventory (e.g., Golden Disks and DoD-wide software maintenance
L0:agreements). If the software or services are available, the requiring official must fulfill the
L0:requirement from the DoD inventory.
L1:(2) If the required commercial software or related services are not in the DoD inventory,
L0:and not on an ESA, the contracting officer or requiring official may fulfill the requirement by
L0:other means. Existing ESAs are listed on the ESI website.
L1:(3) If the commercial software or related services are on an ESA, the contracting officer
L0:or requiring official must review the terms and conditions and prices in accordance with
L0:otherwise applicable source selection requirements.
L1:(4) If an ESA’s terms and conditions and prices represent the best value to the
L0:Government, the contracting officer or requiring official must fulfill the requirement for
L0:software or services through the ESA.
L1:(5) If existing ESAs do not represent the best value to the Government, the software
L0:product manager (SPM) must be given an opportunity to provide the same or a better value
L0:to the Government under the ESAs before the contracting officer or requiring official may
L0:continue with alternate acquisition methods.
L1:(i) The contracting officer or requiring official must notify the SPM of specific
L0:concerns about existing ESA terms and conditions or prices through the ESI webpage.
L1:(ii) The SPM must consider adjusting, within the scope of the ESA, terms and
L0:conditions or prices to provide the best value to the customer.
L1:(A) Within 3 working days, the SPM must—
L1:(1) Update the ESA;
L1:(2) Provide an estimated date by which the update will be accomplished; or
L1:(3) Inform the contracting officer or requiring official that no change will be
L0:made to the ESA.
L1:(B) If the SPM informs the contracting officer or requiring official that no change
L0:will be made to the ESA terms and conditions or prices, the contracting officer or requiring
L0:official may fulfill the requirement by other means.
L1:(C) If the SPM does not respond within 3 working days or does not plan to
L0:adjust the ESA within 90 days, the contracting officer or requiring official may fulfill the
L0:requirement by other means.
L1:(iii) A management official designated by the department or agency may waive the
L0:requirement to obtain commercial software or related services through an ESA after the
L0:steps in paragraphs (5)(i) and (5)(ii)(A) of this section are complete. The rationale for use of
L0:an alternate source must be included in the waiver request and must be provided to the
L0:SPM.

title: 209.101 Definitions
content:
L0:209.101 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Effectively owned or controlled” means that a foreign government or any entity
L0:controlled by a foreign government has the power, either directly or indirectly, whether
L0:exercised or exercisable, to control the election, appointment, or tenure of the Offeror’s
L0:officers or a majority of the Offeror’s board of directors by any means, e.g., ownership,
L0:contract, or operation of law (or equivalent power for unincorporated organizations).
L0:“Entity controlled by a foreign government”—
L1:(1) Means—
L1:(i) Any domestic or foreign organization or corporation that is effectively owned
L0:or controlled by a foreign government; or
L1:(ii) Any individual acting on behalf of a foreign government.
L1:(2) Does not include an organization or corporation that is owned, but is not
L0:controlled, either directly or indirectly, by a foreign government if the ownership of that
L0:organization or corporation by that foreign government was effective before October 23,
L0:1992.
L0:“Foreign government” includes the state and the government of any country (other than
L0:the United States and its outlying areas) as well as any political subdivision, agency, or
L0:instrumentality thereof.
L0:“Proscribed information” means—
L1:(1) Top Secret information;
L1:(2) Communications security (COMSEC) material, excluding controlled
L0:cryptographic items when unkeyed or utilized with unclassified keys;
L1:(3) Restricted Data as defined in the U.S. Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended;
L1:(4) Special Access Program (SAP) information; or
L1:(5) Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI).

title: 209.270-2 Definitions
content:
L0:209.270-2 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L0:“Aviation critical safety item” means a part, an assembly, installation equipment,
L0:launch equipment, recovery equipment, or support equipment for an aircraft or aviation
L0:weapon system if the part, assembly, or equipment contains a characteristic any failure,
L0:malfunction, or absence of which could cause—
L1:(1) A catastrophic or critical failure resulting in the loss of or serious damage to the
L0:aircraft or weapon system;
L1:(2) An unacceptable risk of personal injury or loss of life; or
L1:(3) An uncommanded engine shutdown that jeopardizes safety.
L0:“Design control activity”—
L1:(1) With respect to an aviation critical safety item, means the systems command of
L0:a military department that is specifically responsible for ensuring the air worthiness of
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 9
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 209

L0:and
L1:(2) With respect to a ship critical safety item, means the systems command of a
L0:military department that is specifically responsible for ensuring the seaworthiness of a
L0:ship or ship equipment in which a ship critical safety item is to be used.
L0:“Ship critical safety item” means any ship part, assembly, or support equipment
L0:containing a characteristic the failure, malfunction, or absence of which could cause—
L1:(1) A catastrophic or critical failure resulting in loss of or serious damage to the
L0:ship; or
L1:(2) An unacceptable risk of personal injury or loss of life.

title: 209.270-3 Policy
content:

title: 209.570-2 Policy
content:
L0:209.570-2 Policy.
L1:(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, 10 U.S.C. 4292 prohibits any
L0:entity performing lead system integrator functions in the acquisition of a major system
L0:by DoD from having any direct financial interest in the development or construction of
L0:any individual system or element of any system of systems.
L1:(b) The prohibition in paragraph (a) of this subsection does not apply if—
L1:(1) The Secretary of Defense certifies to the Committees on Armed Services of
L0:the Senate and the House of Representatives that—
L1:(i) The entity was selected by DoD as a contractor to develop or construct
L0:the system or element concerned through the use of competitive procedures; and
L1:(ii) DoD took appropriate steps to prevent any organizational conflict of
L0:interest in the selection process; or
L1:(2) The entity was selected by a subcontractor to serve as a lower-tier
L0:subcontractor, through a process over which the entity exercised no control.
L1:(c) In accordance with section 802 of the National Defense Authorization Act for
L0:Fiscal Year 2008 (Pub. L. 110-181; 10 U.S.C. 4292 note), DoD may award a new
L0:contract for lead system integrator functions in the acquisition of a major system only
L0:if—
L1:(1) The major system has not yet proceeded beyond low-rate initial production;
L0:or
L1:(2) The Secretary of Defense determines in writing that carrying out the
L0:acquisition without continuing to use a contractor to perform lead system integrator
L0:functions would be impracticable and that doing so is in the best interest of DoD. The
L0:authority to make this determination may not be delegated below the level of the Under
L0:Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment. See also 209.570-3(b).
L1:(d) Effective October 1, 2010, DoD is prohibited from awarding a new contract for
L0:lead system integrator functions in the acquisition of a major system to any entity that
L0:was not performing lead system integrator functions in the acquisition of the major
L0:system prior to January 28, 2008.

title: 209.571-3 Policy
content:
L0:209.571-3 Policy.
L1:(a) Agencies must obtain advice on major defense acquisition programs and pre-
L0:major defense acquisition programs from sources that are objective and unbiased; and
L1:(b) Generally, seek to resolve organizational conflicts of interest in a manner that
L0:will promote competition and preserve DoD access to the expertise and experience of
L0:qualified contractors. Accordingly, to the extent feasible, employ organizational conflict
L0:of interest resolution strategies that do not unnecessarily restrict the pool of potential
L0:offerors in current or future acquisitions. Further, contracting activities must not
L0:impose across-the-board restrictions or limitations on the use of particular resolution
L0:methods, except as required under 209.571-7 or as appropriate in particular
L0:acquisitions.
subpart: SUBPART 209.5 — ORGANIZATIONAL AND CONSULTANT CONFLICTS OF

title: 209.571-4 Mitigation
content:
L0:209.571-4 Mitigation.
L1:(a) Mitigation is any action taken to minimize an organizational conflict of interest.
L0:Mitigation may require Government action, contractor action, or a combination of both.
L1:(b) If the contracting officer and the contractor have agreed to mitigation of an
L0:organizational conflict of interest, incorporate into the contract a Government-approved
L0:Organizational Conflict of Interest Mitigation Plan, reflecting the actions a contractor
L0:has agreed to take to mitigate a conflict.
L1:(c) If determining, after consultation with legal counsel, that the otherwise
L0:successful offeror is unable to effectively mitigate an organizational conflict of interest,
L0:then , taking into account both the contract and longer term Government needs, use
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 9
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 209
L0:another approach to resolve the organizational conflict of interest, select another offeror,
L0:or request a waiver in accordance with FAR 9.503 (but see statutory prohibition in
L0:209.571-7).
L1:(d) For any acquisition exceeding $1 billion, brief the senior procurement executive
L0:before determining that an offeror’s mitigation plan is unacceptable.

title: 209.571-6 Identification of organizational conflicts of interest
content:
L0:209.571-6 Identification of organizational conflicts of interest.
L0:When evaluating organizational conflicts of interest for major defense acquisition
L0:programs or pre-major defense acquisition programs, consider—
L1:(a) The ownership of business units performing systems engineering and technical
L0:assistance, professional services, or management support services to a major defense
L0:acquisition program or a pre-major defense acquisition program by a contractor who
L0:simultaneously owns a business unit competing (or potentially competing) to perform
L0:as—
L1:(1) The prime contractor for the same major defense acquisition program; or
L1:(2) The supplier of a major subsystem or component for the same major defense
L0:acquisition program.
L1:(b) The proposed award of a major subsystem by a prime contractor to business
L0:units or other affiliates of the same parent corporate entity, particularly the award of a
L0:subcontract for software integration or the development of a proprietary software
L0:system architecture; and
L1:(c) The performance by, or assistance of, contractors in technical evaluation.

content:
L0:252.209-7006 Limitations on Contractors Acting as Lead System Integrators.
L0:As prescribed in 209.570-4(a), use the following provision:
L0:LIMITATIONS ON CONTRACTORS ACTING AS LEAD SYSTEM INTEGRATORS
L0:(DEC 2022)
L1:(a) Definitions. Lead system integrator, lead system integrator with system
L0:responsibility, and lead system integrator without system responsibility, as used in this
L0:provision, have the meanings given in the clause of this solicitation entitled “Prohibited
L0:Financial Interests for Lead System Integrators” (DFARS 252.209-7007).
L1:(b) General. Unless an exception is granted, no contractor performing lead system
L0:integrator functions in the acquisition of a major system by the Department of Defense
L0:may have any direct financial interest in the development or construction of any
L0:individual system or element of any system of systems.
L1:(c) Representations. (1) The offeror represents that it does
L0:[ ] does not [ ] propose to perform this contract as a lead system integrator with system
L0:responsibility.
L1:(2) The offeror represents that it does [ ] does not [ ] propose to perform this contract
L0:as a lead system integrator without system responsibility.
L1:(3) If the offeror answered in the affirmative in paragraph (c)(1) or (2) of this
L0:provision, the offeror represents that it does [ ] does not [ ] have any direct financial
L0:interest as described in paragraph (b) of this provision with respect to the system(s),
L0:subsystem(s), system of systems, or services described in this solicitation.
L1:(d) If the offeror answered in the affirmative in paragraph (c)(3) of this provision, the
L0:offeror should contact the Contracting Officer for guidance on the possibility of
L0:submitting a mitigation plan and/or requesting an exception.
L1:(e) If the offeror does have a direct financial interest, the offeror may be prohibited
L0:from receiving an award under this solicitation, unless the offeror submits to the
L0:Contracting Officer appropriate evidence that the offeror was selected by a
L0:subcontractor to serve as a lower-tier subcontractor through a process over which the
L0:offeror exercised no control.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 9
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 209
L1:(f) This provision implements the requirements of 10 U.S.C. 4292.

title: 252.209-7007 Prohibited Financial Interests for Lead System Integrators
content:
L0:252.209-7007 Prohibited Financial Interests for Lead System Integrators.
L0:As prescribed in 209.570-4(b), use the following clause:
L0:PROHIBITED FINANCIAL INTERESTS FOR LEAD SYSTEM INTEGRATORS (DEC
L0:2022)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) Lead system integrator includes lead system integrator with system
L0:responsibility and lead system integrator without system responsibility.
L1:(2) Lead system integrator with system responsibility means a prime contractor
L0:for the development or production of a major system, if the prime contractor is not
L0:expected at the time of award to perform a substantial portion of the work on the
L0:system and the major subsystems.
L1:(3) Lead system integrator without system responsibility means a prime
L0:contractor under a contract for the procurement of services, the primary purpose of
L0:which is to perform acquisition functions closely associated with inherently
L0:governmental functions (see section 7.503(d) of the Federal Acquisition Regulation) with
L0:respect to the development or production of a major system.
L1:(b) Limitations. The Contracting Officer has determined that the Contractor meets
L0:the definition of lead system integrator with [ ] without [ ] system responsibility. Unless
L0:an exception is granted, the Contractor shall not have any direct financial interest in
L0:the development or construction of any individual system or element of any system of
L0:systems while performing lead system integrator functions in the acquisition of a major
L0:system by the Department of Defense under this contract.
L1:(c) Agreement. The Contractor agrees that during performance of this contract it will
L0:not acquire any direct financial interest as described in paragraph (b) of this clause, or,
L0:if it does acquire or plan to acquire such interest, it will immediately notify the
L0:Contracting Officer. The Contractor further agrees to provide to the Contracting Officer
L0:all relevant information regarding the change in financial interests so that the
L0:Contracting Officer can determine whether an exception applies or whether the
L0:Contractor will be allowed to continue performance on this contract. If a direct financial
L0:interest cannot be avoided, eliminated, or mitigated to the Contracting Officer’s
L0:satisfaction, the Contracting Officer may terminate this contract for default for the
L0:Contractor’s material failure to comply with the terms and conditions of award or may
L0:take other remedial measures as appropriate in the Contracting Officer’s sole
L0:discretion.
L1:(d) Notwithstanding any other clause of this contract, if the Contracting Officer
L0:determines that the Contractor misrepresented its financial interests at the time of
L0:award or has violated the agreement in paragraph (c) of this clause, the Government
L0:may terminate this contract for default for the Contractor’s material failure to comply
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 9
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 209
L0:with the terms and conditions of award or may take other remedial measures as
L0:appropriate in the Contracting Officer’s sole discretion.
L1:(e) This clause implements the requirements of 10 U.S.C. 4292.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 211.274-1 General
content:
L0:211.274-1 General.

L0:tracking items delivered to DoD that enhances logistics, contracting, and financial
L0:business transactions supporting the United States and coalition troops.

title: 211.274-2 Requirements for item unique identification
content:
L0:211.274-2 Requirements for item unique identification.
L1:(a) DoD item unique identification, or a DoD recognized unique identification
L0:equivalent, is required for all delivered items, including items of contractor-acquired
L0:property delivered on line items (see PGI 245.402-71 for guidance when delivery of
L0:contractor acquired property is required).
L1:(b) The primary inventory control activity (PICA) determines that an item requires
L0:unique item-level traceability. The PICA will designate the item as a “DoD serially
L0:managed item.” DoD serially managed items are identified by the Federal Logistics
L0:Information System DoD serially managed item indicator set to ‘Y’.
L1:(c) Procedures for identifying items that require unique item-level traceability can
L0:be found in department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 8320.04, DoD Serially Managed
L0:Items of Tangible Personal Property and Item Unique Identification 2.0 Standard.

title: 211.274-3 Requirements for valuation
content:
L0:211.274-3 Requirements for valuation.
L1:(a) The statement of work or requirement document must require contractors to
L0:identify the Government's unit acquisition cost for all deliverable end items to

L0:identified in the contract at the time of delivery;
L1:(2) For cost-type or undefinitized line, subline, or exhibit line items, the

L0:delivery; and
L1:(3) For items delivered under a time-and-materials contract, the
L0:contractor's estimated fully burdened unit cost to the Government at the time of
L0:delivery.
L1:(c) The Government's unit acquisition cost of subassemblies, components, and
L0:parts embedded in delivered items must not be separately identified.

title: 252.211-7003 Item Unique Identification and Valuation
content:
L0:252.211-7003 Item Unique Identification and Valuation.
L0:As prescribed in 211.274-5(a), use the following clause:
L0:ITEM UNIQUE IDENTIFICATION AND VALUATION (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Automatic identification device” means a device, such as a reader or
L0:interrogator, used to retrieve data encoded on machine-readable media.
L0:“Concatenated unique item identifier” means—
L1:(1) For items that are serialized within the enterprise identifier, the linking
L0:together of the unique identifier data elements in order of the issuing agency code,
L0:enterprise identifier, and unique serial number within the enterprise identifier; or
L1:(2) For items that are serialized within the original part, lot, or batch
L0:number, the linking together of the unique identifier data elements in order of the
L0:issuing agency code; enterprise identifier; original part, lot, or batch number; and serial
L0:number within the original part, lot, or batch number.
L0:“Data matrix” means a two-dimensional matrix symbology, which is made up of
L0:square or, in some cases, round modules arranged within a perimeter finder pattern
L0:and uses the Error Checking and Correction 200 (ECC200) specification found within
L0:International Standards Organization (ISO)/International Electrotechnical Commission
L1:(IEC) 16022.
L0:“Data qualifier” means a specified character (or string of characters) that
L0:immediately precedes a data field that defines the general category or intended use of
L0:the data that follows.
L0:“DoD recognized unique identification equivalent” means a unique identification
L0:method that is in commercial use and has been recognized by DoD. All DoD recognized
L0:unique identification equivalents are listed at
L0:https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/ds/unique-id.html.
L0:“DoD item unique identification” means a system of marking items delivered to
L0:DoD with unique item identifiers that have machine-readable data elements to
L0:distinguish an item from all other like and unlike items. For items that are serialized
L0:within the enterprise identifier, the unique item identifier shall include the data
L0:elements of the enterprise identifier and a unique serial number. For items that are
L0:serialized within the part, lot, or batch number within the enterprise identifier, the
L0:unique item identifier shall include the data elements of the enterprise identifier; the
L0:original part, lot, or batch number; and the serial number.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 11
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 211
L0:“Enterprise” means the entity (e.g., a manufacturer or vendor) responsible for
L0:assigning unique item identifiers to items.
L0:“Enterprise identifier” means a code that is uniquely assigned to an enterprise
L0:by an issuing agency.
L0:“Government’s unit acquisition cost” means—
L1:(1) For fixed-price type line, subline, or exhibit line items, the unit price
L0:identified in the contract at the time of delivery;
L1:(2) For cost-type or undefinitized line, subline, or exhibit line items, the
L0:Contractor’s estimated fully burdened unit cost to the Government at the time of
L0:delivery; and
L1:(3) For items produced under a time-and-materials contract, the
L0:Contractor’s estimated fully burdened unit cost to the Government at the time of
L0:delivery.
L0:“Issuing agency” means an organization responsible for assigning a globally
L0:unique identifier to an enterprise, as indicated in the Register of Issuing Agency Codes
L0:for ISO/IEC 15459, located at http://www.aimglobal.org/?Reg_Authority15459.
L0:“Issuing agency code” means a code that designates the registration (or
L0:controlling) authority for the enterprise identifier.
L0:“Item” means a single hardware article or a single unit formed by a grouping of
L0:subassemblies, components, or constituent parts.
L0:“Lot or batch number” means an identifying number assigned by the enterprise
L0:to a designated group of items, usually referred to as either a lot or a batch, all of which
L0:were manufactured under identical conditions.
L0:“Machine-readable” means an automatic identification technology media, such
L0:as bar codes, contact memory buttons, radio frequency identification, or optical memory
L0:cards.
L0:“Original part number” means a combination of numbers or letters assigned by
L0:the enterprise at item creation to a class of items with the same form, fit, function, and
L0:interface.
L0:“Parent item” means the item assembly, intermediate component, or
L0:subassembly that has an embedded item with a unique item identifier or DoD
L0:recognized unique identification equivalent.
L0:“Serial number within the enterprise identifier” means a combination of
L0:numbers, letters, or symbols assigned by the enterprise to an item that provides for the
L0:differentiation of that item from any other like and unlike item and is never used again
L0:within the enterprise.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 11
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 211
L0:“Serial number within the part, lot, or batch number” means a combination of
L0:numbers or letters assigned by the enterprise to an item that provides for the
L0:differentiation of that item from any other like item within a part, lot, or batch number
L0:assignment./
L0:“Serialization within the enterprise identifier” means each item produced is
L0:assigned a serial number that is unique among all the tangible items produced by the
L0:enterprise and is never used again. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring unique
L0:serialization within the enterprise identifier.
L0:“Serialization within the part, lot, or batch number” means each item of a
L0:particular part, lot, or batch number is assigned a unique serial number within that
L0:part, lot, or batch number assignment. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring
L0:unique serialization within the part, lot, or batch number within the enterprise
L0:identifier.
L0:“Type designation” means a combination of letters and numerals assigned by
L0:the Government to a major end item, assembly or subassembly, as appropriate, to
L0:provide a convenient means of differentiating between items having the same basic
L0:name and to indicate modifications and changes thereto.
L0:“Unique item identifier” means a set of data elements marked on items that is
L0:globally unique and unambiguous. The term includes a concatenated unique item
L0:identifier or a DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.
L0:“Unique item identifier type” means a designator to indicate which method of
L0:uniquely identifying a part has been used. The current list of accepted unique item
L0:identifier types is maintained at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/ds/unique-
L0:id.html.

L1:(i) The Contractor shall—

title: 252.211-7008 Use of Government-Assigned Serial Numbers
content:
L0:252.211-7008 Use of Government-Assigned Serial Numbers
L0:As prescribed in 211.274-5(b), use the following clause:
L0:USE OF GOVERNMENT-ASSIGNED SERIAL NUMBERS (SEP 2010)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Government-assigned serial number” means a combination of letters or
L0:numerals in a fixed human-readable information format (text) conveying information
L0:about a major end item, which is provided to a contractor by the requiring activity with
L0:accompanying technical data instructions for marking the Government-assigned serial
L0:number on major end items to be delivered to the Government.
L0:“Major end item” means a final combination of component parts and/or
L0:materials which is ready for its intended use and of such importance to operational
L0:readiness that review and control of inventory management functions (procurement,
L0:distribution, maintenance, disposal, and asset reporting) is required at all levels of life
L0:cycle management. Major end items include aircraft; ships; boats; motorized wheeled,
L0:tracked, and towed vehicles for use on highway or rough terrain; weapon and missile
L0:end items; ammunition; and sets, assemblies, or end items having a major end item as a
L0:component.
L0:“Unique item identifier (UII)” means a set of data elements permanently
L0:marked on an item that is globally unique and unambiguous and never changes in
L0:order to provide traceability of the item throughout its total life cycle. The term
L0:includes a concatenated UII or a DoD-recognized unique identification equivalent.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall mark the Government-assigned serial numbers on those
L0:major end items as specified by line item in the Schedule, in accordance with the
L0:technical instructions for the placement and method of application identified in the
L0:terms and conditions of the contract.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall register the Government-assigned serial number along with
L0:the major end item’s UII at the time of delivery in accordance with the provisions of the
L0:clause at DFARS 252.211-7003(d).
L1:(d) The Contractor shall establish the UII for major end items for use throughout
L0:the life of the major end item. The Contractor may elect, but is not required, to use the
L0:Government-assigned serial number to construct the UII.
L0:(End of clause)

L0:PGI 211.7001 Procedures.
L0:Requiring activities are responsible for developing and distributing purchase requests,
L0:except for the requirements for Military Interdepartmental Purchase Requests (MIPRs)
L0:(DD Form 448) addressed in 253.208-1 .
L1:(a) Agencies may use a combined numbering series for MIPRs and internal
L0:purchase requests, following the rules at 253.208-1 (c)(1) for both. If using a separate
L0:numbering sequence for internal purchase requests, agencies must have procedures
L0:that ensure the same number cannot be assigned to both a MIPR and an internal
L0:purchase request. Use of a purely internal tracking number in addition to the purchase
L0:request number is authorized and supported by the data standards. Number the
L0:purchase request by using—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 11
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 211
L1:(1) The requiring activity’s Department of Defense Activity Address Code
L1:(DODAAC), as described in DLM 4000.25 Volume 6, Chapter 2. DODAACs may be
L0:verified at https://home.daas.dla.mil/eDoDAAD/s_search/search_menu.asp.
L1:(2) A serial number of eight alphanumeric characters, excluding “I” and “O”; and
L1:(3) A revision number, with the original request being assigned zero and
L0:subsequent revisions or amendments being numbered consecutively.
L1:(b) Prior to taking action on a purchase request, contracting officers must ensure
L0:that the requiring activity has prepared the purchase requests in uniform contract format
L0:(see FAR 14.201-1 and 15.109), except for procurement of construction (see part 36),
L0:which should follow the current edition of the Construction Specifications Institute
L0:format. Purchase requests shall include all supporting documentation required by local
L0:contract procedures.
L1:(c) Prior to taking action on a purchase request, contracting officers must ensure that
L0:the purchase requests follow the line item rules and data requirements in
L0:DFARS 204.71 . Purchase requests for individual supplies (i.e., not bulk commodities
L0:such as oil) must identify whether the item to be acquired is subject to the item unique
L0:identification requirements of DFARS 211.274-2.
L2:(d)(1) Purchase requests may be unfunded for planning purposes, partially funded,
L0:or fully funded.
L1:(2) Funding data in purchase requests will, at a minimum, identify the following
L0:elements of the funding source: Department Code (e.g. 21 Army), Main Account (e.g.
L0:1804, Operation and Maintenance, Navy), Subaccount (where applicable), and Fiscal
L0:Year. Lists of these codes are published in Supplement 1 to Volume I of the Treasury
L0:Financial Manual, Federal Account Symbols and Titles, generally referred to as The
L0:FAST Book at https://tfx.treasury.gov/reference-books/fast-book.
L1:(3) Agencies must have sufficient procedures in place to enable traceability of
L0:line items identified in the purchase request to those in the resulting contract. In
L0:developing such procedures, agencies must ensure that provisions are made for
L0:circumstances in which the deliverables may be more completely defined during the
L0:process of soliciting offers and making an award.
L1:(e) Contracting officers must not obligate funds that have not been certified as
L0:currently available and suitable. Review purchase requests to ensure they are certified
L0:after agreement on price and prior to award to ensure that the funds are—
L1:(1) Suitable and available for the purpose and amount of the contract; and
L1:(2) Traceable from the purchase request to the resultant contract.
L1:(f) Purchase requests transmitted between requiring systems and contract writing
L0:systems must be transmitted via the Global EXchange system (GEX) using the
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 11
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 211
L0:Purchase Request Data Standard Extensible Markup Language (XML) format
L0:at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/ds/procurement-data-standard.html . Copies
L0:must be sent via the GEX to the Electronic Data Access (EDA) system
L0:at http://eda.ogden.disa.mil . Requiring systems and contract writing systems may use a
L0:format that can be translated to or from the purchase request Data Standard (XML)
L0:format.

title: 212.001-70 Applicability
content:
L0:212.001-70 Applicability.
L1:(a) FAR part 12 procedures. Use of FAR part 12 procedures is based on applicability
L0:of one of the following statutes that provide for treatment as a commercial product or
L0:commercial service and use of FAR part 12 procedures, even though the item may not
L0:meet the definition of “commercial product” or “commercial service” at FAR 2.101 and
L0:does not require a commercial product or commercial service determination:
L1:(1) 41 U.S.C. 1903 - Supplies or services to be used to facilitate defense against
L0:or recovery from cyber, nuclear, biological, chemical, or radiological attack pursuant to
L0:FAR 12.001(b).
L1:(2) 10 U.S.C. 3457 - Supplies or services from nontraditional defense
L0:contractors pursuant to paragraph (d) of this section.
L1:(3) 10 U.S.C. 3458 - Supplies or services resulting from a commercial solutions
L0:opening pursuant to subpart 212.70.
L1:(b) Prior commercial product or commercial service determinations.
L1:(1) Pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 3456(c), except as provided in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of
L0:this section or unless the item was acquired pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section, if
L0:the Commercial Item Database (for website see PGI 212.001-70(b)(A)(1) contains a prior
L0:commerciality determination, or the contracting officer has other evidence that an item
L0:has previously been acquired by DoD using commercial product and commercial service
L0:acquisition procedures under FAR part 12, then the prior contract must serve as a prior
L0:determination that an item is a commercial product or commercial service. The
L0:contracting officer must document the file accordingly.
L2:(2)(i) If the item to be acquired meets the criteria in paragraph (b)(1) of this
L0:section, the item may not be acquired using other than FAR part 12 procedures
L0:unless the head of the contracting activity issues a determination as specified in
L0:paragraph (b)(2)(ii)(B) of this section.
L1:(ii) Pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 3703(d)(1), the contracting officer may presume
L0:that a prior commercial product or commercial service determination made by a DoD
L0:department, agency, or component serves as a determination for subsequent
L0:procurements of such item. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3703(d) and 10 U.S.C.
L0:3456(c), if the contracting officer questions a prior determination to use FAR part 12
L0:procedures and instead chooses to proceed with a procurement of an item previously
L0:determined to be a commercial product or commercial service using procedures other
L0:than FAR part 12 procedures, the contracting officer must request a review by the head
L0:of the contracting activity that will conduct the procurement. Not later than 30 days
L0:after receiving a request for review, the head of the contracting activity will—
L0:appropriate and still applicable; or
L1:(A) Confirm that the prior use of FAR part 12 procedures was
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 12
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 212
L1:(B) Issue a determination that the prior use of FAR part 12 procedures
L0:was improper or that it is no longer appropriate to acquire the item using FAR part 12
L0:procedures, with a written explanation of the basis for the determination.
L1:(c) Commercial product or commercial service determination. Unless the procedures
L0:in paragraph (b) of this section are applicable, when using FAR part 12 procedures for
L0:acquisitions of commercial products and commercial services that exceed the simplified
L0:acquisition threshold, the contracting officer must—
L1:(1) Determine in writing that the acquisition meets the “commercial product” or
L0:“commercial service” definition in FAR 2.101;
L1:(2) Include the written determination in the contract file;
L1:(3) Obtain approval at one level above the contracting officer when a
L0:commercial product or commercial service determination relies on paragraphs (1)(ii),
L1:(3), or (4) of the “commercial product” definition at FAR 2.101 or paragraph (2) of the
L0:“commercial service” definition at FAR 2.101; and
L1:(4) Follow the procedures and guidance at PGI 212.001-70(b) regarding file
L0:documentation and commercial product or commercial service determinations.
L1:(d) Nontraditional defense contractors. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3457,
L0:contracting officers—
L1:(1) Except as provided in paragraph (d)(2) of this section, may treat supplies
L0:and services provided by nontraditional defense contractors as commercial products or
L0:commercial services (see PGI 212.001-70(d)(1));
L1:(2) Will treat services provided by a business unit that is a nontraditional
L0:defense contractor as commercial services, to the extent that such services use the same
L0:pool of employees as used for commercial customers and are priced using methodology
L0:similar to methodology used for commercial pricing; and
L1:(3) Will document the file when treating supplies or services from a
L0:nontraditional defense contractor as commercial products or commercial services in
L0:accordance with paragraph (d)(1) or (2) of this section.
L1:(e) Commercial item guidebook. For a link to the commercial item guidebook, see

title: 212.204 Award
content:
L0:212.204 Award.
L1:(a) Price reasonableness.
L1:(1) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3453(d), agencies must conduct or obtain
L0:market research to support the determination of the reasonableness of price for
L0:commercial products and commercial services contained in any bid or offer submitted in
L0:response to an agency solicitation. To the extent necessary to support such market
L0:research, the contracting officer—
L1:(i) In the case of major weapon systems, for subsystems of major weapon
L0:systems and components and spare parts of major weapon systems and of subsystems of
L0:major weapon systems acquired as commercial products in accordance with subpart
L0:234.70, must use information submitted under 234.7002(e); and
L1:(ii) In the case of other items, may require the offeror to submit other
L0:relevant information.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 12
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 212
L1:(2) If the contracting officer determines that the information obtained through
L0:market research pursuant to paragraph (1) of this section is insufficient to determine
L0:the reasonableness of price, the contracting officer must consider information submitted
L0:by the offeror of recent purchase prices paid by the Government and commercial
L0:customers for the same or similar commercial products or commercial services under
L0:comparable terms and conditions in establishing price reasonableness on a subsequent
L0:purchase if the contracting officer is satisfied that the prices previously paid remain a
L0:valid reference for comparison. In assessing whether the prices previously paid remain
L0:a valid reference for comparison, the contracting officer must consider the totality of
L0:other relevant factors such as the time elapsed since the prior purchase and any
L0:differences in the quantities purchased (10 U.S.C. 3703(e)).
L1:(3) If the contracting officer determines that the offeror cannot provide
L0:sufficient information as described in paragraph (2) of this section to determine the
L0:reasonableness of price, the contracting officer should request the offeror to submit
L0:information on—
L1:(i) Prices paid for the same or similar items sold under different terms and
L0:conditions;
L1:(ii) Prices paid for similar levels of work or effort on related products or
L0:services;
L1:(iii) Prices paid for alternative solutions or approaches; and
L1:(iv) Other relevant information that can serve as the basis for determining
L0:the reasonableness of price.
L1:(4) The contracting officer is not restricted from requiring the contractor to
L0:supply sufficient information to determine the reasonableness of price, regardless of
L0:whether or not the contractor was required to provide such information in connection

title: 212.401-70 General
content:
L0:212.401-70 General.
L0:See DoD Class Deviation 2024-O0011, Special Acquisition Authority for Rapid
L0:Contracting for Combatant Commanders, issued April 15, 2024. When approved in
L0:accordance with this class deviation, contracting officers may use certain temporary
L0:special acquisition authorities for covered contracts, including purchases and/or
L0:payments made with the Governmentwide commercial purchase card, that directly
L0:support covered operations through September 30, 2028. Combatant commanders will
L0:provide a written determination requesting use of the special acquisition authorities.
L0:These authorities include higher micro-purchase thresholds for purchases that directly
L0:support covered operations, as defined in the class deviation. This deviation is effective
L0:until September 30, 2028, unless otherwise rescinded.
L1:(a) Apply the prohibition at 223.7402 to purchases at or below the micro-purchase
L0:threshold.
L1:(b) See PGI 212.401-70 for guidance on use of the higher micro-purchase thresholds
L0:to support a declared contingency operation or to facilitate defense against or recovery
L0:from nuclear, biological, chemical, or radiological attack.

L1:(i) Follow the procedures at PGI 212.403(a)(1)(i)(A) for authorizing,

L1:(ii) “United States,” as used in this section, means the 50 States and the
L0:District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, the
L0:Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, Guam, American Samoa, Wake
L0:Island, Johnston Island, Canton Island, the outer Continental Shelf, and any other
L0:place subject to the jurisdiction of the United States (but not including leased bases).
L1:(iii) Use the Governmentwide commercial purchase card as the method of
L0:purchase and/or method of payment for purchases valued at or below the micro-
L0:purchase threshold. This policy applies to all types of contract actions authorized by the
L0:FAR unless—
L1:(A) The Deputy Secretary of Defense has approved an exception for an
L0:electronic commerce/electronic data interchange system or operational requirement that
L0:results in a more cost-effective payment process;

L0:accept the purchase card; and
L1:(i) The source or sources available for the supply or service do not

title: 212.7000 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:212.7000 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart implements 10 U.S.C. 3458 for the acquisition of innovative commercial
L0:products or commercial services through the use of a general solicitation known as a
L0:commercial solutions opening (CSO).

title: 212.7001 Definition
content:
L0:212.7001 Definition.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Innovative” means—
L1:(a) Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is
L0:new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or
L1:(b) Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a
L0:technology, process, or method existing as of such date.

title: 212.7002 Policy
content:
L0:212.7002 Policy.
L1:(a) Contracting officers may only use a CSO—
L1:(1) To obtain innovative solutions or potential capabilities that fulfill
L0:requirements;
L1:(2) To close capability gaps, or provide potential innovative technological
L0:advancements; and
L1:(3) When meaningful proposals with varying technical or scientific approaches
L0:can be reasonably anticipated.
L1:(b) Notwithstanding FAR 12.104, contracting officers must use fixed-price type
L0:contracts, including fixed-price incentive contracts, for awards resulting from a CSO.
L0:When using a fixed-price incentive contract, see subpart 16.4 for additional
L0:requirements.
L1:(c) Contracting officers must treat products and services acquired using a CSO as
L0:commercial products or commercial services.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 12
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 212
L1:(d) When using a CSO to acquire research and development, contracting officers
L0:must use the procedures of this subpart in conjunction with FAR part 35 and part 235.
L0:A CSO is not subject to the limitations at 235.016 and may be used to fulfill
L0:requirements for research and development, ranging from advanced component
L0:development through operational systems development.

title: 212.7003 Limitations
content:
L0:212.7003 Limitations.
L0:Contracting officers must follow the procedures at PGI 212.7003 to obtain senior
L0:procurement executive approval to award a contract in excess of $100 million resulting
L0:from a CSO.

title: 212.7004 Procedures
content:
L0:212.7004 Procedures.
L0:This section prescribes procedures for the use of a CSO.
L1:(a) The CSO must—
L1:(1) Describe the agency's interest for an individual program requirement or for
L0:broadly defined areas of interest covering the full range of the agency's requirements;
L1:(2) Specify the technical data required that may be necessary to meet DoD’s
L0:minimum requirements (see 227.7102 and 227.7202);
L1:(3) Describe the evaluation factors for selecting proposals to include—
L1:(i) Technical and importance to agency programs as the primary evaluation
L0:factors;
L1:(ii) Price to the extent appropriate, but at a minimum to determine that the
L0:price is fair and reasonable; and
L1:(iii) Relative importance of the factors, and the method of evaluation;
L1:(4) Specify the period of time during which proposals submitted in response to
L0:the CSO will be accepted; and
L1:(5) Contain instructions for the preparation and submission of proposals.
L1:(b) The contracting officer must publicize the CSO through the Governmentwide
L0:point of entry and, if authorized pursuant to FAR subpart 5.5, may also publish a notice
L0:regarding the CSO in noted scientific, technical, or engineering periodicals. The
L0:contracting officer must publish the notice at least annually.
L1:(c) Proposals received in response to the CSO must be evaluated in accordance with
L0:evaluation factors specified therein through a scientific, technological, or other subject-
L0:matter expert peer review process. Written evaluation reports on individual proposals
L0:are required, but proposals need not be evaluated against each other since they are not
L0:submitted in response to a common performance work statement or statement of work.
L1:(d) Synopsis of proposed contract actions under FAR subpart 5.1 of individual
L0:contract actions based upon proposals received in response to the CSO is not required.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 12
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 212
L0:The notice published pursuant to paragraph (b) of this section fulfills the synopsis
L0:requirement.
L1:(e) When a small business concern would otherwise be selected for award but is
L0:considered not responsible, follow the Small Business Administration Certificate of
L0:Competency procedure (see FAR subpart 19.204).
L1:(f) The contracting officer must document the decision that the requirements of this
L0:subpart have been met and include the documentation in the contract file.

title: 212.7005 Congressional notification
content:
L0:212.7005 Congressional notification.
L0:See PGI 212.7005 for congressional notification requirements for contracts valued at
L0:more than $100 million that are awarded pursuant to a CSO.

L0:Effective February 1, 2026, contracting officers shall use—

L0:Defense Pricing, Contracting, and Acquisition Policy web page at 
L0:https://www.acq.osd.mil/dpap/dars/dfarspgi/current/index.html. 
L0:This class deviation implements the following:   
L0:•  Section 2 of E.O. 14275, Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement, which 
L0:establishes the policy that the FAR “should only contain provisions required by 
L0:statute or essential to sound procurement, and any FAR provisions that do not 
L0:advance these objectives should be removed.”

L0:eliminate or revise any unnecessary supplemental regulations or any other internal 
L0:guidance, such as relevant parts of the Financial Management Regulation and 
L0:Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement. 
L0:•  The Office of Management and Budget memorandum, M-25-26 issued on 
L0:May 2, 2025, titled, Overhauling the Federal Acquisition Regulation, which 
L0:provided additional guidance to federal agencies regarding the FAR overhaul.

title: 215.103-270 Limitations and prohibitions
content:
L0:215.103-270 Limitations and prohibitions.
L0:The following limitations and prohibitions apply when considering the use of the
L0:lowest price technically acceptable source selection procedures.
L1:(a) Limitations. Section 813 of the NDAA for FY 2017 (Pub. L. 114-328) limits
L0:use of the lowest price technically acceptable source selection approach.
L1:(1) Use the lowest price technically acceptable source selection approach
L0:when—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 15
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 215
L1:(i) Minimum requirements can be described clearly and comprehensively
L0:and expressed in terms of performance objectives, measures, and standards that
L0:will be used to determine the acceptability of offers,
L1:(ii) No, or minimal, value will be realized from a proposal that exceeds
L0:the minimum technical or performance requirements,
L1:(iii) The proposed technical approaches will require no, or minimal,
L0:subjective judgment by the source selection authority as to the desirability of one
L0:offeror’s proposal versus a competing proposal,
L1:(iv) The source selection authority has a high degree of confidence that
L0:reviewing the technical proposals of all offerors would not result in the
L0:identification of characteristics that could provide value or benefit,
L1:(v) No, or minimal, additional innovation or future technological
L0:advantage will be realized by using a different source selection approach,
L1:(vi) The acquisition consists of goods that are predominantly expendable
L0:in nature, are nontechnical, or have a short life expectancy or short shelf life (See
L0:PGI 215.103.270(a)(1)(vi))
L1:(vii) The contract file contains a determination that the lowest price
L0:reflects full life-cycle costs (as defined at FAR 7.101) of the product(s) or service(s)
L0:being acquired (see PGI 215.103.270(a)(1)(vii) for information on obtaining this
L0:determination), and
L1:(viii) The contracting officer documents the contract file describing the
L0:circumstances justifying the use of the lowest price technically acceptable source
L0:selection approach.
L1:(2) Avoid using the lowest price technically acceptable source selection
L0:approach, to the maximum extent practicable, for acquisitions that are
L0:predominately for—
L1:(i) Information technology services, cybersecurity services, systems
L0:engineering and technical assistance services, advanced electronic testing, or other
L0:knowledge-based professional services;
L1:(ii) Items designated by the requiring activity as personal protective
L0:equipment (except see paragraph (b)(1) of this section); or
L1:(iii) Services designated by the requiring activity as knowledge-based
L0:training or logistics services in contingency operations or other operations outside
L0:the United States.
L1:(b) Prohibitions. Do not use the lowest price technically acceptable source
L0:selection approach to procure—
L1:(1) Items designated by the requiring activity as personal protective
L0:equipment or as an aviation critical safety item, for which the level of quality or
L0:failure of the equipment or item could result in combat casualties. (Section 814 of
L0:the NDAA for FY 2017 (Pub. L. 114-328) and section 882 of the NDAA for FY 2018
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 15
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 215
L0:(Pub. L. 115-91)). See 252.209-7010 for the definition and identification of critical
L0:safety items.
L1:(2) Engineering and manufacturing development for a major defense
L0:acquisition program (10 U.S.C. 4232).

title: 215.103-70 Source selection approach when acquiring tents or other
content:
L0:215.103-70 Source selection approach when acquiring tents or other
L0:temporary structures.
L1:(a) When acquiring tents or other temporary structures for use by the Armed
L0:Forces, award contracts that provide the best value to the Government (section 368
L0:of the NDAA for FY 2012 (Pub. L. 112-81)).
L1:(1) Temporary structures are nonpermanent buildings, including tactical
L0:shelters, nonpermanent modular or pre-fabricated buildings, or portable or
L0:relocatable buildings, such as trailers or equipment configured for occupancy (see
L0:also 246.270-2).
L1:(2) Determination of best value includes consideration of the total life-cycle
L0:costs of such tents or structures, including the costs associated with any equipment,
L0:fuel, or electricity needed to heat, cool, or light such tents or structures (see FAR
L0:7.103(a)(6) and PGI 207.104-70 (b)(1)(ii)).
L1:(b) The requirements of this section apply to any agency or department that
L0:acquires tents or other temporary structures on behalf of DoD (see FAR
L0:17.503(d)(2)).

L0:Basic. As prescribed in 215.110-70(e)(1) and (e)(1)(i), use the following provision:

L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this provision—
L0:“Market prices” means current prices that are established in the course of
L0:ordinary trade between buyers and sellers free to bargain and that can be
L0:substantiated through competition or from sources independent of the offerors.
L0:“Non-Government sales” means sales of the supplies or services to non-
L0:Governmental entities for purposes other than governmental purposes.
L0:“Relevant sales data” means information provided by an offeror on sales of the
L0:same or similar items that can be used to establish price reasonableness taking into
L0:consideration the age, volume, and nature of the transactions (including any related
L0:discounts, refunds, rebates, offsets, or other adjustments).
L0:“Sufficient non-Government sales” means relevant sales data that reflects
L0:market pricing and contains enough information to make adjustments covered by
L0:FAR 15.404-1(b)(2)(ii).
L0:“Uncertified cost data” means the subset of “data other than certified cost or
L0:pricing data” (see FAR 2.101) that relates to cost.
L1:(b) Exceptions from certified cost or pricing data.
L1:(1) In lieu of submitting certified cost or pricing data, the Offeror may
L0:submit a written request for exception by submitting the information described in
L0:paragraphs (b)(1)(i) and (ii) of this provision. The Contracting Officer may require
L0:additional supporting information, but only to the extent necessary to determine
L0:whether an exception should be granted and whether the price is fair and
L0:reasonable.

title: 215.404-170 Price analysis
content:
L0:215.404-170 Price analysis
L1:(a) In the absence of adequate price competition in response to the solicitation,
L0:pricing based on market prices is the preferred method to establish a fair and
L0:reasonable price (see PGI 215.404-170).
L1:(b) If the information obtained through market research is insufficient to
L0:determine the reasonableness of price, the contracting officer must consider
L0:information submitted by the offeror of recent purchase prices paid by the
L0:Government and commercial customers for the same or similar commercial products
L0:or commercial services under comparable terms and conditions. When establishing
L0:price reasonableness for the subsequent purchase, determine if the prices
L0:previously paid remain a valid reference for comparison. Do not base price
L0:reasonableness solely on historical prices paid by the Government (see PGI 215.403-
L0:170(a)). Consider the totality of other relevant factors such as the time elapsed
L0:since the prior purchase, any differences in the quantities purchased, or applicable
L0:terms and conditions (10 U.S.C. 3703(e)).
L1:(c) If the offeror cannot provide sufficient information as described in paragraph
L1:(b) of this section to determine the reasonableness of price, request the offeror
L0:submit information on—
L1:(1) Prices paid for the same or similar items sold under different terms and
L0:conditions;
L1:(2) Prices paid for similar levels of work or effort on related products or
L0:services;
L1:(3) Prices paid for alternative solutions or approaches; and
L1:(4) Other relevant information that can serve as the basis for determining
L0:the reasonableness of price.
L1:(d) If the pricing information submitted is not sufficient to determine the
L0:reasonableness of price, request other relevant information, to include cost data.
L0:However, no cost data may be required in any case in which there are sufficient
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 15
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 215
L0:non-Government sales of the same item to establish reasonableness of price (section
L0:831 of the NDAA for FY 2013 (Pub. L. 112-239).
L1:(e) When evaluating pricing data, consider materially differing terms and
L0:conditions, quantities, and market and economic factors (see PGI 215.404-170(e)).
L0:For similar items, consider material differences between the similar item and the
L0:item being procured (see FAR 15.404-1(b)(2)(ii)). Material differences are those that
L0:could reasonably be expected to influence the determination of price reasonableness.
L0:Consider the following factors when evaluating the relevance of the information
L0:available:
L1:(1) Market prices.
L1:(2) Age of data.
L1:(i) Whether data is too old to be relevant depends on the industry (e.g.,
L0:rapidly evolving technologies), product maturity (e.g., stable), economic factors (e.g.,
L0:new sellers in the marketplace), and various other considerations.
L1:(ii) A pending sale may be relevant if, in the judgement of the
L0:contracting officer, it is probable at the anticipated price, and the sale could
L0:reasonably be expected to materially influence the contracting officer’s
L0:determination of price reasonableness. The contracting officer may consult with the
L0:cognizant administrative contracting officers (ACOs) as they may have information
L0:about pending sales.
L1:(3) Volume and completeness of transaction data. Data must include a
L0:sufficient number of transactions to represent the range of relevant sales to all
L0:types of customers. The data must also include key information, such as date,
L0:quantity sold, part number, part nomenclature, sales price, and customer. If the
L0:number of transactions is insufficient or the data is incomplete, request additional
L0:sales data to evaluate price reasonableness. If the contractor cannot provide
L0:sufficient sales data, request other relevant information.
L1:(4) Nature of transactions. The nature of a sales transaction includes the
L0:information necessary to understand the transaction, such as terms and conditions,
L0:date, quantity sold, sale price, unique requirements, the type of customer
L0:(government, distributor, retail end-user, etc.), and related agreements. It also
L0:includes warranties, key product technical specifications, maintenance agreements,
L0:and preferred customer rewards.
L1:(f) Consider catalog prices to be reliable when they are regularly maintained
L0:and supported by relevant sales data (including any related discounts, refunds,
L0:rebates, offsets, or other adjustments). Request that the offeror support differences
L0:between the proposed price(s), catalog price(s), and relevant sales data.
L1:(g) See PGI 215.404-170(g) for assistance with commercial product, commercial
L0:service, and price reasonableness determinations.
L1:(h) When procuring a service or an end product identified by a material
L0:identifier that is available (see PGI 204.7603), consider the Supplier Performance
L0:Risk System price risk assessments in determining if a proposed price is consistent
L0:with historical prices paid for an item or otherwise creates a risk to the
L0:Government. See also 215.403-170(a).

L1:(4) Verify that relevant variables have not materially changed (e.g.,

L0:capital).
L1:(c) Profit-analysis factors. See PGI 215.404-971 through 215.404-973.

title: 215.405-470 Should-cost review
content:
L0:215.405-470 Should-cost review.
L1:(a) General. See PGI 215.405-470 for guidance on determining whether to perform
L0:a program or overhead should-cost review.
L1:(b) Program should-cost review. Major weapon system should-cost program reviews
L0:must be conducted in a manner that is transparent, objective, and provides for the
L0:efficiency of the DoD systems acquisition process (section 837 of the NDAA for FY 2018
L0:(Pub. L. 115-91)).
L1:(1) Major weapon system should-cost reviews may include the following
L0:features—
L1:(i) A thorough review of each contributing element of the program cost and
L0:the justification for each cost.
L1:(ii) An analysis of non-value added overhead and unnecessary reporting
L0:requirements.
L1:(iii) Benchmarking against similar DoD programs, similar commercial
L0:programs (where appropriate), and other programs by the same contractor at the same
L0:facility.
L1:(iv) An analysis of supply chain management to encourage competition and
L0:incentive cost performance at lower tiers.
L1:(v) A review of how to restructure the program (Government and contractor)
L0:team in a streamlined manner, if necessary.
L1:(vi) Identification of opportunities to break out Government-furnished
L0:equipment versus prime contractor-furnished materials.
L1:(vii) Identification of items or services contracted through third parties that
L0:result in unnecessary pass-through costs.
L1:(viii) Evaluation of ability to use integrated developmental and operational
L0:testing and modeling and simulation to reduce overall costs.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 15
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 215
L1:(ix) Identification of alternative technology and materials to reduce
L0:developmental or lifecycle costs for a program.
L1:(x) Identification and prioritization of cost savings opportunities.
L1:(xi) Establishment of measurable targets and ongoing tracking systems.
L1:(2) The should-cost review must provide for sufficient analysis while
L0:minimizing the impact on program schedule by engaging stakeholders early, relying on
L0:information already available before requesting additional data, and establishing a
L0:team with the relevant expertise early.
L1:(3) The should cost review team must—
L1:(i) Be comprised of members, including third-party experts if necessary,
L0:with the training, skills, and experience in analysis of cost elements, production or
L0:sustainment processes, and technologies relevant to the program under review. The
L0:review team may include members from the Defense Contract Management Agency,
L0:the department or agency’s cost analysis center, and appropriate functional
L0:organizations, as necessary.
L1:(ii) Establish a process for communicating and collaborating with the
L0:contractor throughout the should-cost review, including notification to the contractor
L0:regarding which elements of the contractor’s operations will be reviewed and what
L0:information will be necessary to perform the review, as soon as practicable, both prior to
L0:and during the review.
L1:(iii) Prepare a report, which must ensure, to the maximum extent
L0:practicable, review of current, accurate, and complete data, and identify cost savings
L0:opportunities associated with specific engineering or business changes that can be
L0:quantified and tracked.

title: 252.215-7002 Cost Estimating System Requirements
content:
L0:252.215-7002 Cost Estimating System Requirements.
L0:As prescribed in 215.110-70(a), use the following clause:
L0:COST ESTIMATING SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS (JAN 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions.
L0:“Acceptable estimating system” means an estimating system that complies with
L0:the system criteria in paragraph (d) of this clause, and provides for a system that—
L1:(1) Is maintained, reliable, and consistently applied;
L1:(2) Produces verifiable, supportable, documented, and timely cost estimates
L0:that are an acceptable basis for negotiation of fair and reasonable prices;
L1:(3) Is consistent with and integrated with the Contractor’s related
L0:management systems; and
L1:(4) Is subject to applicable financial control systems.
L0:“Estimating system” means the Contractor's policies, procedures, and practices
L0:for budgeting and planning controls, and generating estimates of costs and other
L0:data included in proposals submitted to customers in the expectation of receiving
L0:contract awards. Estimating system includes the Contractor's—
L1:(1) Organizational structure;
L1:(2) Established lines of authority, duties, and responsibilities;
L1:(3) Internal controls and managerial reviews;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 15
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 215
L1:(4) Flow of work, coordination, and communication; and
L1:(5) Budgeting, planning, estimating methods, techniques, accumulation of
L0:historical costs, and other analyses used to generate cost estimates.
L0:“Material weakness” means a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the
L0:internal control over information in contractor business systems, such that there is
L0:a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of such information will not
L0:be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A reasonable possibility
L0:exists when the likelihood of an event occurring is—
L1:(1) Probable; or
L1:(2) More than remote but less than likely (Section 806 of Pub. L. 116-283).
L1:(b) General. The Contractor shall establish, maintain, and comply with an
L0:acceptable estimating system.
L1:(c) Applicability. Paragraphs (d) and (e) of this clause apply if the Contractor is
L0:a large business and either—
L1:(1) In its fiscal year preceding award of this contract, received Department
L0:of Defense (DoD) prime contracts or subcontracts, totaling $50 million or more for
L0:which certified cost or pricing data were required; or
L1:(2) In its fiscal year preceding award of this contract—
L1:(i) Received DoD prime contracts or subcontracts totaling $10 million or
L0:more (but less than $50 million) for which certified cost or pricing data were
L0:required; and
L1:(ii) Was notified, in writing, by the Contracting Officer that paragraphs
L1:(d) and (e) of this clause apply.
L1:(d) System requirements.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall disclose its estimating system to the
L0:Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO), in writing. If the Contractor wishes the
L0:Government to protect the data and information as privileged or confidential, the
L0:Contractor must mark the documents with the appropriate legends before
L0:submission.
L1:(2) An estimating system disclosure is acceptable when the Contractor has
L0:provided the ACO with documentation that—
L1:(i) Accurately describes those policies, procedures, and practices that the
L0:Contractor currently uses in preparing cost proposals; and
L1:(ii) Provides sufficient detail for the Government to reasonably make an
L0:informed judgment regarding the acceptability of the Contractor's estimating
L0:practices.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 15
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 215
L1:(3) The Contractor shall—
L1:(i) Comply with its disclosed estimating system; and
L1:(ii) Disclose significant changes to the cost estimating system to the
L0:ACO on a timely basis.
L1:(4) The Contractor’s estimating system shall provide for the use of
L0:appropriate source data, utilize sound estimating techniques and good judgment,
L0:maintain a consistent approach, and adhere to established policies and procedures.
L0:An acceptable estimating system shall accomplish the following functions:
L1:(i) Establish clear responsibility for preparation, review, and approval of
L0:cost estimates and budgets.
L1:(ii) Provide a written description of the organization and duties of the
L0:personnel responsible for preparing, reviewing, and approving cost estimates and
L0:budgets.
L1:(iii) Ensure that relevant personnel have sufficient training, experience,
L0:and guidance to perform estimating and budgeting tasks in accordance with the
L0:Contractor's established procedures.
L1:(iv) Identify and document the sources of data and the estimating
L0:methods and rationale used in developing cost estimates and budgets.
L1:(v) Provide for adequate supervision throughout the estimating and
L0:budgeting process.
L1:(vi) Provide for consistent application of estimating and budgeting
L0:techniques.
L1:(vii) Provide for detection and timely correction of errors.
L1:(viii) Protect against cost duplication and omissions.
L1:(ix) Provide for the use of historical experience, including historical
L0:vendor pricing data, where appropriate.
L1:(x) Require use of appropriate analytical methods.
L1:(xi) Integrate data and information available from other management
L0:systems.
L1:(xii) Require management review, including verification of compliance
L0:with the company's estimating and budgeting policies, procedures, and practices.
L1:(xiii) Provide for internal review of, and accountability for, the
L0:acceptability of the estimating system, including the budgetary data supporting
L0:indirect cost estimates and comparisons of projected results to actual results, and
L0:an analysis of any differences.
L1:(xiv) Provide procedures to update cost estimates and notify the
L0:Contracting Officer in a timely manner throughout the negotiation process.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 15
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 215
L1:(xv) Provide procedures that ensure subcontract prices are reasonable
L0:based on a documented review and analysis provided with the prime proposal, when
L0:practicable.
L1:(xvi) Provide estimating and budgeting practices that consistently
L0:generate sound proposals that are compliant with the provisions of the solicitation
L0:and are adequate to serve as a basis to reach a fair and reasonable price.
L1:(xvii) Have an adequate system description, including policies,
L0:procedures, and estimating and budgeting practices, that comply with the Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement.
L1:(e) Material weaknesses.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer will provide an initial determination to the
L0:Contractor, in writing, of any material weaknesses. The initial determination will
L0:describe the underlying deficiency in sufficient detail to allow the Contractor to
L0:understand the weakness or deficiency.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial
L0:determination from the Contracting Officer that identifies material weaknesses in
L0:the Contractor's estimating system. If the Contractor disagrees with the initial
L0:determination, the Contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.
L1:(3) The Contracting Officer will evaluate the Contractor's response and
L0:notify the Contractor, in writing, of the Contracting Officer’s final determination
L0:concerning—
L1:(i) Remaining material weaknesses;
L1:(ii) The adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action; and
L1:(iii) System disapproval, if the Contracting Officer determines that one
L0:or more material weaknesses remain.
L1:(f) If the Contractor receives the Contracting Officer’s final determination of
L0:material weaknesses, the Contractor shall, within 45 days of receipt of the final
L0:determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable
L0:corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the material
L0:weaknesses.
L1:(g) Withholding payments. If the Contracting Officer makes a final
L0:determination to disapprove the Contractor’s estimating system, and the contract
L0:includes the clause at 252.242-7005, Contractor Business Systems, the Contracting
L0:Officer will withhold payments in accordance with that clause.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 15
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 215

title: 252.215-7014 Exception from Certified Cost or Pricing Data Requirements
content:
L0:252.215-7014 Exception from Certified Cost or Pricing Data Requirements
L0:for Foreign Military Sales Indirect Offsets.
L0:As prescribed in 215.110-70(g), use the following clause:
L0:EXCEPTION FROM CERTIFIED COST OR PRICING DATA REQUIREMENTS FOR
L0:FOREIGN MILITARY SALES INDIRECT OFFSETS (DEC 2022)
L1:(a) Definition. As used in this clause—
L0:“Offset” means a benefit or obligation agreed to by a contractor and a foreign
L0:government or international organization as an inducement or condition to purchase
L0:supplies or services pursuant to a foreign military sale (FMS). There are two types of
L0:offsets: direct offsets and indirect offsets.
L1:(1) A direct offset involves benefits or obligations, including supplies or services
L0:that are directly related to the item being purchased and are integral to the deliverable
L0:of the FMS contract. For example, as a condition of a foreign military sale, the
L0:contractor may require or agree to permit the customer to produce in its country certain
L0:components or subsystems of the item being sold. Generally, direct offsets must be
L0:performed within a specified period, because they are integral to the deliverable of the
L0:FMS contract.
L1:(2) An indirect offset involves benefits or obligations, including supplies or
L0:services that are not directly related to the specific item(s) being purchased and are not
L0:integral to the deliverable of the FMS contract. For example, as a condition of a foreign
L0:military sale, the contractor may agree to purchase certain manufactured products,
L0:agricultural commodities, raw materials, or services, or make an equity investment or
L0:grant of equipment required by the FMS customer, or may agree to build a school, road
L0:or other facility. Indirect offsets would also include projects that are related to the FMS
L0:contract but not purchased under said contract (e.g., a project to develop or advance a
L0:capability, technology transfer, or know-how in a foreign company). Indirect offsets
L0:may be accomplished without a clearly defined period of performance.
L1:(b) Exceptions from certified cost or pricing data requirements. Notwithstanding the
L0:requirements of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.215-20, Requirements for
L0:Certified Cost or Pricing Data and Data Other Than Certified Cost or Pricing Data, in
L0:the case of this contract or a subcontract, and FAR 52.215-21, Requirements for
L0:Certified Cost or Pricing Data and Data Other Than Certified Cost or Pricing Data—
L0:Modifications, in the case of modification of this contract or a subcontract, submission of
L0:certified cost or pricing data shall not be required to the extent such data relates to an
L0:indirect offset (10 U.S.C. 3703(a)(4)).
L0:(End of clause)

L1:(1) The weighted guidelines method focuses on four profit factors—
L1:(i) Performance risk,

L1:(2) Assign values to each profit factor; the value multiplied by the base results in the
L0:profit objective for that factor. Except for the cost efficiency special factor, each profit factor

L0:average conditions on the prospective contract when compared to all goods and services
L0:acquired by DoD. The designated range provides values based on above normal or below
L0:normal conditions. In the price negotiation documentation, address conditions that justify
L0:assignment of other than the normal value. The cost efficiency special factor has no normal
L0:value. Exercise sound business judgment in selecting a value when this special factor is
L0:used (see 215.404-971(e)).
L1:(b) Performance risk.

L0:fulfilling the contract requirements. The factor consists of two parts:
L1:(i) Technical--the technical uncertainties of performance.
L1:(ii) Management/cost control--the degree of management effort necessary—
L1:(A) To ensure that contract requirements are met; and
L1:(B) To reduce and control costs.

L0:216.301-3 Limitations.

content: L0:216.304 Cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts.

title: 216.304-2 Limitations
content:
L0:216.304-2 Limitations.
L0:For contracts in connection with a military construction project or military family
L0:housing project, see the prohibition at 216.301-3.
L1:(1) Except as provided in paragraph (2) of this section, annual military
L0:construction appropriations acts prohibit the use of cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts that—
L1:(i) Are funded by a military construction appropriations act;
L1:(ii) Are estimated to exceed $25,000; and
L1:(iii) Will be performed within the United States, except Alaska.
L1:(2) The prohibition in paragraph (1) of this section does not apply to a contract if
L0:it is specifically approved in writing. That written approval must explain the reasons
L0:for granting an exception and follow the approval process described below:
L1:(i) The Secretaries of the military departments are authorized to approve
L0:such contracts that are for environmental work only, provided the environmental work
L0:is not classified as construction, as defined by 10 U.S.C. 2801.
L1:(ii) The Secretary of Defense or designee must approve such contracts that
L0:are not for environmental work only or are for environmental work classified as
L0:construction.
