title: 252.217-7001 Surge Option
content:
L0:252.217-7001 Surge Option.
L0:As prescribed in 217.203-70(b), use the following clause:
L0:SURGE OPTION (DEC 2018)
L1:(a) General. The Government has the option to—
L1:(1) Increase the quantity of supplies or services called for under this contract by
L0:no more than ___ percent or _______________ [insert quantity and description of services
L0:or supplies to be increased]; and/or
L1:(2) Accelerate the rate of delivery called for under this contract, at a price or
L0:cost established before contract award or to be established by negotiation as provided in
L0:this clause.
L1:(b) Schedule.
L1:(1) When the Capabilities Analysis Plan (CAP) is included in the contract, the
L0:option delivery schedule shall be the production rate provided with the Plan. If the
L0:Plan was negotiated before contract award, then the negotiated schedule shall be used.
L1:(2) If there is no CAP in the contract, the Contractor shall, within 30 days from
L0:the date of award, furnish the Contracting Officer a delivery schedule showing the
L0:maximum sustainable rate of delivery for items in this contract. This delivery schedule
L0:shall provide acceleration by month up to the maximum sustainable rate of delivery
L0:achievable within the Contractor's existing facilities, equipment, and subcontracting
L0:structure.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall not revise the option delivery schedule without
L0:approval from the Contracting Officer.
L1:(c) Exercise of option.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer may exercise this option at any time before
L0:acceptance by the Government of the final scheduled delivery.
L1:(2) The Contracting Officer will provide a preliminary oral or written notice to
L0:the Contractor stating the quantities to be added or accelerated under the terms of this
L0:clause, followed by a contract modification incorporating the transmitted information
L0:and instructions. The notice and modification will establish a not-to-exceed price equal
L0:to the highest contract unit price or cost of the added or accelerated items as of the date
L0:of the notice.
L1:(3) The Contractor will not be required to deliver at a rate greater than the
L0:maximum sustainable delivery rate under paragraph (b)(2) of this clause, nor will the
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L0:exercise of this option extend delivery more than 24 months beyond the scheduled final
L0:delivery.
L1:(d) Price negotiation.
L1:(1) Unless the option cost or price was previously agreed upon, the Contractor
L0:shall, within 30 days from the date of option exercise, submit to the Contracting Officer
L0:a cost or price proposal (including a cost breakdown) for the added or accelerated items.
L1:(2) Failure to agree on a cost or price in negotiations resulting from the exercise
L0:of this option shall constitute a dispute concerning a question of fact within the meaning
L0:of the Disputes clause of this contract. However, nothing in this clause shall excuse the
L0:Contractor from proceeding with the performance of the contract, as modified, while any
L0:resulting claim is being settled.

title: 252.217-7003 Changes
content:
L0:252.217-7003 Changes.

L0:CHANGES (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Contracting Officer may, at any time and without notice to the sureties, by
L0:written change order, make changes within the general scope of any job order issued
L0:under the Master Agreement in—

L1:(2) Work itemized;

L1:(4) Time of commencement or completion of the work; and

L1:(b) If a change causes an increase or decrease in the cost of, or time required for,
L0:performance of the job order, whether or not changed by the order, the Contracting
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L0:Officer shall make an equitable adjustment in the price or date of completion, or both,

L1:(1) Within ten days after the Contractor receives notification of the change, the

L1:(d) Failure to agree to any adjustment shall be a dispute within the meaning of the

L0:order as changed.

content:
L0:252.217-7004 Job Orders and Compensation.

L0:JOB ORDERS AND COMPENSATION (MAY 2006)
L1:(a) The Contracting Officer shall solicit bids or proposals and make award of job
L0:orders. The issuance of a job order signed by the Contracting Officer constitutes award.
L0:The job order shall incorporate the terms and conditions of the Master Agreement.
L1:(b) Whenever the Contracting Officer determines that a vessel, its cargo or stores,
L0:would be endangered by delay, or whenever the Contracting Officer determines that
L0:military necessity requires that immediate work on a vessel is necessary, the
L0:Contracting Officer may issue a written order to perform that work and the Contractor
L0:hereby agrees to comply with that order and to perform work on such vessel within its
L0:capabilities.
L1:(1) As soon as practicable after the issuance of the order, the Contracting
L0:Officer and the Contractor shall negotiate a price for the work and the Contracting
L0:Officer shall issue a job order covering the work.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall, upon request, furnish the Contracting Officer with a
L0:breakdown of costs incurred by the Contractor and an estimate of costs expected to be
L0:incurred in the performance of the work. The Contractor shall maintain, and make
L0:available for inspection by the Contracting Officer or the Contracting Officer's
L0:representative, records supporting the cost of performing the work.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L1:(3) Failure of the parties to agree upon the price of the work shall constitute a
L0:dispute within the meaning of the Disputes clause of the Master Agreement. In the

L2:(c)(1) If the nature of any repairs is such that their extent and probable cost cannot

title: 252.217-7005 Inspection and Manner of Doing Work
content:
L0:252.217-7005 Inspection and Manner of Doing Work.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104(a), use the following clause:
L0:(End of clause)
L0:INSPECTION AND MANNER OF DOING WORK (JUL 2009)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall perform work in accordance with the job order, any
L0:drawings and specifications made a part of the job order, and any change or
L0:modification issued under the Changes clause of the Master Agreement.
L2:(b)(1) Except as provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this clause, and unless otherwise
L0:specifically provided in the job order, all operational practices of the Contractor and all
L0:workmanship, material, equipment, and articles used in the performance of work under
L0:the Master Agreement shall be in accordance with the best commercial marine
L0:practices and the rules and requirements of the American Bureau of Shipping, the U.S.
L0:Coast Guard, and the Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers, in effect at the
L0:time of Contractor's submission of bid (or acceptance of the job order, if negotiated).
L1:(2) When Navy specifications are specified in the job order, the Contractor shall
L0:follow Navy standards of material and workmanship. The solicitation shall prescribe
L0:the Navy standard whenever applicable.
L1:(c) The Government may inspect and test all material and workmanship at any
L0:time during the Contractor's performance of the work.
L1:(1) If, prior to delivery, the Government finds any material or workmanship is
L0:defective or not in accordance with the job order, in addition to its rights under the
L0:Guarantees clause of the Master Agreement, the Government may reject the defective
L0:or nonconforming material or workmanship and require the Contractor to correct or
L0:replace it at the Contractor's expense.
L1:(2) If the Contractor fails to proceed promptly with the replacement or
L0:correction of the material or workmanship, the Government may replace or correct the
L0:defective or nonconforming material or workmanship and charge the Contractor the
L0:excess costs incurred.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L1:(3) As specified in the job order, the Contractor shall provide and maintain an
L0:inspection system acceptable to the Government.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall maintain complete records of all inspection work and
L0:shall make them available to the Government during performance of the job order and
L0:for 90 days after the completion of all work required.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall not permit any welder to work on a vessel unless the
L0:welder is, at the time of the work, qualified to the standards established by the U.S.
L0:Coast Guard, American Bureau of Shipping, or Department of the Navy for the type of
L0:welding being performed. Qualifications of a welder shall be as specified in the job
L0:order.
L1:(e) The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Exercise reasonable care to protect the vessel from fire;
L1:(2) Maintain a reasonable system of inspection over activities taking place in
L0:the vicinity of the vessel's magazines, fuel oil tanks, or storerooms containing flammable
L0:materials;
L1:(3) Maintain a reasonable number of hose lines ready for immediate use on the
L0:vessel at all times while the vessel is berthed alongside the Contractor's pier or in dry
L0:dock or on a marine railway;
L1:(4) Unless otherwise provided in a job order, provide sufficient security patrols
L0:to reasonably maintain a fire watch for protection of the vessel when it is in the
L0:Contractor's custody;
L1:(5) To the extent necessary, clean, wash, and steam out or otherwise make safe,
L0:all tanks under alteration or repair;
L1:(6) Furnish the Contracting Officer or designated representative with a copy of
L0:the “gas-free” or “safe-for-hotwork” certificate, provided by a Marine Chemist or Coast
L0:Guard authorized person in accordance with Occupational Safety and Health
L0:Administration regulations (29 CFR 1915.14) before any hot work is done on a tank;
L1:(7) Treat the contents of any tank as Government property in accordance with
L0:the Government Property clause; and
L1:(8) Dispose of the contents of any tank only at the direction, or with the
L0:concurrence, of the Contracting Officer.
L1:(f) Except as otherwise provided in the job order, when the vessel is in the custody of
L0:the Contractor or in dry dock or on a marine railway and the temperature is expected to
L0:go as low as 35 oF, the Contractor shall take all necessary steps to—
L1:(1) Keep all hose pipelines, fixtures, traps, tanks, and other receptacles on the
L0:vessel from freezing; and
L1:(2) Protect the stern tube and propeller hubs from frost damage.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L1:(g) The Contractor shall, whenever practicable—
L1:(1) Perform the required work in a manner that will not interfere with the
L0:berthing and messing of Government personnel attached to the vessel; and
L1:(2) Provide Government personnel attached to the vessel access to the vessel at
L0:all times.
L1:(h) Government personnel attached to the vessel shall not interfere with the
L0:Contractor's work or workers.
L2:(i)(1) The Government does not guarantee the correctness of the dimensions, sizes,
L0:and shapes set forth in any job order, sketches, drawings, plans, or specifications
L0:prepared or furnished by the Government, unless the job order requires that the
L0:Contractor perform the work prior to any opportunity to inspect.
L1:(2) Except as stated in paragraph (i)(1) of this clause, and other than those
L0:parts furnished by the Government, the Contractor shall be responsible for the
L0:correctness of the dimensions, sizes, and shapes of parts furnished under this
L0:agreement.
L1:(j) The Contractor shall at all times keep the site of the work on the vessel free from
L0:accumulation of waste material or rubbish caused by its employees or the work. At the
L0:completion of the work, unless the job order specifies otherwise, the Contractor shall
L0:remove all rubbish from the site of the work and leave the immediate vicinity of the
L0:work area “broom clean.”
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.217-7009 Default
content:
L0:252.217-7009 Default.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104(a), use the following clause:
L0:DEFAULT (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Government may, subject to the provisions of paragraph (b) of this clause,
L0:by written notice of default to the Contractor, terminate the whole or any part of a job
L0:order if the Contractor fails to—
L1:(1) Make delivery of the supplies or to perform the services within the time
L0:specified in a job order or any extension;
L1:(2) Make progress, so as to endanger performance of the job order; or
L1:(3) Perform any of the other provisions of this agreement or a job order.
L1:(b) Except for defaults of subcontractors, the Contractor shall not be liable for any
L0:excess costs if failure to perform the job order arises from causes beyond the control and
L0:without the fault or negligence of the Contractor. Examples of such causes include acts
L0:of God or of the public enemy, acts of the Government in either its sovereign or
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L0:contractual capacity, fires, floods, epidemics, quarantine restrictions, strikes, freight
L0:embargoes, and unusually severe weather.
L1:(c) If the Contractor's failure to perform is caused by the default of a subcontractor,
L0:and if such default arises out of causes beyond the control of both the Contractor and
L0:subcontractor, and without the fault or negligence of either, the Contractor shall not be
L0:liable for any excess costs for failure to perform, unless the supplies or services to be
L0:furnished by the subcontractor were obtainable from other sources in sufficient time to
L0:permit the Contractor to perform the job order within the time specified.
L1:(d) If the Government terminates the job order in whole or in part as provided in
L0:paragraph (a) of this clause—
L1:(1) The Government may, upon such terms and in such manner as the
L0:Contracting Officer may deem appropriate, arrange for the completion of the work so
L0:terminated, at such plant or plants, including that of the Contractor, as may be
L0:designated by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall continue the performance of the job order to the
L0:extent not terminated under the provisions of this clause.
L1:(ii) If the work is to be completed at the plant, the Government may use all
L0:tools, machinery, facilities, and equipment of the Contractor determined by the
L0:Contracting Office to be necessary for that purpose.
L1:(iii) If the cost to the Government of the work procured or completed (after
L0:adjusting such cost to exclude the effect of changes in the plans and specifications made
L0:subsequent to the date of termination) exceeds the price fixed for work under the job
L0:order (after adjusting such price on account of changes in the plans and specifications
L0:made before the date of termination), the Contractor, or the Contractor's surety, if any,
L0:shall be liable for such excess.
L1:(2) The Government, in addition to any other rights provided in this clause,
L0:may require the Contractor to transfer title and delivery to the Government, in the
L0:manner and to the extent directed by the Contracting Officer, any completed supplies
L0:and such partially completed supplies and materials, parts, tools, dies, jigs, fixtures,
L0:plans, drawings, information and contract rights (hereinafter called “manufacturing
L0:materials”) as the Contractor has specifically produced or specifically acquired for the
L0:performance of the terminated part of the job order.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall, upon direction of the Contracting Officer, protect
L0:and preserve property in possession of the Contractor in which the Government has an
L0:interest.
L1:(ii) The Government shall pay to the Contractor the job order price for
L0:completed items of work delivered to and accepted by the Government, and the amount
L0:agreed upon by the Contractor and the Contracting Officer for manufacturing materials
L0:delivered to and accepted by the Government, and for the protection and preservation of
L0:property. Failure to agree shall be a dispute concerning a question of fact within the
L0:meaning of the Disputes clause.
L1:(e) If, after notice of termination of the job order, it is determined that the
L0:Contractor was not in default, or that the default was excusable, the rights and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L0:obligations of the parties shall be the same as if the notice of termination had been
L0:issued for the convenience of the Government.
L1:(f) If the Contractor fails to complete the performance of a job order within the time
L0:specified, or any extension, the actual damage to the Government for the delay will be
L0:difficult or impossible to determine.
L1:(1) In lieu of actual damage, the Contractor shall pay to the Government as
L0:fixed, agreed, and liquidated damages for each calendar day of delay the amount, if any,
L0:set forth in the job order (prorated to the nearest hour for fractional days).
L1:(2) If the Government terminates the job order, the Contractor shall be liable, in
L0:addition to the excess costs provided in paragraph (d) of this clause, for liquidated
L0:damages accruing until such time as the Government may reasonably obtain
L0:completion of the work.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall not be charged with liquidated damages when the
L0:delay arises out of causes beyond the control and without the fault or negligence of the
L0:Contractor. Subject to the provisions of the Disputes clause of the Master Agreement,
L0:the Contracting Officer shall ascertain the facts and the extent of the delay and shall
L0:extend the time for performance when in the judgment of the Contracting Officer, the
L0:findings of fact justify an extension.
L1:(g) The rights and remedies of the Government provided in this clause shall not be
L0:exclusive and are in addition to any other rights and remedies provided by law under
L0:this agreement.

title: 252.217-7010 Performance
content:
L0:252.217-7010 Performance.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104(a), use the following clause:
L0:(End of clause)
L0:PERFORMANCE (JUL 2009)
L1:(a) Upon the award of a job order, the Contractor shall promptly start the work
L0:specified and shall diligently prosecute the work to completion. The Contractor shall
L0:not start work until the job order has been awarded except in the case of emergency
L0:work ordered by the Contracting Officer under the Job Orders and Compensation
L0:clause of the Master Agreement.
L1:(b) The Government shall deliver the vessel described in the job order at the time
L0:and location specified in the job order. Upon completion of the work, the Government
L0:shall accept delivery of the vessel at the time and location specified in the job order.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall, without charge and without specific requirement in a job
L0:order—
L1:(1) Make available at the plant to personnel of the vessel while in dry dock or on
L0:a marine railway, sanitary lavatory and similar facilities acceptable to the Contracting
L0:Officer;
L1:(2) Supply and maintain suitable brows and gangways from the pier, dry dock,
L0:or marine railway to the vessel;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L1:(3) Treat salvage, scrap or other ship's material of the Government resulting
L0:from performance of the work as items of Government-furnished property, in
L0:accordance with the Government Property clause;
L1:(4) Perform, or pay the cost of, any repair, reconditioning or replacement made
L0:necessary as the result of the use by the Contractor of any of the vessel's machinery,
L0:equipment or fittings, including, but not limited to, winches, pumps, rigging, or
L0:pipelines; and
L1:(5) Furnish suitable offices, office equipment and telephones at or near the site
L0:of the work for the Government's use.
L1:(d) The job order will state whether dock and sea trials are required to determine
L0:whether or not the Contractor has satisfactorily performed the work.
L1:(1) If dock and sea trials are required, the vessel shall be under the control of
L0:the vessel's commander and crew.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall not conduct dock and sea trials not specified in the job
L0:order without advance approval of the Contracting Officer. Dock and sea trials not
L0:specified in the job order shall be at the Contractor's expense and risk.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall provide and install all fittings and appliances
L0:necessary for dock and sea trials. The Contractor shall be responsible for care,
L0:installation, and removal of instruments and apparatus furnished by the Government
L0:for use in the trials.

title: 252.217-7012 Liability and Insurance
content:
L0:252.217-7012 Liability and Insurance.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104(a), use the following clause:
L0:LIABILITY AND INSURANCE (AUG 2003)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall exercise its best efforts to prevent accidents, injury, or
L0:damage to all employees, persons, and property, in and about the work, and to the
L0:vessel or part of the vessel upon which work is done.
L1:(b) Loss or damage to the vessel, materials, or equipment.
L1:(1) Unless otherwise directed or approved in writing by the Contracting Officer,
L0:the Contractor shall not carry insurance against any form of loss or damage to the
L0:vessel(s) or to the materials or equipment to which the Government has title or which
L0:have been furnished by the Government for installation by the Contractor. The
L0:Government assumes the risks of loss of and damage to that property.
L1:(2) The Government does not assume any risk with respect to loss or damage
L0:compensated for by insurance or otherwise or resulting from risks with respect to which
L0:the Contractor has failed to maintain insurance, if available, as required or approved by
L0:the Contracting Officer.
L1:(3) The Government does not assume risk of and will not pay for any costs of
L0:the following:
L1:(i) Inspection, repair, replacement, or renewal of any defects in the vessel(s)
L0:or material and equipment due to—
L0:subcontractors;
L1:(A) Defective workmanship performed by the Contractor or its
L0:subcontracts; or
L1:(B) Defective materials or equipment furnished by the Contractor or its
L1:(C) Workmanship, materials, or equipment which do not conform to the
L0:requirements of the contract, whether or not the defect is latent or whether or not the
L0:nonconformance is the result of negligence.
L1:(ii) Loss, damage, liability, or expense caused by, resulting from, or incurred
L0:as a consequence of any delay or disruption, willful misconduct or lack of good faith by
L0:the Contractor or any of its representatives that have supervision or direction of—
L1:(A) All or substantially all of the Contractor's business; or
L1:(B) All or substantially all of the Contractor's operation at any one
L0:plant.
L1:(4) As to any risk that is assumed by the Government, the Government shall be
L0:subrogated to any claim, demand or cause of action against third parties that exists in
L0:favor of the Contractor. If required by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall
L0:execute a formal assignment or transfer of the claim, demand, or cause of action.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L1:(5) No party other than the Contractor shall have any right to proceed directly
L0:against the Government or join the Government as a co-defendant in any action.
L1:(6) Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Contractor shall bear the first $50,000 of
L0:loss or damage from each occurrence or incident, the risk of which the Government
L0:would have assumed under the provisions of this paragraph (b).
L1:(c) Indemnification. The Contractor indemnifies the Government and the vessel
L0:and its owners against all claims, demands, or causes of action to which the
L0:Government, the vessel or its owner(s) might be subject as a result of damage or injury
L0:(including death) to the property or person of anyone other than the Government or its
L0:employees, or the vessel or its owner, arising in whole or in part from the negligence or
L0:other wrongful act of the Contractor or its agents or employees, or any subcontractor, or
L0:its agents or employees.
L1:(1) The Contractor's obligation to indemnify under this paragraph shall not
L0:exceed the sum of $300,000 as a consequence of any single occurrence with respect to
L0:any one vessel.
L1:(2) The indemnity includes, without limitation, suits, actions, claims, costs, or
L0:demands of any kind, resulting from death, personal injury, or property damage
L0:occurring during the period of performance of work on the vessel or within 90 days after
L0:redelivery of the vessel. For any claim, etc., made after 90 days, the rights of the parties
L0:shall be as determined by other provisions of this agreement and by law. The
L0:indemnity does apply to death occurring after 90 days where the injury was received
L0:during the period covered by the indemnity.
L1:(d) Insurance.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall, at its own expense, obtain and maintain the following
L0:insurance—
L1:(i) Casualty, accident, and liability insurance, as approved by the
L0:Contracting Officer, insuring the performance of its obligations under paragraph (c) of
L0:this clause.
L1:(ii) Workers Compensation Insurance (or its equivalent) covering the
L0:employees engaged on the work.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall ensure that all subcontractors engaged on the work
L0:obtain and maintain the insurance required in paragraph (d)(1) of this clause.
L1:(3) Upon request of the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall provide
L0:evidence of the insurance required by paragraph (d) of this clause.
L1:(e) The Contractor shall not make any allowance in the job order price for the
L0:inclusion of any premium expense or charge for any reserve made on account of self-
L0:insurance for coverage against any risk assumed by the Government under this clause.
L1:(f) The Contractor shall give the Contracting Officer written notice as soon as
L0:practicable after the occurrence of a loss or damage for which the Government has
L0:assumed the risk.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L1:(1) The notice shall contain full details of the loss or damage.
L1:(2) If a claim or suit is later filed against the Contractor as a result of the event,
L0:the Contractor shall immediately deliver to the Government every demand, notice,
L0:summons, or other process received by the Contractor or its employees or
L0:representatives.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall cooperate with the Government and, upon request,
L0:shall assist in effecting settlements, securing and giving evidence, obtaining the
L0:attendance of witnesses, and in the conduct of suits. The Government shall reimburse
L0:the Contractor for expenses incurred in this effort, other than the cost of maintaining
L0:the Contractor's usual organization.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall not, except at its own expense, voluntarily make any
L0:payment, assume any obligation, or incur any expense other than what would be
L0:imperative for the protection of the vessel(s) at the time of the event.
L1:(g) In the event or loss of or damage to any vessel(s), material, or equipment which
L0:may result in a claim against the Government under the insurance provisions of this
L0:contract, the Contractor shall promptly notify the Contracting Officer of the loss or
L0:damage. The Contracting Officer may, without prejudice to any other right of the
L0:Government, either—
L1:(1) Order the Contractor to proceed with replacement or repair, in which event
L0:the Contractor shall effect the replacement or repair;
L1:(i) The Contractor shall submit to the Contracting Officer a request for
L0:reimbursement of the cost of the replacement or repair together with whatever
L0:supporting documentation the Contracting Officer may reasonably require, and shall
L0:identify the request as being submitted under the Insurance clause of the agreement.
L1:(ii) If the Government determines that the risk of the loss or damage is
L0:within the scope of the risks assumed by the Government under this clause, the
L0:Government will reimburse the Contractor for the reasonable, allowable cost of the
L0:replacement or repair, plus a reasonable profit (if the work or replacement or repair was
L0:performed by the Contractor) less the deductible amount specified in paragraph (b) of
L0:this clause.
L1:(iii) Payments by the Government to the Contractor under this clause are
L0:outside the scope of and shall not affect the pricing structure of the contract, and are
L0:additional to the compensation otherwise payable to the Contractor under this contract;
L0:or
L1:(2) In the event the Contracting Officer decides that the loss or damage shall
L0:not be replaced or repaired, the Contracting Officer shall—
L1:(i) Modify the contract appropriately, consistent with the reduced
L0:requirements reflected by the unreplaced or unrepaired loss or damage; or
L1:(ii) Terminate the repair of any part or all of the vessel(s) under the
L0:Termination for Convenience of the Government clause of this agreement.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217

title: 252.217-7013 Guarantees
content:
L0:252.217-7013 Guarantees.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104(a), use the following clause:
L0:GUARANTEES (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) In the event any work performed or materials furnished by the contractor under
L0:the Master Agreement prove defective or deficient within 90 days from the date of
L0:redelivery of the vessel(s), the Contractor, as directed by the Contracting Officer and at
L0:its own expense, shall correct and repair the deficiency to the satisfaction of the
L0:Contracting Officer.
L1:(b) If the Contractor or any subcontractor has a guarantee for work performed or
L0:materials furnished that exceeds the 90 day period, the Government shall be entitled to
L0:rely upon the longer guarantee until its expiration.
L1:(c) With respect to any individual work item identified as incomplete at the time of
L0:redelivery of the vessel(s), the guarantee period shall run from the date the item is
L0:completed.
L1:(d) If practicable, the Government shall give the Contractor an opportunity to
L0:correct the deficiency.
L1:(1) If the Contracting Officer determines it is not practicable or is otherwise not
L0:advisable to return the vessel(s) to the Contractor, or the Contractor fails to proceed
L0:with the repairs promptly, the Contracting Officer may direct that the repairs be
L0:performed elsewhere, at the Contractor's expense.
L1:(2) If correction and repairs are performed by other than the Contractor, the
L0:Contracting Officer may discharge the Contractor's liability by making an equitable
L0:deduction in the price of the job order.
L1:(e) The Contractor's liability shall extend for an additional 90 day guarantee period
L0:on those defects or deficiencies that the Contractor corrected.
L1:(f) At the option of the Contracting Officer, defects and deficiencies may be left
L0:uncorrected. In that event, the Contractor and Contracting Officer shall negotiate an
L0:equitable reduction in the job price. Failure to agree upon an equitable reduction shall
L0:constitute a dispute under the Disputes clause of this agreement.

title: 252.217-7016 Plant Protection
content:
L0:252.217-7016 Plant Protection.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104(a), use the following clause:
L0:(End of clause)
L0:PLANT PROTECTION (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall provide, for the plant and work in process, reasonable
L0:safeguards against all hazards, including unauthorized entry, malicious mischief, theft,
L0:vandalism, and fire.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall also provide whatever additional safeguards are necessary
L0:to protect the plant and work in process from espionage, sabotage, and enemy action.
L1:(1) The Government shall reimburse the Contractor for that portion of the costs
L0:of the additional safeguards that is allocable to the contract in the same manner as if
L0:the Contracting Officer had issued a change order for the additional safeguards.
L1:(2) The costs reimbursed shall not include any overhead allowance, unless the
L0:overhead is incident to the construction or installation of necessary security devices or
L0:equipment.
L1:(c) Upon payment by the Government of the cost of any device or equipment
L0:required or approved under paragraph (b) of this clause, title shall vest in the
L0:Government.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall comply with the instructions of the Contracting Officer
L0:concerning its identification and disposition.
L1:(2) No such device or equipment shall become a fixture as a result of its being
L0:affixed to realty not owned by the Government.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217

content:

L1:(b) The Contractor agrees to submit a _______________ [insert type of proposal; e.g.,

title: 252.217-7028 Over and Above Work
content:
L0:252.217-7028 Over and Above Work.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7702, use a clause substantially as follows:
L0:OVER AND ABOVE WORK (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) “Over and above work” means work discovered during the course of
L0:performing overhaul, maintenance, and repair efforts that is—
L1:(i) Within the general scope of the contract;
L1:(ii) Not covered by the line item(s) for the basic work under the contract;
L0:and
L1:(iii) Necessary in order to satisfactorily complete the contract.
L1:(2) “Work request” means a document prepared by the Contractor which
L0:describes over and above work being proposed.
L1:(b) The Contractor and Administrative Contracting Officer shall mutually agree to
L0:procedures for Government administration and Contractor performance of over and
L0:above work requests. If the parties cannot agree upon the procedures, the
L0:Administrative Contracting Officer has the unilateral right to direct the over and above
L0:work procedures to be followed. These procedures shall, as a minimum, cover—
L1:(1) The format, content, and submission of work requests by the Contractor.
L0:Work requests shall contain data on the type of discrepancy disclosed, the specific
L0:location of the discrepancy, and the estimated labor hours and material required to
L0:correct the discrepancy. Data shall be sufficient to satisfy contract requirements and
L0:obtain the authorization of the Contracting Officer to perform the proposed work;
L1:(2) Government review, verification, and authorization of the work; and
L1:(3) Proposal pricing, submission, negotiation, and definitization.
L1:(c) Upon discovery of the need for over and above work, the Contractor shall prepare
L0:and furnish to the Government a work request in accordance with the agreed-to
L0:procedures.
L1:(d) The Government shall—
L1:(1) Promptly review the work request;
L1:(2) Verify that the proposed work is required and not covered under the basic
L0:contract line item(s);
L1:(3) Verify that the proposed corrective action is appropriate; and
L1:(4) Authorize over and above work as necessary.
L1:(e) The Contractor shall promptly submit to the Contracting Officer, a proposal for
L0:the over and above work. The Government and Contractor will then negotiate a
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L0:settlement for the over and above work. Contract modifications will be executed to
L0:definitize all over and above work.
L1:(f) Failure to agree on the price of over and above work shall be a dispute within the
L0:meaning of the Disputes clause of this contract.
L0:(End of clause)

L0:equipment, or other nonrecurring costs already amortized.
L1:(3) The desirability of reserving the right to take title, under the appropriate

L0:PGI 217.7003 Purchase request.
L0:Ensure that the requiring activity provides all of the following in support of the purchase
L0:request—
L1:(a) A certification that the property is eligible for exchange and complies with all
L0:conditions and limitations of DoD Manual 4140.01, Volume 9, DoD Supply Chain Materiel
L0:Management Procedures: Materiel Programs.
L1:(b) A written determination of economic advantage indicating—
L1:(1) The anticipated economic advantage to the Government from use of the
L0:exchange authority;
L1:(2) That exchange allowances shall be applied toward, or in partial payment of, the
L0:items to be acquired; and
L1:(3) That, if required, the exchange property has been rendered safe or innocuous or
L0:has been demilitarized;
L1:(c) All applicable approvals for the exchange; and
L1:(d) A description of the property available for exchange (e.g., nomenclature, location,
L0:serial number, estimated travel value).
L0:PGI 217.7004 Solicitation and award.
L1:(a) Ensure solicitations require offerors to state prices—
L1:(1) For the new items being acquired without any exchange; and
L1:(2) For the new items with the exchange (trade-in allowance) for the exchange
L0:property listed.
L1:(b) The contracting officer is not obligated to award on an exchange basis. If the lowest
L0:evaluated offer is an offer for the new items without any exchange, the contracting officer
L0:may award on that basis and forgo the exchange.
L1:(c) Exchanges may be made only with the successful offeror. When the successful offer
L0:includes an exchange, award one contract for both the acquisition of the new property and
L0:the trade-in of the exchange property. The only exception is when the items must be
L0:acquired against a mandatory Federal supply schedule contract, in which case, award a
L0:separate contract for the exchange.

L0:PGI 217.71—MASTER AGREEMENT FOR REPAIR AND ALTERATION OF VESSELS
L0:PGI 217.7103 Master agreements and job orders.
L0:PGI 217.7103-1 Content and format of master agreements.
L1:(1) A master agreement must contain all clauses required by DFARS 217.7104(a),
L0:statute, and Executive order.
L1:(2) The following format may be adapted to fit specific circumstances:
L0:MASTER AGREEMENT FOR REPAIR AND ALTERATION OF VESSELS
L0:1. This agreement is entered into this ____ day of _____________________ ,____,
L0:by the United States of America (the “Government”:) represented by _________________,
L0:the Contracting Officer, and ___________________________, a corporation organized and
L0:existing under the laws of the State of __________________________ (the “Contractor”).
L0:2. The clauses in this agreement, must be incorporated, by reference or
L0:attachment, in job orders issued under this agreement to effect repairs, alterations, and/or
L0:additions to vessels.
L0:3. By giving 30 days written notice, either party to this agreement has the right to
L0:cancel it without affecting the rights and liabilities under any job order existing at the time of
L0:cancellation. The Contractor shall perform, under the terms of this agreement, all work
L0:covered by any job order awarded before the effective date of the cancellation.
L0:4. This agreement may be modified only by mutual agreement of the parties. A
L0:modification of this agreement must not affect any job order in existence at the time of
L0:modification, unless the parties agree otherwise.
L0:5. The rights and obligations of the parties to this agreement are set forth in this
L0:agreement and the clauses of any job orders issued under this agreement. In the event
L0:there is an inconsistency between this agreement and any job order, the provisions of this
L0:agreement shall govern.
L0:6. This agreement shall remain in effect until cancelled by either party.
L0:THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

L1:(1) The requiring activity, in coordination with the contracting office, prepares the request

L0:delays in beginning performance;

L0:mitigate such risk;

L1:(vi) Establish limitations on the obligation of funds; and
L1:(vii) Provide the definitization schedule of agreed-upon events that support timely
L0:definitization.
L1:(2) A sample format with certain variations for letter contracts is provided at this website:

L1:(iii) The contractor’s proposal.
L1:(2) The maximum not-to-exceed price is the firm-fixed price for firm-fixed price contracts,

title: 209.270 for requirements applicable to replenishment parts for aviation or ship critical safety
content:
L0:209.270 for requirements applicable to replenishment parts for aviation or ship critical safety
L0:items.
L0:PGI 217.7503 Spares acquisition integrated with production.
L1:(1) Spares acquisition integrated with production (SAIP) is a technique used to acquire
L0:replenishment parts concurrently with parts being produced for the end item.
L1:(2) Include appropriately tailored provisions in the contract when SAIP is used.
L0:PGI 217.7504 Acquisition of parts when data is not available.
L0:When acquiring a part for which the Government does not have necessary data with rights
L0:to use in a specification or drawing for competitive acquisition, use one of the following
L0:procedures:
L1:(1) When items of identical design are not required, the acquisition may still be
L0:conducted through full and open competition by using a performance specification or other
L0:similar technical requirement or purchase description that does not contain data with
L0:restricted rights. Two methods are—
L1:(i) Two-step sealed bidding; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 17
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 217
L1:(ii) Brand name or equal purchase descriptions.
L1:(2) When other than full and open competition is authorized under FAR part 6, acquire
L0:the part from the firm that developed or designed the item or process, or its licensees,
L0:provided productive capacity and quality are adequate and the price is fair and reasonable.
L1:(3) When additional sources are needed and the procedures in paragraph (1) are not
L0:practicable, consider the following alternatives:
L1:(i) Encourage the developer to license others to manufacture the parts;
L1:(ii) Acquire the necessary rights in data;
L1:(iii) Use a leader company acquisition technique (FAR subpart 17.4) when complex
L0:technical equipment is involved and establishing satisfactory additional sources will require
L0:technical assistance as well as data; or
L1:(iv) Incorporate a priced option in the contract that allows the Government to require
L0:the contractor to establish a second source.
L1:(4) A design specification may be developed for competitive acquisition through reverse
L0:engineering. Contracting and requiring activities must not do reverse engineering unless—
L1:(i) Significant cost savings can be demonstrated; and
L1:(ii) The action is authorized by the head of the contracting activity.

title: 252.219-7997 Small Business Subcontracting Plan (Test Program)
content:
L0:252.219-7997 Small Business Subcontracting Plan (Test Program).
L0:(DEVIATION 2026-O0037)
L0:As prescribed in 219.109(e)(2)(B), use the following clause:
L0:SMALL BUSINESS SUBCONTRACTING PLAN (TEST PROGRAM) (DEVIATION
L0:2026-O0037) (FEB 2026)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Covered small business concern” means a small business concern, veteran-owned
L0:small business concern, service-disabled veteran-owned small business concern,
L0:HUBZone small business concern, women-owned small business concern, or small
L0:disadvantaged business concern, as these terms are defined in FAR 2.101.
L0:“Electronic Subcontracting Reporting System (eSRS)” means the Governmentwide,
L0:electronic, web-based system for small business subcontracting program reporting.
L0:“Failure to make a good faith effort to comply with a comprehensive subcontracting
L0:plan” means a willful or intentional failure to perform in accordance with the
L0:requirements of the Contractor’s approved comprehensive subcontracting plan or willful
L0:or intentional action to frustrate the plan.
L0:“Subcontract” means any agreement (other than one involving an employer-
L0:employee relationship) entered into by a Federal Government prime Contractor or
L0:subcontractor calling for supplies or services required for performance of the contract or
L0:subcontract.
L1:(b) Test Program. The Contractor’s comprehensive small business subcontracting
L0:plan and its successors, which are authorized by and approved under the Test Program
L0:of 15 U.S.C. 637 note, as amended, shall be included in and made a part of this contract.
L0:Upon expulsion from the Test Program or expiration of the Test Program, the
L0:Contractor shall negotiate an individual subcontracting plan for all future contracts
L0:that meet the requirements of 15 U.S.C. 637(d).
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L1:(c) Eligibility requirements. To become and remain eligible to participate in the Test
L0:Program, a business concern is required to have furnished supplies or services
L0:(including construction) under at least three DoD contracts during the preceding fiscal
L0:year, having an aggregate value of at least $100 million.
L1:(d) Reports.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall report semiannually for the 6-month periods ending
L0:March 31 and September 30, the information in paragraphs (d)(1)(i) through (v) of this
L0:section within 30 days after the end of the reporting period.
L1:(i) A list of contracts covered under its comprehensive small business
L0:subcontracting plan, to include the Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code
L0:and unique entity identifier.
L1:(ii) The amount of first-tier subcontract dollars awarded during the 6-month
L0:period covered by the report to covered small business concerns, with the information
L0:set forth separately by—
L1:(A) North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code;
L1:(B) Major defense acquisition program, as defined in 10 U.S.C. 4201;
L1:(C) Contract number, if the contract is for maintenance, overhaul,
L0:repair, servicing, rehabilitation, salvage, modernization, or modification of supplies,
L0:systems, or equipment, and the total value of the contract, including options, exceeds
L0:$100 million; and
L1:(D) Military department.
L1:(iii) Total number of subcontracts active under the Test Program that would
L0:have otherwise required a subcontracting plan.
L1:(iv) Costs incurred in negotiating, complying with, and reporting on its
L0:comprehensive subcontracting plan.
L1:(v) Costs avoided through the use of a comprehensive subcontracting plan.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall—
L1:(i) Ensure that subcontractors with subcontracting plans agree to submit an
L0:Individual Subcontract Report (ISR) and/or Summary Subcontract Report (SSR) using
L0:the Electronic Subcontracting Reporting System (eSRS).
L1:(ii) Provide its contract number, its unique entity identifier, and the email
L0:address of the Contractor’s official responsible for acknowledging or rejecting the ISR to
L0:all first-tier subcontractors, who will be required to submit ISRs, so they can enter this
L0:information into the eSRS when submitting their reports.
L1:(iii) Require that each subcontractor with a subcontracting plan provide the
L0:prime contract number, its own unique entity identifier, and the email address of the
L0:subcontractor’s official responsible for acknowledging or rejecting the ISRs to its
L0:subcontractors with subcontracting plans who will be required to submit ISRs.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L1:(iv) Acknowledge receipt or reject all ISRs submitted by its subcontractors
L0:using eSRS.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall submit SSRs using eSRS. The reports shall provide
L0:information on subcontract awards to small business concerns, veteran-owned small
L0:business concerns, service-disabled veteran-owned small business concerns, HUBZone
L0:small business concerns, small disadvantaged business concerns, and women-owned
L0:small business concerns. Purchases from a corporation, company, or subdivision that is
L0:an affiliate of the prime Contractor or subcontractor are not included in these reports.
L0:Subcontract award data reported by prime contractors and subcontractors shall be
L0:limited to awards made to their immediate next-tier subcontractors. Credit cannot be
L0:taken for awards made to lower-tier subcontractors unless the Contractor or
L0:subcontractor has been designated to receive a small business or small disadvantaged
L0:business credit from a member firm of the Alaska Native Corporations or an Indian
L0:tribe. Only subcontracts involving performance in the U.S. or its outlying areas should
L0:be included in these reports.
L1:(i) This report may be submitted on a corporate, company, or subdivision
L0:(e.g., plant or division operating as a separate profit center) basis, as negotiated in the
L0:comprehensive subcontracting plan with the Defense Contract Management Agency.
L1:(ii) This report encompasses all subcontracting under prime contracts and
L0:subcontracts with the Department of Defense, regardless of the dollar value of the
L0:subcontracts, and is based on the negotiated comprehensive subcontracting plan.
L1:(iii) The report shall be submitted semi-annually for the six months ending
L0:March 31 and the twelve months ending September 30. Reports are due 30 days after
L0:the close of each reporting period.
L1:(iv) The authority to acknowledge receipt of or reject the SSR resides with
L0:the Defense Contract Management Agency.
L1:(e) Failure to comply. The failure of the Contractor or subcontractor to comply in
L0:good faith with the clause of this contract entitled “Utilization of Small Business
L0:Concerns,” or an approved plan required by this clause, shall be a material breach of the
L0:contract.
L1:(f) Liquidated damages. The Contracting Officer designated to manage the
L0:comprehensive subcontracting plan will exercise the functions of the Contracting
L0:Officer, as identified in paragraphs (f)(1) through (4) of this clause, on behalf of all DoD
L0:departments and agencies that awarded contracts covered by the Contractor’s
L0:comprehensive subcontracting plan.
L1:(1) To determine the need for liquidated damages, the Contracting Officer will
L0:conduct a compliance review during the fiscal year after the close of the fiscal year for
L0:which the plan is applicable. The Contracting Officer will compare the approved
L0:percentage or dollar goals to the total, actual subcontracting dollars covered by the plan.
L1:(2) If the Contractor has failed to meet its approved subcontracting goal(s), the
L0:Contracting Officer will provide the Contractor written notice specifying the failure,
L0:advising of the potential for assessment of liquidated damages, and permitting the
L0:Contractor to demonstrate what good faith efforts have been made. The Contracting
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L0:Officer may take the Contractor’s failure to respond to the notice within 15 working
L0:days (or longer period at the Contracting Officer’s discretion) as an admission that no
L0:valid explanation exists.
L1:(3) If, after consideration of all relevant information, the Contracting Officer
L0:determines that the Contractor failed to make a good faith effort to comply with the
L0:comprehensive subcontracting plan, the Contracting Officer will issue a final decision to
L0:the Contractor to that effect and require the Contractor to pay liquidated damages to
L0:the Government in the amount identified in the comprehensive subcontracting plan.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall have the right of appeal under the clause in this
L0:contract entitled “Disputes” from any final decision of the Contracting Officer.
L1:(g) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include in subcontracts that offer
L0:subcontracting opportunities, are expected to exceed the applicable threshold specified
L0:in FAR 19.109(a)(1) on the date of subcontract award, and are required to include the
L0:clause at FAR 52.219-8, Utilization of Small Business Concerns, the clauses at—
L1:(1) FAR 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan, and Defense Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 252.219-7996, Small Business
L0:Subcontracting Plan (DoD Contracts)-Basic;
L1:(2) FAR 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan, with its Alternate III,
L0:and DFARS 252.219-7996, Small Business Subcontracting Plan (DoD Contracts)-
L0:Alternate I, to allow for submission of SF 294s in lieu of ISRs; or
L1:(3) DFARS 252.219-7997, Small Business Subcontracting Plan (Test Program),
L0:in subcontracts with subcontractors that participate in the Test Program described in
L0:DFARS 219.206-70.
L0:(End of clause)

L0:APPENDIX I—POLICY AND PROCEDURES FOR THE DOD MENTOR-
L0:PROTÉGÉ PROGRAM
L0:I-100 Purpose.
L1:(a) This appendix implements the DoD Mentor-Protégé Program (referred to as the
L0:Program) authorized under 10 U.S.C. 4902. The purpose of the Program is to provide
L0:incentives to DoD contractors to furnish eligible small business concerns with
L0:assistance designed to—
L1:(1) Enhance the capabilities of eligible small business concerns to perform as
L0:subcontractors and suppliers under DoD contracts and other contracts and
L0:subcontracts; and
L1:(2) Increase the participation of such business concerns as subcontractors and
L0:suppliers under DoD contracts, other Federal Government contracts, and commercial
L0:contracts.
L1:(b) Under the Program, eligible companies approved as mentor firms will enter into
L0:mentor-protégé agreements with eligible protégé firms to provide appropriate
L0:developmental assistance to enhance the capabilities of the protégé firms to perform as
L0:subcontractors and suppliers. DoD may provide the mentor firm with either cost
L0:reimbursement or credit against applicable subcontracting goals established under
L0:contracts with DoD or other Federal agencies.
L1:(c) DoD will measure the overall success of the Program by the extent to which the
L0:Program results in—
L1:(1) An increase in the dollar value of contract and subcontract awards to
L0:protégé firms (under DoD contracts, contracts awarded by other Federal agencies, and
L0:commercial contracts) from the date of their entry into the Program until 5 years after
L0:the conclusion of the agreement;
L1:(2) An increase in the number and dollar value of subcontracts awarded to a
L0:protégé firm (or former protégé firm) by its mentor firm (or former mentor firm);
L1:(3) An increase in protégé participation in DoD science and technology
L0:programs; and
L1:(4) An increase in job creation of protégé firms from the date of execution of the
L0:mentor-protégé agreement until 5 years after completion of the mentor-protégé
L0:agreement.
L1:(d) This policy sets forth the procedures for participation in the Program applicable
L0:to companies that are interested in receiving—
L1:(1) Reimbursement through a separate contract line item in a DoD contract or a
L0:separate contract with DoD; or
L1:(2) Credit toward applicable subcontracting goals for costs incurred under the
L0:Program.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L0:I-101 Definitions.
L0:As used in this appendix—
L0:“Affiliation” means, with respect to a relationship between a mentor firm and a
L0:protégé firm, a relationship described under 13 CFR 121.103.
L0:“Eligible entity employing the severely disabled” means a business entity operated
L0:on a for-profit or nonprofit basis that—
L1:(1) Uses rehabilitative engineering to provide employment opportunities for
L0:severely disabled individuals and integrates severely disabled individuals into its
L0:workforce;
L1:(2) Employs severely disabled individuals at a rate that averages not less than
L0:20 percent of its total workforce;
L1:(3) Employs each severely disabled individual in its workforce generally on the
L0:basis of 40 hours per week; and
L1:(4) Pays not less than the minimum wage prescribed pursuant to section 6 of
L0:the Fair Labor Standards Act (29 U.S.C. 206) to those employees who are severely
L0:disabled individuals.
L0:“Severely disabled individual” means an individual who is blind or severely disabled
L0:as defined in 41 U.S.C. 8501.
L0:I-102 Participant eligibility.
L1:(a) To be eligible to participate as a mentor, an entity must—
L1:(1) Be a for-profit entity that is eligible for the award of Federal contracts;
L1:(2) Demonstrate that it—
L1:(i) Is qualified to provide assistance that will contribute to the purpose of
L0:the Program;
L1:(ii) Is of good financial health and character;
L1:(iii) Is not on a Federal list of debarred or suspended contractors; and
L1:(iv) Is an other than small business concern, unless approved by the

L1:(3) Be capable of imparting value to a protégé firm because of experience gained

L1:(b) To be eligible to participate as a protégé, an entity must be—
L1:(1) A small business concern;
L1:(2) Eligible for the award of Federal contracts;
L1:(3) Not more than the Small Business Administration (SBA) size standard for
L0:its primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code;
L1:(4) Not owned or managed by individuals or entities that directly or indirectly

L1:(5) At least one of the following:

L1:(ii) A women-owned small business concern.
L1:(iii) A service-disabled veteran-owned small business concern.
L1:(iv) An entity owned and controlled by an Indian tribe.
L1:(v) An entity owned and controlled by a Native Hawaiian organization.
L1:(vi) An entity owned and controlled by socially and economically
L0:disadvantaged individuals.
L1:(vii) A qualified organization employing severely disabled individuals.
L1:(viii) A nontraditional defense contractor.
L1:(ix) An entity that currently provides goods or services in the private sector
L0:that are critical to enhancing the capabilities of the defense supplier base and fulfilling
L0:key DoD needs.
L1:(c) Mentor firms may rely in good faith on a written representation that the entity
L0:meets the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section, except that a mentor firm is
L0:required to confirm a protégé’s status as a HUBZone small business concern (see FAR
L0:19.302-2).
L1:(d) If at any time the SBA (or DoD in the case of entities employing severely
L0:disabled individuals) determines that a protégé is ineligible, assistance the mentor firm
L0:furnishes to the protégé after the date of the determination may not be considered
L0:assistance furnished under the Program.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L1:(e) A mentor firm may not enter into an agreement with a protégé firm if SBA has
L0:made a determination of affiliation. If SBA has not made such a determination and if
L0:the DoD OSBP has reason to believe, based on SBA’s regulations regarding affiliation,
L0:that the mentor firm is affiliated with the protégé firm, then DoD OSBP will request a
L0:determination regarding affiliation from SBA.
L1:(f) A company may not be approved for participation in the Program as a mentor
L0:firm if, at the time of requesting participation in the Program, it is currently debarred
L0:or suspended from contracting with the Federal Government pursuant to FAR subpart
L0:9.4.
L1:(g) If the mentor firm is suspended or debarred while performing under an approved
L0:mentor-protégé agreement, the mentor firm—
L1:(1) May continue to provide assistance to its protégé firms in accordance with
L0:the approved mentor-protégé agreement entered into prior to the imposition of such
L0:suspension or debarment;
L1:(2) May not be reimbursed or take credit for any costs of providing
L0:developmental assistance to its protégé firm, incurred more than 30 days after the
L0:imposition of such suspension or debarment; and
L1:(3) Must promptly give notice of its suspension or debarment to its protégé firm
L0:and the Director, OSBP, of the cognizant military department or defense agency.

L0:I-103 Incentives for mentors.
L0:Mentors incurring costs through September 30, 2026, pursuant to a mentor-protégé
L0:agreement approved prior to December 23, 2022, and mentors incurring costs pursuant
L0:to a mentor-protégé agreement approved on or after December 23, 2023, may be eligible
L0:for—
L1:(a) Credit toward the attainment of its applicable subcontracting goals for
L0:unreimbursed costs incurred in providing developmental assistance to its protégé
L0:firm(s);
L1:(b) Reimbursement pursuant to the execution of a separately priced contract line
L0:item added to a DoD contract; or
L1:(c) Reimbursement pursuant to entering into a separate DoD contract upon
L0:determination by the Director, OSBP, of the cognizant military department or defense
L0:agency that unusual circumstances justify using a separate contract.
L0:I-104 Selection of protégé firms.
L1:(a) Mentor firms will be solely responsible for selecting protégé firms that qualify
L0:under I-102(b). Mentor firms are encouraged to identify and select concerns that have
L0:not previously received significant prime contract awards from DoD or any other
L0:Federal agency.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L1:(b) The selection of protégé firms by mentor firms may not be protested, except as in
L0:paragraph (c) of this section.
L1:(c) Any interested party may file a protest of the selection of a protégé firm directly
L0:with the Director, OSBP, OASD (IBP) or the Director, OSBP, of the cognizant military
L0:department or defense agency. In the event of a protest regarding the size or status of
L0:an entity selected to be a protégé firm, the Director, OSBP, OASD(IBP), or the Director,
L0:OSBP, of the military department or defense agency must refer the protest to the SBA
L0:to resolve in accordance with 13 CFR part 121 (with respect to size) or other parts of
L0:title 13 of the CFR or this appendix (with respect to the protégé’s socioeconomic status).
L0:The Director, OSBP, OASD(IBP), or the Director, OSBP, of the military department or
L0:defense agency shall decide protests concerning all other aspects of a protégé’s eligibility
L0:for the Program (e.g., nontraditional defense contractor or entity employing the severely
L0:disabled).
L1:(d) For purposes of the Small Business Act, no determination of affiliation or control
L0:(either direct or indirect) may be found between a protégé firm and its mentor firm on
L0:the basis that the mentor firm has agreed to furnish (or has furnished) to its protégé
L0:firm, pursuant to a mentor-protégé agreement, any form of developmental assistance
L0:described in I-106(d).
L1:(e) A protégé firm may not be a party to more than one DoD mentor-protégé
L0:agreement at a time and may only participate in the Program during the 5-year period
L0:beginning on the date the protégé firm enters into its first mentor-protégé agreement.
L0:This does not preclude a protégé firm from concurrent participation in mentor-protégé
L0:programs with other agencies.
L0:I-105 Mentor approval process.
L1:(a) An entity seeking to participate as a mentor must apply to the Mentor-Protégé
L0:Program Director, OSBP, OASD(IBP), to establish its initial eligibility as a mentor.
L1:(b) The application must provide the following information:
L1:(1) A statement that the entity meets the requirements in I-102(a), specifying
L0:the criteria in I-102(a)(3) under which the entity is applying.
L1:(2) A summary of the entity’s historical and recent activities and
L0:accomplishments under its small and disadvantaged business utilization program.
L1:(3) The total dollar amount of DoD contracts and subcontracts that the entity
L0:received during the 2 preceding fiscal years. (Show prime contracts and subcontracts
L0:separately per year.)
L1:(4) The total dollar amount of all other Federal agency contracts and
L0:subcontracts that the entity received during the 2 preceding fiscal years. (Show prime
L0:contracts and subcontracts separately per year.)
L1:(5) The total dollar amount of subcontracts that the entity awarded under DoD
L0:contracts during the 2 preceding fiscal years.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L1:(6) The total dollar amount of subcontracts that the entity awarded under all
L0:other Federal agency contracts during the 2 preceding fiscal years.
L1:(7) The total dollar amount and percentage of subcontracts that the entity
L0:awarded to firms qualifying under I-102(b)(5)(ii) through (viii) during the 2 preceding
L0:fiscal years. (Show DoD subcontract awards separately.) If the entity was required to
L0:submit a Summary Subcontract Report (SSR) in the Electronic Subcontracting
L0:Reporting System, the request must include copies of the final reports for the 2
L0:preceding fiscal years.
L1:(8) Information on the company’s ability to provide developmental assistance to
L0:eligible protégés.
L1:(c) A template of the mentor application is available at
L0:https://business.defense.gov/Programs/Mentor-Protégé-Program/MPP-Resources/.
L1:(d) Companies that apply for participation and are not approved will be provided
L0:the reasons and an opportunity to submit additional information for reconsideration.
L0:I-106 Development of mentor-protégé agreements.
L1:(a) Prospective mentors and their protégés may choose to execute letters of intent
L0:prior to negotiation of mentor-protégé agreements.
L1:(b) The agreements should be structured after completion of a preliminary
L0:assessment of the developmental needs of the protégé firm and mutual agreement
L0:regarding the developmental assistance to be provided to address those needs and
L0:enhance the protégé’s ability to perform successfully under contracts or subcontracts.
L1:(c) A mentor firm may not require a protégé firm to enter into a mentor-protégé
L0:agreement as a condition for award of a contract by the mentor firm, including a
L0:subcontract under a DoD contract awarded to the mentor firm.
L1:(d) The mentor-protégé agreement may provide for the mentor firm to furnish any
L0:or all of the following types of developmental assistance:
L1:(1) Assistance by mentor firm personnel in—
L1:(i) General business management, including organizational management,
L0:financial management, and personnel management, marketing and technology
L0:commercialization, compliance systems, and overall business planning;
L1:(ii) Engineering and technical matters such as production, inventory
L0:control, manufacturing, test and evaluation, quality assurance; acquisition or transfer
L0:of hardware, tooling, or software; and technology transfer and transition; and
L1:(iii) Any other assistance designed to develop the capabilities of the protégé
L0:firm under the developmental program described in I-107(g).
L1:(2) Award of subcontracts to the protégé firm under DoD contracts or other
L0:contracts on a noncompetitive basis.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L1:(3) Payment of progress payments for the performance of subcontracts by a
L0:protégé firm in amounts as provided for in the subcontract; but in no event may any
L0:such progress payment exceed 100 percent of the costs incurred by the protégé firm for
L0:the performance of the subcontract. Provision of progress payments by a mentor firm to
L0:a protégé firm at a rate other than the customary rate for the firm must be
L0:implemented in accordance with FAR 32.504(c).
L1:(4) Advance payments under such subcontracts. The mentor firm must
L0:administer advance payments in accordance with FAR subpart 32.4.
L1:(5) Loans.
L1:(6) Assistance that the mentor firm obtains for the protégé firm from one or
L0:more of the following:
L1:(i) Small Business Development Centers (15 U.S.C. 648).
L1:(ii) Entities providing procurement technical assistance under the
L0:Procurement Technical Assistance Cooperative Agreement Program (10 U.S.C. Chapter
L0:388).
L1:(iii) Historically Black colleges and universities.
L1:(iv) Minority institutions of higher education.
L1:(v) Women’s business centers (15 U.S.C. 656).
L1:(vi) Manufacturing innovation institutes.
L1:(e) Pursuant to FAR 31.109, approved mentor firms seeking either reimbursement
L0:or credit are strongly encouraged to enter into an advance agreement with the
L0:contracting officer responsible for determining final indirect cost rates under FAR 42.5.
L0:The purpose of the advance agreement is to establish the accounting treatment of the
L0:costs of the developmental assistance pursuant to the mentor-protégé agreement prior
L0:to the incurring of any costs by the mentor firm. An advance agreement is an attempt
L0:by both the Government and the mentor firm to avoid possible subsequent dispute
L0:based on questions related to reasonableness, allocability, or allowability of the costs of
L0:developmental assistance under the Program. Absent an advance agreement, mentor
L0:firms are advised to establish the accounting treatment of such costs and to address the
L0:need for any changes to their cost accounting practices that may result from the
L0:implementation of a mentor-protégé agreement, prior to incurring any costs, and
L0:irrespective of whether costs will be reimbursed or credited.
L1:(f) Developmental assistance provided under an approved mentor-protégé
L0:agreement is distinct from, and must not duplicate, any effort that is the normal and
L0:expected product of the award and administration of the mentor firm's subcontracts.
L0:Costs associated with the latter must be accumulated and charged in accordance with
L0:the contractor's approved accounting practices; they are not considered developmental
L0:assistance costs eligible for either credit or reimbursement under the Program.
L1:(g) The agreement shall demonstrate, through its execution, how it will contribute
L0:to the overall mission of DoD and/or fill or address an identified critical gap or
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L0:vulnerability. Focus areas include, but are not limited to, manufacturing, research and
L0:development, and knowledge-based services.
L0:I-107 Elements of a mentor-protégé agreement.
L0:Each mentor-protégé agreement shall contain—
L1:(a) The name, address, email address, and telephone number of the mentor and
L0:protégé points of contact;
L1:(b) The NAICS code(s) that represent the contemplated supplies or services to be
L0:provided by the protégé firm to the mentor firm and a statement that, at the time the
L0:agreement is submitted for approval, the protégé firm does not exceed the size standard
L0:in I-102(b)(3);
L1:(c) A statement that the protégé firm is eligible to participate in accordance with I-
L0:102(b);
L1:(d) A statement that the mentor is eligible to participate in accordance with I-
L0:102(a);
L1:(e) Assurances that—
L1:(1) The mentor firm does not share, directly or indirectly, with the protégé firm
L0:ownership or management of the protégé firm;
L1:(2) The mentor firm does not have an agreement, at the time the mentor firm
L0:enters into a mentor-protégé agreement, to merge with the protégé firm;
L1:(3) The owners and managers of the mentor firm are not the parent, child,
L0:spouse, sibling, aunt, uncle, niece, nephew, grandparent, grandchild, or first cousin of
L0:an owner or manager of the protégé firm;
L1:(4) The mentor firm has not, during the 2-year period before entering into a
L0:mentor-protégé agreement, employed any officer, director, principal stockholder,
L0:managing member, or key employee of the protégé firm;
L1:(5) The mentor firm has not engaged in a joint venture with the protégé firm
L0:during the 2-year period before entering into a mentor-protégé agreement, unless such
L0:joint venture was approved by SBA prior to making any offer on a contract;
L1:(6) The mentor firm is not, directly or indirectly, the primary party providing
L0:contracts to the protégé firm, as measured by the dollar value of the contracts; and
L1:(7) The SBA has not made a determination of affiliation or control;
L1:(f) A preliminary assessment of the developmental needs of the protégé firm;
L1:(g) A developmental program for the protégé firm, including—
L1:(1) The type of assistance the mentor will provide to the protégé and how that
L0:assistance will—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L1:(i) Increase the protégé’s ability to participate in DoD, Federal, and/or
L0:commercial contracts and subcontracts; and
L1:(ii) Increase small business subcontracting opportunities in industry
L0:categories where eligible protégés or other small business firms are not dominant in the
L0:company’s vendor base;
L1:(iii) Increase the protégé firm’s cybersecurity readiness posture and ability to
L0:comply with Federal acquisition regulations.
L1:(2) Factors to assess the protégé firm's developmental progress under the
L0:Program, including specific milestones for providing each element of the identified
L0:assistance;
L1:(3) A description of the quantitative and qualitative benefits to DoD from the
L0:agreement, if applicable; and
L1:(4) Goals for additional awards for which the protégé firm can compete outside
L0:the Program;
L1:(h) The assistance the mentor will provide to the protégé firm in understanding
L0:Federal contract regulations, including the FAR and DFARS, after award of a
L0:subcontract under the Program, if applicable;
L1:(i) An estimate of the dollar value and type of subcontracts that the mentor firm will
L0:award to the protégé firm, and the period of time over which the subcontracts will be
L0:awarded;
L1:(j) A statement from the protégé firm indicating its commitment to comply with the
L0:requirements for reporting and for review of the agreement during the duration of the
L0:agreement and for 5 years thereafter;
L1:(k) A program participation term for the agreement that does not exceed 3 years.
L0:The agreement may be extended for a period not to exceed 2 years if approved by the
L0:Director, OSBP, OASD(IBP). The Director, OSBP, of the cognizant military
L0:department or defense agency will submit requests for an extension of the agreement to
L0:the Director, OSBP, OASD(IBP) for approval. The request will include a justification
L0:describing the unusual circumstances that warrant a term in excess of 3 years;
L1:(l) Procedures for the mentor firm to notify the protégé firm in writing at least 30
L0:days in advance of the mentor firm's intent to voluntarily withdraw its participation in
L0:the Program. A mentor firm may voluntarily terminate its mentor-protégé
L0:agreement(s) only if it no longer wants to be a participant in the Program as a mentor
L0:firm. Otherwise, a mentor firm must terminate a mentor-protégé agreement for cause;
L1:(m) Procedures for the mentor firm to terminate the mentor-protégé agreement for
L0:cause which provide that—
L1:(1) The mentor firm must furnish the protégé firm a written notice of the
L0:proposed termination, stating the specific reasons for such action, at least 30 days in
L0:advance of the effective date of such proposed termination;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L1:(2) The protégé firm must have 30 days to respond to such notice of proposed
L0:termination, and may rebut any findings believed to be erroneous and offer a remedial
L0:program;
L1:(3) Upon prompt consideration of the protégé firm's response, the mentor firm
L0:must either withdraw the notice of proposed termination and continue the protégé
L0:firm's participation, or issue the notice of termination; and
L1:(4) The decision of the mentor firm regarding termination for cause, conforming
L0:with the requirements of this section, will be final and is not reviewable by DoD;
L1:(n) Procedures for a protégé firm to notify the mentor firm in writing at least 30
L0:days in advance of the protégé firm's intent to voluntarily terminate the mentor-protégé
L0:agreement;
L1:(o) Additional terms and conditions as may be agreed upon by both parties; and
L1:(p) Signatures and dates for both parties to the mentor-protégé agreement.
L0:I-108 Submission and approval of mentor-protégé agreements.
L1:(a) Upon solicitation or as determined by the cognizant military department or
L0:defense agency, mentors will submit—
L1:(1) A mentor application pursuant to I-105, if the mentor has not been
L0:previously approved to participate;
L1:(2) A signed mentor-protégé agreement pursuant to I-107;
L1:(3) A statement as to whether the mentor is seeking credit or reimbursement of
L0:costs incurred;
L1:(4) The estimated cost of the technical assistance to be provided, broken out per
L0:year;
L1:(5) A justification if program participation term is greater than 3 years
L0:(agreements may not exceed 5 years) (see I-107(k)); and
L1:(6) For reimbursable agreements, a specific justification for developmental costs
L0:in excess of $1 million per year.
L1:(b) When seeking reimbursement of costs, the military department or defense
L0:agency may require additional information.
L1:(c) The mentor-protégé agreement must be approved by the Director, OSBP, of the
L0:military department or defense agency prior to incurring costs eligible for credit.
L1:(d) The military department or defense agency will execute a contract modification
L0:or a separate contract, if justified pursuant to I-103(b)(3), prior to the mentor’s incurring
