L1:(e) Credit agreements that are not associated with an existing DoD program and/or
L0:military department or defense agency will be submitted for approval to the Director,
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L0:OSBP, Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA), via the mentor’s cognizant
L0:administrative contracting officer.
L1:(f) A prospective mentor that has identified Program funds to be made available
L0:from a DoD program manager must provide the information in paragraph (a) of this
L0:section through the program manager to the Director, OSBP, of the military
L0:department or defense agency with a letter signed by the program manager indicating
L0:the amount of funding that has been identified for the developmental assistance
L0:program.
L0:I-109 Reimbursable agreements.
L0:The following provisions apply to all reimbursable mentor-protégé agreements
L0:including agreements that provide for both reimbursement and subcontracting credit:
L1:(a) Assistance provided in the form of progress payments to a protégé firm in excess
L0:of the customary progress payment rate for the firm will be reimbursed only if
L0:implemented in accordance with FAR 32.504(c).
L1:(b) Assistance provided in the form of advance payments will be reimbursed only if
L0:the payments have been provided to a protégé firm under subcontract terms and
L0:conditions similar to those in the clause at FAR 52.232-12, Advance Payments.
L0:Reimbursement of any advance payments will be made pursuant to the inclusion of the
L0:clause at DFARS 252.232-7005, Reimbursement of Subcontractor Advance Payments—
L0:DoD Mentor-Protégé Program, in appropriate contracts. In requesting reimbursement,
L0:the mentor firm agrees that the risk of any financial loss due to the failure or inability
L0:of a protégé firm to repay any unliquidated advance payments will be the sole
L0:responsibility of the mentor firm.
L1:(c) The primary forms of developmental assistance authorized for reimbursement
L0:under the Program are identified in I-106(d). On a case-by-case basis, Directors, OSBP,
L0:of the military departments or defense agencies at their discretion, may approve
L0:additional incidental expenses for reimbursement, provided these expenses do not
L0:exceed 10 percent of the total estimated cost of the agreement.
L1:(d) The total amount reimbursed to a mentor firm for costs of assistance furnished
L0:to a protégé firm in a fiscal year may not exceed $1 million unless the Director, OSBP,
L0:of the military department or defense agency determines in writing that unusual
L0:circumstances justify reimbursement at a higher amount. Request for authority to
L0:reimburse in excess of $1 million must detail the unusual circumstances and must be
L0:endorsed and submitted by the program manager to the Director, OSBP, of the military
L0:department or defense agency.
L1:(e) DoD may not reimburse any fee to the mentor firm for services provided to the
L0:protégé firm pursuant to I-106(d)(6) or for business development expenses incurred by
L0:the mentor firm under a contract awarded to the mentor firm while participating in a
L0:joint venture with the protégé firm.
L1:(f) Developmental assistance costs that are incurred pursuant to an approved
L0:reimbursable mentor-protégé agreement, and have been charged to, but not reimbursed
L0:through, a separate contract, or through a separately priced contract line item added to
L0:a DoD contract, will not be otherwise reimbursed, as either a direct or indirect cost,
L0:under any other DoD contract, irrespective of whether the costs have been recognized
L0:for credit against applicable subcontracting goals.

L0:I-110 Credit agreements.
L0:Sections I-110.1 and I-110.2 apply to all credit agreements, including agreements that
L0:provide for both credit and reimbursement.
L0:I-110.1 Program provisions applicable to credit agreements.
L1:(a) Developmental assistance costs incurred by a mentor firm for providing
L0:assistance to a protégé firm pursuant to an approved credit mentor-protégé agreement
L0:may be credited as if the costs were incurred under a subcontract award to that protégé,
L0:for the purpose of determining the performance of the mentor firm in attaining an
L0:applicable subcontracting goal established under any contract containing a
L0:subcontracting plan pursuant to the clause at FAR 52.219-9, Small Business
L0:Subcontracting Plan, or the provisions of the DoD Test Program for Negotiation of
L0:Comprehensive Small Business Subcontracting Plans. Unreimbursed developmental
L0:assistance costs incurred for a protégé firm that is an eligible entity employing severely
L0:disabled individuals may be credited toward the mentor firm's small disadvantaged
L0:business subcontracting goal, even if the protégé firm is not a small disadvantaged
L0:business concern.
L1:(b) Costs that have been reimbursed through inclusion in indirect expense pools
L0:may also be credited as subcontract awards for determining the performance of the
L0:mentor firm in attaining an applicable subcontracting goal established under any
L0:contract containing a subcontracting plan. However, costs that have not been
L0:reimbursed because they are not reasonable, allocable, or allowable will not be
L0:recognized for crediting purposes.
L1:(c) Other costs that are not eligible for reimbursement pursuant to I-106(d) may be
L0:recognized for credit only if requested, identified, and incorporated in an approved
L0:mentor-protégé agreement.
L1:(d) The amount of credit a mentor firm may receive for any such unreimbursed
L0:developmental assistance costs must be equal to—
L1:(1) Four times the total amount of such costs attributable to assistance provided
L0:by small business development centers, historically Black colleges and universities,
L0:minority institutions, and procurement technical assistance centers.
L1:(2) Three times the total amount of such costs attributable to assistance
L0:furnished by the mentor's employees.
L1:(3) Two times the total amount of other such costs incurred by the mentor in
L0:carrying out the developmental assistance program.
L0:I-110.2 Credit adjustments.
L1:(a) Adjustments may be made to the amount of credit claimed if the Director, OSBP,
L0:OASD(IBP), determines that—
L1:(1) A mentor firm's performance in the attainment of its subcontracting goals
L0:through actual subcontract awards declined from the prior fiscal year without
L0:justifiable cause; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 19
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 219
L1:(2) Imposition of such a limitation on credit appears to be warranted to prevent
L0:abuse of this incentive for the mentor firm's participation in the Program.
L1:(b) The mentor firm must be afforded the opportunity to explain the decline in small
L0:business subcontract awards before imposition of any such limitation on credit. In
L0:making the final decision to impose a limitation on credit, the Director, OSBP,
L0:OASD(IBP), must consider

title: 222.402-170 Installation support contracts
content:
L0:222.402-170 Installation support contracts.
L1:(a) Apply both the Service Contract Labor Standards statute and the Construction
L0:Wage Rate Requirements statute to installation support contracts if—
L1:(1) The contract is principally for services but also requires a substantial and
L0:segregable amount of construction, alteration, renovation, painting, or repair work; and
L1:(2) The aggregate dollar value of such construction work exceeds or is expected
L0:to exceed $2,000.
L1:(b) Service Contract Labor Standards statute coverage under the contract. Contract
L0:installation support requirements, such as plant operation and installation services (i.e.,
L0:custodial, snow removal, etc.) are subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards.
L0:Apply Service Contract Labor Standards clauses and minimum wage and fringe benefit
L0:requirements to all contract service calls or orders for such maintenance and support
L0:work.
L1:(c) Construction Wage Rate Requirements statute coverage under the contract.
L0:Contract construction, alteration, renovation, painting, and repair requirements (i.e.,
L0:roof shingling, building structural repair, paving repairs, etc.) are subject to the
L0:Construction Wage Rate Requirements statute. Apply Construction Wage Rate
L0:Requirements clauses and minimum wage requirements to all contract service calls or
L0:orders for construction, alteration, renovation, painting, or repairs to buildings or other
L0:works.
L1:(d) Repairs versus maintenance. Some contract work may be characterized as either
L0:Construction Wage Rate Requirements painting/repairs or Service Contract Labor
L0:Standards maintenance. For example, replacing broken windows, spot painting, or
L0:minor patching of a wall could be covered by either the Construction Wage Rate
L0:Requirements or the Service Contract Labor Standards. In instances where a contract
L0:service call or order requires construction trade skills (i.e., carpenter, plumber, painter,
L0:etc.), but uncertainty exists whether the work required is Service Contract Labor
L0:Standards maintenance or Construction Wage Rate Requirements painting/repairs,
L0:apply the following rules:
L1:(1) Consider individual service calls or orders requiring a total of 32 or more
L0:work hours to be repair work subject to the Construction Wage Rate Requirements.
L1:(2) Consider individual service calls or orders requiring fewer than 32 work
L0:hours to be maintenance subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 22
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 222
L1:(3) Consider painting work of 200 square feet or more, to be performed under an
L0:individual service call or order, subject to the Construction Wage Rate Requirements
L0:statute regardless of the total work hours required.
L1:(e) Where requirements are identifiable, make the determination of labor standards
L0:application when of drafting the solicitation. Otherwise, make the determination when
L0:placing the service call or order. The service call or order must identify the labor
L0:standards law and contract wage determination that applies to the work required.
L1:(f) Do not avoid application of the Construction Wage Rate Requirements statute by
L0:splitting individual tasks between orders or contracts.

L0:headquarters, or any other organization on labor relations matters or disputes; or

L0:The contract administration office must—
L1:(1) Notify the labor advisor, the contracting officer, and the head of the contracting
L0:activity when interference is likely; and
L1:(2) Disseminate information on labor disputes in accordance with departmental
L0:procedures.
L0:PGI 222.104-170 Impact of labor disputes on defense programs.
L1:(a) If the dispute involves a product, project (including construction), or service that must
L0:be obtained in order to meet schedules for urgently needed military programs or
L0:requirements, each department and agency must consider the degree of impact of potential
L0:or actual labor disputes, and each contracting activity involved must obtain and develop data
L0:reflecting the impact of a labor dispute. Upon determining the impact, the head of the
L0:contracting activity must submit a report of findings and recommendations to the labor
L0:advisor.
L2:(b)(i) The report to the labor advisor must be in narrative form and must include—
L1:(A) Location of dispute and name of contractor or subcontractor involved;
L1:(B) A description of the impact, including how the specific items or services
L0:affect the specific programs or requirements;
L1:(C) Identity of alternate sources available to furnish the supply or service within
L0:the time required; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 22
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 222
L1:(D) A description of any action taken to reduce the impact.
L1:(ii) The head of the contracting activity must submit impact reports to the agency
L0:head when—
L1:(A) Specifically requested; or
L1:(B) The department or agency considers the impact to be of sufficient urgency
L0:to warrant the attention of the agency head.
L1:(iii) The labor advisor will expand the report submitted under paragraph (b)(ii) of this
L0:subsection by addressing the following, as appropriate:
L1:(A) Description of military program, project, or service. Identify item, project, or
L0:service that will be or is being affected by the work stoppage. Describe its normal use and
L0:current functions in combat, combat support, or deterrent operations. For components or
L0:raw materials, identify the end item(s) for which they are used.
L1:(B) Requirements and assets. Identify requirements and assets in appropriate
L0:detail in terms commonly used by the DoD component.
L1:(1) For production programs, include requirements for each using military
L0:service. Where applicable, state in detail production schedule, inventory objectives, assets
L0:against these objectives, and critical shortages. For spares and highly expendable items,
L0:such as ground and air ammunition, show usage (consumption) rates and assets in
L0:absolute terms and in terms of daily, weekly, or monthly supplies. For components, include
L0:requirements for spares.
L1:(2) For projects, describe the potential adverse effects of a delay in meeting
L0:schedules, and its impact on the national security.
L1:(3) For services, describe how a loss or interruption affects the ability to
L0:support Defense operations in terms of traffic requirements, assets, testing programs, etc.
L1:(C) Possible measures to minimize strike impact. Describe—
L1:(1) Capabilities, if any, to substitute items or to use alternate sources and
L0:indicate the number of other facilities available and the relative capabilities of such facilities
L0:in meeting total requirements;
L0:service affected by a work stoppage; and
L1:(2) How much time would be required to replace the loss of the facilities or
L1:(3) The feasibility of transferring assets from theater to theater to relieve
L0:deficits in some areas of urgency.

L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 222
L1:(D) Conclusion.
L0:work stoppage.

L1:(2) Estimate the degree of criticality of a program, project, or service

L0:PGI 222.104-171 Removal of items from contractors' facilities affected by work
L0:stoppages.
L1:(a) When a contractor is unable to deliver urgent and critical items because of a work
L0:stoppage at its facility, before removing any items from the facility—
L1:(i) Contact the labor advisor to obtain the opinion of the national office of the
L0:Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service or other mediation agency regarding the effect
L0:movement of the items would have on labor negotiations. Normally removals will not be
L0:made if they will adversely affect labor negotiations.
L1:(ii) Provide a written request for removal of the material to the cognizant contract
L0:administration office. The request should include the following information:
L1:(A) Contract number.
L1:(B) A statement as to the urgency and criticality of the item needed.
L1:(C) A description of the items to be moved (nature of the item, amount,
L0:approximate weight and cubic feet, item number, etc.).
L1:(D) Mode of transportation by which the items are to be moved, if different than
L0:in the contract, and whether by Government or commercial bill of lading.
L1:(E) Destination of the material, if different from that specified in the contract.
L1:(iii) With the assistance of the labor advisor or the contract administration office,
L0:attempt to have both the management and the labor representatives involved agree to
L0:shipment of the material by normal means.
L1:(iv) If agreement for removal of the needed items cannot be reached following the
L0:procedures in paragraphs (a) (i) through (iii) of this section, the commander of the contract
L0:administration office, after obtaining approval from the labor advisor, may seek the
L0:concurrence of the parties to the dispute to permit movement of the material by military
L0:vehicles with military personnel. On receipt of such concurrences, the commander may
L0:proceed to make necessary arrangements to move the material.
L1:(v) If agreement for removal of the needed items cannot be reached following any
L0:of the procedures in paragraphs (a) (i) through (iv) of this section, refer the matter to the

L0:PGI 222.104-172 Acquisition of stevedoring services during labor disputes.
L1:(a) Use the following procedures only in the order listed when a labor dispute delays

L1:(1) Attempt to have management and labor voluntarily agree to exempt military

L1:(4) Utilize civil service stevedores to perform the work performed by contract

L1:(b) Notify the labor advisor when a deviation from the procedures in paragraph (a) of this

title: 223.7102 Policy
content:
L0:223.7102 Policy.
L1:(a) 10 U.S.C. 2692 prohibits storage, treatment, or disposal on DoD installations of
L0:toxic or hazardous materials that are not owned either by DoD or by a member of the
L0:armed forces (or a dependent of the member) assigned to or provided military housing
L0:on the installation, unless an exception in 223.7104 applies.
L1:(b) When storage of toxic or hazardous materials is authorized based on an
L0:imminent danger, the storage provided must be temporary and must cease once the
L0:imminent danger no longer exists. In all other cases of storage or disposal, the storage
L0:or disposal must be terminated as determined by the Secretary of Defense.

title: 223.7104 Exceptions
content:
L0:223.7104 Exceptions.
L1:(a) The prohibition of 10 U.S.C. 2692 does not apply to any of the following:
L1:(1) The storage, treatment, or disposal of materials that will be or have been
L0:used in connection with an activity of DoD or in connection with a service to be
L0:performed on a DoD installation for the benefit of DoD.
L1:(2) The storage of strategic and critical materials in the National Defense
L0:Stockpile under an agreement for such storage with the Administrator of General
L0:Services Administration.
L1:(3) The temporary storage or disposal of explosives in order to protect the public
L0:or to assist agencies responsible for Federal, State, or local law enforcement in storing
L0:or disposing of explosives when no alternative solution is available, if such storage or
L0:disposal is made in accordance with an agreement between the Secretary of Defense
L0:and the head of the Federal, State, or local agency concerned.
L1:(4) The temporary storage or disposal of explosives in order to provide
L0:emergency lifesaving assistance to civil authorities.
L1:(5) The disposal of excess explosives produced under a DoD contract, if the head
L0:of the military department concerned determines, in each case, that an alternative
L0:feasible means of disposal is not available to the contractor, taking into consideration
L0:public safety, available resources of the contractor, and national defense production
L0:requirements.
L1:(6) The temporary storage of nuclear materials or nonnuclear classified
L0:materials in accordance with an agreement with the Secretary of Energy.
L1:(7) The storage of materials that constitute military resources intended for use
L0:during peacetime civil emergencies in accordance with applicable DoD regulations.
L1:(8) The temporary storage of materials of other Federal agencies in order to
L0:provide assistance and refuge for commercial carriers of such material during a
L0:transportation emergency.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 23
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 223
L1:(9) The storage of any material that is not owned by DoD, if the Secretary of the
L0:military department concerned determines that the material is required or generated in
L0:connection with the authorized and compatible use of a facility of DoD, including the
L0:use of such a facility for testing material or training personnel.
L1:(10) The treatment and disposal of any toxic or hazardous materials not owned
L0:by DoD, if the Secretary of the military department concerned determines that the
L0:material is required or generated in connection with the authorized and compatible use
L0:of a facility of that military department and the Secretary enters into a contract or
L0:agreement with the prospective user that—
L1:(i) Is consistent with the best interest of national defense and environmental
L0:security; and
L1:(ii) Provides for the prospective user's continued financial and
L0:environmental responsibility and liability with regard to the material.
L1:(11) The storage of any material that is not owned by DoD if the Secretary of
L0:the military department concerned determines that the material is required or
L0:generated in connection with the use of a space launch facility located on a DoD
L0:installation or on other land controlled by the United States.
L1:(b) The Secretary of Defense may grant an exception to the prohibition in 10 U.S.C.
L0:2692 when essential to protect the health and safety of the public from imminent
L0:danger if the Secretary otherwise determines the exception is essential and if the
L0:storage or disposal authorized does not compete with private enterprise.

title: 223.7301 Policy
content:
L0:223.7301 Policy.
L0:In accordance with the DoD policy memorandum of April 8, 2009, Minimizing the Use
L0:of Hexavalent Chromium, DoD policy is to minimize hexavalent chromium (an anti-
L0:corrosive) in items acquired by DoD (deliverables and construction material), due to the
L0:serious human health and environmental risks related to its use.
subpart: SUBPART 223.73 — MINIMIZING THE USE OF MATERIALS CONTAINING

title: 223.7302 [Reserved]
content: L0:223.7302 [Reserved]
subpart: SUBPART 223.73 — MINIMIZING THE USE OF MATERIALS CONTAINING

title: 223.7303 Prohibition
content:
L0:223.7303 Prohibition.
L1:(a) Except as provided in 223.7304 and 223.7305, no contract may include a
L0:specification or standard that results in a deliverable or construction material
L0:containing more than 0.1 percent hexavalent chromium by weight in any homogeneous
L0:material in the deliverable or construction material where proven substitutes are
L0:available that provide acceptable performance for the application.
L1:(b) This prohibition is in addition to any imposed by the Clean Air Act regardless of
L0:the place of performance.
subpart: SUBPART 223.73 — MINIMIZING THE USE OF MATERIALS CONTAINING

title: 223.7304 Exceptions
content:
L0:223.7304 Exceptions.
L0:The prohibition in 223.7303 does not apply to—
L1:(a) Legacy systems and their related parts, subsystems, and components that
L0:already contain hexavalent chromium. However, the appropriate official must consider
L0:alternatives to hexavalent chromium during system modifications, follow-on
L0:procurements of legacy systems, or maintenance procedure updates; and
L1:(b) Additional sustainment related contracts (e.g., parts, services) for a system in
L0:which use of hexavalent chromium was previously approved.
subpart: SUBPART 223.73 — MINIMIZING THE USE OF MATERIALS CONTAINING

title: 223.7305 Authorization and approval
content:
L0:223.7305 Authorization and approval.
L1:(a) The prohibition in 223.7303 does not apply to critical defense applications if no
L0:substitute can meet performance requirements. The DoD policy of April 8, 2009,
L0:“Minimizing the Use of Hexavalent Chromium,” contains requirements for weighing
L0:use of hexavalent chromium versus substitutes. DoD Program Managers must consider
L0:the following factors—
L1:(1) Cost effectiveness of alternative materials or processes;
L1:(2) Technical feasibility of alternative materials or processes;
L1:(3) Environment, safety, and occupational health risks associated with the use
L0:of the hexavalent chromium or substitute materials in each specific application;
L1:(4) Achieving a DoD Manufacturing Readiness Level of at least eight for any
L0:qualified alternative;
L1:(5) Materiel availability of hexavalent chromium and the proposed alternatives
L0:over the projected life span of the system; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 23
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 223
L1:(6) Corrosion performance difference of alternative materials or processes as
L0:determined by agency corrosion subject matter experts.
L1:(b) However, unless an exception in 223.7304 applies, the incorporation of
L0:hexavalent chromium in items acquired by DoD must be specifically authorized at a
L0:level no lower than a general or flag officer or a member of the Senior Executive Service
L0:from the Program Executive Office or equivalent level, in coordination with the
L0:component Corrosion Control and Prevention Executive. Follow the procedures in PGI
L0:223.7305.

content:
L0:252.223-7001 Hazard Warning Labels.

title: 252.223-7002 Safety Precautions for Ammunition and Explosives
content:
L0:252.223-7002 Safety Precautions for Ammunition and Explosives.
L0:As prescribed in 223.370-5, use the following clause:
L0:SAFETY PRECAUTIONS FOR AMMUNITION AND EXPLOSIVES (NOV 2023)
L1:(a) Definition. “Ammunition and explosives,” as used in this clause—
L1:(1) Means liquid and solid propellants and explosives, pyrotechnics,
L0:incendiaries and smokes in the following forms:
L1:(i) Bulk,
L1:(ii) Ammunition;
L1:(iii) Rockets;
L1:(iv) Missiles;
L1:(v) Warheads;
L1:(vi) Devices; and
L1:(vii) Components of (i) through (vi), except for wholly inert items.
L1:(2) This definition does not include the following, unless the Contractor is using
L0:or incorporating these materials for initiation, propulsion, or detonation as an integral
L0:or component part of an explosive, an ammunition or explosive end item, or of a weapon
L0:system—
L1:(i) Inert components containing no explosives, propellants, or pyrotechnics;
L1:(ii) Flammable liquids;
L1:(iii) Acids;
L1:(iv) Oxidizers;
L1:(v) Powdered metals; or
L1:(vi) Other materials having fire or explosive characteristics.
L1:(b) Safety requirements.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall comply with the requirements of DoD Manual 4145.26,
L0:DoD Contractors’ Safety Manual for Ammunition and Explosives, hereafter referred to
L0:as “the manual,” in effect on the date of the solicitation for this contract. The
L0:Contractor shall also comply with any other additional requirements included in the
L0:schedule of this contract.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 23
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 223
L1:(2) The Contractor shall allow the Government access to the Contractor's
L0:facilities, personnel, and safety program documentation. The Contractor shall allow
L0:authorized Government representatives to evaluate safety programs, implementation,
L0:and facilities.
L1:(c) Noncompliance with the manual.
L1:(1) If the Contracting Officer notifies the Contractor of any noncompliance with
L0:the manual or schedule provisions, the Contractor shall take immediate steps to correct
L0:the noncompliance. The Contractor is not entitled to reimbursement of costs incurred to
L0:correct noncompliances unless such reimbursement is specified elsewhere in the
L0:contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor has 30 days from the date of notification by the Contracting
L0:Officer to correct the noncompliance and inform the Contracting Officer of the actions
L0:taken. The Contracting Officer may direct a different time period for the correction of
L0:noncompliances.
L1:(3) If the Contractor refuses or fails to correct noncompliances within the time
L0:period specified by the Contracting Officer, the Government has the right to direct the
L0:Contractor to cease performance on all or part of this contract. The Contractor shall not
L0:resume performance until the Contracting Officer is satisfied that the corrective action
L0:was effective and the Contracting Officer so informs the Contractor.
L1:(4) The Contracting Officer may remove Government personnel at any time the
L0:Contractor is in noncompliance with any safety requirement of this clause.
L1:(5) If the direction to cease work or the removal of Government personnel
L0:results in increased costs to the Contractor, the Contractor shall not be entitled to an
L0:adjustment in the contract price or a change in the delivery or performance schedule
L0:unless the Contracting Officer later determines that the Contractor had in fact complied
L0:with the manual or schedule provisions. If the Contractor is entitled to an equitable
L0:adjustment, it shall be made in accordance with the Changes clause of this contract.
L1:(d) Mishaps. If a mishap involving ammunition or explosives occurs, the Contractor
L0:shall—
L1:(1) Notify the Contracting Officer immediately;
L1:(2) Conduct an investigation in accordance with other provisions of this contract
L0:or as required by the Contracting Officer; and
L1:(3) Submit a written report to the Contracting Officer.
L1:(e) Contractor responsibility for safety.
L1:(1) Nothing in this clause, nor any Government action or failure to act in
L0:surveillance of this contract, shall relieve the Contractor of its responsibility for the
L0:safety of—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 23
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 223
L1:(i) The Contractor's personnel and property;
L1:(ii) The Government's personnel and property; or
L1:(iii) The general public.
L1:(2) Nothing in this clause shall relieve the Contractor of its responsibility for
L0:complying with applicable Federal, State, and local laws, ordinances, codes, and
L0:regulations (including those requiring the obtaining of licenses and permits) in
L0:connection with the performance of this contract.
L1:(f) Contractor responsibility for contract performance.
L1:(1) Neither the number or frequency of inspections performed by the
L0:Government, nor the degree of surveillance exercised by the Government, relieve the
L0:Contractor of its responsibility for contract performance.
L1:(2) If the Government acts or fails to act in surveillance or enforcement of the
L0:safety requirements of this contract, this does not impose or add to any liability of the
L0:Government.
L1:(g) Subcontractors.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall insert this clause, including this paragraph (g), in
L0:every subcontract that involves ammunition or explosives.
L1:(i) The clause shall include a provision allowing authorized Government
L0:safety representatives to evaluate subcontractor safety programs, implementation, and
L0:facilities as the Government determines necessary.
L1:(ii) NOTE: The Government Contracting Officer or authorized
L0:representative shall notify the prime Contractor of all findings concerning subcontractor
L0:safety and compliance with the manual. The Contracting Officer or authorized
L0:representative may furnish copies to the subcontractor. The Contractor in turn shall
L0:communicate directly with the subcontractor, substituting its name for references to
L0:“the Government”. The Contractor and higher tier subcontractors shall also include
L0:provisions to allow direction to cease performance of the subcontract if a serious
L0:uncorrected or recurring safety deficiency potentially causes an imminent hazard to
L0:DoD personnel, property, or contract performance.
L1:(2) The Contractor agrees to ensure that the subcontractor complies with all
L0:contract safety requirements. The Contractor will determine the best method for
L0:verifying the adequacy of the subcontractor's compliance.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall ensure that the subcontractor understands and agrees
L0:to the Government's right to access to the subcontractor's facilities, personnel, and
L0:safety program documentation to perform safety surveys. The Government performs
L0:these safety surveys of subcontractor facilities solely to prevent the occurrence of any
L0:mishap which would endanger the safety of DoD personnel or otherwise adversely
L0:impact upon the Government's contractual interests.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 23
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 223
L1:(4) The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer or authorized
L0:representative before issuing any subcontract when it involves ammunition or
L0:explosives. If the proposed subcontract represents a change in the place of performance,
L0:the Contractor shall request approval for such change in accordance with the clause of
L0:this contract entitled “Change in Place of Performance--Ammunition and Explosives”.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.223-7006 Prohibition on Storage, Treatment, and Disposal of Toxic or
content:
L0:252.223-7006 Prohibition on Storage, Treatment, and Disposal of Toxic or
L0:Hazardous Materials.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 223.7106 and 223.7106(a), use the following clause:
L0:PROHIBITION ON STORAGE, TREATMENT, AND DISPOSAL OF TOXIC OR
L0:HAZARDOUS MATERIALS—BASIC (SEP 2014)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Storage” means a non-transitory, semi-permanent or permanent holding,
L0:placement, or leaving of material. It does not include a temporary accumulation of a
L0:limited quantity of a material used in or a waste generated or resulting from authorized
L0:activities, such as servicing, maintenance, or repair of Department of Defense (DoD)
L0:items, equipment, or facilities.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 23
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 223
L0:“Toxic or hazardous materials” means—
L1:(i) Materials referred to in section 101(14) of the Comprehensive Environmental
L0:Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) of 1980 (42 U.S.C. 9601(14)) and
L0:materials designated under section 102 of CERCLA (42 U.S.C. 9602) (40 CFR Part 302);
L1:(ii) Materials that are of an explosive, flammable, or pyrotechnic nature; or
L1:(iii) Materials otherwise identified by the Secretary of Defense as specified in
L0:DoD regulations.
L1:(b) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2692, the Contractor is prohibited from storing,
L0:treating, or disposing of toxic or hazardous materials not owned by DoD on a DoD
L0:installation, except to the extent authorized by a statutory exception to 10 U.S.C. 2692
L0:or as authorized by the Secretary of Defense. A charge may be assessed for any storage
L0:or disposal authorized under any of the exceptions to 10 U.S.C. 2692. If a charge is to
L0:be assessed, then such assessment shall be identified elsewhere in the contract with
L0:payment to the Government on a reimbursable cost basis.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, including this
L0:paragraph (c), in all subcontracts that require, may require, or permit a subcontractor
L0:access to a DoD installation, at any subcontract tier.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Alternate I. As prescribed in 223.7106 and 223.7106(b), use the following clause,
L0:which adds a new paragraph (c) and revises and redesignates paragraph (c) of the basic
L0:clause as paragraph (d):
L0:PROHIBITION ON STORAGE, TREATMENT, AND DISPOSAL OF TOXIC OR
L0:HAZARDOUS MATERIALS—ALTERNATE I (SEP 2014)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Storage” means a non-transitory, semi-permanent or permanent holding,
L0:placement, or leaving of material. It does not include a temporary accumulation of a
L0:limited quantity of a material used in or a waste generated or resulting from authorized
L0:activities, such as servicing, maintenance, or repair of Department of Defense (DoD)
L0:items, equipment, or facilities.
L0:“Toxic or hazardous materials” means—
L1:(i) Materials referred to in section 101(14) of the Comprehensive Environmental
L0:Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) of 1980 (42 U.S.C. 9601(14)) and
L0:materials designated under section 102 of CERCLA (42 U.S.C. 9602) (40 CFR Part 302);
L1:(ii) Materials that are of an explosive, flammable, or pyrotechnic nature; or
L1:(iii) Materials otherwise identified by the Secretary of Defense as specified in
L0:DoD regulations.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 23
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 223
L1:(b) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2692, the Contractor is prohibited from storing,
L0:treating, or disposing of toxic or hazardous materials not owned by DoD on a DoD
L0:installation, except to the extent authorized by a statutory exception to 10 U.S.C. 2692
L0:or as authorized by the Secretary of Defense. A charge may be assessed for any storage
L0:or disposal authorized under any of the exceptions to 10 U.S.C. 2692. If a charge is to
L0:be assessed, then such assessment shall be identified elsewhere in the contract with
L0:payment to the Government on a reimbursable cost basis.
L1:(c) With respect to treatment or disposal authorized pursuant to DFARS
L0:223.7104(10) (10 U.S.C. 2692(b)(10), and notwithstanding any other provision of the
L0:contract, the Contractor assumes all financial and environmental responsibility and
L0:liability resulting from any treatment or disposal of toxic or hazardous materials not
L0:owned by DoD on a military installation. The Contractor shall indemnify, defend, and
L0:hold the Government harmless for all costs, liability, or penalties resulting from the
L0:Contractor’s treatment or disposal of toxic or hazardous materials not owned by DoD on
L0:a military installation.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, including this
L0:paragraph (d), in all subcontracts that require, may require, or permit a subcontractor
L0:access to a DoD installation, at any tier. Inclusion of the substance of this clause in
L0:subcontracts does not relieve the prime Contractor of liability to the Government under

content:

title: 252.223-7008 Prohibition of Hexavalent Chromium
content:
L0:252.223-7008 Prohibition of Hexavalent Chromium.
L0:As prescribed in 223.7306, use the following clause:
L0:(End of clause)
L0:PROHIBITION OF HEXAVALENT CHROMIUM (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Homogeneous material” means a material that cannot be mechanically disjointed
L0:into different materials and is of uniform composition throughout.
L1:(1) Examples of homogeneous materials include individual types of plastics,
L0:ceramics, glass, metals, alloys, paper, board, resins, and surface coatings.
L1:(2) Homogeneous material does not include conversion coatings that chemically
L0:modify the substrate.
L0:“Mechanically disjointed” means that the materials can, in principle, be separated
L0:by mechanical actions such as unscrewing, cutting, crushing, grinding, and abrasive
L0:processes.
L1:(b) Prohibition.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 23
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 223
L1:(1) Unless otherwise specified by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall
L0:not provide any deliverable or construction material under this contract that—
L1:(i) Contains hexavalent chromium in a concentration greater than 0.1
L0:percent by weight in any homogenous material; or
L1:(ii) Requires the removal or reapplication of hexavalent chromium materials
L0:during subsequent sustainment phases of the deliverable or construction material.
L1:(2) This prohibition does not apply to hexavalent chromium produced as a by-
L0:product of manufacturing processes.
L1:(c) If authorization for incorporation of hexavalent chromium in a deliverable or
L0:construction material is required, the Contractor shall submit a request to the
L0:Contracting Officer.
L1:(d) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause,
L0:including this paragraph (d), in all subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial
L0:products or commercial services, that are for supplies, maintenance and repair services,
L0:or construction materials.

content:
L0:225.771-3 Government support.

L0:operational area; and

title: 225.771-4 Law of war training
content:
L0:225.771-4 Law of war training.
L1:(a) Basic training. Basic law of war training is required for all contractor personnel
L0:supporting U.S. Armed Forces deployed outside the United States. The basic training
L0:normally will be provided through a military-run training center. The contracting
L0:officer may authorize the use of an alternate basic training source, provided the
L0:servicing DoD legal advisor concurs with the course content.
L1:(b) Advanced law of war training. (1) The types of personnel that must obtain
L0:advanced law of war training include the following:
L1:(i) Private security contractors.
L1:(ii) Security guards in or near areas of military operations.
L1:(iii) Interrogators, linguists, interpreters, guards, report writers,
L0:information technology technicians, or others who will come into contact with enemy
L0:prisoners of war, civilian internees, retained persons, other detainees, terrorists, or
L0:criminals who are captured, transferred, confined, or detained during or in the
L0:aftermath of hostilities.
L1:(iv) Other personnel when deemed necessary by the contracting officer.
L1:(2) If contractor personnel will be required to obtain advanced law of war
L0:training, the solicitation and contract must specify—
L1:(i) The types of personnel subject to advanced law of war training
L0:requirements;
L1:(ii) Whether the training will be provided by the Government or the
L0:contractor;
L1:(iii) If the training will be provided by the Government, the source of the
L0:training; and
L1:(iv) If the training will be provided by the contractor, a requirement for
L0:coordination of the content with the servicing DoD legal advisor to ensure that training
L0:content is commensurate with the duties and responsibilities of the personnel to be
L0:trained.

title: 225.871-1 Scope
content:
L0:225.871-1 Scope.
L0:This section implements 22 U.S.C. 2767 and 10 U.S.C. 2350b.

title: 225.871-2 Definitions
content:
L0:225.871-2 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L0:“Cooperative project” means a jointly managed arrangement—
L1:(1) Described in a written agreement between the parties;
L1:(2) Undertaken to further the objectives of standardization, rationalization, and
L0:interoperability of the armed forces of NATO member countries; and
L1:(3) Providing for—
L1:(i) One or more of the other participants to share with the United States the
L0:cost of research and development, testing, evaluation, or joint production (including
L0:follow-on support) of certain defense articles;
L1:(ii) Concurrent production in the United States and in another member country
L0:of a defense article jointly developed; or
L1:(iii) Acquisition by the United States of a defense article or defense service from
L0:another member country.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:“Other participant” means a cooperative project participant other than the United
L0:States.

title: 225.871-3 General
content:
L0:225.871-3 General.
L1:(a) Cooperative project authority. (1) Departments and agencies possessing the
L0:necessary authority may enter into cooperative project agreements with NATO or with
L0:one or more member countries of NATO under DoDD 5530.3, International
L0:Agreements.
L1:(2) Under laws and regulations governing the negotiation and implementation
L0:of cooperative project agreements, departments and agencies may enter into contracts,
L0:or incur other obligations, on behalf of other participants without charge to any
L0:appropriation or contract authorization.
L1:(3) Agency heads are authorized to solicit and award contracts to implement
L0:cooperative projects.
L1:(b) Contracts implementing cooperative projects must comply with all applicable
L0:laws relating to Government acquisition, unless a waiver is granted under 225.871-4. A
L0:waiver of certain laws and regulations may be obtained if the waiver—
L1:(1) Is required by the terms of a written cooperative project agreement;
L1:(2) Will significantly further NATO standardization, rationalization, and
L0:interoperability; and
L1:(3) Is approved by the appropriate DoD official.

title: 225.872-3 Solicitation procedures
content:
L0:225.872-3 Solicitation procedures.
L1:(a) Except for items developed under the U.S./Canadian Development Sharing
L0:Program, use the criteria for soliciting and awarding contracts to small business
L0:concerns under FAR Part 19 without regard to whether potential qualifying country
L0:sources exist for the end product. Do not consider an offer of a qualifying country end
L0:product if the solicitation is identified for the exclusive participation of small business
L0:concerns.
L1:(b) Send solicitations directly to qualifying country sources. Solicit Canadian
L0:sources through the Canadian Commercial Corporation in accordance with 225.870.
L1:(c) Use international air mail if solicitation destinations are outside the United
L0:States and security classification permits such use.
L1:(d) If unusual technical or security requirements preclude the acquisition of
L0:otherwise acceptable defense equipment from qualifying country sources, review the
L0:need for such requirements. Do not impose unusual technical or security requirements
L0:solely for the purpose of precluding the acquisition of defense equipment from qualifying
L0:countries.
L1:(e) Do not automatically exclude qualifying country sources from submitting offers
L0:because their supplies have not been tested and evaluated by the department or agency.
L1:(1) Consider the adequacy of qualifying country service testing on a case-by-case
L0:basis. Departments or agencies that must limit solicitations to sources whose items
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:have been tested and evaluated by the department or agency must consider supplies
L0:from qualifying country sources that have been tested and accepted by the qualifying
L0:country for service use.
L1:(2) The department or agency may perform a confirmatory test, if necessary.
L1:(3) Apply U.S. test and evaluation standards, policies, and procedures when the
L0:department or agency decides that confirmatory tests of qualifying country end
L0:products are necessary.
L1:(4) If these provisions might adversely delay service programs, obtain the
L0:concurrence of the Under Secretary of Defense (Acquisition and Sustainment), before
L0:excluding the qualifying country source from consideration.
L1:(f) Permit industry representatives from a qualifying country to attend symposia,
L0:program briefings, prebid conferences (see 15.101), and similar meetings that address
L0:U.S. defense equipment needs and requirements. When practical, structure these
L0:meetings to allow attendance by representatives of qualifying country concerns.

title: 225.7000 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:225.7000 Scope of subpart.
L1:(a) This subpart states restrictions on the acquisition of foreign products and
L0:services, imposed by DoD appropriations and authorization acts and other statutes.
L0:Refer to the acts to verify current applicability of the restrictions.
L1:(b) Nothing in this subpart affects the applicability of the Buy American statute or
L0:the Balance of Payments Program.
subpart: SUBPART 225.70 — AUTHORIZATION ACTS, APPROPRIATIONS ACTS, AND

title: 225.7001 Definitions
content:
L0:225.7001 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Assembly” means an item forming a portion of a system or subsystem that—
L1:(1) Can be provisioned and replaced as an entity; and
L1:(2) Incorporates multiple, replaceable parts.
L0:“Bearing components” means the bearing element, retainer, inner race, or outer race.
L0:“Component” means any item supplied to the Government as part of an end item or of
L0:another component, except that for use in 225.7004-2(b)(6), the term means an article,
L0:material, or supply incorporated directly into an end product.
L0:“Covered country” means—
L1:(1) The Democratic People’s Republic of North Korea;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(2) The People’s Republic of China;
L1:(3) The Russian Federation; and
L1:(4) The Islamic Republic of Iran (10 U.S.C. 4872 and 4875).
L0:“End item”, as used in sections 225.7003 and 225.7018, means the final production
L0:product when assembled or completed and ready for delivery under a line item of the
L0:contract (10 U.S.C. 4863(m)).
L0:“End product” means supplies delivered under a line item of the contract.
L0:“Large medium-speed diesel engines” means diesel engines whose revolutions per
L0:minute (RPM) fall between 300 and 1500 RPM with a displacement greater than 1500
L0:cubic inches per cylinder.
L0:“Structural component of a tent”—
L1:(1) Means a component that contributes to the form and stability of the tent (e.g.,
L0:poles, frames, flooring, guy ropes, pegs); and
L1:(2) Does not include equipment such as heating, cooling, or lighting.
L0:“Subsystem” means a functional grouping of items that combine to perform a major
L0:function within an end item, such as electrical power, altitude control, and propulsion.

citation: R-DFARS 225.7002 — Restrictions on food, clothing, fabrics, hand or measuring tools, and
subpart: SUBPART 225.70 — AUTHORIZATION ACTS, APPROPRIATIONS ACTS, AND

title: 225.7002-1 Restrictions
content:
L0:225.7002-1 Restrictions.
L1:(a) The following restrictions implement 10 U.S.C. 4862 (the “Berry Amendment”).
L0:Except as provided in 225.7002-2, do not acquire—
L1:(1) Any of the following items, either as end products or components, unless the
L0:items have been grown, reprocessed, reused, or produced in the United States:
L1:(i) Food.
L1:(ii) Clothing and the materials and components thereof, other than sensors,
L0:electronics, or other items added to, and not normally associated with, clothing and the
L0:materials and components thereof. Clothing includes items such as outerwear,
L0:headwear, underwear, nightwear, footwear, hosiery, handwear, belts, badges, and
L0:insignia. For additional guidance and examples, see PGI 225.7002-1(a)(1)(ii).
L2:(iii)(A) Tents and the structural components of tents;
L1:(B) Tarpaulins; or
L1:(C) Covers.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(iv) Cotton and other natural fiber products.
L1:(v) Woven silk or woven silk blends.
L1:(vi) Spun silk yarn for cartridge cloth.
L1:(vii) Synthetic fabric or coated synthetic fabric, including all textile fibers
L0:and yarns that are for use in such fabrics.
L1:(viii) Canvas products.
L1:(ix) Wool (whether in the form of fiber or yarn or contained in fabrics,
L0:materials, or manufactured articles).
L1:(x) Any item of individual equipment (Product or Service Code (PSC) 8465)
L0:manufactured from or containing any of the fibers, yarns, fabrics, or materials listed in
L0:this paragraph (a)(1).
L1:(2) Hand or measuring tools, unless the tools were produced in the United
L0:States. For additional guidance, see PGI 225.7002-1(a)(2).
L1:(b) In accordance with section 8123 of the Department of Defense Appropriations
L0:Act, 2014 (Pub. L. 113-76, division C, title VIII), and the same provision in subsequent
L0:Defense appropriations acts, except as provided in 225.7002-2, do not acquire a flag of
L0:the United States (PSC 8345), unless such flag, including the materials and components
L0:thereof, is manufactured in the United States, consistent with the requirements at 10
L0:U.S.C. 4862. This restriction does not apply to the acquisition of any end items or
L0:components related to flying or displaying the flag (e.g., flag poles and accessories).

title: 225.7002-2 Exceptions
content:
L0:225.7002-2 Exceptions.
L0:Acquisitions in the following categories are not subject to the restrictions in 225.7002-1:
L1:(a) Acquisitions not exceeding $200,000, except for athletic footwear purchased by
L0:DoD for use by members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine Corps upon their
L0:initial entry into the Armed Forces (37 U.S.C. 418(b)(4)).
L1:(b) Acquisitions of any of the items in 225.7002-1, if the secretary concerned
L0:determines that items grown, reprocessed, reused, or produced in the United States
L0:cannot be acquired as and when needed in a satisfactory quality and sufficient quantity
L0:at U.S. market prices. (See the requirement in 205.301 for synopsis within 7 days after
L0:contract award when using this exception.)
L1:(1) The following officials are authorized, without power of redelegation, to
L0:make such a domestic nonavailability determination:
L1:(i) The Under Secretary of Defense (Acquisition and Sustainment).
L1:(ii) The Secretary of the Army.
L1:(iii) The Secretary of the Navy.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(iv) The Secretary of the Air Force.
L1:(v) The Director of the Defense Logistics Agency.
L1:(2) The supporting documentation for the determination must include an
L0:analysis and written certification by the requiring activity, with specificity, why
L0:alternatives that would not require a domestic nonavailability determination are
L0:unacceptable.
L1:(3) Defense agencies other than the Defense Logistics Agency must follow the
L0:procedures at PGI 225.7002-2(b)(3) when submitting a request for a domestic
L0:nonavailability determination.
L1:(c) Acquisitions of items listed in FAR 25.104(a).
L1:(d) Acquisitions outside the United States in support of combat operations.
L1:(e) Acquisitions of perishable foods by or for activities located outside the United
L0:States for personnel of those activities.
L1:(f) Acquisitions of food or hand or measuring tools—
L1:(1) In support of contingency operations; or
L1:(2) For which the use of other than competitive procedures are approved on the
L0:basis of unusual and compelling urgency in accordance with FAR 6.103-2.
L1:(g) Emergency acquisitions by activities located outside the United States for
L0:personnel of those activities.
L1:(h) Acquisitions by vessels in foreign waters.
L1:(i) Acquisitions of items specifically for commissary resale.
L1:(j) Acquisitions of incidental amounts of cotton, other natural fibers, or wool
L0:incorporated in an end product, for which the estimated value of the cotton, other
L0:natural fibers, or wool—
L1:(1) Is not more than 10 percent of the total price of the end product; and
L1:(2) Does not exceed the threshold at 225.7002-2(a).
L1:(k) Acquisitions of waste and byproducts of cotton or wool fiber for use in the
L0:production of propellants and explosives.
L1:(l) Acquisitions of foods manufactured or processed in the United States, regardless
L0:of where the foods (and any component if applicable) were grown or produced.
L0:However, in accordance with section 8118 of the DoD Appropriations Act for Fiscal Year
L0:2005 (Pub. L. 108-287), this exception does not apply to fish, shellfish, or seafood
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:manufactured or processed in the United States or fish, shellfish, or seafood contained
L0:in foods manufactured or processed in the United States.
L1:(m) Acquisitions of fibers and yarns that are for use in synthetic fabric or coated
L0:synthetic fabric (but not the purchase of the synthetic or coated synthetic fabric itself),
L0:if—
L1:(1) The fabric is to be used as a component of an end product that is not a textile
L0:product. Examples of textile products, made in whole or in part of fabric, include—
L1:(i) Draperies, floor coverings, furnishings, and bedding PSG 72, Household
L0:and Commercial Furnishings and Appliances);
L1:(ii) Items made in whole or in part of fabric in PSG 83,
L0:Textile/leather/furs/apparel/findings/tents/flags, or Federal Supply Group 84, Clothing,
L0:Individual Equipment and Insignia;
L1:(iii) Upholstered seats (whether for household, office, or other use); and
L1:(iv) Parachutes (Product or Service Group (PSG) 1670); or
L1:(2) The fibers and yarns are para-aramid fibers and continuous filament para-
L0:aramid yarns manufactured in a qualifying country.
L1:(n) Acquisitions of chemical warfare protective clothing when the acquisition
L0:furthers an agreement with a qualifying country. (See 225.003(10) and the requirement
L0:in 205.301 for synopsis within 7 days after contract award when using this exception.)
L1:(o) Acquisitions that are interagency, State, or local purchases that are executed by
L0:DoD as a result of the transfer of contracts from the General Services Administration or
L0:for which DoD serves as an item manager for products on behalf of the General Services
L0:Administration. According to section 897 of the National Defense Authorization Act for
L0:Fiscal Year 2016 (Pub. L. 114-92), such contracts must not be subject to requirements
L0:under subchapter II of chapter 385 (including 10 U.S.C. 4862), to the extent such
L0:contracts are for purchases of products by other Federal agencies or State or local
L0:governments.

title: 225.7003-1 Definitions
content:
L0:225.7003-1 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L0:“Alloy” means a metal consisting of a mixture of a basic metallic element and one or
L0:more metallic, or non-metallic, alloying elements.
L1:(1) For alloys named by a single metallic element (e.g., titanium alloy), it means
L0:that the alloy contains 50 percent or more of the named metal (by mass).
L1:(2) If two metals are specified in the name (e.g., nickel-iron alloy), those metals are
L0:the two predominant elements in the alloy, and together they constitute 50 percent or
L0:more of the alloy (by mass).
L0:“Automotive item” —
L1:(1) Means a self-propelled military transport tactical vehicle, primarily intended for
L0:use by military personnel or for carrying cargo, such as—
L1:(i) A high-mobility multipurpose wheeled vehicle;
L1:(ii) An armored personnel carrier; or
L1:(iii) A troop/cargo-carrying truckcar, truck, or van; and
L1:(2) Does not include—
L1:(i) A commercially available off-the-shelf vehicle; or
L1:(ii) Construction equipment (such as bulldozers, excavators, lifts, or loaders) or
L0:other self-propelled equipment (such as cranes or aircraft ground support equipment).
L0:“Commercial derivative military article” means an item acquired by the Department of
L0:Defense that is or will be produced using the same production facilities, a common
L0:supply chain, and the same or similar production processes that are used for the
L0:production of articles predominantly used by the general public or by nongovernmental
L0:entities for purposes other than governmental purposes.
L0:“Electronic component” means an item that operates by controlling the flow of electrons
L0:or other electrically charged particles in circuits, using interconnections of electrical
L0:devices such as resistors, inductors, capacitors, diodes, switches, transistors, or
L0:integrated circuits. The term does not include structural or mechanical parts of an
L0:assembly containing an electronic component and does not include any high
L0:performance magnets that may be used in the electronic component.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:“High performance magnet” means a permanent magnet that obtains a majority of its
L0:magnetic properties from rare earth metals (such as samarium).
L0:“Produce” means—
L1:(1) Atomization;
L1:(2) Sputtering; or
L1:(3) Final consolidation of non-melt derived metal powders.
L0:“Specialty metal” means—
L1:(1) Steel—
L1:(i) With a maximum alloy content exceeding one or more of the following limits:
L0:manganese, 1.65 percent; silicon, 0.60 percent; or copper, 0.60 percent; or
L1:(ii) Containing more than 0.25 percent of any of the following elements:
L0:aluminum, chromium, cobalt, molybdenum, nickel, niobium (columbium), titanium,
L0:tungsten, or vanadium;
L1:(2) Metal alloys consisting of—
L1:(i) Nickel or iron-nickel alloys that contain a total of alloying metals other than
L0:nickel and iron in excess of 10 percent; or
L1:(ii) Cobalt alloys that contain a total of alloying metals other than cobalt and
L0:iron in excess of 10 percent;
L1:(3) Titanium and titanium alloys; or
L1:(4) Zirconium and zirconium alloys.
L0:“Steel” means an iron alloy that includes between .02 and 2 percent carbon and may
L0:include other elements.

title: 225.7004-1 Definitions
content:
L0:225.7004-1 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L0:“National technology and industrial base” means the persons and organizations that are
L0:engaged in production activities conducted within the United States, Australia, Canada,
L0:New Zealand, and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (United
L0:Kingdom). (10 U.S.C. 4801)
L0:“Star tracker” means a navigational tool used in a satellite weighing more than 400
L0:pounds whose principal purpose is to support the national security, defense, or
L0:intelligence needs of the U.S. Government.

title: 225.7004-2 do not apply to a contract or subcontract that does not exceed the simplified
content:
L0:225.7004-2 do not apply to a contract or subcontract that does not exceed the simplified
L0:acquisition threshold.
L1:(b) Buses. The restriction at 225.7004-2(a) does not apply in the following
L0:circumstances:
L1:(1) Buses manufactured outside the national technology and industrial base are
L0:needed for temporary use because buses manufactured in the national technology and
L0:industrial base are not available to satisfy requirements that cannot be postponed.
L0:Such use may not, however, exceed the lead time required for acquisition and delivery
L0:of buses manufactured in the national technology and industrial base.
L1:(2) The requirement for buses is temporary in nature. For example, to meet a
L0:special, nonrecurring requirement or a sporadic and infrequent recurring requirement,
L0:buses manufactured outside the national technology and industrial base may be used
L0:for temporary periods of time. Such use may not however, exceed the period of time
L0:needed to meet the special requirement.
L1:(3) Buses manufactured outside the national technology and industrial base are
L0:available at no cost to the U.S. Government.
L1:(c) Components for naval vessels. The restriction at 225.7004-2(b) does not apply to
L0:acquisition of spare or repair parts needed to support components for naval vessels
L0:manufactured outside the United States. Support includes the purchase of spare
L0:gyrocompasses, electronic navigation chart systems, steering controls, propulsion and
L0:machinery control systems, totally enclosed lifeboats, and welded shipboard anchor and
L0:mooring chain.
L1:(d) Components for auxiliary ships. The restriction at 225.7004-2(c) does not apply
L0:to large medium-speed engines for icebreakers or special mission ships.
L1:(e) Star trackers. The restriction at 225.7004-2(e) does not apply to acquisition
L0:programs that have received Milestone A approval as defined in 10 U.S.C. 4211 before
L0:October 1, 2021, as documented by the requiring activity official performing program
L0:management responsibilities. Include the Milestone A approval documentation in the
L0:contract file.

title: 225.7004-5 Additional restrictions on anchor and mooring chain
content:
L0:225.7004-5 Additional restrictions on anchor and mooring chain.
L1:(a) In accordance with section 8041 of the Fiscal Year 1991 DoD Appropriations Act
L0:(Pub. L. 101-511) and similar sections in subsequent DoD appropriations acts, do not
L0:acquire welded shipboard anchor and mooring chain, unless—
L1:(1) It is manufactured in the United States, including cutting, heat treating,
L0:quality control, testing, and welding (both forging and shot blasting process); and
L1:(2) The cost of the components manufactured in the United States exceeds 50
L0:percent of the total cost of components.
L1:(b) The statute at 10 U.S.C. 4864 also restricts acquisition of welded shipboard
L0:anchor and mooring chain, when used as a component of a naval vessel; however, the
L0:Appropriations Act restriction described in paragraph (a) of this section takes
L0:precedence over the restriction of 10 U.S.C. 4864 cited in 225.7004-2(b)(6).
citation: R-DFARS 225.7004-5 — Additional restrictions on anchor and mooring chain

title: 225.7004-6 Waiver of restrictions
content:
L0:225.7004-6 Waiver of restrictions.
L1:(a) Welded shipboard anchor and mooring chain. (1) In accordance with section
L0:8016 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 (Pub. L. 117-328), the secretary of
L0:the department responsible for acquisition may waive the restrictions in 225.7004-
L0:2(b)(6) and 225.7004-5, on a case-by-case basis, if—
L1:(i) Sufficient domestic suppliers are not available to meet DoD requirements
L0:on a timely basis; and
L1:(ii) The acquisition is necessary to acquire capability for national security
L0:purposes.
L1:(2) Document the waiver in a written determination and findings containing—
L1:(i) The factors supporting the waiver; and
L1:(ii) A certification that the acquisition must be made in order to acquire
L0:capability for national security purposes.
L1:(3) Provide a copy of the determination and findings to the House and Senate
L0:Committees on Appropriations.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(b) Star trackers . The waiver criteria at paragraph (c) of this section apply, except
L0:that the USD(A&S) may delegate the authority to waive a restriction for a star tracker
L0:for a particular foreign country to the service acquisition executive, without power of
L0:redelegation (section 1603, National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021
L0:(Pub. L. 116-283)).
L1:(c) Waiver of restrictions of 10 U.S.C. 4864(a). The restrictions on certain foreign
L0:purchases at 225.7004-2 may be waived, except as provided in paragraphs (a) and (b) of
L0:this section, as follows:
L2:(1)(i) USD(A&S), without power of delegation, may waive a restriction for a
L0:particular item for a particular foreign country upon determination that—
L1:(A) U.S. producers of the item would not be jeopardized by competition
L0:from a foreign country, and that country does not discriminate against defense items
L0:produced in the United States to a greater degree than the United States discriminates
L0:against defense items produced in that country; or
L1:(B) Application of the restriction would impede cooperative programs
L0:entered into between DoD and a foreign country, or would impede the reciprocal
L0:procurement of defense items under a memorandum of understanding providing for
L0:reciprocal procurement of defense items under 225.872, and that country does not
L0:discriminate against defense items produced in the United States to a greater degree
L0:than the United States discriminates against defense items produced in that country.
L1:(ii) A notice of the determination to exercise the waiver authority must be
L0:published in the Federal Register and submitted to the congressional defense
L0:committees at least 15 days before the effective date of the waiver.
L1:(iii) The effective period of the waiver must not exceed 1 year.
L1:(iv) For contracts entered into prior to the effective date of a waiver,
L0:provided adequate consideration is received to modify the contract, the waiver must be
L0:applied as directed or authorized in the waiver to—
L0:waiver; and
L1:(A) Subcontracts entered into on or after the effective date of the
L1:(B) Options for the procurement of items that are exercised after the
L0:the application of the waiver.
L1:(2) The head of the contracting activity may waive a restriction on a case-by-
L0:case basis upon execution of a determination and findings that any of the following
L0:applies:
L1:(i) The restriction would cause unreasonable delays.
L1:(ii) Satisfactory quality items manufactured in the national technology and
L0:industrial base are not available.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(iii) Application of the restriction would result in the existence of only one
L0:source for the item in the national technology and industrial base.
L1:(iv) Application of the restriction is not in the national security interests of
L0:the United States.
L1:(v) Application of the restriction would adversely affect a U.S. company.
L1:(3) A restriction is waived when it would cause unreasonable costs. The cost of
L0:an item of national technology and industrial base origin is unreasonable if it exceeds
L0:150 percent of the offered price, inclusive of duty, of items that are not of national
L0:technology and industrial base origin.

citation: R-DFARS 225.7009 — Restriction on ball and roller bearings
subpart: SUBPART 225.70 — AUTHORIZATION ACTS, APPROPRIATIONS ACTS, AND

title: 225.7009-1 Scope
content:
L0:225.7009-1 Scope.
L0:This section implements section 8065 of the Fiscal Year 2002 DoD Appropriations Act
L0:(Pub. L. 107-117) and the same restriction in subsequent DoD appropriations acts.
subpart: SUBPART 225.70 — AUTHORIZATION ACTS, APPROPRIATIONS ACTS, AND

title: 225.7009-2 Restriction
content:
L0:225.7009-2 Restriction.
L1:(a) Do not acquire ball and roller bearings unless—
L1:(1) The bearings are manufactured in the United States or Canada; and
L1:(2) For each ball or roller bearing, the cost of the bearing components
L0:manufactured in the United States or Canada exceeds 50 percent of the total cost of the
L0:bearing components of that ball or roller bearing.
L1:(b) The restriction at 225.7003-2 may also apply to bearings that are made from
L0:specialty metals, such as high carbon chrome steel (bearing steel).
subpart: SUBPART 225.70 — AUTHORIZATION ACTS, APPROPRIATIONS ACTS, AND

title: 225.7009-3 Exception
content:
L0:225.7009-3 Exception.
L0:The restriction in 225.7009-2 does not apply to contracts or subcontracts for the
L0:acquisition of commercial products, except for commercial ball and roller bearings
L0:acquired as end items.

content:

L0:timely basis; and
L1:(b) The acquisition must be made in order to acquire capability for national security
L0:purposes.

subpart: SUBPART 225.70 — AUTHORIZATION ACTS, APPROPRIATIONS ACTS, AND

title: 225.7011-1 Restriction
content:
L0:225.7011-1 Restriction.
L1:(a) In accordance with Section 8111 of the Fiscal Year 1992 DoD Appropriations Act
L0:(Pub. L. 102-172) and similar sections in subsequent DoD appropriations acts, do not
L0:acquire any of the following types of carbon, alloy, or armor steel plate for use in a
L0:Government-owned facility or a facility under the control of (e.g., leased by) DoD, unless
L0:it is melted and rolled in the United States or Canada:
L1:(1) Carbon, alloy, or armor steel plate in Federal Supply Class 9515.
L1:(2) Carbon, alloy, or armor steel plate described by specifications of the
L0:American Society for Testing Materials or the American Iron and Steel Institute.
L1:(b) This restriction—
L1:(1) Applies to the acquisition of carbon, alloy, or armor steel plate as a finished
L0:steel mill product that may be used “as is” or may be used as an intermediate material
L0:for the fabrication of an end product; and
L1:(2) Does not apply to the acquisition of an end product (e.g., a machine tool), to
L0:be used in the facility, that contains carbon, alloy, or armor steel plate as a component.

title: 225.7013-0 Scope

subpart: SUBPART 225.70 — AUTHORIZATION ACTS, APPROPRIATIONS ACTS, AND

title: 225.7013-1 Definitions
content:
L0:225.7013-1 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L0:“Corrective and preventive maintenance or repair” means—
L1:(1) Maintenance or repair actions performed as a result of a failure in order to
L0:return or restore equipment to acceptable performance levels; and
L1:(2) Scheduled maintenance or repair actions to prevent or discover functional
L0:failures.
L0:“Facilities maintenance” means the effort required to—
L1:(1) Provide housekeeping services throughout the ship;
L1:(2) Perform coating maintenance and repair to exterior and interior surfaces due to
L0:normal environmental conditions; and
L1:(3) Clean mechanical spaces, mission zones, and topside spaces.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
subpart: SUBPART 225.70 — AUTHORIZATION ACTS, APPROPRIATIONS ACTS, AND

title: 225.7013-2 Restrictions
content:
L0:225.7013-2 Restrictions.
L1:(a) Contract award (10 U.S.C. 8679). Do not award a contract to construct in a
L0:foreign shipyard—
L1:(1) A vessel for any of the armed forces; or
L1:(2) A major component of the hull or superstructure of a vessel for any of the
L0:armed forces.
L1:(b) Overhaul, repair, or maintenance (10 U.S.C. 8680). (1) Do not overhaul, repair,
L0:or maintain, in a shipyard outside the United States or Guam, a naval vessel (or any
L0:other vessel under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy) homeported in the
L0:United States or Guam.
L1:(2) This restriction on overhaul, repair, or maintenance does not apply to—
L1:(i) Voyage repairs; or
L1:(ii) Repairs necessary to correct damage sustained due to hostile actions or
L0:interventions.
L1:(3) For a naval vessel classified as a littoral combat ship and operating on
L0:deployment—
L1:(i) Corrective and preventive maintenance or repair, whether intermediate
L0:or depot level, and facilities maintenance may be performed if the work is performed by
L0:U.S. Government personnel or U.S. contractor personnel—
L1:(A) In a foreign shipyard;
L1:(B) At a facility outside of a foreign shipyard; or
L1:(C) At any other facility convenient to the vessel;
L1:(ii) Foreign workers may be used to perform corrective and preventive
L0:maintenance or repair, only if the Secretary of the Navy, without power of delegation,
L0:determines that travel by U.S. Government or contractor personnel to perform the
L0:maintenance or repair is not advisable for health or safety reasons; and
L1:(iii) Foreign contractors may perform facilities maintenance only as approved
L0:by the Secretary of the Navy.

subpart: SUBPART 225.70 — AUTHORIZATION ACTS, APPROPRIATIONS ACTS, AND

title: 225.7017-1 Definitions
content:
L0:225.7017-1 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L0:“Caribbean Basin country photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device that—
L1:(1) Is wholly manufactured in a Caribbean Basin country; or
L1:(2) In the case of a photovoltaic device that consists in whole or in part of materials
L0:from another country, has been substantially transformed in a Caribbean Basin country
L0:into a new and different article of commerce with a name, character, or use distinct
L0:from that of the article or articles from which it was transformed, provided that the
L0:photovoltaic device is not subsequently substantially transformed outside of a
L0:Caribbean Basin country.
L0:“Covered contract” means an energy savings performance contract, a utility services
L0:contract, or a private housing contract awarded by DoD, to be performed in the United
L0:States, if such contract results in DoD ownership of photovoltaic devices, by means
L0:other than DoD purchase as end products. DoD is deemed to own a photovoltaic device
L0:if the device is—
L1:(1) Installed in the United States on DoD property or in a facility owned by DoD;
L0:and
L1:(2) Reserved for the exclusive use of DoD in the United States for the full economic
L0:life of the device.
L0:“Designated country photovoltaic device” means a World Trade Organization
L0:Government Procurement Agreement (WTO GPA) country photovoltaic device, a Free
L0:Trade Agreement country photovoltaic device, a least developed country photovoltaic
L0:device, or a Caribbean Basin country photovoltaic device.
L0:“Domestic photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device that is manufactured in the
L0:United States.
L0:“Foreign photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device other than a domestic
L0:photovoltaic device.
L0:“Free Trade Agreement country photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device that—
L1:(1) Is wholly manufactured in a Free Trade Agreement country; or
L1:(2) In the case of a photovoltaic device that consists in whole or in part of materials
L0:from another country, has been substantially transformed in a Free Trade Agreement
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:country into a new and different article of commerce with a name, character, or use
L0:distinct from that of the article or articles from which it was transformed, provided that
L0:the photovoltaic device is not subsequently substantially transformed outside of a Free
L0:Trade Agreement country.
L0:“Least developed country photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device that—
L1:(1) Is wholly manufactured in a least developed country; or
L1:(2) In the case of a photovoltaic device that consists in whole or in part of materials
L0:from another country, has been substantially transformed in a least developed country
L0:into a new and different article of commerce with a name, character, or use distinct
L0:from that of the article or articles from which it was transformed, provided that the
L0:photovoltaic device is not subsequently substantially transformed outside of a least
L0:developed country.
L0:“Photovoltaic device” means a device that converts light directly into electricity through
L0:a solid-state, semiconductor process.
L0:“Qualifying country photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device manufactured in a
L0:qualifying country.
L0:“U.S.-made photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device that—
L1:(1) Is manufactured in the United States; or
L1:(2) Is substantially transformed in the United States into a new and different article
L0:of commerce with a name, character, or use distinct from that of the article or articles
L0:from which it was transformed, provided that the photovoltaic device is not
L0:subsequently substantially transformed outside of the United States.
L0:“WTO GPA country photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device that—

title: 225.7017-2 Restriction
content:
L0:225.7017-2 Restriction.
L0:In accordance with section 846 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal
L0:Year 2011 (Pub. L. 111-383), photovoltaic devices provided under any covered contract
L0:must comply with 41 U.S.C. chapter 83, Buy American, subject to the exceptions to that
L0:statute provided in the Trade Agreements Act of 1979 (19 U.S.C. 2501 et seq.).
