title: 225.7017-3 Exceptions
content:
L0:225.7017-3 Exceptions.
L0:DoD requires the contractor to utilize domestic photovoltaic devices in covered contracts
L0:that exceed the simplified acquisition threshold, with the following exceptions:
L1:(a) Qualifying country. Qualifying country photovoltaic devices may be utilized in
L0:any covered contract, because 225.103(a)(i)(A) provides an exception to the Buy
L0:American statute for products of qualifying countries, as defined in 225.003.
L1:(b) Buy American—unreasonable cost. For a covered contract that utilizes
L0:photovoltaic devices valued at less than $174,000, the exception for unreasonable cost
L0:may apply (see FAR 25.103(c)). If the cost of a foreign photovoltaic device plus 50
L0:percent is less than the cost of a domestic photovoltaic device, then the foreign
L0:photovoltaic device may be utilized.
L1:(c) Trade agreements—(1) Free Trade Agreements. For a covered contract that
L0:utilizes photovoltaic devices, photovoltaic devices may be utilized from a country
L0:covered under the acquisition by a Free Trade Agreement, depending upon dollar
L0:threshold (see FAR subpart 25.4).
L1:(2) World Trade Organization—Government Procurement Agreement. For
L0:covered contracts that utilize photovoltaic devices that are valued at $174,000 or more,
L0:only U.S.-made photovoltaic devices, designated country photovoltaic devices, or
L0:qualifying country photovoltaic devices may be utilized.

title: 225.7018-1 Definitions
content:
L0:225.7018-1 Definitions.

title: 225.7018-2 Restriction
content:
L0:225.7018-2 Restriction.
L1:(a) General. Except as provided in 225.7018-3 and 225.7018-4—
L1:(1) Effective through December 31, 2026, do not acquire any covered material
L0:melted or produced in any covered country, or any end item, manufactured in any
L0:covered country, that contains a covered material; and
L1:(2) Effective January 1, 2027, do not acquire any covered material mined,
L0:refined, separated, melted, or produced in any covered country, or any end item,
L0:manufactured in any covered country, that contains a covered material. (Section 854,
L0:Pub. L. 118-31; 10 U.S.C. 4872.)
L1:(b) Samarium-cobalt magnets and neodymium-iron-boron magnets. (1) Effective
L0:through December 31, 2026, for samarium-cobalt magnets and neodymium-iron-boron
L0:magnets, this restriction includes—
L1:(i) Melting samarium with cobalt to produce the samarium-cobalt alloy or
L0:melting neodymium with iron and boron to produce the neodymium-iron-boron alloy;
L0:and
L1:(ii) All subsequent phases of production of the magnets, such as powder
L0:formation, pressing, sintering or bonding, and magnetization.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(2) Effective January 1, 2027, for samarium-cobalt magnets this restriction
L0:includes the entire supply chain from mining or production of a cobalt and samarium
L0:ore or feedstock, including recycled material, through production of finished magnets,
L0:except as provided at 225.7018-3.
L1:(3) The restriction on melting and producing of samarium-cobalt magnets is in
L0:addition to any applicable restrictions on melting of specialty metals at 225.7003 and
L0:the clause at 252.225-7009, Restriction on Acquisition of Certain Articles Containing
L0:Specialty Metals.
L1:(4) Effective January 1, 2027, for neodymium-iron-boron magnets, this
L0:restriction includes the entire supply chain from mining of neodymium, iron, and boron
L0:through production of finished magnets, except as provided at 225.7018-3.
L1:(c) Tantalum metals and alloys. (1) Effective through December 31, 2026, for
L0:production of tantalum metals of any kind and alloys, this restriction includes the
L0:reduction or melting of any form of tantalum to create tantalum metal including
L0:unwrought, powder, mill products, and alloys. The restriction also covers all
L0:subsequent phases of production of tantalum metals and alloys.
L1:(2) Effective January 1, 2027, for production of tantalum metals of any kind and
L0:alloys, this restriction includes mining or production of a tantalum ore or feedstock,
L0:including recycled material, through production of metals of any kind and alloys, except
L0:as provided at 225.7018-3.
L1:(d) Tungsten metal powder and tungsten heavy alloy. (1) Effective through
L0:December 31, 2026, for production of tungsten metal powder and tungsten heavy alloy,
L0:this restriction includes—
L1:(i) Atomization;
L1:(ii) Calcination and reduction into powder;
L1:(iii) Final consolidation of non-melt derived metal powders; and
L1:(iv) All subsequent phases of production of tungsten metal powder, tungsten
L0:heavy alloy, or any finished or semi-finished component containing tungsten heavy
L0:alloy.
L1:(2) Effective January 1, 2027, for production of tungsten metal powder,
L0:tungsten heavy alloy, or any finished or semi-finished component containing tungsten
L0:heavy alloy, this restriction includes mining or production of a tungsten ore or
L0:feedstock, including recycled material, through production of tungsten metal powders,
L0:except as provided at 225.7018-3.

title: 225.7018-3 Exceptions
content:
L0:225.7018-3 Exceptions.
L0:The restriction in section 225.7018-2 does not apply to an acquisition—
L1:(a) At or below the simplified acquisition threshold;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(b) Outside the United States of an item for use outside the United States; or
L1:(c) Of an end item containing a covered material that is—
L1:(1) A commercially available off-the-shelf item (but see PGI 225.7018-3(c)(1)
L0:with regard to commercially available samarium-cobalt magnets), other than—
L1:(i) A commercially available off-the-shelf item that is—
L1:(A) 50 percent or more tungsten by weight effective through December
L0:31, 2026; or
L0:2027;
L1:(B) 50 percent or more covered material by weight effective January 1,
L1:(ii) Effective through December 31, 2026, a tantalum metal, tantalum alloy,
L0:or tungsten heavy alloy mill product, such as bar, billet, slab, wire, cube, sphere, block,
L0:blank, plate, or sheet, that has not been incorporated into an end item, subsystem,
L0:assembly, or component; or
L1:(iii) Effective January 1, 2027, a covered material that is a mill product such
L0:as bar, billet, slab, wire, cube, sphere, block, blank, plate, or sheet, that has not been
L0:incorporated into an end item, subsystem, assembly, or component;
L1:(2) An electronic device, unless the Secretary of Defense, upon the
L0:recommendation of the Strategic and Critical Materials Board of Directors pursuant to
L0:50 U.S.C. 98h-1 determines that the domestic availability of a particular electronic
L0:device is critical to national security (but see PGI 225.7018-3(c)(2) with regard to
L0:samarium-cobalt magnets used in electronic components); or
L1:(3) A neodymium-iron-boron magnet manufactured from recycled material if
L0:the milling of the recycled material and sintering of the final magnet takes place in the
L0:United States.
L1:(d) If the authorized agency official concerned, as specified in 225.7018-4,
L0:determines that compliant covered materials of satisfactory quality and quantity, in the
L0:required form, cannot be procured as and when needed at a reasonable price.
L1:(1) For tantalum metal, tantalum alloy, or tungsten heavy alloy, the term
L0:“required form” refers to the form of the mill product, such as bar, billet, wire, slab,
L0:plate, or sheet, in the grade appropriate for the production of a finished end item to be
L0:delivered to the Government under the contract; or a finished component assembled
L0:into an end item to be delivered to the Government under the contract.
L1:(2) For samarium-cobalt magnets or neodymium-iron-boron magnets, the term
L0:“required form” refers to the form and properties of the magnets.

title: 225.7018-4 Nonavailability determination
content:
L0:225.7018-4 Nonavailability determination.
L1:(a) Individual nonavailability determinations. (1) The head of the contracting
L0:activity is authorized to make a nonavailability determination described in 225.7018-
L0:3(d) on an individual basis (e.g., applies to only one contract).
L1:(2) The supporting documentation for the determination must include an
L0:analysis and written certification by the requiring activity that describes, with
L0:specificity, why alternatives that would not require a nonavailability determination are
L0:unacceptable. The template for an individual nonavailability determination is available
L0:at PGI 225.7018-4(a)(2).
L1:(3) Provide to USD(A&S) DASD (Industrial Policy), in accordance with the
L0:procedures at PGI 225.7018-4(a)(3)—
L1:(i) A copy of individual nonavailability determinations with supporting
L0:documentation; and
L1:(ii) Notification when individual nonavailability determinations are
L0:requested but denied.
L1:(b) Class nonavailability determinations. A class nonavailability determination
L0:(e.g., a nonavailability determinations that applies to more than one contract) requires
L0:the approval of the USD(A&S). Follow the procedures at PGI 225.7018-4(b) when
L0:submitting a request for a class nonavailability determination.
L1:(1) At least 30 days before making a nonavailability determination that would
L0:apply to more than one contract, the USD(A&S) will, to the maximum extent
L0:practicable, and in a manner consistent with the protection of national security and
L0:confidential business information—
L1:(i) Publish a notice in the GPE (https://www.sam.gov) of the intent to make
L0:the nonavailability determination; and
L1:(ii) Solicit information relevant to such notice from interested parties,
L0:including producers of mill products from covered materials.
L1:(2) The USD(A&S)—
L1:(i) Will take into consideration all information submitted in response to the
L0:notice in making a class nonavailability determination;
L1:(ii) May consider other relevant information that cannot be made part of the
L0:public record consistent with the protection of national security information and
L0:confidential business information; and
L1:(iii) Will ensure that any such nonavailability determination and the
L0:rationale for the determination are made publicly available to the maximum extent
L0:consistent with the protection of national security and confidential business
L0:information.

title: 225.7019-1 Definitions
content:
L0:225.7019-1 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L0:“Covered military installation” means a military installation in Europe identified by
L0:DoD as a main operating base.
L0:“Furnished energy” means energy furnished to a covered military installation in any
L0:form and for any purpose, including heating, cooling, and electricity.
L0:“Main operating base” means a facility outside the United States and its territories with
L0:permanently stationed operating forces and robust infrastructure.

title: 225.7019-2 Prohibition
content:
L0:225.7019-2 Prohibition.
L0:In accordance with section 2821 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal
L0:Year 2020 (Pub. L. 116-92), contracts for the acquisition of furnished energy for a
L0:covered military installation must not use any energy sourced from inside the Russian
L0:Federation as a means of generating the furnished energy for the covered military
L0:installation. The prohibition—
L1:(a) Applies to all forms of energy that are furnished to a covered military
L0:installation; and
L1:(b) Does not apply to energy converted by a third party into another form of energy
L0:and not directly delivered to a covered military installation.
subpart: SUBPART 225.70 — AUTHORIZATION ACTS, APPROPRIATIONS ACTS, AND

title: 225.7019-3 Waiver
content:
L0:225.7019-3 Waiver.
L1:(a) Request and approval of waiver. The requiring activity may submit to the
L0:contracting activity a request for waiver of the prohibition in 225.7019-2 for a specific
L0:contract for the acquisition of furnished energy for a covered military installation. The
L0:head of the contracting activity, without power of redelegation, may approve the waiver,
L0:upon certification to the congressional defense committees that—
L1:(1) The waiver of section 2821 is necessary to ensure an adequate supply of
L0:furnished energy for the covered military installation; and
L1:(2) National security requirements have been balanced against the potential
L0:risk associated with reliance upon the Russian Federation for furnished energy.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(b) Submission of waiver notice. (1) Not later than 14 days before the execution of
L0:any energy contract for which a waiver is granted under paragraph (a) of this section,
L0:the head of the contracting activity must submit to the congressional defense
L0:committees a notice of the waiver. See PGI 225.7019-3 for waiver procedures.
L1:(2) The waiver notice must include the following:
L1:(i) The rationale for the waiver, including the basis for the certifications
L0:required by paragraph (a) of this section.
L1:(ii) An assessment of how the waiver may impact DoD’s European energy
L0:resilience strategy.
L1:(iii) An explanation of the measures DoD is taking to mitigate the risk of
L0:using Russian Federation furnished energy.

L0:225.7023-1 Definitions.

L0:equipment or clothing; or

content:

L0:acquisition threshold, the contracting officer—

L0:of access to a facility or equipment by a host-nation government that may prevent it

title: 225.7300 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:225.7300 Scope of subpart.
L1:(a) This subpart contains policies and procedures for acquisitions for foreign
L0:military sales (FMS) under the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. Chapter 39).
L0:Section 22 of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2762) authorizes DoD to enter into
L0:contracts for resale to foreign countries or international organizations.
L1:(b) This subpart does not apply to—
L1:(1) FMS made from inventories or stocks;
L1:(2) Acquisitions for replenishment of inventories or stocks; or
L1:(3) Acquisitions made under DoD cooperative logistic supply support
L0:arrangements.
subpart: SUBPART 225.73 — ACQUISITIONS FOR FOREIGN MILITARY SALES

title: 225.7301 General
content:
L0:225.7301 General.
L1:(a) The U.S. Government sells defense articles and services to foreign governments
L0:or international organizations through FMS agreements. The agreement is
L0:documented in a Letter of Offer and Acceptance (LOA) (see the Defense Security
L0:Cooperation Agency (DSCA) Security Assistance Management Manual (DSCA 5105.38-
L0:M)).
L1:(b) Conduct FMS acquisitions under the same acquisition and contract
L0:management procedures used for other defense acquisitions.
L1:(c) Follow the additional procedures at PGI 225.7301(c) for preparation of
L0:solicitations and contracts that include FMS requirements.
L1:(d) See 229.170 for policy on contracts financed under U.S. assistance programs that
L0:involve payment of foreign country value added taxes or customs duties.

title: 225.7302 Preparation of letter of offer and acceptance
content:
L0:225.7302 Preparation of letter of offer and acceptance.
L0:For FMS programs that will require an acquisition, assist the DoD implementing
L0:agency responsible for preparing the Letter of Offer and Acceptance (LOA) by—
L1:(1) Working with prospective contractors to—
L1:(i) Identify, in advance of the LOA, any unusual provisions or deviations (such
L0:as those requirements for Pseudo LOAs identified at PGI 225.7301);
L1:(ii) Advise the contractor if the DoD implementing agency expands, modifies, or
L0:does not accept any key elements of the prospective contractor’s proposal;
L1:(iii) Identify any logistics support necessary to perform the contract (such as
L0:those requirements identified at PGI 225.7301); and
L1:(iv) For noncompetitive acquisitions over $10,000, ask the prospective
L0:contractor for information on price, delivery, and other relevant factors. The request for
L0:information must identify the fact that the information is for a potential foreign military
L0:sale and must identify the foreign customer; and
L1:(2) Working with the DoD implementing agency responsible for preparing the LOA,
L0:as specified in PGI 225.7302.

title: 225.7303 Pricing acquisitions for FMS
content:
L0:225.7303 Pricing acquisitions for FMS.
L1:(a) Price FMS contracts using the same principles used in pricing other defense
L0:contracts. However, application of the pricing principles in FAR parts 15 and 31 to an
L0:FMS contract may result in prices that differ from other defense contract prices for the
L0:same item due to the considerations in this section.
L1:(b) If the foreign government has conducted a competition resulting in adequate
L0:price competition (see FAR 15.403-2(b)(1)), do not require the submission of certified
L0:cost or pricing data. The contracting officer should consult with the foreign government
L0:through security assistance personnel to determine if adequate price competition has
L0:occurred.

title: 225.7303-1 do not exist, except as provided in 225.7303-5, recognize the reasonable and
content:
L0:225.7303-1 do not exist, except as provided in 225.7303-5, recognize the reasonable and
L0:allocable costs of doing business with a foreign government or international
L0:organization, even though such costs might not be recognized in the same amounts in
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:pricing other defense contracts. Examples of such costs include, but are not limited to,
L0:the following:
L1:(1) Selling expenses (not otherwise limited by FAR Part 31), such as—
L1:(i) Maintaining international sales and service organizations;
L1:(ii) Sales commissions and fees in accordance with FAR subpart 3.4;
L1:(iii) Sales promotions, demonstrations, and related travel for sales to foreign
L0:governments. Section 126.8 of the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (22 CFR
L0:126.8) may require Government approval for these costs to be allowable, in which case
L0:the appropriate Government approval must be obtained; and
L1:(iv) Configuration studies and related technical services undertaken as a
L0:direct selling effort to a foreign country.
L1:(2) Product support and post-delivery service expenses, such as—
L1:(i) Operations or maintenance training, training or tactics films, manuals,
L0:or other related data; and
L1:(ii) Technical field services provided in a foreign country related to accident
L0:investigations, weapon system problems, or operations/tactics enhancement, and
L0:related travel to foreign countries.
L1:(3) Offsets. For additional information see 225.7306.
L1:(i) An offset agreement is the contractual arrangement between the FMS
L0:customer and the U.S. defense contractor that identifies the offset obligation imposed by
L0:the FMS customer that has been accepted by the U.S. defense contractor as a condition
L0:of the FMS customer’s purchase. These agreements are distinct and independent of the
L0:LOA and the FMS contract. Further information about offsets and LOAs may be found
L0:in the Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA) Security Assistance Management
L0:Manual (DSCA 5105.38-M), chapter 6, paragraph 6.3.9.
L0:(http://samm.dsca.mil/chapter/chapter-6).
L1:(ii) A U.S. defense contractor may recover all costs incurred for offset
L0:agreements with a foreign government or international organization if the LOA is
L0:financed wholly with foreign government or international organization customer cash or
L0:repayable foreign military finance credits.
L1:(iii) The U.S. Government assumes no obligation to satisfy or administer
L0:the offset agreement or to bear any of the associated costs.
L1:(iv) Indirect offset costs are deemed reasonable for purposes of FAR parts 15
L0:and 31 with no further analysis necessary on the part of the contracting officer,
L0:provided that the U.S. defense contractor submits to the contracting officer a signed
L0:offset agreement or other documentation showing that the FMS customer has made the
L0:provision of an indirect offset a condition of the FMS acquisition. FMS customers are
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:placed on notice through the LOA that indirect offset costs are deemed reasonable
L0:without any further analysis by the contracting officer.
L1:(4) Costs that are the subject of advance agreement under the appropriate
L0:provisions of FAR part 31; or where the advance understanding places a limit on the
L0:amounts of cost that will be recognized as allowable in defense contract pricing, and the
L0:agreement contemplated that it will apply only to DoD contracts for the U.S.
L0:Government’s own requirement (as distinguished from contracts for FMS).
L1:(b) Costs not allowable under FAR part 31 are not allowable in pricing FMS
L0:contracts, except as noted in paragraphs (c) and (e) of this section.
L1:(c) The limitations for all contractors described in 231.205-18(c)(iii) and (iv) do not
L0:apply to FMS contracts, except as provided in 225.7303-5. The allowability of
L0:independent research and development (IR&D) costs and bid and proposal (B&P) costs
L0:on contracts for FMS not wholly paid for from funds made available on a nonrepayable
L0:basis is limited to the contract’s allocable share of the contractor’s total IR&D
L0:expenditures and total B&P expenditures. In pricing contracts for such FMS—
L1:(1) Use the best estimate of reasonable costs in forward pricing; and
L1:(2) Use actual expenditures, to the extent that they are reasonable, in
L0:determining final cost.
L1:(d) Under paragraph (e)(1)(A) of Section 21 of the Arms Export Control Act (22
L0:U.S.C. 2761), the United States must charge for administrative services to recover the
L0:estimated cost of administration of sales made under the Army Export Control Act.
L1:(e) The limitations in 231.205-1 on allowability of costs associated with leasing
L0:Government equipment do not apply to FMS contracts.

title: 225.7303-5 Acquisitions wholly paid for from nonrepayable funds
content:
L0:225.7303-5 Acquisitions wholly paid for from nonrepayable funds.
L1:(a) In accordance with 22 U.S.C. 2762(d), price FMS wholly paid for from funds
L0:made available on a nonrepayable basis on the same costing basis regarding profit,
L0:overhead, IR&D/B&P, and other costing elements as is applicable to acquisitions of like
L0:items purchased by DoD for its own use.
L1:(b) Direct costs associated with meeting a foreign customer’s additional or unique
L0:requirements are allowable under such contracts. Indirect burden rates applicable to
L0:such direct costs are permitted at the same rates applicable to acquisitions of like items
L0:purchased by DoD for its own use.
L1:(c) A U.S. defense contractor may not recover costs incurred for offset agreements
L0:with a foreign government or international organization if the LOA is financed with
L0:funds made available on a nonrepayable basis.
citation: R-DFARS 225.7303-5 — Acquisitions wholly paid for from nonrepayable funds
subpart: SUBPART 225.73 — ACQUISITIONS FOR FOREIGN MILITARY SALES

title: 225.7304 FMS customer involvement
content:
L0:225.7304 FMS customer involvement.
L1:(a) FMS customers may request that a defense article or defense service be obtained
L0:from a particular contractor. In such cases, FAR 6.103-4 provides authority to contract
L0:without full and open competition. The FMS customer may also request that a
L0:subcontract be placed with a particular firm. Honor such requests from the FMS
L0:customer only if the LOA or other written direction sufficiently fulfills the requirements
L0:of FAR subpart 6.1.
L1:(b) FMS customers should be encouraged to participate with U.S. Government
L0:acquisition personnel in discussions with industry to—
L1:(1) Develop technical specifications;
L1:(2) Establish delivery schedules;
L1:(3) Identify any special warranty provisions or other requirements unique to
L0:the FMS customer; and
L1:(4) Review prices of varying alternatives, quantities, and options needed to
L0:make price-performance tradeoffs.
L1:(c) Do not disclose to the FMS customer any data, including certified cost or pricing
L0:data, that is contractor proprietary unless the contractor authorizes its release.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(d) Except as provided in paragraph (e)(3) of this section, the degree of FMS
L0:customer participation in contract negotiations is left to the discretion of the contracting
L0:officer after consultation with the contractor. Provide an explanation to the FMS
L0:customer if its participation in negotiations will be limited. Factors that may limit FMS
L0:customer participation include situations where—
L1:(1) The contract includes requirements for more than one FMS customer;
L1:(2) The contract includes unique U.S. requirements; or
L1:(3) Contractor proprietary data is a subject of negotiations.
L1:(e) Do not allow representatives of the FMS customer to—
L1:(1) Direct the exclusion of certain firms from the solicitation process (they may
L0:suggest the inclusion of certain firms);
L1:(2) Interfere with a contractor’s placement of subcontracts; or
L1:(3) Observe or participate in negotiations between the U.S. Government and
L0:the contractor involving certified cost or pricing data, unless a deviation is granted in
L0:accordance with subpart 201.4.
L1:(f) Do not accept directions from the FMS customer on source selection decisions or
L0:contract terms (except that, upon timely notice, the contracting officer may attempt to
L0:obtain any special contract provisions, warranties, or other unique requirements
L0:requested by the FMS customer).
L1:(g) Do not honor any requests by the FMS customer to reject any bid or proposal.
L1:(h) If an FMS customer requests additional data concerning FMS contract prices,
L0:after consultation with the contractor, provide sufficient data to demonstrate the
L0:reasonableness of the price and reasonable responses to relevant questions concerning
L0:contract price. This data—
L1:(1) May include tailored responses, top-level pricing summaries, historical
L0:prices, or an explanation of any significant differences between the actual contract price
L0:and the estimated contract price included in the initial LOA; and
L1:(2) May be provided orally, in writing, or by any other method acceptable to the
L0:contracting officer.

title: 225.7306 Offset arrangements
content:
L0:225.7306 Offset arrangements.
L0:In accordance with the Presidential policy statement of April 16, 1990, DoD does not
L0:encourage, enter into, or commit U.S. firms to FMS offset arrangements. The decision
L0:whether to engage in offsets, and the responsibility for negotiating and implementing
L0:offset arrangements, resides with the companies involved. (See also 225.7303-2(a)(3).)

title: 225.7500 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:225.7500 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart states policies and procedures implementing the Balance of Payments
L0:Program. It applies to contracts for the acquisition of—
L1:(a) Supplies for use outside the United States; and
L1:(b) Construction to be performed outside the United States.

title: 225.7501 Policy
content:
L0:225.7501 Policy.
L0:Acquire only domestic end products for use outside the United States, and use only
L0:domestic construction material for construction to be performed outside the United
L0:States, including end products and construction material for foreign military sales,
L0:unless—
L1:(a) Before issuing the solicitation—
L1:(1) The estimated cost of the acquisition or the value of a particular
L0:construction material is at or below the simplified acquisition threshold;
L1:(2) The end product or particular construction material is—
L1:(i) Listed in FAR 25.104;
L1:(ii) A petroleum product;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(iii) A spare part for foreign-manufactured vehicles, equipment, machinery,
L0:or systems, provided the acquisition is restricted to the original manufacturer or its
L0:supplier;
L1:(iv) An industrial gas;
L0:.
L1:(v) A brand drug specified by the Defense Medical Materiel Board; or
L1:(vi) Information technology that is a commercial product, using fiscal year
L0:2004 or subsequent funds (section 535 of Division F of the Consolidated Appropriations
L0:Act, 2004 (Pub. L. 108-199), and the same provision in subsequent appropriations acts);
L1:(3) The acquisition is covered by the World Trade Organization Government
L0:Procurement Agreement;
L1:(4) The acquisition of foreign end products or construction material is required
L0:by a treaty or executive agreement between governments;
L1:(5) [Reserved];
L1:(6) The end product is acquired for commissary resale; or
L1:(7) The contracting officer determines that a requirement can best be filled by a
L0:foreign end product or construction material, including determinations that—
L1:(i) A subsistence product is perishable and delivery from the United States
L0:would significantly impair the quality at the point of consumption;
L1:(ii) An end product or construction material, by its nature or as a practical
L0:matter, can best be acquired in the geographic area concerned, e.g., ice or books; or bulk
L0:material, such as sand, gravel, or other soil material, stone, concrete masonry units, or
L0:fired brick;
L1:(iii) A particular domestic construction material is not available;
L1:(iv) The cost of domestic construction material would exceed the cost of
L0:foreign construction material by more than 50 percent, calculated on the basis of—
L1:(A) A particular construction material; or
L0:Program to the total acquisition; or
L1:(B) The comparative cost of application of the Balance of Payments
L1:(v) Use of a particular domestic construction material is impracticable;
L1:(b) After receipt of offers—
L1:(1) The evaluated low offer (see subpart 225.5) is an offer of an end product
L0:that—
L1:(i) Is a qualifying country end product;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(ii) Is an eligible product; or
L1:(iii) [Reserved]
L1:(iv) Is a nonqualifying country end product, but application of the Balance of
L0:Payments Program evaluation factor would not result in award on a domestic offer; or
L1:(2) [Reserved]
L1:(c) At any time during the acquisition process, the head of the agency determines
L0:that applying the restrictions of the Balance of Payments Program to the end product or
L0:construction material is not in the public interest.

title: 225.7900 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:225.7900 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart implements—
L1:(a) Section 890(a) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2008
L0:(Pub. L. 110-181); and
L1:(b) The requirements regarding export control of Title I of the Security Cooperation
L0:Act of 2010 (Pub. L. 111-266); the Treaty Between the Government of the United States
L0:of America and the Government of Australia Concerning Defense Trade Cooperation
L0:(the U.S.-Australia DTC Treaty); and the Treaty Between the Government of the
L0:United States of America and the Government the United Kingdom of Great Britain
L0:and Northern Ireland Concerning Defense Trade Cooperation (the U.S.-U.K. DTC
L0:Treaty). See PGI 225.7902 for additional information.

title: 225.7901 Export-controlled items
content:
L0:225.7901 Export-controlled items.
L0:This section implements section 890(a) of the National Defense Authorization Act for
L0:Fiscal Year 2008 (Pub. L. 110-181).

title: 225.7901-1 Definitions
content:
L0:225.7901-1 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L0:“Export-controlled items” means items subject to the Export Administration
L0:Regulations (EAR) (15 CFR Parts 730-774) or the International Traffic in Arms
L0:Regulations (ITAR) (22 CFR Parts 120-130). The term includes:
L1:(1) “Defense items”, defined in the Arms Export Control Act, 22 U.S.C. 2778(j)(4)(A),
L0:as defense articles, defense services, and related technical data, and further defined in
L0:the ITAR, 22 CFR Part 120.
L1:(2) “Items”, defined in the EAR as “commodities”, “software”, and “technology,”
L0:terms that are also defined in the EAR, 15 CFR 772.1.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225

title: 225.7901-2 General
content:
L0:225.7901-2 General.
L0:Certain types of items are subject to export controls in accordance with the Arms Export
L0:Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2751, et seq.), the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (22
L0:CFR parts 120-130), the Export Administration Act of 1979, as amended (50 U.S.C.
L0:App. 2401 et seq.), and the Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR parts 730-774).
L0:See PGI 225.7901-2 for additional information.

title: 225.7901-3 Policy
content:
L0:225.7901-3 Policy.
L1:(a) Both the Government and the contractor should be aware of export controls as
L0:they apply to the performance of DoD contracts.
L1:(b) The contractor bears responsibility to comply with all applicable laws and
L0:regulations regarding export-controlled items. This responsibility exists independent of,
L0:and is not established or limited by, this section.

title: 225.7901-4 Contract clause
content:
L0:225.7901-4 Contract clause.
L0:Insert the clause at 252.225-7048, Export-Controlled Items, in all solicitations and
L0:contracts.

title: 225.7902 implements requirements that relate to exports that a prospective contractor may
content:
L0:225.7902 implements requirements that relate to exports that a prospective contractor may
L0:make under a DoD solicitation or that a contractor may make in performance of a DoD
L0:contract. The company must continue to comply with domestic laws and regulations,
L0:including those pertaining to the movement of defense articles within the United States.
L0:PGI 225.7902-4 Procedures.
L1:(1) Since the DTC Treaties apply only to eligible items, a solicitation or contract falls
L0:within the scope of the DTC Treaties, and is thus eligible for DTC Treaty coverage (i.e., falls
L0:within the scope of the DTC Treaties) if it will acquire at least one defense article that is not
L0:otherwise exempt from the DTC Treaties and is required for—
L1:(i) Combined military or counterterrorism operations as described in the
L0:Implementing Arrangements;
L1:(ii) Cooperative security and defense research, development, production, and
L0:support programs that are identified pursuant to the Implementing Arrangements;
L1:(iii) Cases where the government or Australia or the government of the United
L0:Kingdom is the end user in mutually agreed specific security and defense projects, that are
L0:identified pursuant to the Implementing Arrangements; or
L1:(iv) U.S. Government end use under a solicitation or contract.
L1:(2) Since the DTC Treaties apply only to eligible items, a solicitation or contract falls
L0:within the scope of the DTC Treaties and is thus eligible for DTC Treaty coverage when it
L0:will acquire at least one defense article that is DTC Treaty-eligible and the contract falls
L0:within the scope of the DTC Treaties. Article 3, section (2) of each DTC Treaty and Section
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:4 of each Implementing Arrangement require the DTC Treaty Participants to maintain lists of
L0:defense articles to be exempted from the scope of the DTC Treaties. These exempted
L0:technology lists are incorporated in Supplement No. 1 to part of the ITAR.
L1:(3) The DTC Treaties do not apply to defense articles initially being acquired pursuant to
L0:the U.S. Foreign Military Sales (FMS) program, although, once the defense articles are
L0:acquired by the Australia or United Kingdom under an FMS case, the DTC Treaty applies as
L0:though the defense articles were exported under the DTC Treaty, subject to PGI 225.7902-
L0:2.
L1:(4) If a company obtains an export license, or other authorization, for the export of
L0:defense articles that might otherwise have been eligible for export without a license under a
L0:DTC Treaty, the terms of the export license, or other authorization, must apply unless and
L0:until the company obtains approval to transition to DTC Treaty coverage. The process and
L0:requirements for transition are described in 22 CFR 126.16(i) and 22 CFR 126.17(i),
L0:respectively.
citation: R-DFARS 225.7902 — implements requirements that relate to exports that a prospective contractor may
subpart: SUBPART 252.2 — TEXT OF PROVISIONS AND CLAUSES

title: 225.7902-1 Definitions
content:
L0:225.7902-1 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L0:“Approved Community” means the U.S. Government, U.S. entities that are registered
L0:and eligible exporters, and certain government and industry facilities in Australia or
L0:the United Kingdom that are approved and listed by the U.S. Government.
L0:“Defense articles” means articles, services, and related technical data, including
L0:software, in tangible or intangible form, listed on the United States Munitions List of
L0:the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), as modified or amended.
L0:“Defense Trade Cooperation (DTC) Treaty” means—
L1:(1) The Treaty Between the Government of the United States of America and the
L0:government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland concerning
L0:Defense Trade Cooperation, signed at Washington and London on June 21 and 26,
L0:2007; or
L1:(2) The Treaty Between the Government of the United States of America and the
L0:Government of Australia Concerning Defense Trade Cooperation, signed at Sydney on
L0:September 5, 2007.
L0:“Export” means the initial movement of defense articles from the United States
L0:Community to the United Kingdom Community and the Australia community.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:“Qualifying defense articles” means defense articles that are not exempt from the scope
L0:of the DTC Treaties as defined in 22 CFR 126.16(g) and 22 CFR 126.17(g).
L0:“Transfer” means the movement of previously exported defense articles within the
L0:Approved Community. “United Kingdom Community member” means a United
L0:Kingdom government authority or nongovernmental entity or facility on the United
L0:Kingdom Community list accessible at http://pmddtc.state.gov.
L0:“U.S. DoD Treaty-eligible requirements” means any defense article acquired by the DoD
L0:for use in a combined military or counterterrorism operation, cooperative research,
L0:development, production or support program, or DoD end use, as described in Article 3
L0:of the U.S.-U.K. DTC Treaty and sections 2 and 3 of the associated Implementing
L0:Arrangement; and Article 3 of the U.S.-Australia DTC Treaty and sections 2 and 3 of
L0:the associated Implementing Arrangement.

title: 225.7902-2 Purpose
content:
L0:225.7902-2 Purpose.
L0:The DTC Treaties permit the export of certain U.S. defense articles, technical data, and
L0:defense services, without U.S. export licenses or other written authorization under the
L0:International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR) into and within the Approved
L0:Community, as long as the exports are in support of purposes specified in the DTC
L0:Treaties. All persons must continue to comply with statutory and regulatory
L0:requirements outside of DFARS and ITAR concerning the import of defense articles and
L0:defense services or the possession or transfer of defense articles, including, but not
L0:limited to, regulations issued by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and
L0:Explosives found at 27 CFR parts 447, 478, and 479, which are unaffected by the DTC
L0:Treaties. The Approved Community consists of U.S. entities that are registered with
L0:the Department of State and are eligible exporters, the U.S. Government, and certain
L0:governmental and commercial facilities in Australia and the United Kingdom that are
L0:approved and listed by the U.S. Government. See PGI 225.7902-2 for additional
L0:information.

title: 225.7902-3 Policy
content:
L0:225.7902-3 Policy.
L0:DoD will facilitate maximum use of the DTC Treaties by prospective contractors
L0:responding to DoD solicitations and by contractors eligible to export qualifying defense
L0:articles under DoD contracts in accordance with 22 CFR 126.16(g) and 22 CFR
L0:126.17(g).

title: 225.7902-4 Procedures
content:
L0:225.7902-4 Procedures.
L1:(a) For all solicitations and contracts that may be eligible for DTC Treaty coverage
L0:(see PGI 225.7902-4(1)), the program manager must identify in writing and submit to
L0:the contracting officer prior to issuance of a solicitation and prior to award of a
L0:contract—
L1:(1) The qualifying DTC Treaty Scope paragraph (Article 3(1)(a), 3(1)(b), or
L0:3(1)(d) of the U.S.-Australia DTC Treaty or Article (3)(1)(a), (3(1)(b), or 3(1)(d) of the
L0:U.S.-U.K. DTC Treaty); and
L1:(2) The qualifying defense article(s) using the categories described in 22 CFR
L0:126.16(g) and 22 CFR 126.17(g).
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(b) If applicable, the program manager must also identify in writing and submit to
L0:the contracting officer any specific Part C, DTC Treaty-exempted technology list items,
L0:terms and conditions for applicable contract line item numbers (See PGI 225.7902-4(2)).

title: 225.7902-5 Solicitation provision and contract clause
content:
L0:225.7902-5 Solicitation provision and contract clause.
L1:(a) Insert the provision at 252.225-7046, Exports by Approved Community Members
L0:in Response to the Solicitation, in solicitations containing the clause at 252.225-7047.
L2:(b)(1) Insert the clause at 252.225-7047, Exports by Approved Community Members

L1:(i) Export-controlled items are expected to be involved in the performance of
L0:the contract and the clause at 252.225-7048 is used; and
L1:(ii) At least one contract line item is intended to satisfy a U.S. DoD Treaty-
L0:eligible requirement.
L1:(2) Complete paragraph (b) of the clause using information the program
L0:manager provided as required by 225.7902-4(a).

title: 252.225-7000 Buy American--Balance of Payments Program Certificate
content:
L0:252.225-7000 Buy American--Balance of Payments Program Certificate.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 225.601(1), use the following provision:
L0:BUY AMERICAN—BALANCE OF PAYMENTS PROGRAM CERTIFICATE—BASIC
L0:(FEB 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. “Commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item,” “component,”
L0:“critical component,” “critical item,” “domestic end product,” “foreign end product,”
L0:“qualifying country,” “qualifying country end product,” and “United States,” as used in
L0:this provision, have the meanings given in the 252.225-7001, Buy American and
L0:Balance of Payments Program—Basic clause of this solicitation.
L1:(b) Evaluation. The Government—
L1:(1) Will evaluate offers in accordance with the policies and procedures of Part
L0:225 of the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement; and

L1:(iii) Transportation on U.S. carriers—expenditures for transportation

L1:(d) Nothing in this clause requires the establishment or maintenance of detailed

title: 252.225-7008 Restriction on Acquisition of Specialty Metals
content:
L0:252.225-7008 Restriction on Acquisition of Specialty Metals.
L0:As prescribed in 225.7003-5(a)(1), use the following clause:
L0:RESTRICTION ON ACQUISITION OF SPECIALTY METALS (MAR 2013)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Alloy” means a metal consisting of a mixture of a basic metallic element and one or
L0:more metallic, or non-metallic, alloying elements.
L1:(i) For alloys named by a single metallic element (e.g., titanium alloy), it means
L0:that the alloy contains 50 percent or more of the named metal (by mass).
L1:(ii) If two metals are specified in the name (e.g, nickel-iron alloy), those metals
L0:are the two predominant elements in the alloy, and together they constitute 50 percent
L0:or more of the alloy (by mass).
L0:“Produce” means—
L1:(i) Atomization;
L1:(ii) Sputtering; or
L1:(iii) Final consolidation of non-melt derived metal powders.
L0:“Specialty metal” means—
L1:(i) Steel—
L1:(A) With a maximum alloy content exceeding one or more of the following
L0:limits: manganese, 1.65 percent; silicon, 0.60 percent; or copper, 0.60 percent; or
L1:(B) Containing more than 0.25 percent of any of the following elements:
L0:aluminum, chromium, cobalt, molybdenum, nickel, niobium (columbium), titanium,
L0:tungsten, or vanadium;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(ii) Metal alloys consisting of—
L1:(A) Nickel or iron-nickel alloys that contain a total of alloying metals other
L0:than nickel and iron in excess of 10 percent; or
L1:(B) Cobalt alloys that contain a total of alloying metals other than cobalt
L0:and iron in excess of 10 percent;
L1:(iii) Titanium and titanium alloys; or
L1:(iv) Zirconium and zirconium alloys.
L0:“Steel” means an iron alloy that includes between .02 and 2 percent carbon and may
L0:include other elements.
L1:(b) Any specialty metal delivered under this contract shall be melted or produced in
L0:the United States or its outlying areas.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.225-7008 — Restriction on Acquisition of Specialty Metals

title: 252.225-7009 Restriction on Acquisition of Certain Articles Containing
content:
L0:252.225-7009 Restriction on Acquisition of Certain Articles Containing
L0:Specialty Metals.
L0:As prescribed in 225.7003-5(a)(2), use the following clause:
L0:RESTRICTION ON ACQUISITION OF CERTAIN ARTICLES CONTAINING
L0:SPECIALTY METALS (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Alloy” means a metal consisting of a mixture of a basic metallic element and one or
L0:more metallic, or non-metallic, alloying elements.
L1:(i) For alloys named by a single metallic element (e.g., titanium alloy), it means
L0:that the alloy contains 50 percent or more of the named metal (by mass).
L1:(ii) If two metals are specified in the name (e.g, nickel-iron alloy), those metals
L0:are the two predominant elements in the alloy, and together they constitute 50 percent
L0:or more of the alloy (by mass).
L0:“Assembly” means an item forming a portion of a system or subsystem that—
L1:(i) Can be provisioned and replaced as an entity; and
L1:(ii) Incorporates multiple, replaceable parts.
L0:“Commercial derivative military article” means an item acquired by the Department
L0:of Defense that is or will be produced using the same production facilities, a common
L0:supply chain, and the same or similar production processes that are used for the
L0:production of articles predominantly used by the general public or by nongovernmental
L0:entities for purposes other than governmental purposes.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:“Commercially available off-the-shelf item”—
L1:(i) Means any item of supply that is—
L1:(A) A commercial product (as defined in paragraph (1) of the definition of
L0:“commercial product” in section 2.101 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation);
L1:(B) Sold in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(C) Offered to the Government, under this contract or a subcontract at any
L0:tier, without modification, in the same form in which it is sold in the commercial
L0:marketplace; and
L1:(ii) Does not include bulk cargo, as defined in 46 U.S.C. 40102(4), such as
L0:agricultural products and petroleum products.
L0:“Component” means any item supplied to the Government as part of an end item or
L0:of another component.
L0:“Electronic component” means an item that operates by controlling the flow of
L0:electrons or other electrically charged particles in circuits, using interconnections of
L0:electrical devices such as resistors, inductors, capacitors, diodes, switches, transistors,
L0:or integrated circuits. The term does not include structural or mechanical parts of an
L0:assembly containing an electronic component, and does not include any high
L0:performance magnets that may be used in the electronic component.
L0:“End item” means the final production product when assembled or completed and
L0:ready for delivery under a line item of this contract.
L0:“High performance magnet” means a permanent magnet that obtains a majority of
L0:its magnetic properties from rare earth metals (such as samarium).
L0:“Produce” means—
L1:(i) Atomization;
L1:(ii) Sputtering; or
L1:(iii) Final consolidation of non-melt derived metal powders.
L0:“Qualifying country” means any country listed in the definition of “Qualifying
L0:country” at 225.003 of the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement
L1:(DFARS).
L0:“Specialty metal” means—
L1:(i) Steel—
L1:(A) With a maximum alloy content exceeding one or more of the following
L0:limits: manganese, 1.65 percent; silicon, 0.60 percent; or copper, 0.60 percent; or
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(B) Containing more than 0.25 percent of any of the following elements:
L0:aluminum, chromium, cobalt, molybdenum, nickel, niobium (columbium), titanium,
L0:tungsten, or vanadium;
L1:(ii) Metal alloys consisting of—
L1:(A) Nickel or iron-nickel alloys that contain a total of alloying metals other
L0:than nickel and iron in excess of 10 percent; or
L1:(B) Cobalt alloys that contain a total of alloying metals other than cobalt
L0:and iron in excess of 10 percent;
L1:(iii) Titanium and titanium alloys; or
L1:(iv) Zirconium and zirconium alloys.
L0:“Steel” means an iron alloy that includes between .02 and 2 percent carbon and may
L0:include other elements.
L0:“Subsystem” means a functional grouping of items that combine to perform a major
L0:function within an end item, such as electrical power, attitude control, and propulsion.
L1:(b) Restriction. Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this clause, any specialty
L0:metals incorporated in items delivered under this contract shall be melted or produced
L0:in the United States, its outlying areas, or a qualifying country.
L1:(c) Exceptions. The restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause does not apply to—
L1:(1) Electronic components.
L2:(2)(i) Commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) items, other than—
L1:(A) Specialty metal mill products, such as bar, billet, slab, wire, plate, or
L0:sheet, that have not been incorporated into COTS end items, subsystems, assemblies,
L0:or components;
L0:castings are incorporated into COTS end items, subsystems, or assemblies;
L1:(B) Forgings or castings of specialty metals, unless the forgings or
L1:(C) Commercially available high performance magnets that contain
L0:specialty metal, unless such high performance magnets are incorporated into COTS end
L0:items or subsystems; and
L1:(D) COTS fasteners, unless—
L0:subsystems, assemblies, or components; or
L1:(1) The fasteners are incorporated into COTS end items,
L0:paragraph (c)(3) of this clause.
L1:(2) The fasteners qualify for the commercial product exception in
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(ii) A COTS item is considered to be “without modification” if it is not
L0:modified prior to contractual acceptance by the next higher tier in the supply chain.
L1:(A) Specialty metals in a COTS item that was accepted without
L0:modification by the next higher tier are excepted from the restriction in paragraph (b) of
L0:this clause, and remain excepted, even if a piece of the COTS item subsequently is
L0:removed (e.g., the end is removed from a COTS screw or an extra hole is drilled in a
L0:COTS bracket).
L1:(B) Specialty metals that were not contained in a COTS item upon
L0:acceptance, but are added to the COTS item after acceptance, are subject to the
L0:restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause (e.g., a special reinforced handle made of
L0:specialty metal is added to a COTS item).
L1:(C) If two or more COTS items are combined in such a way that the
L0:resultant item is not a COTS item, only the specialty metals involved in joining the
L0:COTS items together are subject to the restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause (e.g., a
L0:COTS aircraft is outfitted with a COTS engine that is not the COTS engine normally
L0:provided with the aircraft).
L1:(D) For COTS items that are normally sold in the commercial
L0:marketplace with various options, items that include such options are also COTS items.
L0:However, if a COTS item is offered to the Government with an option that is not
L0:normally offered in the commercial marketplace, that option is subject to the restriction
L0:in paragraph (b) of this clause (e.g. - An aircraft is normally sold to the public with an
L0:option for installation kits. The Department of Defense requests a military-unique kit.
L0:The aircraft is still a COTS item, but the military-unique kit is not a COTS item and
L0:must comply with the restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause unless another
L0:exception applies).
L1:(3) Fasteners that are commercial products, if the manufacturer of the fasteners
L0:certifies it will purchase, during the relevant calendar year, an amount of domestically
L0:melted or produced specialty metal, in the required form, for use in the production of
L0:fasteners for sale to the Department of Defense and other customers, that is not less
L0:than 50 percent of the total amount of the specialty metal that it will purchase to carry
L0:out the production of such fasteners for all customers.
L1:(4) Items manufactured in a qualifying country.
L1:(5) Specialty metals for which the Government has determined in accordance
L0:with DFARS 225.7003-3 that specialty metal melted or produced in the United States,
L0:its outlying areas, or a qualifying country cannot be acquired as and when needed in—
L1:(i) A satisfactory quality;
L1:(ii) A sufficient quantity; and
L1:(iii) The required form. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 4863(m)(4), the term
L0:“required form” in this clause refers to the form of the mill product, such as bar, billet,
L0:wire, slab, plate, or sheet, in the grade appropriate for the production of a finished end
L0:item to be delivered to the Government under this contract; or a finished component
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:assembled into an end item to be delivered to the Government under this contract.
L1:(6) End items containing a minimal amount of otherwise noncompliant
L0:specialty metals (i.e., specialty metals not melted or produced in the United States, an
L0:outlying area, or a qualifying country, that are not covered by one of the other
L0:exceptions in this paragraph (c)), if the total weight of such noncompliant metals does
L0:not exceed 2 percent of the total weight of all specialty metals in the end item, as
L0:estimated in good faith by the Contractor. This exception does not apply to high
L0:performance magnets containing specialty metals.
L1:(d) Compliance for commercial derivative military articles.
L1:(1) As an alternative to the compliance required in paragraph (b) of this clause,
L0:the Contractor may purchase an amount of domestically melted or produced specialty
L0:metals in the required form, for use during the period of contract performance in the
L0:production of the commercial derivative military article and the related commercial
L0:article, if—
L1:(i) The Contracting Officer has notified the Contractor of the items to be
L0:delivered under this contract that have been determined by the Government to meet
L0:the definition of “commercial derivative military article”; and
L1:(ii) For each item that has been determined by the Government to meet the
L0:definition of “commercial derivative military article,” the Contractor has certified, as
L0:specified in the provision of the solicitation entitled “Commercial Derivative Military
L0:Article—Specialty Metals Compliance Certificate” (DFARS 252.225-7010), that the
L0:Contractor and its subcontractor(s) will enter into a contractual agreement or
L0:agreements to purchase an amount of domestically melted or produced specialty metal
L0:in the required form, for use during the period of contract performance in the production
L0:of each commercial derivative military article and the related commercial article, that is
L0:not less than the Contractor’s good faith estimate of the greater of—
L1:(A) An amount equivalent to 120 percent of the amount of specialty
L0:metal that is required to carry out the production of the commercial derivative military
L0:article (including the work performed under each subcontract); or
L1:(B) An amount equivalent to 50 percent of the amount of specialty
L0:metal that will be purchased by the Contractor and its subcontractors for use during
L0:such period in the production of the commercial derivative military article and the
L0:related commercial article.
L1:(2) For the purposes of this alternative, the amount of specialty metal that is
L0:required to carry out production of the commercial derivative military article includes
L0:specialty metal contained in any item, including COTS items.
L1:(e) Subcontracts.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall exclude and reserve paragraph (d) and this paragraph
L2:(e)(1) when flowing down this clause to subcontracts.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall insert paragraphs (a) through (c) and this paragraph
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L2:(e)(2) of this clause in subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial products,
L0:that are for items containing specialty metals to ensure compliance of the end products
L0:that the Contractor will deliver to the Government. When inserting this clause in
L0:subcontracts, the Contractor shall—
L1:(i) Modify paragraph (c)(6) of this clause only as necessary to facilitate
L0:management of the minimal content exception at the prime contract level. The minimal
L0:content exception does not apply to specialty metals contained in high-performance
L0:magnets; and
L1:(ii) Not further alter the clause other than to identify the appropriate parties.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.225-7039 Defense Contractors Performing Private Security Functions
content:
L0:252.225-7039 Defense Contractors Performing Private Security Functions
L0:Outside the United States.
L0:As prescribed in 225.702-6, insert the following clause:
L0:DEFENSE CONTRACTORS PERFORMING PRIVATE SECURITY FUNCTIONS
L0:OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:“Full cooperation”—
L1:(1) Means disclosure to the Government of the information sufficient to
L0:identify the nature and extent of the incident and the individuals responsible for
L0:the conduct. It includes providing timely and complete response to Government
L0:auditors’ and investigators’ requests for documents and access to employees with
L0:information;
L1:(2) Does not foreclose any contractor rights arising in law, the FAR or the
L0:terms of the contract. It does not require—
L1:(i) The contractor to waive its attorney-client privilege or the protections
L0:afforded by the attorney work product doctrine; or
L1:(ii) Any officer, director, owner, or employee of the contractor, including
L0:a sole proprietor, to waive his or her attorney-client privilege or Fifth Amendment
L0:rights; and
L1:(3) Does not restrict the contractor from—
L1:(i) Conducting an internal investigation; or
L1:(ii) Defending a proceeding or dispute arising under the contract or
L0:related to a potential or disclosed violation.
L0:“Private security functions” means the following activities engaged in by a
L0:contractor:
L1:(1) Guarding of personnel, facilities, designated sites or property of a Federal
L0:agency, the contractor or subcontractor, or a third party.
L1:(2) Any other activity for which personnel are required to carry weapons in the
L0:performance of their duties in accordance with the terms of this contract.
L1:(b) Applicability. If this contract is performed both in a designated area and in
L0:an area that is not designated, the clause only applies to performance in the
L0:designated area. Designated areas are areas outside the United States of—
L1:(1) Contingency operations;
L1:(2) Combat operations, as designated by the Secretary of Defense;
L1:(3) Other significant military operations (as defined in 32 CFR part 159),
L0:designated by the Secretary of Defense upon agreement of the Secretary of State;
L1:(4) Peace operations, consistent with Joint Publication 3-07.3; or
L1:(5) Other military operations or military exercises, when designated by the
L0:Combatant Commander.
L1:(c) Requirements. The Contractor shall—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(1) Ensure that all Contractor personnel who are responsible for performing
L0:private security functions under this contract comply with 32 CFR part 159 and any
L0:orders, directives, or instructions to contractors performing private security
L0:functions that are identified in the contract for—
L1:(i) Registering, processing, accounting for, managing, overseeing and
L0:keeping appropriate records of personnel performing private security functions;
L1:(ii) Authorizing, accounting for and registering in Synchronized
L0:Predeployment and Operational Tracker (SPOT), weapons to be carried by or
L0:available to be used by personnel performing private security functions;
L1:(iii) Identifying and registering in SPOT armored vehicles, helicopters
L0:and other military vehicles operated by Contractors performing private security
L0:functions; and
L1:(iv) In accordance with orders and instructions established by the
L0:applicable Combatant Commander, reporting incidents in which—
L0:functions;
L1:(A) A weapon is discharged by personnel performing private security
L0:killed, or injured;
L1:(B) Personnel performing private security functions are attacked,
L0:of conduct by Contractor personnel;
L1:(C) Persons are killed or injured or property is destroyed as a result
L1:(D) A weapon is discharged against personnel performing private
L0:security functions or personnel performing such functions believe a weapon was so
L0:discharged; or
L1:(E) Active, non-lethal countermeasures (other than the discharge of
L0:a weapon) are employed by personnel performing private security functions in
L0:response to a perceived immediate threat;
L1:(2) Ensure that Contractor personnel who are responsible for performing
L0:private security functions under this contract are briefed on and understand their
L0:obligation to comply with—
L1:(i) Qualification, training, screening (including, if applicable, thorough
L0:background checks) and security requirements established by 32 CFR part 159;
L1:(ii) Applicable laws and regulations of the United States and the host
L0:country and applicable treaties and international agreements regarding
L0:performance of private security functions;
L1:(iii) Orders, directives, and instructions issued by the applicable
L0:Combatant Commander or relevant Chief of Mission relating to weapons,
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:equipment, force protection, security, health, safety, or relations and interaction
L0:with locals; and
L1:(iv) Rules on the use of force issued by the applicable Combatant
L0:Commander or relevant Chief of Mission for personnel performing private security
L0:functions;
L1:(3) Provide full cooperation with any Government-authorized investigation
L0:of incidents reported pursuant to paragraph (c)(1)(iv) of this clause and incidents of
L0:alleged misconduct by personnel performing private security functions under this
L0:contract by providing—
L1:(i) Access to employees performing private security functions; and
L1:(ii) Relevant information in the possession of the Contractor regarding
L0:the incident concerned; and
L1:(4) Comply with ANSI/ASIS PSC.1-2012, American National Standard,
L0:Management System for Quality of Private Security Company Operations—
L0:Requirements with Guidance or the International Standard ISO 18788,
L0:Management System for Private Security Operations—Requirements with
L0:Guidance (located at http://www.acq.osd.mil/log/PS/psc.html).
L1:(d) Remedies. In addition to other remedies available to the Government—
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer may direct the Contractor, at its own expense, to
L0:remove and replace any Contractor or subcontractor personnel performing private
L0:security functions who fail to comply with or violate applicable requirements of this
L0:clause or 32 CFR part 159. Such action may be taken at the Government’s
L0:discretion without prejudice to its rights under any other provision of this contract;
L1:(2) The Contractor’s failure to comply with the requirements of this clause
L0:will be included in appropriate databases of past performance and considered in any
L0:responsibility determination or evaluation of past performance; and
L1:(3) If this is an award-fee contract, the Contractor’s failure to comply with
L0:the requirements of this clause shall be considered in the evaluation of the
L0:Contractor’s performance during the relevant evaluation period, and the
L0:Contracting Officer may treat such failure to comply as a basis for reducing or
L0:denying award fees for such period or for recovering all or part of award fees
L0:previously paid for such period.
L1:(e) Rule of construction. The duty of the Contractor to comply with the
L0:requirements of this clause shall not be reduced or diminished by the failure of a
L0:higher- or lower-tier Contractor or subcontractor to comply with the clause
L0:requirements or by a failure of the contracting activity to provide required
L0:oversight.
L1:(f) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause,
L0:including this paragraph (f), in subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:products or commercial services, when private security functions will be performed
L0:outside the United States in areas of—
L1:(1) Contingency operations;
L1:(2) Combat operations, as designated by the Secretary of Defense;
L1:(3) Other significant military operations (as defined in 32 CFR part 159),
L0:designated by the Secretary of Defense upon agreement of the Secretary of State;
L1:(4) Peace operations, consistent with Joint Publication 3-07.3; or
L1:(5) Other military operations or military exercises, when designated by the
L0:Combatant Commander.
L0:(End of clause)
