title: 252.225-7040 Contractor Personnel Supporting U.S. Armed Forces Deployed
content:
L0:252.225-7040 Contractor Personnel Supporting U.S. Armed Forces Deployed
L0:Outside the United States.
L0:As prescribed in 222.771-5(a), use the following clause:
L0:CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL SUPPORTING U.S. ARMED FORCES DEPLOYED
L0:OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES (AUG 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Combatant Commander” means the commander of a unified or specified combatant
L0:command established in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 161.
L0:“Contractors authorized to accompany the Force,” or “CAAF,” means contractor
L0:personnel, including all tiers of subcontractor personnel, who are authorized to
L0:accompany U.S. Armed Forces in applicable operations and have been afforded CAAF
L0:status through a letter of authorization. CAAF generally include all U.S. citizen n and
L0:third-country national employees not normally residing within the operational area
L0:whose area of performance is in the direct vicinity of U.S. Armed Forces and who
L0:routinely are collocated with the U.S. Armed Forces (especially in non-permissive
L0:environments). Personnel collocated with U.S. Armed Forces shall be afforded CAAF
L0:status through a letter of authorization. In some cases, Combatant Commander
L0:subordinate commanders may designate mission-essential host nation or local national
L0:contractor employees (e.g., interpreters) as CAAF. CAAF includes contractors
L0:previously identified as contractors deploying with the U.S. Armed Forces. CAAF
L0:status does not apply to contractor personnel in support of applicable operations within
L0:the boundaries and territories of the United States.
L0:“Designated operational area” means a geographic area designated by the
L0:combatant commander or subordinate joint force commander for the conduct or
L0:support of specified military operations.
L0:“Designated reception site” means the designated place for the reception,
L0:staging, integration, and onward movement of contractors deploying during a
L0:contingency. The designated reception site includes assigned joint reception centers
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:and other Service or private reception sites.
L0:“Law of war” means that part of international law that regulates the conduct of
L0:armed hostilities. The law of war encompasses all international law for the conduct of
L0:hostilities binding on the United States or its individual citizens, including treaties and
L0:international agreements to which the United States is a party, and applicable
L0:customary international law.
L0:“Non-CAAF” means personnel who are not designated as CAAF, such as local
L0:national (LN) employees and non-LN employees who are permanent residents in
L0:the operational area or third-country nationals not routinely residing with U.S.
L0:Armed Forces (and third-country national expatriates who are permanent residents
L0:in the operational area) who perform support functions away from the close
L0:proximity of, and do not reside with, U.S. Armed Forces. Government-furnished
L0:support to non-CAAF is typically limited to force protection, emergency medical
L0:care, and basic human needs (e.g., bottled water, latrine facilities, security, and food
L0:when necessary) when performing their jobs in the direct vicinity of U.S. Armed
L0:Forces. Non-CAAF status does not apply to contractor personnel in support of
L0:applicable operations within the boundaries and territories of the United States.
L0:“Subordinate joint force commander” means a sub-unified commander or joint
L0:task force commander.
L1:(b) General.
L1:(1) This clause applies to both CAAF and non-CAAF when performing in a
L0:designated operational area outside the United States to support U.S. Armed Forces
L0:deployed outside the United States in—
L1:(i) Contingency operations;
L1:(ii) Peace operations, consistent with Joint Publication 3-07.3; or
L1:(iii) Other military operations or military exercises, when designated by the
L0:Combatant Commander or as directed by the Secretary of Defense.
L1:(2) Contract performance in support of U.S. Armed Forces deployed outside the
L0:United States may require work in dangerous or austere conditions. Except as
L0:otherwise provided in the contract, the Contractor accepts the risks associated with
L0:required contract performance in such operations.
L1:(3) When authorized in accordance with paragraph (j) of this clause to carry
L0:arms for personal protection, Contractor personnel are only authorized to use force for
L0:individual self-defense.
L1:(4) Unless immune from host nation jurisdiction by virtue of an international
L0:agreement or international law, inappropriate use of force by contractor personnel
L0:supporting the U.S. Armed Forces can subject such personnel to United States or host
L0:nation prosecution and civil liability (see paragraphs (d) and (j)(3) of this clause).
L1:(5) Service performed by Contractor personnel subject to this clause is not
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:active duty or service under 38 U.S.C. 106 note.
L1:(c) Support.
L2:(1)(i) The Combatant Commander will develop a security plan for protection of
L0:Contractor personnel in locations where there is not sufficient or legitimate civil
L0:authority, when the Combatant Commander decides it is in the interests of the
L0:Government to provide security because—
L1:(A) The Contractor cannot obtain effective security services;
L1:(B) Effective security services are unavailable at a reasonable cost; or
L1:(C) Threat conditions necessitate security through military means.
L1:(ii) In appropriate cases, the Combatant Commander may provide security
L0:through military means, commensurate with the level of security provided DoD
L0:civilians.
L2:(2)(i) Generally, CAAF will be afforded emergency medical and dental care if
L0:injured while supporting applicable operations. Additionally, non-CAAF employees who
L0:are injured while in the vicinity of U. S. Armed Forces will normally receive emergency
L0:medical and dental care. Emergency medical and dental care includes medical care
L0:situations in which life, limb, or eyesight is jeopardized. Examples of emergency
L0:medical and dental care include examination and initial treatment of victims of sexual
L0:assault; refills of prescriptions for life-dependent drugs; repair of broken bones,
L0:lacerations, infections; and traumatic injuries to the dentition. Hospitalization will be
L0:limited to stabilization and short-term medical treatment with an emphasis on return
L0:to duty or placement in the patient movement system.
L1:(ii) When the Government provides medical treatment or transportation of
L0:Contractor personnel to a selected civilian facility, the Contractor shall ensure that the
L0:Government is reimbursed for any costs associated with such treatment or
L0:transportation.
L1:(iii) Medical or dental care beyond this standard is not authorized.
L1:(3) Contractor personnel must have a Synchronized Predeployment and
L0:Operational Tracker (SPOT)-generated letter of authorization signed by the
L0:Contracting Officer in order to process through a deployment center or to travel to,
L0:from, or within the designated operational area. The letter of authorization also will
L0:identify any additional authorizations, privileges, or Government support that
L0:Contractor personnel are entitled to under this contract. Contractor personnel who are
L0:issued a letter of authorization shall carry it with them at all times while deployed.
L1:(4) Unless specified elsewhere in this contract, the Contractor is responsible for
L0:all other support required for its personnel engaged in the designated operational area
L0:under this contract.
L1:(d) Compliance with laws and regulations.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(1) The Contractor shall comply with, and shall ensure that its personnel
L0:supporting U.S. Armed Forces deployed outside the United States as specified in
L0:paragraph (b)(1) of this clause are familiar with and comply with, all applicable—
L1:(i) United States, host country, and third country national laws;
L1:(ii) Provisions of the law of war, as well as any other applicable treaties and
L0:international agreements;
L1:(iii) United States regulations, directives, instructions, policies, and
L0:procedures; and
L1:(iv) Orders, directives, and instructions issued by the Combatant
L0:Commander, including those relating to force protection, security, health, safety, or
L0:relations and interaction with local nationals.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall institute and implement an effective program to
L0:prevent violations of the law of war by its employees and subcontractors, including law
L0:of war training in accordance with paragraph (e)(1)(vii) of this clause.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall ensure that CAAF and non-CAAF are aware—
L1:(i) Of the DoD definition of “sexual assault” in DoD Directive 6495.01,
L0:Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Program;
L1:(ii) That the offenses addressed by the definition are covered under the
L0:Uniform Code of Military Justice (see paragraph (e)(2)(iv) of this clause). Other sexual
L0:misconduct may constitute offenses under the Uniform Code of Military Justice,
L0:Federal law, such as the Military Extraterritorial Jurisdiction Act, or host nation laws;
L0:and
L1:(iii) That the offenses not covered by the Uniform Code of Military Justice
L0:may nevertheless have consequences to the contractor employees (see paragraph (h)(1)
L0:of this clause).
L1:(4) The Contractor shall report to the appropriate investigative authorities,
L0:identified in paragraph (d)(6) of this clause, any alleged offenses under—
L1:(i) The Uniform Code of Military Justice (chapter 47 of title 10, United
L0:States Code) (applicable to contractors serving with or accompanying an armed force in
L0:the field during a declared war or contingency operations); or
L1:(ii) The Military Extraterritorial Jurisdiction Act (chapter 212 of title 18,
L0:United States Code).
L1:(5) The Contractor shall provide to all contractor personnel who will perform
L0:work on a contract in the deployed area, before beginning such work, information on the
L0:following:
L1:(i) How and where to report an alleged crime described in paragraph (d)(4)
L0:of this clause.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(ii) Where to seek victim and witness protection and assistance available to
L0:contractor personnel in connection with an alleged offense described in paragraph (d)(4)
L0:of this clause.
L1:(iii) That this section does not create any rights or privileges that are not
L0:authorized by law or DoD policy.
L1:(6) The appropriate investigative authorities to which suspected crimes shall be
L0:reported include the following—
L1:(i) US Army Criminal Investigation Command at http://www.cid.army.mil/;
L1:(ii) Air Force Office of Special Investigations at https://www.osi.af.mil/;
L1:(iii) Navy Criminal Investigative Service at http://www.ncis.navy.mil/;
L1:(iv) Defense Criminal Investigative Service at http://www.dodig.mil/;
L1:(v) To any command of any supported military element or the command of
L0:any base.
L1:(7) Personnel seeking whistleblower protection from reprisals for reporting
L0:criminal acts shall seek guidance through the DoD Inspector General hotline at 800-
L0:424-9098 or www.dodig.mil/. Personnel seeking other forms of victim or witness
L0:protections should contact the nearest military law enforcement office.
L2:(8)(i) The Contractor shall ensure that Contractor employees supporting the U.S.
L0:Armed Forces are aware of their rights to—
L0:passport or driver’s license, regardless of the documents’ issuing authority;
L1:(A) Hold their own identity or immigration documents, such as
L1:(B) Receive agreed upon wages on time;
L1:(C) Take lunch and work-breaks;
L1:(D) Elect to terminate employment at any time;
L1:(E) Identify grievances without fear of reprisal;
L0:understand;
L1:(F) Have a copy of their employment contract in a language they
L0:minimum wage;
L1:(G) Receive wages that are not below the legal host-country
L0:to signing their employment contract; and
L1:(H) Be notified of their rights, wages, and prohibited activities prior
L0:housing and safety standards.
L1:(I) If housing is provided, live in housing that meets host-country
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(ii) The Contractor shall post these rights in employee work spaces in
L0:English and in any foreign language(s) spoken by a significant portion of the
L0:workforce.
L1:(iii) The Contractor shall enforce the rights of Contractor personnel
L0:supporting the U.S. Armed Forces.
L1:(e) Preliminary personnel requirements.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall ensure that the following requirements are met prior to
L0:deploying CAAF (specific requirements for each category will be specified in the
L0:statement of work or elsewhere in the contract):
L1:(i) All required security and background checks are complete and
L0:acceptable.
L1:(ii) All CAAF deploying in support of an applicable operation—
L0:performance of their contracted duties;
L1:(A) Are medically, dentally, and psychologically fit for deployment and
L1:(B) Meet the minimum medical screening requirements, including
L0:theater-specific medical qualifications as established by the geographic Combatant
L0:Commander (as posted to the Geographic Combatant Commander’s website or other
L0:venue); and
L0:contract.
L1:(C) Have received all required immunizations as specified in the
L1:(1) During predeployment processing, the Government will provide,
L0:at no cost to the Contractor, any military-specific immunizations and/or medications not
L0:available to the general public.
L0:the deployment center.
L1:(2) All other immunizations shall be obtained prior to arrival at
L1:(3) All CAAF and selected non-CAAF, as specified in the statement
L0:of work, shall bring to the designated operational area a copy of the U.S. Centers for
L0:Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Form 731, International Certificate of
L0:Vaccination or Prophylaxis as Approved by the World Health Organization, (also known
L0:as “shot record” or “Yellow Card”) that shows vaccinations are current.
L1:(iii) Deploying personnel have all necessary passports, visas, and other
L0:documents required to enter and exit a designated operational area and have a Geneva
L0:Conventions identification card, or other appropriate DoD identity credential, from the
L0:deployment center.
L1:(iv) Special area, country, and theater clearance is obtained for all personnel
L0:deploying. Clearance requirements are in DoD Directive 4500.54E, DoD Foreign
L0:Clearance Program. For this purpose, CAAF are considered non-DoD contactor
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:personnel traveling under DoD sponsorship.
L1:(v) All deploying personnel have received personal security training. At a
L0:minimum, the training shall—
L1:(A) Cover safety and security issues facing employees overseas;
L1:(B) Identify safety and security contingency planning activities; and
L1:(C) Identify ways to utilize safety and security personnel and other
L0:resources appropriately.
L1:(vi) All personnel have received isolated personnel training, if specified in
L0:the contract, in accordance with DoD Instruction 1300.23, Isolated Personnel Training
L0:for DoD Civilian and Contractors.
L1:(vii) Personnel have received law of war training as follows:
L0:provided through—
L1:(A) Basic training is required for all CAAF. The basic training will be
L1:(1) A military-run training center; or
L0:the Contracting Officer.
L1:(2) A web-based source, if specified in the contract or approved by
L1:(B) Advanced training, commensurate with their duties and
L0:responsibilities, may be required for some Contractor personnel as specified in the
L0:contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall notify all personnel who are not a host country
L0:national, or who are not ordinarily resident in the host country, that—
L1:(i) Such employees, and dependents residing with such employees, who
L0:engage in conduct outside the United States that would constitute an offense
L0:punishable by imprisonment for more than one year if the conduct had been engaged in
L0:within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, may
L0:potentially be subject to the criminal jurisdiction of the United States in accordance
L0:with the Military Extraterritorial Jurisdiction Act of 2000 (18 U.S.C. 3621, et seq.);
L1:(ii) Pursuant to the War Crimes Act (18 U.S.C. 2441), Federal criminal
L0:jurisdiction also extends to conduct that is determined to constitute a war crime when
L0:committed by a civilian national of the United States;
L1:(iii) Other laws may provide for prosecution of U.S. nationals who commit
L0:offenses on the premises of U.S. diplomatic, consular, military or other U.S.
L0:Government missions outside the United States (18 U.S.C. 7(9)); and
L1:(iv) In time of declared war or a contingency operation, CAAF are subject to
L0:the jurisdiction of the Uniform Code of Military Justice under 10 U.S.C. 802(a)(10).
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(v) Such employees are required to report offenses alleged to have been
L0:committed by or against Contractor personnel to appropriate investigative authorities.
L1:(vi) Such employees will be provided victim and witness protection and
L0:assistance.
L1:(f) Processing and departure points. CAAF shall—
L1:(1) Process through the deployment center designated in the contract, or as
L0:otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer, prior to deploying. The deployment
L0:center will conduct deployment processing to ensure visibility and accountability of
L0:Contractor personnel and to ensure that all deployment requirements are met,
L0:including the requirements specified in paragraph (e)(1) of this clause;
L1:(2) Use the point of departure and transportation mode directed by the
L0:Contracting Officer; and
L1:(3) Process through a designated reception site (DRS) upon arrival at the
L0:deployed location. The DRS will validate personnel accountability, ensure that specific
L0:designated operational area entrance requirements are met, and brief Contractor
L0:personnel on theater-specific policies and procedures.
L1:(g) Personnel data.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall use the Synchronized Predeployment and Operational
L0:Tracker (SPOT) web-based system, to enter and maintain the data for all CAAF
L0:and, as designated by the Under Secretary of Defense (Acquisition and
L0:Sustainment) or the Combatant Commander, non-CAAF supporting U.S. Armed
L0:Forces deployed outside the United States as specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this
L0:clause.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall enter the required information about their contractor
L0:personnel prior to deployment and shall continue to use the SPOT web-based
L0:system at https://spot.dmdc.mil to maintain accurate, up-to-date information
L0:throughout the deployment for all Contractor personnel. Changes to status of
L0:individual Contractor personnel relating to their in-theater arrival date and their
L0:duty location, to include closing out the deployment with their proper status (e.g.,
L0:mission complete, killed, wounded) shall be annotated within the SPOT database in
L0:accordance with the timelines established in the SPOT Business Rules at
L0:https://www.acq.osd.mil/asds/log/cso/ocs/spot.html.
L1:(h) Contractor personnel.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer may direct the Contractor, at its own expense, to
L0:remove and replace any Contractor personnel who jeopardize or interfere with mission
L0:accomplishment or who fail to comply with or violate applicable requirements of this
L0:contract. Such action may be taken at the Government’s discretion without prejudice to
L0:its rights under any other provision of this contract, including the Termination for
L0:Default clause.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall identify all personnel who occupy a position designated
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:as mission essential and ensure the continuity of essential Contractor services during
L0:designated operations, unless, after consultation with the Contracting Officer,
L0:Contracting Officer’s representative, or local commander, the Contracting Officer
L0:directs withdrawal due to security conditions.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall ensure that Contractor personnel follow the guidance
L0:at paragraph (e)(2)(v) of this clause and any specific Combatant Commander guidance
L0:on reporting offenses alleged to have been committed by or against Contractor
L0:personnel to appropriate investigative authorities.
L1:(4) Contractor personnel shall return all U.S. Government-issued
L0:identification, to include the Common Access Card, to appropriate U.S. Government
L0:authorities at the end of their deployment (or, for non-CAAF, at the end of their
L0:employment under this contract).
L1:(i) Military clothing and protective equipment.
L1:(1) Contractor personnel are prohibited from wearing military clothing unless
L0:specifically authorized in writing by the Combatant Commander. If authorized to wear
L0:military clothing, Contractor personnel must—
L1:(i) Wear distinctive patches, arm bands, nametags, or headgear, in order to
L0:be distinguishable from military personnel, consistent with force protection measures;
L0:and
L1:(ii) Carry the written authorization with them at all times.
L1:(2) Contractor personnel may wear military-unique organizational clothing and
L0:individual equipment (OCIE) required for safety and security, such as ballistic, nuclear,
L0:biological, or chemical protective equipment.
L1:(3) The deployment center, or the Combatant Commander, shall issue OCIE
L0:and shall provide training, if necessary, to ensure the safety and security of Contractor
L0:personnel.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall ensure that all issued OCIE is returned to the point of
L0:issue, unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(j) Weapons.
L1:(1) If the Contractor requests that its personnel performing in the designated
L0:operational area be authorized to carry weapons for individual self-defense, the request
L0:shall be made through the Contracting Officer to the Combatant Commander, in
L0:accordance with DoD Instruction 3020.41, Operational Contractor Support. The
L0:Combatant Commander will determine whether to authorize in-theater Contractor
L0:personnel to carry weapons and what weapons and ammunition will be allowed.
L1:(2) If Contractor personnel are authorized to carry weapons in accordance with
L0:paragraph (j)(1) of this clause, the Contracting Officer will notify the Contractor what
L0:weapons and ammunition are authorized.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(3) The Contractor shall ensure that its personnel who are authorized to carry
L0:weapons—
L1:(i) Are adequately trained to carry and use them—
L1:(A) Safely;
L0:force issued by the Combatant Commander; and
L1:(B) With full understanding of, and adherence to, the rules of the use of
L1:(C) In compliance with applicable agency policies, agreements, rules,
L0:regulations, and other applicable law;
L1:(ii) Are not barred from possession of a firearm by 18 U.S.C. 922;
L1:(iii) Adhere to all guidance and orders issued by the Combatant
L0:Commander regarding possession, use, safety, and accountability of weapons and
L0:ammunition;
L1:(iv) Comply with applicable Combatant Commander and local commander
L0:force-protection policies; and
L1:(v) Understand that the inappropriate use of force could subject them to
L0:U.S. or host-nation prosecution and civil liability.
L1:(4) Whether or not weapons are Government-furnished, all liability for the use
L0:of any weapon by Contractor personnel rests solely with the Contractor and the
L0:Contractor employee using such weapon.
L1:(5) Upon redeployment or revocation by the Combatant Commander of the
L0:Contractor’s authorization to issue firearms, the Contractor shall ensure that all
L0:Government-issued weapons and unexpended ammunition are returned as directed by
L0:the Contracting Officer.
L1:(k) Vehicle or equipment licenses. Contractor personnel shall possess the required
L0:licenses to operate all vehicles or equipment necessary to perform the contract in the
L0:designated operational area.
L1:(l) Purchase of scarce goods and services. If the Combatant Commander has
L0:established an organization for the designated operational area whose function is to
L0:determine that certain items are scarce goods or services, the Contractor shall
L0:coordinate with that organization local purchases of goods and services designated as
L0:scarce, in accordance with instructions provided by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(m) Evacuation.
L1:(1) If the Combatant Commander orders a mandatory evacuation of some or all
L0:personnel, the Government will provide assistance, to the extent available, to United
L0:States and third country national Contractor personnel.
L1:(2) In the event of a non-mandatory evacuation order, unless authorized in
L0:writing by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall maintain personnel on location
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:sufficient to meet obligations under this contract.
L1:(n) Next of kin notification and personnel recovery.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall be responsible for notification of the employee-
L0:designated next of kin in the event an employee dies, requires evacuation due to an
L0:injury, or is isolated, missing, detained, captured, or abducted.
L1:(2) In the case of isolated, missing, detained, captured, or abducted Contractor
L0:personnel, the Government will assist in personnel recovery actions in accordance with
L0:DoD Directive 3002.01E, Personnel Recovery in the Department of Defense.
L1:(o) Mortuary affairs. Contractor personnel who die while in support of the U.S.
L0:Armed Forces shall be covered by the DoD mortuary affairs program as described in
L0:DoD Directive 1300.22, Mortuary Affairs Policy, and DoD Instruction 3020.41,
L0:Operational Contractor Support.
L1:(p) Changes. In addition to the changes otherwise authorized by the Changes
L0:clause of this contract, the Contracting Officer may, at any time, by written order
L0:identified as a change order, make changes in the place of performance or Government-
L0:furnished facilities, equipment, material, services, or site. Any change order issued in
L0:accordance with this paragraph (p) shall be subject to the provisions of the Changes
L0:clause of this contract.
L1:(q) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall incorporate the substance of this clause,
L0:including this paragraph (q), in all subcontracts when subcontractor personnel are
L0:supporting U.S. Armed Forces deployed outside the United States in—
L1:(1) Contingency operations;
L1:(2) Peace operations consistent with Joint Publication 3-07.3; or
L1:(3) Other military operations or military exercises, when designated by the
L0:Combatant Commander or as directed by the Secretary of Defense.

L0:“commercial product” in section 2.101 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR));

L1:(iii) Offered to the Government, under a contract or subcontract at any tier,
L0:without modification, in the same form in which it is sold in the commercial
L0:marketplace; and
L1:(2) Does not include bulk cargo, as defined in 46 U.S.C. 40102(4), such as
L0:agricultural products and petroleum products.
L0:“Component” means any article, material, or supply incorporated directly into
L0:construction material.
L0:“Construction material” means an article, material, or supply brought to the
L0:construction site by the Contractor or a subcontractor for incorporation into the building
L0:or work. The term also includes an item brought to the site preassembled from articles,
L0:materials, or supplies. However, emergency life safety systems, such as emergency
L0:lighting, fire alarm, and audio evacuation systems, that are discrete systems
L0:incorporated into a public building or work and that are produced as complete systems,
L0:are evaluated as a single and distinct construction material regardless of when or how
L0:the individual parts or components of those systems are delivered to the construction
L0:site. Materials purchased directly by the Government are supplies, not construction
L0:material.
L0:“Cost of components” means—
L1:(1) For components purchased by the Contractor, the acquisition cost, including
L0:transportation costs to the place of incorporation into the end product (whether or not
L0:such costs are paid to a domestic firm), and any applicable duty (whether or not a duty-
L0:free entry certificate is issued); or
L1:(2) For components manufactured by the Contractor, all costs associated with
L0:the manufacture of the component, including transportation costs as described in
L0:paragraph (1) of this definition, plus allocable overhead costs, but excluding profit. Cost
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:of components does not include any costs associated with the manufacture of the
L0:construction material.
L0:“Critical component” means a component that is mined, produced, or manufactured
L0:in the United States and deemed critical to the U.S. supply chain. The list of critical
L0:components is at FAR 25.105.
L0:“Critical item” means domestic construction material or a domestic end product that
L0:is deemed critical to the U.S. supply chain. The list of critical items is at FAR 25.105.
L0:“Domestic construction material” means—

L0:iron or steel or a combination of both—

L0:United States; or

L0:United States exceeds 60 percent of the cost of all its components, except that the
L0:percentage will be 65 percent for items delivered in calendar years 2024 through 2028
L0:and 75 percent for items delivered starting in calendar year 2029, unless an alternate
L0:percentage is established for a contract in accordance with FAR 25.201(c). Components
L0:of foreign origin of the same class or kind for which nonavailability determinations have
L0:been made are treated as domestic. Components of unknown origin are treated as
L0:foreign; or
L1:(B) The construction material is a COTS item; or
L1:(2) For construction material that consists wholly or predominantly of iron or
L0:steel or a combination of both, a construction material manufactured in the United
L0:States if the cost of iron and steel not produced in the United States (excluding
L0:fasteners) as estimated in good faith by the contractor, constitutes less than 5 percent of
L0:the cost of all the components used in such construction material (produced in the
L0:United States means that all manufacturing processes of the iron or steel must take
L0:place in the United States, except metallurgical processes involving refinement of steel
L0:additives). The cost of iron and steel not produced in the United States includes but is
L0:not limited to the cost of iron or steel mill products (such as bar, billet, slab, wire, plate,
L0:or sheet), castings, or forgings, not produced in the United States, utilized in the
L0:manufacture of the end product and a good faith estimate of the cost of all iron or steel
L0:components not produced in the United States, excluding COTS fasteners. Iron or steel
L0:components of unknown origin are treated as foreign. If the construction material
L0:contains multiple components, the cost of all the materials used in such construction
L0:material is calculated in accordance with the definition of “cost of components” in this
L0:clause.
L0:“Predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both” means that the cost of the
L0:iron and steel content exceeds 50 percent of the total cost of all its components. The cost
L0:of iron and steel is the cost of the iron or steel mill products (such as bar, billet, slab,
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:wire, plate, or sheet), castings, or forgings utilized in the manufacture of the product
L0:and a good faith estimate of the cost of iron or steel components excluding COTS
L0:fasteners.
L0:“Steel” means an alloy that includes at least 50 percent iron, between 0.02 and 2
L0:percent carbon, and may include other elements.
L0:“United States” means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and outlying areas.
L1:(b) Domestic preference. This clause implements the Balance of Payments Program

L1:(3) The construction material or components listed by the Government as

L0:paragraphs (b) and (c) than the basic clause:
L0:BALANCE OF PAYMENTS PROGRAM—CONSTRUCTION MATERIAL UNDER
L0:TRADE AGREEMENTS—ALTERNATE V (FEB 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Bahraini or Mexican construction material” means a construction material that—
L1:(1) Is wholly the growth, product, or manufacture of Bahrain or Mexico; or
L1:(2) In the case of a construction material that consists in whole or in part of
L0:materials from another country, has been substantially transformed in Bahrain or
L0:Mexico into a new and different construction material distinct from the materials from
L0:which it was transformed.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:“Caribbean Basin country construction material” means a construction material
L0:that—
L0:or
L1:(1) Is wholly the growth, product, or manufacture of a Caribbean Basin country;
L1:(2) In the case of a construction material that consists in whole or in part of
L0:materials from another country, has been substantially transformed in a Caribbean
L0:Basin country into a new and different construction material distinct from the materials
L0:from which it was transformed.
L0:“Commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item”—
L1:(1) Means any item of supply (including construction material) that is—
L1:(i) A commercial product (as defined in paragraph (1) of the definition of
L0:“commercial product” in section 2.101 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR));
L1:(ii) Sold in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(iii) Offered to the Government, under a contract or subcontract at any tier,
L0:without modification, in the same form in which it is sold in the commercial
L0:marketplace; and
L1:(2) Does not include bulk cargo, as defined in section 3 of the Shipping Act of
L0:1984 (46 U.S.C. 40102), such as agricultural products and petroleum products.
L0:“Component” means any article, material, or supply incorporated directly into
L0:construction material.
L0:“Construction material” means an article, material, or supply brought to the
L0:construction site by the Contractor or a subcontractor for incorporation into the building
L0:or work. The term also includes an item brought to the site preassembled from articles,
L0:materials, or supplies. However, emergency life safety systems, such as emergency
L0:lighting, fire alarm, and audio evacuation systems, that are discrete systems
L0:incorporated into a public building or work and that are produced as complete systems,
L0:are evaluated as a single and distinct construction material regardless of when or how
L0:the individual parts or components of those systems are delivered to the construction
L0:site. Materials purchased directly by the Government are supplies, not construction
L0:material.
L0:“Cost of components” means—
L1:(1) For components purchased by the Contractor, the acquisition cost, including
L0:transportation costs to the place of incorporation into the end product (whether or not
L0:such costs are paid to a domestic firm), and any applicable duty (whether or not a duty-
L0:free entry certificate is issued); or
L1:(2) For components manufactured by the Contractor, all costs associated with
L0:the manufacture of the component, including transportation costs as described in
L0:paragraph (1) of this definition, plus allocable overhead costs, but excluding profit. Cost
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:of components does not include any costs associated with the manufacture of the
L0:construction material.
L0:“Critical component” means a component that is mined, produced, or manufactured
L0:in the United States and deemed critical to the U.S. supply chain. The list of critical
L0:components is at FAR 25.105.
L0:“Critical item” means domestic construction material or a domestic end product that
L0:is deemed critical to the U.S. supply chain. The list of critical items is at FAR 25.105.
L0:“Designated country” means—
L1:(1) A World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement (WTO
L0:GPA) country (Armenia, Aruba, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada,
L0:Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany,
L0:Greece, Hong Kong, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Korea (Republic of),
L0:Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Moldova, Montenegro,
L0:Netherlands, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania,
L0:Singapore, Slovak Republic, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan (known in
L0:the World Trade Organization as “the Separate Customs Territory of Taiwan, Penghu,
L0:Kinmen, and Matsu” (Chinese Taipei)), Ukraine, or the United Kingdom);
L1:(2) A Free Trade Agreement country (Australia, Bahrain, Chile, Colombia,
L0:Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Korea (Republic
L0:of), Mexico, Morocco, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, or Singapore);
L1:(3) A least developed country (Afghanistan, Angola, Bangladesh, Benin,
L0:Bhutan, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros,
L0:Democratic Republic of Congo, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Gambia,
L0:Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Haiti, Kiribati, Laos, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi,
L0:Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Nepal, Niger, Rwanda, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe,
L0:Senegal, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, Timor-Leste,
L0:Togo, Tuvalu, Uganda, Vanuatu, Yemen, or Zambia); or
L1:(4) A Caribbean Basin country (Antigua and Barbuda, Aruba, Bahamas,
L0:Barbados, Belize, Bonaire, British Virgin Islands, Curacao, Dominica, Grenada,
L0:Guyana, Haiti, Jamaica, Montserrat, Saba, St. Kitts and Nevis, St. Lucia, St. Vincent
L0:and the Grenadines, Sint Eustatius, Sint Maarten, or Trinidad and Tobago).
L0:“Designated country construction material” means a construction material that is a
L0:WTO GPA country construction material, a Free Trade Agreement country construction
L0:material, a least developed country construction material, or a Caribbean Basin country
L0:construction material.
L0:“Domestic construction material” means—
L1:(1) For construction material that does not consist wholly or predominantly of
L0:iron or steel or a combination of both—
L1:(i) An unmanufactured construction material mined or produced in the
L0:United States; or
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(ii) A construction material manufactured in the United States, if—
L1:(A) The cost of its components mined, produced, or manufactured in the
L0:United States exceeds, for the entire period of performance for a contract awarded in:
L0:calendar year 2023, 60 percent of the cost of all its components; calendar years 2024
L0:through 2028, 65 percent of the cost of all its components; or calendar year 2029 or
L0:later, 75 percent of the cost of all its components. Components of foreign origin of the
L0:same class or kind for which nonavailability determinations have been made are
L0:treated as domestic. Components of unknown origin are treated as foreign; or
L1:(B) The construction material is a COTS item; or
L1:(2) For construction material that consists wholly or predominantly of iron or
L0:steel or a combination of both, a construction material manufactured in the United
L0:States if the cost of iron and steel not produced in the United States (excluding
L0:fasteners) as estimated in good faith by the contractor, constitutes less than 5 percent of
L0:the cost of all the components used in such construction material (produced in the
L0:United States means that all manufacturing processes of the iron or steel must take
L0:place in the United States, except metallurgical processes involving refinement of steel
L0:additives). The cost of iron and steel not produced in the United States includes but is
L0:not limited to the cost of iron or steel mill products (such as bar, billet, slab, wire, plate,
L0:or sheet), castings, or forgings, not produced in the United States, utilized in the
L0:manufacture of the construction material and a good faith estimate of the cost of all iron
L0:or steel components not produced in the United States, excluding COTS fasteners. Iron
L0:or steel components of unknown origin are treated as foreign. If the construction
L0:material contains multiple components, the cost of all the materials used in such
L0:construction material is calculated in accordance with the definition of “cost of
L0:components” in this clause.
L0:“Free Trade Agreement country construction material” means a construction
L0:material that—
L1:(1) Is wholly the growth, product, or manufacture of a Free Trade Agreement
L0:country; or
L1:(2) In the case of a construction material that consists in whole or in part of
L0:materials from another country, has been substantially transformed in a Free Trade
L0:Agreement country into a new and different construction material distinct from the
L0:material from which it was transformed.
L0:“Least developed country construction material” means a construction material
L0:that—
L0:or
L1:(1) Is wholly the growth, product, or manufacture of a least developed country;
L1:(2) In the case of a construction material that consists in whole or in part of
L0:materials from another country has been substantially transformed in a least developed
L0:country into a new and different construction material distinct from the materials from
L0:which it was transformed.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:“Predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both” means that the cost of the
L0:iron and steel content exceeds 50 percent of the total cost of all its components. The cost
L0:of iron and steel is the cost of the iron or steel mill products (such as bar, billet, slab,
L0:wire, plate, or sheet), castings, or forgings utilized in the manufacture of the product
L0:and a good faith estimate of the cost of iron or steel components excluding COTS
L0:fasteners.
L0:“Steel” means an alloy that includes at least 50 percent iron, between 0.02 and 2
L0:percent carbon, and may include other elements.
L0:“United States” means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and outlying areas.
L0:“WTO GPA country construction material” means a construction material that—
L1:(1) Is wholly the growth, product, or manufacture of a WTO GPA country; or
L1:(2) In the case of a construction material that consists in whole or in part of
L0:materials from another country, has been substantially transformed in a WTO GPA
L0:country into a new and different construction material distinct from the materials from
L0:which it was transformed.
L1:(b) This clause implements the Balance of Payments Program by providing a
L0:preference for domestic construction material. In addition, the Contracting Officer has
L0:determined that the WTO GPA and all Free Trade Agreements except United States-
L0:Mexico-Canada Agreement and the Bahrain Free Trade Agreement apply to this
L0:acquisition. Therefore, the Balance of Payments Program restrictions are waived for
L0:designated country construction material other than Bahraini or Mexican construction
L0:material.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall use only domestic or designated country construction
L0:material other than Bahraini or Mexican construction material in performing this
L0:contract, except for—
L1:(1) Construction material valued at or below the simplified acquisition
L0:threshold in FAR part 2; or
L1:(2) Information technology that is a commercial product; or
L1:(3) The construction material or components listed by the Government as
L0:follows:
L0:[Contracting Officer to list applicable excepted materials or indicate “none”].
L0:Alternate VI. [Reserved]
L0:Alternate VII. [Reserved]
L0:(End of clause)

L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225

content:

L0:As prescribed in 225.7019-4(a), use the following provision:
L0:REPRESENTATION REGARDING PROHIBITION ON USE OF CERTAIN ENERGY
L0:SOURCED FROM INSIDE THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION (AUG 2021)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this provision—
L0:“Covered military installation” means a military installation in Europe
L0:identified by DoD as a main operating base.
L0:“Furnished energy” means energy furnished to a covered military installation in any
L0:form and for any purpose, including heating, cooling, and electricity.
L0:“Main operating base” means a facility outside the United States and its
L0:territories with permanently stationed operating forces and robust infrastructure.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(b) Prohibition. In accordance with section 2821 of the National Defense
L0:Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 (Pub. L. 116-92), contracts for the acquisition of
L0:furnished energy for a covered military installation shall not use any energy sourced
L0:from inside the Russian Federation as a means of generating the furnished energy for
L0:the covered military installation, unless a waiver is approved. The prohibition—
L1:(1) Applies to all forms of energy that are furnished to a covered military
L0:installation; and
L1:(2) Does not apply to energy converted by a third party into another form of
L0:energy and not directly delivered to a covered military installation.
L1:(c) Representation. By submission of its offer, the Offeror represents that the
L0:Offeror will not use or provide any energy sourced from inside the Russian Federation
L0:as a means of generating the furnished energy for the covered military installation in
L0:the performance of any contract, subcontract, or other contractual instrument resulting
L0:from this solicitation.
L0:(End of provision)

L0:technology transfer, in-county procurement, marketing and financial assistance, and joint

L0:directly related to the item being purchased. For example, as a condition of a U.S. sale, the
L0:contractor may require or agree to permit the purchaser to produce in its country certain

L0:are unrelated to the item being purchased. For example, as a condition of a sale the
L0:contractor may agree to purchase certain of the customer's manufactured products,
L0:agricultural commodities, raw materials, or services. Indirect offsets may be accomplished

L0:PGI 225.79—EXPORT CONTROL
L0:PGI 225.7901 Export-controlled items.
L0:PGI 225.7901-2 General.
L1:(1) DoD Focal Point on Export Controls.
L1:(i) Within DoD, the focal point on export controls is the Defense Technology Security
L0:Administration (DTSA). Official authorities and responsibilities of DTSA are established in
L0:DoD Directive 5105.72.
L1:(ii) Initial DoD acquisition workforce questions regarding the applicability of the
L0:Export Administration Regulations (EAR) or the International Traffic in Arms Regulations
L1:(ITAR) to specific procurements or items, or interpretation of DoD issuances regarding
L0:export controls, may be directed to the DTSA Policy Directorate, by phone at 571-372-
L0:2438/2377 or by visiting the DTSA web site at: http://www.dtsa.mil/SitePages/contact-
L0:us/default.aspx.
L1:(2) Regulations. The Department of State and the Department of Commerce are the
L0:lead agencies responsible for regulations governing the export of defense articles,
L0:commercial products or commercial services, and dual use items.
L1:(i) The International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), issued by the Department of
L0:State, control the export of defense-related articles and services, including technical data,
L0:ensuring compliance with the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2751 et seq.). The United
L0:States Munitions List (USML) identifies defense articles, services, and related technical data
L0:that are inherently military in character and could, if exported, jeopardize national security or
L0:foreign policy interests of the United States.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(A) The ITAR is published in Title 22 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR),
L0:Parts 120 through 130 (22 CFR 120-130). The official version of the ITAR is maintained at
L0:https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-22.
L1:(B) The USML is part of the ITAR, in 22 CFR Part 121, and is available at the
L0:web sites in paragraph (2) (i) (A) of this section.
L1:(C) The Department of State is responsible for compliance with the ITAR.
L0:Depending on the nature of questions you may have, you may contact the following
L0:Department of State office to obtain additional information:
L0:U.S. Department of State
L0:Bureau of Political Military Affairs
L0:Directorate of Defense Trade Controls
L0:Office of Defense Trade Controls Compliance
L0:https://www.state.gov/bureaus-offices/under-secretary-for-arms-control-and-international-
L0:security-affairs/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/directorate-of-defense-trade-controls-pm-
L0:ddtc/.
L1:(D) Contracting officers should not answer any questions a contractor may ask
L0:regarding how to comply with the ITAR. If asked, the contracting officer should direct the
L0:contractor’s attention to paragraph (c) of the clause at DFARS 252.225-7048 and may
L0:inform the contractor that the Department of State publishes guidance regarding ITAR
L0:compliance at https://www.state.gov/bureaus-offices/under-secretary-for-arms-control-and-
L0:international-security-affairs/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/directorate-of-defense-trade-
L0:controls-pm-ddtc/.
L1:(E) Contracting officers should not answer any questions a contractor may ask
L0:regarding the State Department requirement, mentioned in the clause at 252.225-7048,
L0:for contractors to register with the Department of State in accordance with the ITAR. If
L0:asked, the contracting officer should direct the contractor’s attention to paragraph (b) of
L0:the clause, which directs the contractor to consult with the Department of State
L0:regarding any questions relating to compliance with the ITAR. (The registration
L0:requirements are in Subpart 122.1 of the ITAR. Subpart 122.1 requires any person who
L0:engages in the United States in the business of either manufacturing or exporting
L0:defense articles or furnishing defense services to register with the Directorate of
L0:Defense Trade Controls.)
L1:(ii) The Export Administration Regulations (EAR), issued by the Department of
L0:Commerce, control the export of dual-use items, (items that have both commercial and
L0:military or proliferation applications) and purely commercial products or commercial
L0:services. These items include commodities, software, and technology. Many items subject
L0:to the EAR are set forth by Export Control Classification Number on the Commerce Control
L0:List.
L1:(A) The EAR is published in Title 15 of the Code of Federal Regulations, Parts
L0:730 through 774 (15 CFR Parts 730-774), available at https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-
L0:15/subtitle-B/chapter-VII/subchapter-C.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225

L0:CFR Part 774, and is available at https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-15/subtitle-B/chapter-
L0:VII/subchapter-C.
L1:(C) The Department of Commerce is responsible for compliance with the EAR.
L0:Depending on the nature of questions you may have, you may contact the following
L0:Department of Commerce office to obtain additional information:
L0:U.S. Department of Commerce
L0:Bureau of Industry and Security
L0:Office of Exporter Services (OExS)

L1:(D) Contracting officers should not answer any questions a contractor may ask

L1:(3) National Security Decision Directive (NSDD) 189, National Policy on the Transfer of
L0:Scientific, Technical, and Engineering Information.
L1:(i) NSDD 189 establishes a national policy that, to the maximum extent possible,
L0:the products of fundamental research must remain unrestricted. NSDD 189 provides that
L0:no restrictions may be placed upon the conduct or reporting of federally funded fundamental
L0:research that has not received national security classification, except as provided in
L0:applicable U.S. statutes. As a result, contracts confined to the performance of unclassified
L0:fundamental research generally do not involve any export-controlled items, as defined in
L0:paragraph (a) of the clause at DFARS 252.225-7048.
L1:(ii) NSDD 189 does not take precedence over statutes. NSDD 189 does not
L0:exempt any research, whether basic, fundamental, or applied, from statutes that apply to
L0:export controls such as the Arms Export Control Act, the Export Administration Act of 1979,
L0:as amended, or the U.S. International Emergency Economic Powers Act, or the regulations
L0:that implement those statutes (the ITAR and the EAR). Thus, if export-controlled items are
L0:used to conduct research or are generated as part of the research efforts, the export control
L0:laws and regulations apply to the controlled items.
L1:(iii) NSDD 189 is available at http://www.fas.org/irp/offdocs/nsdd/nsdd-189.htm.

L0:PGI 225.7902 Defense Trade Cooperation Treaties.
L0:The following documents are accessible at: http://pmddtc.state.gov/:
L0:• DTC Treaties.
L0:• Implementing Arrangements.
L0:• The provisions of the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) (22 CFR 126.16
L1:(Australia) and 22 CFR 126.17 (United Kingdom)) pertaining to the DTC Treaties.
L0:• List of Defense Articles Exempted from DTC Treaty Coverage (also in 22 CFR 126
L0:Supplement No. 1).
L0:• List of Approved Community Members.
L0:• Definitions.
L0:PGI 225.7902-2 Purpose.
L1:(1) Background.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L1:(i) The U.S. Government controls exports of defense articles, technical data, and
L0:defense services. The controls are imposed by the Arms Export Control Act (AECA) and the
L0:Department of State regulation that implements the AECA export controls, also known as
L0:the ITAR.
L1:(ii) Under the ITAR, the Department of State manages an export licensing system in
L0:which government approvals are often necessary for companies to hold discussions about
L0:potential projects, pursue joint activities, ship hardware, or transfer know-how to one
L0:another, and even sometimes to move engineers and other personnel within branches of the
L0:same company located in different countries. This process can be challenging for U.S.
L0:exporters and for foreign firms in their supply chains.
L1:(iii) Given the close allied relationship of the United States with Australia and the
L0:United Kingdom, the President and the respective Prime Ministers decided to reform the
L0:defense trade system between their countries with the goal of facilitating the exchange of
L0:certain defense articles, technical data, and defense services between their militaries and
L0:security authorities, and their industries. They negotiated bilateral Defense Trade
L0:Cooperation DTC Treaties to achieve this goal. These bilateral DTC Treaties establish
L0:permissions for export without export licenses for each country, if an export meets the DTC
L0:Treaty requirements. Other exports remain under the AECA and the ITAR. The DTC
L0:Treaties are intended solely to waive certain requirements of the ITAR for specific
L0:transactions within the scope of the DTC Treaties not remove any requirements for
L0:contractors to comply with domestic U.S. law.
L1:(iv) The Department of State regulations implementing the DTC Treaties are in the
L0:ITAR.
L1:(2) How the DTC Treaties work.
L1:(i) The DTC Treaties establish Approved Communities. The “Approved Community”
L0:for each DTC Treaty is defined in DFARS clause 252.225-7047. Exports of most U.S.
L0:defense articles, technical data, and defense services are permitted to go into and to move
L0:within the Approved Community, without the need for government approvals and export
L0:licenses (provided that all persons comply with statutory and regulatory requirements
L0:outside of DFARS and ITAR concerning the import of defense articles and defense services
L0:or the possession or transfer of defense articles, including, but not limited to, regulations
L0:issued by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives found at 27 C.F.R. Parts
L0:447, 478, and 479, which are unaffected by the DTC Treaties) when in support of the
L0:following:
L0:• Combined U.S.-Australia or U.S.-U.K. military or counterterrorism operations.
L0:• U.S.-Australia or U.S.-U.K. cooperative security and defense research, development,
L0:production, and support programs.
L0:• Specific security and defense projects that are for the government of Australia or the
L0:government of the United Kingdom use only.
L0:• U.S. Government end use.
L1:(ii) Under the DTC Treaties, instead of a U.S. exporter preparing and requesting
L0:Department of State approval of an export license or other written authorization for a project,
L0:the exporter may elect to use the applicable DTC Treaty if Treaty conditions are met. If
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:using a DTC Treaty, the exporter will check the Department of State website or other
L0:appropriate reference and verify that—
L0:• The Australian or U.K. partner is on the list of approved companies/facilities (i.e., a
L0:member of the Approved Community);
L0:• The effort is in support of at least one of the scope areas identified in paragraph (2)(i) of
L0:this section; and
L0:• The defense article is not on the exempted technology list. (Also in 22 CFR 126
L0:Supplement No. 1).
L0:If all three conditions are met, then the U.S. exporter and the Australian or U.K. partner may
L0:use the DTC Treaty exemptions in the ITAR to move qualifying defense articles without the
L0:need to obtain export licenses or other written authorizations, provided compliance with
L0:paragraph (2)(i) of this section.
L1:(iii) A company using a DTC Treaty, in addition to checking the three lists (as
L0:explained in paragraph (2)(ii) of this section), must also comply with requirements in the
L0:applicable DTC Treaty and the associated Implementing Arrangements, and the provisions
L0:of the ITAR pertaining to the DTC Treaty. These include marking and recordkeeping
L0:requirements to ensure that export-controlled items are recognized as such and treated
L0:accordingly. For example, instead of normal ITAR requirements, the provisions of the ITAR
L0:pertaining to the DTC Treaties establish the requirements that apply. Similarly, DFARS

title: 252.225-7058 Postaward Disclosure of Employment of Individuals Who
content:
L0:252.225-7058 Postaward Disclosure of Employment of Individuals Who
L0:Work in the People’s Republic of China.
L0:As prescribed in 225.7021-4(b), use the following clause:
L0:POSTAWARD DISCLOSURE OF EMPLOYMENT OF INDIVIDUALS WHO
L0:WORK IN THE PEOPLE’S REPUBLIC OF CHINA (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Covered contract” means any DoD contract or subcontract with a value in
L0:excess of $5 million, not including contracts for commercial products and
L0:commercial services.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 25
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 225
L0:“Covered entity” means any corporation, company, limited liability company,
L0:limited partnership, business trust, business association, or other similar entity,
L0:including any subsidiary thereof, performing work on a covered contract in the
L0:People’s Republic of China, including by leasing or owning real property used in the
L0:performance of the covered contract in the People’s Republic of China.
L1:(b) Disclosure requirement.
L1:(1) In accordance with section 855 of the National Defense Authorization
L0:Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81, 10 U.S.C. 4651 note prec.), DoD may not
L0:award, extend, or exercise an option on a covered contract with a covered entity
L0:unless such covered entity submits each required disclosure of its use of workforce
L0:and facilities in the People’s Republic of China, if it employs one or more individuals
L0:who perform work in the People’s Republic of China on a covered contract.
L1:(2) If the Contractor is a covered entity, the Contractor shall disclose for the
L0:Government’s fiscal years 2023 and 2024, the Contractor’s employment of one or
L0:more individuals who perform work in the People’s Republic of China on any
L0:covered contract. The disclosures shall include—
L1:(i) The total number of such individuals who perform work in the
L0:People’s Republic of China on the covered contracts funded by DoD; and
L1:(ii) A description of the physical presence, including street address or
L0:addresses in the People’s Republic of China, where work on the covered contract is
L0:performed.
L1:(c) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall insert this clause, including this
L0:paragraph (c), without alteration other than to identify the appropriate parties, in
L0:all subcontracts that meet the definition of a covered contract.
L0:(End of clause)

L0:RESTRICTION ON ACQUISITION OF CERTAIN SATELLITE COMPONENTS
L0:(MAY 2024)

L0:“Star tracker” means a navigational tool used in a satellite weighing more than
L0:400 pounds whose principal purpose is to support the national security, defense, or
L0:intelligence needs of the U.S. Government.
L1:(b) Restriction. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 4864, a star tracker must be
L0:manufactured in the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, or the United
L0:Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (United Kingdom). The Contractor
L0:shall deliver under this contract only star trackers manufactured in the United
L0:States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, or the United Kingdom.

L0:including this paragraph (c), in subcontracts for star trackers that exceed the
L0:simplified acquisition threshold, including subcontracts for commercial products
L0:and commercial services.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 226.7101 Definition
content:
L0:226.7101 Definition.
L0:“Vicinity,” as used in this subpart, means the county or counties in which the military
L0:installation to be closed or realigned is located and all adjacent counties, unless
L0:otherwise defined by the agency head.
subpart: SUBPART 226.71 — PREFERENCE FOR LOCAL AND SMALL BUSINESSES

title: 226.7102 Policy
content:
L0:226.7102 Policy.
L0:Provide businesses within the vicinity, including small and small disadvantaged
L0:businesses the maximum practicable opportunity to participate in acquisitions,
L0:including those for environmental restoration and mitigation, that support the closure
L0:or realignment of a military installation (10 U.S.C. 2687).
subpart: SUBPART 226.71 — PREFERENCE FOR LOCAL AND SMALL BUSINESSES

title: 226.7103 Procedure
content:
L0:226.7103 Procedure.
L0:In considering acquisitions for award through the 8(a) program (see 219.108 and FAR
L0:19.108) or in making set-aside decisions under 219.104 and FAR 19.104 for acquisitions
L0:in support of a base closure or realignment—
L1:(a) Determine whether there is a reasonable expectation of receiving offers from
L0:responsible business concerns located in the vicinity of the military installation that is
L0:being closed or realigned.
L1:(b) If offers are not expected from business concerns in the vicinity, consider 8(a) or
L0:other set-aside programs provided in part 219 and FAR part 19.
L1:(c) If offers are expected from business concerns in the vicinity—
L1:(1) Consider the 8(a) program only if at least one eligible 8(a) contractor is
L0:located in the vicinity.
L1:(2) Set aside the acquisition for small business only if at least one of the
L0:expected offers is from a small business located in the vicinity.
subpart: SUBPART 226.71 — PREFERENCE FOR LOCAL AND SMALL BUSINESSES

title: 226.7104 Other considerations
content:
L0:226.7104 Other considerations.
L0:When planning for contracts for services related to base closure activities at a military
L0:installation affected by a closure or realignment under a base closure law, consider
L0:including, as a factor in source selection, the extent to which offerors specifically identify
L0:and commit, in their proposals, to a plan to hire residents of the vicinity of the military
L0:installation that is being closed or realigned.

L0:This subpart implements section 853 of the National Defense Authorization Act for
L0:Fiscal Year 2004 (Pub. L. 108-136, 10 U.S.C. 3901 note prec.). This subpart does not
L0:supersede the requirement to use the mandatory sources in FAR part 8 or the small
L0:business programs in FAR part 19.

title: 226.7201 Definitions
content:
L0:226.7201 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Eligible contractor” means a business entity operated on a for-profit or nonprofit
L0:basis that—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 26
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 226
L1:(1) Employs severely disabled individuals at a rate that averages not less than
L0:33 percent of its total workforce over the 12-month period prior to issuance of the
L0:solicitation;
L1:(2) Pays not less than the minimum wage prescribed pursuant to 29 U.S.C. 206
L0:to the employees who are severely disabled individuals; and
L1:(3) Provides, for its employees, health insurance and a retirement plan
L0:comparable to those provided for employees by business entities of similar size in its
L0:industrial sector or geographic region.
L0:“Severely disabled individual” means an individual with a disability (as defined in
L0:42 U.S.C. 12102) who has a severe physical or mental impairment that seriously limits
L0:one or more functional capacities.

title: 226.7202 Policy
content:
L0:226.7202 Policy.
L0:Contracting officers may use this Demonstration Project to award one or more contracts
L0:to an eligible contractor for the purpose of providing defense contracting opportunities
L0:for entities that employ severely disabled individuals. To determine if there are eligible
L0:contractors capable of fulfilling the agency’s requirement, conduct market research as
L0:described in part 210 and FAR part 10. When electing to use this Demonstration
L0:Project, see PGI 226.7202.

title: 226.7203 Solicitation provision
content:

L0:Insert the provision at 252.226-7002, Representation for Demonstration Project for
L0:Contractors Employing Persons with Disabilities, in solicitations when using this
L0:Demonstration Project, including solicitations using FAR part 12 procedures for the
L0:acquisition of commercial products and commercial services.

title: 252.226-7001 Utilization of Indian Organizations, Indian-Owned Economic
content:
L0:252.226-7001 Utilization of Indian Organizations, Indian-Owned Economic
L0:Enterprises, and Native Hawaiian Small Business Concerns.
L0:As prescribed in 226.102-2, use the following clause:
L0:UTILIZATION OF INDIAN ORGANIZATIONS, INDIAN-OWNED ECONOMIC
L0:ENTERPRISES, AND NATIVE HAWAIIAN SMALL BUSINESS CONCERNS
L0:(JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Indian” means—
L1:(1) Any person who is a member of any Indian tribe, band, group, pueblo, or
L0:community that is recognized by the Federal Government as eligible for services from
L0:the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) in accordance with 25 U.S.C. 1452(c); and
L1:(2) Any “Native” as defined in the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (43
L0:U.S.C. 1601 et seq.).
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 26
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 226
L0:“Indian organization” means the governing body of any Indian tribe or entity
L0:established or recognized by the governing body of an Indian tribe for the purposes of 25
L0:U.S.C. Chapter 17.
L0:“Indian-owned economic enterprise” means any Indian-owned (as determined by the
L0:Secretary of the Interior) commercial, industrial, or business activity established or
L0:organized for the purpose of profit, provided that Indian ownership constitutes not less
L0:than 51 percent of the enterprise.
L0:“Indian tribe” means any Indian tribe, band, group, pueblo, or community, including
L0:native villages and native groups (including corporations organized by Kenai, Juneau,
L0:Sitka, and Kodiak) as defined in the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, that is
L0:recognized by the Federal Government as eligible for services from BIA in accordance
L0:with 25 U.S.C. 1452(c).
L0:“Interested party” means a contractor or an actual or prospective offeror whose
L0:direct economic interest would be affected by the award of a subcontract or by the
L0:failure to award a subcontract.
L0:“Native Hawaiian small business concern” means an entity that is—
L1:(1) A small business concern as defined in Section 3 of the Small Business Act
L0:(15 U.S.C. 632) and relevant implementing regulations; and
L1:(2) Owned and controlled by a Native Hawaiian as defined in 25 U.S.C. 4221(9).
L1:(b) The Contractor shall use its best efforts to give Indian organizations, Indian-
L0:owned economic enterprises, and Native Hawaiian small business concerns the
L0:maximum practicable opportunity to participate in the subcontracts it awards, to the
L0:fullest extent consistent with efficient performance of the contract.
L1:(c) The Contracting Officer and the Contractor, acting in good faith, may rely on the
L0:representation of an Indian organization, Indian-owned economic enterprise, or Native
L0:Hawaiian small business concern as to its eligibility, unless an interested party
L0:challenges its status or the Contracting Officer has independent reason to question that
L0:status.
L1:(d) In the event of a challenge to the representation of a subcontractor, the
L0:Contracting Officer will refer the matter to—
L2:(1)(i) For matters relating to Indian organizations or Indian-owned economic
L0:enterprises:
L0:U.S. Department of the Interior
L0:Bureau of Indian Affairs
L0:Attn: Bureau Procurement Chief
L0:12220 Sunrise Valley Drive
L0:Reston, VA 20191
L0:Phone: 703-390-6433
L0:Website: https://www.bia.gov/
L1:(ii) The BIA will determine the eligibility and will notify the Contracting
L0:Officer.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 26
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 226
L2:(2)(i) For matters relating to Native Hawaiian small business concerns:
L0:Department of Hawaiian Home Lands
L0:PO Box 1879
L0:Honolulu, HI 96805
L0:Phone: 808-620-9500
L0:Website: http://dhhl.hawaii.gov/
L1:(ii) The Department of Hawaiian Home Lands will determine the eligibility
L0:and will notify the Contracting Officer.
L1:(e) No incentive payment will be made—
L1:(1) While a challenge is pending; or
L1:(2) If a subcontractor is determined to be an ineligible participant.
L2:(f)(1) The Contractor, on its own behalf or on behalf of a subcontractor at any tier,
L0:may request an incentive payment in accordance with this clause.
L1:(2) The incentive amount that may be requested is 5 percent of the estimated
L0:cost, target cost, or fixed price included in the subcontract at the time of award to the
L0:Indian organization, Indian-owned economic enterprise, or Native Hawaiian small
L0:business concern.
L1:(3) In the case of a subcontract for commercial products or commercial services,
L0:the Contractor may receive an incentive payment only if the subcontracted items are
L0:produced or manufactured in whole or in part by an Indian organization, Indian-owned
L0:economic enterprise, or Native Hawaiian small business concern.
L1:(4) The Contractor has the burden of proving the amount claimed and shall
L0:assert its request for an incentive payment prior to completion of contract performance.
L1:(5) The Contracting Officer, subject to the terms and conditions of the contract
L0:and the availability of funds, will authorize an incentive payment of 5 percent of the
L0:estimated cost, target cost, or fixed price included in the subcontract awarded to the
L0:Indian organization, Indian-owned economic enterprise, or Native Hawaiian small
L0:business concern.
L1:(6) If the Contractor requests and receives an incentive payment on behalf of a
L0:subcontractor, the Contractor is obligated to pay the subcontractor the incentive
L0:amount.
L1:(g) The Contractor shall insert the substance of this clause, including this
L0:paragraph (g), in all subcontracts exceeding $500,000.
L0:(End of clause)

L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 226
L0:REPRESENTATION FOR DEMONSTRATION PROJECT FOR CONTRACTORS
L0:EMPLOYING PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES (DEC 2019)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this provision—
L0:“Eligible contractor” means a business entity operated on a for-profit or nonprofit
L0:basis that—
L1:(1) Employs severely disabled individuals at a rate that averages not less than

L1:(3) Provides, for its employees, health insurance and a retirement plan
L0:comparable to those provided for employees by business entities of similar size in its
L0:industrial sector or geographic region.
L0:“Severely disabled individual” means an individual with a disability (as defined in

L0:employ severely disabled individuals. To be eligible for award, an offeror must be an

L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 26

L0:PGI 226.72—DEMONSTRATION PROJECT FOR CONTRACTORS EMPLOYING
L0:PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES
L0:PGI 226.7202 Procedures.
L0:PGI 226.7202-1 Presolicitation
L0:When electing to use the Demonstration Project—
L1:(a) Prepare a written justification, in accordance with FAR part 6.103-5, limiting the

L0:not an eligible contractor; however, the contract will not count toward DoD’s small
L0:disadvantaged business goal.
