title: 227.7100 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:227.7100 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart—
L1:(a) Prescribes policies and procedures for the acquisition of technical data, computer
L0:software, computer software documentation, and the rights to use, modify, reproduce,
L0:release, perform, display, or disclose technical data. It implements the following laws
L0:and Executive Order:
L1:(1) 10 U.S.C. 3013.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(2) 10 U.S.C. 3208(d).
L1:(3) 10 U.S.C. 3771-3775.
L1:(4) 10 U.S.C. 3781-3786.
L1:(5) 10 U.S.C. 8687.
L1:(6) 17 U.S.C. 1301, et seq.
L1:(7) Public Law 103-355.
L1:(8) Executive Order 12591 (subsection 1(b)(7)).
L1:(b) Does not apply to—
L1:(1) Releases of technical data, computer software, and computer software
L0:documentation to litigation support contractors (see subpart 204.74); or
L1:(2) Computer software or computer software documentation acquired under
L0:Federal Supply Schedule contracts or orders.

title: 227.7101 Definitions
content:
L0:227.7101 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Commercial computer software” means software developed or regularly used for
L0:nongovernmental purposes which—
L1:(1) Has been sold, leased, or licensed to the public;
L1:(2) Has been offered for sale, lease, or license to the public;
L1:(3) Has not been offered, sold, leased, or licensed to the public but will be available
L0:for commercial sale, lease, or license in time to satisfy the delivery requirements of this
L0:contract; or
L1:(4) Satisfies a criterion expressed in paragraph (1), (2), or (3) of this definition and
L0:would require only minor modification to meet the requirements of this contract.
L0:“Computer program” means a set of instructions, rules, or routines recorded in a form
L0:that is capable of causing a computer to perform a specific operation or series of
L0:operations.
L0:“Computer software” means computer programs, source code, source code listings,
L0:object code listings, design details, algorithms, processes, flow charts, formulae and
L0:related material that would enable the software to be reproduced, recreated, or
L0:recompiled. Computer software does not include computer data bases or computer
L0:software documentation.
L0:“Computer software documentation” means owner’s manuals, user’s manuals,
L0:installation instructions, operating instructions, and other similar items, regardless of
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:storage medium, that explain the capabilities of the computer software or provide
L0:instructions for using the software.
L0:“Contractor” means a contractor to include a contractor’s subcontractors, suppliers, or
L0:potential subcontractors or suppliers at any tier.
L0:“Covered Government support contractor” means a contractor (other than a litigation
L0:support contractor covered by 252.204-7014) under a contract, the primary purpose of
L0:which is to furnish independent and impartial advice or technical assistance directly to
L0:the Government in support of the Government’s management and oversight of a
L0:program or effort, rather than to directly furnish an end item or service to accomplish a
L0:program or effort, provided that the contractor—
L1:(1) Is not affiliated with the prime contractor or a first-tier subcontractor on the
L0:program or effort, or with any direct competitor of such prime contractor or any such
L0:first-tier subcontractor in furnishing end items or services of the type developed or
L0:produced on the program or effort; and
L1:(2) Receives access to technical data or computer software for performance of a
L0:Government contract that contains the clause at 252.227-7994, Limitations on the Use
L0:or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with Restrictive Legends.
L0:“Detailed manufacturing or process data” means technical data that describe the steps,
L0:sequences, and conditions of manufacturing, processing or assembly used by the
L0:manufacturer to produce an item or component or to perform a process.
L0:“Developed” means—
L1:(1) (Applicable to technical data other than computer software documentation.) An
L0:item, component, or process exists and is workable. Thus, the item or component must
L0:have been constructed or the process practiced. Workability is generally established
L0:when the item, component, or process has been analyzed or tested sufficiently to
L0:demonstrate to reasonable people skilled in the applicable art that there is a high
L0:probability that it will operate as intended. Whether, how much, and what type of
L0:analysis or testing is required to establish workability depends on the nature of the
L0:item, component, or process, and the state of the art. To be considered “developed,” the
L0:item, component, or process need not be at the stage where it could be offered for sale or
L0:sold on the commercial market, nor must the item, component, or process be actually
L0:reduced to practice within the meaning of Title 35 of the United States Code;
L1:(2) A computer program has been successfully operated in a computer and tested to
L0:the extent sufficient to demonstrate to reasonable persons skilled in the art that the
L0:program can reasonably be expected to perform its intended purpose;
L1:(3) Computer software, other than computer programs, has been tested or analyzed
L0:to the extent sufficient to demonstrate to reasonable persons skilled in the art that the
L0:software can reasonably be expected to perform its intended purpose; or
L1:(4) Computer software documentation the contractor must deliver under a contract
L0:has been written, in any medium, in sufficient detail to comply with requirements
L0:under that contract.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:“Developed exclusively at private expense” means development was accomplished
L0:entirely with costs charged to indirect cost pools, costs not allocated to a Government
L0:contract, or any combination thereof.
L1:(1) Private expense determinations should be made at the lowest practicable level.
L1:(2) Under fixed-price contracts, when total costs are greater than the firm-fixed-
L0:price or ceiling price of the contract, the additional development costs necessary to
L0:complete development shall not be considered when determining whether development
L0:was at Government, private, or mixed expense.
L0:“Developed exclusively with Government funds” means development was not
L0:accomplished exclusively or partially at private expense.
L0:“Developed with mixed funding” means development was accomplished partially with
L0:costs charged to indirect cost pools and/or costs not allocated to a government contract,
L0:and partially with costs charged directly to a government contract.
L0:“Form, fit, and function data” means technical data that describe the required overall
L0:physical, functional, and performance characteristics (along with the qualification
L0:requirements, if applicable) of an item, component, or process to the extent necessary to
L0:permit identification of physically and functionally interchangeable items.
L0:“Generated means”, with regard to technical data or computer software, first created in
L0:the performance of this contract.
L0:“Government purpose” means any activity in which the United States Government is a
L0:party, including cooperative agreements with international or multi-national defense
L0:organizations, or sales or transfers by the United States Government to foreign
L0:governments or international organizations. Government purposes include competitive
L0:procurement, but do not include the rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform,
L0:display, or disclose technical data, computer software, or computer software
L0:documentation for commercial purposes or authorize others to do so.
L0:“Government purpose rights” means the rights to—
L1:(1) Use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical data,
L0:computer software, or computer software documentation within the Government
L0:without restriction; and
L1:(2) Release or disclose technical data, computer software, or computer software
L0:documentation outside the Government and authorize persons to whom release or
L0:disclosure has been made to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or
L0:disclose that data or software for United States Government purposes.
L0:“Limited rights” means the rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display,
L0:or disclose technical data, in whole or in part, within the Government. The Government
L0:may not, without the written permission of the party asserting limited rights, release or
L0:disclose the technical data outside the Government, use the technical data for
L0:manufacture, or authorize the technical data to be used by another party, except that
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:the Government may reproduce, release, or disclose such data or authorize the use or
L0:reproduction of the data by persons outside the Government if—
L1:(1) The reproduction, release, disclosure, or use is—
L1:(i) Necessary for emergency repair and overhaul; or
L1:(ii) A release or disclosure to—
L1:(A) A covered Government support contractor in performance of its covered
L0:Government support contract for use, modification, reproduction, performance, display,
L0:or release or disclosure to a person authorized to receive limited rights technical data; or
L1:(B) A foreign government, of technical data other than detailed
L0:manufacturing or process data, when use of such data by the foreign government is in
L0:the interest of the Government and is required for evaluational or informational
L0:purposes;
L1:(2) The recipient of the technical data is subject to a prohibition on the further
L0:reproduction, release, disclosure, or use of the technical data; and
L1:(3) The contractor or subcontractor asserting the restriction is notified of such
L0:reproduction, release, disclosure, or use.
L0:“Offeror” means an offeror to include an offeror’s subcontractors, suppliers, or potential
L0:subcontractors or suppliers at any tier.
L0:“Other than commercial computer software” means software that does not qualify as
L0:commercial computer software under the definition of “commercial computer software”
L0:of this clause.
L0:“Restricted rights” apply only to other than commercial computer software and mean
L0:the Government’s rights to—
L1:(1) Use a computer program with one computer at one time. The program may not
L0:be accessed by more than one terminal or central processing unit or time shared unless
L0:otherwise permitted by this contract;
L1:(2) Transfer a computer program to another Government agency without the
L0:further permission of the Contractor if the transferor destroys all copies of the program
L0:and related computer software documentation in its possession and notifies the licensor
L0:of the transfer. Transferred programs remain subject to the provisions of this clause;
L1:(3) Make a reasonable number of copies of the computer software required for the
L0:purposes of safekeeping (archive), backup, modification, or other activities authorized in

title: 227.7103-1 Policy
content:
L0:227.7103-1 Policy.
L1:(a) DoD policy is to acquire only the technical data, computer software, and
L0:computer software documentation, and the associated rights, necessary to satisfy
L0:agency needs.
L1:(b) Contracting officers must ensure that solicitations and contracts—
L1:(1) Specify the technical data, computer software, and computer software
L0:documentation the contractor must deliver under a contract and delivery schedules for
L0:the data;
L1:(2) Specify procedures for determining the acceptability of technical data,
L0:computer software, and computer software documentation;
L1:(3) Specify separate line items, to the extent practicable, for the technical data,
L0:computer software, and computer software documentation the contractor must deliver
L0:under a contract and require offerors and contractors to price each deliverable data or
L0:computer software item separately; and
L1:(4) Require offerors and contractors to identify, to the extent practicable,
L0:technical data and computer software they will furnish or deliver with restrictions on
L0:the Government’s rights in the technical data or computer software.
L1:(c) Do not require offerors, either as a condition of being responsive to a solicitation
L0:or as a condition for award, to sell or otherwise relinquish to the Government any rights
L0:in computer software developed at private expense or technical data related to items,
L0:components or processes developed at private expense except for the data or the
L0:software identified at 227.7103-5(a)(2), (4) through (9), and (12) through (15).
L1:(d) Do not prohibit offerors and contractors from furnishing or offering to furnish
L0:computer software, items, components, or processes developed at private expense solely
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:because the Government’s rights to use, modify, release, reproduce, perform, display, or
L0:disclose computer software or technical data related to those items may be restricted.
L1:(e) Solicitations for major systems development contracts must not require offerors
L0:to submit proposals that would permit the Government to competitively acquire items
L0:identical to items developed at private expense unless a determination is made at a
L0:level above the contracting officer (10 U.S.C. 3208). The determination must address
L0:the following:
L1:(1) The offeror will not be able to satisfy program schedule or delivery
L0:requirements.
L1:(2) The offeror’s proposal to meet mobilization requirements does not satisfy
L0:mobilization needs.
L1:(f) For acquisitions involving major weapon systems or subsystems of major weapon
L0:systems, the acquisition plan must address acquisition strategies that provide for
L0:technical data, computer software, computer software documentation, and the
L0:associated license rights in accordance with 207.106-70.
L1:(g) The Government’s rights in a vessel design, and in any useful article embodying
L0:a vessel design, must be consistent with the Government’s rights in technical data
L0:related to the design (10 U.S.C. 8687; 17 U.S.C. 1301(a)(3)).

title: 227.7103-5 Government rights
content:
L0:227.7103-5 Government rights.
L0:The standard license rights that a licensor grants to the Government are unlimited
L0:rights, government purpose rights, limited rights, or restricted rights. In unusual
L0:situations, the standards rights may not satisfy the Government’s needs, or the
L0:Government may be willing to accept lesser rights in data or computer software in
L0:return for other consideration. In those cases, a special license may be negotiated.
L0:However, the licensor is not obligated to provide the Government greater rights, and
L0:the contracting officer is not required to accept lesser rights than the rights provided in
L0:the standard grant of license. The situations under which a particular grant of license
L0:applies are listed in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section.
L1:(a) Unlimited rights. The Government obtains unlimited rights in technical data,
L0:computer software, or computer software documentation that are—
L1:(1) Technical data related to an item, component, or process which has been or
L0:will be developed exclusively with Government funds;
L1:(2) Studies, analyses, test data, or similar data produced in the performance of
L0:a contract when the study, analysis, test, or similar work was specified as an element of
L0:performance;
L1:(3) Created exclusively with Government funds in the performance of a contract
L0:that does not require the development, manufacture, construction, or production of
L0:items, components, or processes;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(4) Form, fit, and function data;
L1:(5) Necessary for installation, operation, maintenance, or training purposes
L0:(other than detailed manufacturing or process data);
L1:(6) Corrections or changes to—
L1:(i) Government-furnished technical data; or
L1:(ii) Government-furnished computer software or computer software
L0:documentation;
L1:(7) Technical data, computer software, or computer software documentation
L0:that—
L1:(i) Is publicly available; or
L1:(ii) Was previously released or disclosed by the contractor or subcontractor
L0:without restrictions on further use, release or disclosure other than a release or
L0:disclosure resulting from—
L0:data or computer software to another party; or
L1:(A) The sale, transfer, or other assignment of interest in the technical
L0:another party;

L0:which the Government has obtained unlimited rights under another Government
L0:contract or as a result of negotiations; or
L1:(9) Technical data, computer software, or computer software documentation
L0:furnished to the Government, under a Government contract or subcontract , with—
L1:(i) Restricted rights in computer software, limited rights in technical data,
L0:or government purpose license rights and the restrictive conditions have expired; or

L0:such technical data or computer software for commercial purposes has expired.

L0:Government contract.
L1:(b) Government purpose rights. (1) The Government obtains government purpose
L0:rights in—

L0:production of items, components, or processes; or
L1:(iii) Computer software developed with mixed funding.
L1:(2) The period during which government purpose rights are effective is
L0:negotiable. A five year period is nominal. Either the Government or the contractor may
L0:request a different period.
L1:(3) The government purpose rights period begins upon execution of the contract,
L0:subcontract, or similar contractual instrument that required the development. Upon
L0:expiration of the Government rights period, the Government has unlimited rights in the
L0:data or software including the right to authorize others to use the data or software for
L0:commercial purposes.
L1:(4) During the government purpose rights period, the Government may not use,
L0:or authorize other persons to use, technical data or computer software marked with
L0:government purpose rights legends for commercial purposes. The Government will not
L0:release or disclose data or software in which it has government purpose rights to any
L0:person, or authorize others to do so, unless—
L1:(i) Prior to release or disclosure, the intended recipient is subject to the use
L0:and nondisclosure agreement at 227.7103-7; or
L1:(ii) The intended recipient is a Government contractor receiving access to
L0:the data or software for performance of a Government contract that contains the clause

L1:(5) When the Government will release or disclose technical data or computer

L0:prior to release or disclosure, to include that clause in lieu of requiring the contractor to

L2:(6)(i) Agencies must establish procedures to prevent the release or disclosure of

L0:entities that are not subject to use and disclosure restrictions. .
L1:(ii) Public announcements in the System for Award Management or other

L1:(c) Limited rights. (1) The Government obtains limited rights in technical data—

L1:(d) Restricted rights. (1) The Government obtains restricted rights in other than

L2:(2)(i) Contractors are not required to provide the Government additional rights
L0:in computer software delivered or otherwise provided to the Government with restricted
L0:rights.
L1:(ii) When the Government has a need for additional rights, negotiate with
L0:the contractor to determine acceptable terms for transferring such rights. Any resulting

L0:rights.
L1:(ii) When negotiating to obtain, relinquish, or increase the Government’s

title: 227.7103-7 Use and nondisclosure agreement
content:
L0:227.7103-7 Use and nondisclosure agreement.
L1:(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, agencies may not provide
L0:technical data or computer software delivered to the Government with restrictions on
L0:use, modification, reproduction, release, performance, display, or disclosure to third
L0:parties, until the intended recipient completes and signs the use and nondisclosure
L0:agreement at paragraph (c) of this section.
L1:(1) In an attachment to the use and nondisclosure agreement, the Government
L0:must stipulate the specific conditions under which an intended recipient will be
L0:authorized to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical
L0:data or computer software subject to limited rights, restricted rights, or SBIR/STTR
L0:data rights.
L1:(2) Modify paragraph (1)(d) of the use and nondisclosure agreement in
L0:paragraph (c) of this section to enter the conditions for an intended release, disclosure or
L0:authorized use of technical data or computer software subject to special license rights,
L0:consistent with the license requirements, governing the recipient’s obligations regarding
L0:use, modification, reproduction, release, performance, display, or disclosure of the data
L0:or software.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(b) Requirements for use and nondisclosure agreements does not apply to
L0:Government contractors needing access to a third party’s data or software for the
L0:performance of a Government contract that contains the clause at 252.227-7994,
L0:Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked
L0:with Restrictive Legends.
L1:(c) The prescribed use and nondisclosure agreement is:
L0:Use and NonDisclosure Agreement
L0:The undersigned, ________________ (Insert Name) ________________, an authorized
L0:representative of the ________________ (Insert Company Name) ________________,
L0:(which is hereinafter referred to as the “Recipient”) requests the Government to provide
L0:the Recipient with technical data or computer software (hereinafter referred to as
L0:“Data”) in which the Government’s use, modification, reproduction, release,
L0:performance, display or disclosure rights are restricted. Those Data are identified in an
L0:attachment to this Agreement. In consideration for receiving such Data, the Recipient
L0:agrees to use the Data strictly in accordance with this Agreement:
L1:(1) The Recipient shall—
L1:(a) Use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose Data marked with
L0:government purpose rights or SBIR/STTR data rights legends (after expiration of the
L0:SBIR/STTR data protection period provided in the SBIR/STTR data rights legend) only
L0:for government purposes and shall not do so for any commercial purpose. The Recipient
L0:shall not release, perform, display, or disclose these Data, without the express written
L0:permission of the contractor whose name appears in the restrictive legend (the
L0:“Contractor”), to any person other than its subcontractors or suppliers, or prospective
L0:subcontractors or suppliers, who require these Data to submit offers for, or perform,
L0:contracts with the Recipient. The Recipient shall require its subcontractors or
L0:suppliers, or prospective subcontractors or suppliers, to sign a use and nondisclosure
L0:agreement prior to disclosing or releasing these Data to such persons. Such agreement
L0:must be consistent with the terms of this agreement.
L1:(b) Use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical data marked
L0:with limited rights legends or SBIR/STTR data rights legends only as specified in the
L0:attachment to this Agreement. Release, performance, display, or disclosure to other
L0:persons is not authorized unless specified in the attachment to this Agreement or
L0:expressly permitted in writing by the Contractor. The Recipient shall promptly notify
L0:the Contractor of the execution of this Agreement and identify the Contractor’s Data
L0:that has been or will be provided to the Recipient, the date and place the Data were or
L0:will be received, and the name and address of the Government office that has provided
L0:or will provide the Data.
L1:(c) Use computer software marked with restricted rights or SBIR/STTR data rights
L0:legends only in performance of Contract Number ____[insert contract number(s))]. The
L0:recipient shall not, for example, enhance, decompile, disassemble, or reverse engineer
L0:the software; time share, or use a computer program with more than one computer at a
L0:time. The recipient may not release, perform, display, or disclose such software to
L0:others unless expressly permitted in writing by the licensor whose name appears in the
L0:restrictive legend. The Recipient shall promptly notify the software licensor of the
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:execution of this Agreement and identify the software that has been or will be provided
L0:to the Recipient, the date and place the software were or will be received, and the name
L0:and address of the Government office that has provided or will provide the software.
L1:(d) Use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose Data marked with
L0:special license rights legends. [To be completed by the contracting officer. See 227.7103-
L0:7(a)(2). Omit if none of the data requested is marked with special license rights
L0:legends.]
L1:(2) The Recipient agrees to adopt or establish operating procedures and physical
L0:security measures designed to protect these Data from inadvertent release or disclosure
L0:to unauthorized third parties.
L1:(3) The Recipient agrees to accept these Data “as is” without any Government
L0:representation as to suitability for intended use or warranty whatsoever. This
L0:disclaimer does not affect any obligation the Government may have regarding Data
L0:specified in a contract for the performance of that contract.
L1:(4) The Recipient may enter into any agreement directly with the Contractor with
L0:respect to the use, modification, reproduction, release, performance, display, or
L0:disclosure of these Data.
L1:(5) The Recipient agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the Government, its agents,
L0:and employees from every claim or liability, including attorneys’ fees, court costs, and
L0:expenses arising out of, or in any way related to, the misuse or unauthorized
L0:modification, reproduction, release, performance, display, or disclosure of Data received
L0:from the Government with restrictive legends by the Recipient or any person to whom
L0:the Recipient has released or disclosed the Data.
L1:(6) The Recipient is executing this Agreement for the benefit of the Contractor. The
L0:Contractor is a third party beneficiary of this Agreement who, in addition to any other
L0:rights it may have, is intended to have the rights of direct action against the Recipient
L0:or any other person to whom the Recipient has released or disclosed the Data, to seek
L0:damages from any breach of this Agreement or to otherwise enforce this Agreement.
L1:(7) The Recipient agrees to destroy these Data, and all copies of the Data in its
L0:possession, no later than 30 days after the date shown in paragraph (8) of this
L0:Agreement, to have all persons to whom it released the Data do so by that date, and to
L0:notify the Contractor that the Data have been destroyed.
L1:(8) This Agreement shall be effective for the period commencing with the Recipient’s
L0:execution of this Agreement and ending upon ________ (Insert Date) ________. The
L0:obligations imposed by this Agreement shall survive the expiration or termination of
L0:the Agreement.

title: 227.7103-9 Copyright
content:
L0:227.7103-9 Copyright.
L1:(a) Copyright license. (1) Contractors are required to grant or obtain for the
L0:Government license rights permitting the Government to reproduce data, distribute
L0:copies of the data, software, or software documentation, publicly perform or display the
L0:data, software, or software documentation or, through the right to modify data, prepare

L0:may exercise these rights varies for each of the standard data rights licenses obtained

L0:restricted rights license in computer software.
L1:(2) Contractors are not permitted to incorporate a third party’s copyrighted data

L0:which the Government will not receive a copyright license only when the Government’s
L0:requirements cannot be satisfied without the third-party material or when the use of
L0:the third-party material will result in cost savings to the Government which outweigh
L0:the lack of a copyright license.

title: 227.7103-10 Contractor identification and marking of technical data or
content:
L0:227.7103-10 Contractor identification and marking of technical data or
L0:computer software to be delivered with restrictive markings.
L1:(a) Contractor marking requirements. Contractors are required to—
L1:(1) Place restrictive markings on the data or software, provide instructions for
L0:the placement of the restrictive markings, and authorize the use of certain restrictive
L0:markings when restricting the Government’s rights in technical data or computer
L0:software; and
L1:(2) Deliver, furnish, or otherwise provide to the Government any technical data
L0:or computer software in which the Government has previously obtained rights with the
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:Government’s preexisting rights in that data or software, unless restrictions on the
L0:Government’s rights have expired. When restrictions still apply, the contractor is
L0:permitted to mark the data or software with the appropriate restrictive legend for
L0:which the data or software qualified.
L1:(b) Unmarked technical data. (1) Presume technical data or computer software
L0:delivered or otherwise provided with unlimited rights under a contract without
L0:restrictive markings may be released or disclosed without restriction. To the extent
L0:practicable, if a contractor has requested permission (see paragraph (b)(2) of this
L0:section) to correct an inadvertent omission of markings, do not release or disclose the
L0:technical data or computer software pending evaluation of the request.
L1:(2) A contractor may request permission to have appropriate legends placed on
L0:unmarked technical data or computer software at its expense. The request must be
L0:received by the contracting officer within 6 months following the furnishing or delivery
L0:of such data or software, or any extension of that time approved by the contracting
L0:officer. The person making the request must:
L1:(i) Identify the technical data or computer software that should have been
L0:marked;
L1:(ii) Demonstrate that the omission of the marking was inadvertent, the
L0:proposed marking is justified and conforms with the requirements for the marking of
L0:technical data or computer software contained in the contract; and
L1:(iii) Acknowledge, in writing, that the Government has no liability with
L0:respect to any disclosure, reproduction, or use of the technical data or computer
L0:software made prior to the addition of the marking or resulting from the omission of the
L0:marking.
L1:(3) Contracting officers should grant permission to mark only if the technical
L0:data or computer software were not distributed outside the Government or were
L0:distributed outside the Government with restrictions on further use or disclosure.

title: 227.7103-11 Contractor procedures and records
content:
L0:227.7103-11 Contractor procedures and records.
L1:(a) Contractors, and their subcontractors or suppliers that will deliver technical

title: 227.7103-12 Government right to establish conformity of markings
content:
L0:227.7103-12 Government right to establish conformity of markings.
L1:(a) Nonconforming markings. (1) The marking requirements in the applicable
L0:clauses prescribe the content and format of authorized markings on technical data and
L0:computer software. All other markings are nonconforming markings. An authorized
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:marking that is not in the form, or differs in substance, from the marking requirements
L0:in the clauses at 252.227-7989 and 252.227-7993 is also a nonconforming marking.
L1:(2) Notify the contractor or offeror of technical data or computer software
L0:bearing nonconforming markings to provide that person an opportunity to correct or
L0:strike the nonconforming marking at that person’s expense. If the contractor or offeror
L0:fails to correct the nonconformity and deliver the corrected data within 60 days
L0:following the person’s receipt of the data or software, the contracting officer may correct
L0:or strike the nonconformity at that person’s expense. Prior to correction, the
L0:Government may use the data in accordance with the proper restrictive marking.
L1:(b) Unjustified markings. (1) An unjustified marking is an authorized marking
L0:that does not accurately depict restrictions applicable to the Government’s use,
L0:modification, reproduction, release, performance, display, or disclosure of the marked
L0:technical data or computer software. Accordingly, a limited rights legend placed on
L0:technical data related to items, components, or processes developed under a
L0:Government contract either exclusively at Government expense or with mixed funding
L0:(situations under which the Government obtains unlimited or government purpose
L0:rights) is an unjustified marking. Similarly, a restricted rights legend placed on
L0:computer software developed under a Government contract either exclusively at
L0:Government expense or with mixed funding is an unjustified marking.
L1:(2) The contracting officer has the right to review and challenge the validity of
L0:unjustified markings. However, at any time during performance of a contract and
L0:notwithstanding existence of a challenge, the contracting officer and the person who has
L0:asserted a restrictive marking may agree that the restrictive marking is not justified.
L0:Upon such agreement, the contracting officer may either—
L1:(i) Strike or correct the unjustified marking at that person’s expense; or
L1:(ii) Instruct the person asserting the restriction to correct the technical data
L0:or computer software at that person’s expense. If the person fails to correct or strike the
L0:unjustified restriction and deliver the corrected data or software to the contracting
L0:officer within 60 days following this instruction, strike or correct the unjustified
L0:marking at that person’s expense.
citation: R-DFARS 227.7103-12 — Government right to establish conformity of markings

title: 227.7103-13 Government right to review, verify, challenge, and validate
content:
L0:227.7103-13 Government right to review, verify, challenge, and validate
L0:asserted restrictions.
L1:(a) General. (1) An offeror’s assertion of restrictions on the Government’s rights to
L0:use, modify, reproduce, release, or disclose technical data or computer software do not,
L0:by themselves, determine the extent of the Government’s rights in the technical data or
L0:computer software.
L1:(2) Review asserted restrictions before acceptance of technical data and
L0:computer software deliverables under a contract.
L1:(3) The contracting officer may challenge asserted restrictions when reasonable
L0:grounds exist to believe an assertion is not valid.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(b) Pre-award considerations. See 227.7103-3(a) for guidance on pre-award review
L0:of asserted restrictions.
L1:(c) Challenge considerations and presumption.
L1:(1) Requirements to initiate a challenge. (i) Contracting officers must have
L0:reasonable grounds to challenge the validity of an asserted restriction. Before issuing a
L0:challenge to an asserted restriction, carefully consider all available information related
L0:to the assertion.
L1:(ii) A need for additional license rights is not, by itself, a sufficient basis for
L0:requesting information concerning an asserted restriction.
L1:(iii) Follow the procedures at 227.7103-5(e) when the Government needs
L0:additional license rights but has no grounds to challenge an asserted restriction.
L1:(2) Commercial products and commercial services—presumption regarding
L0:development exclusively at private expense.
L1:(i) Presume that a commercial product or commercial service was developed
L0:exclusively at private expense whether or not a contractor or subcontractor submits a
L0:justification in response to a challenge notice. Under 10 U.S.C. 3772(a)(1) and 3784,
L0:there is a presumption and procedures regarding validation of asserted restrictions for
L0:technical data related to commercial products or commercial services on the basis of
L0:development exclusively at private expense.
L1:(ii) Do not challenge a contractor’s assertion that a commercial product or
L0:commercial service was developed exclusively at private expense unless the
L0:Government can specifically state the reasonable grounds to question the validity of the
L0:assertion. The challenge notice must include sufficient information to demonstrate that
L0:the commercial product or commercial service was not developed exclusively at private
L0:expense. To sustain the challenge, provide information demonstrating that the
L0:commercial product or commercial service was not developed exclusively at private
L0:expense.
L1:(ii) The challenge notice and all related correspondence are subject to
L0:handling procedures for classified information and controlled unclassified information.
L1:(iv) A contractor’s or subcontractor’s failure to respond to the challenge
L0:notice cannot be the sole basis for issuing a final decision denying the validity of an
L0:asserted restriction.
L1:(d) Challenge and validation.
L1:(1) Challenge period. Review asserted restrictions before acceptance of
L0:technical data or computer software deliverable under the contract. Challenge
L0:assertions within six years after final payment under the contract or six years after
L0:delivery of the data or software, whichever is later. There is no time limit for
L0:challenging restrictive markings if the technical data or computer software—
L1:(i) Are publicly available without restrictions;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(ii) Have been provided to the United States without restriction;
L1:(iii) Have been otherwise made available without restriction other than a
L0:release or disclosure resulting from the sale, transfer, or other assignment of interest in
L0:the technical data or computer software to another party or the sale or transfer of some
L0:or all of a business entity or its assets to another party; or
L1:(iv) Is the subject of a fraudulently asserted use or release restriction.
L1:(2) Pre-challenge requests for information.
L1:(i) Contracting officers may request the person asserting a restriction to
L0:furnish a written explanation of the facts and supporting documentation for the
L0:assertion in detail to enable the contracting officer to determine the basis of the
L0:restrictive markings. Request additional supporting documentation when the
L0:explanation does not, in the contracting officer’s opinion, establish the validity of the
L0:assertion.
L1:(ii) Consider challenging the assertion when—
L0:contracting officer’s request for information or additional supporting documentation; or
L1:(A) The person asserting the restriction fails to respond to the
L0:related to the validity of a restrictive marking, does not justify the asserted restriction.
L1:(B) The information submitted, or any other available information
L1:(3) Transacting matters directly with subcontracts. Contracting officers should
L0:permit, after obtaining the contractor’s agreement, a subcontractor or supplier to
L0:transact challenge and validation matters directly with the Government when—
L1:(i) A subcontractor’s or supplier’s business interests in its technical data or
L0:computer software would be compromised if the data were disclosed to a higher tier
L0:contractor;
L1:(ii) The contractor will unlikely respond in a timely manner to a challenge,
L0:and an untimely response would jeopardize a subcontractor’s or suppliers right to assert
L0:restrictions; or
L1:(iii) A subcontractor or supplier requests it.
L1:(4) Challenge notice.
L1:(i) Do not issue a challenge notice unless reasonable grounds exist to
L0:question the validity of an assertion. For commercial products or commercial services,
L0:also see paragraph (c)(2) of this section.
L1:(ii) No requirement exists to request information under paragraph (d)(2) of
L0:this section before issuing a challenge.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(iii) Issue challenge notices, in writing, to the contractor or, after
L0:consideration of the situations described in paragraph (d)(3) of this section, the person
L0:asserting the restriction. See PGI 227.7103-13(d)(4)(iii) for procedures regarding
L0:challenge notices.
L1:(5) Extension of response time. If the contractor submits a written request for
L0:additional time to prepare a response, the contracting officer will extend the time for
L0:response as appropriate, in accordance with paragraph (f)(2) of the clause at 252.225-
L0:7999.
L1:(6) Contracting officer’s final decision. Issue a final decision for each challenged
L0:assertion, whether or not the contractor justified the assertion.
L1:(i) Failure to respond. If the person asserting the restriction fails to
L0:respond to the challenge within 60 days or any extension of time the contracting officer
L0:granted, issue a final decision that the assertion is not justified as soon as practicable.
L1:(ii) Assertion justified. If the assertion is determined to be justified based on
L0:the response to the challenge notice, issue the final decision sustaining the validity of
L0:the restriction. The contracting officer will issue this final decision within 60 days after
L0:receipt of the response to the challenge notice, or within a longer period that the
L0:contracting officer has notified the contractor or subcontractor that the Government will
L0:require. The contracting officer will provide notification of any longer period for
L0:issuance of a final decision within 60 days after receipt of the response to the challenge
L0:notice. The Contracting Officer will provide notification of any longer period for
L0:issuance of a final decision within 60 days after receipt of the response to the challenge
L0:notice. If the contractor made the asserted restriction subsequent to submitting its
L0:offer, then add the asserted restriction to the contract attachment.
L1:(iii) Assertion not justified. If the assertion is determined not to be justified
L0:based on the information provided, issue a final decision. The decision must be issued
L0:within 60 days after receipt of the response to the challenge notice, or within a longer
L0:period that the contracting officer has notified the contractor or subcontractor that the
L0:Government will require. The Contracting Officer will provide notification of any longer
L0:period for issuance of a final decision within 60 days after receipt of the response to the
L0:challenge notice. As provided in paragraph (h) of the clause, the Government is
L0:obligated to continue to respect the asserted restrictions through final disposition of any
L0:appeal unless the agency head notifies the person asserting the restriction that urgent
L0:or compelling circumstances dictate otherwise.
L1:(7) Multiple challenges to an asserted restriction. When more than one
L0:contracting officer challenges an asserted restriction, the contracting officer who made
L0:the earliest challenge is responsible for coordinating the Government challenges. That
L0:contracting officer must consult with all other contracting officers making challenges,
L0:verify that all challenges apply to the same asserted restriction and, after consulting
L0:with the contractor, subcontractor, or supplier asserting the restriction, issue a schedule
L0:that provides that person a reasonable opportunity to respond to each challenge.
L1:(8) Validation. Only a contracting officer’s final decision, actions of an agency
L0:board of contract appeals, or a court of competent jurisdiction sustaining the validity of
L0:an asserted restriction, constitutes validation of the asserted restriction.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
citation: R-DFARS 227.7103-13 — Government right to review, verify, challenge, and validate

title: 227.7103-14 Conformity, acceptance, and warranty of technical data and
content:
L0:227.7103-14 Conformity, acceptance, and warranty of technical data and
L0:computer software.
L1:(a) [Reserved]
L1:(b) Conformity and acceptance. (1) Solicitations and contracts requiring the
L0:delivery of technical data, including computer software documentation, must specify the
L0:requirements that the data must satisfy to be acceptable. Contracting officers, or their
L0:authorized representatives, are responsible for determining whether technical data
L0:tendered for acceptance conform to the contractual requirements.
L1:(2) The clause at 252.227-7996, Technical Data—Withholding of Payment,
L0:provides for withholding up to 10 percent of the contract price pending either correction
L0:or replacement of the nonconforming technical data, or negotiation of an equitable
L0:reduction in contract price. The amount subject to withholding may be expressed as a
L0:fixed dollar amount or as a percentage of the contract price. In either case, consider the
L0:relative value and importance of the data when determining the amount.
L1:(3) Do not accept technical data that do not conform to the contractual
L0:requirements in all respects. Except for nonconforming restrictive markings (see
L0:paragraph (b)(4) of this section), require correction or replacement of nonconforming
L0:data (or an equitable reduction in contract price when correction or replacement of the
L0:nonconforming data is not practicable or is not in the Government’s interests) in
L0:accordance with—
L1:(i) The provisions of a contract clause providing for inspection and
L0:acceptance of deliverables and remedies for nonconforming deliverables; or
L1:(ii) The procedures at FAR 46.407(c) through (g), if the contract does not
L0:contain an inspection clause providing remedies for nonconforming deliverables.
L1:(4) Follow the procedures at 227.7103-12(a)(2) if nonconforming markings are
L0:the sole reason technical data fail to conform to contractual requirements. The
L0:contracting officer may withhold an amount for payment, consistent with the terms of
L0:the clause at 252.227-7996, pending correction of the nonconforming markings.
L2:(5)(i) Specify, in solicitations and contracts requiring the delivery of computer
L0:software, requirements the software must satisfy to be acceptable under the contract.
L1:(ii) Contracting officers, or their authorized representatives, are responsible

L0:follow the procedures at 227.7103-12(a) if nonconforming markings are the sole reason

L0:nonconforming data is not practicable or is not in the Government’s interests) in

L0:acceptance of deliverables and remedies for nonconforming deliverables; or
L1:(A) The provisions of a contract clause providing for inspection and
L1:(B) The procedures at FAR part 46.407(c) through (g), if the contract

L1:(c) Warranty. (1) Consider the intended use of the technical data (including repair

L0:Data, and its alternates, or a substantially similar clause when the Government needs a
L0:specific warranty of technical data.
L1:(3) Warranties for Computer Software. (i) Weapon systems. Computer software
L0:that is a component of a weapon system or major subsystem should be warranted as

L1:(ii) Non-weapon systems. The contracting officer must approve use of a

L0:When approval for a warranty is obtained, modify the clause at 252.246-7001, Warranty
L0:of Data, and its alternates, as necessary for use with computer software.

title: 227.7104-1 Policy
content:
L0:227.7104-1 Policy.
L1:(a) Do not require an offeror, either as a condition of being responsive to a
L0:solicitation or as a condition for award, to sell or otherwise relinquish to the
L0:Government any rights in technical data related to items, components, or processes
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:developed under a SBIR/STTR contract or any rights in computer software generated
L0:under a SBIR/STTR contract except for the standard rights identified at 227.7104-2.
L1:(b) Do not prohibit contractors and offerors from furnishing or offering to furnish
L0:items, components, or processes developed under a SBIR/STTR contract or computer
L0:software generated under a SBIR/STTR contract solely because the Government’s
L0:rights to use, modify, release, reproduce, perform, display, or disclose such computer
L0:software or technical data related to those items, components, or processes may be
L0:restricted.
L1:(c) Consistent with the guidance in this section, 227.7103-3(a)(5), and other
L0:acquisition guidance applicable to SBIR/STTR solicitations, the Government may use
L0:information provided by offerors in response to a solicitation in the source selection
L0:process to evaluate the impact of proposed restrictions on the Government’s ability to
L0:use or disclose technical data or computer software.
L1:(d) SBIR/STTR data rights apply to SBIR/STTR data that are delivered, developed,
L0:or generated in the performance of a contract or agreement that is covered by
L0:SBIR/STTR policies, including contracts and subcontracts that include phase III work.
L0:Phase III work refers to work that derives from, extends, or completes an effort made
L0:under prior SBIR/STTR contracts or agreements, and is funded by sources other than
L0:SBIR/STTR programs (see PGI 227.7104-1).
L1:(e) For SBIR/STTR data that is other than commercial technical data, and other
L0:than commercial computer software and computer software documentation, see—
L1:(1) 227.7103-9 for guidance on copyright licenses;
L1:(2) 227.7103-3 and 227.7103-10 for guidance on contractor identification and
L0:marking of technical data and computer software to be delivered with restrictive
L0:markings;
L1:(3) 227.7103-11 for guidance on maintenance of contractor records; and
L1:(4) 227.7103-12 for guidance on nonconforming and unjustified markings.

title: 227.7104-2 Rights in SBIR or STTR data
content:
L0:227.7104-2 Rights in SBIR or STTR data.
L1:(a) The Government obtains the following standard license rights in SBIR/STTR
L0:data:
L1:(1) Unlimited rights in the technical data and computer software listed in
L0:paragraph (c)(1) of the clause at 252.227-7993, Rights in Other Than Commercial
L0:Technical Data and Computer Software-Small Business Innovation Research Program
L0:and Small Business Technology Transfer Program.
L1:(2) SBIR/STTR data rights in all other technical data and computer software
L0:developed or generated under the phase I, II, or III SBIR/STTR contract or subcontract
L0:and marked with the SBIR/STTR data rights marking.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(i) SBIR/STTR data rights provide the Government limited rights in such
L0:technical data and restricted rights in such computer software during the SBIR/STTR
L0:data protection period commencing on the date of contract award and ending 20 years
L0:after that date unless, after award, the agency and the contractor negotiate for some
L0:other protection period for the SBIR/STTR data.
L1:(ii) Upon expiration of the SBIR/STTR data protection period, the
L0:Government has government purpose rights in the SBIR/STTR data. These
L0:government purpose rights do not expire. See PGI 227.7104-2 for additional guidance
L0:on the SBIR/STTR data protection period.
L1:(b) During the SBIR/STTR data protection period, the Government may not release
L0:or disclose technical data or computer software subject to SBIR/STTR data rights to any
L0:person except as authorized for limited rights technical data or restricted rights
L0:computer software, respectively.
L1:(c) The Government and contractor or subcontractor may negotiate special license
L0:rights only after contract award. The Government must not condition contract award
L0:on the contractor or subcontractor negotiating or consenting to negotiate special license
L0:rights. Negotiation of special license rights is authorized only after contract award by
L0:mutual agreement of the parties.
L1:(d) The Small Business Administration’s SBIR and STTR Program Policy Directive
L0:(effective May 3, 2023) provides for special consideration regarding the handling (e.g.,
L0:disclosure, reverse engineering) of prototypes generated under SBIR and STTR awards,
L0:to avoid effects that may appear to be inconsistent with the SBIR and STTR program
L0:objectives and to allow the SBIR/STTR awardee to retain rights in SBIR/STTR data
L0:during the SBIR/STTR data protection period.
L1:(e) The clause at 252.227-7993 specifies the Government’s license rights in
L0:SBIR/STTR data. However, the following clauses or guidance specify the Government’s
L0:license rights in any data that are not SBIR/STTR data:
L1:(1) For technical data related to other than commercial products or commercial

L1:(3) For other than commercial computer software or computer software

L1:(4) For commercial computer software and computer software documentation,

title: 227.7105-1 General
content:
L0:227.7105-1 General.
L1:(a) Existing works include motion pictures, television recordings, video recordings,
L0:and other audiovisual works in any medium; sound recordings in any medium; musical,
L0:dramatic, and literary works; pantomimes and choreographic works; pictorial, graphic,
L0:and sculptural works; and works of a similar nature. Usually, these or similar works
L0:were not first created, developed, generated, originated, prepared, or produced under a
L0:Government contract. Therefore, the Government must obtain a license in the work if
L0:it intends to reproduce the work, distribute copies of the work, prepare derivative
L0:works, or perform or display the work publicly. When the Government is not
L0:responsible for the content of an existing work, it should require the copyright owner to
L0:indemnify the Government for liabilities that may arise out of the content, performance,
L0:use, or disclosure of such data.
L2:(b)(1) Follow the procedures at 227.7106 for special works that will be first created,
L0:developed, generated, originated, prepared, or produced under a Government contract
L0:and the Government—
L1:(i) Needs to control distribution of the work; or
L1:(ii) Has a specific need to obtain indemnity for liabilities that may arise out
L0:of the creation, content, performance, use, or disclosure of the work or from libelous or
L0:other unlawful material contained in the work.
L1:(2) Follow the procedures at 227.7103 when the Government does not need to
L0:control distribution of such works or obtain such indemnities.

title: 227.7105-2 Acquisition of existing works without modification
content:
L0:227.7105-2 Acquisition of existing works without modification.
L1:(a) No specific contract clause governs the Government’s rights in existing works.
L0:Negotiate contract terms related to use and distribution of existing works when—
L1:(1) The existing works will be acquired without modification; and
L1:(2) The Government requires the right to reproduce, prepare derivative works,
L0:or publicly perform or display the existing works; or
L1:(3) The Government has a specific need to obtain indemnity for liabilities that
L0:may arise out of the content, performance, use, or disclosure of such data.
L1:(b) Negotiated terms should provide the Government, and others acting on its
L0:behalf, a paid-up, non-exclusive, irrevocable, world-wide license to reproduce, prepare
L0:derivative works and publicly perform or display the works called for by a contract and
L0:to authorize others to do so for government purposes.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(c) A contract clause is not required to acquire existing works such as books,
L0:magazines and periodicals, in any storage or retrieval medium, when the Government
L0:will not reproduce the books, magazines or periodicals, or prepare derivative works.

title: 227.7200 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:227.7200 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart—
L1:(a) Prescribes policies and procedures for the acquisition of technical data, computer
L0:software and computer software documentation related to commercial products,
L0:components, services, processes, and computer software, and the rights to use, modify,
L0:reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose such data or software. It implements
L0:the following laws and Executive order:
L1:(1) 10 U.S.C. 3013.
L1:(2) 10 U.S.C. 3208(d).
L1:(3) 10 U.S.C. 3771-3775.
L1:(4) 10 U.S.C. 3781-3786.
L1:(5) 10 U.S.C. 4576.
L1:(6) Executive Order 12591 (subsection 1(b)(7)).
L1:(b) Does not apply to—
L1:(1) Technical data, computer software, or computer software documentation
L0:acquired under General Services Administration (GSA) schedule contracts; or
L1:(2) Releases of technical data, computer software, or computer software
L0:documentation to litigation support contractors (see subpart 204.74).

title: 227.7201 Definitions
content:
L0:227.7201 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Commercial computer software” means software developed or regularly used for
L0:nongovernmental purposes which—
L1:(1) Has been sold, leased, or licensed to the public;
L1:(2) Has been offered for sale, lease, or license to the public;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(3) Has not been offered, sold, leased, or licensed to the public but will be available
L0:for commercial sale, lease, or license in time to satisfy the delivery requirements of this
L0:contract; or
L1:(4) Satisfies a criterion expressed in paragraph (1), (2), or (3) of this definition and
L0:would require only minor modification to meet the requirements of this contract.
L0:“Computer software” means computer programs, source code, source code listings,
L0:object code listings, design details, algorithms, processes, flow charts, formulae and
L0:related material that would enable the software to be reproduced, recreated, or
L0:recompiled. Computer software does not include computer data bases or computer
L0:software documentation.
L0:“Computer software documentation” means owner’s manuals, user’s manuals,
L0:installation instructions, operating instructions, and other similar items, regardless of
L0:storage medium, that explain the capabilities of the computer software or provide
L0:instructions for using the software.
L0:“Contractor” means a contractor to include a contractor’s subcontractors, suppliers, or
L0:potential subcontractors or suppliers at any tier
L0:“Covered Government support contractor” means a contractor (other than a litigation
L0:support contractor covered by 252.204-7014) under a contract, the primary purpose of
L0:which is to furnish independent and impartial advice or technical assistance directly to
L0:the Government in support of the Government’s management and oversight of a
L0:program or effort, rather than to directly furnish an end item or service to accomplish a
L0:program or effort, provided that the contractor—
L1:(1) Is not affiliated with the prime contractor or a first-tier subcontractor on the
L0:program or effort, or with any direct competitor of such prime contractor or any such
L0:first-tier subcontractor in furnishing end items or services of the type developed or
L0:produced on the program or effort; and
L1:(2) Receives access to technical data or computer software for performance of a
L0:Government contract that contains the clause at 252.227-7994, Limitations on the Use
L0:or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with Restrictive Legends.
L0:“Offeror” means an offeror to include an offeror’s subcontractors, suppliers, or potential
L0:subcontractors or suppliers at any tier
L0:“Technical data” means recorded information, regardless of the form or method of the
L0:recording, of a scientific or technical nature (including computer software
L0:documentation). The term does not include computer software or financial,
L0:administrative, cost or pricing, or management information, or information incidental to
L0:contract administration.

title: 227.7208 Technical data related to commercial products, commercial
content:
L0:227.7208 Technical data related to commercial products, commercial
L0:components, commercial services, or commercial processes.
citation: R-DFARS 227.7208 — Technical data related to commercial products, commercial

title: 227.7208-1 Policy
content:
L0:227.7208-1 Policy.
L1:(a) DoD policy is to acquire only the technical data customarily provided to the
L0:public with a commercial product, commercial service, or commercial process, except
L0:technical data that—
L1:(1) Are form, fit, or function data;
L1:(2) Are required for repair or maintenance of commercial products or
L0:commercial processes, or for the proper installation, operating, or handling of a
L0:commercial product, either as a stand alone unit or as a part of a military system, when
L0:such data are not customarily provided to commercial users or the data provided to
L0:commercial users is not sufficient for military purposes; or
L1:(3) Describe the modifications made at Government expense to a commercial
L0:product, commercial service, or commercial process in order to meet the requirements of
L0:a Government solicitation.
L1:(b) To encourage offerors and contractors to offer or use commercial products to
L0:satisfy military requirements, do not require (except for the technical data described in
L0:paragraph (a) of this section) offerors, and contractors to—
L1:(1) Furnish technical information related to commercial products, commercial
L0:services, or commercial processes that is not customarily provided to the public; or
L1:(2) Relinquish to, or otherwise provide, the Government rights to use, modify,
L0:reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical data related to commercial
L0:products, commercial services, or commercial processes except for a mutually agreed
L0:transfer of rights.
L1:(c) The Government’s rights in a vessel design, and in any useful article embodying
L0:a vessel design, must be consistent with the Government’s rights in technical data
L0:related to the design (10 U.S.C. 8687; 17 U.S.C. 1301(a)(3)).

title: 227.7208-2 Rights in technical data
content:
L0:227.7208-2 Rights in technical data.
L1:(a) The Government has specific license rights in technical data related to
L0:commercial products, commercial services, or commercial processes.
L1:(1) DoD may use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose data
L0:only within the Government.
L1:(2) The data may not be used to manufacture additional quantities of the
L0:commercial products and, except for emergency repair or overhaul and for covered
L0:Government support contractors, may not be released or disclosed to, or used by, third
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:parties without the contractor’s written permission. Those restrictions do not apply to
L0:the technical data described in 227.7208-1(a).
L1:(b) If the Government requires additional rights, negotiate with the contractor to
L0:determine whether acceptable terms exist for transferring such rights. Any resulting
L0:license agreement, made part of the contract, must list or describe all technical data for
L0:which the contractor has granted the Government additional rights, and specify the
L0:additional rights granted

title: 227.7208-3 Government right to review, verify, challenge, and validate
content:
L0:227.7208-3 Government right to review, verify, challenge, and validate
L0:asserted restrictions.
L0:Follow the procedures at 227.7103-13 regarding the validation of asserted restrictions
L0:on technical data related to commercial products or commercial services.
citation: R-DFARS 227.7208-3 — Government right to review, verify, challenge, and validate

title: 227.7208-4 Contract clauses
content:
L0:227.7208-4 Contract clauses.
L2:(a)(1) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, insert the clause at
L0:252.227-7990, Technical Data—Commercial Products and Commercial Services, in
L0:solicitations and contracts, including solicitations and contracts using FAR part 12
L0:procedures for the acquisition of commercial products and commercial services, when
L0:the contract will require delivery of technical data related to commercial products,
L0:commercial components, commercial services, or commercial processes.
L1:(2) Insert the clause at 252.227-7990 with its Alternate I in solicitations and
L0:contracts, including solicitations and contracts using FAR part 12 procedures for the
L0:acquisition of commercial products and commercial services, for the development or
L0:delivery of a vessel design or any useful article embodying a vessel design.
L2:(b)(1) Government development funding. When the Government has paid for any
L0:portion of the development of a commercial product or commercial service, insert the
L0:clause at 252.227-7989, Rights in Technical Data, Computer Software, and Computer
L0:Software Documentation—Other Than Commercial Products and Commercial Services,
L0:in addition to the clause at 252.227-7990.
L1:(2) Applicability. For technical data, the clause at 252.227-7989 governs the
L0:technical data related to the Government-funded portions, and the clause at 252.227-
L0:7990 governs the technical data related to the portions developed exclusively at private
L0:expense. These clauses do not apply to commercial computer software or commercial
L0:software documentation.
L1:(c) Insert the clause at 252.227-7997, Validation of Asserted Restrictions on
L0:Technical Data, in solicitations and contracts using FAR part 12 procedures for the
L0:acquisition of commercial products and commercial services that include the clause at

title: 252.227-7990 Technical Data—Commercial Products and Commercial
content:
L0:252.227-7990 Technical Data—Commercial Products and Commercial
L0:Services. (DEVIATION 2026-O0036)
L0:As prescribed in 227.7203-6(a)(1), use the following clause:
L0:TECHNICAL DATA—COMMERCIAL PRODUCTS AND COMMERCIAL SERVICES
L0:(DEVIATION 2026-O0036) (FEB 2026)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Commercial product and commercial service” includes commercial components and
L0:commercial processes but does not include commercial computer software.
L0:“Covered Government support contractor” means a contractor (other than a litigation
L0:support contractor covered by 252.204-7014) under a contract, the primary purpose of
L0:which is to furnish independent and impartial advice or technical assistance directly to
L0:the Government in support of the Government’s management and oversight of a
L0:program or effort (rather than to directly furnish an end item or service to accomplish a
L0:program or effort), provided that the contractor—
L1:(1) Is not affiliated with the prime contractor or a first-tier subcontractor on the
L0:program or effort, or with any direct competitor of such prime contractor or any such
L0:first-tier subcontractor in furnishing end items or services of the type developed or
L0:produced on the program or effort; and
L1:(2) Receives access to technical data or computer software for performance of a
L0:Government contract that contains the clause at 252.227-7994, Limitations on the Use
L0:or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with Restrictive Legends.
L0:“Form, fit, and function data” means technical data that describe the required overall
L0:physical, functional, and performance characteristics (along with the qualification
L0:requirements, if applicable) of an item, component, or process to the extent necessary to
L0:permit identification of physically and functionally interchangeable items.
L0:“Technical data” means recorded information, regardless of the form or method of
L0:recording, of a scientific or technical nature (including computer software
L0:documentation). The term does not include computer software or financial,
L0:administrative, cost or pricing, or management information, or information incidental to
L0:contract administration.
L1:(b) Applicability. This clause governs the technical data related to any portion of a
L0:commercial product or commercial service that was developed exclusively at private
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:expense. If the commercial product or commercial service was developed in any part at
L0:Government expense—
L1:(1) The clause at Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS)
L0:252.227-7993, Rights in Other Than Commercial Technical Data and Computer
L0:Software—Small Business Innovation Research Program and Small Business
L0:Technology Transfer Program, governs technical data that are generated during any
L0:portion of performance that is covered under the Small Business Innovation Research
L1:(SBIR) Program or Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Program; and
L1:(2) The clause at DFARS 252.227-7989, Rights in Technical Data, Computer
L0:Software, and Computer Software Documentation—Other Than Commercial Products
L0:and Commercial Services, governs the technical data related to any portion of a
L0:commercial product or commercial service that was developed in any part at
L0:Government expense and is not covered under the SBIR or STTR program.
L1:(c) License. (1) The Government shall have the unrestricted right to use, modify,
L0:reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical data, and to permit others to
L0:do so, that—
L1:(i) Have been provided to the Government or others without restrictions on
L0:use, modification, reproduction, release, or further disclosure other than a release or
L0:disclosure resulting from the sale, transfer, or other assignment of interest in the
L0:technical data to another party or the sale or transfer of some or all of a business entity
L0:or its assets to another party;
L1:(ii) Are form, fit, and function data;
L1:(iii) Are a correction or change to technical data furnished to the Contractor
L0:by the Government;
L1:(iv) Are necessary for operation, maintenance, installation, or training
L0:(other than detailed manufacturing or process data); or
L1:(v) Have been provided to the Government under a prior contract or
L0:licensing agreement through which the Government has acquired the rights to use,
L0:modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose the data without restrictions.
L1:(2) Except as provided in paragraph (c)(1) of this clause, the Government may
L0:use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical data within the
L0:Government only. The Government will not—
L1:(i) Use the technical data to manufacture additional quantities of the
L0:commercial products; or
L1:(ii) Release, perform, display, disclose, or authorize use of the technical data
L0:outside the Government without the Contractor’s written permission unless a release,
L0:disclosure, or permitted use is necessary for emergency repair or overhaul of the
L0:commercial products furnished under this contract, or for performance of work by
L0:covered Government support contractors.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(3) The Contractor acknowledges that—
L1:(i) The Government is authorized to release or disclose technical data
L0:covered by paragraph (c)(2) of this clause to covered Government support contractors;
L1:(ii) The Government will notify the Contractor of such release or disclosure;
L1:(iii) The Contractor or the party asserting restrictions in a restrictive legend
L0:may—
L1:(A) Require each such covered Government support contractor to enter
L0:into a nondisclosure agreement directly with the Contractor or the party asserting
L0:restrictions regarding the use of the data; or
L0:and
L1:(B) Waive in writing the requirement for a nondisclosure agreement;
L1:(iv) Any such nondisclosure agreement shall address the restrictions on the
L0:covered Government support contractor’s use of the data as set forth in the clause at
L0:DFARS 252.227-7994, Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished
L0:Information Marked with Restrictive Legends. The nondisclosure agreement shall not
L0:include any additional terms and conditions unless mutually agreed to by the parties to
L0:the nondisclosure agreement.
L1:(d) Additional license rights. The Contractor, its subcontractors, and suppliers are
L0:not required to provide the Government additional rights to use, modify, reproduce,
L0:release, perform, display, or disclose technical data. However, if the Government
L0:desires to obtain additional rights in technical data, the Contractor agrees to promptly
L0:enter into negotiations with the Contracting Officer to determine whether there are
L0:acceptable terms for transferring such rights. The Contractor shall ensure that any
L0:resulting special license agreement, made part of the contract, lists or describes all
L0:technical data for which the Government has been granted additional rights and
L0:specifies those additional rights.
L1:(e) Release from liability. The Contractor agrees that the Government, and other
L0:persons to whom the Government may have released or disclosed technical data
L0:delivered or otherwise furnished under this contract, shall have no liability for any
L0:release or disclosure of technical data that are not marked to indicate that such data are
L0:licensed data subject to use, modification, reproduction, release, performance, display,
L0:or disclosure restrictions.
L1:(f) Subcontractors or suppliers. (1) The Contractor shall recognize and protect the
L0:rights afforded its subcontractors and suppliers under 10 U.S.C. 3771-3775, 10 U.S.C.
L0:3781-3786, and 15 U.S.C. 638(j)(1)(B)(iii) and (v).
L1:(2) Whenever any technical data related to commercial products or commercial
L0:services developed in any part at private expense will be obtained from a subcontractor
L0:or supplier for delivery to the Government under this contract, the Contractor shall use
L0:this clause in the subcontract or other contractual instrument, including subcontracts
L0:and other contractual instruments for commercial products or commercial services, and
L0:require its subcontractors or suppliers to do so, without alteration, except to identify the
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:parties. This clause will govern the technical data related to any portion of a
L0:commercial product or commercial service that was developed exclusively at private
L0:expense, and the Contractor shall use the following clauses to govern the technical data
L0:related to any portion of a commercial product or commercial service that was developed
L0:in any part at Government expense:
L1:(i) Use the clause at DFARS 252.227-7989, Rights in Technical Data,
L0:Computer Software, and Computer Software Documentation—Other Than Commercial
L0:Products and Commercial Services, to govern any technical data that are not generated
L0:during any portion of performance that is covered under the SBIR or STTR program.
L1:(ii) Use the clause at 252.227-7993, Rights in Other Than Commercial
L0:Technical Data and Computer Software—Small Business Innovation Research Program
L0:and Small Business Technology Transfer Program, to govern technical data that are
L0:generated during any portion of performance that is covered under the SBIR or STTR
L0:program.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Alternate I (DEVIATION 2026-O0036) (FEB 2026). As prescribed in 227.7102-4(a)(2),
L0:add the following definition of “Vessel design” in alphabetical order to paragraph (a) and
L0:add (c)(4) to the basic clause:
L1:(a) “Vessel design” means the design of a vessel, boat, or craft, and its components,
L0:including the hull, decks, superstructure, and the exterior surface shape of all external
L0:shipboard equipment and systems. The term includes designs covered by 10 U.S.C.
L0:8687, and designs protectable under 17 U.S.C. 1301, et seq.
L2:(c)(4) Vessel designs. For a vessel design (including a vessel design embodied in a
L0:useful article) that is developed or delivered under this contract, the Government shall
L0:have the right to make and have made any useful article that embodies the vessel
L0:design, to import the article, to sell the article, and to distribute the article for sale or to
L0:use the article in trade, to the same extent that the Government is granted rights in the
L0:technical data related to the vessel design.
citation: R-DFARS 252.227-7990 — Technical Data—Commercial Products and Commercial
