title: 252.227-7989 Rights in Technical Data, Computer Software, and Computer
content:
L0:252.227-7989 Rights in Technical Data, Computer Software, and Computer
L0:Software Documentation—Other Than Commercial Products and
L0:Commercial Services. (DEVIATION 2026-O0036)
L0:As prescribed in 227.7103-6(a) and (c), use the following clause:
L0:RIGHTS IN TECHNICAL DATA, COMPUTER SOFTWARE, AND COMPUTER
L0:SOFTWARE DOCUMENTATION—OTHER THAN COMMERCIAL PRODUCTS OR
L0:COMMERCIAL SERVICES (DEVIATION 2026-O0036) (FEB 2026)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Commercial computer software” means software developed or regularly used for
L0:nongovernmental purposes which—
L1:(1) Has been sold, leased, or licensed to the public;
L1:(2) Has been offered for sale, lease, or license to the public;
L1:(3) Has not been offered, sold, leased, or licensed to the public but will be
L0:available for commercial sale, lease, or license in time to satisfy the delivery
L0:requirements of this contract; or
L1:(4) Satisfies a criterion expressed in paragraph (1), (2), or (3) of this definition
L0:and would require only minor modification to meet the requirements of this contract.
L0:“Computer database” means a collection of data recorded in a form capable of being
L0:processed by a computer. The term does not include computer software.
L0:“Computer program” means a set of instructions, rules, or routines recorded in a form
L0:that is capable of causing a computer to perform a specific operation or series of
L0:operations.
L0:“Computer software” means computer programs, source code, source code listings,
L0:object code listings, design details, algorithms, processes, flow charts, formulae and
L0:related material that would enable the software to be reproduced, recreated, or
L0:recompiled. Computer software does not include computer databases or computer
L0:software documentation.
L0:“Computer software documentation” means owner’s manuals, user’s manuals,
L0:installation instructions, operating instructions, and other similar items, regardless of
L0:storage medium, that explain the capabilities of the computer software or provide
L0:instructions for using the software.
L0:“Covered Government support contractor” means a contractor (other than a litigation
L0:support contractor covered by 252.204-7014) under a contract, the primary purpose of
L0:which is to furnish independent and impartial advice or technical assistance directly to
L0:the Government in support of the Government’s management and oversight of a
L0:program or effort, rather than to directly furnish an end item or service to accomplish a
L0:program or effort, provided that the contractor—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(1) Is not affiliated with the prime contractor or a first-tier subcontractor on the
L0:program or effort, or with any direct competitor of such prime contractor or any such
L0:first-tier subcontractor in furnishing end items or services of the type developed or
L0:produced on the program or effort; and
L1:(2) Receives access to technical data or computer software for performance of a
L0:Government contract that contains the clause at 252.227-7994, Limitations on the Use
L0:or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with Restrictive Legends.
L0:“Detailed manufacturing or process data” means technical data that describe the steps,
L0:sequences, and conditions of manufacturing, processing or assembly used by the
L0:manufacturer to produce an item or component or to perform a process.
L0:“Developed” means—
L1:(1) (Applicable to technical data other than computer software documentation.)
L0:An item, component, or process exists and is workable. Thus, the item or component
L0:must have been constructed or the process practiced. Workability is generally
L0:established when the item, component, or process has been analyzed or tested
L0:sufficiently to demonstrate to reasonable people skilled in the applicable art that there
L0:is a high probability that it will operate as intended. Whether, how much, and what
L0:type of analysis or testing is required to establish workability depends on the nature of
L0:the item, component, or process, and the state of the art. To be considered “developed,”
L0:the item, component, or process need not be at the stage where it could be offered for
L0:sale or sold on the commercial market, nor must the item, component, or process be
L0:actually reduced to practice within the meaning of Title 35 of the United States Code;
L1:(2) A computer program has been successfully operated in a computer and
L0:tested to the extent sufficient to demonstrate to reasonable persons skilled in the art
L0:that the program can reasonably be expected to perform its intended purpose;
L1:(3) Computer software, other than computer programs, has been tested or
L0:analyzed to the extent sufficient to demonstrate to reasonable persons skilled in the art
L0:that the software can reasonably be expected to perform its intended purpose; or
L1:(4) Computer software documentation the contractor must deliver under a
L0:contract has been written, in any medium, in sufficient detail to comply with
L0:requirements under that contract.
L0:“Developed exclusively at private expense” means development was accomplished
L0:entirely with costs charged to indirect cost pools, costs not allocated to a Government
L0:contract, or any combination thereof.
L1:(1) Private expense determinations should be made at the lowest practicable
L0:level.
L1:(2) Under fixed-price contracts, when total costs are greater than the firm-fixed-
L0:price or ceiling price of the contract, the additional development costs necessary to
L0:complete development shall not be considered when determining whether development
L0:was at Government, private, or mixed expense.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:“Developed exclusively with Government funds” means development was not
L0:accomplished exclusively or partially at private expense.
L0:“Developed with mixed funding” means development was accomplished partially with
L0:costs charged to indirect cost pools and/or costs not allocated to a government contract,
L0:and partially with costs charged directly to a government contract.
L0:“Form, fit, and function data” means technical data that describe the required overall
L0:physical, functional, and performance characteristics (along with the qualification
L0:requirements, if applicable) of an item, component, or process to the extent necessary to
L0:permit identification of physically and functionally interchangeable items.
L0:“Generated” means, with regard to technical data or computer software, first created in
L0:the performance of this contract.
L0:“Government purpose” means any activity in which the United States Government is a
L0:party, including cooperative agreements with international or multi-national defense
L0:organizations, or sales or transfers by the United States Government to foreign
L0:governments or international organizations. Government purposes include competitive
L0:procurement, but do not include the rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform,
L0:display, or disclose technical data, computer software, or computer software
L0:documentation for commercial purposes or authorize others to do so.
L0:“Government purpose rights” means the rights to—
L1:(1) Use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical data,
L0:computer software, or computer software documentation within the Government
L0:without restriction; and
L1:(2) Release or disclose technical data, computer software, or computer software
L0:documentation outside the Government and authorize persons to whom release or
L0:disclosure has been made to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or
L0:disclose that data or software for United States Government purposes.
L0:“Limited rights” means the rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display,
L0:or disclose technical data, in whole or in part, within the Government. The Government
L0:may not, without the written permission of the party asserting limited rights, release or
L0:disclose the technical data outside the Government, use the technical data for
L0:manufacture, or authorize the technical data to be used by another party, except that
L0:the Government may reproduce, release, or disclose such data or authorize the use or
L0:reproduction of the data by persons outside the Government if—
L1:(1) The reproduction, release, disclosure, or use is—
L1:(i) Necessary for emergency repair and overhaul; or
L1:(ii) A release or disclosure to—
L0:covered Government support contract for use, modification, reproduction, performance,
L1:(A) A covered Government support contractor in performance of its
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:display, or release or disclosure to a person authorized to receive limited rights technical
L0:data; or
L1:(B) A foreign government, of technical data other than detailed
L0:manufacturing or process data, when use of such data by the foreign government is in
L0:the interest of the Government and is required for evaluational or informational
L0:purposes;
L1:(2) The recipient of the technical data is subject to a prohibition on the further
L0:reproduction, release, disclosure, or use of the technical data; and
L1:(3) The contractor or subcontractor asserting the restriction is notified of such
L0:reproduction, release, disclosure, or use.
L0:“Minor modification” means a modification that does not significantly alter the
L0:nongovernmental function or purpose of the software or is of the type customarily
L0:provided in the commercial marketplace.
L0:“Other than commercial computer software” means software that does not qualify as
L0:commercial computer software under the definition of “commercial computer software”
L0:of this clause.
L0:“Restricted rights” apply only to other than commercial computer software and mean
L0:the Government’s rights to—
L1:(1) Use a computer program with one computer at one time. The program may not
L0:be accessed by more than one terminal or central processing unit or time shared unless
L0:otherwise permitted by this contract;
L1:(2) Transfer a computer program to another Government agency without the
L0:further permission of the Contractor if the transferor destroys all copies of the program
L0:and related computer software documentation in its possession and notifies the licensor
L0:of the transfer. Transferred programs remain subject to the provisions of this clause;
L1:(3) Make a reasonable number of copies of the computer software required for the
L0:purposes of safekeeping (archive), backup, modification, or other activities authorized in
L0:paragraphs (1), (2), (4) and (5) of this definition;
L1:(4) Modify computer software provided that the Government may—
L1:(i) Use the modified software only as provided in paragraphs (1) and (3) of this
L0:definition; and
L1:(ii) Not release or disclose the modified software except as provided in
L0:paragraphs (2) and (5) of this clause;
L1:(5) Use, modify, reproduce, perform, display, or release or disclose the computer
L0:software, and permit contractors, subcontractors, or covered Government support
L0:contractors to do so, for purposes set forth in subparagraph (i) of this paragraph, subject
L0:to the conditions set forth in subparagraphs (ii) of this paragraph:
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L2:(i)(A) In performance of service contracts (see FAR 37.101), to diagnose and
L0:correct deficiencies, to modify the software to enable a computer program to be
L0:combined with, adapted to, or merged with other computer programs, or when
L0:necessary to respond to urgent tactical situations, provided that the Government
L0:notifies the party which has granted restricted rights that any such release or
L0:disclosure to particular contractors or subcontractors was made;
L1:(B) To perform emergency repairs or overhaul of items or components
L0:procured under this or a related contract, when necessary to perform such repairs or
L0:overhaul; or
L1:(C) For the management and oversight of a program or effort by a person
L0:authorized to receive restricted rights computer software, including in the performance
L0:of covered Government support contracts.
L2:(ii)(A) Any contractor, subcontractor, or covered Government support contractor
L0:receiving access to the software for the purposes of subparagraphs (i), (ii), or (iii) of this
L0:paragraph shall be subject to the use and nondisclosure agreement at 227.7103-7 or be
L0:performing a Government contract that contains the clause at 252.227-7994,
L0:Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked
L0:with Restrictive Legends;
L1:(B) The Government must not permit any recipient of the software under
L0:this paragraph to decompile, disassemble, or reverse engineer the software, or use
L0:software decompiled, disassembled, or reverse engineered by the Government pursuant
L0:to paragraph (4) of this definition, for any other purpose; and
L1:(C) Any use, modification, reproduction, performance, display, release, or
L0:disclosure of the computer software under this paragraph remains subject to the
L0:limitations in paragraphs (1) through (4) of this definition.
L0:“Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer
L0:(SBIR/STTR) data” means all technical data or computer software developed or
L0:generated in the performance of a phase I, II, or III SBIR/STTR contract or subcontract.
L0:“Technical data” means recorded information, regardless of the form or method of the
L0:recording, of a scientific or technical nature (including computer software
L0:documentation). The term does not include computer software or financial,
L0:administrative, cost or pricing, or management information, or information incidental to
L0:contract administration.
L0:“Unlimited rights” means rights to use, modify, reproduce, perform, display, release, or
L0:disclose technical data, computer software, or computer software documentation in

L0:Other Than Commercial Technical Data and Computer Software—Small Business
L0:Innovation Research Program and Small Business Technology Transfer Program, to
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:govern technical data, computer software, or computer software documentation that is
L0:SBIR/STTR data.
L1:(3) Technical data, computer software, or computer software documentation a
L0:subcontractor or supplier must deliver shall normally be delivered to the next higher-
L0:tier contractor, subcontractor, or supplier. However, when there is a requirement in the
L0:prime contract for data which may be submitted with other than unlimited rights by a
L0:subcontractor or supplier, then said subcontractor or supplier may fulfill its
L0:requirement by submitting such data or software directly to the Government, rather
L0:than through a higher-tier contractor, subcontractor, or supplier.
L1:(4) The Contractor and higher-tier subcontractors or suppliers shall not use the
L0:award of a contract as economic leverage to obtain rights in technical data, computer
L0:software, or computer software documentation from their subcontractors or suppliers.
L1:(5) In no event shall the Contractor use its obligation to recognize and protect
L0:subcontractor or supplier rights in technical data, computer software, or computer
L0:software documentation as an excuse for failing to satisfy its contractual obligations to
L0:the Government.

L0:Alternate I (DEVIATION 2026-O0036) (FEB 2026). As prescribed in 227.7103-6(b)(1)
L0:and (d), add the following paragraph (m) to the basic clause:

L0:computer software in which the Government has obtained unlimited rights or a license

L1:(2) The Government will not publish a deliverable technical data or computer
L0:software item or items identified in this contract as being subject to paragraph (m) of

L0:publishes that item or items for sale and promptly notifies the Contracting Officer of
L0:such publication(s). Any such publication shall include a notice identifying the number
L0:of this contract and the Government’s rights in the published data or software.
L1:(3) This limitation on the Government’s right to publish for sale shall continue
L0:as long as the data are reasonably available to the public for purchase.
L0:Alternate II (DEVIATION 2026-O0036) (FEB 2026). As prescribed in 227.7103-6(b)(2),
L0:add the following definition of “Vessel design” in alphabetical order to paragraph (a) and

L1:(a) “Vessel design” means the design of a vessel, boat, or craft, and its components,
L0:including the hull, decks, superstructure, and the exterior surface shape of all external
L0:shipboard equipment and systems. The term includes designs covered by 10 U.S.C.
L0:8687, and designs protectable under 17 U.S.C. 1301, et seq.

L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L2:(c)(7) Vessel designs. For a vessel design (including a vessel design embodied in a

title: 252.227-7993 clause:
content:
L0:252.227-7993 clause:
L1:(1) Redelivery of SBIR data.
L1:(i) SBIR data first generated under a prior SBIR clause and redelivered under the
L0:current SBIR clause. In this example, a contractor generates and delivers SBIR data under
L0:a 2016 phase II SBIR contract that includes a prior version of the clause at DFARS 252.227-
L0:7993. The contractor delivers identical data in a contiguous series of follow-on contracts,
L0:including a later phase III contract that is an extension of the research effort in the 2016
L0:contract. That phase III contract includes the current version of the clause at DFARS
L0:252.227-7993. The contractor asserts SBIR data rights in these data. The 2016 contract
L0:included the clause at DFARS 252.227-7993, which defined the SBIR data protection period
L0:as the period commencing with contract award and ending upon the date 5 years after
L0:completion of the project from which such data were generated. This previous definition of
L0:the SBIR data protection period applies to the redelivered SBIR data in the contiguous
L0:series of follow-on contracts, including the later phase III contract. The SBIR data protection
L0:period is extended because the later contract derives from, extends, or completes an effort
L0:made under a prior SBIR contract that included the prior version of the clause at DFARS
L0:252.227-7993. This is the case even under later contracts that include the current version of
L0:the clause at DFARS 252.227-7993 with a non-extendable 20-year SBIR/STTR data
L0:protection period. In addition, the SBIR data protection period from the prior version of the
L0:clause at DFARS 252.227-7993 may be extended indefinitely for subsequent redeliveries of
L0:identical SBIR data as long as the SBIR project has not been completed.
L1:(ii) SBIR data first delivered with the 20-year SBIR data protection period and later
L0:redelivered under the current SBIR clause. In another example, a contractor generates and
L0:delivers SBIR data under a 2021 phase II SBIR contract. The contractor delivers identical
L0:data under a later phase III contract that is an extension of the research effort in the 2021
L0:contract. The contractor asserts SBIR data rights in these data. That 2021 contract
L0:included a version of the DFARS 252.227-7993 clause that defines the SBIR data protection
L0:period as the period commencing on the date of contract award and ending 20 years after
L0:that date. The same definition of the SBIR/STTR data protection period applies to the
L0:redelivered SBIR data in the later phase III contract. Redelivery of identical SBIR data under
L0:any later contract will not extend the 20-year SBIR data protection period.
L1:(2) Modifications to previously delivered SBIR or STTR data. A contractor generates
L0:and delivers SBIR/STTR data under a phase II STTR contract with the current version of the
L0:clause at DFARS 252.227-7993. The contractor develops and delivers modified STTR data
L0:under a later phase III contract. The contractor asserts SBIR/STTR data rights in these
L0:data. The previously delivered portions of the STTR data will be governed by the previous
L0:SBIR/STTR data protection period, while the newly developed portions of the STTR data will
L0:be governed by a new 20-year SBIR/STTR data protection period.
L1:(3) SBIR or STTR data delivered under a contract and the contractor was not awarded a
L0:SBIR or STTR contract. A subcontractor was awarded a SBIR phase I contract. Later, the
L0:subcontractor performed SBIR phase III work under a contract awarded to a contractor who
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:was not awarded a SBIR or STTR contract. The subcontractor furnished technical data and
L0:computer software deliverables related to SBIR phase III work performed under this
L0:contract. This technical data and computer software was furnished to the Government with
L0:SBIR data rights. The clause at DFARS 252.227-7993 should have been included either in
L0:the initial contract or via a contract modification, and the Government’s rights in this SBIR
L0:data are subject to the terms of the clause at DFARS 252.227-7993.
L0:PGI 227.7106 Contracts for special works.
L1:(c) Examples of special works include, but are not limited, to audiovisual works, scripts,
L0:soundtracks, musical compositions, and adaptations; histories of departments, agencies,
L0:services or units thereof; surveys of Government establishments; instructional works or
L0:guidance to Government officers and employees on the discharge of their official duties;
L0:reports, books, studies, surveys or similar documents; collections of data containing
L0:information pertaining to individuals that, if disclosed, would violate the right of privacy or
L0:publicity of the individuals to whom the information relates; or investigative reports.

title: 252.227-7994 Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished
content:
L0:252.227-7994 Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished
L0:Information Marked with Restrictive Legends. (DEVIATION 2026-O0036)
L0:As prescribed in 227.7103-6(e) or 227.7104-4(b)(4), use the following clause:
L0:LIMITATIONS ON THE USE OR DISCLOSURE OF GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED
L0:INFORMATION MARKED WITH RESTRICTIVE LEGENDS
L0:(DEVIATION 2026-O0036) (FEB 2026)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) For contracts in which the Government will furnish the Contractor with
L0:technical data, the terms “covered Government support contractor,” “limited rights,”
L0:“restricted rights”, and “Government purpose rights” are defined in the clause at
L0:252.227-7989, Rights in Technical Data, Computer Software, and Computer Software
L0:Documentation—Other Than Commercial Products and Commercial Services.
L1:(2) For Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Program and Small
L0:Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Program contracts, the terms “covered
L0:Government support contractor,” “government purpose rights,” “limited rights,”
L0:“restricted rights,” and “SBIR/STTR data rights” are defined in the clause at 252.227-
L0:7993, Rights in Other Than Commercial Technical Data and Computer Software—
L0:Small Business Innovation Research Program and Small Business Technology Transfer
L0:Program.
L1:(b) Technical data or computer software provided to the Contractor as Government-
L0:furnished information (GFI) under this contract may be subject to restrictions on use,
L0:modification, reproduction, release, performance, display, or further disclosure.
L1:(1) GFI marked with limited rights, restricted rights, or SBIR/STTR data
L0:rights legends. (i) The Contractor shall use, modify, reproduce, perform, or display
L0:technical data received from the Government with limited rights legends, computer
L0:software received with restricted rights legends, or SBIR/STTR technical data or
L0:computer software received with SBIR/STTR data rights legends (during the
L0:SBIR/STTR data protection period) only in the performance of this contract. The
L0:Contractor shall not, without the express written permission of the party whose name
L0:appears in the legend, release or disclose such data or software to any unauthorized
L0:person.
L1:(ii) If the Contractor is a covered Government support contractor, the
L0:Contractor is also subject to the additional terms and conditions at paragraph (b)(5) of
L0:this clause.
L1:(2) GFI marked with government purpose rights legends. The Contractor shall
L0:use technical data or computer software received from the Government with
L0:government purpose rights legends for government purposes only. The Contractor shall
L0:not, without the express written permission of the party whose name appears in the
L0:restrictive legend, use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, or display such data or
L0:software for any commercial purpose or disclose such data or software to a person other
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:than its subcontractors, suppliers, or prospective subcontractors or suppliers, who
L0:require the data or software to submit offers for, or perform, contracts under this
L0:contract. Prior to disclosing the data or software, the Contractor shall require the
L0:persons to whom disclosure will be made to complete and sign the nondisclosure
L0:agreement at 227.7103-7 of the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement
L1:(DFARS).
L1:(3) GFI marked with specially negotiated license rights legends. (i) The
L0:Contractor shall use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, or display technical data or
L0:computer software received from the Government with specially negotiated license
L0:legends only as permitted in the license. Such data or software may not be released or
L0:disclosed to other persons unless permitted by the license and, prior to release or
L0:disclosure, the intended recipient has completed the nondisclosure agreement at
L0:DFARS 227.7103-7. The Contractor shall modify paragraph (1)(c) of the nondisclosure
L0:agreement to reflect the recipient’s obligations regarding use, modification,
L0:reproduction, release, performance, display, and disclosure of the data or software.
L1:(ii) If the Contractor is a covered Government support contractor, the
L0:Contractor may also be subject to some or all of the additional terms and conditions at
L0:paragraph (b)(5) of this clause, to the extent such terms and conditions are required by
L0:the specially negotiated license.
L1:(4) GFI technical data marked with commercial restrictive legends. (i) The
L0:Contractor shall use, modify, reproduce, perform, or display technical data that are or
L0:are related to a commercial product or commercial service and are received from the
L0:Government with a commercial restrictive legend (i.e., marked to indicate that such
L0:data are subject to use, modification, reproduction, release, performance, display, or
L0:disclosure restrictions) only in the performance of this contract. The Contractor shall
L0:not, without the express written permission of the party whose name appears in the
L0:legend, use the technical data to manufacture additional quantities of the commercial
L0:products or commercial services, or release or disclose such data to any unauthorized
L0:person.
L1:(ii) If the Contractor is a covered Government support contractor, the
L0:Contractor is also subject to the additional terms and conditions at paragraph (b)(5) of
L0:this clause.
L1:(5) Covered Government support contractors. If the Contractor is a covered
L0:Government support contractor receiving technical data or computer software marked
L0:with restrictive legends pursuant to paragraphs (b)(1)(ii), (b)(3)(ii), or (b)(4)(ii) of this
L0:clause, the Contractor further agrees and acknowledges that—
L1:(i) The technical data or computer software will be accessed and used for the
L0:sole purpose of furnishing independent and impartial advice or technical assistance
L0:directly to the Government in support of the Government’s management and oversight
L0:of the program or effort to which such technical data or computer software relates, as
L0:stated in this contract, and shall not be used to compete for any Government or non-
L0:Government contract;
L1:(ii) The Contractor shall take all reasonable steps to protect the technical
L0:data or computer software against any unauthorized release or disclosure;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(iii) The Contractor shall ensure that the party whose name appears in the
L0:legend is notified of the access or use within 30 days of the Contractor’s access or use of
L0:such data or software;
L1:(iv) The Contractor shall enter into a nondisclosure agreement with the
L0:party whose name appears in the legend, if required to do so by that party, and that any
L0:such nondisclosure agreement will implement the restrictions on the Contractor’s use of
L0:such data or software as set forth in this clause. The nondisclosure agreement shall not
L0:include any additional terms and conditions unless mutually agreed to by the parties to
L0:the nondisclosure agreement; and
L1:(v) That a breach of these obligations or restrictions may subject the
L0:Contractor to—
L1:(A) Criminal, civil, administrative, and contractual actions in law and
L0:equity for penalties, damages, and other appropriate remedies by the United States;
L0:and
L0:party whose name appears in the legend.
L1:(B) Civil actions for damages and other appropriate remedies by the
L1:(c) Indemnification and creation of third party beneficiary rights. The Contractor
L0:agrees—
L1:(1) To indemnify and hold harmless the Government, its agents, and employees
L0:from every claim or liability, including attorneys fees, court costs, and expenses, arising
L0:out of, or in any way related to, the misuse or unauthorized modification, reproduction,
L0:release, performance, display, or disclosure of technical data or computer software
L0:received from the Government with restrictive legends by the Contractor or any person
L0:to whom the Contractor has released or disclosed such data or software; and
L1:(2) That the party whose name appears on the restrictive legend, in addition to
L0:any other rights it may have, is a third-party beneficiary who has the right of direct
L0:action against the Contractor, or any person to whom the Contractor has released or
L0:disclosed such data or software, for the unauthorized duplication, release, or disclosure
L0:of technical data or computer software subject to restrictive legends.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall ensure that its employees are subject to use and
L0:nondisclosure obligations consistent with this clause prior to the employees being
L0:provided access to or use of any GFI covered by this clause.

title: 252.227-7997 Validation of Asserted Restrictions. (DEVIATION 2026-O0036)
content:
L0:252.227-7997 Validation of Asserted Restrictions. (DEVIATION 2026-O0036)
L0:As prescribed in 227.7103-6(g), 227.7104-4(b)(6), or 227.7203-6(c), use the following
L0:clause:
L0:VALIDATION OF ASSERTED RESTRICTIONS (DEVIATION 2026-O0036)
L0:(FEB 2026)
L1:(a) Definitions. The terms used in this clause are defined in the 252.227-7989,
L0:Rights in Technical Data, Computer Software, and Computer Software
L0:Documentation—Other Than Commercial Products and Commercial Services, clause of
L0:this contract.
L1:(b) Technical data related to commercial products or commercial services—
L0:presumption regarding development exclusively at private expense. For technical data
L0:related to commercial products or commercial services, the Contracting Officer will
L0:presume that the Contractor’s or a subcontractor’s asserted use or release restrictions
L0:with respect to a commercial product or commercial service are justified on the basis
L0:that the item was developed exclusively at private expense. The Contracting Officer
L0:will not issue a challenge unless there are reasonable grounds to question the validity of
L0:the assertion that the commercial item was developed exclusively at private expense.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(c) Justification. The Contractor or subcontractor at any tier is responsible for
L0:maintaining records sufficient to justify the validity of its asserted restrictions on the
L0:rights of the Government and others to use, duplicate, release, or disclose technical data
L0:or computer software delivered, required to be delivered, or otherwise provided to the
L0:Government under the contract or subcontract. Except as provided in paragraph (b) of
L0:this clause, the Contractor or subcontractor shall be prepared to furnish to the
L0:Contracting Officer a written justification for such asserted restrictions in response to a
L0:challenge under paragraph (e) of this clause.
L1:(d) Prechallenge request for information related to asserted restrictions on technical
L0:data. (1) The Contracting Officer may request the Contractor or subcontractor to
L0:furnish a written explanation for any asserted restriction on the right of the United
L0:States or others to use, disclose, or release technical data. If, upon review of the
L0:explanation submitted, the Contracting Officer cannot determine the basis of the
L0:asserted restriction, the Contracting Officer may further request the Contractor or
L0:subcontractor to furnish additional information in the records of, or otherwise in the
L0:possession of or reasonably available to, the Contractor or subcontractor to justify the
L0:validity of any asserted restriction on technical data delivered, to be delivered, or
L0:otherwise provided to the Government under the contract or subcontract (e.g., a
L0:statement of facts accompanied with supporting documentation). The Contractor or
L0:subcontractor shall submit such written data as requested by the Contracting Officer
L0:within the time required or such longer period as may be mutually agreed.
L1:(2) If the Contracting Officer, after reviewing the written data furnished
L0:pursuant to paragraph (d)(1) of this clause, or any other available information related to
L0:the validity of an asserted restriction, determines that reasonable grounds exist to
L0:question the current validity of the asserted restriction and that continued adherence to
L0:the asserted restriction would make impracticable the subsequent competitive
L0:acquisition of the item or process to which the technical data relates, the Contracting
L0:Officer will follow the procedures in paragraph (f) of this clause.
L1:(3) If the Contractor or subcontractor fails to respond to the Contracting
L0:Officer’s request for information under paragraph (d)(1) of this clause, and the
L0:Contracting Officer determines that continued adherence to the asserted restriction
L0:would make impracticable the subsequent competitive acquisition of the item or process
L0:to which the technical data relates, the Contracting Officer may challenge the validity of
L0:the asserted restriction as described in paragraph (f) of this clause.
L1:(e) Prechallenge request for information related to assertion restrictions on computer
L0:software. (1) The Contracting Officer may request the Contractor to provide sufficient
L0:information to enable the Contracting Officer to evaluate the Contractor’s asserted
L0:restrictions. Such information shall be based upon the records required by this clause
L0:or other information reasonably available to the Contractor.
L1:(2) Based upon the information provided, if the—
L1:(i) Contractor agrees that an asserted restriction is not valid, the
L0:Contracting Officer may—
L0:expense; or
L1:(A) Strike or correct the unjustified marking at the Contractor’s
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(B) Return the computer software to the Contractor for correction at the
L0:Contractor’s expense. If the Contractor fails to correct or strike the unjustified marking
L0:and return the corrected software to the Contracting Officer within 60 days following
L0:receipt of the software, the Contracting Officer may correct or strike the marking at the
L0:Contractor’s expense;
L1:(ii) Contracting Officer concludes that the asserted restriction is appropriate
L0:for this contract, the Contracting Officer shall so notify the Contractor in writing.
L1:(3) The Contractor’s failure to provide a timely response to a Contracting
L0:Officer’s request for information or failure to provide sufficient information to enable the
L0:Contracting Officer to evaluate an asserted restriction shall constitute reasonable
L0:grounds for questioning the validity of an asserted restriction.
L1:(f) Challenge. (1) Notwithstanding any provision of this contract concerning
L0:inspection and acceptance, if the Contracting Officer determines that a challenge to the
L0:asserted restriction is warranted, the Contracting Officer will send a written challenge
L0:notice to the Contractor or subcontractor making the asserted restriction. The
L0:challenge notice and all related correspondence shall be subject to handling procedures
L0:for classified information and controlled unclassified information. Such challenge will—
L1:(i) State the specific grounds for challenging the asserted restriction
L0:including, for technical data related to commercial products or commercial services,
L0:sufficient information to reasonably demonstrate that the commercial product or
L0:commercial service was not developed exclusively at private expense;
L1:(ii) Require a response within 60 days justifying the assertion based upon
L0:records kept in accordance with paragraph (c) of this clause and providing sufficient
L0:evidence as to the current validity of the asserted restriction;
L1:(iii) State that a Contracting Officer’s final decision, issued pursuant to
L0:paragraph (h) of this clause, or action of a court of competent jurisdiction or Board of
L0:Contract Appeals that sustained the validity of an identical assertion made by the
L0:Contractor (or a licensee) sustaining the validity of a prior asserted restriction identical
L0:to the current asserted restriction, within the 3-year period preceding the current
L0:challenge, shall serve as justification for the current asserted restriction if the prior
L0:validated restriction was asserted by the same Contractor or subcontractor (or any
L0:licensee of such Contractor or subcontractor) to which such notice is being provided; and
L1:(iv) State that failure to respond to the challenge notice may result in
L0:issuance of a final decision pursuant to paragraph (g) of this clause.
L1:(2) The Contracting Officer will extend the time for response as appropriate if
L0:the Contractor or subcontractor submits a written request showing the need for
L0:additional time to prepare a response.
L1:(3) The Contractor’s or subcontractor’s written response shall be considered a
L0:claim within the meaning of the 41 U.S.C. 7101, Contract Disputes, and shall be
L0:certified in the form prescribed at 33.207 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation,
L0:regardless of dollar amount.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(4) A Contractor or subcontractor receiving challenges to the same asserted
L0:restrictions from more than one Contracting Officer shall notify each Contracting
L0:Officer of the existence of more than one challenge. The notice shall also state which
L0:Contracting Officer initiated the first in time unanswered challenge. The Contracting
L0:Officer initiating the first in time unanswered challenge after consultation with the
L0:Contractor or subcontractor and the other Contracting Officers, will formulate and
L0:distribute a schedule for responding to each of the challenge notices to all interested
L0:parties. The schedule will afford the Contractor or subcontractor a reasonable
L0:opportunity to respond to each challenge notice. All parties will be bound by this
L0:schedule.
L1:(5) The Contracting Officer may request additional supporting documentation
L0:if, in the Contracting Officer’s opinion, the Contractor’s explanation does not provide
L0:sufficient evidence to justify the validity of the asserted restrictions. The Contractor
L0:agrees to promptly respond to the Contracting Officer’s request for additional
L0:supporting documentation.
L1:(6) Notwithstanding challenge by the Contracting Officer, the parties may
L0:agree on the disposition of an asserted restriction at any time prior to a Contracting
L0:Officer’s final decision or, if the Contractor has appealed that decision, filed suit, or
L0:provided notice of an intent to file suit, at any time prior to a decision by a court of
L0:competent jurisdiction or Board of Contract Appeals.
L1:(g) Final decision when Contractor or subcontractor fails to respond. Upon a failure
L0:of a Contractor or subcontractor to submit any response to the challenge notice or a
L0:request for additional information (under paragraphs (f)(1) and (f)(5) of this clause), the
L0:Contracting Officer will issue a final decision to the Contractor or subcontractor in
L0:accordance with the Disputes clause of this contract. In order to sustain the challenge
L0:for commercial products or commercial services, the Contracting Officer will provide
L0:information demonstrating that the commercial product or commercial service was not
L0:developed exclusively at private expense. This final decision will be issued as soon as
L0:possible after the expiration of the time period of paragraph (f)(1)(ii) or (f)(2) of this
L0:clause. Following issuance of the final decision, the Contracting Officer will comply
L0:with the procedures in paragraphs (h)(2)(ii) through (iv) of this clause.
L1:(h) Final decision when Contractor or subcontractor responds. (1) If the
L0:Contracting Officer determines that the Contractor or subcontractor has justified the
L0:validity of the asserted restriction, the Contracting Officer will issue a final decision to
L0:the Contractor or subcontractor that sustains the validity of the asserted restriction and
L0:that states that the Government will continue to be bound by the asserted restriction.
L0:The Contracting Officer will issue this final decision within 60 days after receipt of the
L0:Contractor’s or subcontractor’s response to the challenge notice, or within such longer
L0:period that the Contracting Officer has notified the Contractor or subcontractor that the
L0:Government will require. The Contracting Officer will provide notification of any longer
L0:period for issuance of a final decision within 60 days after receipt of the response to the
L0:challenge notice.
L2:(2)(i) If the Contracting Officer determines that the validity of the asserted
L0:restriction is not justified, the Contracting Officer will issue a final decision to the
L0:Contractor or subcontractor in accordance with the Disputes clause of this contract. To
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:sustain the challenge for technical data related to commercial products or commercial
L0:services, the Contracting Officer will provide information demonstrating that the
L0:commercial product or commercial service was not developed exclusively at private
L0:expense. Notwithstanding paragraph (e) of the Disputes clause, the final decision will
L0:be issued within 60 days after receipt of the Contractor’s or subcontractor’s response to
L0:the challenge notice, or within such longer period that the Contracting Officer has
L0:notified the Contractor or subcontractor that the Government will require. The
L0:notification of a longer period for issuance of a final decision will be made within 60
L0:days after receipt of the response to the challenge notice.
L1:(ii) The Government agrees that it will continue to be bound by the asserted
L0:restriction for a period of 90 days from the issuance of the Contracting Officer’s final
L0:decision under paragraph (h)(2)(i) of this clause. The Contractor or subcontractor
L0:agrees that, if it intends to file suit in the United States Court of Federal Claims, it will
L0:provide a notice of intent to file suit to the Contracting Officer within 90 days from the
L0:issuance of the Contracting Officer’s final decision under paragraph (h)(2)(i) of this
L0:clause. If the Contractor or subcontractor fails to appeal to an agency Board of Contract
L0:Appeals, file suit in an appropriate court, or provide a notice of intent to file suit in an
L0:appropriate court to the Contracting Officer within the 90-day period, the Government
L0:may cancel or ignore the restrictive markings that are based on the asserted
L0:restrictions, and the failure of the Contractor or subcontractor to take the required
L0:action constitutes agreement with such Government action.
L1:(iii) The Government agrees that it will continue to be bound by the
L0:asserted restriction where a notice of intent to file suit in the United States Court of
L0:Federal Claims is provided to the Contracting Officer within 90 days from the issuance
L0:of the final decision under paragraph (h)(2)(i) of this clause. The Government will no
L0:longer be bound, and the Contractor or subcontractor agrees that the Government may
L0:strike or ignore the restrictive marking that is based on the asserted restriction, if the
L0:Contractor or subcontractor fails to file its suit within 1 year after issuance of the final
L0:decision. Notwithstanding the foregoing, where the head of an agency determines, on a
L0:nondelegable basis, that urgent or compelling circumstances will not permit waiting for
L0:the filing of a suit in the United States Court of Federal Claims, the Contractor or
L0:subcontractor agrees that the agency may, following notice to the Contractor or
L0:subcontractor, authorize release or disclosure of the technical data or computer
L0:software. The Government agrees not to release or disclose such technical data or
L0:computer software unless, prior to release or disclosure, the intended recipient is subject
L0:to the use and nondisclosure agreement at Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation
L0:Supplement (DFARS) 227.7103-7, or is a Government contractor receiving access to the
L0:technical data or computer software for performance of a Government contract that
L0:contains the clause at DFARS 252.227-7994, Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of
L0:Government-Furnished Information Marked with Restrictive Legends. Such agency
L0:determination may be made at any time after issuance of the final decision and will not
L0:affect the Contractor’s or subcontractor’s right to damages against the United States
L0:where its asserted restrictions are ultimately upheld or to pursue other relief, if any, as
L0:may be provided by law.
L1:(iv) The Government agrees that it will be bound by the asserted
L0:restrictions where an appeal or suit is filed pursuant to the Contract Disputes statute
L0:until final disposition by an agency Board of Contract Appeals or the United States
L0:Court of Federal Claims. Notwithstanding the foregoing, where the head of an agency
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L0:determines, on a nondelegable basis, following notice to the Contractor that urgent or
L0:compelling circumstances will not permit awaiting the decision by such Board of
L0:Contract Appeals or the United States Court of Federal Claims, the Contractor or
L0:subcontractor agrees that the agency may authorize release or disclosure of the
L0:technical data or computer software. The Government agrees not to release or disclose
L0:such technical data or computer software unless, prior to release or disclosure, the
L0:intended recipient is subject to the use and nondisclosure agreement at Defense Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 227.7103-7, or is a Government contractor
L0:receiving access to the technical data or computer software for performance of a
L0:Government contract that contains the clause at DFARS 252.227-7994, Limitations on
L0:the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with Restrictive
L0:Legends. Such agency determination may be made at any time after issuance of the
L0:final decision and will not affect the Contractor’s or subcontractor’s right to damages
L0:against the United States where its asserted restrictions are ultimately upheld or to
L0:pursue other relief, if any, as may be provided by law.
L1:(i) Final disposition of appeal or suit. (1) If the Contractor or subcontractor appeals
L0:or files suit and if, upon final disposition of the appeal or suit, the Contracting Officer’s
L0:decision is sustained—
L1:(i) The restrictive marking that is based on the asserted restriction on the
L0:technical data or computer software shall be cancelled, corrected or ignored; and
L1:(ii) If the asserted restriction is found not to be substantially justified, the
L0:Contractor or subcontractor, as appropriate, shall be liable to the Government for
L0:payment of the cost to the Government of reviewing the asserted restriction and the fees
L0:and other expenses (as defined in 28 U.S.C. 2412(d)(2)(A)) incurred by the Government
L0:in challenging the asserted restriction, unless special circumstances would make such
L0:payment unjust.
L1:(2) If the Contractor or subcontractor appeals or files suit and if, upon final
L0:disposition of the appeal or suit, the Contracting Officer’s decision is not sustained—
L1:(i) The Government will continue to be bound by the restrictive marking;
L0:and
L1:(ii) The Government will be liable to the Contractor or subcontractor for
L0:payment of fees and other expenses (as defined in 28 U.S.C. 2412(d)(2)(A)) incurred by
L0:the Contractor or subcontractor in defending the marking, if the challenge by the
L0:Government is found not to have been made in good faith.
L1:(j) Duration of right to challenge. (1) The Government may review the validity of
L0:any restriction on technical data or computer software, delivered or that the Contractor
L0:must deliver under a contract, asserted by the Contractor or subcontractor. During the
L0:period within 6 years of final payment on a contract or within 6 years of delivery of the
L0:technical data or computer software to the Government, whichever is later, the
L0:Contracting Officer may review and make a written determination to challenge the
L0:restriction. The Government may, however, challenge a restriction on the release,
L0:disclosure, or use of technical data or computer software at any time if such technical
L0:data or computer software—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(i) Are publicly available;
L1:(ii) Have been furnished to the United States without restriction;
L1:(iii) Have been otherwise made available without restriction; or
L1:(iv) Are the subject of a fraudulently asserted use or release restriction.
L1:(2) Only the Contracting Officer’s final decision resolving a formal challenge by
L0:sustaining the validity of a restrictive marking or actions of an agency Board of
L0:Contract Appeals or a court of competent jurisdiction that sustain the validity of an
L0:asserted restriction constitute “validation” as addressed in 10 U.S.C. 3785(c).
L1:(k) Decision not to challenge. A decision by the Government, or a determination by
L0:the Contracting Officer, to not challenge the restrictive marking or asserted restriction
L0:shall not constitute “validation.”
L1:(l) Privity of contract. The Contractor or subcontractor agrees that the Contracting
L0:Officer may transact matters under this clause directly with subcontractors at any tier
L0:that assert restrictions. However, this clause neither creates nor implies privity of
L0:contract between the Government and subcontractor.
L1:(m) Flowdown. The Contractor or subcontractor agrees to insert this clause in
L0:contractual instruments, including subcontracts and other contractual instruments for
L0:commercial products or commercial services, with its subcontractors or suppliers at any
L0:tier requiring the delivery of technical data or computer software. The clause may not
L0:be altered other than to identify the appropriate parties.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.227-7038 Patent Rights—Ownership by the Contractor (Large Business)
content:
L0:252.227-7038 Patent Rights—Ownership by the Contractor (Large Business).
L0:As prescribed in 227.303(2), use the following clause:
L0:PATENT RIGHTS—OWNERSHIP BY THE CONTRACTOR (LARGE BUSINESS)
L0:(JUN 2012)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Invention” means—
L1:(1) Any invention or discovery that is or may be patentable or otherwise
L0:protectable under Title 35 of the United States Code; or
L1:(2) Any variety of plant that is or may be protectable under the Plant Variety
L0:Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 2321, et seq.).
L0:“Made”—
L1:(1) When used in relation to any invention other than a plant variety, means
L0:the conception or first actual reduction to practice of the invention; or
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 27
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 227
L1:(2) When used in relation to a plant variety, means that the Contractor has at
L0:least tentatively determined that the variety has been reproduced with recognized
L0:characteristics.
L0:“Nonprofit organization” means—
L1:(1) A university or other institution of higher education;
L1:(2) An organization of the type described in the Internal Revenue Code at 26
L0:U.S.C. 501(c)(3) and exempt from taxation under 26 U.S.C. 501(a); or
L1:(3) Any nonprofit scientific or educational organization qualified under a State
L0:nonprofit organization statute.
L0:“Practical application” means—
L2:(1)(i) To manufacture, in the case of a composition or product;
L1:(ii) To practice, in the case of a process or method; or
L1:(iii) To operate, in the case of a machine or system; and
L1:(2) In each case, under such conditions as to establish that—
L1:(i) The invention is being utilized; and
L1:(ii) The benefits of the invention are, to the extent permitted by law or
L0:Government regulations, available to the public on reasonable terms.
L0:“Subject invention” means any invention of the Contractor made in the performance of
L0:work under this contract.
L1:(b) Contractor’s rights—(1) Ownership. The Contractor may elect to retain
L0:ownership of each subject invention throughout the world in accordance with the
L0:provisions of this clause.
L1:(2) License. (i) The Contractor shall retain a nonexclusive royalty-free license
L0:throughout the world in each subject invention to which the Government obtains title,
L0:unless the Contractor fails to disclose the invention within the times specified in
L0:paragraph (c) of this clause. The Contractor’s license-
L0:corporate structure of which the Contractor is a part;

title: 228.102-1 General
content:
L0:228.102-1 General.
L0:The requirement for performance and payment bonds is waived for cost-reimbursement
L0:contracts. However, for cost-type contracts with fixed-price construction subcontracts
L0:over $40,000, require the prime contractor to obtain from each of its construction
L0:subcontractors performance and payment protections in favor of the prime contractor as
L0:follows:
L1:(1) For fixed-price construction subcontracts over $40,000, but not exceeding
L0:$150,000, payment protection sufficient to pay labor and material costs, using any of the
L0:alternatives listed at FAR 28.102-1(b)(1).
L1:(2) For fixed-price construction subcontracts over $150,000—
L1:(i) A payment bond sufficient to pay labor and material costs; and
L1:(ii) A performance bond in an equal amount if available at no additional cost.

title: 228.370-1 Definitions
content:
L0:228.370-1 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L0:“Aircraft” means, unless otherwise provided in the contract Schedule, any item,
L0:other than a rocket or missile, intended for flight (e.g., fixed-winged aircraft, blended
L0:wing/lifting bodies, helicopters, vertical take-off or landing aircraft, lighter-than-air
L0:airships, and unmanned aerial vehicles), including emerging technologies that would
L0:commonly be considered aircraft. New production articles become aircraft at a stage of
L0:manufacture or production when a wing, portion of a wing, or engine is attached to a
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L0:fuselage. Blended wing/lifting bodies become aircraft at a stage of manufacture or
L0:production when the center portion and a lifting surface become attached.
L0:“Civil aircraft” means an aircraft other than a public aircraft or state aircraft.
L0:“Contractor managerial personnel” means the contractor’s directors, officers,
L0:managers, superintendents, or equivalent representatives who have supervision or
L0:direction of—
L1:(1) All, or substantially all, of the contractor’s business;
L1:(2) All, or substantially all, of the contractor’s operation at any one plant or
L0:separate location; or
L1:(3) A separate and complete major industrial operation.
L0:“Covered aircraft” means an aircraft owned by or to be delivered to the Government
L0:and, when determined by the contracting officer and specifically identified as such in
L0:the contract Schedule, may include contractor-furnished aircraft that are not intended
L0:for induction into the DoD inventory, including—
L1:(1) Aircraft furnished by the Government to the contractor under a contract
L0:while in the contractor’s possession, care, custody, or control regardless of their location
L0:or state of disassembly or reassembly;
L1:(2) Items removed from a Government-furnished aircraft that are—
L1:(i) Intended for reinstallation on that particular aircraft, which retain their
L0:status as covered aircraft while awaiting installation; and
L1:(ii) Not intended for reinstallation on that particular aircraft, which lose
L0:their status as covered aircraft once removal is complete;
L1:(3) New production aircraft when wholly outside of buildings on the contractor’s
L0:premises or other places described in the contract Schedule (e.g., hush houses, run
L0:stations, and paint facilities); and
L1:(4) Commercial aircraft, to include commercially available off-the-shelf aircraft,
L0:become covered aircraft when the commercial aircraft arrives at the contractor’s place of
L0:performance for modification under the terms of the contract.
L0:“Crewmember” means, unless otherwise provided in the contract Schedule,
L0:personnel required in the flight manual, assigned for the purpose of conducting any
L0:flight on behalf of the contractor. It also includes any operator of an unmanned aerial
L0:vehicle.
L0:“Flight” means any flight approved in writing by the Government flight
L0:representative, to include taxi test made in the performance of the contract, or flight for
L0:the purpose of safeguarding the aircraft. All aircraft off the contractor's premises shall
L0:be considered to be in flight when on the ground or water for reasonable periods of time
L0:following emergency landings, landings made in performance of the contract, or
L0:landings approved in writing by the contracting officer.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L0:“Public aircraft” means an aircraft that meets the definition in 49 U.S.C.
L0:40102(a)(41) and the qualifications in 49 U.S.C. 40125. Specifically, a public aircraft
L0:means any of the following:
L1:(1) An aircraft used only for the Government, except as provided in paragraphs
L1:(5) and (7) of this definition.
L1:(2) An aircraft owned by the Government and operated by any person for
L0:purposes related to crew training, equipment development, or demonstration, except as
L0:provided in paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(3) An aircraft owned and operated by the government of a State, the District of
L0:Columbia, or a territory or possession of the United States or a political subdivision of
L0:one of these governments, except as provided in paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(4) An aircraft exclusively leased for at least 90 continuous days by the
L0:government of a State, the District of Columbia, or a territory or possession of the
L0:United States or a political subdivision of one of these governments, except as provided
L0:in paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(5) An aircraft owned or operated by the armed forces or chartered to provide
L0:transportation or other commercial air service to the armed forces under the conditions
L0:specified by 49 U.S.C. 40125(c). In the preceding sentence, the term “other commercial
L0:air service” means an aircraft operation that—
L1:(i) Is within the United States territorial airspace;
L1:(ii) The Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration determines is
L0:available for compensation or hire to the public; and
L1:(iii) Must comply with all applicable civil aircraft rules under title 14, Code
L0:of Federal Regulations.
L1:(6) An unmanned aircraft that is owned and operated by, or exclusively leased
L0:for at least 90 continuous days by, an Indian Tribal government, as defined in section
L0:102 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C.
L0:5122), except as provided in paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(7) As described in 49 U.S.C. 40125(b), an aircraft described in paragraph (1),
L1:(2), (3), or (4) of this definition does not qualify as a public aircraft in situations where
L0:the aircraft is used for commercial purposes or to carry an individual other than a
L0:crewmember or a qualified non-crewmember.
L0:“Public aircraft operation” means operation of an aircraft that meets the legal
L0:definition of public aircraft established in 49 U.S.C. 40102(a)(41) and the legal
L0:qualifications for public aircraft status outlined in 49 U.S.C. 40125.
L0:“State aircraft” means an aircraft operated by the Government for sovereign,
L0:noncommercial purposes such as military, customs, and police services. Military
L0:aircraft are afforded status as state aircraft. In very rare circumstances, DoD-
L0:contracted aircraft may be designated, in writing, by a responsible Government official
L0:pursuant to DoD Directive 4500.54E, DoD Foreign Clearance Program, to be operated
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L0:in state aircraft status, and States may choose to treat them as deemed state aircraft
L0:when they are operating under a Government contract.
L0:“Workmanship error” means damage to the aircraft that is the result of an
L0:incorrectly performed skill-based task, operation, or action that was originally planned
L0:or intended.

title: 228.370-2 General
content:
L0:228.370-2 General.
L1:(a) Assignment of a Government flight representative. See PGI 228.370-2(a) for
L0:procedures on assigning a Government flight representative (GFR) when using the
L0:clauses at 252.228-7001 and 252.228-7007.
L1:(b) Preaward survey. Before awarding any contract that includes the clause at
L0:252.228-7001, Ground and Flight Risk, the contracting officer should obtain a preaward
L0:survey of the offeror’s proposed aircraft flight and ground operations facility. If the
L0:offeror proposed subcontracting any aircraft work, the preaward survey should include
L0:a review of the subcontractor’s facility. For acquisitions falling under the exceptions at
L0:228.371(b)(1)(iii), (iv), and (vi), the contracting officer must review the documentation
L0:the offeror submitted with the proposal in response to the DD Form 1423, Contract
L0:Data Requirements List, to ensure the offeror’s commercial insurance provides the
L0:appropriate coverage required by the clause at 252.228-7001.
L1:(c) Foreign military sales. The exception for foreign military sales (FMS) contracts
L0:at 228.371(b)(1)(iii) only applies to FMS cases where the FMS customer has explicitly
L0:refused assumption of risk of loss. If the FMS customer has accepted the standard
L0:Letter of Offer and Acceptance Standard Terms and Conditions, as described in DoD
L0:5105.38-M, Security Assistance Management Manual, they have assumed risk of loss.
L1:(d) Commercial derivative aircraft. The exception at 228.371(b)(1)(iv) for
L0:commercial derivative aircraft only applies if the contractor is a licensed and certified
L0:Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) repair station for the specific model of aircraft
L0:under contract, when work is being performed pursuant to the FAA license under 14
L0:CFR part 145. The FAA’s repair station search tool is available at https://av-
L0:info.faa.gov/repairstation.asp. All aircraft flying public aircraft operations operate
L0:under airworthiness certificates maintained by the military services. The FAA
L0:airworthiness certificate in the exception in this paragraph (d) underlies the military
L0:service certificate.
L1:(e) Insurance. The clause at 252.228-7001, Ground and Flight Risk, is intended to
L0:reduce acquisition costs by eliminating the costs of commercial insurance premiums.
L0:This clause also is intended to encourage the contractor to perform safe and effective
L0:operations through inclusion of a contractor’s share of loss (i.e., a deductible).
L0:Additionally, the clause requires compliance with the combined regulation/instruction
L0:entitled “Contractor’s Flight and Ground Operations” (Air Force Instruction 10-220,
L0:Army Regulation 95-20, Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) Instruction 3710.1
L1:(Series), Coast Guard Instruction M13020.3 (Series), and Defense Contract
L0:Management Agency Instruction 8210-1 (Series)), which provides procedures to
L0:mitigate the risk of loss to the Government. For this reason, paragraph (e)(4)(ii) of the
L0:clause at 252.228-7001 specifies that insurance premium costs are unallowable. In
L0:addition, paragraph (d)(4) of the clause provides that the Government’s assumption of
L0:risk does not apply where the loss or damage is covered by available insurance.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L1:(f) Damage to Government aircraft.
L1:(1) Whenever damage to Government aircraft is reported, each incident should
L0:be evaluated on its own merits. When the cost of repair exceeds the contractor’s share
L0:of loss provisions, the contracting officer must make a liability determination in
L0:accordance with paragraph (g) of this section.
L1:(2) Contracting officers should consult with the requiring activity and the
L0:assigned contract administration office on replacement, repair, or beyond economic
L0:repair decisions.
L1:(3) See PGI 228.370-2(f) for an example of accident or mishap damage versus
L0:workmanship-error damage.
L1:(g) Contracting officer determination of liability.
L1:(1) When making a liability determination, the contracting officer should seek
L0:input from the GFR and legal counsel, as needed.
L1:(2) The Government’s assumption of risk must not extend to damage, loss, or
L0:destruction of covered aircraft that—
L1:(i) Is the result of willful misconduct or lack of good faith on the part of the
L0:contractor’s managerial personnel, including the contractor’s oversight of
L0:subcontractors;
L1:(ii) Is sustained during flight if either the flight or the crewmembers have
L0:not been approved in advance and in writing by the GFR, who has been authorized in
L0:accordance with the combined regulation/instruction entitled “Contractor’s Flight and
L0:Ground Operations”;
L1:(iii) Occurs in the course of transportation by rail, or by conveyance on
L0:public streets, highways, or waterways, unless the transportation is limited to the
L0:vicinity of the contractor’s premises, and incidental to work performed under the
L0:contract as described in the Schedule;
L1:(iv) Is covered by insurance;
L1:(v) Occurs after the contracting officer has, in writing, revoked the
L0:Government’s assumption of risk; or
L1:(vi) Is sustained due to workmanship errors.
L1:(h) Notice of revocation of the Government’s assumption of risk. The liability
L0:provisions of the clause at FAR 52.245-1, Government Property, do not apply to the
L0:aircraft impacted by a notice of revocation.
L1:(1) Preliminary notice of revocation.
L1:(i) When finding that contractor managerial personnel have failed to comply
L0:with the combined regulation/instruction, as required by paragraph (b) of the clause at
L0:252.228-7001, including finding the covered aircraft are exposed to unreasonable
L0:conditions, the contracting officer must issue a preliminary notice of revocation of the
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L0:Government’s assumption of risk to the contractor and must require the contractor to
L0:comply with contract requirements. Factors for the contracting officer to consider in
L0:determining exposure to unreasonable conditions include, but are not limited to, the
L0:following:
L1:(A) Lack of adequate hangar fire suppression or firefighting vehicles;
L1:(B) Failure to provide adequate procedures to the GFR; or
L1:(C) Systemic failure to comply with approved procedures.
L1:(ii) The preliminary notice of revocation will state the timeframe for the
L0:contractor to correct the noncompliance or conditions.
L1:(2) Notice of revocation. If the contractor fails to correct the cited
L0:noncompliance or conditions within the specified timeframe, the contracting officer
L0:must issue to the contractor a notice of revocation of the Government’s assumption of
L0:risk for any covered aircraft.
L1:(i) Thereafter the contractor assumes the entire risk for damage, loss, or
L0:destruction of the previously covered aircraft.
L1:(ii) Any costs incurred by the contractor, including the costs of the
L0:contractor’s self-insurance, insurance premiums paid to insure the contractor’s
L0:assumption of risk, deductibles associated with such purchased insurance, etc., to
L0:mitigate its risk are unallowable costs.
L1:(iii) The notice of revocation does not relieve the contractor of its obligation
L0:to comply with all other provisions of the clause at 252.228-7001, including the
L0:combined regulation/instruction entitled “Contractor’s Flight and Ground Operations”.
L1:(iv) Within 3 days of receipt of the contractor’s notice of correction, the
L0:contracting officer must notify the contractor whether the Government will resume risk
L0:of loss. The contracting officer must determine that the noncompliance or cited
L0:conditions have been corrected prior to resuming assumption of risk.
L1:(v) Any disputes regarding the contracting officer’s notice of revocation must
L0:be subject to FAR clause 52.233-1, Disputes.
L1:(i) Procedures in the event of damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft.
L1:(1) In the event of damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft, except in
L0:cases covered by paragraph (j)(2) of this section, the contracting officer must evaluate
L0:the contractor’s statement of—
L1:(i) The damaged, lost, or destroyed aircraft;
L1:(ii) The time and origin of the damage, loss, or destruction;
L1:(iii) All known interests in commingled property of which aircraft are a part;
L0:and
L1:(iv) The insurance, if any, covering the interest in commingled property.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L1:(2) If a new production aircraft is damaged, lost, or destroyed before it has
L0:become a covered aircraft, the Government bears no responsibility for risk of loss.
L1:(3) If a new production aircraft is damaged, lost, or destroyed after it has
L0:become a covered aircraft, the contracting officer must provide written direction to the
L0:contractor to take action in accordance with the contracting officer’s written direction
L0:that the aircraft shall be—
L1:(i) Replaced;
L1:(ii) Repaired to the condition immediately prior to the damage; or
L1:(iii) Considered beyond economic repair. The contracting officer must
L0:decide whether further actions are required under the contract.
L1:(4) If a covered aircraft that has been furnished by the Government to the
L0:contractor is damaged, lost, or destroyed while covered, the contracting officer must
L0:provide written direction to the contractor that the aircraft shall be—
L1:(i) Repaired; or
L1:(ii) Considered beyond economic repair. The contracting officer must decide
L0:further actions required under the contract.
L1:(5) The contracting officer must make an equitable adjustment for expenditures
L0:made in performing the obligations under paragraph (h) of the clause at 252.228-7001.
L1:(j) Contracting officer determination of the contractor’s share of loss.
L1:(1) The contractor’s share of loss or damage to covered aircraft, except for loss or
L0:damage caused by negligence of Government personnel, is the least of—
L1:(i) $200,000;
L1:(ii) 20 percent of the price or estimated acquisition cost of affected aircraft;
L0:or
L1:(iii) 20 percent of the price or estimated cost of the contract, task order, or
L0:delivery order.
L1:(2) If the Government requires covered aircraft to be replaced or repaired by the
L0:contractor, any resulting equitable adjustment must not include reimbursement of the
L0:contractor’s share of loss.
L1:(3) In the event the Government does not decide to replace or repair the covered
L0:aircraft, the clause at 252.228-7001 requires the contractor to credit the contract price
L0:or pay the Government, as directed by the contracting officer, the least of—
L1:(i) $200,000;
L1:(ii) 20 percent of the price or estimated acquisition cost of affected aircraft;
L0:or
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L1:(iii) 20 percent of the price or estimated cost of the contract, task order, or
L0:delivery order.
L1:(4) The costs incurred by the contractor for its share of the loss and for insuring
L0:against that loss are unallowable costs, including but not limited to—
L1:(i) The contractor’s share of loss under the Government’s self-insurance;
L1:(ii) The costs of the contractor’s self-insurance;
L1:(iii) The deductible for any contractor-purchased insurance;
L1:(iv) Insurance premiums paid for contractor-purchased insurance; and
L1:(v) Costs associated with determining, litigating, and defending against the
L0:contractor’s liability.
L1:(k) Reimbursement from a third party. If the contracting officer finds or has reason
L0:to believe that the contractor has been reimbursed or otherwise compensated by a third
L0:party for damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft and has also been compensated
L0:by the Government, then the contracting officer must demand an equitable
L0:reimbursement. If the contracting officer requests that the contractor provide
L0:reasonable assistance in obtaining recovery, such effort must be an allowable expense of
L0:the contractor.

title: 228.370-3 Aircraft not owned by or to be delivered to the Government
content:
L0:228.370-3 Aircraft not owned by or to be delivered to the Government.
L1:(a) When a contract involves aircraft not owned by or to be delivered to the
L0:Government, the contracting officer may use the clause at 252.228-7001 only if the
L0:contracting officer determines that it is in the best interest of the Government.
L1:(b) Potential factors for the contracting officer to consider when deciding which
L0:course of action is in the best interest of the Government include, but are not limited to,
L0:whether—
L1:(1) The cost of hull insurance exceeds the replacement cost of the aircraft;
L1:(2) Insurance is not available (e.g., high-risk experimental flights and
L0:operations of aircraft in a war zone); or
L1:(3) Ground or flight activities that involve contractor-owned and contractor-
L0:operated aircraft may pose risk to Government aircraft (e.g., due to close proximity in
L0:flight).
