title: 252.228-7001 Ground and Flight Risk
content:
L0:252.228-7001 Ground and Flight Risk.
L0:As prescribed in 228.371(b), use the following clause:
L0:GROUND AND FLIGHT RISK (MAR 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Aircraft” means, unless otherwise provided in the contract Schedule, any item,
L0:other than a rocket or missile, intended for flight (e.g., fixed-winged aircraft, blended
L0:wing/lifting bodies, helicopters, vertical take-off or landing aircraft, lighter-than-air
L0:airships, and unmanned aerial vehicles), including emerging technologies that would
L0:commonly be considered aircraft. New production articles become aircraft at a stage of
L0:manufacture or production when a wing, portion of a wing, or engine is attached to a
L0:fuselage. Blended wing/lifting bodies become aircraft at a stage of manufacture or
L0:production when the center portion and a lifting surface become attached.
L0:“Contractor’s managerial personnel” means the Contractor’s directors, officers,
L0:managers, superintendents, or equivalent representatives who have supervision or
L0:direction of—
L1:(1) All, or substantially all, of the Contractor’s business;
L1:(2) All, or substantially all, of the Contractor’s operation at any one plant or
L0:separate location; or
L1:(3) A separate and complete major industrial operation.
L0:“Contractor's premises” means those premises, including subcontractors’ premises,
L0:designated in the Schedule or in writing by the Contracting Officer, and any other place
L0:the aircraft is moved for safeguarding.
L0:“Covered aircraft” means an aircraft owned by or to be delivered to the Government
L0:and, when determined by the contracting officer and specifically identified as such in
L0:the contract Schedule, may include contractor-furnished aircraft that are not intended
L0:for induction into the DoD inventory, including—
L1:(1) Aircraft furnished by the Government to the Contractor under this contract
L0:while in the Contractor’s possession, care, custody, or control regardless of their location
L0:or state of disassembly or reassembly;
L1:(2) Items removed from a Government-furnished aircraft that are—
L1:(i) Intended for reinstallation on that particular aircraft, which retain their
L0:status as covered aircraft while awaiting installation; and
L1:(ii) Not intended for reinstallation on that particular aircraft, which lose
L0:their status as covered aircraft once removal is complete;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L1:(3) New production aircraft when wholly outside of buildings on the
L0:Contractor’s premises or other places described in the Schedule (e.g., hush houses, run
L0:stations, and paint facilities); and
L1:(4) Commercial aircraft, to include commercially available off-the-shelf aircraft,
L0:become covered aircraft when the commercial aircraft arrives at the Contractor’s place
L0:of performance for modification under the terms of the contract.
L0:“Crewmember” means, unless otherwise provided in the Schedule, personnel
L0:required in the flight manual, assigned for the purpose of conducting any flight on
L0:behalf of the Contractor. It also includes any operator of an unmanned aerial vehicle.
L0:“Flight” means any flight approved in writing by the Government flight
L0:representative, to include taxi test made in the performance of this contract, or flight for
L0:the purpose of safeguarding the aircraft. All aircraft off the Contractor's premises shall
L0:be considered to be in flight when on the ground or water for reasonable periods of time
L0:following emergency landings, landings made in performance of the contract, or
L0:landings approved in writing by the contracting officer.
L0:“Workmanship error” means damage to the aircraft that is the result of an
L0:incorrectly performed skill-based task, operation, or action that was originally planned
L0:or intended.
L1:(b) Combined regulation/instruction. The Contractor shall be bound by the
L0:operating procedures contained in the combined regulation/instruction entitled
L0:“Contractor’s Flight and Ground Operations” (Air Force Instruction 10-220, Army
L0:Regulation 95-20, NAVAIR Instruction 3710.1 (Series), Coast Guard Instruction
L0:M13020.3 (Series), and Defense Contract Management Agency Instruction 8210-1
L1:(Series)) in effect on the date of contract award. Compliance with the combined
L0:regulation/instruction is required from the time of contract award throughout the period
L0:of performance of the contract, regardless of the Government’s assumption of risk under
L0:the contract.
L1:(c) Government as self-insurer. The Government self-insures and assumes the risk
L0:of damage to, or loss or destruction of, covered aircraft subject to the following
L0:conditions:
L1:(1) The Contractor’s liability to the Government for damage, loss, or destruction
L0:of covered aircraft is limited to the Contractor’s share of loss as defined at paragraph (h)
L0:of this clause, except when one of the exclusions at paragraph (d) applies.
L1:(2) The liability provisions of this clause take precedence over the liability
L0:provisions of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) clause 52.245-1, Government
L0:Property, with respect to covered aircraft.
L1:(3) The Contractor is not liable for loss, damage, or destruction of covered
L0:aircraft as the result of normal wear and tear, or intentional damage or destruction as
L0:required in the Schedule.
L1:(4) Conditions for Government assumption of risk in flight are as follows:
L1:(i) The Contractor’s crewmembers are approved in writing by the
L0:Government flight representative (GFR).
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L1:(ii) The flight is approved in writing by the GFR.
L1:(d) Exclusions from the Government’s assumption of risk. The Government’s
L0:assumption of risk under this clause shall not extend to damage, loss, or destruction of
L0:covered aircraft which—
L1:(1) Is the result of willful misconduct or lack of good faith on the part of the
L0:Contractor’s managerial personnel, including the Contractor’s oversight of
L0:subcontractors;
L1:(2) Is sustained during flight if either the flight or the crewmembers have not
L0:been approved in advance and in writing by the GFR, who has been authorized in
L0:accordance with the combined regulation/instruction entitled “Contractor’s Flight and
L0:Ground Operations”;
L1:(3) Occurs in the course of transportation by rail, or by conveyance on public
L0:streets, highways, or waterways, unless the transportation is limited to the vicinity of
L0:the Contractor’s premises, and incidental to work performed under the contract as
L0:described in the Schedule;
L1:(4) Is covered by insurance;
L1:(5) Occurs after the Contracting Officer has, in writing, revoked the
L0:Government’s assumption of risk in accordance with paragraph (e)(3) of this clause;
L0:or
L1:(6) Is sustained due to workmanship errors.
L1:(e) Revoking the Government’s assumption of risk.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer, when finding that the Contractor’s managerial
L0:personnel have failed to comply with paragraph (b) of this clause, will issue a
L0:preliminary notice of revocation requiring the Contractor to comply with contract
L0:requirements within a timeframe specified by the Contracting Officer. In determining
L0:exposure to unreasonable conditions, the Contracting Officer will consider factors
L0:including, but not limited to, the following: lack of adequate hangar fire suppression or
L0:firefighting vehicles, failure to provide adequate procedures to the GFR, or systemic
L0:failure to comply with approved procedures.
L1:(2) Upon receipt of the preliminary notice of revocation, the Contractor shall
L0:promptly correct the noncompliance or cited conditions, regardless of whether there is
L0:agreement that the conditions are unreasonable.
L1:(3) If the Contracting Officer finds that the Contractor failed to correct the cited
L0:noncompliance or conditions within the specified timeframe, the Contracting Officer will
L0:issue a notice of revocation of the Government’s assumption of risk for any covered
L0:aircraft.
L1:(4) If the Contracting Officer issues a notice of revocation pursuant to the terms
L0:of this clause—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L1:(i) The Contractor shall thereafter assume the entire risk for damage, loss,
L0:or destruction of the previously covered aircraft;
L1:(ii) Any costs incurred by the Contractor (including the costs of the
L0:Contractor’s self-insurance, insurance premiums paid to insure the Contractor’s
L0:assumption of risk, deductibles associated with such purchased insurance, etc.) to
L0:mitigate its risk are unallowable costs; and
L1:(iii) The liability provisions of the clause at FAR 52.245-1, Government
L0:Property, are not applicable to the aircraft impacted by the notice of revocation.
L1:(5) The Contractor shall promptly notify the Contracting Officer when the
L0:noncompliance or cited conditions have been corrected. Within 3 days of receipt of the
L0:Contractor’s notice of correction, the Contracting Officer will notify the Contractor
L0:whether the Government will resume risk of loss. The Contracting Officer will
L0:determine that the noncompliance or cited conditions have been corrected prior to
L0:resuming assumption of risk.
L1:(6) The notice of revocation does not relieve the Contractor of its obligation to
L0:comply with all other provisions of this clause, including the combined
L0:regulation/instruction entitled “Contractor’s Flight and Ground Operations.”
L1:(7) Any disputes regarding the Contracting Officer’s notice of revocation shall
L0:be subject to FAR clause 52.233-1, Disputes.
L1:(f) Contractor’s exclusion of insurance costs. The Contractor warrants that the
L0:contract price does not and will not include, except as may be authorized in this clause,
L0:any charge or contingency reserve for insurance (including the Contractor’s share of
L0:loss) covering damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft when the risk has been
L0:assumed by the Government even if the assumption may be terminated for covered
L0:aircraft.
L1:(g) Procedures in the event of damage, loss, or destruction.
L1:(1) In the event of damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft, the
L0:Contractor shall take all reasonable steps to protect the aircraft from further damage, to
L0:separate damaged and undamaged aircraft, and to put all aircraft in the best possible
L0:order. Except in cases covered by paragraph (h)(2) of this clause, the Contractor shall
L0:furnish to the Contracting Officer a statement of—
L1:(i) The damaged, lost, or destroyed aircraft;
L1:(ii) The time and origin of the damage, loss, or destruction;
L1:(iii) All known interests in commingled property of which aircraft are a part;
L0:and
L1:(iv) The insurance, if any, covering the interest in commingled property.
L1:(2) If a new production aircraft is damaged, lost, or destroyed before it has
L0:become a covered aircraft, the Government bears no responsibility for risk of loss.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L1:(3) If a new production aircraft is damaged, lost, or destroyed after it has
L0:become a covered aircraft, the Contractor shall take action in accordance with the
L0:Contracting Officer’s written direction that the aircraft shall be—
L1:(i) Replaced;
L1:(ii) Repaired to the condition immediately prior to the damage; or
L1:(iii) Considered beyond economic repair. The Contracting Officer will decide
L0:whether further actions are required under the contract.
L1:(4) If a covered aircraft that has been furnished by the Government to the
L0:Contractor is damaged, lost, or destroyed while covered, the Contractor shall take action
L0:in accordance with the Contracting Officer’s written direction that the aircraft shall
L0:be—
L1:(i) Repaired; or
L1:(ii) Considered beyond economic repair. The Contracting Officer will decide
L0:further actions required under the contract.
L1:(5) The Contracting Officer will make an equitable adjustment for expenditures
L0:made in performing the obligations under this paragraph (g).
L1:(h) Contractor’s share of loss.
L1:(1) The Contractor’s share of loss or damage to covered aircraft, except for loss
L0:or damage caused by negligence of Government personnel, is the least of—
L1:(i) $200,000;
L1:(ii) 20 percent of the price or estimated acquisition cost of affected aircraft;
L0:or
L1:(iii) 20 percent of the price or estimated cost of the contract, task order, or
L0:delivery order.
L1:(2) If the Government requires covered aircraft be replaced or repaired by the
L0:Contractor, any resulting equitable adjustment shall not include reimbursement of the
L0:Contractor’s share of loss.
L1:(3) In the event the Government does not decide to replace or repair, the
L0:Contractor agrees to credit the contract price or pay the Government, as directed by the
L0:Contracting Officer, the least of—
L1:(i) $200,000;
L1:(ii) 20 percent of the price or estimated acquisition cost of affected aircraft;
L0:or
L1:(iii) 20 percent of the price or estimated cost of the contract, task order, or
L0:delivery order.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L1:(4) The costs incurred by the Contractor for its share of the loss and for insuring
L0:against that loss are unallowable costs, including but not limited to—
L1:(i) The Contractor’s share of loss under the Government’s self-insurance;
L1:(ii) The costs of the Contractor’s self-insurance;
L1:(iii) The deductible for any Contractor-purchased insurance;
L1:(iv) Insurance premiums paid for Contractor-purchased insurance; and
L1:(v) Costs associated with determining, litigating, and defending against the
L0:Contractor’s liability.
L1:(i) Reimbursement from a third party. In the event the Contractor is reimbursed or
L0:compensated by a third party for damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft and
L0:has also been compensated by the Government, the Contractor shall equitably
L0:reimburse the Government. The Contractor shall do nothing to prejudice the
L0:Government’s right to recover against third parties for damage, loss, or destruction.
L0:Upon the request of the Contracting Officer or authorized representative, the
L0:Contractor shall at Government expense furnish to the Government all reasonable
L0:assistance and cooperation (including the prosecution of suit and the execution of
L0:instruments of assignment or subrogation) in obtaining recovery.
L1:(j) Liability to third parties. Unless the flight and crewmembers have been
L0:approved in writing by the GFR, the Contractor shall not be reimbursed for liability to
L0:third parties for loss or damage to property or for death or bodily injury caused by
L0:covered aircraft during flight, even if the Government has accepted such liability under
L0:any other provisions of the contract.
L1:(k) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall incorporate the requirements of this clause,
L0:including this paragraph (k), in subcontracts to include subcontracts for commercial
L0:products and commercial services, except—
L1:(1) The Contractor shall not include paragraph (f) of this clause in subcontracts
L0:for commercial products or commercial services; and
L1:(2) The Contractor shall not incorporate the requirements of this clause in
L0:subcontracts with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) part 145 repair stations
L0:performing work pursuant to their FAA license.

title: 252.228-7003 Capture and Detention
content:
L0:252.228-7003 Capture and Detention.
L0:As prescribed in 228.371(c), use the following clause:
L0:CAPTURE AND DETENTION (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) As used in this clause—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L1:(1) “Captured person” means any employee of the Contractor who is—
L1:(i) Assigned to duty outside the United States for the performance of this
L0:contract; and
L1:(ii) Found to be missing from his or her place of employment under
L0:circumstances that make it appear probable that the absence is due to the action of the
L0:force of any power not allied with the United States in a common military effort; or
L1:(iii) Known to have been taken prisoner, hostage, or otherwise detained by
L0:the force of such power, whether or not actually engaged in employment at the time of
L0:capture; provided, that at the time of capture or detention, the person was either—
L0:employment under this contract; or
L1:(A) Engaged in activity directly arising out of and in the course of
L0:this contract.
L1:(B) Captured in an area where required to be only in order to perform
L1:(2) A “period of detention” begins with the day of capture and continues until
L0:the captured person is returned to the place of employment, the United States, or is able
L0:to be returned to the jurisdiction of the United States, or until the person's death is
L0:established or legally presumed to have occurred by evidence satisfactory to the
L0:Contracting Officer, whichever occurs first.
L1:(3) “United States” comprises geographically the 50 states and the District of
L0:Columbia.
L1:(4) “War Hazards Compensation Act” refers to the statute compiled in Chapter
L0:12 of Title 42, U.S. Code (sections 1701-1717), as amended.
L1:(b) If pursuant to an agreement entered into prior to capture, the Contractor is
L0:obligated to pay and has paid detention benefits to a captured person, or the person's
L0:dependents, the Government will reimburse the Contractor up to an amount equal to
L0:the lesser of—
L1:(1) Total wage or salary being paid at the time of capture due from the
L0:Contractor to the captured person for the period of detention; or
L1:(2) That amount which would have been payable if the detention had occurred
L0:under circumstances covered by the War Hazards Compensation Act.
L1:(c) The period of detention shall not be considered as time spent in contract
L0:performance, and the Government shall not be obligated to make payment for that time
L0:except as provided in this clause.
L1:(d) The obligation of the Government shall apply to the entire period of detention,
L0:except that it is subject to the availability of funds from which payment can be made.
L0:The rights and obligations of the parties under this clause shall survive prior expiration,
L0:completion, or termination of this contract.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L1:(e) The Contractor shall not be reimbursed under this clause for payments made if
L0:the employees were entitled to compensation for capture and detention under the War
L0:Hazards Compensation Act, as amended.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.228-7007 Public Aircraft and State Aircraft Operations—Liability
content:
L0:252.228-7007 Public Aircraft and State Aircraft Operations—Liability.
L0:As prescribed in 228.371(f), use the following clause:
L0:PUBLIC AIRCRAFT AND STATE AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS—LIABILITY
L0:(MAR 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Civil aircraft” means an aircraft other than a public aircraft or state aircraft.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L0:“Public aircraft” means an aircraft that meets the definition in 49 U.S.C.
L0:40102(a)(41) and the qualifications in 49 U.S.C. 40125. Specifically, a public aircraft
L0:means any of the following:
L1:(1) An aircraft used only for the Government, except as provided in paragraphs
L1:(5) and (7) of this definition.
L1:(2) An aircraft owned by the Government and operated by any person for
L0:purposes related to crew training, equipment development, or demonstration, except as
L0:provided in paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(3) An aircraft owned and operated by the government of a State, the District of
L0:Columbia, or a territory or possession of the United States or a political subdivision of
L0:one of these governments, except as provided in paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(4) An aircraft exclusively leased for at least 90 continuous days by the
L0:government of a State, the District of Columbia, or a territory or possession of the
L0:United States or a political subdivision of one of these governments, except as provided
L0:in paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(5) An aircraft owned or operated by the armed forces or chartered to provide
L0:transportation or other commercial air service to the armed forces under the conditions
L0:specified by 49 U.S.C. 40125(c). In the preceding sentence, the term “other commercial
L0:air service” means an aircraft operation that—
L1:(i) Is within the United States territorial airspace;
L1:(ii) The Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration determines is
L0:available for compensation or hire to the public; and
L1:(iii) Must comply with all applicable civil aircraft rules under title 14, Code
L0:of Federal Regulations.
L1:(6) An unmanned aircraft that is owned and operated, or exclusively leased for
L0:at least 90 continuous days, by an Indian Tribal government, as defined in section 102
L0:of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C.
L0:5122), except as provided in paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(7) As described in 49 U.S.C. 40125(b), an aircraft described in paragraph (1),
L1:(2), (3), or (4) of this definition does not qualify as a public aircraft when the aircraft is
L0:used for commercial purposes or to carry an individual other than a crewmember or a
L0:qualified non-crewmember.
L0:“Public aircraft operation” means operation of an aircraft that meets the legal
L0:definition of public aircraft established in 49 U.S.C. 40102(a)(41) and the legal
L0:qualifications for public aircraft status outlined in 49 U.S.C. 40125.
L0:“State aircraft” means an aircraft operated by the Government for sovereign,
L0:noncommercial purposes such as military, customs, and police services. Military
L0:aircraft are afforded status as state aircraft. In very rare circumstances, DoD-
L0:contracted aircraft may be designated, in writing, by a responsible Government official
L0:pursuant to DoD Directive 4500.54E, DoD Foreign Clearance Program, to be operated
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L0:in state aircraft status, and such status cannot be deemed without a written
L0:designation by an authorized Government official.
L1:(b) Combined regulation/instruction. Upon award, for contract performance to be
L0:conducted as a public aircraft operation, the Contractor shall be bound by the operating
L0:procedures contained in the combined regulation/instruction entitled “Contractor’s
L0:Flight and Ground Operations” (Air Force Instruction 10-220, Army Regulation 95-20,
L0:NAVAIR Instruction 3710.1 (Series), Coast Guard Instruction M13020.3 (Series), and
L0:Defense Contract Management Agency Instruction 8210-1 (Series)) in effect on the date
L0:of contract award.
L1:(c) Contractor liability for operations for contract performance conducted as public
L0:aircraft operations or state aircraft operations.
L1:(1) The Contractor assumes responsibility for all damage or injury to persons or
L0:property, including the Contractor’s employees and property, and Government
L0:personnel and property, occasioned through the use, maintenance, and operation of the
L0:Contractor’s aircraft or other equipment by, or the action of, the Contractor or the
L0:Contractor’s employees and agents.
L1:(2) The Contractor, at the Contractor’s expense, shall maintain adequate public
L0:liability and property damage insurance, including hull insurance for the Contractor’s
L0:aircraft, during the duration of this contract, insuring the Contractor against all claims
L0:for injury or damage.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall maintain workers’ compensation and other legally
L0:required insurance with respect to the Contractor’s own employees and agents.
L1:(4) The Government will in no event be liable or responsible for damage or
L0:injury to any person or property occasioned through the use, maintenance, or operation
L0:of any aircraft or other equipment by, or the action of, the Contractor or the Contractor’s
L0:employees and agents in performing under this contract, and the Government shall be
L0:indemnified and saved harmless against claims for damage or injury in such cases.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228

L0:reported, particularly when the cost of repair exceeds the contractor’s share of loss
L0:provisions, the contracting officer must make a proper liability determination. For most
L0:situations, determining whether an incident is an accident or mishap, or a workmanship error
L0:can be made based on intent of the employee(s) involved. Although each incident involving
L0:damage should be evaluated on its own merits, use the following general rules and
L0:examples when determining if an incident constitutes an accident or mishap (damage
L0:normally covered under the clause at 252.228-7001) or a workmanship error (damage not
L0:normally covered under the clause at 252.228-7001).
L1:(1) An accident or mishap is the result of a task, operation, or action that was not
L0:originally planned or intended. For example, a mechanic was pushing a stand next to the
L0:aircraft and scratches the inlet coating. The intent of the task was to move the stand, not to
L0:scratch the coating. This would be considered accident or mishap damage to the aircraft,
L0:and a contractor should expect to be reimbursed under the clause at 252.228-7001 (minus
L0:the appropriate contractor share of loss).
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 28
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 228
L2:(2)(i) A workmanship error consists of damage that is the result of an incorrectly
L0:performed skill-based task, operation, or action that was originally planned or intended, but
L0:the end result was not within allowable limits. For example, a mechanic was scraping
L0:coating off an inlet and removed too much material. The intent of the task was to scrape the
L0:inlet coating, but too much was removed. This would not be considered aircraft damage
L0:reimbursed under the clause at 252.228-7001.
L1:(ii) Missing a step in a procedure or checklist item is not considered a skill-
L0:based error and therefore is not considered workmanship error damage.

L0:“Commodities,” as used in this section, means any materials, articles, supplies, goods, or

title: 229.170-2 Policy
content:
L0:229.170-2 Policy.
L1:(a) By law, bilateral agreements with foreign governments must include a provision
L0:that commodities acquired under contracts funded by U.S. assistance programs must be
L0:exempt from taxation by the foreign government. If taxes or customs duties
L0:nevertheless are imposed, the foreign government must reimburse the amount of such
L0:taxes to the U.S. Government (Section 579 of Division E of the Consolidated
L0:Appropriations Act, 2003 (Pub. L. 108-7).
L1:(b) This foreign tax exemption—
L1:(1) Applies to a contract or subcontract for commodities when—
L1:(i) The funds are appropriated by the annual foreign operations
L0:appropriations act; and
L1:(ii) The value of the contract or subcontract is $500 or more;
L1:(2) Does not apply to the acquisition of services;
L1:(3) Generally, is implemented through letters of offer and acceptance, other
L0:country-to-country agreements, or Federal interagency agreements; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 29
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 229
L1:(4) Requires reporting of noncompliance for effective implementation.

L1:(a) “Direct Contractor,” as used in this clause, means an individual, company, or

L0:Friendship, Defense and Cooperation between the United States Government and
L0:the Kingdom of Spain, dated July 2, 1982. The Agreement relates to contracts to be
L0:performed in whole or part in Spain, the provisions of which are hereby incorporated
L0:into and made a part of this contract by reference.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall apply to the appropriate Spanish authorities for approval of
L0:status as a Direct Contractor in order to complete duty-free import of non-Spanish
L0:equipment, materials, and supplies represented as necessary for contract performance
L0:by the Contracting Officer. Orders for equipment, materials, and supplies placed prior
L0:to official notification of such approval shall be at the Contractor’s own risk. The
L0:Contractor must submit its documentation in sufficient time to permit processing by the
L0:appropriate United States and Spanish Government agencies prior to the arrival of the
L0:equipment, materials, or supplies in Spain. Seasonal variations in processing times are
L0:common, and the Contractor should program its projects accordingly. Any delay or

L0:performance (except as expressly allowed in other provisions of this contract), constitute
L0:a direct or constructive change, or otherwise provide a basis for additional compensation
L0:or adjustment of any kind.
L1:(d) To ensure that all duty-free imports are properly accounted for, exported, or
L0:disposed of, in accordance with Spanish law, the Contractor shall obtain a written bank
L0:letter of guaranty payable to the Treasurer of the United States, or such other authority
L0:as may be designated by the Contracting Officer, in the amount set forth in paragraph
L1:(g) of this clause, prior to effecting any duty-free imports for the performance of this
L0:contract.
L1:(e) If the Contractor fails to obtain the required guaranty, the Contractor agrees
L0:that the Contracting Officer may withhold a portion of the contract payments in order

title: 231.205-70 External restructuring costs
content:
L0:231.205-70 External restructuring costs.
L1:(a) Scope. This subsection contains policies and procedures for allowing contractor
L0:external restructuring costs when savings would result for DoD and implements 10
L0:U.S.C. 3761.
L1:(b) Definitions. As used in this section--
L0:“Business combination” means a transaction whereby assets or operations of
L0:two or more companies not previously under common ownership or control are
L0:combined, whether by merger, acquisition, or sale/purchase of assets.
L0:“External restructuring activities” means restructuring activities occurring
L0:after a business combination, affecting the operations of companies not previously
L0:under common ownership or control. They exclude restructuring within a single
L0:company or only affecting one company from the combination. External restructuring
L0:activities are a direct outgrowth of a business combination and normally occur within 3
L0:years of the business combination.
L0:“Restructuring activities” means nonroutine, nonrecurring, or extraordinary
L0:activities to combine facilities, operations, or workforce, to eliminate redundant
L0:capabilities, improve future operations, and reduce overall costs. Restructuring
L0:activities exclude routine or ongoing repositionings and redeployments of a contractor’s
L0:productive facilities or workforce (e.g., normal plant rearrangement or employee
L0:relocation), and exclude other routine or ordinary activities charged as indirect costs
L0:that would otherwise have been incurred (e.g., planning and analysis, contract
L0:administration and oversight, or recurring financial and administrative support).
L0:“Restructuring costs” means both direct and indirect costs of restructuring
L0:activities. Allowable restructuring costs include, but are not limited to, severance pay
L0:for employees, early retirement incentive payments for employees, employee retraining
L0:costs, relocation expense for retained employees, and relocation and rearrangement of
L0:plant and equipment. For purposes of this definition, restructuring costs under $2.5
L0:million related to external restructuring activities allocated to DoD contracts are not
L0:subject to the audit, review, and determination requirements of paragraph (c)(4) of this
L0:subsection; instead, standard cost allowability rules in FAR Part 31 apply.
L0:“Restructuring savings” means both direct and indirect cost reductions
L0:resulting from restructuring activities. Cost reassignments to future periods are not
L0:restructuring savings.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 31
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 231
L1:(c) Limitations on cost allowability. Restructuring costs associated with external
L0:restructuring activities are not allowed unless—
L1:(1) The costs are allowable in accordance with FAR Part 31 and DFARS Part
L0:231;
L1:(2) An audit of projected restructuring costs and restructuring savings is
L0:performed;

L0:written determination that the audited projected savings, on a present value basis, for
L0:DoD resulting from the restructuring will exceed either
L1:(A) The costs allowed by a factor of at least two to one; or
L0:preservation of a critical capability that DoD might otherwise lose.
L1:(B) The costs allowed, and the business combination will result in the
L2:(ii)(A) If the amount of restructuring costs is expected to exceed $25 million
L0:over a 5-year period, the designated official is the Under Secretary of Defense
L0:(Acquisition and Sustainment) or the Principal Deputy. This authority cannot be
L0:delegated below the Assistant Secretary of Defense level.
L0:is the Director of the Defense Contract Management Agency.
L1:(B) For all other cases, on a nondelegable basis, the designated official
L1:(d) Procedures and ACO responsibilities. As soon as it is known that the contractor
L0:will incur restructuring costs for external restructuring activities, the ACO shall follow
L0:the procedures at PGI 231.205-70(d).
L1:(e) Information needed to obtain a determination.
L1:(1) The novation agreement (if one is required).
L1:(2) The contractor’s restructuring proposal.
L1:(3) The proposed advance agreement.
L1:(4) The audit report.
L1:(5) Any other pertinent information.
L1:(6) The ACO’s recommendation for a determination. This recommendation
L0:must clearly indicate one of the following, consistent with paragraph (c)(4)(i) of this
L0:subsection:
L1:(i) The audited projected savings for DoD will exceed the costs allowed by a
L0:factor of at least two to one on a present value basis.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 31
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 231
L1:(ii) The business combination will result in the preservation of a critical
L0:capability that might otherwise be lost to DoD, and the audited projected savings for
L0:DoD will exceed the costs allowed on a present value basis.
L1:(f) Contracting officer responsibilities.
L1:(1) The contracting officer, with the ACO’s input, should consider a repricing
L0:clause in noncompetitive fixed-price contracts negotiated during the period between
L1:(i) The time a business combination is announced; and
L1:(ii) The time the contractor’s forward pricing rates are adjusted to reflect
L0:the impact of restructuring.
L1:(2) Use of a repricing clause depends on the specific situation, including
L1:(i) When the restructuring will take place;
L1:(ii) When restructuring savings will begin to be realized;
L1:(iii) The contract performance period;
L1:(iv) Whether the contracting parties can reasonably estimate the
L0:restructuring impact on the contract; and
L1:(v) The size of the potential dollar impact of restructuring on the contract.
L1:(3) If the contracting officer decides to use a repricing clause, the clause must
L0:provide for a downward-only price adjustment to ensure that DoD receives its
L0:appropriate share of restructuring net savings.

title: 232.901 Applicability
content:
L0:232.901 Applicability.
L1:(1) Except for FAR 32.908, FAR subpart 32.9, Prompt Payment, does not apply
L0:when—
L1:(i) There is—
L1:(A) An emergency, as defined in the Disaster Relief Act of 1974;
L1:(B) A contingency operation (see FAR 2.101(b)); or
L1:(C) The release or threatened release of hazardous substances (as defined in
L0:4 U.S.C. 9606, section 106);
L1:(ii) The head of the contracting activity has made a determination, after
L0:consultation with the cognizant comptroller, that conditions exist that limit normal
L0:business operations; and
L1:(iii) Payments will be made in the operational area or made contingent upon
L0:receiving supporting documentation (i.e., contract, invoice, and receiving report) from
L0:the operational area.
L1:(2) Criteria limiting normal business operations during emergencies and
L0:contingency operations that restrict the use of FAR 32.9 may include such conditions
L0:as—
L1:(i) Support infrastructure, hardware, communications capabilities, and
L0:bandwidth are not consistently available such that normal business operations can be
L0:carried out;
L1:(ii) Support resources, facilities, and banking needs are not consistently
L0:available for use as necessary in carrying out normal business operations;
L1:(iii) Military mission priorities override the availability of appropriately skilled
L0:personnel in support of back-office operations;
L1:(iv) Mobility impairments and security concerns restrict free movement of
L0:personnel and documents necessary for timely processing;
L1:(v) Foreign vendors are not familiar with or do not understand DoD contract
L0:requirements (i.e., proper invoice, receiving documentation, and contracting terms); or
L1:(vi) Documents received in support of payment requests and shipments require
L0:language translations that cannot be performed and documented within normal
L0:business processing times.
L1:(3) Subsequent Determinations. The head of the contracting activity must make
L0:subsequent determinations, after consultation with the cognizant comptroller, as the
L0:operational area evolves into either a more stable or less stable environment.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 32
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 232
L1:(i) If the head of the contracting activity determines that the operational area
L0:has evolved into a more stable environment, the contracting officer must notify, by
L0:issuance of a contract modification, each contractor performing in the operational area
L0:under review. The modification deactivates this clause 252.232-7011 and activates the
L0:applicable FAR Prompt Payment clause in the contract.
L1:(ii) If after deactivation of this clause, the head of the contracting activity
L0:subsequently determines that the operational area has evolved into a less stable
L0:environment, the head of the contracting activity will make a determination that
L0:conditions exist that limit normal business operations. The contracting officer will then
L0:reactivate this clause 252.232-7011 by issuance of a contract modification.

title: 232.1001 Policy
content:
L0:232.1001 Policy.
L1:(a) As with all contract financing, the purpose of performance-based payments is to
L0:assist the contractor in the payment of costs incurred during the performance of the
L0:contract. See PGI 232.1001(a) for additional information on use of performance-based
L0:payments. However, in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3802(a)(2), performance-based
L0:payments must not be conditioned upon costs incurred in contract performance, but on
L0:the achievement of performance outcomes. Subject to the criteria in 232.1003-70, all
L0:companies, including nontraditional defense contractors, are eligible for performance-
L0:based payments, consistent with best commercial practices.
L1:(d) The contracting officer must use the following standard payment terms for
L0:performance-based payments: The contractor entitlement date, if any, specified in the
L0:contract, or 14 days after receipt by the designated billing office of a proper request for
L0:payment, whichever is later.

content:
L0:232.1003-70 Criteria for use.
L0:In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3802(c)(1), a contractor’s financial statements must
L0:comply with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, in order to receive performance-
L0:based payments. 10 U.S.C. 3802(c)(2) does not grant the Defense Contract Audit
L0:Agency the authority to audit compliance with Generally Accepted Accounting
L0:Principles.

title: 232.1004 Procedures
content:
L0:232.1004 Procedures.
L1:(b) Establishing performance-based finance payment amounts.
L1:(i) The contracting officer should include in a solicitation both the progress
L0:payments and performance-based payments provisions and clauses prescribed in this
L0:part, when considering both types of payment methods. Only one type of financing will
L0:be included in the resultant contract, except as may be authorized on separate orders
L0:subject to FAR 32.1003(c)).
L1:(ii) The contracting officer must analyze the performance-based payment
L0:schedule using the performance-based payments (PBP) analysis tool. The PBP analysis
L0:tool is on the Defense Pricing, Contracting, and Acquisition Policy website in the Price,
L0:Cost and Finance section. The PBP analysis tool and Performance Based Payment
L0:Guidebook are available at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/pcf/pricing-
L0:topics.html#pdp.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 32
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 232
L1:(A) When considering performance-based payments, obtain from the
L0:offeror/contractor a proposed performance-based payments schedule that includes all
L0:performance-based payments events, completion criteria and event values along with
L0:the projected monthly expenditure profile in order to negotiate the value of the
L0:performance events such that the performance-based payments are not expected to
L0:result in an unreasonably low or negative level of contractor investment in the contract.
L0:If performance-based payments are deemed practical, the Government will evaluate
L0:and negotiate the details of the performance-based payments schedule.

title: 232.7100 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:232.7100 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart prescribes policies and procedures concerning the effect of levies pursuant
L0:to 26 U.S.C. 6331(h) on contract payments. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is
L0:authorized to levy up to 100 percent of all payments made under a DoD contract, up to
L0:the amount of the tax debt.

title: 232.7101 Policy and procedures
content:
L0:232.7101 Policy and procedures.
L1:(a) Contractors are required to—
L1:(1) Promptly notify the contracting officer when a levy may result in an
L0:inability to perform the contract; and
L1:(2) Advise the contracting officer whether the inability to perform may
L0:adversely affect national security.
L1:(b) The contracting officer must promptly notify the Principal Director, Defense
L0:Pricing, Contracting, and Acquisition Policy (DPCAP) when the contractor’s
L0:inability to perform will adversely affect national security or will result in
L0:significant additional costs to the Government. Follow the procedures at PGI
L0:232.7101(b) for reviewing the contractor’s rationale and submitting the required
L0:notification.
L1:(c) The Principal Director, DPCAP, will promptly evaluate the contractor’s
L0:rationale and will notify the IRS, the contracting officer, and the payment office, as
L0:appropriate, in accordance with the procedures at PGI 232.7101(c).
L1:(d) The contracting officer must then notify the contractor in accordance with
L0:paragraph (c) of the clause at 252.232-7010 and in accordance with the procedures
L0:at PGI 232.7101(d).

L0:is segregated and a single progress payment rate is used.

L0:payment proration is performed on a lot-wide, versus contract-wide, basis.

L0:PGI 232.71—LEVIES ON CONTRACT PAYMENTS
L0:PGI 232.7101 Policy and procedures.
L0:Background. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is authorized to collect overdue taxes
L0:through a continuous levy up to 100 percent of the debt on certain vendor contract
L0:payments disbursed by the Defense Finance and Accounting Service. The levy is
L0:continuous until the overdue taxes are paid in full, or other arrangements are made to
L0:satisfy the debt. Contractors are required to promptly notify the procuring contracting
L0:officer when a tax levy that may result in an inability to perform the contract is imposed,
L0:so that the contracting officer and the Principal Director, Defense Pricing, Contracting,
L0:and Acquisition Policy (DPCAP), can take appropriate action to mitigate any possible
L0:adverse effect on national security.
L1:(b) Procuring contracting officer procedures for reviewing the contractor’s rationale
L0:and submitting the required documentation.
L1:(i) When the procuring contracting officer receives notification from the
L0:contractor that the tax levy may result in an inability to perform the contract, the
L0:procuring contracting officer must promptly review the contractor’s assessment and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 32
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 232
L0:either agree or disagree that the levy may result in an inability to perform. The
L0:procuring contracting officer must alert the administrative contracting officer and the
L0:cognizant contract auditor when a notice of levy has been received and must obtain any
L0:necessary assistance from the administrative contracting officer or contract auditor
L0:when performing this review.
L1:(ii) If the procuring contracting officer does not agree with the contractor’s
L0:assessment, the procuring contracting officer must notify the contractor of this
L0:determination, and no further action will be taken.
L1:(iii) If the procuring contracting officer agrees with the contractor’s assessment
L0:that the levy may result in an inability to perform the contract, the procuring contracting
L0:officer must document, in writing, whether the inability to perform—
L1:(A) Adversely affects national security; and/or
L1:(B) Will result in significant additional costs to the Government (e.g., cost of
L0:re-procurement, loss of contract financing payments when the product produced to date
L0:is not salvageable).
L1:(iv) If the procuring contracting officer believes that the levy will impact national
L0:security and/or result in significant additional costs to DoD, the procuring contracting
L0:officer must, in accordance with agency procedures, promptly notify the Principal
L0:Director, DPCAP, via email at osd.pentagon.ousd-a-s.mbx.asda-dp-c-
L0:contractpolicy@mail.mil. The notification to the Principal Director, DPCAP, must
L0:include—
L1:(A) The rationale supporting the recommendation that the levy may result in
L0:an inability to perform the contract;
L1:(B) A description of the adverse effect on national security, if applicable;
L0:and
L1:(C) A description and estimate of the additional costs to the Government, if
L0:applicable. Since prompt notification to the Principal Director, DPCAP, is essential, the
L0:procuring contracting officer should not delay the notification while trying to achieve
L0:more precise data.
L1:(c) Principal Director, DPCAP, procedures. The Principal Director, DPCAP, will
L0:promptly evaluate the procuring contracting officer’s notification package.
L1:(i) If the Principal Director, DPCAP, disagrees with the recommendation of the
L0:procuring contracting officer, the Principal Director, DPCAP, will notify the procuring
L0:contracting officer through the same agency channels that were used for submission of
L0:the notification.
L1:(ii) If the Principal Director, DPCAP, agrees with the recommendation of the

L1:(B) When there is not an adverse effect on national security, but the levy will

title: 236.202-371 Statutory Fee Limitation
content:
L0:236.202-371 Statutory Fee Limitation
L1:(a) The statutes at 10 U.S.C. 7540, 8612, and 9540, for the Departments of the
L0:Army, Navy, and Air Force, respectively, limit the contract price (or fee) for
L0:architect-engineer services for the preparation of designs, plans, drawings, and
L0:specifications to 10 percent of the project's estimated construction cost. (See PGI
L0:236.202-371).
L1:(b) The 10 percent limit also applies to contract modifications, including
L0:modifications involving—
L1:(1) Work not initially included in the contract; apply the 10 percent limit to the
L0:revised total estimated construction cost; and
L1:(2) Redesign work; apply the 10 percent limit by—
L1:(i) Adding the estimated construction cost of the redesign features to he
L0:original estimated construction cost;
L1:(ii) Adding the contract cost for the original design to the contract cost for
L0:redesign; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 36
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 236
L1:(iii) Dividing the total contract design cost by the total estimated
L0:construction cost. The resulting percentage may not exceed the 10 percent statutory
L0:limitation.
L1:(c) The 10 percent limit applies only to that portion of the contract (or modification)
L0:price attributable to the preparation of designs, plans, drawings, and specifications. If a
L0:contract or modification also includes other services, the part of the price attributable to
L0:the other services is not subject to the 10 percent limit.

content:

L0:AIRFIELD SAFETY PRECAUTIONS (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) “Landing areas” means—
L1:(i) The primary surfaces, comprising the surface of the runway, runway
L0:shoulders, and lateral safety zones. The length of each primary surface is the same as
L0:the runway length. The width of each primary surface is 2,000 feet (1,000 feet on each
L0:side of the runway centerline);
L1:(ii) The “clear zone” beyond the ends of each runway, i.e., the extension of
L0:the primary surface for a distance of 1,000 feet beyond each end of each runway;
L1:(iii) All taxiways, plus the lateral clearance zones along each side for the
L0:length of the taxiways (the outer edge of each lateral clearance zone is laterally 250 feet
L0:from the far or opposite edge of the taxiway, e.g., a 75-foot-wide taxiway would have a
L0:combined width of taxiway and lateral clearance zones of 425 feet); and
L1:(iv) All aircraft parking aprons, plus the area 125 feet in width extending
L0:beyond each edge all around the aprons.
L1:(2) “Safety precaution areas” means those portions of approach-departure
L0:clearance zones and transitional zones where placement of objects incident to contract
L0:performance might result in vertical projections at or above the approach-departure
L0:clearance, or the transitional surface.
L1:(i) The “approach-departure clearance surface” is an extension of the
L0:primary surface and the clear zone at each end of each runway, for a distance of 50,000
L0:feet, first along an inclined (glide angle) and then along a horizontal plane, both flaring
L0:symmetrically about the runway centerline extended.
L1:(A) The inclined plane (glide angle) begins in the clear zone 200 feet
L0:past the end of the runway (and primary surface) at the same elevation as the end of
L0:the runway. It continues upward at a slope of 50:1 (1 foot vertically for each 50 feet
L0:horizontally) to an elevation of 500 feet above the established airfield elevation. At that
L0:point the plane becomes horizontal, continuing at that same uniform elevation to a
L0:point 50,000 feet longitudinally from the beginning of the inclined plane (glide angle)
L0:and ending there.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 36
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 236
L1:(B) The width of the surface at the beginning of the inclined plane (glide
L0:angle) is the same as the width of the clear zone. It then flares uniformly, reaching the
L0:maximum width of 16,000 feet at the end.
L1:(ii) The “approach-departure clearance zone” is the ground area under the
L0:approach-departure clearance surface.
L1:(iii) The “transitional surface” is a sideways extension of all primary
L0:surfaces, clear zones, and approach-departure clearance surfaces along inclined planes.

L0:at all times and, specifically, free from small stones which might damage aircraft
L0:propellers or jet aircraft;
L1:(5) Operate mobile equipment according to the safety provisions of this clause,
L0:while actually performing work on the airfield. At all other times, the Contractor shall
L0:remove all mobile equipment to locations—
L1:(i) Approved by the Contracting Officer;
L1:(ii) At a distance of at least 750 feet from the runway centerline, plus any
L0:additional distance; and
L1:(iii) Necessary to ensure compliance with the other provisions of this clause;
L0:and

title: 252.236-7007 Additive or Deductive Items
content:
L0:252.236-7007 Additive or Deductive Items.
L0:As prescribed in 236.101-71(b)(5), use the following provision:
L0:ADDITIVE OR DEDUCTIVE ITEMS (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The low offeror and the items to be awarded shall be determined as follows—
L1:(1) Prior to the opening of bids, the Government will determine the amount of
L0:funds available for the project.
L1:(2) The low offeror shall be the Offeror that—
L1:(i) Is otherwise eligible for award; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 36
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 236
L1:(ii) Offers the lowest aggregate amount for the first or base bid item, plus or
L0:minus (in the order stated in the list of priorities in the bid schedule) those additive or
L0:deductive items that provide the most features within the funds determined available.
L1:(3) The Contracting Officer shall evaluate all bids on the basis of the same
L0:additive or deductive items.
L1:(i) If adding another item from the bid schedule list of priorities would make
L0:the award exceed the available funds for all offerors, the Contracting Officer will skip
L0:that item and go to the next item from the bid schedule of priorities; and
L1:(ii) Add that next item if an award may be made that includes that item and
L0:is within the available funds.
L1:(b) The Contracting Officer will use the list of priorities in the bid schedule only to
L0:determine the low offeror. After determining the low offeror, an award may be made on
L0:any combination of items if—
L1:(1) It is in the best interest of the Government;
L1:(2) Funds are available at the time of award; and
L1:(3) The low offeror's price for the combination to be awarded is less than the
L0:price offered by any other responsive, responsible offeror.
L1:(c) Example. The amount available is $100,000. Offeror A's base bid and four
L0:additives (in the order stated in the list of priorities in the bid Schedule) are $85,000,
L0:$10,000, $8,000, $6,000, and $4,000. Offeror B's base bid and four additives are
L0:$80,000, $16,000, $9,000, $7,000, and $4,000. Offeror A is the low offeror. The
L0:aggregate amount of offeror A's bid for purposes of award would be $99,000, which
L0:includes a base bid plus the first and fourth additives. The second and third additives
L0:were skipped because each of them would cause the aggregate bid to exceed $100,000.

content:

title: 237.873-1 Scope
content:
L0:237.873-1 Scope.
L0:This section implements policies prohibiting interrogation of detainees by contractor
L0:personnel, as required by Section 1038 of Pub. L. 111-84.

title: 237.873-2 Definitions
content:
L0:237.873-2 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section-
L0:“Detainee” means any person captured, detained, held, or otherwise under the
L0:hostilities. This includes, but is not limited to, enemy prisoners of war, civilian
L0:internees, and retained personnel. This does not include DoD personnel or DoD
L0:contractor personnel being held for law enforcement purposes.
L0:“Interrogation of detainees” means a systematic process of formally and officially
L0:questioning a detainee for the purpose of obtaining reliable information to satisfy
L0:foreign intelligence collection requirements.

title: 237.873-3 Policy
content:
L0:237.873-3 Policy.
L1:(a) No detainee may be interrogated by contractor personnel.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
L1:(b) Contractor personnel with proper training and security clearances may be
L0:used as linguists, interpreters, report writers, information technology technicians,
L0:and other employees filling ancillary positions, including as trainers of and advisors
L0:to interrogators, in interrogations of detainees if—
L1:(1) Such personnel are subject to the same laws, rules, procedures, and
L0:policies pertaining to detainee operations and interrogations as those that apply to
L0:Government personnel in such positions in such interrogations; and
L1:(2) Appropriately qualified and trained DoD personnel (military or civilian)
L0:are available to oversee the contractor’s performance and to ensure that contractor
L0:personnel do not perform activities that are prohibited under this section.
L1:(3) See PGI 237.873-3 for a listing of applicable DoD policies pertaining to
L0:detainee operations and interrogations.

content:

L0:to this paragraph for an additional 30-day period, if the Secretary determines that
L0:such a renewal is vital to the national security interests of the United States. Not
L0:later than five days after issuance of the waiver, the Secretary shall submit written
L0:notification to Congress. See specific waiver procedures at DoDI 1100.22.

L0:tuition under the off-duty educational program.
L1:(b) As used in the subpart—
L1:(1) “Facilities” does not include the institution's dining rooms or dormitories;
L0:and
L1:(2) “Fees” does not include charges for meals or lodging.

title: 237.7201 Educational service agreement
content:
L0:237.7201 Educational service agreement.
L1:(a) An educational service agreement is not a contract but is an ordering agreement
L0:under which the Government may order educational services.
L1:(b) Educational service agreements provide for ordering educational services
L0:when—
L1:(1) The Government pays normal tuition and fees for educational services
L0:provided to a student by the institution under its normal schedule of tuition and fees
L0:applicable to all students generally; and
L1:(2) Enrollment is at the institution under the institution's normal rules and in
L0:courses and curricula which the institution offers to all students meeting admission
L0:requirements.

title: 237.7202 Limitations
content:
L0:237.7202 Limitations.
L0:Educational service agreements are not used to provide special courses or special fees
L0:for Government students.

title: 237.7203 Duration
content:
L0:237.7203 Duration.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
L1:(a) Educational service agreements are for an indefinite duration and remain in
L0:effect until terminated.
L1:(b) The issuing activity must establish procedures to review each educational
L0:service agreement at least once each year. Review dates should consider the
L0:institution's academic calendar and occur at least 30 days before the beginning of a
L0:term. The purpose of the review is to incorporate changes to reflect requirements of any
L0:statute, Executive Order, FAR, or DFARS.
L1:(c) If the contracting officer and the institution do not agree on required changes,
L0:terminate the agreement.

title: 237.7300 Scope
content:
L0:237.7300 Scope.
L0:This subpart implements acquisition of temporary or intermittent services of students

L0:development laboratories (10 U.S.C. 4143).
subpart: SUBPART 237.73 — -SERVICES OF STUDENTS AT RESEARCH AND

title: 237.7301 Definitions
content:
L0:237.7301 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L1:(a) “Institution of higher learning” means any public or private post-secondary
L0:school, junior college, college, university, or other degree granting educational
L0:institution that—
L1:(1) Is located in the United States or its outlying areas;
L1:(2) Has an accredited education program approved by an appropriate
L0:accrediting body; and
L1:(3) Offers a program of study at any level beyond high school.
L1:(b) “Student” means an individual enrolled (or accepted for enrollment) at an
L0:institution of higher learning before the term of the student technical support contract.
L0:The individual must remain in good standing in a curriculum designed to lead to the
L0:granting of a recognized degree, during the term of the contract.
L1:(c) “Technical support” means any scientific or engineering work in support of the
L0:mission of the DoD laboratory involved. It does not include administrative or clerical
L0:services.
subpart: SUBPART 237.73 — -SERVICES OF STUDENTS AT RESEARCH AND

title: 237.7302 Policy
content:
L0:237.7302 Policy.
L0:Acquisition of services of students at institutions of higher learning is generally by
L0:contract between a nonprofit organization employing the student and the Government.

L0:students. These services are not subject to the requirements of FAR Part 19, FAR
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
L0:13.102, or DFARS part 219. Award authority for these contracts is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)
L0:and 10 U.S.C. 4143.

title: 237.7400 Scope
content:
L0:237.7400 Scope.

L0:open competition, with local governments for police, fire protection, airfield operation, or
L0:other community services at military installations to be closed under the Defense
L0:Authorization Amendments and Base Closure and Realignment Act (Pub. L. 100-526),
L0:as amended, and the Defense Base Closure and Realignment Act of 1990 (Pub. L. 101-
L0:510), as amended.

title: 237.7401 Policy
content:
L0:237.7401 Policy.
L0:The authority in 206.103-5(c)(ii) to contract with local governments—
L1:(a) May be exercised without regard to the provisions of 10 U.S.C. Chapter 146,
L0:Contracting for Performance of Civilian Commercial or Industrial Type Functions;
L1:(b) May not be exercised earlier than 180 days before the date the installation is
L0:scheduled to be closed;

L0:being acquired under contract with the local government are in the best interests of the
L0:DoD.

title: 237.7600 Scope
content:
L0:237.7600 Scope.
L0:This subpart prescribes procedures for the acquisition of essential contractor
L0:services which support mission-essential functions.

title: 237.7601 Definitions
content:
L0:237.7601 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Essential contractor service” and “mission-essential functions” are defined in the
L0:clause at 252.237-7023, Continuation of Essential Contractor Services.

title: 237.7602 Policy
content:
L0:237.7602 Policy.
L1:(a) Contractors providing services designated as essential contractor services
L0:must permit continuation of such services during periods of crisis in accordance
L0:with the terms and conditions of their contracts. Generally, only specifically
L0:designated service functions, identified by the functional commander or civilian
L0:equivalent, are considered mission-essential functions, not the entire contract.
L1:(b) For Government-determined essential contractor services, the contractor
L0:shall provide a mission-essential contractor services plan to be incorporated in the
L0:contract. The contracting officer, with input from the functional manager, will
L0:assess the sufficiency of the contractor-provided plan. During a crisis, plan
L0:activation requires contracting officer authorization at the direction of the
L0:appropriate functional commander or civilian equivalent.
L1:(c) Follow the procedures at PGI 207for preparing acquisition plans.

L0:essential functions.

L0:Contractor Services in all solicitations for services that include the clause 252.237-7023.

title: 237.7800 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:237.7800 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart implements 10 U.S.C. 2387, which requires, under certain

L0:Force, 341st Training Squadron, for veterinary screening and care (10 U.S.C. 2583).

title: 237.7801 Definition
content:
L0:237.7801 Definition.
L0:As used in this subpart—

L1:(1) Performs a service for DoD pursuant to a contract; and
L1:(2) Is trained and kenneled by an entity that provides such a dog pursuant to
L0:such a contract.
subpart: SUBPART 237.78 — TRANSFER AND ADOPTION OF MILITARY ANIMALS

title: 237.7802 Policy
content:
L0:237.7802 Policy.
L1:(a) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2387, DoD will transfer a contract working dog
L0:to the Department of the Air Force, 341st Training Squadron, for veterinary
L0:screening and care after the service life of the dog has terminated.
L1:(b) The service life of a contract working dog may be terminated if—
L1:(1) The final contractual obligation of the dog preceding transfer is with
L0:DoD; and
L1:(2) The dog cannot be used by another department or agency of the Federal
L0:Government due to age, injury, or performance.
L1:(c) A contract working dog that has reached the end of its service life will be
L0:transferred for care, reclassification as a military animal, and placement for
L0:adoption (10 U.S.C. 2583).
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237

title: 252.237-7998 Training for Contractor Personnel Interacting with Detainees
content:
L0:252.237-7998 Training for Contractor Personnel Interacting with Detainees.
L0:As prescribed in 237.871-4, insert the following clause:
L0:TRAINING FOR CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL INTERACTING WITH DETAINEES
L0:(DEVIATION 2026-O0023) (FEB 2026)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Combatant Commander” means the commander of a unified or specified
L0:combatant command established in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 161.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
L0:“Detainee” means a person in the custody or under the physical control of the
L0:Department of Defense on behalf of the United States Government as a result of armed
L0:conflict or other military operation by United States armed forces.
L0:“Personnel interacting with detainees” means personnel who, in the course of
L0:their duties, are expected to interact with detainees.
L1:(b) Training requirement. This clause implements Section 1092 of the National
L0:Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2005 (Pub. L. 108-375).
L1:(1) The Combatant Commander responsible for the area where a detention or
L0:interrogation facility is located will arrange for training to be provided to contractor
L0:personnel interacting with detainees. The training will address the international
L0:obligations and laws of the United States applicable to the detention of personnel,
L0:including the Geneva Conventions. The Combatant Commander will arrange for a
L0:training receipt document to be provided to personnel who have completed the training.
L2:(2)(i) The Contractor shall arrange for its personnel interacting with detainees
L0:to—
L1:(A) Receive the training specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this clause—
L1:(1) Prior to interacting with detainees, or as soon as possible if, for
L0:compelling reasons, the Contracting Officer authorizes interaction with detainees prior
L0:to receipt of such training; and
L1:(2) Annually thereafter; and
L1:(B) Provide a copy of the training receipt document specified in paragraph
L2:(b)(1) of this clause to the Contractor for retention.
L1:(ii) To make these arrangements, the following points of contact apply:
L0:[Contracting Officer to insert applicable contact information cited in PGI 237.871-3(b).]
L1:(3) The Contractor shall retain a copy of the training receipt document(s)
L0:provided in accordance with paragraphs (b)(1) and (2) of this clause until the contract is
L0:closed, or 3 years after all work required by the contract has been completed and
L0:accepted by the Government, whichever is sooner.
L1:(c) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause,
L0:including this paragraph (c), in all subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial
L0:services, that may require subcontractor personnel to interact with detainees in the
L0:course of their duties.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
citation: R-DFARS 252.237-7998 — Training for Contractor Personnel Interacting with Detainees

title: 252.237-7004 Area of Performance
content:
L0:252.237-7004 Area of Performance.
L0:As prescribed in 237.7003(a) and (a)(2), insert the following clause:
L0:AREA OF PERFORMANCE (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The area of performance is as specified in the contract.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall take possession of the remains at the place where they are
L0:located, transport them to the Contractor's place of preparation, and later transport
L0:them to a place designated by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(c) The Contractor will not be reimbursed for transportation when both the place
L0:where the remains were located, and the delivery point are within the area of
L0:performance.
L1:(d) If remains are located outside the area of performance, the Contracting Officer
L0:may place an order with the Contractor under this contract or may obtain the services
L0:elsewhere. If the Contracting Officer requires the Contractor to transport the remains
L0:into the area of performance, the Contractor shall be paid the amount per mile in the
L0:schedule for the number of miles required to transport the remains by a reasonable
L0:route from the point where located to the boundary of the area of performance.
L1:(e) The Contracting Officer may require the Contractor to deliver remains to any
L0:point within 100 miles of the area of performance. In this case, the Contractor shall be
L0:paid the amount per mile in the schedule for the number of miles required to transport
L0:the remains by a reasonable route from the boundary of the area of performance to the
L0:delivery point.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7010 Prohibition on Interrogation of Detainees by Contractor
content:
L0:252.237-7010 Prohibition on Interrogation of Detainees by Contractor
L0:Personnel.
L0:As prescribed in 237.873-5, insert the following clause:
L0:PROHIBITION ON INTERROGATION OF DETAINEES BY CONTRACTOR
L0:PERSONNEL (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Detainee” means any person captured, detained, held, or otherwise under the
L0:hostilities. This includes, but is not limited to, enemy prisoners of war, civilian
L0:internees, and retained personnel. This does not include DoD personnel or DoD
L0:contractor personnel being held for law enforcement purposes.
L0:“Interrogation of detainees” means a systematic process of formally and officially
L0:questioning a detainee for the purpose of obtaining reliable information to satisfy
L0:foreign intelligence collection requirements.

L0:including this paragraph (c), in all subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial

title: 252.237-7023 Continuation of Essential Contractor Services
content:
L0:252.237-7023 Continuation of Essential Contractor Services.
L0:As prescribed in 237.7603(a), use the following clause:
L0:CONTINUATION OF ESSENTIAL CONTRACTOR SERVICES (OCT 2010)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause-
L1:(1) “Essential contractor service” means a service provided by a firm or
L0:individual under contract to DoD to support mission-essential functions, such as
L0:support of vital systems, including ships owned, leased, or operated in support of
L0:military missions or roles at sea; associated support activities, including installation,
L0:garrison, and base support services; and similar services provided to foreign military
L0:sales customers under the Security Assistance Program. Services are essential if the
L0:effectiveness of defense systems or operations has the potential to be seriously impaired
L0:by the interruption of these services, as determined by the appropriate functional
L0:commander or civilian equivalent.
L1:(2) “Mission-essential functions” means those organizational activities that
L0:must be performed under all circumstances to achieve DoD component missions or
L0:responsibilities, as determined by the appropriate functional commander or civilian
L0:equivalent. Failure to perform or sustain these functions would significantly affect
L0:DoD’s ability to provide vital services or exercise authority, direction, and control.
L1:(b) The Government has identified all or a portion of the contractor services
L0:performed under this contract as essential contractor services in support of mission
L0:essential functions. These services are listed in attachment __, Mission-Essential
L0:Contractor Services, dated __________.
L2:(c)(1) The Mission-Essential Contractor Services Plan submitted by the
L0:Contractor, is incorporated in this contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall maintain and update its plan as necessary. The
L0:Contractor shall provide all plan updates to the Contracting Officer for approval.
L1:(3) As directed by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall participate
L0:in training events, exercises, and drills associated with Government efforts to test
L0:the effectiveness of continuity of operations procedures and practices.
L2:(d)(1) Notwithstanding any other clause of this contract, the contractor shall be
L0:responsible to perform those services identified as essential contractor services
L0:during crisis situations (as directed by the Contracting Officer), in accordance with
L0:its Mission-Essential Contractor Services Plan.
L1:(2) In the event the Contractor anticipates not being able to perform any of
L0:the essential contractor services identified in accordance with paragraph (b) of this
L0:section during a crisis situation, the Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer
L0:or other designated representative as expeditiously as possible and use its best
L0:efforts to cooperate with the Government in the Government’s efforts to maintain
L0:the continuity of operations.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
L1:(e) The Government reserves the right in such crisis situations to use Federal
L0:employees, military personnel or contract support from other contractors, or to
L0:enter into new contracts for essential contractor services.
L1:(f) Changes. The Contractor shall segregate and separately identify all costs
L0:incurred in continuing performance of essential services in a crisis situation. The
L0:Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer of an increase or decrease in costs
L0:within ninety days after continued performance has been directed by the
L0:Contracting Officer, or within any additional period that the Contracting Officer
L0:approves in writing, but not later than the date of final payment under the contract.
L0:The Contractor’s notice shall include the Contractor’s proposal for an equitable
L0:adjustment and any data supporting the increase or decrease in the form prescribed
L0:by the Contracting Officer. The parties shall negotiate an equitable price
L0:adjustment to the contract price, delivery schedule, or both as soon as is practicable
L0:after receipt of the Contractor’s proposal.
L1:(g) The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, including this
L0:paragraph (g), in subcontracts for the essential services.
L0:(End of Clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.237-7023 — Continuation of Essential Contractor Services

L0:To comply with the certification requirement at DFARS 237.876, complete a

L0:contract file:
L0:Certification of Nonpersonal Services
L0:This certification and enclosed worksheet are designed to ensure that the agency
L0:does not award a personal-services contract unless specifically authorized by statute
L0:(e.g., 10 U.S.C. 129b, 5 U.S.C. 3109, or 10 U.S.C. 1091). Therefore, this
L0:documentation should be completed in conjunction with the submission of a service-
L0:contract requirement to the contracting officer.
L0:A personal services contract is characterized by the employer-employee
L0:relationship it creates between the Government and the contractor’s personnel. The
L0:Government is normally required to obtain its employees by direct hire under
L0:competitive appointment procedures required by civil service laws. Obtaining
L0:personal services by contract, rather than by direct hire, circumvents those laws
L0:unless Congress has specifically authorized acquisition of the services by contract.
L0:An employer-employee relationship under a service contract occurs when the
L0:Government exercises relatively continuous supervision and control over contractor
L0:personnel performing the contract.

L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
