L0:PGI 237.7204 Format and clauses for educational service agreements.
L0:Educational service agreements under this subpart must be in the following format. Add to
L0:the schedule any other provisions necessary to describe the requirements, if they are
L0:consistent with the following provisions and the policy of acquiring educational services in
L0:the form of standard course offerings at the prevailing rates of the institution:
L0:EDUCATIONAL SERVICE AGREEMENT
L0:Agreement No. ______________
L0:1. This agreement entered into on the __________ day of ______________ _____, is
L0:between the Government, represented by the Contracting Officer, and the Contractor,
L0:_________(name of institution)________________, an educational institution located in
L0:_________(city)_________, ____(state)__________.
L0:2. This agreement is for educational services to be provided by the Contractor to
L0:Government personnel at the Contractor's institution. The Contractor shall provide
L0:instruction with standard offerings of courses available to the public.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
L0:3. The Government will pay for services under the Contractor's normal schedule of
L0:tuition and fees applicable to the public and in effect at the time the services are performed.
L0:4. The Government will review this agreement annually before the anniversary of its
L0:orders, the Federal Acquisition Regulation, or the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation
L0:Supplement. Changes required to be made by modification to this agreement or by
L0:issuance of a superseding agreement. If mutual agreement on the changes cannot be
L0:reached, the Government will terminate this agreement.
L0:5. The parties may amend this agreement only by mutual consent.
L0:6. This agreement shall start on the date in paragraph 1 and shall continue until
L0:terminated.
L0:7. The estimated annual cost of this agreement is $_________. This estimate is for
L0:administrative purposes only and does not impose any obligation on the Government to
L0:request any services or make any payment.
L0:8. Advance payments are authorized by 10 U.S.C. 2396(a)(3).
L0:9. Submit invoices to: ____________(name and address of activity)______________.
L0:1. Ordering procedures and services to be provided.
L0:SCHEDULE PROVISIONS
L1:(a) The Contractor shall promptly deliver to the Contracting Officer one copy of each
L0:catalog applicable to this agreement, and one copy of any subsequent revision.
L1:(b) The Government will request educational services under this agreement by a
L0:(insert type of request, such as, delivery order, official Government order, or other written
L0:communication). The (insert type of request, such as, delivery order, official Government
L0:order, or other written communication) will contain the number of this agreement and will
L0:designate as students at the Contractor's institution one or more Government-selected
L0:persons who have already been accepted for admission under the Contractor's usual
L0:admission standards.
L1:(c) All students under this agreement shall register in the same manner, be subject
L0:to the same academic regulations, and have the same privileges, including the use of all
L0:facilities and equipment as any other students enrolled in the institution.
L1:(d) Upon enrolling each student under this agreement, the Contractor shall, where
L0:the resident or nonresident status involves a difference in tuition or fees—
L1:(i) Determine the resident or nonresident status of the student;
L1:(ii) Notify the student and the Contracting Officer of the determination. If there is
L0:an appeal of the determination;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
L1:(iii) If there is an appeal of the determination, process the appeal under the
L0:Contractor's standard procedures;
L1:(iv) Notify the student and Contracting Officer of the result; and
L1:(v) Make the determination a part of the student's permanent record.
L1:(e) The Contractor shall not furnish any instruction or other services to any student
L0:under this agreement before the effective date of a request for services in the form specified
L0:in paragraph (b) of this schedule.
L0:2. Change in curriculum. The Contracting Officer may vary the curriculum for any
L0:student enrolled under this agreement but shall not require or make any change in any
L0:course without the Contractor's consent.
L0:3. Payment.
L1:(a) The Government will pay the Contractor the normal tuition and fees which the
L0:Contractor charges any students pursuing the same or similar curricula, except for any
L0:tuition and fees which this agreement excludes. The Contractor may change any tuition and
L0:fees, provided—
L1:(1) The Contractor publishes the revisions in a catalog or otherwise publicly
L0:announces the revisions;
L1:(2) Applies the revisions uniformly to all students studying the same or similar
L0:curricula;
L0:date.
L1:(3) Provides the Contracting Officer notice of changes before their effective
L1:(b) The Contractor shall not establish any tuition or fees which apply solely to
L0:students under this agreement.
L1:(c) If the Contractor regularly charges higher tuition and fees for nonresident
L0:students, the Contractor may charge the Government the normal nonresident tuition and
L0:fees for students under this agreement who are nonresidents. The Government shall not
L0:claim resident tuition and fees for any student solely on the basis of the student residing in
L0:the State as a consequence of enrollment under this agreement.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall charge the Government only the tuition and fees which
L0:relate directly to enrollment as a student. Tuition and fees may include—
L1:(i) Penalty fees for late registration or change of course caused by the
L0:Government;
L1:(ii) Mandatory health fees and health insurance charges; and
L1:(iii) Any flat rate charge applicable to all students registered for research that
L0:appears in the Contractor's publicly announced fee schedule.
L1:(e) The Contractor shall not charge the Government for—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
L1:(i) Permit charges, such as vehicle registration or parking fees, unless
L0:specifically authorized in the request for service; and
L1:(ii) Any equipment, refundable deposits, or any items or services (such as
L0:computer time) related to student research.
L1:(f) Normally, the Contractor shall not directly charge individual students for
L0:application fees or any other fee chargeable to this agreement. However, if the Contractor's
L0:standard procedures require payment of any fee before the student is enrolled under this
L0:agreement, the Contractor may charge the student. When the Contractor receives payment
L0:from the Government, the Contractor shall fully reimburse the student.
L1:(g) For each term the Contractor enrolls students under this agreement, the
L0:Contractor shall submit _______ copies of an invoice listing charges for each student
L0:separately. The Contractor shall submit invoices within ______ days after the start of the
L0:term and shall include—
L1:(i) Agreement number and inclusive dates of the term;
L1:(ii) Name of each student;
L1:(iii) A list showing each course for each student if the school charges by credit
L0:hour;
L1:(iv) The resident or nonresident status of each student (if applicable to the
L0:Contractor's school); and
L1:(v) A breakdown of charges for each student, including credit hours, tuition,
L0:application fee, and other fees. Provide a total for each student and a grand total for all
L0:students listed on the invoice.
L1:(h) If unforeseen events require additional charges that are otherwise payable
L0:under the Contractor's normal tuition and fee schedule, the Contractor may submit a
L0:supplemental invoice or make the adjustment on the next regular invoice under this
L0:agreement. The Contractor shall clearly identify and explain the supplemental invoice or the
L0:adjustment.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall apply any credits resulting from withdrawal of students, or
L0:from any other cause under its standard procedures, to subsequent invoices submitted
L0:under this agreement. Credits should appear on the first invoice submitted after the action
L0:resulting in the credits. If no subsequent invoice is submitted, the Contractor shall deliver to
L0:the Contracting Officer a check drawn to the order of the office designated for contract
L0:administration. The Contractor shall identify the reason for the credit and the applicable
L0:term dates in all cases.
L0:4. Withdrawal of students.
L1:(a) The Government may, at its option and at any time, withdraw financial support
L0:for any student by issuing official orders. The Government will furnish ______ copies of the
L0:orders to the Contractor within a reasonable time after publication.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 37
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 237
L1:(b) The Contractor may request withdrawal by the Government of any student for
L0:academic or disciplinary reasons.
L1:(c) If withdrawal occurs before the end of a term, the Government will pay any
L0:tuition and fees due for the current term. The Contractor shall credit the Government with
L0:any charges eligible for refund under the Contractor's standard procedures for any students
L0:in effect on the date of withdrawal.
L1:(d) Withdrawal of students by the Government will not be the basis for any special
L0:charge or claim by the Contractor other than charges under the Contractor's standard
L0:procedures.
L0:5. Transcripts. Within a reasonable time after withdrawal of a student for any reason, or
L0:after graduation, the Contractor shall send to the Contracting Officer (or to an address
L0:supplied by the Contracting Officer) one copy of an official transcript showing all work by the
L0:student at the institution until such withdrawal or graduation.
L0:6. Student teaching. The Government does not anticipate the Contractor awarding
L0:fellowships and assistantships to students attending school under this agreement. However,
L0:for graduate students, should both the student and the Contractor decide it to be in the
L0:student's best interests to assist in the institution's teaching program, the Contractor may
L0:provide nominal compensation for part-time service. Base the compensation on the
L0:Contractor's practices and procedures for other students of similar accomplishment in that
L0:department or field. The Contractor shall apply the compensation as a credit against any
L0:invoices presented for payment for any period in which the student performed the part-time
L0:teaching service.
L0:7. Termination of agreement.
L1:(a) Either party may terminate this agreement by giving 30 days advance written
L0:notice of the effective date of termination. In the event of termination, the Government shall
L0:have the right, at its option, to continue to receive educational services for those students
L0:already enrolled in the contractor's institution under this agreement until such time that the
L0:students complete their courses or curricula or the Government withdraws them from the
L0:Contractor's institution. The terms and conditions of this agreement in effect on the effective
L0:date of the termination shall continue to apply to such students remaining in the Contractor's
L0:institution.
L1:(b) Withdrawal of students under Schedule provision 4 shall not be considered a
L0:termination within the meaning of this provision 7.
L1:(c) Termination by either party shall not be the basis for any special charge or claim
L0:by the Contractor, other than as provided by the Contractor's standard procedures.

title: 239.7400 Scope
content:
L0:239.7400 Scope.
L0:This subpart prescribes policy and procedures for acquisition of telecommunications
L0:services and maintenance of telecommunications security. Telecommunications
L0:services meet the definition of information technology.

title: 239.7401 Definitions
content:
L0:239.7401 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L0:Common carrier means any entity engaged in the business of providing
L0:telecommunications services which are regulated by the Federal Communications
L0:Commission or other governmental body.
L0:Foreign carrier means any person, partnership, association, joint-stock company,
L0:trust, governmental body, or corporation not subject to regulation by a U.S.
L0:governmental regulatory body and not doing business as a citizen of the United
L0:States, providing telecommunications services outside the territorial limits of the
L0:United States.
L0:Governmental regulatory body means the Federal Communications Commission,
L0:any statewide regulatory body, or any body with less than statewide jurisdiction
L0:when operating under the State authority. The following are not “governmental
L0:regulatory bodies”—
L1:(1) Regulatory bodies whose decisions are not subject to judicial appeal; and
L1:(2) Regulatory bodies which regulate a company owned by the same entity
L0:which creates the regulatory body.
L0:Long-haul telecommunications means all general and special purpose long-
L0:distance telecommunications facilities and services (including commercial satellite
L0:services, terminal equipment and local circuitry supporting the long-haul service) to
L0:or from the post, camp, base, or station switch and/or main distribution frame
L0:(except for trunk lines to the first-serving commercial central office for local
L0:communications services).
L0:Noncommon carrier means any entity other than a common carrier offering
L0:telecommunications facilities, services, or equipment for lease.
L0:Securing, sensitive information, and telecommunications systems have the
L0:meaning given in the clause at 252.239-7016, Telecommunications Security
L0:Equipment, Devices, Techniques, and Services.
L0:Telecommunications means the transmission, emission, or reception of signals,
L0:signs, writing, images, sounds, or intelligence of any nature, by wire, cable,
L0:satellite, fiber optics, laser, radio, or any other electronic, electric, electromagnetic,
L0:or acoustically coupled means.
L0:Telecommunications services means the services acquired, whether by lease or
L0:contract, to meet the Government's telecommunications needs. The term includes
L0:the telecommunications facilities and equipment necessary to provide such services.

title: 239.7402 Policy
content:
L0:239.7402 Policy.
L1:(a) Acquisition. DoD policy is to acquire telecommunications services from
L0:common and noncommon telecommunications carriers—
L1:(1) On a competitive basis, except when acquisition using other than full
L0:and open competition is justified;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L1:(2) Recognizing the regulations, practices, and decisions of the Federal
L0:Communications Commission (FCC) and other governmental regulatory bodies on
L0:rates, cost principles, and accounting practices; and
L1:(3) Making provision in telecommunications services contracts for adoption
L0:of—
L1:(i) FCC approved practices; or
L1:(ii) The generally accepted practices of the industry on those issues
L0:concerning common carrier services where—
L1:(A) The governmental regulatory body has not expressed itself;
L1:(B) The governmental regulatory body has declined jurisdiction; or
L1:(C) There is no governmental regulatory body to decide.
L1:(b) Security. (1) The contracting officer must ensure, in accordance with agency
L0:procedures, that purchase requests identify—
L1:(i) The nature and extent of information requiring security during
L0:telecommunications;
L1:(ii) The requirement for the contractor to secure telecommunications
L0:systems;
L1:(iii) The telecommunications security equipment, devices, techniques, or
L0:services with which the contractor's telecommunications security equipment,
L0:devices, techniques, or services must be interoperable; and
L1:(iv) The approved telecommunications security equipment, devices,
L0:techniques, or services, such as found in the National Security Agency's Information
L0:Systems Security Products and Services Catalogue.
L1:(2) Contractors and subcontractors must provide all telecommunications
L0:security techniques or services required for performance of Government contracts.

title: 239.7408 Special construction
content: L0:239.7408 Special construction.

title: 239.7408-1 General
content:
L0:239.7408-1 General.
L1:(a) Special construction normally involves a common carrier giving a special
L0:service or facility related to the performance of the basic telecommunications service
L0:requirements. This may include—
L1:(1) Moving or relocating equipment;
L1:(2) Providing temporary facilities;
L1:(3) Expediting provision of facilities; or
L1:(4) Providing specially constructed channel facilities to meet Government
L0:requirements.
L1:(b) Use this subpart instead of FAR part 36 for acquisition of “special
L0:construction.”
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L1:(c) Special construction costs may be—
L1:(1) A contingent liability for using telecommunications services for a shorter
L0:time than the minimum to reimburse the contractor for unamortized
L0:nonrecoverable costs. These costs are usually expressed in terms of a termination
L0:liability, as provided in the contract or by tariff;
L1:(2) A onetime special construction charge;
L1:(3) Recurring charges for constructed facilities;
L1:(4) A minimum service charge;
L1:(5) An expediting charge; or
L1:(6) A move or relocation charge.
L1:(d) When a common carrier submits a proposal or quotation which has special
L0:construction requirements, the contracting officer must require a detailed special
L0:construction proposal. Analyze all special construction proposals to—
L1:(1) Determine the adequacy of the proposed construction;
L1:(2) Disclose excessive or duplicative construction; and
L1:(3) When different forms of charge are possible, provide for the form of
L0:charge most advantageous to the Government.
L1:(e) When possible, analyze and approve special construction charges before
L0:receiving the service. Impose a ceiling on the special construction costs before
L0:authorizing the contractor to proceed, if prior approval is not possible. The
L0:contracting officer must approve special construction charges before final payment.

title: 239.7600 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:239.7600 Scope of subpart.
L0:This subpart prescribes policies and procedures for the acquisition of cloud
L0:computing services.

title: 239.7601 Definitions
content:
L0:239.7601 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:Authorizing official, as described in DoD Instruction 8510.01, Risk Management
L0:Framework (RMF) for DoD Information Technology (IT), means the senior Federal
L0:official or executive with the authority to formally assume responsibility for
L0:operating an information system at an acceptable level of risk to organizational
L0:operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational
L0:assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.
L0:Cloud computing means a model for enabling ubiquitous, convenient, on-demand
L0:network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources (e.g., networks,
L0:servers, storage, applications, and services) that can be rapidly provisioned and
L0:released with minimal management effort or service provider interaction. This
L0:includes other commercial terms, such as on-demand self-service, broad network
L0:access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, and measured service. It also includes
L0:commercial offerings for software-as-a-service, infrastructure-as-a-service, and
L0:platform-as-a-service.
L0:Government data means any information, document, media, or machine readable
L0:material regardless of physical form or characteristics, that is created or obtained
L0:by the Government in the course of official Government business.
L0:Government-related data means any information, document, media, or machine
L0:readable material regardless of physical form or characteristics that is created or
L0:obtained by a contractor through the storage, processing, or communication of
L0:Government data. This does not include a contractor's business records (e.g.,
L0:financial records, legal records, etc.) or data such as operating procedures, software
L0:coding, or algorithms that are not uniquely applied to the Government data.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L0:Information system means a discrete set of information resources organized for
L0:the collection, processing, maintenance, use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition
L0:of information.
L0:Media means physical devices or writing surfaces including, but not limited to,
L0:magnetic tapes, optical disks, magnetic disks, large-scale integration memory chips,
L0:and printouts onto which information is recorded, stored, or printed within an
L0:information system.

title: 239.7602 Policy and responsibilities
content: L0:239.7602 Policy and responsibilities.

title: 239.7602-1 General
content:
L0:239.7602-1 General.
L1:(a) Generally, DoD must acquire cloud computing services using commercial
L0:terms and conditions that are consistent with Federal law, and an agency's needs,
L0:including those requirements specified in this subpart. Some examples of
L0:commercial terms and conditions are license agreements, End User License
L0:Agreements (EULAs), Terms of Service (TOS), or other similar legal instruments or
L0:agreements. Contracting officers must incorporate any applicable service provider
L0:terms and conditions into the contract by attachment or other appropriate
L0:mechanism. Contracting officers must carefully review commercial terms and
L0:conditions and consult counsel to ensure these are consistent with Federal law,
L0:regulation, and the agency's needs.
L2:(b)(1) Except as provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, the contracting
L0:officer must only award a contract to acquire cloud computing services from a cloud
L0:service provider (e.g., contractor or subcontractor, regardless of tier) that has been
L0:granted provisional authorization by Defense Information Systems Agency, at the
L0:level appropriate to the requirement, to provide the relevant cloud computing
L0:services in accordance with the Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide
L1:(SRG) (version in effect at the time the solicitation is issued or as authorized by the
L0:contracting officer) found at https://public.cyber.mil/dccs/.
L1:(2) The contracting officer may award a contract to acquire cloud computing
L0:services from a cloud service provider that has not been granted provisional
L0:authorization when—
L1:(i) The requirement for a provisional authorization is waived by the DoD
L0:Chief Information Officer; or
L1:(ii) The cloud computing service requirement is for a private, on-
L0:premises version that will be provided from U.S. Government facilities. Under this
L0:circumstance, the cloud service provider must obtain a provisional authorization
L0:prior to operational use.
L1:(c) When contracting for cloud computing services, the contracting officer must
L0:ensure the following information is provided by the requiring activity:
L1:(1) Government data and Government-related data descriptions.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L1:(2) Data ownership, licensing, delivery and disposition instructions specific
L0:to the relevant types of Government data and Government-related data (e.g., DD
L0:Form 1423, Contract Data Requirements List; work statement task; line item).
L0:Disposition instructions must provide for the transition of data in commercially
L0:available, or open and non-proprietary format (and for permanent records, in
L0:accordance with disposition guidance issued by National Archives and Record
L0:Administration).
L1:(3) Appropriate requirements to support applicable inspection, audit,
L0:investigation, or other similar authorized activities specific to the relevant types of
L0:Government data and Government-related data, or specific to the type of cloud
L0:computing services being acquired.
L1:(4) Appropriate requirements to support and cooperate with applicable
L0:system-wide search and access capabilities for inspections, audits, investigations,
L0:and similar authorized activities.

title: 239.7602-2 Required storage of data within the United States or outlying
content:
L0:239.7602-2 Required storage of data within the United States or outlying
L0:areas.
L1:(a) Cloud computing service providers are required to maintain within the 50
L0:states, the District of Columbia, or outlying areas of the United States, all
L0:Government data that is not physically located on DoD premises, unless otherwise
L0:authorized by the authorizing official, as described in DoD Instruction 8510.01, in
L0:accordance with the SRG.
L1:(b) The contracting officer must provide written notification to the contractor
L0:when the contractor is permitted to maintain Government data at a location outside
L0:the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and outlying areas of the United States. See
L0:PGI 239.7602-2 for additional guidance.
citation: R-DFARS 239.7602-2 — Required storage of data within the United States or outlying

title: 252.239-7002 Access
content:
L0:252.239-7002 Access.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7411(a), use the following clause:
L0:ACCESS (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Subject to military security regulations, the Government shall permit the
L0:Contractor access at all reasonable times to Contractor furnished facilities.
L0:However, if the Government is unable to permit access, the Government at its own

L0:negligence.
L1:(b) During periods when the Government does not permit Contractor access, the

title: 252.239-7004 Orders for Facilities and Services
content:
L0:252.239-7004 Orders for Facilities and Services.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7411(a), use the following clause:
L0:(End of clause)
L0:ORDERS FOR FACILITIES AND SERVICES (SEP 2019)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Governmental regulatory body means the Federal Communications Commission,
L0:any statewide regulatory body, or any body with less than statewide jurisdiction
L0:when operating under the state authority. Regulatory bodies whose decisions are
L0:not subject to judicial appeal and regulatory bodies which regulate a company
L0:owned by the same entity that creates the regulatory body are not governmental
L0:regulatory bodies.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall acknowledge a communication service authorization or
L0:other type order for supplies and facilities by—
L1:(1) Commencing performance after receipt of an order; or
L1:(2) Written acceptance by a duly authorized representative.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall furnish the services and facilities under this
L0:agreement/contract in accordance with all applicable tariffs, rates, charges,
L0:regulations, requirements, terms, and conditions of—
L1:(1) Service and facilities furnished or offered by the Contractor to the
L0:general public or the Contractor's subscribers; or
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L1:(2) Service as lawfully established by a governmental regulatory body.
L1:(d) The Government will not prepay for services.
L1:(e) For nontariffed services, the Contractor shall charge the Government at the
L0:lowest rate and under the most favorable terms and conditions for similar service
L0:and facilities offered to any other customer.
L1:(f) Recurring charges for services and facilities shall, in each case, start with the
L0:satisfactory beginning of service or provision of facilities or equipment and are
L0:payable monthly in arrears.
L1:(g) Expediting charges are costs necessary to get services earlier than normal.
L0:Examples are overtime pay or special shipment. When authorized, expediting
L0:charges shall be the additional costs incurred by the Contractor and the
L0:subcontractor. The Government shall pay expediting charges only when—
L1:(1) They are provided for in the tariff established by a governmental
L0:regulatory body; or
L1:(2) They are authorized in a communication service authorization or other
L0:contractual document.
L1:(h) When services normally provided are technically unacceptable and the
L0:development, fabrication, or manufacture of special equipment is required, the
L0:Government may—
L1:(1) Provide the equipment; or
L1:(2) Direct the Contractor to acquire the equipment or facilities. If the
L0:Contractor acquires the equipment or facilities, the acquisition shall be competitive,
L0:if practicable.
L1:(i) If at any time the Government defers or changes its orders for any of the
L0:services but does not cancel or terminate them, the amount paid or payable to the
L0:Contractor for the services deferred or modified shall be equitably adjusted under
L0:applicable tariffs filed by the Contractor with the regulatory commission in effect at
L0:the time of deferral or change. If no tariffs are in effect, the Government and the
L0:Contractor shall equitably adjust the rates by mutual agreement. Failure to agree
L0:on any adjustment shall be a dispute concerning a question of fact within the
L0:meaning of the Disputes clause of this contract.

title: 252.239-7007 Cancellation or Termination of Orders
content:
L0:252.239-7007 Cancellation or Termination of Orders.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7411(a), use the following clause:
L0:(End of clause)
L0:CANCELLATION OR TERMINATION OF ORDERS (SEP 2019)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L0:Actual nonrecoverable costs means the installed costs of the facilities and
L0:equipment, less cost of reusable materials, and less net salvage value.
L0:Basic cancellation liability means the actual nonrecoverable cost, which the
L0:Government shall reimburse the Contractor at the time services are cancelled.
L0:Basic termination liability means the nonrecoverable cost amortized in equal
L0:monthly increments throughout the liability period.
L0:Installed costs means the actual cost of equipment and materials specifically
L0:provided or used, plus the actual cost of installing (including engineering, labor,
L0:supervision, transportation, rights-of-way, and any other items which are
L0:chargeable to the capital accounts of the Contractor), less any costs the government
L0:may have directly reimbursed the Contractor under the Special Construction and
L0:Equipment Charges clause of this agreement/contract.
L0:Net salvage value means the salvage value less the cost of removal.
L1:(b) If the Government cancels any of the services ordered under this
L0:agreement/contract, before the services are made available to the Government, or
L0:terminates any of these services after they are made available to the Government,
L0:the Government will reimburse the Contractor for the actual nonrecoverable costs
L0:the Contractor has reasonably incurred in providing facilities and equipment for
L0:which the Contractor has no foreseeable reuse. The Government will not reimburse
L0:the Contractor for any actual nonrecoverable costs incurred after notice of award,
L0:but prior to execution of the order.
L1:(c) When feasible, the Contractor shall reuse cancelled or terminated facilities or
L0:equipment to minimize the charges to the Government.
L1:(d) If at any time the Government requires that telecommunications facilities or
L0:equipment be relocated within the Contractor's service area, the Government will
L0:have the option of paying the costs of relocating the facilities or equipment in lieu of
L0:paying any termination or cancellation charge under this clause. The basic
L0:cancellation liability or basic termination liability applicable to the facilities or
L0:equipment in their former location shall continue to apply to the facilities and
L0:equipment in their new location. Monthly recurring charges shall continue to be
L0:paid during the period.
L1:(e) When there is another requirement or foreseeable reuse in place of cancelled
L0:or terminated facilities or equipment, no charge shall apply and the basic
L0:cancellation liability or basic termination liability shall be appropriately reduced.
L0:When feasible, the Contractor shall promptly reuse discontinued channels or
L0:facilities, including equipment for which the Government is obligated to pay a
L0:minimum service charge.
L1:(f) The amount of the Government's liability upon cancellation or termination of
L0:any of the services ordered under this agreement/contract will be determined under
L0:applicable tariffs governing cancellation and termination charges which—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L1:(1) Are filed by the Contractor with a governmental regulatory body, as
L0:defined in the Orders For Facilities and Services clause of this agreement/contract;
L1:(2) Are in effect on the date of termination; and
L1:(3) Provide specific cancellation or termination charges for the facilities and
L0:equipment involved or show how to determine the charges.
L1:(g) The amount of the Government's liability upon cancellation or termination of
L0:any of the services ordered under this agreement/contract, which are not subject to
L0:a governmental regulatory body, will be determined under a mutually agreed
L0:schedule in the communication services authorization (CSA) or other contractual
L0:document.
L1:(h) If no applicable tariffs are in effect on the date of cancellation or termination
L0:or set forth in the applicable CSA or other contractual document, the Government's
L0:liability will be determined under the following settlement procedures—
L1:(1) The Contractor agrees to provide the Contracting Officer, in such
L0:reasonable detail as the Contracting Officer may require, inventory schedules
L0:covering all items of property or facilities in the Contractor's possession, the cost of
L0:which is included in the Basic Cancellation or Termination Liability for which the
L0:Contractor has no foreseeable reuse.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall use its best efforts to sell property or facilities when
L0:the Contractor has no foreseeable reuse or when the Government has not exercised
L0:its option to take title under the Title to Telecommunications Facilities and
L0:Equipment clause of this agreement/contract. The Contractor shall apply any
L0:proceeds of the sale to reduce any payments by the Government to the Contractor
L0:under a cancellation or termination settlement.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall record actual nonrecoverable costs under established
L0:accounting procedures prescribed by the cognizant governmental regulatory
L0:authority or, if no such procedures have been prescribed, under generally accepted
L0:accounting procedures applicable to the provision of telecommunication services for
L0:public use.
L1:(4) The net salvage value shall be deducted from the Contractor's installed cost.
L0:In determining net salvage value, the Contractor shall consider the foreseeable
L0:reuse of the facilities and equipment by the Contractor. The Contractor shall make
L0:allowance for the cost of dismantling, removal, reconditioning, and disposal of the
L0:facilities and equipment when necessary either for the sale of facilities or their
L0:reuse by the Contractor in another location.
L1:(5) Upon termination of services, the Government will reimburse the Contractor
L0:for the nonrecoverable cost less such costs amortized to the date services are
L0:terminated and establish the liability period as mutually agreed to but not to exceed
L0:ten years. In the case of either a cancellation or a termination, the Government's
L0:presumed maximum liability will be capped by the unpaid non-recurring charges
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L0:and the monthly recurring charges set out in the contract/agreement. The
L0:presumed maximum liability for monthly recurring charges shall be capped at
L0:monthly recurring charges for the minimum service period and any required notice
L0:period.
L1:(6) When the basic cancellation liability or basic termination liability
L0:established by the CSA or other contractual document is based on estimated costs,
L0:the Contractor agrees to settle on the basis of actual cost at the time of cancellation
L0:or termination.
L1:(7) The Contractor agrees that, if after settlement but within the termination
L0:liability period of the services, should the Contractor make reuse of equipment or
L0:facilities which were treated as nonreusable or nonsalvable in the settlement, the
L0:Contractor shall reimburse the Government for the value of the equipment or
L0:facilities.
L1:(8) The Contractor agrees to exclude—
L1:(i) Any costs which are not included in determining cancellation and
L0:termination charges under the Contractor's standard practices or procedures; and
L1:(ii) Charges not ordinarily made by the Contractor for similar facilities or
L0:equipment, furnished under similar circumstances.
L1:(i) The Government may, under such terms and conditions as it may
L0:prescribe, make partial payments and payments on account against costs incurred
L0:by the Contractor in connection with the cancelled or terminated portion of this
L0:agreement/contract. The Government may make these payments if the Contracting
L0:Officer determines that the total of the payments is within the amount the
L0:Contractor is entitled. If the total of the payments is in excess of the amount finally
L0:agreed or determined to be due under this clause, the Contractor shall pay the
L0:excess to the Government upon demand.
L1:(j) Failure to agree shall be a dispute concerning a question of fact within the
L0:meaning of the Disputes clause.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.239-7010 Cloud Computing Services
content:
L0:252.239-7010 Cloud Computing Services.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7604(b), use the following clause:
L0:(End of provision)
L0:CLOUD COMPUTING SERVICES (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Authorizing official, as described in DoD Instruction 8510.01, Risk Management
L0:Framework (RMF) for DoD Information Technology (IT), means the senior Federal
L0:official or executive with the authority to formally assume responsibility for
L0:operating an information system at an acceptable level of risk to organizational
L0:operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational
L0:assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.
L0:Cloud computing means a model for enabling ubiquitous, convenient, on-demand
L0:network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources (e.g., networks,
L0:servers, storage, applications, and services) that can be rapidly provisioned and
L0:released with minimal management effort or service provider interaction. This
L0:includes other commercial terms, such as on-demand self-service, broad network
L0:access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, and measured service. It also includes
L0:commercial offerings for software-as-a-service, infrastructure-as-a-service, and
L0:platform-as-a-service.
L0:Compromise means disclosure of information to unauthorized persons, or a
L0:violation of the security policy of a system, in which unauthorized intentional or
L0:unintentional disclosure, modification, destruction, or loss of an object, or the
L0:copying of information to unauthorized media may have occurred.
L0:Cyber incident means actions taken through the use of computer networks that
L0:result in a compromise or an actual or potentially adverse effect on an information
L0:system and/or the information residing therein.
L0:Government data means any information, document, media, or machine readable
L0:material regardless of physical form or characteristics, that is created or obtained
L0:by the Government in the course of official Government business.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L0:Government-related data means any information, document, media, or machine
L0:readable material regardless of physical form or characteristics that is created or
L0:obtained by a contractor through the storage, processing, or communication of
L0:Government data. This does not include contractor's business records e.g. financial
L0:records, legal records etc. or data such as operating procedures, software coding or
L0:algorithms that are not uniquely applied to the Government data.
L0:Information system means a discrete set of information resources organized for
L0:the collection, processing, maintenance, use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition
L0:of information.
L0:Media means physical devices or writing surfaces including, but not limited to,
L0:magnetic tapes, optical disks, magnetic disks, large-scale integration memory chips,
L0:and printouts onto which information is recorded, stored, or printed within an
L0:information system.
L0:Spillage security incident that results in the transfer of classified or controlled
L0:unclassified information onto an information system not accredited (i.e., authorized)
L0:for the appropriate security level.
L1:(b) Cloud computing security requirements. The requirements of this clause are
L0:applicable when using cloud computing to provide information technology services
L0:in the performance of the contract.
L1:(1) If the Contractor indicated in its offer that it “does not anticipate the use
L0:of cloud computing services in the performance of a resultant contract,” in response
L0:to provision 252.239-7009, Representation of Use of Cloud Computing, and after the
L0:award of this contract, the Contractor proposes to use cloud computing services in
L0:the performance of the contract, the Contractor shall obtain approval from the
L0:Contracting Officer prior to utilizing cloud computing services in performance of the
L0:contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall implement and maintain administrative, technical,
L0:and physical safeguards and controls with the security level and services required
L0:in accordance with the Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide (SRG)
L0:(version in effect at the time the solicitation is issued or as authorized by the
L0:Contracting Officer) found at https://public.cyber.mil/dccs/dccs-documents/
L0:unless notified by the Contracting Officer that this requirement has been waived by
L0:the DoD Chief Information Officer.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall maintain within the United States or outlying
L0:areas all Government data that is not physically located on DoD premises, unless
L0:the Contractor receives written notification from the Contracting Officer to use
L0:another location, in accordance with DFARS 239.7602-2(a).
L1:(c) Limitations on access to, and use and disclosure of Government data and
L0:Government-related data.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L1:(1) The Contractor shall not access, use, or disclose Government data unless
L0:specifically authorized by the terms of this contract or a task order or delivery order
L0:issued hereunder.
L1:(i) If authorized by the terms of this contract or a task order or delivery
L0:order issued hereunder, any access to, or use or disclosure of, Government data
L0:shall only be for purposes specified in this contract or task order or delivery order.
L1:(ii) The Contractor shall ensure that its employees are subject to all such
L0:access, use, and disclosure prohibitions and obligations.
L1:(iii) These access, use, and disclosure prohibitions and obligations shall
L0:survive the expiration or termination of this contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall use Government-related data only to manage the
L0:operational environment that supports the Government data and for no other
L0:purpose unless otherwise permitted with the prior written approval of the
L0:Contracting Officer.
L1:(d) Cloud computing services cyber incident reporting. The Contractor shall
L0:report all cyber incidents that are related to the cloud computing service provided
L0:under this contract. Reports shall be submitted to DoD via http://dibnet.dod.mil/.
L1:(e) Malicious software. The Contractor or subcontractors that discover and
L0:isolate malicious software in connection with a reported cyber incident shall submit
L0:the malicious software in accordance with instructions provided by the Contracting
L0:Officer.
L1:(f) Media preservation and protection. When a Contractor discovers a cyber
L0:incident has occurred, the Contractor shall preserve and protect images of all
L0:known affected information systems identified in the cyber incident report (see
L0:paragraph (d) of this clause) and all relevant monitoring/packet capture data for at
L0:least 90 days from the submission of the cyber incident report to allow DoD to
L0:request the media or decline interest.
L1:(g) Access to additional information or equipment necessary for forensic analysis.
L0:Upon request by DoD, the Contractor shall provide DoD with access to additional
L0:information or equipment that is necessary to conduct a forensic analysis.
L1:(h) Cyber incident damage assessment activities. If DoD elects to conduct a
L0:damage assessment, the Contracting Officer will request that the Contractor
L0:provide all of the damage assessment information gathered in accordance with
L0:paragraph (f) of this clause.
L1:(i) Records management and facility access.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall provide the Contracting Officer all Government
L0:data and Government-related data in the format specified in the contract.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L1:(2) The Contractor shall dispose of Government data and Government-
L0:related data in accordance with the terms of the contract and provide the
L0:confirmation of disposition to the Contracting Officer in accordance with contract
L0:closeout procedures.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall provide the Government, or its authorized
L0:representatives, access to all Government data and Government-related data,
L0:access to contractor personnel involved in performance of the contract, and physical
L0:access to any Contractor facility with Government data, for the purpose of audits,
L0:investigations, inspections, or other similar activities, as authorized by law or
L0:regulation.
L1:(j) Notification of third party access requests. The Contractor shall notify the
L0:Contracting Officer promptly of any requests from a third party for access to
L0:Government data or Government-related data, including any warrants, seizures, or
L0:subpoenas it receives, including those from another Federal, State, or local agency.
L0:The Contractor shall cooperate with the Contracting Officer to take all measures to
L0:protect Government data and Government-related data from any unauthorized
L0:disclosure.
L1:(k) Spillage. Upon notification by the Government of a spillage, or upon the
L0:Contractor's discovery of a spillage, the Contractor shall cooperate with the
L0:Contracting Officer to address the spillage in compliance with agency procedures.
L1:(l) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include this clause, including this
L0:paragraph (l), in all subcontracts that involve or may involve cloud services,
L0:including subcontracts for commercial services.

title: 252.239-7011 Special construction and equipment charges
content:
L0:252.239-7011 Special construction and equipment charges.

L0:constructing any facilities or providing any equipment, unless the Contracting
L0:Officer authorizes direct reimbursement.

L0:Government's contribution. Determine the value of the facilities and equipment on
L0:the basis of their foreseeable reuse by the Contractor at the time their use is
L0:discontinued or on the basis of the net salvage value, whichever is greater. The
L0:Contractor shall promptly pay the Government the amount of any credit.
L1:(c) The amount of the direct special construction charge shall not exceed—
L1:(1) The actual costs to the Contractor; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 39
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 239
L1:(2) An amount properly allocable to the services to be provided to the
L0:Government.
L1:(d) The amount of the direct special construction charge shall not include costs
L0:incurred by the Contractor which are covered by—
L1:(1) A cancellation or termination liability; or
L1:(2) The Contractor's recurring or other nonrecurring charges.
L1:(e) The Contractor represents that—
L1:(1) Recurring charges for the services, facilities, and equipment do not
L0:include in the rate base any costs that have been reimbursed by the Government to
L0:the Contractor; and
L1:(2) Depreciation charges are based only on the cost of facilities and
L0:equipment paid by the Contractor and not reimbursed by the Government.
L1:(f) If it becomes necessary for the Contractor to incur costs to replace any
L0:facilities or equipment, the Government shall assume those costs or reimburse the
L0:Contractor for replacement costs at mutually acceptable rates under the following
L0:circumstances—
L1:(1) The Government paid direct special construction charges; or
L1:(2) The Government reimbursed the Contractor for those facilities or
L0:equipment as a part of the recurring charges; and
L1:(3) The need for replacement was due to circumstances beyond the control
L0:and without the fault of the Contractor.
L1:(g) Before incurring any costs under paragraph (f) of this clause, the
L0:Government shall have the right to terminate the service under the Cancellation or
L0:Termination of Orders clause of this contract.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 242.7000 Contractor business system deficiencies
content:
L0:242.7000 Contractor business system deficiencies.
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this subpart—
L0:“Acceptable contractor business systems” means contractor business systems that
L0:comply with the terms and conditions of the applicable business system clauses listed in
L0:the definition of “contractor business systems” in this section.
L0:“Contractor business systems” means—
L1:(i) Accounting system, if the contract includes the clause at 252.242-7999,
L0:Accounting System Administration;
L1:(ii) Earned value management system, if the contract includes the clause at
L0:252.234-7999, Earned Value Management System;
L1:(iii) Estimating system, if the contract includes the clause at 252.215-7002, Cost
L0:Estimating System Requirements;
L1:(iv) Material management and accounting system, if the contract includes the
L0:clause at 252.242-7997, Material Management and Accounting System;
L1:(v) Property management system, if the contract includes the clause at 252.245-
L0:7003, Contractor Property Management System Administration; and
L1:(vi) Purchasing system, if the contract includes the clause at 252.244-7998,
L0:Contractor Purchasing System Administration.
L0:“Covered contract” means a contract that is subject to the Cost Accounting Standards
L0:under 41 U.S.C. chapter 15, as implemented in regulations found at 48 CFR 9903.201-1
L0:(10 U.S.C. 3841 note prec).
L1:(b) Determination to withhold payments. If the contracting officer makes a final
L0:determination to disapprove a contractor’s business system in accordance with the
L0:clause at 252.242-7998, Contractor Business Systems, the contracting officer must—
L1:(1) In accordance with agency procedures, identify one or more covered
L0:contracts containing the clause at 252.242-7998 from which payments will be withheld.
L0:When identifying the covered contracts from which to withhold payments, the
L0:contracting officer must ensure that the total amount of payment withholding under
L0:252.242-7998, when there are material weaknesses in multiple contractor business
L0:systems, does not exceed 10 percent of progress payments, performance-based
L0:payments, and interim payments under cost-reimbursement, labor-hour, and time-and-
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 42
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 242
L0:materials contracts billed under each of the identified covered contracts. Similarly, the
L0:contracting officer must ensure that the total amount of payment withholding under the
L0:clause at 252.242-7998 for each business system does not exceed 5 percent of progress
L0:payments, performance-based payments, and interim payments under cost-
L0:reimbursement, labor-hour, and time-and-materials contracts billed under each of the
L0:identified covered contracts. The contracting officer has the sole discretion to identify
L0:the covered contracts from which to withhold payments.
L1:(2) Promptly notify the contractor, in writing, of the contracting officer’s
L0:determination to implement payment withholding in accordance with the clause at
L0:252.242-7998. Include the notice of payment withholding in the written final
L0:determination for the contractor business system and inform the contractor that—
L1:(i) Payments must be withheld from the contract or contracts identified in
L0:the written determination in accordance with the clause at 252.242-7998 until the
L0:contracting officer determines that there are no remaining material weaknesses; and
L1:(ii) The contracting officer reserves the right to take other actions within the
L0:terms and conditions of the contract.
L1:(3) Provide a copy of the determination to all contracting officers administering
L0:the selected contracts from which payments will be withheld. The contracting officer
L0:must also provide a copy of the determination to the auditor; payment office; affected
L0:contracting officers at the buying activities; and cognizant contracting officers in
L0:contract administration activities.
L1:(c) Monitoring contractor’s corrective action. In consultation with the auditor or
L0:functional specialist, monitor the contractor's progress in correcting the weaknesses.
L0:Notify the contractor of any decision to decrease or increase the amount of payment
L0:withholding in accordance with the clause at 252.242-7998.
L1:(d) Correction of material weaknesses.
L1:(1) If the contractor notifies the contracting officer that the contractor has
L0:corrected the material weaknesses, the contracting officer must request the auditor or
L0:functional specialist to review the correction to verify that the weaknesses have been
L0:corrected. If, after receipt of verification, the contracting officer determines that the
L0:contractor has corrected all material weaknesses as directed by the contracting officer’s
L0:final determination, the contracting officer must discontinue the withholding of
L0:payments, release any payments previously withheld, and approve the system, unless
L0:other material weaknesses remain.
L1:(2) Prior to the receipt of verification, the contracting officer may discontinue
L0:withholding payments pending receipt of verification, and release any payments
L0:previously withheld, if the contractor submits evidence that the material weaknesses
L0:have been corrected, and the contracting officer, in consultation with the auditor or
L0:functional specialist, determines that there is a reasonable expectation that the
L0:corrective actions have been implemented by the contractor and are expected to correct
L0:the material weaknesses.
L1:(3) Within 90 days of receipt of the contractor notification that the contractor
L0:has corrected the material weaknesses, the contracting officer must—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 42
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 242
L1:(i) Make a determination that—
L1:(A) The contractor has corrected all material weaknesses as directed by
L0:the contracting officer’s final determination in accordance with paragraph (d)(1) of this
L0:section;
L0:been implemented in accordance with paragraph (d)(2) of this section; or
L1:(B) There is a reasonable expectation that the corrective actions have
L1:(C) The contractor has not corrected all material weaknesses as
L0:directed by the contracting officer’s final determination in accordance with paragraph
L2:(d)(1) of this section, or there is not a reasonable expectation that the corrective actions
L0:have been implemented in accordance with paragraph (d)(2) of this section; or
L1:(ii) Reduce withholding directly related to the material weaknesses covered
L0:under the corrective action plan by at least 50 percent of the amount being withheld
L0:from progress payments and performance-based payments, and direct the contractor, in
L0:writing, to reduce the percentage withheld on interim cost vouchers by at least 50
L0:percent, until the contracting officer makes a determination in accordance with
L0:paragraph (d)(3)(i) of this section.
L1:(4) If, at any time, the contracting officer determines that the contractor has
L0:failed to correct the material weaknesses identified in the contractor's notification, the
L0:contracting officer will continue, reinstate, or increase withholding from progress
L0:payments and performance-based payments, and direct the contractor, in writing, to
L0:continue, reinstate, or increase the percentage withheld on interim cost vouchers to the
L0:percentage initially withheld, until the contracting officer determines that the
L0:contractor has corrected all material weaknesses as directed by the contracting officer’s
L0:final determination.
L1:(e) Sample formats. See PGI 242.7000 for sample formats of contracting officer
L0:determinations for use with the clause at 252.242-7998.

title: 242.7200 Scope of subpart
content:
L0:242.7200 Scope of subpart.
L1:(a) This subpart provides policies, procedures, and standards for use in the
L0:evaluation of a contractor's material management and accounting system (MMAS).
L1:(b) The policies, procedures, and standards in this subpart—
L1:(1) Apply only when the contractor has contracts exceeding the simplified
L0:acquisition threshold that are not for the acquisition of commercial products or
L0:commercial services and are either—
L1:(i) Cost-reimbursement contracts; or
L1:(ii) Fixed-price contracts with progress payments made on the basis of costs
L0:incurred by the contractor as work progresses under the contract; and
L1:(2) Do not apply to small businesses, educational institutions, or nonprofit
L0:organizations.

title: 242.7201 Definitions
content:
L0:242.7201 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Acceptable material management and accounting system” means a material
L0:management and accounting system that generally complies with the system criteria in
L0:paragraph (d) of the clause at 252.242-7997, Material Management and Accounting
L0:System.
L0:“Material management and accounting system (MMAS)” means the contractor’s
L0:system or systems for planning, controlling, and accounting for the acquisition, use,
L0:issuing, and disposition of material. Material management and accounting systems
L0:may be manual or automated. They may be stand-alone systems, or they may be
L0:integrated with planning, engineering, estimating, purchasing, inventory, accounting,
L0:or other systems.
L0:“Valid time-phased requirements” means material that is—
L1:(1) Needed to fulfill the production plan, including reasonable quantities for

content:
L0:242.7600 Scope of subpart
L0:This subpart prescribes policies and procedures for the postaward orientation of
L0:contractors and subcontractors through (a) a conference or (b) a letter or other form

title: 242.7601 General
content:
L0:242.7601 General.
L1:(a) A postaward orientation aids both Government and contractor personnel to (l)
L0:achieve a clear and mutual understanding of all contract requirements and (2) identify
L0:and resolve potential problems. However, it is not a substitute for the contractor's fully
L0:understanding the work requirements at the time offers are submitted, nor is it to be
L0:used to alter the final agreement arrived at in any negotiations leading to contract
L0:award.
L1:(b) Postaward orientation is encouraged to assist—
L1:(1) Small business concerns;
L1:(2) Small disadvantaged business concerns;
L1:(3) Veteran-owned small business concerns;
L1:(4) Service-disabled veteran-owned small business concerns;
L1:(5) HUBZone small business concerns; and
L1:(6) Women-owned small business concerns (including economically
L0:disadvantaged women-owned small business concerns and women-owned small
L0:business concerns eligible under the Women-Owned Small Business Program).
L1:(c) While cognizant Government or contractor personnel may request the contracting
L0:officer to arrange for orientation, it is up to the contracting officer to decide whether a
L0:postaward orientation in any form is necessary.

L0:As prescribed in 242.7204, use the following clause:
L0:MATERIAL MANAGEMENT AND ACCOUNTING SYSTEM
L0:(DEVIATION 2026-O0050) (MAR 2026)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Acceptable material management and accounting system” means a material
L0:management and accounting system that generally complies with the system criteria in
L0:paragraph (d) of this clause.

L0:2.101.

L0:“Material management and accounting system (MMAS)” means the Contractor’s
L0:system or systems for planning, controlling, and accounting for the acquisition, use,
L0:issuing, and disposition of material. Material management and accounting systems
L0:may be manual or automated. They may be stand-alone systems, or they may be
L0:integrated with planning, engineering, estimating, purchasing, inventory, accounting,
L0:or other systems.
L0:“Material weakness” means a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the internal
L0:control over information in contractor business systems, such that there is a reasonable
L0:possibility that a material misstatement of such information will not be prevented, or
L0:detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A reasonable possibility exists when the
L0:likelihood of an event occurring is—
L1:(1) Probable; or
L1:(2) More than remote but less than likely (section 806 of Pub. L. 116-283).
L0:“Valid time-phased requirements” means material that is—
L1:(1) Needed to fulfill the production plan, including reasonable quantities for
L0:scrap, shrinkage, yield, etc.; and
L1:(2) Charged or billed to contracts or other cost objectives in a manner consistent
L0:with the need to fulfill the production plan.
L1:(b) General. The Contractor shall—

L1:(i) Reasonably forecasts material requirements;
L1:(ii) Ensures that costs of purchased and fabricated material charged or

L0:material transactions; and
L1:(2) Assess its MMAS and take reasonable action to comply with the MMAS
L0:standards in paragraph (e) of this clause.

L0:MMAS policies, procedures, and operating instructions; and
L1:(3) Disclose significant changes in its MMAS to the ACO at least 30 days prior
L0:to implementation.

L1:(2) Ensure that costs of purchased and fabricated material charged or allocated

L1:(e) Withholding payments.

L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 242

title: 243.370-3 Definitization schedule
content:
L0:243.370-3 Definitization schedule.
L1:(a) Unpriced change orders must contain definitization schedules that provide
L0:for definitization by the earlier of—
L1:(1) The date that is 180 days after issuance of the change order (this date
L0:may be extended but may not exceed the date that is 180 days after the contractor
L0:submits a qualifying proposal); or
L1:(2) The date on which the amount of funds obligated under the change order
L0:is equal to more than 50 percent of the not-to-exceed price.
L1:(b) Submission of a qualifying proposal in accordance with the definitization
L0:schedule is a material element of the contract. If the contractor does not submit a
L0:timely qualifying proposal, the contracting officer may suspend or reduce progress
L0:payments under FAR 32.503-6, or take other appropriate action.

title: 243.370-4 Limitations on obligations
content:
L0:243.370-4 Limitations on obligations.
L1:(a) The Government must not obligate more than 50 percent of the not-to-exceed
L0:price before definitization. However, if a contractor submits a qualifying proposal
L0:before the Government obligates 50 percent of the not-to-exceed price, the
L0:Government may increase the limitation on obligations before definitization to no
L0:more than 75 percent (see PGI 232.102-70 for coverage on provisional delivery
L0:payments).
L1:(b) Obligations should be consistent with the contractor’s requirements for the
L0:undefinitized period.

L0:PGI 245.604 Sale of surplus personal property.
L0:When selling surplus personal property, plant clearance officers are required to follow
L0:the following procedures.
L1:(a) Best value sales approach. Plant clearance officers must determine a best
L0:value sales approach, considering costs, risks, and benefits, e.g., potential sales
L0:proceeds.
L1:(b) Invitation for bid procedures. The plant clearance officer may direct the
L0:contractor to issue informal invitations for bid (orally, telephonically, or by other informal
L0:media), provided—
L1:(1) Maximum practical competition is obtained;
L1:(2) Sources solicited are recorded; and
L1:(3) Informal bids are confirmed in writing.
L1:(c) Sale approval and award. Plant clearance officers must—
L1:(1) Evaluate bids to establish that the sale price is fair and reasonable, taking
L0:into consideration—
L1:(i) Knowledge or tests of the market;
L1:(ii) Current published prices for the property;
L1:(iii) The nature, condition, quantity, and location of the property; and
L1:(iv) Past sale history for like or similar items;
L1:(2) Approve award to the responsible bidder whose bid is most advantageous to
L0:the Government. The plant clearance officer must not approve award to any bidder who
L0:is an ineligible transferee, as defined in 252.245-7005, Management and Reporting of
L0:Government Property; and
L1:(3) Notify the contractor of the bidder to whom an award will be made within 5
L0:business days from receipt of bids.
L1:(d) Negotiated sales.
L1:(1) Negotiated sales include purchases or retention at less than cost by the
L0:contractor. Negotiated sales are authorized when—
L1:(i) The plant clearance officer determines that this method is essential to
L0:expeditious plant clearance; and
L1:(ii) The Government's interests are adequately protected.
L1:(2) Negotiated sales must be at fair and reasonable prices, not less than those
L0:reasonably expected under competitive sales.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(3) Conditions justifying negotiated sales are—
L1:(i) No acceptable bids are received under competitive sale;
L1:(ii) Anticipated sales proceeds do not warrant competitive sale;
L1:(iii) Specialized nature of the property would not create bidder interest;
L1:(iv) Removal of the property would reduce its value or result in
L0:disproportionate handling expenses; or
L1:(v) Such action is essential to the Government's interests.
L1:(e) Plant clearance officers must consider any special disposal requirements such
L0:as demilitarization or trade security control requirements in accordance with DoDM

L0:Trade Security Controls (TSCs) for Transfers of DoD Personal Property to Parties
L0:Outside DoD Control, respectively.

L0:“Major defense equipment” is defined in DoD Directive 2140.2, Recoupment of
L0:Nonrecurring Costs on Sales of U.S. Items, as any item of significant military
L0:equipment on the United States Munitions List having a nonrecurring research,
L0:development, test, and evaluation cost of more than $50 million or a total

L1:(b) General.
L1:(1) Approval. A contractor may use Government property on work for
L0:foreign governments and international organizations only when approved in writing

L0:As prescribed in 245.107(3), insert the following clause:
L0:CONTRACTOR PROPERTY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM ADMINISTRATION (JAN
L0:2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Acceptable property management system means a property system that complies
L0:with the system criteria in paragraph (c) of this clause.
L0:Material weakness means a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the
L0:internal control over information in contractor business systems, such that there is
L0:a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of such information will not
L0:be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A reasonable possibility
L0:exists when the likelihood of an event occurring is—
L1:(1) Probable; or
L1:(2) More than remote but less than likely (section 806 of Pub. L. 116-283).
L0:Property management system means the Contractor's system or systems for
L0:managing and controlling Government property.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(b) General. The Contractor shall establish and maintain an acceptable property
L0:management system. Failure to maintain an acceptable property management
L0:system, as defined in this clause, may result in disapproval of the system by the
L0:Contracting Officer and/or withholding of payments.
L1:(c) System criteria. The Contractor's property management system shall be in
L0:accordance with paragraphs (b) and (f) of the contract clause at Federal Acquisition
L0:Regulation 52.245-1.
L1:(d) Material weaknesses. (1) The Contracting Officer will provide an initial
L0:determination to the Contractor, in writing, of any material weaknesses. The initial
L0:determination will describe the underlying deficiency in sufficient detail to allow
L0:the Contractor to understand the weaknesses or deficiency.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial
L0:determination from the Contracting Officer that identifies material weaknesses in
L0:the Contractor's property management system. If the Contractor disagrees with the
L0:initial determination, the Contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for
L0:disagreeing.
L1:(3) The Contracting Officer will evaluate the Contractor's response and
L0:notify the Contractor, in writing, of the Contracting Officer's final determination
L0:concerning—
L1:(i) Remaining material weaknesses;
L1:(ii) The adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action; and
L1:(iii) System disapproval, if the Contracting Officer determines that one
L0:or more material weaknesses remain.
L1:(e) If the Contractor receives the Contracting Officer's final determination of
L0:material weaknesses, the Contractor shall, within 45 days of receipt of the final
L0:determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable
L0:corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the material
L0:weaknesses.
L1:(f) Withholding payments. If the Contracting Officer makes a final
L0:determination to disapprove the Contractor's property management system, and the
L0:contract includes the clause at 252.242-7005, Contractor Business Systems, the
L0:Contracting Officer will withhold payments in accordance with that clause.
L0:(End of clause)
