title: 252.245-7005 Management and Reporting of Government Property
content:
L0:252.245-7005 Management and Reporting of Government Property.
L0:As prescribed in 245.107(4), use the following clause:
L0:MANAGEMENT AND REPORTING OF GOVERNMENT PROPERTY (JAN 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L0:As is means that the Government makes no warranty with respect to the
L0:serviceability and/or suitability of the Government property for contract
L0:performance and that the Government will not pay for any repairs, replacement,
L0:and/or refurbishment of the property.
L0:Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code means—
L1:(1) An identifier assigned to entities located in the United States or its
L0:outlying areas by the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Commercial and Government
L0:Entity (CAGE) Branch to identify a commercial or government entity by unique
L0:location; or
L1:(2) An identifier assigned by a member of the North Atlantic Treaty
L0:Organization (NATO) or by the NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA) to
L0:entities located outside the United States and its outlying areas that the DLA
L0:Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Branch records and maintains in the
L0:CAGE master file. This type of code is known as a NATO CAGE (NCAGE) code.
L0:Contractor-acquired property, contractor inventory, Government property,
L0:Government-furnished property, and loss of Government property have the meanings
L0:given in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.245-1, Government Property,
L0:clause of this contract.
L0:Demilitarization means the act of eliminating the functional capabilities and
L0:inherent military design features from DoD personal property. Methods and degree
L0:range from removal and destruction of critical features to total destruction by
L0:cutting, tearing, crushing, mangling, shredding, melting, burning, etc.
L0:Export-controlled items has the meaning given in the Defense Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 252.225-7048, Export-Controlled
L0:Items, clause of this contract.
L0:Ineligible transferee means an individual, an entity, or a country—
L1:(1) Excluded from Federal programs by the General Services Administration
L0:as identified in the System for Award Management Exclusions located at
L0:https://sam.gov;
L1:(2) Delinquent on obligations to the U.S. Government under surplus sales
L0:contracts;
L1:(3) Designated by the Department of Defense as ineligible, debarred, or
L0:suspended from defense contracts; or
L1:(4) Subject to denial, debarment, or other sanctions under export control
L0:laws and related laws and regulations, and orders administered by the Department
L0:of State, the Department of Commerce, the Department of Homeland Security, or
L0:the Department of the Treasury.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L0:Item unique identification means a system of assigning, reporting, and marking
L0:DoD property with unique item identifiers that have machine-readable data
L0:elements to distinguish an item from all other like and unlike items.
L0:National stock number means a 13-digit stock number used to identify items of
L0:supply. It consists of a four-digit Federal Supply Code and a nine-digit National
L0:Item Identification Number.
L0:Reparable item means an item, typically in unserviceable condition, furnished to
L0:the contractor for maintenance, repair, modification, or overhaul.
L0:Scrap means property that has no value except for its basic material content. For
L0:purposes of demilitarization, scrap is defined as recyclable waste and discarded
L0:materials derived from items that have been rendered useless beyond repair,
L0:rehabilitation, or restoration such that the item's original identity, utility, form, fit,
L0:and function have been destroyed. Items can be classified as scrap if processed by
L0:cutting, tearing, crushing, mangling, shredding, or melting. Intact or recognizable
L0:components and parts are not “scrap.”
L0:Serially-managed item means an item designated by DoD to be uniquely
L0:tracked, controlled, or managed in maintenance, repair, and/or supply systems by
L0:means of its serial number or unique item identifier.
L0:Serviceable or usable property means property with potential for reutilization or
L0:sale as is or with minor repairs or alterations.
L0:Supply condition code means a classification of materiel in terms of readiness for
L0:issue and use or to identify action underway to change the status of materiel.
L0:Unique item identifier (UII) means a set of data elements marked on an item
L0:that is globally unique and unambiguous. The term includes a concatenated UII or
L0:a DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.
L1:(b) Reporting Government property. (1) The Contractor shall use the
L0:Government Furnished Property (GFP) module of the Procurement Integrated
L0:Enterprise Environment (PIEE) to—
L1:(i) Report receipt of GFP;
L1:(ii) Report the transfer of GFP to another DoD contract;
L1:(iii) Report the shipment of GFP to the Government or to a contractor. The
L0:GFP module generates the electronic equivalent of the DD Form 1149, DD Form
L0:1348-1, or other required shipping documents;
L1:(iv) Report when serially-managed items of GFP are incorporated into a higher-
L0:level component, assembly, or end item;
L1:(v) Report the loss of Government property in accordance with paragraph
L3:(f)(1)(vii) of the FAR 52.245-1 clause of this contract;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(vi) Complete the plant clearance inventory schedule in accordance with
L0:paragraph (j)(2) of the FAR 52.245-1 clause of this contract, unless disposition
L0:instructions are otherwise included in this contract. The GFP module generates the
L0:electronic equivalent of the Standard Form (SF) 1428, Inventory Disposal Schedule;
L0:and
L1:(vii) Submit a request to buy back or to convert to GFP items of Contractor-
L0:acquired property.
L1:(2) Information regarding the GFP module is available in the GFP Module
L0:Vendor Guide at https://dodprocurementtoolbox.com/site-pages/gfp-resources.
L0:Users may also register for access to the GFP module and obtain training on the
L0:PIEE home page at https://piee.eb.mil.
L1:(3) In complying with paragraphs (b)(1)(i) through (iv) of this clause, the
L0:Contractor shall report the updated status of the property to the GFP module
L0:within 7 business days of the date the change in status occurs, unless otherwise
L0:specified in the contract.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall use Wide Area WorkFlow in accordance with
L0:DFARS Appendix F, Material Inspection and Receiving Report, to report the
L0:shipment of reparable items after completion of repair, maintenance, modification,
L0:or overhaul.
L1:(5) When Government property is in the possession of subcontractors, the
L0:Contractor shall ensure that reporting is accomplished using the data elements
L0:required in paragraph (c) of this clause.
L1:(c) Records of Government property. To facilitate reporting of Government
L0:property to the GFP module, the Contractor's property records, in addition to the
L0:requirements of paragraph (f)(1)(iii) of the FAR 52.245-1 clause of this contract,
L0:shall enable recording of the following data elements:
L1:(1) National stock number (NSN). If an NSN is not available, use either the
L0:combination of the manufacturer's CAGE code and part number, or model number.
L1:(2) CAGE code on the accountable Government contract.
L1:(3) Received/sent (shipped) date.
L1:(4) Accountable Government contract number.
L1:(5) Serial number (for serially-managed items that do not have a UII); and
L1:(6) Supply condition code (only required for reporting of reparable items).
L0:For information on Federal supply condition codes, see DLM 4000.25, Defense
L0:Logistics Management Standards (DLMS), Volume 2, Supply Standards and
L0:Procedures, Appendix 2.5 at
L0:https://www.dla.mil/HQ/InformationOperations/DLMS/elibrary/manuals/v2/.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(d) Marking, reporting, and UII registration of GFP requirements. The
L0:Contractor—
L1:(1) Shall assign the UII and mark the reparable items identified as serially
L0:managed in the GFP attachment to this contract with an item unique identification
L1:(IUID) data matrix, when the technical drawing for the item is accessible to the
L0:Contractor and includes IUID data matrix location and marking method;
L1:(2) Shall report the UII either before or during shipment of the repaired
L0:item;
L1:(3) Is not required to mark items that were previously marked with an IUID
L0:data matrix and registered in accordance with DFARS 252.211-7003, Item Unique
L0:Identification and Valuation; and
L1:(4) Shall assign a new UII, then mark and register the item, when the
L0:conditions of paragraph (d)(1) are met, if an item is found to be marked but not
L0:registered in the IUID Registry.
L1:(e) Disposing of Government property. (1) The Contractor shall complete the
L0:plant clearance inventory schedule using the plant clearance capability of the GFP
L0:module of the PIEE to generate an electronic equivalent of the SF 1428, Inventory
L0:Disposal Schedule. The plant clearance inventory schedule requires the following:
L1:(i) If known, the applicable Federal supply code (FSC) for all items,
L0:except items in scrap condition.
L1:(ii) If known, the manufacturer name for all aircraft components under
L0:Federal supply group 16 or 17 and FSCs 2620, 2810, 2915, 2925, 2935, 2945, 2995,
L0:4920, 5821, 5826, 5841, 6340, and 6615.
L1:(iii) The manufacturer name, make, model number, model year, and
L0:serial number for all aircraft under FSCs 1510 and 1520.
L1:(2) If the schedules are acceptable, the plant clearance officer will confirm
L0:acceptance in the GFP module plant clearance capability, which will transmit a
L0:notification to the Contractor. The electronic acceptance is equivalent to the DD
L0:Form 1637, Notice of Acceptance of Inventory.
L1:(f) Demilitarization, mutilation, and destruction. If demilitarization, mutilation,
L0:or destruction of contractor inventory is required, the Contractor shall demilitarize,
L0:mutilate, or destroy contractor inventory, in accordance with the terms and
L0:conditions of the contract and consistent with Defense Demilitarization Manual,
L0:DoD Manual (DoDM) 4160.28-M, edition in effect as of the date of this contract. If
L0:the property is available for purchase, the plant clearance officer may authorize the
L0:purchaser to demilitarize, mutilate, or destroy as a condition of sale provided the
L0:property is not inherently dangerous to public health and safety.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(g) Classified Contractor inventory. The Contractor shall dispose of classified
L0:contractor inventory in accordance with applicable security guides and regulations
L0:or as directed by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(h) Inherently dangerous Contractor inventory. Contractor inventory that is
L0:dangerous to public health or safety shall not be disposed of unless rendered
L0:innocuous or until adequate safeguards are provided.
L1:(i) Contractor inventory located in foreign countries. Consistent with contract
L0:terms and conditions, property disposition shall be in accordance with foreign and
L0:U.S. laws and regulations, including laws and regulations involving export controls,
L0:host nation requirements, final governing standards, and government-to-
L0:government agreements. The Contractor's responsibility to comply with all
L0:applicable laws and regulations regarding export-controlled items exists
L0:independent of, and is not established or limited by, the information provided by
L0:this clause.
L1:(j) Disposal of scrap—(1) Contractor scrap procedures.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall include, within its property management
L0:procedure, a process for the accountability and management of Government-owned
L0:scrap. The process shall, at a minimum, provide for the effective and efficient
L0:disposition of scrap, including sales to scrap dealers, so as to minimize costs,
L0:maximize sales proceeds, and contain the necessary internal controls for mitigating
L0:the improper release of non-scrap property.
L1:(ii) The Contractor may commingle Government and contractor-owned
L0:scrap and provide routine disposal of scrap, with plant clearance officer
L0:concurrence, when determined to be effective and efficient.
L1:(2) Scrap warranty. The plant clearance officer may require the Contractor
L0:to secure from scrap buyers a DD Form 1639, Scrap Warranty.
L1:(k) Sale of surplus Contractor inventory—
L1:(1) Sales procedures.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall conduct sales of contractor inventory (both
L0:useable property and scrap) in accordance with the requirements of this contract
L0:and plant clearance officer direction. The Contractor shall include in its invitation
L0:for bids the sales terms and conditions provided by the plant clearance officer.
L1:(ii) The Contractor may conduct internet-based sales, to include use of a
L0:third party.
L1:(iii) If the Contractor wishes to bid on the sale, the Contractor or its
L0:employees shall submit bids to the plant clearance officer prior to soliciting bids
L0:from other prospective bidders.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(iv) The Contractor shall solicit bids to obtain adequate competition.
L0:Negotiated sales are subject to obtaining such competition as is feasible under the
L0:circumstances of the negotiated sale.
L1:(v) The Contractor shall solicit bids at least 15 calendar days before bid
L0:opening to allow adequate opportunity to inspect the property and prepare bids.
L1:(vi) For large sales, the Contractor may use summary lists of items offered as bid
L0:sheets with detailed descriptions attached.
L1:(vii) In addition to providing notice of the proposed sale to prospective
L0:bidders, the Contractor may, when the results are expected to justify the additional
L0:expense, display a notice of the proposed sale in appropriate public places, e.g.,
L0:publish a sales notice on the internet, in appropriate trade journals or magazines,
L0:and in local newspapers.
L1:(viii) The plant clearance officer or designated Government
L0:representative will witness the bid opening. The Contractor shall submit the bid
L0:abstract in electronic format to the plant clearance officer within 2 days of bid
L0:opening. If the Contractor is unable to submit the bid abstract electronically, the
L0:Contractor may submit 2 copies of the abstract manually within 2 days of bid
L0:opening. The plant clearance officer will not approve award to any bidder who is an
L0:ineligible transferee.
L1:(2) Required terms and conditions for sales contracts. The Contractor shall
L0:include the following terms and conditions in sales contracts:
L1:(i) For sales contracts or other documents transferring title:
L0:“The Purchaser certifies that the property covered by this contract will be used
L0:in [insert name of country]. In the event of resale or export by the Purchaser of
L0:any of the property, the Purchaser agrees to obtain the appropriate U.S. and
L0:foreign export or re-export license approval.”
L1:(ii) For sales contracts that require demilitarization, mutilation, or
L0:destruction of property:
L0:“The following items [insert list provided by plant clearance officer] require
L0:demilitarization, mutilation, or destruction by the Purchaser. Additional
L0:instructions are provided in accordance with Defense Demilitarization Manual,
L0:DoDM 4160.28-M, edition in effect as of the date of this sales contract. A
L0:Government representative will certify and verify demilitarization of items.
L0:Prepare demilitarization certificates in accordance with DoDM 4160.28, Volume
L0:2, section 4.5, DEMIL Certificate (see figure 2, Example DEMIL Certificate).”
L1:(iii) Removal and title transfer:
L0:“Property requiring demilitarization shall not be removed, and title shall not
L0:pass to the Purchaser, until demilitarization has been accomplished and verified
L0:by a Government representative.”
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(iv) Assumption of cost incident to demilitarization:
L0:“The Purchaser agrees to assume all costs incident to the demilitarization and to
L0:restore the working area to its present condition after removing the
L0:demilitarized property.”
L1:(v) Failure to demilitarize:
L0:“If the Purchaser fails to demilitarize, mutilate, or destroy the property as
L0:specified in the sales contract, the Contractor may, upon giving 10 days written
L0:notice to the Purchaser—
L1:(A) Repossess, demilitarize, and return the property to the
L0:Purchaser, in which case the Purchaser hereby agrees to pay to the Contractor,
L0:prior to the return of the property, all costs incurred by the Contractor in
L0:repossessing, demilitarizing, and returning the property;
L1:(B) Repossess, demilitarize, and resell the property, and charge the
L0:defaulting Purchaser with all costs incurred by the Contractor. The Contractor
L0:shall deduct these costs from the purchase price and refund the balance of the
L0:purchase price, if any, to the Purchaser. In the event the costs exceed the purchase
L0:price, the defaulting Purchaser hereby agrees to pay these costs to the Contractor;
L0:or
L1:(C) Repossess and resell the property under similar terms and
L0:conditions and charge the defaulting Purchaser with all costs incurred by the
L0:Contractor. The Contractor shall deduct these costs from the original purchase price
L0:and refund the balance of the purchase price, if any, to the defaulting Purchaser.
L0:Should the excess costs to the Contractor exceed the purchase price, the defaulting
L0:Purchaser hereby agrees to pay these costs to the Contractor.”
L1:(l) Restrictions on purchase or retention of Contractor inventory. The Contractor
L0:may not knowingly sell the inventory to any person or that person's agent,
L0:employee, or household member if that person—
L1:(1) Is a civilian employee of DoD or the U.S. Coast Guard;
L1:(2) Is a member of the Armed Forces of the United States, including the
L0:U.S. Coast Guard; or
L1:(3) Has any functional or supervisory responsibilities for or within DoD's
L0:property disposal, disposition, or plant clearance programs or for the disposal of
L0:contractor inventory.
L1:(m) Proceeds from sales of surplus property. Unless otherwise provided in the
L0:contract, the proceeds of any sale, purchase, or retention shall be—
L1:(1) Forwarded to the Contracting Officer;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(2) Credited to the Government as part of the settlement agreement
L0:pursuant to the termination of the contract;
L1:(3) Credited to the price or cost of the contract; or
L1:(4) Applied as otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L0:PGI Part 245—GOVERNMENT PROPERTY
L0:PGI 245.1—GENERAL
L0:PGI 245.102-70 Policy.
L1:(1) A basic principle of the Federal Acquisition Regulations System is that, upon
L0:contract award, contractors bring all the necessary organization, experience, accounting
L0:and operational controls, property, and technical skills, or the ability to obtain them
L0:(reference FAR 9.104-1 (e), (f), and (g) of General Standards). Therefore, upon
L0:contract award, responsible contractors should have the means to provide effective and
L0:efficient stewardship of Government property.
L1:(2) Government property, as defined at FAR 45.101, must be contractually
L0:accountable to a single contract and only one contract at a time. This requirement
L0:applies to both Government-furnished property and contractor-acquired property.
L0:Although accountable to only one contract at a time, contract terms and conditions may
L0:allow Government property to be used on other contracts (see FAR 52.245-9, Use and
L0:Charges).
L0:PGI 245.103 General.
L0:PGI 245.103-70 Furnishing Government property to contractors.
L1:(1) The requiring activity (project or program manager, or purchase request
L0:generator), as part of its responsibility for acquisition planning (FAR part 7, Acquisition
L0:Planning), is the decision point as to whether or not to furnish property to contractors.
L0:The basis for any decision to provide Government property must be documented by the
L0:requiring activity and provided to the contracting officer. Such documentation is not
L0:required when contractors are furnished property for repair, modification, or overhaul
L0:under a contract.
L1:(2) Prior to furnishing Government property to the contractor, the contracting officer
L0:must ensure that each of the requirements of FAR 45.102 are addressed as follows,
L0:and documented in the contracting file—
L1:(i) Element 1: In the Government’s best interest. Discussion should be specific,
L0:factual, and where necessary, address actual or projected dollars and percentages.
L0:Merely selecting one or two objectives supported by a general, perfunctory discussion
L0:does not address this element satisfactorily. Discussion should address the following
L0:factors:
L1:(A) Economy - Furnishing Government property is the lowest cost or price
L0:alternative.
L1:(B) Standardization - There is a critical need for precise replication.
L1:(C) Security - Government property is needed due to national security
L0:issues/concerns.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(D) Expedite production - Government property is crucial to achieving
L0:timely or accelerated delivery of a supply item or service.
L1:(E) Scarcity - The Government can obtain scarce items or is the only
L0:source of property necessary for successful execution of a contract.
L1:(F) Maintain the industrial base - Government property is needed to ensure
L0:future capability to obtain a particular supply item or service.
L1:(G) Contract type - Government property will enable the Government to
L0:obtain a more favorable contract type.
L1:(ii) Element 2: Overall benefit. Demonstrate that the overall benefit to
L0:the acquisition significantly outweighs the increased cost of administration, including
L0:property disposal.
L1:(A) Property in the hands of contractors drives program costs.
L0:Therefore, in order to make the case that providing Government property to the
L0:contractor is worthwhile, the associated costs must be considered and the business
L0:decision justified. The costs of Government property removal and disposal, including
L0:demilitarization and disposal of environmentally-regulated property, must be included.
L1:(B) Costs must be either less than what the contractor might
L0:otherwise incur, or the demonstrated benefit to the Government must outweigh these
L0:additional contract costs.
L1:(iii) Element 3: Government assumption of risk. Demonstrate that providing the
L0:property does not substantially increase the Government’s risk.
L1:(A) Risk must be discussed and documented. A risk analysis is warranted
L0:to demonstrate that the Government is not substantially increasing its risk. For
L0:example, when furnishing Government property, the Government is ordinarily
L0:responsible for suitability of use, timely delivery, and replacement of defective
L0:Government property.
L1:(B) Other risks may need to be considered, discussed, and documented.
L1:(iv) Element 4: Government requirements cannot otherwise be met. Document
L0:why the furnishing of Government property is critical and significant to meeting
L0:acquisition plan objectives.
L0:PGI 245.103-71 Transferring Government property accountability.
L1:(1) Use only the Standard Form 30 to execute transfers of Government property
L0:accountability between existing contracts. No other forms or documents, such as the
L0:DD Form 1149, Requisition and Invoice/Shipping Document, are authorized for the
L0:transfer of Government property accountability from one contract to another.
L1:(2) Modifications for the transfer of Government property accountability must:
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(i) Use the Government-furnished property (GFP) attachment prescribed at
L0:PGI 245.103-72.
L1:(ii) Incorporate FAR clauses 52.245-1, Government Property, and 52.245-9,
L0:Use and Charges, and the associated DFARS clauses (see 245.107, Contract clauses)
L0:to the extent that the gaining contract lacks the required clauses.
L0:PGI 245.103-72 Government-furnished property attachments to solicitations and
L0:awards.
L1:(a) When Government-furnished property (GFP) is anticipated, create the GFP
L0:attachment in the GFP module of the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment
L1:(PIEE) at https://piee.eb.mil/piee-landing to—
L1:(1) Specify the required GFP data elements; and
L1:(2) Identify GFP serially-managed items, GFP nonserially-managed items, and
L0:GFP items that may be requisitioned from the DoD supply system by the contractor; and
L1:(3) Accomplish the electronic transmission of the GFP attachment to the
L0:contract in the Electronic Data Access application in the PIEE.
L1:(4) Where the GFP attachment is classified, the PIEE GFP Module must not be
L0:used, but a property attachment with similar data is required for the contract.
L1:(b) Classified contracts are not exempt from including GFP attachments solely
L0:because the contracts are classified.
L1:(c) For more information on the GFP attachments,
L0:see https://dodprocurementtoolbox.com/site-pages/gfp-attachments.
L0:PGI 245.103-73 Government property under sustainment contracts.
L1:(1) Sustainment contracts, including those for performance-based logistics,
L0:sustainment support, contractor logistics support, life-cycle product support, contractor
L0:inventory control points, and weapon systems product support (see 10 U.S.C. 4324(d)),
L0:may require the contractor to hold or manage Government inventory. In such cases,
L0:regularly scheduled (typically, semiannually) inventory reporting from the contractor is
L0:required to ensure that inventory levels meet program requirements and Government
L0:inventory in excess of authorized amounts is identified. The requiring activity is
L0:responsible for providing the contracting officer with reporting requirements for
L0:Government inventory. See the Data Item Description DI-PSSS-80727A, Government
L0:Furnished Material (GFM) by National Stock Number, and the instructions for
L0:completing the DD Form 1423 Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) for inventory
L0:reporting requirements on sustainment contracts available at
L0:http://dodprocurementtoolbox.com/site-pages/gfp-resources.
L1:(2) During acquisition planning, pricing contracts, exercising options, and assessing
L0:past performance, contracting officers should review the requiring activity’s assessment
L0:of the information generated by the inventory reporting requirements.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 45
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 245
L1:(3) In some circumstances, under fixed-price sustainment contracts, contract
L0:deliverables consist of non-hardware items, such as operational readiness rate goals or
L0:mean time between failures of a system. In order to meet these deliverables,
L0:contractors are required to provide certain property items to the Government. In such
L0:cases, the contract does not include specific delivery line items requiring formal delivery
L0:of the property. By extension, the Government will not have title to the property at the
L0:time the contractor provides the property. Not separately priced line items must be
L0:included in the contract for the delivery of items in accordance with FAR 4.1003. Tables
L0:of unit acquisition prices may be included in the contract to use as the unit price on the
L0:receiving report.
L0:PGI 245.103-74 Contracting office responsibilities.
L1:(1) Prepare the GFP attachments in accordance with the procedures in PGI

title: 246.101 Definitions
content:
L0:246.101 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Discipline Working Group” is defined in the clause at 252.246-7004, Safety of
L0:Facilities, Infrastructure, and Equipment for Military Operations.

title: 246.102 Policy
content:
L0:246.102 Policy.
L0:Departments and agencies must also—

title: 246.270-1 Scope
content:
L0:246.270-1 Scope.
L0:This section establishes policies and procedures intended to ensure the safety and
L0:habitability of facilities, infrastructure, and equipment acquired for use by DoD
L0:military or civilian personnel during military operations performed outside the
L0:United States, Guam, Puerto Rico, and the Virgin Islands (section 807 of the
L0:National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Pub. L. 111-84).

title: 246.270-2 Policy
content:
L0:246.270-2 Policy.
L1:(a) Contracts (including task and delivery orders) for the construction,
L0:installation, repair, maintenance, or operation of facilities, infrastructure, and
L0:equipment configured for occupancy, including but not limited to, existing host
L0:nation facilities, new construction, and relocatable buildings acquired for use by
L0:DoD military or civilian personnel, must require a pre-occupancy safety and
L0:habitability inspection.
L1:(b) To minimize safety and health risks, each contract covered by this policy
L0:must require the contractor’s compliance with the Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC)
L0:1-200-01 and its referenced standards for—
L1:(1) Fire protection;
L1:(2) Structural integrity;
L1:(3) Electrical systems;
L1:(4) Plumbing;
L1:(5) Water treatment;
L1:(6) Waste disposal; and
L1:(7) Telecommunications networks.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 46
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 246
L1:(c) Existing host nation facilities constructed to standards equivalent to or more
L0:stringent than UFC 1-200-01 are acceptable upon a written determination of the
L0:acceptability of the standards by the Discipline Working Group.
L1:(d) Inspections to ensure compliance with UFC 1-200-01 standards must be
L0:conducted in accordance with the inspection clause of the contract.

title: 246.702-70 Definitions
content:
L0:246.702-70 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Acceptance,” as used in the warranty clauses at FAR 52.246-17, Warranty of
L0:Supplies of a Noncomplex Nature; FAR 52.246-18, Warranty of Supplies of a
L0:Complex Nature; FAR 52.246-19, Warranty of Systems and Equipment Under
L0:Performance Specifications or Design Criteria; and FAR 52.246-20, Warranty of
L0:Services, includes the execution of an official document (e.g., DD Form 250,
L0:Material Inspection and Receiving Report) by an authorized representative of the
L0:Government.
L0:“Defect” means any condition or characteristic in any supply or service furnished
L0:by the contractor under the contract that is not in compliance with the
L0:requirements of the contract.
L0:“Enterprise” means the entity (e.g., a manufacturer or vendor) responsible for
L0:granting the warranty and/or assigning unique item identifiers to serialized
L0:warranty items.
L0:“Enterprise identifier” means a code that is uniquely assigned to an enterprise
L0:by an issuing agency.
L0:“Issuing agency” means an organization responsible for assigning a globally
L0:unique identifier to an enterprise, as indicated in the Register of Issuing Agency
L0:Codes for International Standards Organization/International Electrotechnical
L0:Commission 15459, located at http://www.aimglobal.org/?Reg_Authority15459.
L0:“Serialized item” means each item produced is assigned a serial number that is
L0:unique among all the collective tangible items produced by the enterprise, or each
L0:item of a particular part, lot, or batch number is assigned a unique serial number
L0:within that part, lot, or batch number assignment within the enterprise identifier.
L0:The enterprise is responsible for ensuring unique serialization within the enterprise
L0:identifier or within the part, lot, or batch numbers, and that serial numbers, once
L0:assigned, are never used again.
L0:“Unique item identifier” means a set of data elements marked on an item that is
L0:globally unique and unambiguous.
L0:“Warranty tracking” means the ability to trace a warranted item from delivery
L0:through completion of the effectivity of the warranty.

title: 252.246-7003 Notification of Potential Safety Issues
content:
L0:252.246-7003 Notification of Potential Safety Issues.
L0:As prescribed in 246.370(a), use the following clause:
L0:NOTIFICATION OF POTENTIAL SAFETY ISSUES (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Credible information means information that, considering its source and the
L0:surrounding circumstances, supports a reasonable belief that an event has occurred
L0:or will occur.
L0:Critical safety item means a part, subassembly, assembly, subsystem,
L0:installation equipment, or support equipment for a system that contains a
L0:characteristic, any failure, malfunction, or absence of which could have a safety
L0:impact.
L0:Safety impact means the occurrence of death, permanent total disability,
L0:permanent partial disability, or injury or occupational illness requiring
L0:hospitalization; loss of a weapon system; or property damage exceeding $1,000,000.
L0:Subcontractor means any supplier, distributor, vendor, or firm that furnishes
L0:supplies or services to or for the Contractor or another subcontractor under this
L0:contract.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall provide notification, in accordance with paragraph (c) of
L0:this clause, of—
L1:(1) All nonconformances for parts identified as critical safety items acquired
L0:by the Government under this contract; and
L1:(2) All nonconformances or deficiencies that may result in a safety impact
L0:for systems, or subsystems, assemblies, subassemblies, or parts integral to a
L0:system, acquired by or serviced for the Government under this contract.
L1:(c) The Contractor—
L1:(1) Shall notify the Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO) and the
L0:Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) as soon as practicable, but not later than 72
L0:hours, after discovering or acquiring credible information concerning
L0:nonconformances and deficiencies described in paragraph (b) of this clause; and
L1:(2) Shall provide a written notification to the ACO and the PCO within 5
L0:working days that includes—
L1:(i) A summary of the defect or nonconformance;
L1:(ii) A chronology of pertinent events;
L1:(iii) The identification of potentially affected items to the extent known
L0:at the time of notification;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 46
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 246
L1:(iv) A point of contact to coordinate problem analysis and resolution; and
L1:(v) Any other relevant information.
L1:(d) The Contractor—
L1:(1) Is responsible for the notification of potential safety issues occurring
L0:with regard to an item furnished by any subcontractor; and
L1:(2) Shall facilitate direct communication between the Government and the
L0:subcontractor as necessary.
L1:(e) Notification of safety issues under this clause shall be considered neither an
L0:admission of responsibility nor a release of liability for the defect or its
L0:consequences. This clause does not affect any right of the Government or the
L0:Contractor established elsewhere in this contract.
L2:(f)(1) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause,
L0:including this paragraph (f), in subcontracts for—
L1:(i) Parts identified as critical safety items;
L1:(ii) Systems and subsystems, assemblies, and subassemblies integral to
L0:a system; or
L1:(iii) Repair, maintenance, logistics support, or overhaul services for
L0:systems and subsystems, assemblies, subassemblies, and parts integral to a system.
L1:(2) For those subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial products
L0:or commercial services, described in paragraph (f)(1) of this clause, the Contractor
L0:shall require the subcontractor to provide the notification required by paragraph (c)
L0:of this clause to—
L1:(i) The Contractor or higher-tier subcontractor; and
L1:(ii) The ACO and the PCO, if the subcontractor is aware of the ACO and
L0:the PCO for the contract.
L0:(End of clause)

L0:otherwise misrepresented to be an authentic, unmodified electronic part from the
L0:original manufacturer, or a source with the express written authority of the original
L0:manufacturer or current design activity, including an authorized aftermarket
L0:manufacturer. Unlawful or unauthorized substitution includes used electronic
L0:parts represented as new, or the false identification of grade, serial number, lot
L0:number, date code, or performance characteristics.
L0:Electronic part means an integrated circuit, a discrete electronic component
L0:(including, but not limited to, a transistor, capacitor, resistor, or diode), or a circuit
L0:assembly (section 818(f)(2) of Pub. L. 112-81).
L0:Obsolete electronic part means an electronic part that is no longer available from
L0:the original manufacturer or an authorized aftermarket manufacturer.
L0:Original component manufacturer means an organization that designs and/or
L0:engineers a part and is entitled to any intellectual property rights to that part.
L0:Original equipment manufacturer means a company that manufactures products
L0:that it has designed from purchased components and sells those products under the
L0:company's brand name.
L0:Original manufacturer means the original component manufacturer, the original
L0:equipment manufacturer, or the contract manufacturer.
L0:Suspect counterfeit electronic part means an electronic part for which credible
L0:evidence (including, but not limited to, visual inspection or testing) provides
L0:reasonable doubt that the electronic part is authentic.
L1:(b) Acceptable counterfeit electronic part detection and avoidance system. The
L0:Contractor shall establish and maintain an acceptable counterfeit electronic part
L0:detection and avoidance system. Failure to maintain an acceptable counterfeit
L0:electronic part detection and avoidance system, as defined in this clause, may result
L0:in disapproval of the purchasing system by the Contracting Officer and/or
L0:withholding of payments and affect the allowability of costs of counterfeit electronic
L0:parts or suspect counterfeit electronic parts and the cost of rework or corrective
L0:action that may be required to remedy the use or inclusion of such parts (see
L0:DFARS 231.205-71).
L1:(c) System criteria. A counterfeit electronic part detection and avoidance system
L0:shall include risk-based policies and procedures that address, at a minimum, the
L0:following areas:
L1:(1) The training of personnel.
L1:(2) The inspection and testing of electronic parts, including criteria for
L0:acceptance and rejection. Tests and inspections shall be performed in accordance
L0:with accepted Government- and industry-recognized techniques. Selection of tests
L0:and inspections shall be based on minimizing risk to the Government.
L0:Determination of risk shall be based on the assessed probability of receiving a
L0:counterfeit electronic part; the probability that the inspection or test selected will
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 46
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 246
L0:detect a counterfeit electronic part; and the potential negative consequences of a
L0:counterfeit electronic part being installed (e.g., human safety, mission success)
L0:where such consequences are made known to the Contractor.
L1:(3) Processes to abolish counterfeit parts proliferation.
L1:(4) Risk-based processes that enable tracking of electronic parts from the
L0:original manufacturer to product acceptance by the Government, whether the
L0:electronic parts are supplied as discrete electronic parts or are contained in
L0:assemblies, in accordance with paragraph (c) of the clause at 252.246-7008, Sources
L0:of Electronic Parts (also see paragraph (c)(2) of this clause).
L1:(5) Use of suppliers in accordance with the clause at 252.246-7008.
L1:(6) Reporting and quarantining of counterfeit electronic parts and suspect
L0:counterfeit electronic parts. Reporting is required to the Contracting Officer and to
L0:the Government-Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP) when the Contractor
L0:becomes aware of, or has reason to suspect that, any electronic part or end item,
L0:component, part, or assembly containing electronic parts purchased by the DoD, or
L0:purchased by a Contractor for delivery to, or on behalf of, the DoD, contains
L0:counterfeit electronic parts or suspect counterfeit electronic parts. Counterfeit
L0:electronic parts and suspect counterfeit electronic parts shall not be returned to the
L0:seller or otherwise returned to the supply chain until such time that the parts are
L0:determined to be authentic.
L1:(7) Methodologies to identify suspect counterfeit parts and to rapidly
L0:determine if a suspect counterfeit part is, in fact, counterfeit.
L1:(8) Design, operation, and maintenance of systems to detect and avoid
L0:counterfeit electronic parts and suspect counterfeit electronic parts. The Contractor
L0:may elect to use current Government- or industry-recognized standards to meet this
L0:requirement.
L1:(9) Flowdown of counterfeit detection and avoidance requirements,
L0:including applicable system criteria provided herein, to subcontractors at all levels
L0:in the supply chain that are responsible for buying or selling electronic parts or
L0:assemblies containing electronic parts, or for performing authentication testing.
L1:(10) Process for keeping continually informed of current counterfeiting
L0:information and trends, including detection and avoidance techniques contained in
L0:appropriate industry standards, and using such information and techniques for
L0:continuously upgrading internal processes.
L1:(11) Process for screening GIDEP reports and other credible sources of
L0:counterfeiting information to avoid the purchase or use of counterfeit electronic
L0:parts.
L1:(12) Control of obsolete electronic parts in order to maximize the availability
L0:and use of authentic, originally designed, and qualified electronic parts throughout
L0:the product's life cycle.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 46
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 246
L1:(d) Government review and evaluation of the Contractor's policies and
L0:procedures will be accomplished as part of the evaluation of the Contractor's
L0:purchasing system in accordance with 252.244-7001, Contractor Purchasing System
L0:Administration—Basic, or Contractor Purchasing System Administration—
L0:Alternate I.
L1:(e) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause,
L0:excluding the introductory text and including only paragraphs (a) through (e), in
L0:subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial products, for electronic parts or
L0:assemblies containing electronic parts.
L0:(End of clause)

L0:252.246-7008 Sources of Electronic Parts.
L0:As prescribed in 246.870-3(b), use the following clause:
L0:SOURCES OF ELECTRONIC PARTS (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Authorized aftermarket manufacturer means an organization that fabricates a
L0:part under a contract with, or with the express written authority of, the original
L0:component manufacturer based on the original component manufacturer's designs,
L0:formulas, and/or specifications.
L0:Authorized supplier means a supplier, distributor, or an aftermarket
L0:manufacturer with a contractual arrangement with, or the express written
L0:authority of, the original manufacturer or current design activity to buy, stock,
L0:repackage, sell, or distribute the part.
L0:Contract manufacturer means a company that produces goods under contract for
L0:another company under the label or brand name of that company.
L0:Contractor-approved supplier means a supplier that does not have a contractual
L0:agreement with the original component manufacturer for a transaction, but has
L0:been identified as trustworthy by a contractor or subcontractor.
L0:Electronic part means an integrated circuit, a discrete electronic component
L0:(including, but not limited to, a transistor, capacitor, resistor, or diode), or a circuit
L0:assembly (section 818(f)(2) of Pub. L. 112-81).
L0:Original component manufacturer means an organization that designs and/or
L0:engineers a part and is entitled to any intellectual property rights to that part.
L0:Original equipment manufacturer means a company that manufactures products
L0:that it has designed from purchased components and sells those products under the
L0:company's brand name.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 46
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 246
L0:Original manufacturer means the original component manufacturer, the original
L0:equipment manufacturer, or the contract manufacturer.
L1:(b) Selecting suppliers. In accordance with section 818(c)(3) of the National
L0:Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (Pub. L. 112-81), as amended by
L0:section 817 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2015 (Pub. L.
L0:113-291 and section 885 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year
L0:2016 (Pub. L. 114-92)), the Contractor shall—
L1:(1) First obtain electronic parts that are in production by the original
L0:manufacturer or an authorized aftermarket manufacturer or currently available in
L0:stock from—
L1:(i) The original manufacturers of the parts;
L1:(ii) Their authorized suppliers; or
L1:(iii) Suppliers that obtain such parts exclusively from the original
L0:manufacturers of the parts or their authorized suppliers;
L1:(2) If electronic parts are not available as provided in paragraph (b)(1) of
L0:this clause, obtain electronic parts that are not in production by the original
L0:manufacturer or an authorized aftermarket manufacturer, and that are not
L0:currently available in stock from a source listed in paragraph (b)(1) of this clause,
L0:from suppliers identified by the Contractor as contractor-approved suppliers,
L0:provided that—
L1:(i) For identifying and approving such contractor-approved suppliers,
L0:the Contractor uses established counterfeit prevention industry standards and
L0:processes (including inspection, testing, and authentication), such as the DoD-
L0:adopted standards at https://assist.dla.mil;
L1:(ii) The Contractor assumes responsibility for the authenticity of parts
L0:provided by such contractor-approved suppliers; and
L1:(iii) The Contractor's selection of such contractor-approved suppliers is
L0:subject to review, audit, and approval by the Government, generally in conjunction
L0:with a contractor purchasing system review or other surveillance of purchasing
L0:practices by the contract administration office, or if the Government obtains
L0:credible evidence that a contractor-approved supplier has provided counterfeit
L0:parts. The Contractor may proceed with the acquisition of electronic parts from a
L0:contractor-approved supplier unless otherwise notified by DoD; or
L2:(3)(i) Take the actions in paragraphs paragraph (b)(3)(ii) of this clause if the
L0:Contractor—
L1:(A) Obtains an electronic part from—
L0:paragraph (b)(1) or (b)(2) of this clause, due to nonavailability from such sources; or
L1:(1) A source other than any of the sources identified in
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 46
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 246
L0:refuses to accept flowdown of this clause; or
L1:(2) A subcontractor (other than the original manufacturer) that
L1:(B) Cannot confirm that an electronic part is new or previously
L0:unused and that it has not been comingled in supplier new production or stock with
L0:used, refurbished, reclaimed, or returned parts.
L1:(ii) If the contractor obtains an electronic part or cannot confirm an
L0:electronic part pursuant to paragraph (b)(3)(i) of this clause—
L1:(A) Promptly notify the Contracting Officer in writing. If such
L0:notification is required for an electronic part to be used in a designated lot of
L0:assemblies to be acquired under a single contract, the Contractor may submit one
L0:notification for the lot, providing identification of the assemblies containing the
L0:parts (e.g., serial numbers);
L0:accordance with existing applicable industry standards; and
L1:(B) Be responsible for inspection, testing, and authentication, in
L0:such electronic parts available to the Government upon request.
L1:(C) Make documentation of inspection, testing, and authentication of
L1:(c) Traceability. If the Contractor is not the original manufacturer of, or
L0:authorized supplier for, an electronic part, the Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Have risk-based processes (taking into consideration the consequences of
L0:failure of an electronic part) that enable tracking of electronic parts from the
L0:original manufacturer to product acceptance by the Government, whether the
L0:electronic part is supplied as a discrete electronic part or is contained in an
L0:assembly;
L1:(2) If the Contractor cannot establish this traceability from the original
L0:manufacturer for a specific electronic part, be responsible for inspection, testing,
L0:and authentication, in accordance with existing applicable industry standards; and
L2:(3)(i) Maintain documentation of traceability (paragraph (c)(1) of this
L0:clause) or the inspection, testing, and authentication required when traceability
L0:cannot be established (paragraph (c)(2) of this clause) in accordance with FAR
L0:subpart 4.7; and
L1:(ii) Make such documentation available to the Government upon
L0:request.
L1:(d) Government sources. Contractors and subcontractors are still required to
L0:comply with the requirements of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this clause, as applicable,
L0:if—
L1:(1) Authorized to purchase electronic parts from the Federal Supply
L0:Schedule;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 46
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 246
L1:(2) Purchasing electronic parts from suppliers accredited by the Defense
L0:Microelectronics Activity; or
L1:(3) Requisitioning electronic parts from Government inventory/stock under
L0:the authority of 252.251-7000, Ordering from Government Supply Sources.
L1:(i) The cost of any required inspection, testing, and authentication of
L0:such parts may be charged as a direct cost.
L1:(ii) The Government is responsible for the authenticity of the
L0:requisitioned parts. If any such part is subsequently found to be counterfeit or
L0:suspect counterfeit, the Government will—
L1:(A) Promptly replace such part at no charge; and
L1:(B) Consider an adjustment in the contract schedule to the extent
L0:that replacement of the counterfeit or suspect counterfeit electronic parts caused a
L0:delay in performance.
L1:(e) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause,
L0:including this paragraph (e), in subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial
L0:products, that are for electronic parts or assemblies containing electronic parts,
L0:unless the subcontractor is the original manufacturer.

title: 247.570 Scope
content:
L0:247.570 Scope.
L0:This subpart—
L1:(a) Implements—
L1:(1) The Military Cargo Preference Act of 1904 (“the 1904 Act”), 10 U.S.C. 2631,
L0:which applies to the ocean transportation of cargo owned by, destined for use by, or
L0:otherwise transported by DoD;
L1:(2) Section 1017 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal
L0:Year (FY) 2007 (Pub. L. 109-364) (10 U.S.C. 2631 note), which requires consideration, in
L0:solicitations requiring a covered vessel, of the extent to which offerors have had
L0:overhaul, repair, and maintenance work performed in shipyards located in the United
L0:States or Guam;
L1:(3) Section 3504 of the NDAA for FY 2009 (Pub. L. 110-417) (10 U.S.C. chapter
L0:257 note), which addresses requirements that apply to riding gang members and DoD-
L0:exempted individuals (see 252.247-7027(c)) who perform work on U.S.-flag vessels
L0:under DoD contracts for transportation services documented under 46 U.S.C. chapter
L0:121; and
L1:(4) Section 1024 of the NDAA for FY 2021 (Pub. L. 116-283), which updates the
L0:listed circumstances where DoD may waive the requirement that DoD supplies be
L0:transported by sea in vessels belonging to the United States or vessels of the United
L0:States, and it modifies the requirement for reflagging or repair work in the United
L0:States for vessels used under time-charter contracts.
L1:(b) Does not specifically implement the Cargo Preference Act of 1954 (“the 1954
L0:Act”), 46 U.S.C. chapter 553. The 1954 Act is applicable to DoD, but DFARS coverage is
L0:not required because compliance with the 1904 Act historically has resulted in DoD
L0:exceeding the 1954 Act's requirements; and
L1:(c) Does not implement—
L1:(1) Section 27 of the Merchant Marine Act, 1920 (46 U.S.C. chapters 121 and
L0:552), commonly known as the “Jones Act,” for the application of coastwise trade; or
L1:(2) Waivers thereof pursuant to 46 U.S.C. 501.

title: 247.571 Definitions
content:
L0:247.571 Definitions.
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Corrective and preventive maintenance or repair” means—
L1:(1) Maintenance or repair actions performed as a result of a failure in order to
L0:return or restore equipment to acceptable performance levels; and
L1:(2) Scheduled maintenance or repair actions to prevent or discover functional
L0:failures.
L0:“Covered vessel” means a vessel—
L1:(1) Owned, operated, or controlled by the offeror; and
L1:(2) Qualified to engage in the carriage of cargo in the coastwise or noncontiguous
L0:trade under 46 U.S.C. 12112 and 50501 and 46 U.S.C. chapter 551.
L0:“Foreign-flag vessel” means any vessel that is not a U.S.-flag vessel.
L0:“Ocean transportation” means any water-borne transportation aboard a ship, vessel,
L0:boat, barge, ferry, or the like outside the internal waters of the United States (as
L0:defined in 33 CFR 2.24).
L0:“Overhaul, repair, and maintenance work” means work requiring a shipyard period
L0:greater than or equal to 5 calendar days.
L0:“Reflagging or repair work” means work performed on a vessel—
L1:(1) To enable the vessel to meet applicable standards to become a vessel of the
L0:United States; or
L1:(2) To convert the vessel to a more useful military configuration.
L0:“Supplies” means supplies that are clearly identifiable for eventual use by or owned by
L0:DoD at the time of transportation by sea, or are otherwise transported by DoD,
L0:regardless of ownership or use by DoD. An item is clearly identifiable for eventual use
L0:by DoD if, for example, the contract documentation contains a reference to a DoD
L0:contract number or a military destination.
L0:“U.S.-flag vessel” means either a vessel belonging to the United States or a vessel of the
L0:United States as that term is defined in 46 U.S.C. 116.
subpart: SUBPART 247.5 — OCEAN TRANSPORTATION BY U.S.-FLAG VESSELS

title: 247.572 Policy
content:
L0:247.572 Policy.
L1:(a) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2631(a), DoD contractors are required to transport
L0:supplies exclusively on U.S.-flag vessels. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2631(b), DoD (see
L0:247.573(a)) may waive this requirement when a U.S.-flag vessel—
L1:(1) Is not available at a fair and reasonable rate for commercial vessels of the
L0:United States; or
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L1:(2) Is not otherwise available.
L1:(b) Contracts must provide for the use of vessels belonging to the United States
L0:when security classifications prohibit the use of other than vessels belonging to the
L0:United States.
L1:(c) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2631(c)—
L1:(1) Any vessel used under a time charter contract for the transportation of
L0:supplies under this section are required to have the following work performed in the
L0:United States or its outlying areas:
L1:(i) Reflagging or repair work, if the reflagging or repair work is performed—
L0:to the solicitation for the contract; and
L1:(A) On a vessel for which the contractor submitted an offer in response
L1:(B) Prior to acceptance of the vessel by the Government.
L1:(ii) Corrective and preventive maintenance or repair work for the duration
L0:of the contract, to the greatest extent practicable.
L1:(2) The Secretary of Defense may waive this requirement if the Secretary
L0:determines that such waiver is critical to the national security of the United States. In
L0:accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2631(c)(2), DoD must immediately submit, in writing, a
L0:notice to the congressional committees listed at 10 U.S.C. 2631(e) of such a waiver and
L0:the reason for the waiver.
L1:(d) In accordance with section 1017 of the NDAA for FY 2007 (Pub. L. 109-364),
L0:when obtaining carriage requiring a covered vessel, the consider the extent to which
L0:offerors have had overhaul, repair, and maintenance work for covered vessels
L0:performed in shipyards located in the United States or Guam.
L1:(e) In accordance with section 3504 of the NDAA for FY 2009 (Pub. L. 110-417), do
L0:not award, renew or extend, or exercise an option under a charter of, or contract for
L0:carriage of cargo by, a U.S.-flag vessel documented under 46 U.S.C. chapter 121, unless
L0:the contract contains the clause at 252.247-7027.

L1:(2) Follow the procedures at PGI 247.573(b)(2) when direct purchase of ocean
L0:transportation services is the principal purpose of the contract.
L1:(3) See PGI 247.573(b)(3) for agency and department procedures relating to
L0:annual reporting requirements of waivers granted for nonavailability of U.S.-flag
L0:vessels.
L1:(4) Follow the procedures at PGI 247.573(b)(4) to accomplish security
L0:background checks pursuant to clause 252.247-7027, Riding Gang Member
L0:Requirements.
L2:(5)(i) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2631(d), exercise contractual rights and
L0:remedies against contractors who fail to comply. Such remedies may include the
L0:determination that a contractor is ineligible for award of future contracts, termination
L0:of an existing contract, or suspension or debarment of the contractor. See part 242
L0:regarding assessments of the contractor's past performance.
L1:(ii) Consider an equitable adjustment in the event of a contractor's
L0:unauthorized use of foreign-flag vessels in the performance of a contract.

title: 252.247-7000 Hardship conditions
content:
L0:252.247-7000 Hardship conditions.
L0:As prescribed in 247.270-4(a), use the following clause:
L0:HARDSHIP CONDITIONS (AUG 2000)
L1:(a) If the Contractor finds unusual ship, dock, or cargo conditions associated with
L0:loading or unloading a particular cargo, that will work a hardship on the Contractor if
L0:loaded or unloaded at the basic commodity rates, the Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Notify the Contracting Officer before performing the work, if feasible, but no
L0:later than the vessel sailing time; and
L1:(2) Submit any associated request for price adjustment to the Contracting
L0:Officer within 10 working days of the vessel sailing time.
L1:(b) Unusual conditions include, but are not limited to, inaccessibility of place of
L0:stowage to the ship's cargo gear, side port operations, and small quantities of cargo in
L0:any one hatch.
L1:(c) The Contracting Officer will investigate the conditions promptly after receiving
L0:the notice. If the Contracting Officer finds that the conditions are unusual and do
L0:materially affect the cost of loading or unloading, the Contracting Officer will authorize
L0:payment at the applicable man-hour rates set forth in the schedule of rates of this
L0:contract.

title: 252.247-7002 Revision of prices
content:
L0:252.247-7002 Revision of prices.
L0:As prescribed in 247.270-4(b), use the following clause:
L0:REVISION OF PRICES (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Definition. Wage adjustment, as used in this clause, means a change in the
L0:wages, salaries, or other terms or conditions of employment which—
L1:(1) Substantially affects the cost of performing this contract;
L1:(2) Is generally applicable to the port where work under this contract is
L0:performed; and
L1:(3) Applies to operations by the Contractor on non-Government work as well as
L0:to work under this contract.
L1:(b) General. The prices fixed in this contract are based on wages and working
L0:conditions established by collective bargaining agreements, and on other conditions in
L0:effect on the date of this contract. The Contracting Officer and the Contractor may
L0:agree to increase or decrease such prices in accordance with this clause.
L1:(c) Demand for negotiation. (1) At any time, subject to the limitations specified in
L0:this clause, either the Contracting Officer or the Contractor may deliver to the other a
L0:written demand that the parties negotiate to revise the prices under this contract.
L1:(2) No such demand shall be made before 90 days after the date of this contract,
L0:and thereafter neither party shall make a demand having an effective date within 90
L0:days of the effective date of any prior demand. However, this limitation does not apply
L0:to a wage adjustment during the 90 day period.
L1:(3) Each demand shall specify a date (the same as or subsequent to the date of
L0:the delivery of the demand) as to when the revised prices shall be effective. This date is
L0:the effective date of the price revision.
L1:(i) If the Contractor makes a demand under this clause, the demand shall
L0:briefly state the basis of the demand and include the statements and data referred to in
L0:paragraph (d) of this clause.
L1:(ii) If the demand is made by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall
L0:furnish the statements and data within 30 days of the delivery of the demand.
L1:(d) Submission of data. At the times specified in paragraphs (c)(3)(i) and (ii) of this
L0:clause, the Contractor shall submit—
L1:(1) A new estimate and breakdown of the unit cost and the proposed prices for
L0:the services the Contractor will perform under this contract after the effective date of
L0:the price revision, itemized to be consistent with the original negotiations of the
L0:contract;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L1:(2) An explanation of the difference between the original (or last preceding)
L0:estimate and the new estimate;
L1:(3) Such relevant operating data, cost records, overhead absorption reports, and
L0:accounting statements as may be of assistance in determining the accuracy and
L0:reliability of the new estimate;
L1:(4) A statement of the actual costs of performance under this contract to the
L0:extent that they are available at the time of the negotiation of the revision of prices
L0:under this clause; and
L1:(5) Any other relevant data usually furnished in the case of negotiations of
L0:prices under a new contract. The Government may examine and audit the Contractor's
L0:accounts, records, and books as the Contracting Officer considers necessary.
L1:(e) Negotiations. (1) Upon the filing of the statements and data required by
L0:paragraph (d) of this clause, the Contractor and the Contracting Officer shall negotiate
L0:promptly in good faith to agree upon prices for services the Contractor will perform on
L0:and after the effective date of the price revision.
L1:(2) If the prices in this contract were established by competitive negotiation,
L0:they shall not be revised upward unless justified by changes in conditions occurring
L0:after the contract was awarded.
L1:(3) The agreement reached after each negotiation will be incorporated into the
L0:contract by supplemental agreement.
L1:(f) Disagreements. If, within 30 days after the date on which statements and data are
L0:required pursuant to paragraph (c) of this clause, the Contracting Officer and the
L0:Contractor fail to agree to revised prices, the failure to agree shall be resolved in
L0:accordance with the Disputes clause of this contract. The prices fixed by the Contracting
L0:Officer will remain in effect for the balance of the contract, and the Contractor shall
L0:continue performance.
L1:(g) Retroactive changes in wages or working conditions. (1) In the event of a
L0:retroactive wage adjustment, the Contractor or the Contracting Officer may request an
L0:equitable adjustment in the prices in this contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall request a price adjustment within 30 days of any
L0:retroactive wage adjustment. The Contractor shall support its request with—
L1:(i) An estimate of the changes in cost resulting from the retroactive wage
L0:adjustment;
L1:(ii) Complete information upon which the estimate is based; and
L1:(iii) A certified copy of the collective bargaining agreement, arbitration
L0:award, or other document evidencing the retroactive wage adjustment.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L1:(3) Subject to the limitation in paragraph (g)(2) of this clause as to the time of
L0:making a request, completion or termination of this contract shall not affect the
L0:Contractor's right under paragraph (g) of this clause.
L1:(4) In case of disagreement concerning any question of fact, including whether
L0:any adjustment should be made, or the amount of such adjustment, the disagreement
L0:will be resolved in accordance with the Disputes clause of this contract.
L1:(5) The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing of any request
L0:by or on behalf of the employees of the Contractor which may result in a retroactive
L0:wage adjustment. The notice shall be given within 20 days after the request, or if the
L0:request occurs before contract execution, at the time of execution.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.247-7007 Liability and insurance
content:
L0:252.247-7007 Liability and insurance.
L0:As prescribed in 247.270-4(c), use the following clause:
L0:LIABILITY AND INSURANCE (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall be—
L1:(1) Liable to the Government for loss or damage to property, real and personal,
L0:owned by the Government or for which the Government is liable;
L1:(2) Responsible for, and hold the Government harmless from, loss of or damage
L0:to property not included in paragraph (a)(1); and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L1:(3) Responsible for, and hold the Government harmless from, bodily injury and
L0:death of persons, resulting either in whole or in part from the negligence or fault of the
L0:Contractor, its officers, agents, or employees in the performance of work under this
L0:contract.
L1:(b) For the purpose of this clause, all cargo loaded or unloaded under this contract is
L0:agreed to be property owned by the Government or property for which the Government
L0:is liable.
L1:(1) The amount of the loss or damage as determined by the Contracting Officer
L0:will be withheld from payments otherwise due the Contractor.
L1:(2) Determination of liability and responsibility by the Contracting Officer will
L0:constitute questions of fact within the meaning of the Disputes clause of this contract.
L1:(c) The general liability and responsibility of the Contractor under this clause are
L0:subject only to the following specific limitations. The Contractor is not responsible to the
L0:Government for, and does not agree to hold the Government harmless from, loss or
L0:damage to property or bodily injury to or death of persons if—
L1:(1) The unseaworthiness of the vessel, or failure or defect of the gear or
L0:equipment furnished by the Government, contributed jointly with the fault or
L0:negligence of the Contractor in causing such damage, injury, or death; and
L1:(i) The Contractor, his officers, agents, and employees, by the exercise of due
L0:diligence, could not have discovered such unseaworthiness or defect of gear or
L0:equipment; or
L1:(ii) Through the exercise of due diligence could not otherwise have avoided
L0:such damage, injury, or death.
L1:(2) The damage, injury, or death resulted solely from an act or omission of the
L0:Government or its employees, or resulted solely from proper compliance by officers,
L0:agents, or employees of the Contractor with specific directions of the Contracting
L0:Officer.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall at its own expense acquire and maintain insurance during
L0:the term of this contract, as follows—
L1:(1) Standard workmen's compensation and employer's liability insurance and
L0:longshoremen's and harbor workers' compensation insurance, or such of these as may
L0:be proper under applicable state or Federal statutes.
L1:(i) The Contractor may, with the prior approval of the Contracting Officer,
L0:be a self-insurer against the risk of this paragraph (d)(1).
L1:(ii) This approval will be given upon receipt of satisfactory evidence that the
L0:Contractor has qualified as a self-insurer under applicable provision of law.
L1:(2) Bodily injury liability insurance in an amount of not less than $300,000 on
L0:account of any one occurrence.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L1:(3) Property damage liability insurance (which shall include any and all
L0:property, whether or not in the care, custody, or control of the Contractor) in an amount
L0:of not less than $300,000 for any one occurrence.
L1:(e) Each policy shall provide, by appropriate endorsement or otherwise, that
L0:cancellation or material change in the policy shall not be effective until after a 30 day
L0:written notice is furnished the Contracting Officer.
L1:(f) The Contractor shall furnish the Contracting Officer with satisfactory evidence of
L0:the insurance required in paragraph (d) before performance of any work under this
L0:contract.
L1:(g) The Contractor shall, at its own cost and expense, defend any suits, demands,
L0:claims, or actions, in which the United States might be named as a co-defendant of the
L0:Contractor, resulting from the Contractor's performance of work under this contract.
L0:This requirement is without regard to whether such suit, demand, claim, or action was
L0:the result of the Contractor's negligence. The Government shall have the right to
L0:appear in such suit, participate in defense, and take such actions as may be necessary
L0:to protect the interest of the United States.
L1:(h) It is expressly agreed that the provisions in paragraphs (d) through (g) of this
L0:clause shall not in any manner limit the liability or extend the liability of the Contractor
L0:as provided in paragraphs (a) through (c) of this clause.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Equitably reimburse the Government if the Contractor is indemnified,
L0:reimbursed, or relieved of any loss or damage to Government property;
L1:(2) Do nothing to prevent the Government's right to recover against third
L0:parties for any such loss or damage; and
L1:(3) Furnish the Government, upon the request of the Contracting Officer, at the
L0:Government's expense, all reasonable assistance and cooperation in obtaining recovery,
L0:including the prosecution of suit and the execution of instruments of assignment in
L0:favor of the Government.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.247-7016 Contractor liability for loss or damage
content:
L0:252.247-7016 Contractor liability for loss or damage.
L0:As prescribed in 247.271-3(d), use the following clause:
L0:CONTRACTOR LIABILITY FOR LOSS OR DAMAGE (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Article means any shipping piece or package and its contents.
L0:Schedule means the level of service for which specific types of traffic apply as described
L0:in DoD 4500.34-R, Personal Property Traffic Management Regulation.
L1:(b) For shipments picked up under Schedule I, Outbound Services, or delivered
L0:under Schedule II, Inbound Services—
L1:(1) If notified within one year after delivery that the owner has discovered loss
L0:or damage to the owner's property, the Contractor agrees to indemnify the Government
L0:for loss or damage to the property which arises from any cause while it is in the
L0:Contractor's possession. The Contractor's liability is—
L1:(i) Non-negligent damage. For any cause, other than the Contractor's
L0:negligence, indemnification shall be at a rate not to exceed sixty cents per pound per
L0:article.
L1:(ii) Negligent damage. When loss or damage is caused by the negligence of
L0:the Contractor, the liability is for the full cost of satisfactory repair or for the current
L0:replacement value of the article.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall make prompt payment to the owner of the property for
L0:any loss or damage for which the Contractor is liable.
L1:(3) In the absence of evidence or supporting documentation which places
L0:liability on a carrier or another contractor, the destination contractor shall be presumed
L0:to be liable for the loss or damage, if timely notified.
L1:(c) For shipments picked up or delivered under Schedule III, Intra-City and Intra-
L0:Area—
L1:(1) If notified of loss or damage within 75 days following delivery, the Contractor
L0:agrees to indemnify the Government for loss or damage to the owner's property.
L1:(2) The Contractor's liability shall be for the full cost of satisfactory repair, or for
L0:the current replacement value of the article less depreciation, up to a maximum liability
L0:of $1.25 per pound times the net weight of the shipment.
L1:(3) The Contractor has full salvage rights to damaged items which are not repairable
L0:and for which the Government has received compensation at replacement value.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L0:(End of clause)
