title: 252.247-7023 Transportation of Supplies by Sea
content:
L0:252.247-7023 Transportation of Supplies by Sea.
L0:As prescribed in 247.574(a) and (a)(1), use the following basic clause:
L0:TRANSPORTATION OF SUPPLIES BY SEA—BASIC (OCT 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Foreign-flag vessel means any vessel that is not a U.S.-flag vessel.
L0:Ocean transportation means any water-borne transportation aboard a ship, vessel, boat,
L0:barge, ferry, or the like outside the internal waters of the United States as defined in 33
L0:CFR 2.24.
L0:Subcontractor means a supplier, materialman, distributor, or vendor at any level below
L0:the prime contractor whose contractual obligation to perform results from, or is
L0:conditioned upon, award of the prime contract and who is performing any part of the
L0:work or other requirement of the prime contract.
L0:Supplies means supplies that are clearly identifiable for eventual use by or owned by
L0:DoD at the time of transportation by sea, or are otherwise transported by DoD,
L0:regardless of ownership or use by DoD. An item is clearly identifiable for eventual use
L0:by DoD if, for example, the contract documentation contains a reference to a DoD
L0:contract number or a military destination.
L0:U.S.-flag vessel means either a vessel belonging to the United States or a vessel of the
L0:United States as that term is defined in 46 U.S.C. 116.
L1:(b) If the transportation of supplies by sea is anticipated under this contract, the
L0:Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Notify the Contracting Officer and Maritime Administration (MARAD) at
L0:Cargo.Marad@dot.gov—
L1:(i) Within 3 business days after contract award; or
L1:(ii) Immediately prior to the shipment departure date necessary to meet
L0:delivery schedules, whichever is earlier; and
L1:(2) Include in the notification—
L1:(i) A statement of the Contractor's intent to transport supplies by sea;
L1:(ii) The contract number; and
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L1:(iii) The task-order or delivery-order number, when applicable.
L2:(c)(1) The Contractor shall use U.S.-flag vessels when transporting any supplies by
L0:sea under this contract.
L1:(2) A subcontractor transporting supplies by sea under this contract shall use
L0:U.S.-flag vessels if—
L1:(i) This contract is a construction contract; or
L1:(ii) The supplies being transported are—
L1:(A) Other than commercial products or
L1:(B) Commercial products that—
L1:(1) The Contractor is reselling or distributing to the Government without adding
L0:value (generally, the Contractor does not add value to items that it contracts for f.o.b.
L0:destination shipment);
L1:(2) Are shipped in direct support of U.S. military contingency operations,
L0:exercises, or forces deployed in humanitarian or peacekeeping operations; or
L1:(3) Are commissary or exchange cargoes transported outside of the Defense
L0:Transportation System in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2643.
L1:(d) The Contractor and its subcontractors may request, via the Contracting Officer, a
L0:waiver of the requirement to use a U.S.-flag vessel, or identification of any available
L0:U.S.-flag vessels, if the Contractor or a subcontractor sufficiently explains that—
L1:(1) U.S.-flag vessels are not available at a fair and reasonable rate for
L0:commercial vessels of the United States; or
L1:(2) U.S.-flag vessels are otherwise not available.
L1:(e) The Contractor must submit any request for use of foreign-flag vessels in writing
L0:to the Contracting Officer at least 45 days prior to the sailing date necessary to meet its
L0:delivery schedules. The Contracting Officer will process requests submitted after such
L0:date(s) as expeditiously as possible, however, if a DoD waiver is not approved prior to
L0:the shipper's sailing date, this will not of itself constitute a compensable delay under
L0:this or any other clause of this contract. Requests shall contain at a minimum—
L1:(1) Type, weight, and cube of cargo;
L1:(2) Required shipping date(s) and required delivery date(s);
L1:(3) Special handling and discharge requirements;
L1:(4) Loading and discharge points;
L1:(5) Name of shipper and consignee;
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L1:(6) Prime contract number; and
L1:(7) A documented description of current, diligent efforts made to secure U.S.-flag
L0:vessels, including points of contact (with names and telephone numbers) with at least
L0:two U.S.-flag carriers contacted. Copies of quotes will suffice for this purpose. Copies of
L0:telephone notes, emails, and other relevant communications will otherwise be
L0:considered for this purpose.
L1:(f) The Contractor shall, within 30 days after each shipment covered by this clause,
L0:provide the Contracting Officer and MARAD at Cargo.Marad@dot.gov, Attention:
L0:Military Team, one copy of the rated on board vessel operating carrier's ocean bill of
L0:lading, which shall contain the following information:
L1:(1) Prime contract number;
L1:(2) Name of vessel;
L1:(3) Vessel flag of registry;
L1:(4) Date of loading;
L1:(5) Port of loading;
L1:(6) Port of final discharge;
L1:(7) Description of commodity;
L1:(8) Gross weight in pounds and cubic feet if available;
L1:(9) Total ocean freight in U.S. dollars; and
L1:(10) Name of the carrier.
L1:(g) If this contract exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold, the Contractor shall
L0:provide with its final invoice under this contract a representation that to the best of its
L0:knowledge and belief—
L1:(1) No ocean transportation was used in the performance of this contract;
L1:(2) Ocean transportation was used and only U.S.-flag vessels were used for all
L0:ocean shipments under the contract;
L1:(3) Ocean transportation was used, and the Contractor had received a prior-
L0:approved waiver for U.S.-flag vessels for all foreign-flag ocean transportation; or
L1:(4) Ocean transportation was used and some or all of the shipments were made
L0:on foreign-flag vessels without the written consent of DoD. The Contractor shall
L0:describe these shipments in the following format:
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L0:Item Description
L0:Contract Line Items
L0:Quantity
L0:Total
L1:(h) If this contract exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold and the final invoice

title: 252.247-7025 Reflagging or Repair Work
content:
L0:252.247-7025 Reflagging or Repair Work.
L0:As prescribed in 247.574(b), use the following clause:
L0:REFLAGGING OR REPAIR WORK (OCT 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Corrective and preventive maintenance or repair means—
L1:(1) Maintenance or repair actions performed as a result of a failure in order to
L0:return or restore equipment to acceptable performance levels; and
L1:(2) Scheduled maintenance or repair actions to prevent or discover functional
L0:failures.
L0:Reflagging or repair work means work performed on a vessel—
L1:(1) To enable the vessel to meet applicable standards to become a vessel of the
L0:United States; or
L1:(2) To convert the vessel to a more useful military configuration.
L1:(b) Requirement. Unless DoD waives this requirement, the Contractor shall ensure
L0:performance of the following in the United States or its outlying areas:
L1:(1) Reflagging or repair work, if the reflagging or repair work is performed—
L1:(i) On a vessel for which the Contractor submitted an offer in response to the
L0:solicitation for this contract; and
L1:(ii) Prior to acceptance of the vessel by the Government.
L1:(2) Corrective and preventive maintenance or repair work for the duration of the
L0:contract, to the greatest extent practicable.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.247-7026 Evaluation Preference for Use of Domestic Shipyards—
content:
L0:252.247-7026 Evaluation Preference for Use of Domestic Shipyards—
L0:Applicable to Acquisition of Carriage by Vessel for DoD Cargo in the
L0:Coastwise or Noncontiguous Trade.
L0:As prescribed in 247.574(c), use the following provision:
L0:EVALUATION PREFERENCE FOR USE OF DOMESTIC SHIPYARDS—
L0:APPLICABLE TO ACQUISITION OF CARRIAGE BY VESSEL FOR DOD CARGO IN
L0:THE COASTWISE OR NONCONTIGUOUS TRADE (OCT 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this provision—
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L0:Covered vessel means a vessel—
L1:(1) Owned, operated, or controlled by the offeror; and
L1:(2) Qualified to engage in the carriage of cargo in the coastwise or noncontiguous
L0:trade under 46 U.S.C. 12112 and 50501 and 46 U.S.C. chapter 551.
L0:Foreign shipyard means a shipyard that is not a U.S. shipyard.
L0:Overhaul, repair, and maintenance work means work requiring a shipyard period
L0:greater than or equal to 5 calendar days.
L0:U.S. shipyard means a shipyard that is located in any State of the United States or in
L0:Guam.
L1:(b) This solicitation includes an evaluation criterion that considers the extent to
L0:which the Offeror has had overhaul, repair, and maintenance work for covered vessels
L0:performed in U.S. shipyards.
L1:(c) The Offeror shall provide the following information with its offer, addressing all
L0:covered vessels for which overhaul, repair, and maintenance work has been performed
L0:during the period covering the current calendar year, up to the date of proposal
L0:submission, and the preceding four calendar years:
L1:(1) Name of vessel.
L1:(2) Description and cost of qualifying shipyard work performed in U.S.
L0:shipyards.
L1:(3) Description and cost of qualifying shipyard work performed in foreign
L0:shipyards and whether—
L1:(i) Such work was performed as emergency repairs in foreign shipyards due
L0:to accident, emergency, Act of God, or an infirmity to the vessel, and safety
L0:considerations warranted taking the vessel to a foreign shipyard; or
L1:(ii) Such work was paid for or reimbursed by the U.S. Government.
L1:(4) Names of shipyards that performed the work.
L1:(5) Inclusive dates of work performed.
L1:(d) Offerors are responsible for submitting accurate information. The Contracting
L0:Officer—
L1:(1) Will use the information to evaluate offers in accordance with the criteria
L0:specified in the solicitation; and
L1:(2) Reserves the right to request supporting documentation if determined
L0:necessary in the proposal evaluation process.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L1:(e) The Department of Defense will provide the information submitted in response to
L0:this provision to the congressional defense committees, as required by section 1017 of
L0:Public Law 109-364 (10 U.S.C. 2631 note).

title: 252.247-7027 Riding Gang Member Requirements
content:
L0:252.247-7027 Riding Gang Member Requirements.
L0:As prescribed in 247.574(d), use the following clause:
L0:(End of provision)
L0:RIDING GANG MEMBER REQUIREMENTS (MAY 2018)
L1:(a) Definition. Riding gang member, as used in this clause, has the same definition
L0:as “riding gang member” in title 46 U.S.C. 2101.
L1:(b) Requirements relating to riding gang members. Notwithstanding 46 U.S.C. 8106,
L0:the Contractor shall ensure each riding gang member holds a valid U.S. Merchant
L0:Mariner's Document issued under 46 U.S.C. chapter 73, or a transportation security
L0:card issued under section 70105 of such title.
L1:(c) Exemption. (1) An individual is exempt from the requirements of paragraph (b) of
L0:this clause and shall not be treated as a riding gang member for the purposes of section
L0:8106 of title 46, if that individual is on a vessel for purposes other than engaging in the
L0:operation or maintenance of the vessel and is—
L1:(i) One of the personnel who accompanies, supervises, guards, or maintains
L0:unit equipment aboard a ship, commonly referred to as supercargo personnel;
L1:(ii) One of the force protection personnel of the vessel;
L1:(iii) A specialized repair technician; or
L1:(iv) An individual who is otherwise required by the Secretary of Defense or
L0:designee to be aboard the vessel.
L1:(2) Any individual who is exempt under paragraph (c)(1) of this clause must
L0:pass a DoD background check before going aboard the vessel.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall—
L1:(A) Render all necessary assistance to U.S. Armed Forces personnel
L0:with respect to the identification and screening of exempted individuals. This will
L0:require, at a minimum, the Contractor to submit the name and other biographical
L0:information necessary to the Government official specified in the contract for the
L0:purposes of conducting a background check; and
L1:(B) Deny access or immediately remove any individual(s) from the vessel
L0:deemed unsuitable for any reason by the Government agency conducting the
L0:background checks. The Contractor agrees to replace any such individual promptly and
L0:require such replacements to fully comply with all screening requirements.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 47
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 247
L1:(ii) The head of the contracting activity may waive this requirement if the
L0:individual possesses a valid U.S. Merchant Mariner's Document issued under 46 U.S.C.
L0:chapter 73, or a transportation security card issued under section 70105 of such title.
L1:(3) An individual exempted under paragraph (c)(1) of this clause is not treated
L0:as a riding gang member and shall not be counted as an individual in addition to the
L0:crew for the purposes of 46 U.S.C. 3304.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 249.501-70 Special termination costs
content:
L0:249.501-70 Special termination costs.
L1:(a) The clause at 252.249-7000, Special Termination Costs, may be used in an
L0:incrementally funded contract when its use is approved by the agency head.
L1:(b) The clause is authorized when—
L1:(1) The contract term is two years or more;
L1:(2) The contract is estimated to require—
L1:(i) Total RDT&E financing in excess of $25 million; or
L1:(ii) Total production investment in excess of $100 million; and
L1:(3) Adequate funds are available to cover the contingent reserve liability for
L0:special termination costs.
L1:(c) The contractor and the contracting officer must agree upon an amount that
L0:represents their best estimate of the total special termination costs to which the
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 49
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 249
L0:contractor would be entitled in the event of termination of the contract. Insert this
L0:amount in paragraph (c) of the clause.
L2:(d)(1) Consider substituting an alternate paragraph (c) for paragraph (c) of the basic
L0:clause when—
L1:(i) The contract covers an unusually long performance period; or
L1:(ii) The contractor's cost risk associated with contingent special termination
L0:costs is expected to fluctuate extensively over the period of the contract.
L1:(2) The alternate paragraph (c) should provide for periodic negotiation and
L0:adjustment of the amount reserved for special termination costs. Occasions for periodic
L0:adjustment may include—
L1:(i) The Government's incremental assignment of funds to the contract;
L1:(ii) The time when certain performance milestones are accomplished by the
L0:contractor; or
L1:(iii) Other specific time periods agreed upon by the contracting officer and
L0:the contractor.

L1:(b) Settlement proposals. Ensure that the Canadian Commercial Corporation
L0:submits—
L1:(1) Termination settlement proposals that—

L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 49

title: 249.7003 Notification of anticipated contract terminations or reductions
content:
L0:249.7003 Notification of anticipated contract terminations or reductions.
L1:(a) Section 1372 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1994
L0:(Pub. L. 103-160) and section 824 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal
L0:Year 1997 (Pub. L. 104-201) are intended to help establish benefit eligibility under the
L0:Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (29 U.S.C. Chapter 32) for employees of
L0:DoD contractors and subcontractors adversely affected by termination or substantial

L0:appropriations act; and

L0:anticipated termination of or substantial reduction in the funding of affected
L0:contracts—
L1:(i) Directly to the Secretary of Labor; and
L1:(ii) Through the contracting officer to each prime contractor.
L1:(c) When subcontracts have been issued, the prime contractor is responsible for—

L0:first-tier subcontractors with a subcontract valued equal to or greater than $700,000;

L0:greater than $150,000; and

L0:valued greater than $150,000 at all tiers.

L0:acquire a major system (as defined in 10 U.S.C. 3041(a)).
L1:(b) Scope. This clause implements section 1372 of the National Defense
L0:Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1994 (Pub. L. 103-160) and section 824 of the National

L0:(29 U.S.C. Chapter 32) for employees of DoD contractors and subcontractors adversely
L0:affected by contract terminations or substantial reductions under major defense
L0:programs.
L0:Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 49
L0:Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Part 249
L1:(c) Notice to employees and state and local officials.

title: 252.203-7000 Requirements Relating to Compensation of Former DoD Officials
content:
L0:252.203-7000 Requirements Relating to Compensation of Former DoD Officials.
L0:As prescribed in 203.171-4 (a), use the following clause:
L0:REQUIREMENTS RELATING TO COMPENSATION OF FORMER DOD OFFICIALS (SEP 2011)
L1:(a) Definition. “Covered DoD official,” as used in this clause, means an individual that—
L1:(1) Leaves or left DoD service on or after January 28, 2008; and
L1:(2)(i) Participated personally and substantially in an acquisition as defined in 41 U.S.C. 131 with a value in excess of $10
L0:million, and serves or served—
L1:(A) In an Executive Schedule position under subchapter II of chapter 53 of Title 5, United States Code;
L1:(B) In a position in the Senior Executive Service under subchapter VIII of chapter 53 of Title 5, United States Code; or
L1:(C) In a general or flag officer position compensated at a rate of pay for grade O-7 or above under section 201 of Title 37,
L0:United States Code; or
L1:(ii) Serves or served in DoD in one of the following positions: program manager, deputy program manager, procuring
L0:contracting officer, administrative contracting officer, source selection authority, member of the source selection evaluation
L0:board, or chief of a financial or technical evaluation team for a contract in an amount in excess of $10 million.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall not knowingly provide compensation to a covered DoD official within 2 years after the official
L0:leaves DoD service, without first determining that the official has sought and received, or has not received after 30 days of
L0:seeking, a written opinion from the appropriate DoD ethics counselor regarding the applicability of post-employment
L0:restrictions to the activities that the official is expected to undertake on behalf of the Contractor.
L1:(c) Failure by the Contractor to comply with paragraph (b) of this clause may subject the Contractor to rescission of this
L0:contract, suspension, or debarment in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 2105(c).
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.203-7000 — Requirements Relating to Compensation of Former DoD Officials

title: 252.203-7001 Prohibition on Persons Convicted of Fraud or Other Defense Contract-Related Felonies
content:
L0:252.203-7001 Prohibition on Persons Convicted of Fraud or Other Defense Contract-Related Felonies.
L0:As prescribed in 203.570-3 , use the following clause:
L0:PROHIBITION ON PERSONS CONVICTED OF FRAUD OR OTHER DEFENSE-CONTRACT-RELATED FELONIES
L0:(JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) “Arising out of a contract with the DoD” means any act in connection with—
L1:(i) Attempting to obtain;
L1:(ii) Obtaining; or
L1:(iii) Performing a contract or first-tier subcontract of any agency, department, or component of the Department of Defense
L1:(DoD).
L1:(2) “Conviction of fraud or any other felony” means any conviction for fraud or a felony in violation of state or Federal
L0:criminal statutes, whether entered on a verdict or plea, including a plea of nolo contendere, for which sentence has been
L0:imposed.
L1:(3) “Date of conviction” means the date judgment was entered against the individual.
L1:(b) Any individual who is convicted after September 29, 1988, of fraud or any other felony arising out of a contract with
L0:the DoD is prohibited from serving—
L1:(1) In a management or supervisory capacity on this contract;
L1:(2) On the board of directors of the Contractor;
L1:(3) As a consultant, agent, or representative for the Contractor; or
L1:(4) In any other capacity with the authority to influence, advise, or control the decisions of the Contractor with regard to
L0:this contract.
L1:(c) Unless waived, the prohibition in paragraph (b) of this clause applies for not less than 5 years from the date of
L0:conviction.
L1:(d) 10 U.S.C. 4656 provides that the Contractor shall be subject to a criminal penalty of not more than $500,000 if
L0:convicted of knowingly—
L1:(1) Employing a person under a prohibition specified in paragraph (b) of this clause; or
L1:(2) Allowing such a person to serve on the board of directors of the contractor or first-tier subcontractor.
L1:(e) In addition to the criminal penalties contained in 10 U.S.C. 4656, the Government may consider other available
L0:remedies, such as—
L1:(1) Suspension or debarment;
L1:(2) Cancellation of the contract at no cost to the Government; or
L1:(3) Termination of the contract for default.
L1:(f) The Contractor may submit written requests for waiver of the prohibition in paragraph (b) of this clause to the
L0:Contracting Officer. Requests shall clearly identify—
L1:(1) The person involved;
L1:(2) The nature of the conviction and resultant sentence or punishment imposed;
L1:(3) The reasons for the requested waiver; and
L1:(4) An explanation of why a waiver is in the interest of national security.
L1:(g) Subcontracts. The Contractor agrees to include the substance of this clause, appropriately modified to reflect the
L0:identity and relationship of the parties, in all first-tier subcontracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold in Part 2
L0:of the Federal Acquisition Regulation, except those for commercial products, commercial services, or commercial
L0:components.
L1:(h) Pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 4656(c), defense contractors and subcontractors may obtain information as to whether a
L0:particular person has been convicted of fraud or any other felony arising out of a contract with the DoD by contacting The
L0:Office of Justice Programs, The Denial of Federal Benefits Office, U.S. Department of Justice, telephone 301-937-1542;
L0:www.ojp.usdoj.gov/BJA/grant/DPFC.html.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.203-7001 — Prohibition on Persons Convicted of Fraud or Other Defense Contract-Related Felonies

content:

L0:incident,” “information system,” and “technical information” are defined in clause 252.204-7012 , Safeguarding Covered
L0:Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting.

title: 252.204-7010 Requirement for Contractor to Notify DoD if the Contractors Activities are Subject to Reporting
content:
L0:252.204-7010 Requirement for Contractor to Notify DoD if the Contractors Activities are Subject to Reporting
L0:Under the U.S.-International Atomic Energy Agency Additional Protocol.
L0:As prescribed in 204.470-3 , use the following clause:
L0:REQUIREMENT FOR CONTRACTOR TO NOTIFY DOD IF THE CONTRACTOR’S ACTIVITIES ARE SUBJECT TO
L0:REPORTING UNDER THE U.S.-INTERNATIONAL ATOMIC ENERGY AGENCY ADDITIONAL PROTOCOL (JAN
L0:2009)
L1:(a) If the Contractor is required to report any of its activities in accordance with Department of Commerce regulations (15
L0:CFR Part 781 et seq.) or Nuclear Regulatory Commission regulations (10 CFR Part 75) in order to implement the
L0:declarations required by the U.S.-International Atomic Energy Agency Additional Protocol (U.S.-IAEA AP), the
L0:Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Immediately provide written notification to the following DoD Program Manager:
L0:[Contracting Officer to insert Program Manager’s name, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, and facsimile
L0:number];
L1:(2) Include in the notification—
L1:(i) Where DoD contract activities or information are located relative to the activities or information to be declared to the
L0:Department of Commerce or the Nuclear Regulatory Commission; and
L1:(ii) If or when any current or former DoD contract activities and the activities to be declared to the Department of
L0:Commerce or the Nuclear Regulatory Commission have been or will be co-located or located near enough to one another
L0:to result in disclosure of the DoD activities during an IAEA inspection or visit; and
L1:(3) Provide a copy of the notification to the Contracting Officer.
L1:(b) After receipt of a notification submitted in accordance with paragraph (a) of this clause, the DoD Program Manager will
L0:—
L1:(1) Conduct a security assessment to determine if and by what means access may be granted to the IAEA; or
L1:(2) Provide written justification to the component or agency treaty office for a national security exclusion, in accordance
L0:with DoD Instruction 2060.03, Application of the National Security Exclusion to the Agreements Between the United
L0:States of America and the International Atomic Energy Agency for the Application of Safeguards in the United States of
L0:America. DoD will notify the Contractor if a national security exclusion is applied at the Contractor’s location to prohibit
L0:access by the IAEA.
L1:(c) If the DoD Program Manager determines that a security assessment is required—
L1:(1) DoD will, at a minimum—
L1:(i) Notify the Contractor that DoD officials intend to conduct an assessment of vulnerabilities to IAEA inspections or visits;
L1:(ii) Notify the Contractor of the time at which the assessment will be conducted, at least 30 days prior to the assessment;
L1:(iii) Provide the Contractor with advance notice of the credentials of the DoD officials who will conduct the assessment;
L0:and
L1:(iv) To the maximum extent practicable, conduct the assessment in a manner that does not impede or delay operations at
L0:the Contractor’s facility; and
L1:(2) The Contractor shall provide access to the site and shall cooperate with DoD officials in the assessment of
L0:vulnerabilities to IAEA inspections or visits.
L1:(d) Following a security assessment of the Contractor’s facility, DoD officials will notify the Contractor as to—
L1:(1) Whether the Contractor’s facility has any vulnerabilities where potentially declarable activities under the U.S.-IAEA
L0:AP are taking place;
L1:(2) Whether additional security measures are needed; and
L1:(3) Whether DoD will apply a national security exclusion.
L1:(e) If DoD applies a national security exclusion, the Contractor shall not grant access to IAEA inspectors.
L1:(f) If DoD does not apply a national security exclusion, the Contractor shall apply managed access to prevent disclosure of
L0:program activities, locations, or information in the U.S. declaration.
L1:(g) The Contractor shall not delay submission of any reports required by the Department of Commerce or the Nuclear
L0:Regulatory Commission while awaiting a DoD response to a notification provided in accordance with this clause.
L1:(h) The Contractor shall incorporate the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (h), in all subcontracts that are
L0:subject to the provisions of the U.S.-IAEA AP.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.204-7010 — Requirement for Contractor to Notify DoD if the Contractors Activities are Subject to Reporting

title: 252.204-7012 Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
content:
L0:252.204-7012 Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting.
L0:As prescribed in 204.7304 (c), use the following clause:
L0:SAFEGUARDING COVERED DEFENSE INFORMATION AND CYBER INCIDENT REPORTING (MAY 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Adequate security” means protective measures that are commensurate with the consequences and probability of loss,
L0:misuse, or unauthorized access to, or modification of information.
L0:“Compromise” means disclosure of information to unauthorized persons, or a violation of the security policy of a system,
L0:in which unauthorized intentional or unintentional disclosure, modification, destruction, or loss of an object, or the copying
L0:of information to unauthorized media may have occurred.
L0:“Contractor attributional/proprietary information” means information that identifies the contractor(s), whether directly or
L0:indirectly, by the grouping of information that can be traced back to the contractor(s) (e.g., program description, facility
L0:locations), personally identifiable information, as well as trade secrets, commercial or financial information, or other
L0:commercially sensitive information that is not customarily shared outside of the company.
L0:“Controlled technical information” means technical information with military or space application that is subject to
L0:controls on the access, use, reproduction, modification, performance, display, release, disclosure, or dissemination.
L0:Controlled technical information would meet the criteria, if disseminated, for distribution statements B through F using the
L0:criteria set forth in DoD Instruction 5230.24, Distribution Statements on Technical Documents. The term does not include
L0:information that is lawfully publicly available without restrictions.
L0:“Covered contractor information system” means an unclassified information system that is owned, or operated by or for, a
L0:contractor and that processes, stores, or transmits covered defense information.
L0:“Covered defense information” means unclassified controlled technical information or other information, as described in
L0:the Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Registry at http://www.archives.gov/cui/registry/category-list.html, that
L0:requires safeguarding or dissemination controls pursuant to and consistent with law, regulations, and Governmentwide
L0:policies, and is—
L1:(1) Marked or otherwise identified in the contract, task order, or delivery order and provided to the contractor by or on
L0:behalf of DoD in support of the performance of the contract; or
L1:(2) Collected, developed, received, transmitted, used, or stored by or on behalf of the contractor in support of the
L0:performance of the contract.
L0:“Cyber incident” means actions taken through the use of computer networks that result in a compromise or an actual or
L0:potentially adverse effect on an information system and/or the information residing therein.
L0:“Forensic analysis” means the practice of gathering, retaining, and analyzing computer-related data for investigative
L0:purposes in a manner that maintains the integrity of the data.
L0:“Information system” means a discrete set of information resources organized for the collection, processing, maintenance,
L0:use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition of information.
L0:“Malicious software” means computer software or firmware intended to perform an unauthorized process that will have
L0:adverse impact on the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information system. This definition includes a virus,
L0:worm, Trojan horse, or other code-based entity that infects a host, as well as spyware and some forms of adware.
L0:“Media” means physical devices or writing surfaces including, but is not limited to, magnetic tapes, optical disks, magnetic
L0:disks, large-scale integration memory chips, and printouts onto which covered defense information is recorded, stored, or
L0:printed within a covered contractor information system.
L0:‘‘Operationally critical support’’ means supplies or services designated by the Government as critical for airlift, sealift,
L0:intermodal transportation services, or logistical support that is essential to the mobilization, deployment, or sustainment of
L0:the Armed Forces in a contingency operation.
L0:“Rapidly report” means within 72 hours of discovery of any cyber incident.
L0:“Technical information” means technical data or computer software, as those terms are defined in the clause at DFARS
citation: R-DFARS 252.204-7012 — Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting

title: 252.204-7014 ) under a contract, the primary purpose of which is to furnish independent and impartial advice or technical
content:
L0:252.204-7014 ) under a contract, the primary purpose of which is to furnish independent and impartial advice or technical
L0:assistance directly to the Government in support of the Government’s management and oversight of a program or effort
L0:(rather than to directly furnish an end item or service to accomplish a program or effort), provided that the contractor—
L1:(1) Is not affiliated with the prime contractor or a first-tier subcontractor on the program or effort, or with any direct
L0:competitor of such prime contractor or any such first-tier subcontractor in furnishing end items or services of the type
L0:developed or produced on the program or effort; and
L1:(2) Receives access to technical data or computer software for performance of a Government contract that contains the
L0:clause at 252.227-7025, Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with
L0:Restrictive Legends.
L0:“Form, fit, and function data” means technical data that describe the required overall physical, functional, and performance
L0:characteristics (along with the qualification requirements, if applicable) of an item, component, or process to the extent
L0:necessary to permit identification of physically and functionally interchangeable items.
L0:“Technical data” means recorded information, regardless of the form or method of recording, of a scientific or technical
L0:nature (including computer software documentation). The term does not include computer software or financial,
L0:administrative, cost or pricing, or management information, or information incidental to contract administration.
L1:(b) Applicability. This clause governs the technical data pertaining to any portion of a commercial product or commercial
L0:service that was developed exclusively at private expense. If the commercial product or commercial service was developed
L0:in any part at Government expense—
L1:(1) The clause at Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 252.227-7018, Rights in Other Than
L0:Commercial Technical Data and Computer Software—Small Business Innovation Research Program and Small Business
L0:Technology Transfer Program, governs technical data that are generated during any portion of performance that is covered
L0:under the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Program or Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Program;
L0:and
L1:(2) The clause at DFARS 252.227-7013, Rights in Technical Data—Other Than Commercial Products and Commercial
L0:Services, governs the technical data pertaining to any portion of a commercial product or commercial service that was
L0:developed in any part at Government expense and is not covered under the SBIR or STTR program.
L1:(c) License.
L1:(1) The Government shall have the unrestricted right to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose
L0:technical data, and to permit others to do so, that—
L1:(i) Have been provided to the Government or others without restrictions on use, modification, reproduction, release, or
L0:further disclosure other than a release or disclosure resulting from the sale, transfer, or other assignment of interest in the
L0:technical data to another party or the sale or transfer of some or all of a business entity or its assets to another party;
L1:(ii) Are form, fit, and function data;
L1:(iii) Are a correction or change to technical data furnished to the Contractor by the Government;
L1:(iv) Are necessary for operation, maintenance, installation, or training (other than detailed manufacturing or process data);
L0:or
L1:(v) Have been provided to the Government under a prior contract or licensing agreement through which the Government
L0:has acquired the rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose the data without restrictions.
L1:(2) Except as provided in paragraph (c)(1) of this clause, the Government may use, modify, reproduce, release, perform,
L0:display, or disclose technical data within the Government only. The Government shall not—
L1:(i) Use the technical data to manufacture additional quantities of the commercial products; or
L1:(ii) Release, perform, display, disclose, or authorize use of the technical data outside the Government without the
L0:Contractor's written permission unless a release, disclosure, or permitted use is necessary for emergency repair or overhaul
L0:of the commercial products furnished under this contract, or for performance of work by covered Government support
L0:contractors.
L1:(3) The Contractor acknowledges that—
L1:(i) Technical data covered by paragraph (c)(2) of this clause are authorized to be released or disclosed to covered
L0:Government support contractors;
L1:(ii) The Contractor will be notified of such release or disclosure;
L1:(iii) The Contractor (or the party asserting restrictions as identified in a restrictive legend) may require each such covered
L0:Government support contractor to enter into a nondisclosure agreement directly with the Contractor (or the party asserting
L0:restrictions) regarding the covered Government support contractor’s use of such data, or alternatively, that the Contractor
L0:(or party asserting restrictions) may waive in writing the requirement for an nondisclosure agreement; and
L1:(iv) Any such nondisclosure agreement shall address the restrictions on the covered Government support contractor’s use
L0:of the data as set forth in the clause at DFARS 252.227-7025, Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of GovernmentFurnished Information Marked with Restrictive Legends. The nondisclosure agreement shall not include any additional
L0:terms and conditions unless mutually agreed to by the parties to the nondisclosure agreement.
L1:(d) Additional license rights. The Contractor, its subcontractors, and suppliers are not required to provide the Government
L0:additional rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical data. However, if the
L0:Government desires to obtain additional rights in technical data, the Contractor agrees to promptly enter into negotiations
L0:with the Contracting Officer to determine whether there are acceptable terms for transferring such rights. All technical data
L0:in which the Contractor has granted the Government additional rights shall be listed or described in a special license
L0:agreement made part of this contract. The license shall enumerate the additional rights granted the Government in such
L0:data.
L1:(e) Release from liability. The Contractor agrees that the Government, and other persons to whom the Government may
L0:have released or disclosed technical data delivered or otherwise furnished under this contract, shall have no liability for any
L0:release or disclosure of technical data that are not marked to indicate that such data are licensed data subject to use,
L0:modification, reproduction, release, performance, display, or disclosure restrictions.
L1:(f) Subcontractors or suppliers.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall recognize and protect the rights afforded its subcontractors and suppliers under 10 U.S.C. 3771-
L0:3775,10 U.S.C. 3781-3786, and 15 U.S.C. 638(j)(1)(B)(iii) and (v).
L1:(2) Whenever any technical data related to commercial products or commercial services developed in any part at private
L0:expense will be obtained from a subcontractor or supplier for delivery to the Government under this contract, the
L0:Contractor shall use this clause in the subcontract or other contractual instrument, including subcontracts and other

title: 252.204-7016 , Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services—Representation, that it “does not provide
content:
L0:252.204-7016 , Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services—Representation, that it “does not provide
L0:covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a part of its offered products or services to the Government
L0:in the performance of any contract, subcontract, or other contractual instrument.”
L1:(a) Definitions. “Covered defense telecommunications equipment or services,” “covered mission,” “critical technology,”
L0:and “substantial or essential component,” as used in this provision, have the meanings given in the 252.204-7018 clause,
L0:Prohibition on the Acquisition of Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services, of this solicitation.
L1:(b) Prohibition. Section 1656 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 (Pub. L. 115-91) prohibits
L0:agencies from procuring or obtaining, or extending or renewing a contract to procure or obtain, any equipment, system, or
L0:service to carry out covered missions that uses covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial
L0:or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system.
L1:(c) Procedures. The Offeror shall review the list of excluded parties in the System for Award Management (SAM) at
L0:https://www.sam.gov for entities that are excluded when providing any equipment, system, or service to carry out covered
L0:missions that uses covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of
L0:any system, or as critical technology as part of any system, unless a waiver is granted.
L1:(d) Representation. If in its annual representations and certifications in SAM the Offeror has represented in paragraph (c)
L0:of the provision at 252.204-7016 , Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services—Representation, that it
L0:“does” provide covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a part of its offered products or services to
L0:the Government in the performance of any contract, subcontract, or other contractual instrument, then the Offeror shall
L0:complete the following additional representation:
L0:The Offeror represents that it [ ] will [ ] will not provide covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a

L0:identifier, and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code, if known).
L1:(4) For equipment, the entity that produced or provided the covered defense telecommunications equipment (include entity
L0:name, unique entity identifier, CAGE code, and whether the entity was the OEM or a distributor, if known).

title: 252.204-7018 Prohibition on the Acquisition of Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services
content:
L0:252.204-7018 Prohibition on the Acquisition of Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services.
L0:As prescribed in 204.2105 (c), use the following clause:
L0:PROHIBITION ON THE ACQUISITION OF COVERED DEFENSE TELECOMMUNICATIONS EQUIPMENT OR
L0:SERVICES (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Covered defense telecommunications equipment or services” means—
L1:(1) Telecommunications equipment produced by Huawei Technologies Company or ZTE Corporation, or any subsidiary or
L0:affiliate of such entities;
L1:(2) Telecommunications services provided by such entities or using such equipment; or
L1:(3) Telecommunications equipment or services produced or provided by an entity that the Secretary of Defense reasonably
L0:believes to be an entity owned or controlled by, or otherwise connected to, the government of a covered foreign country.
L0:“Covered foreign country” means—
L1:(1) The People’s Republic of China; or
L1:(2) The Russian Federation.
L0:“Covered missions” means—
L1:(1) The nuclear deterrence mission of DoD, including with respect to nuclear command, control, and communications,
L0:integrated tactical warning and attack assessment, and continuity of Government; or
L1:(2) The homeland defense mission of DoD, including with respect to ballistic missile defense.
L0:“Critical technology” means—
L1:(1) Defense articles or defense services included on the United States Munitions List set forth in the International Traffic in
L0:Arms Regulations under subchapter M of chapter I of title 22, Code of Federal Regulations;
L1:(2) Items included on the Commerce Control List set forth in Supplement No. 1 to part 774 of the Export Administration
L0:Regulations under subchapter C of chapter VII of title 15, Code of Federal Regulations, and controlled—
L1:(i) Pursuant to multilateral regimes, including for reasons relating to national security, chemical and biological weapons
L0:proliferation, nuclear nonproliferation, or missile technology; or
L1:(ii) For reasons relating to regional stability or surreptitious listening;
L1:(3) Specially designed and prepared nuclear equipment, parts and components, materials, software, and technology covered
L0:by part 810 of title 10, Code of Federal Regulations (relating to assistance to foreign atomic energy activities);
L1:(4) Nuclear facilities, equipment, and material covered by part 110 of title 10, Code of Federal Regulations (relating to
L0:export and import of nuclear equipment and material);
L1:(5) Select agents and toxins covered by part 331 of title 7, Code of Federal Regulations, part 121 of title 9 of such Code, or
L0:part 73 of title 42 of such Code; or
L1:(6) Emerging and foundational technologies controlled pursuant to section 1758 of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018
L0:(50 U.S.C. 4817).
L0:“Substantial or essential component” means any component necessary for the proper function or performance of a piece of
L0:equipment, system, or service.
L1:(b) Prohibition. In accordance with section 1656 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 (Pub. L.
L0:115-91), the contractor shall not provide to the Government any equipment, system, or service to carry out covered
L0:missions that uses covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of
L0:any system, or as critical technology as part of any system, unless the covered defense telecommunication equipment or
L0:services are covered by a waiver described in Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement 204.2104 .
L1:(c) Procedures. The Contractor shall review the list of excluded parties in the System for Award Management (SAM) at
L0:https://www.sam.gov for entities that are excluded when providing any equipment, system, or service, to carry out covered
L0:missions, that uses covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of
L0:any system, or as critical technology as part of any system, unless a waiver is granted.
L1:(d) Reporting.
L1:(1) In the event the Contractor identifies covered defense telecommunications equipment or services used as a substantial
L0:or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system, during contract performance, the
L0:Contractor shall report at https://dibnet.dod.mil the information in paragraph (d)(2) of this clause.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall report the following information pursuant to paragraph (d)(1) of this clause:
L1:(i) Within 3 business days from the date of such identification or notification: the contract number; the order number(s), if
L0:applicable; supplier name; brand; model number (original equipment manufacturer number, manufacturer part number, or
L0:wholesaler number); item description; and any readily available information about mitigation actions undertaken or
L0:recommended.
L1:(ii) Within 30 business days of submitting the information in paragraph (d)(2)(i) of this clause: any further available
L0:information about mitigation actions undertaken or recommended. In addition, the Contractor shall describe the efforts it
L0:undertook to prevent use or submission of a covered defense telecommunications equipment or services, and any additional
L0:efforts that will be incorporated to prevent future use or submission of covered telecommunications equipment or services.
L1:(e) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall insert the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (e), in all subcontracts
L0:and other contractual instruments, including subcontracts for the acquisition of commercial products or commercial
L0:services.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.204-7018 — Prohibition on the Acquisition of Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services

L0:assessment organization (C3PAO)) assessments, with—
L1:(A) No changes in compliance with the requirements at 32 CFR part 170 since the Conditional CMMC Status date (see 32
L0:CFR 170.16 and 170.17); and
L1:(B) A corresponding affirmation of continuous compliance by an affirming official (see 32 CFR 170.4); and
L1:(ii) Not older than 180 days for Conditional Level 3 (Defense Industrial Base Cybersecurity Assessment Center
L1:(DIBCAC)) assessments, with—
L1:(A) No changes in compliance with the requirements at 32 CFR part 170 since the Conditional CMMC Status date (see 32
L0:CFR 170.18); and
L1:(B) A corresponding affirmation of continuous compliance by an affirming official;
L1:(2) With regard to Final CMMC Status—
L1:(i) Not older than 1 year for Final Level 1 (Self), with—
L1:(A) No changes in compliance with the requirements at 32 CFR part 170 since the Final CMMC Status date (see 32 CFR
L0:170.15); and
L1:(B) A corresponding affirmation of continuous compliance, not older than 1 year, by an affirming official;
L1:(ii) Not older than 3 years for Final Level 2 (Self) assessments and Final Level 2 (C3PAO) assessments, with—
L1:(A) No changes in compliance with the requirements at 32 CFR part 170 since the Final CMMC Status date (see 32 CFR
L0:170.16 and 170.17); and
L1:(B) A corresponding affirmation of continuous compliance, not older than 1 year, by an affirming official; and
L1:(iii) Not older than 3 years for Final Level 3 (DIBCAC) assessments, with—
L1:(A) No changes in compliance with the requirements at 32 CFR part 170 since the Final CMMC Status date (see 32 CFR
L0:170.18); and
L1:(B) A corresponding affirmation of continuous compliance, not older than 1 year, by an affirming official; and
L1:(3) With regard to affirmation of continuous compliance (32 CFR 170.22), not older than 1 year with no changes in
L0:compliance with the requirements at 32 CFR part 170.
L0:“Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) status” means the result of meeting or exceeding the minimum
L0:required score for the corresponding assessment. The potential statuses are as follows:
L1:(1) Final Level 1 (Self).
L1:(2) Conditional Level 2 (Self).
L1:(3) Final Level 2 (Self).
L1:(4) Conditional Level 2 (C3PAO).
L1:(5) Final Level 2 (C3PAO).
L1:(6) Conditional Level 3 (DIBCAC).
L1:(7) Final Level 3 (DIBCAC).
L0:“Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification unique identifier (CMMC UID)” means 10 alpha-numeric characters assigned
L0:to each CMMC assessment and reflected in theSupplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) for each contractor information
L0:system.
L0:“Federal contract information (FCI)” means information, not intended for public release, that is provided by or generated
L0:for the Government under a contract to develop or deliver a product or service to the Government. It does not include
L0:information provided by the Government to the public, such as on public websites, or simple transactional information,
L0:such as information necessary to process payments.
L0:“Plan of action and milestones” means a document that identifies tasks to be accomplished. It details resources required to
L0:accomplish the elements of the plan, any milestones in meeting the tasks, and scheduled completion dates for the
L0:milestones, as defined in National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800-115 (32 CFR 170.21).
L1:(b) Framework. The Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) is a framework for assessing a contractor’s
L0:compliance with applicable information security protections (see 32 CFR part 170).
L1:(c) Duplication. The CMMC assessments will not duplicate efforts from any other comparable DoD assessment, except for
L0:rare circumstances when a reassessment may be necessary, for example, when there are indications of issues with
L0:cybersecurity and/or compliance with CMMC requirements.
L1:(d) Requirements. The Contractor shall—
L1:(1)(i) Have and maintain for the duration of the contract a current CMMC status at the following CMMC level, or higher:
L0:____________ [Contracting Officer insert: CMMC Level 1 (Self); CMMC Level 2 (Self); CMMC Level 2 (C3PAO); or
L0:CMMC Level 3 (DIBCAC) ] for all information systems used in performance of the contract, task order, or delivery order
L0:that process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI; and
L1:(ii) Consult 32 CFR 170.23 related to the flowdown of the CMMC requirements, and flow down the correct CMMC level
L0:to subcontracts and other contractual instruments;
L1:(2) Only process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI on contractor information systems that have a CMMC status at the CMMC
L0:level requiredin paragraph (d)(1) of this clause, or higher;
L1:(3) Complete on an annual basis, and maintain as current,an affirmation, by the affirming official (see 32 CFR 170.4), of
L0:continuous compliance with the requirements associated with the CMMC level required in paragraph (d)(1) of this clause
L0:in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) (https://piee.eb.mil) for each CMMC UID applicable to each of the
L0:contractor information systems that process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI and that are used in performance of the contract;
L1:(4) Ensure all subcontractors and suppliers complete prior to subcontract award, and maintain on an annual basis,an
L0:affirmation, by the affirming official (see 32 CFR 170.4), of continuous compliance with the requirements associated with
L0:the CMMC level required for the subcontract or other contractual instrument for each of the subcontractor information
L0:systems that process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI and that are used in performance of the subcontract; and
L1:(5) If the Contractor has a CMMC Status of Conditional, successfully close out a valid plan of action and milestones (32
L0:CFR 170.21) to achieve a CMMC Status of Final.
L1:(e) Reporting. The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Submit to the Contracting Officer—
L1:(i) The CMMC UID(s) issued by SPRS for contractor information systems that will process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI
L0:during performance of the contract; and
L1:(ii) Any changes in the CMMC UIDs generated in SPRS throughout the life of the contract, task order, or delivery order, if
L0:applicable;
L1:(2)Enter into SPRS the results of a current self-assessment for each CMMC UID, not covered by a C3PAO assessment or
L0:DIBCAC assessment, applicable to each of the contractor information systems that process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI
L0:and that are used in performance of the contract; and
L1:(3) Complete in SPRS on an annual basis and maintain as current an affirmation of continuous compliance by the affirming
L0:official (see 32 CFR 170.4) for each self-assessment, C3PAO assessment, or DIBCAC assessment required under the
L0:contract in SPRS.
L1:(f) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Insert the substance of this clause, including this paragraph ( f) and excluding paragraph (e)(1), in subcontracts and
L0:other contractual instruments, including those for the acquisition of commercial products and commercial services,
L0:excluding commercially available off-the-shelf items , if the subcontract or other contractual instrument will contain a
L0:requirement to process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI; and
L1:(2) Prior to awarding a subcontract or other contractual instrument, ensure that the subcontractor has a current CMMC
L0:certificate or current CMMC status at the CMMC level that is appropriate for the information that is being flowed down to
L0:the subcontractor based on the requirements at 32 CFR 170.23.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.204-7024 Notice on the Use of the Supplier Performance Risk System
content:
L0:252.204-7024 Notice on the Use of the Supplier Performance Risk System.
L0:As prescribed in 204.7604, use the following provision .
L0:NOTICE ON THE USE OF THE SUPPLIER PERFORMANCE RISK SYSTEM (MAR 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this provision—
L0:“Item risk” means the probability that a product, based on intended use, will introduce performance risk resulting in safety
L0:issues, mission degradation, or monetary loss.
L0:“Price risk” means a measure of whether a proposed price for a product or service is consistent with historical prices paid
L0:for that item or service.
L0:“Supplier risk” means the probability that an award may subject the procurement to the risk of unsuccessful performance or
L0:to supply chain risk (see Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement 239.7301).
L1:(b) The Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS), available at https://piee.eb.mil/, will be used in the evaluation of the
L0:Quoter or Offeror’s performance. SPRS retrieves item, price, quality, delivery, and contractor information on contracts
L0:from Government reporting systems in order to develop risk assessments.
L1:(c) The Contracting Officer will consider SPRS risk assessments during the evaluation of quotations or offers received in
L0:response to this solicitation as follows:
L1:(1) Item risk will be considered to determine whether the procurement represents a high performance risk to the
L0:Government.
L1:(2) Price risk will be considered in determining if a proposed price is consistent with historical prices paid for a product or
L0:a service or otherwise creates a risk to the Government.
L1:(3) Supplier risk, including but not limited to quality and delivery, will be considered to assess the risk of unsuccessful
L0:performance and supply chain risk.
L1:(d) SPRS risk assessments are generated daily. Quoters or Offerors are able to access their risk assessments by following
L0:the access instructions in the SPRS user's guide available at https://www.sprs.csd.disa.mil/reference.htm. Quoters and
L0:Offerors are granted access to SPRS for their own risk assessment classifications only. SPRS reporting procedures and risk
L0:assessment methodology are detailed in the SPRS user's guide. The method to challenge a rating generated by SPRS is also
L0:provided in the user's guide. SPRS evaluation criteria are available at
L0:https://www.sprs.csd.disa.mil/pdf/SPRS_DataEvaluationCriteria.pdf.
L1:(e) The Contracting Officer may consider any other available and relevant information when evaluating a quotation or an
L0:offer.
L0:(End of provision)
citation: R-DFARS 252.204-7024 — Notice on the Use of the Supplier Performance Risk System

title: 252.209-7007 Prohibited Financial Interests for Lead System Integrators
content:
L0:252.209-7007 Prohibited Financial Interests for Lead System Integrators.
L0:As prescribed in 209.570-4 (b), use the following clause:
L0:PROHIBITED FINANCIAL INTERESTS FOR LEAD SYSTEM INTEGRATORS (DEC 2022)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) “Lead system integrator” includes “lead system integrator with system responsibility” and “lead system integrator
L0:without system responsibility.”
L1:(2) “Lead system integrator with system responsibility” means a prime contractor for the development or production of a
L0:major system, if the prime contractor is not expected at the time of award to perform a substantial portion of the work on
L0:the system and the major subsystems.
L1:(3) “Lead system integrator without system responsibility” means a prime contractor under a contract for the procurement
L0:of services, the primary purpose of which is to perform acquisition functions closely associated with inherently
L0:governmental functions (see section 7.503(d) of the Federal Acquisition Regulation) with respect to the development or
L0:production of a major system.
L1:(b) Limitations. The Contracting Officer has determined that the Contractor meets the definition of lead system integrator
L0:with [ ] without [ ] system responsibility. Unless an exception is granted, the Contractor shall not have any direct financial
L0:interest in the development or construction of any individual system or element of any system of systems while performing
L0:lead system integrator functions in the acquisition of a major system by the Department of Defense under this contract.
L1:(c) Agreement. The Contractor agrees that during performance of this contract it will not acquire any direct financial
L0:interest as described in paragraph (b) of this clause, or, if it does acquire or plan to acquire such interest, it will immediately
L0:notify the Contracting Officer. The Contractor further agrees to provide to the Contracting Officer all relevant information
L0:regarding the change in financial interests so that the Contracting Officer can determine whether an exception applies or
L0:whether the Contractor will be allowed to continue performance on this contract. If a direct financial interest cannot be
L0:avoided, eliminated, or mitigated to the Contracting Officer’s satisfaction, the Contracting Officer may terminate this
L0:contract for default for the Contractor’s material failure to comply with the terms and conditions of award or may take
L0:other remedial measures as appropriate in the Contracting Officer’s sole discretion.
L1:(d) Notwithstanding any other clause of this contract, if the Contracting Officer determines that the Contractor
L0:misrepresented its financial interests at the time of award or has violated the agreement in paragraph (c) of this clause, the
L0:Government may terminate this contract for default for the Contractor’s material failure to comply with the terms and
L0:conditions of award or may take other remedial measures as appropriate in the Contracting Officer’s sole discretion.
L1:(e) This clause implements the requirements of 10 U.S.C. 4292.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.209-7007 — Prohibited Financial Interests for Lead System Integrators

title: 252.209-7012 Prohibition Relating to Conflicts of Interest in Consulting Services—Certification
content:
L0:252.209-7012 Prohibition Relating to Conflicts of Interest in Consulting Services—Certification.
L0:As prescribed in 209.572(e), use the following provision:
L0:PROHIBITION RELATING TO CONFLICTS OF INTEREST IN CONSULTING SERVICES—CERTIFICATION (OCT
L0:2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this provision—
L0:“Consulting services” means advisory and assistance services, except that “consulting services” does not include the
L0:provision of products or services related to—
L1:(1) Compliance with legal, audit, accounting, tax, reporting, or other requirements of the laws and standards of countries;
L0:or
L1:(2) Participation in a judicial, legal, or equitable dispute resolution proceeding.
L0:“Contract oversight entity”means any of the following:
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer.
L1:(2) The Contracting Officer’s Representative.
L1:(3) The Defense Contract Management Agency.
L1:(4) The Defense Contract Audit Agency.
L1:(5) The DoD Office of Inspector General or any subcomponent of that office.
L1:(6) The Government Accountability Office.
L0:“Covered contract” means a DoD contract involving consulting services.
L0:“Covered foreign entity” means any of the following:
L1:(1) The government of the People’s Republic of China, the Chinese Communist Party, the People’s Liberation Army, the
L0:Ministry of State Security, or other security service or intelligence agency of the People’s Republic of China.
L1:(2) The government of the Russian Federation or any entity sanctioned by the Secretary of the Treasury under Executive
L0:Order 13662, Blocking Property of Additional Persons Contributing to the Situation in Ukraine.
L1:(3) The government of any country, if the Secretary of State determines that such government has repeatedly provided
L0:support for acts of international terrorism, pursuant to any of the following:
L1:(i) Section 1754(c)(1)(A) of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (50 U.S.C. 4318(c)(1)(A)).
L1:(ii) Section 620A of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2371).
L1:(iii) Section 40 of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2780).
L1:(iv) Any other provision of law.
L1:(4) Any entity included on any of the following lists maintained by the Department of Commerce (see the Export
L0:Administration Regulations at 15 CFR subchapter C):
L1:(i) The Entity List in supplement no. 4 to 15 CFR part 744.
L1:(ii) The Denied Persons List as described in 15 CFR 764.3(a)(2).
L1:(iii) The Unverified List in supplement no. 6 to 15 CFR part 744.
L1:(iv) The Military End User List in supplement no. 7 to 15 CFR part 744.
L1:(5) Any entity identified by the Secretary of Defense pursuant to section 1237(b) of the National Defense Authorization
L0:Act for Fiscal Year 1999 (Pub. L. 105-261; 50 U.S.C. 1701 note).
L1:(6) Any entity on the Non-Specially Designated Nationals Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List
L0:maintained by the Office of Foreign Assets Control of the Department of the Treasury under Executive Order 14032,
L0:Addressing the Threat From Securities Investments That Finance Certain Companies of the People’s Republic of China.
L1:(b) Prohibition. DoD cannot award to the Offeror a contract assigned a North American Industry Classification System
L0:code beginning with 5416 if the Offeror—
L1:(1) Cannot certify that neither the Offeror nor any of its subsidiaries or affiliates hold a contract or subcontract that
L0:involves consulting services with one or more covered foreign entities; and
L1:(2) Does not maintain a conflict-of-interest mitigation plan as described in paragraph (d) of this provision.
L1:(c) Certification. The Offeror certifies that—
L1:(1)(i) It does [ ] does not [ ] hold a contract or subcontract that involves consulting services with one or more covered
L0:foreign entities; and
L1:(ii) Its subsidiaries or affiliates do [ ] do not [ ] hold a contract or subcontract that involves consulting services with one or
L0:more covered foreign entities; and
L1:(2) It does [ ] does not [ ] maintain a conflict-of-interest mitigation plan described in paragraph (d) of this provision.
L1:(d) Conflict-of-interest mitigation plan. If the Offeror answered in the affirmative in paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this
L0:provision, then the Offeror shall submit its conflict-of-interest mitigation plan to the Contracting Officer for approval. The
L0:Offeror may contact the Contracting Officer for guidance on submitting the Offeror’s conflict-of-interest mitigation plan.
L1:(1) The Offeror’s conflict-of-interest mitigation plan shall be auditable by a contract oversight entity and shall include—
L1:(i) An identification, unless otherwise prohibited by law or regulation, of any covered contracts of the Offeror or its
L0:subsidiaries or affiliates with a covered foreign entity. If the Offeror is unable to identify one or more covered foreign
L0:entities due to confidentiality obligations, the Offeror shall identify such entities as a covered foreign entity;
L1:(ii) A written analysis, including a course of action for avoiding, neutralizing, or mitigating the actual or potential conflict
L0:of interest of such a covered contract;
L1:(iii) A description of the procedures by which the Offeror or its subsidiaries or affiliates will ensure that individuals who
L0:will perform the scope of a covered contract will not, for the duration of such contract, also provide any consulting services
L0:to any covered foreign entity; and
L1:(iv) A description of the procedures by which the Offeror or its subsidiaries or affiliates will submit to the contract
L0:oversight entities a notice of an unmitigated conflict of interest with respect to a covered contract within 15 days of
L0:determining that such a conflict has arisen.
L1:(2) The Contracting Officer will incorporate the Offeror’s approved conflict-of-interest mitigation plan into any contract
L0:awarded to the Offeror resulting from this solicitation.
L0:(End of provision)

title: 252.211-7003 Item Unique Identification and Valuation
content:
L0:252.211-7003 Item Unique Identification and Valuation.
L0:As prescribed in 211.274-5 (a), use the following clause:
L0:ITEM UNIQUE IDENTIFICATION AND VALUATION (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Automatic identification device” means a device, such as a reader or interrogator, used to retrieve data encoded on
L0:machine-readable media.
L0:“Concatenated unique item identifier” means—
L1:(1) For items that are serialized within the enterprise identifier, the linking together of the unique identifier data elements in
L0:order of the issuing agency code, enterprise identifier, and unique serial number within the enterprise identifier; or
L1:(2) For items that are serialized within the original part, lot, or batch number, the linking together of the unique identifier
L0:data elements in order of the issuing agency code; enterprise identifier; original part, lot, or batch number; and serial
L0:number within the original part, lot, or batch number.
L0:“Data matrix” means a two-dimensional matrix symbology, which is made up of square or, in some cases, round modules
L0:arranged within a perimeter finder pattern and uses the Error Checking and Correction 200 (ECC200) specification found
L0:within International Standards Organization (ISO)/International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 16022.
L0:“Data qualifier” means a specified character (or string of characters) that immediately precedes a data field that defines the
L0:general category or intended use of the data that follows.
L0:“DoD recognized unique identification equivalent” means a unique identification method that is in commercial use and has
L0:been recognized by DoD. All DoD recognized unique identification equivalents are listed at
L0:https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/ds/unique-id.html .
L0:“DoD item unique identification” means a system of marking items delivered to DoD with unique item identifiers that have
L0:machine-readable data elements to distinguish an item from all other like and unlike items. For items that are serialized
L0:within the enterprise identifier, the unique item identifier shall include the data elements of the enterprise identifier and a
L0:unique serial number. For items that are serialized within the part, lot, or batch number within the enterprise identifier, the
L0:unique item identifier shall include the data elements of the enterprise identifier; the original part, lot, or batch number; and
L0:the serial number.
L0:“Enterprise” means the entity (e.g., a manufacturer or vendor) responsible for assigning unique item identifiers to items.
L0:“Enterprise identifier” means a code that is uniquely assigned to an enterprise by an issuing agency.
L0:“Government’s unit acquisition cost” means—
L1:(1) For fixed-price type line, subline, or exhibit line items, the unit price identified in the contract at the time of delivery;
L1:(2) For cost-type or undefinitized line, subline, or exhibit line items, the Contractor’s estimated fully burdened unit cost to
L0:the Government at the time of delivery; and
L1:(3) For items produced under a time-and-materials contract, the Contractor’s estimated fully burdened unit cost to the
L0:Government at the time of delivery.
L0:“Issuing agency” means an organization responsible for assigning a globally unique identifier to an enterprise, as indicated
L0:in the Register of Issuing Agency Codes for ISO/IEC 15459, located at http://www.aimglobal.org/?Reg_Authority15459.
L0:“Issuing agency code” means a code that designates the registration (or controlling) authority for the enterprise identifier.
L0:“Item” means a single hardware article or a single unit formed by a grouping of subassemblies, components, or constituent
L0:parts.
L0:“Lot or batch number” means an identifying number assigned by the enterprise to a designated group of items, usually
L0:referred to as either a lot or a batch, all of which were manufactured under identical conditions.
L0:“Machine-readable” means an automatic identification technology media, such as bar codes, contact memory buttons, radio
L0:frequency identification, or optical memory cards.
L0:“Original part number” means a combination of numbers or letters assigned by the enterprise at item creation to a class of
L0:items with the same form, fit, function, and interface.
L0:“Parent item” means the item assembly, intermediate component, or subassembly that has an embedded item with a unique
L0:item identifier or DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.
L0:“Serial number within the enterprise identifier” means a combination of numbers, letters, or symbols assigned by the
L0:enterprise to an item that provides for the differentiation of that item from any other like and unlike item and is never used
L0:again within the enterprise.
L0:“Serial number within the part, lot, or batch number” means a combination of numbers or letters assigned by the enterprise
L0:to an item that provides for the differentiation of that item from any other like item within a part, lot, or batch number
L0:assignment.
L0:“Serialization within the enterprise identifier” means each item produced is assigned a serial number that is unique among
L0:all the tangible items produced by the enterprise and is never used again. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring unique
L0:serialization within the enterprise identifier.
L0:“Serialization within the part, lot, or batch number” means each item of a particular part, lot, or batch number is assigned a
L0:unique serial number within that part, lot, or batch number assignment. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring unique
L0:serialization within the part, lot, or batch number within the enterprise identifier.
L0:“Type designation” means a combination of letters and numerals assigned by the Government to a major end item,
L0:assembly or subassembly, as appropriate, to provide a convenient means of differentiating between items having the same
L0:basic name and to indicate modifications and changes thereto.
L0:“Unique item identifier” means a set of data elements marked on items that is globally unique and unambiguous. The term
L0:includes a concatenated unique item identifier or a DoD recognized unique identification equivalent.
L0:“Unique item identifier type” means a designator to indicate which method of uniquely identifying a part has been used.
L0:The current list of accepted unique item identifier types is maintained at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/ds/uniqueid.html .
