title: 252.211-7008 Use of Government-Assigned Serial Numbers
content:
L0:252.211-7008 Use of Government-Assigned Serial Numbers
L0:As prescribed in 211.274-5 (b), use the following clause:
L0:USE OF GOVERNMENT-ASSIGNED SERIAL NUMBERS (SEP 2010)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Government-assigned serial number” means a combination of letters or numerals in a fixed human-readable information
L0:format (text) conveying information about a major end item, which is provided to a contractor by the requiring activity
L0:with accompanying technical data instructions for marking the Government-assigned serial number on major end items to
L0:be delivered to the Government.
L0:“Major end item” means a final combination of component parts and/or materials which is ready for its intended use and of
L0:such importance to operational readiness that review and control of inventory management functions (procurement,
L0:distribution, maintenance, disposal, and asset reporting) is required at all levels of life cycle management. Major end items
L0:include aircraft; ships; boats; motorized wheeled, tracked, and towed vehicles for use on highway or rough terrain; weapon
L0:and missile end items; ammunition; and sets, assemblies, or end items having a major end item as a component.
L0:“Unique item identifier (UII)” means a set of data elements permanently marked on an item that is globally unique and
L0:unambiguous and never changes in order to provide traceability of the item throughout its total life cycle. The term
L0:includes a concatenated UII or a DoD-recognized unique identification equivalent.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall mark the Government-assigned serial numbers on those major end items as specified by line item
L0:in the Schedule, in accordance with the technical instructions for the placement and method of application identified in the
L0:terms and conditions of the contract.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall register the Government-assigned serial number along with the major end item’s UII at the time of
L0:delivery in accordance with the provisions of the clause at DFARS 252.211-7003 (d).
L1:(d) The Contractor shall establish the UII for major end items for use throughout the life of the major end item. The
L0:Contractor may elect, but is not required, to use the Government-assigned serial number to construct the UII.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.211-7008 — Use of Government-Assigned Serial Numbers

title: 252.215-7002 Cost Estimating System Requirements
content:
L0:252.215-7002 Cost Estimating System Requirements.
L0:As prescribed in 215.408 (1), use the following clause:
L0:COST ESTIMATING SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS (JAN 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions.
L0:“Acceptable estimating system” means an estimating system that complies with the system criteria in paragraph (d) of this
L0:clause, and provides for a system that—
L1:(1) Is maintained, reliable, and consistently applied;
L1:(2) Produces verifiable, supportable, documented, and timely cost estimates that are an acceptable basis for negotiation of
L0:fair and reasonable prices;
L1:(3) Is consistent with and integrated with the Contractor’s related management systems; and
L1:(4) Is subject to applicable financial control systems.
L0:“Estimating system” means the Contractor's policies, procedures, and practices for budgeting and planning controls, and
L0:generating estimates of costs and other data included in proposals submitted to customers in the expectation of receiving
L0:contract awards. Estimating system includes the Contractor's—
L1:(1) Organizational structure;
L1:(2) Established lines of authority, duties, and responsibilities;
L1:(3) Internal controls and managerial reviews;
L1:(4) Flow of work, coordination, and communication; and
L1:(5) Budgeting, planning, estimating methods, techniques, accumulation of historical costs, and other analyses used to
L0:generate cost estimates.
L0:“Material weakness” means a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the internal control over information in
L0:contractor business systems, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of such information will
L0:not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A reasonable possibility exists when the likelihood of an
L0:event occurring is—
L1:(1) Probable; or
L1:(2) More than remote but less than likely (section 806 of Pub. L. 116-283).
L1:(b) General. The Contractor shall establish, maintain, and comply with an acceptable estimating system.
L1:(c) Applicability. Paragraphs (d) and (e) of this clause apply if the Contractor is a large business and either—
L1:(1) In its fiscal year preceding award of this contract, received Department of Defense (DoD) prime contracts or
L0:subcontracts, totaling $50 million or more for which certified cost or pricing data were required; or
L1:(2) In its fiscal year preceding award of this contract—
L1:(i) Received DoD prime contracts or subcontracts totaling $10 million or more (but less than $50 million) for which
L0:certified cost or pricing data were required; and
L1:(ii) Was notified, in writing, by the Contracting Officer that paragraphs (d) and (e) of this clause apply.
L1:(d) System requirements.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall disclose its estimating system to the Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO), in writing. If the
L0:Contractor wishes the Government to protect the data and information as privileged or confidential, the Contractor must
L0:mark the documents with the appropriate legends before submission.
L1:(2) An estimating system disclosure is acceptable when the Contractor has provided the ACO with documentation that—
L1:(i) Accurately describes those policies, procedures, and practices that the Contractor currently uses in preparing cost
L0:proposals; and
L1:(ii) Provides sufficient detail for the Government to reasonably make an informed judgment regarding the acceptability of
L0:the Contractor's estimating practices.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall—
L1:(i) Comply with its disclosed estimating system; and
L1:(ii) Disclose significant changes to the cost estimating system to the ACO on a timely basis.
L1:(4) The Contractor’s estimating system shall provide for the use of appropriate source data, utilize sound estimating
L0:techniques and good judgment, maintain a consistent approach, and adhere to established policies and procedures. An
L0:acceptable estimating system shall accomplish the following functions:
L1:(i) Establish clear responsibility for preparation, review, and approval of cost estimates and budgets.
L1:(ii) Provide a written description of the organization and duties of the personnel responsible for preparing, reviewing, and
L0:approving cost estimates and budgets.
L1:(iii) Ensure that relevant personnel have sufficient training, experience, and guidance to perform estimating and budgeting
L0:tasks in accordance with the Contractor's established procedures.
L1:(iv) Identify and document the sources of data and the estimating methods and rationale used in developing cost estimates
L0:and budgets.
L1:(v) Provide for adequate supervision throughout the estimating and budgeting process.
L1:(vi) Provide for consistent application of estimating and budgeting techniques.
L1:(vii) Provide for detection and timely correction of errors.
L1:(viii) Protect against cost duplication and omissions.
L1:(ix) Provide for the use of historical experience, including historical vendor pricing data, where appropriate.
L1:(x) Require use of appropriate analytical methods.
L1:(xi) Integrate data and information available from other management systems.
L1:(xii) Require management review, including verification of compliance with the company's estimating and budgeting
L0:policies, procedures, and practices.
L1:(xiii) Provide for internal review of, and accountability for, the acceptability of the estimating system, including the
L0:budgetary data supporting indirect cost estimates and comparisons of projected results to actual results, and an analysis of
L0:any differences.
L1:(xiv) Provide procedures to update cost estimates and notify the Contracting Officer in a timely manner throughout the
L0:negotiation process.
L1:(xv) Provide procedures that ensure subcontract prices are reasonable based on a documented review and analysis provided
L0:with the prime proposal, when practicable.
L1:(xvi) Provide estimating and budgeting practices that consistently generate sound proposals that are compliant with the
L0:provisions of the solicitation and are adequate to serve as a basis to reach a fair and reasonable price.
L1:(xvii) Have an adequate system description, including policies, procedures, and estimating and budgeting practices, that
L0:comply with the Federal Acquisition Regulation and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement.
L1:(e) Material weaknesses .
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer will provide an initial determination to the Contractor, in writing, of any material weaknesses.
L0:The initial determination will describe the underlying deficiency in sufficient detail to allow the Contractor to understand
L0:the weakness or deficiency.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that
L0:identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor’s estimating system. If the Contractor disagrees with the initial
L0:determination, the Contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.
L1:(3) The Contracting Officer will evaluate the Contractor's response and notify the Contractor, in writing, of the Contracting
L0:Officer’s final determination concerning—
L1:(i) Remaining material weaknesses;
L1:(ii) The adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action; and
L1:(iii) System disapproval, if the Contracting Officer determines that one or more material weaknesses remain.
L1:(f) If the Contractor receives the Contracting Officer’s final determination of material weaknesses, the Contractor shall,
L0:within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable
L0:corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the material weaknesses.
L1:(g) Withholding payments. If the Contracting Officer makes a final determination to disapprove the Contractor’s estimating
L0:system, and the contract includes the clause at 252.242-7005 , Contractor Business Systems, the Contracting Officer will
L0:withhold payments in accordance with that clause.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.215-7010 Requirements for Certified Cost or Pricing Data and Data Other Than Certified Cost or Pricing Data
content:
L0:252.215-7010 Requirements for Certified Cost or Pricing Data and Data Other Than Certified Cost or Pricing Data.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 215.408 (5)(i) and (5)(i)(A), use the following provision:
L0:REQUIREMENTS FOR CERTIFIED COST OR PRICING DATA AND DATA OTHER THAN CERTIFIED COST OR
L0:PRICING DATA—BASIC (MAY 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this provision—
L0:“Market prices” means current prices that are established in the course of ordinary trade between buyers and sellers free to
L0:bargain and that can be substantiated through competition or from sources independent of the offerors.
L0:“Non-Government sales” means sales of the supplies or services to non-Governmental entities for purposes other than
L0:governmental purposes.
L0:“Relevant sales data” means information provided by an offeror on sales of the same or similar items that can be used to
L0:establish price reasonableness taking into consideration the age, volume, and nature of the transactions (including any
L0:related discounts, refunds, rebates, offsets, or other adjustments).
L0:Sufficient non-Government sales means relevant sales data that reflects market pricing and contains enough information to
L0:make adjustments covered by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.404-1(b)(2)(ii)(B).
L0:“Uncertified cost data” means the subset of “data other than certified cost or pricing data” (see FAR 2.101) that relates to
L0:cost.
L1:(b) Exceptions from certified cost or pricing data.
L1:(1) In lieu of submitting certified cost or pricing data, the Offeror may submit a written request for exception by submitting
L0:the information described in paragraphs (b)(1)(i) and (ii) of this provision. The Contracting Officer may require additional
L0:supporting information, but only to the extent necessary to determine whether an exception should be granted and whether
L0:the price is fair and reasonable.
L1:(i) Exception for prices set by law or regulation - Identification of the law or regulation establishing the prices offered. If
L0:the prices are controlled under law by periodic rulings, reviews, or similar actions of a governmental body, attach a copy of
L0:the controlling document, unless it was previously submitted to the contracting office.
L1:(ii) Commercial product or commercial service exception. For a commercial product or commercial service exception, the
L0:Offeror shall submit, at a minimum, information that is adequate for determining commerciality and evaluating the
L0:reasonableness of the price for this acquisition, including prices at which the same product or service or similar products or
L0:services have been sold in the commercial market. Such information shall include—
L1:(A) For items previously determined to be commercial, the contract number and military department, defense agency, or
L0:other DoD component that rendered such determination, and if available, a Government point of contact;
L1:(B) For subsystems of a major weapon system and components and spare parts of a major weapon system or subsystem of
L0:a major weapon system that have not previously been determined to be commercial—
L1:(1) The comparable commercial product the Offeror sells to the general public or nongovernmental entities;
L1:(2) A comparison between the physical characteristics and functionality of the comparable commercial product and the
L0:subsystem, component, or spare part, including—
L1:(i) For products under paragraph (3)(i) of the “commercial product” definition at FAR 2.101, a description of the
L0:modification and documentation to support that the modification is customarily available in the marketplace; or
L1:(ii) For products under paragraph (3)(ii) of the “commercial product” definition at FAR 2.101, a detailed description of the
L0:modification and detailed technical data to demonstrate that the modification is minor (e.g., information on production
L0:processes and material differences); and
L1:(3) The national stock number (NSN) for the comparable commercial product, if one is assigned, and the NSN for the
L0:subsystem, component, or spare part, if one is assigned; or
L1:(4) If the Offeror does not sell a comparable commercial product to the general public or nongovernmental entities for
L0:purposes other than government purposes, the Offeror shall—
L1:(i) Notify the Contracting Officer in writing that it does not sell such a comparable product; and
L1:(ii) Provide the Contracting Officer with a comparison of the physical characteristics and functionality of the most
L0:comparable commercial product in the commercial market.
L1:(C) For items priced based on a catalog—
L1:(1) A copy of or identification of the Offeror’s current catalog showing the price for that item; and
L1:(2) If the catalog pricing provided with this proposal is not consistent with all relevant sales data, a detailed description of
L0:differences or inconsistencies between or among the relevant sales data, the proposed price, and the catalog price
L0:(including any related discounts, refunds, rebates, offsets, or other adjustments);
L1:(D) For items priced based on market pricing, a description of the nature of the commercial market, the methodology used
L0:to establish a market price, and all relevant sales data. The description shall be adequate to permit DoD to verify the
L0:accuracy of the description;
L1:(E) For items included on an active Federal Supply Service Multiple Award Schedule contract, proof that an exception has
L0:been granted for the schedule item; or
L1:(F) For items provided by nontraditional defense contractors, a statement that the entity is not currently performing and has
L0:not performed, for at least the 1-year period preceding the solicitation of sources by DoD for the procurement or
L0:transaction, any contract or subcontract for DoD that is subject to full coverage under the cost accounting standards
L0:prescribed pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1502 and the regulations implementing such section.
L1:(2) The Offeror grants the Contracting Officer or an authorized representative the right to examine, at any time before
L0:award, books, records, documents, or other directly pertinent records to verify any request for an exception under this
L0:provision, and to determine the reasonableness of price.
L1:(c) Requirements for certified cost or pricing data. If the Offeror is not granted an exception from the requirement to
L0:submit certified cost or pricing data, the following applies:
L1:(1) The Offeror shall prepare and submit certified cost or pricing data and supporting attachments in accordance with the
L0:instructions contained in Table 15-2 of FAR 15.408, which is incorporated by reference with the same force and effect as
L0:though it were inserted here in full text. The instructions in Table 15-2 are incorporated as a mandatory format to be used in
L0:any resultant contract, unless the Contracting Officer and the Offeror agree to a different format and change this provision
L0:to use Alternate I.
L1:(2) As soon as practicable after agreement on price, but before contract award (except for unpriced actions such as letter
L0:contracts), the Offeror shall submit a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data, as prescribed by FAR 15.406-2.
L1:(3) The Offeror is responsible for determining whether a subcontractor qualifies for an exception from the requirement for
L0:submission of certified cost or pricing data on the basis of adequate price competition, i.e., two or more responsible
L0:offerors, competing independently, submit priced offers that satisfy the Government’s expressed requirement in accordance
L0:with FAR 15.403-1(c)(1)(ii).
L1:(d) Requirements for data other than certified cost or pricing data.
L1:(1) Data other than certified cost or pricing data submitted in accordance with this provision shall include the minimum
L0:information necessary to permit a determination that the proposed price is fair and reasonable, to include the requirements
L0:in Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement ( DFARS) 215.402(a)(i), 215.404-1(b), and 234.7002(e).
L1:(2) In cases in which uncertified cost data is required, the information shall be provided in the form in which it is regularly
L0:maintained by the Offeror or prospective subcontractor in its business operations.
L1:(3) If the Offeror redacts data that identifies the customer (see DFARS 234.7002(e)(2)), then the Offeror shall include, for
L0:each sale, the following signed statement with the data submitted:
L0:“By submission of this data, the Offeror [Offeror insert company name] certifies that the customer was [Offeror insert one
L0:or more of the following as applicable: a government customer; a commercial customer purchasing the same or similar
L0:product for governmental purposes (e.g., Federal, state, local, or foreign government); or a commercial customer
L0:purchasing the same or similar product for a commercial, mixed, or unknown purpose ].”
L1:(4) Within 10 days of a written request from the Contracting Officer for additional information to permit an adequate
L0:evaluation of the proposed price in accordance with FAR 15.403-3 or DFARS 234.7002(e), the Offeror shall provide either
L0:the requested information, or a written explanation for the inability to fully comply.
L1:(5) Subcontract price evaluation. (i) Offerors shall obtain from subcontractors the minimum information necessary to
L0:support a determination of price reasonableness, as described in FAR part 15 and DFARS part 215.
L1:(ii) No cost data may be required from a prospective subcontractor in any case in which there are sufficient nonGovernment sales of the same item to establish reasonableness of price.
L1:(iii) If the Offeror relies on relevant sales data for similar items to determine the price is reasonable, the Offeror shall obtain
L0:only that technical information necessary (A) To support the conclusion that items are technically similar; and
L1:(B) To explain any technical differences that account for variances between the proposed prices and the sales data
L0:presented.
L1:(e) Subcontracts. The Offeror shall insert the substance of this provision, including this paragraph (e), in subcontracts
L0:exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold defined in FAR part 2. The Offeror shall require prospective subcontractors
L0:to adhere to the requirements of https://www.acquisition.gov/node/36356/printable/print
L1:(1) Paragraphs (c) and (d) of this provision for subcontracts above the threshold for submission of certified cost or pricing
L0:data in FAR 15.403-4; and
L1:(2) Paragraph (d) of this provision for subcontracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold defined in FAR part 2.
L0:(End of provision)
L0:Alternate I. As prescribed in 215.408(5)(i) and (5)(i)(B), use the following provision, which includes a different paragraph
L1:(c)(1).

L1:(4) The Offeror shall provide information described as follows: [Insert description of the data and the format that are

L0:FAR 15.403-3 or DFARS 234.7002(e)].
L1:(5) Within 10 days of a written request from the Contracting Officer for additional information to support proposal
L0:analysis, the Offeror shall provide either the requested information, or a written explanation for the inability to fully
L0:comply.
L1:(6) Subcontract price evaluation.
L1:(i) Offerors shall obtain from subcontractors the information necessary to support a determination of price reasonableness,
L0:as described in FAR part 15 and DFARS part 215.
L1:(ii) No cost information may be required from a prospective subcontractor in any case in which there are sufficient nonGovernment sales of the same item to establish reasonableness of price.
L1:(iii) If the Offeror relies on relevant sales data for similar items to determine the price is reasonable, the Offeror shall obtain
L0:only that technical information necessary—
L1:(A) To support the conclusion that items are technically similar; and
L1:(B) To explain any technical differences that account for variances between the proposed prices and the sales data
L0:presented.
L1:(e) Subcontracts. The Offeror shall insert the substance of this provision, including this paragraph (e), in all subcontracts
L0:exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold defined in FAR part 2. The Offeror shall require prospective subcontractors
L0:to adhere to the requirements of—
L1:(1) Paragraph (c) and (d) of this provision for subcontracts above the threshold for submission of certified cost or pricing
L0:data in FAR 15.403-4; and
L1:(2) Paragraph (d) of this provision for subcontracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold defined in FAR part 2.
L0:(End of provision)

title: 252.215-7014 Exception from Certified Cost or Pricing Data Requirements for Foreign Military Sales Indirect
content:
L0:252.215-7014 Exception from Certified Cost or Pricing Data Requirements for Foreign Military Sales Indirect
L0:Offsets.
L0:As prescribed in 215.408 (8), use the following clause:
L0:EXCEPTION FROM CERTIFIED COST OR PRICING DATA REQUIREMENTS FOR FOREIGN MILITARY SALES
L0:INDIRECT OFFSETS (JUN 2018)
L1:(a) Definition. As used in this clause—
L0:“Offset” means a benefit or obligation agreed to by a contractor and a foreign government or international organization as
L0:an inducement or condition to purchase supplies or services pursuant to a foreign military sale (FMS). There are two types
L0:of offsets: direct offsets and indirect offsets.
L1:(1) A direct offset involves benefits or obligations, including supplies or services that are directly related to the item being
L0:purchased and are integral to the deliverable of the FMS contract. For example, as a condition of a foreign military sale, the
L0:contractor may require or agree to permit the customer to produce in its country certain components or subsystems of the
L0:item being sold. Generally, direct offsets must be performed within a specified period, because they are integral to the
L0:deliverable of the FMS contract.
L1:(2) An indirect offset involves benefits or obligations, including supplies or services that are not directly related to the
L0:specific item(s) being purchased and are not integral to the deliverable of the FMS contract. For example, as a condition of
L0:a foreign military sale, the contractor may agree to purchase certain manufactured products, agricultural commodities, raw
L0:materials, or services, or make an equity investment or grant of equipment required by the FMS customer, or may agree to
L0:build a school, road or other facility. Indirect offsets would also include projects that are related to the FMS contract but not
L0:purchased under said contract (e.g., a project to develop or advance a capability, technology transfer, or know-how in a
L0:foreign company). Indirect offsets may be accomplished without a clearly defined period of performance.
L1:(b) Exceptions from certified cost or pricing data requirements. Notwithstanding the requirements of Federal Acquisition
L0:Regulation (FAR) 52.215-20, Requirements for Certified Cost or Pricing Data and Data Other Than Certified Cost or
L0:Pricing Data, in the case of this contract or a subcontract, and FAR 52.215-21, Requirements for Certified Cost or Pricing
L0:Data and Data Other Than Certified Cost or Pricing Data—Modifications, in the case of modification of this contract or a
L0:subcontract, submission of certified cost or pricing data shall not be required to the extent such data relates to an indirect
L0:offset (10 U.S.C. 3703(a)(4)).
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.215-7014 — Exception from Certified Cost or Pricing Data Requirements for Foreign Military Sales Indirect

L1:(2) When required, the minimum postaward debriefing information will include the following:

L0:written source selection decision document, redacted to protect the confidential and proprietary information of other
L0:offerors for the contract award.
L1:(ii) For contracts in excess of $150 million, disclosure of the agency’s written source selection decision document, redacted
L0:to protect the confidential and proprietary information of other offerors for the contract award.
L1:(3) If a required postaward debriefing is provided—
L1:(i) The debriefed Offeror may submit additional written questions related to the debriefing not later than 2 business days
L0:after the date of the debriefing;
L1:(ii) The agency will respond in writing to timely submitted additional questions within 5 business days after receipt by the
L0:contracting officer; and
L1:(iii) The postaward debriefing will not be considered to be concluded until the later of—
L1:(A) The date that the postaward debriefing is delivered, orally or in writing; or
L1:(B) If additional written questions related to the debriefing are timely received, the date the agency delivers its written
L0:response.
L1:(c) Contract performance. The Government may suspend performance of or terminate the awarded contract upon notice
L0:from the Government Accountability Office of a protest filed within the time periods listed in paragraphs (c)(1) through (3)
L0:of this provision, whichever is later:
L1:(1) Within 10 days after the date of contract award.
L1:(2) Within 5 days after a debriefing date offered to the protestor under a timely debriefing request in accordance with
L0:Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.506 unless an earlier debriefing date is negotiated as a result.
L1:(3) Within 5 days after a postaward debriefing under FAR 15.506 is concluded in accordance with Defense Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation Supplement 215.506-70 (b).

title: 252.216-7000 Economic Price Adjustment—Basic Steel, Aluminum, Brass, Bronze, or Copper Mill Products
content:
L0:252.216-7000 Economic Price Adjustment—Basic Steel, Aluminum, Brass, Bronze, or Copper Mill Products.
L0:As prescribed in 216.203-4 -70(a)(1), use the following clause:
L0:ECONOMIC PRICE ADJUSTMENT—BASIC STEEL, ALUMINUM, BRASS, BRONZE, OR COPPER MILL
L0:PRODUCTS (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Established price” means a price which is an established catalog or market price for a commercial product sold in
L0:substantial quantities to the general public.
L0:“Unit price” excludes any part of the price which reflects requirements for preservation, packaging, and packing beyond
L0:standard commercial practice.
L1:(b) As represented by the Contractor in its offer, the unit price stated for ____________________(Identify the item) is not
L0:in excess of the Contractor's established price in effect on the date set for opening of bids (or the contract date if this is a
L0:negotiated contract) for like quantities of the same item. This price is the net price after applying any applicable standard
L0:trade discounts offered by the Contractor from its catalog, list, or schedule price.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall promptly notify the Contracting Officer of the amount and effective date of each decrease in any
L0:established price.
L1:(1) Each corresponding contract unit price shall be decreased by the same percentage that the established price is
L0:decreased.
L1:(2) This decrease shall apply to items delivered on or after the effective date of the decrease in the Contractor's established
L0:price.
L1:(3) This contract shall be modified accordingly.
L1:(d) If the Contractor's established price is increased after the date set for opening of bids (or the contract date if this is a
L0:negotiated contract), upon the Contractor's written request to the Contracting Officer, the corresponding contract unit price
L0:shall be increased by the same percentage that the established price is increased, and this contract shall be modified
L0:accordingly, provided—
L1:(1) The aggregate of the increases in any contract unit price under this contract shall not exceed 10 percent of the original
L0:contract unit price;
L1:(2) The increased contract unit price shall be effective on the effective date of the increase in the applicable established
L0:price if the Contractor's written request is received by the Contracting Officer within ten days of the change. If it is not, the
L0:effective date of the increased unit price shall be the date of receipt of the request by the Contracting Officer; and
L1:(3) The increased contract unit price shall not apply to quantities scheduled for delivery before the effective date of the
L0:increased contract unit price unless the Contractor's failure to deliver before that date results from causes beyond the
L0:control and without the fault or negligence of the Contractor, within the meaning of the Default clause of this contract.
L1:(4) The Contracting Officer shall not execute a modification incorporating an increase in a contract unit price under this
L0:clause until the increase is verified.
L1:(e) Within 30 days after receipt of the Contractor's written request, the Contracting Officer may cancel, without liability to
L0:either party, any portion of the contract affected by the requested increase and not delivered at the time of such
L0:cancellation, except as follows—
L1:(1) The Contractor may, after that time, deliver any items that were completed or in the process of manufacture at the time
L0:of receipt of the cancellation notice, provided the Contractor notifies the Contracting Officer of such items within 10 days
L0:after the Contractor receives the cancellation notice.
L1:(2) The Government shall pay for those items at the contract unit price increased to the extent provided by paragraph (d) of
L0:this clause.
L1:(3) Any standard steel supply item shall be deemed to be in the process of manufacture when the steel for that item is in the
L0:state of processing after the beginning of the furnace melt.
L1:(f) Pending any cancellation of this contract under paragraph (e) of this clause, or if there is no cancellation, the Contractor
L0:shall continue deliveries according to the delivery schedule of the contract. The Contractor shall be paid for those
L0:deliveries at the contract unit price increased to the extent provided by paragraph (d) of this clause.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.216-7000 — Economic Price Adjustment—Basic Steel, Aluminum, Brass, Bronze, or Copper Mill Products

title: 252.216-7001 Economic Price Adjustment-Nonstandard Steel Items
content:
L0:252.216-7001 Economic Price Adjustment-Nonstandard Steel Items.
L0:As prescribed in 216.203-4 -70(b), use the following clause:
L0:ECONOMIC PRICE ADJUSTMENT—NONSTANDARD STEEL ITEMS (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Base labor index” means the average of the labor indices for the three months which consist of the month of bid opening
L0:(or offer submission) and the months immediately preceding and following that month.
L0:“Base steel index” means the Contractor's established price (see Note 6) including all applicable extras of $________ per
L0:____________ (see Note 1) for _______________ (see Note 2) on the date set for bid opening (or the date of submission
L0:of the offer).
L0:“Current labor index” means the average of the labor indices for the month in which delivery of supplies is required to be
L0:made and the month preceding.
L0:“Current steel index” means the Contractor's established price (see Note 6) for that item, including all applicable extras in
L0:effect ___ days (see Note 3) prior to the first day of the month in which delivery is required.
L0:“Established price” is—
L1:(1) A price which is an established catalog or market price of a commercial product sold in substantial quantities to the
L0:general public; and
L1:(2) The net price after applying any applicable standard trade discounts offered by the Contractor from its catalog, list, or
L0:schedule price. (But see Note 6.)
L0:“Labor index” means the average straight time hourly earnings of the Contractor's employees in the ____________ shop of
L0:the Contractor's ________________ plant (see Note 4) for any particular month.
L0:“Month” means calendar month. However, if the Contractor's accounting period does not coincide with the calendar month,
L0:then that accounting period shall be used in lieu of “month.”
L1:(b) Each contract unit price shall be subject to revision, under the terms of this clause, to reflect changes in the cost of labor
L0:and steel. For purpose of this price revision, the proportion of the contract unit price attributable to costs of labor not
L0:otherwise included in the price of the steel item identified under the “base steel index” definition in paragraph (a) shall be
L0:_____ percent, and the proportion of the contract unit price attributable to the cost of steel shall be _____ percent. (See
L0:Note 5.)
L1:(c)(1) Unless otherwise specified in this contract, the labor index shall be computed by dividing the total straight time
L0:earnings of the Contractor's employees in the shop identified in paragraph (a) for any given month by the total number of
L0:straight time hours worked by those employees in that month.
L1:(2) Any revision in a contract unit price to reflect changes in the cost of labor shall be computed solely by reference to the
L0:“base labor index” and the “current labor index.”
L1:(d) Any revision in a contract unit price to reflect changes in the cost of steel shall be computed solely by reference to the
L0:“base steel index” and the “current steel index.”
L1:(e)(1) Each contract unit price shall be revised for each month in which delivery of supplies is required to be made.
L1:(2) The revised contract unit price shall apply to the deliveries of those quantities required to be made in that month
L0:regardless of when actual delivery is made.
L1:(3) Each revised contract unit price shall be computed by adding—
L1:(i) The adjusted cost of labor (obtained by multiplying ____ percent of the contract unit price by a fraction, of which the
L0:numerator shall be the current labor index and the denominator shall be the base labor index);
L1:(ii) The adjusted cost of steel (obtained by multiplying ____ percent of the contract unit price by a fraction, of which the
L0:numerator shall be the current steel index and the denominator shall be the base steel index); and
L1:(iii) The amount equal to ____ percent of the original contract unit price (representing that portion of the unit price which
L0:relates neither to the cost of labor nor the cost of steel, and which is therefore not subject to revision (see Note 5)).
L1:(4) The aggregate of the increases in any contract unit price under this contract shall not exceed ten percent of the original
L0:contract unit price.
L1:(5) Computations shall be made to the nearest one-hundredth of one cent.
L1:(f)(1) Pending any revisions of the contract unit prices, the Contractor shall be paid the contract unit price for deliveries
L0:made.
L1:(2) Within 30 days after final delivery (or such other period as may be authorized by the Contracting Officer), the
L0:Contractor shall furnish a statement identifying the correctness of—
L1:(i) The average straight time hourly earnings of the Contractor's employees in the shop identified in paragraph (a) that are
L0:relevant to the computations of the “base labor index” and the “current labor index;” and
L1:(ii) The Contractor's established prices (see Note 6), including all applicable extras for like quantities of the item that are
L0:relevant to the computation of the “base steel index” and the “current steel index.”
L1:(3) Upon request of the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall make available all records used in the computation of the
L0:labor indices.
L1:(4) Upon receipt of the statement, the Contracting Officer will compute the revised contract unit prices and modify the
L0:contract accordingly. No modification to this contract will be made pursuant to this clause until the Contracting Officer has
L0:verified the revised established price (see Note 6).
L1:(g)(1) In the event any item of this contract is subject to a total or partial termination for convenience, the month in which
L0:the Contractor receives notice of the termination, if prior to the month in which delivery is required, shall be considered the
L0:month in which delivery of the terminated item is required for the purposes of determining the current labor and steel
L0:indices under paragraphs (c) and (d).
L1:(2) For any item which is not terminated for convenience, the month in which delivery is required under the contract shall
L0:continue to apply for determining those indices with respect to the quantity of the non-terminated item.
L1:(3) If this contract is terminated for default, any price revision shall be limited to the quantity of the item which has been
L0:delivered by the Contractor and accepted by the Government prior to receipt by the Contractor of the notice of termination.
L1:(h) If the Contractor's failure to make delivery of any required quantity arises out of causes beyond the control and without
L0:the fault or negligence of the Contractor, within the meaning of the clause of this contract entitled “Default,” the quantity
L0:not delivered shall be delivered as promptly as possible after the cessation of the cause of the failure, and the delivery
L0:schedule set forth in this contract shall be amended accordingly.
L0:NOTES:
L0:1 Offeror insert the unit price and unit measure of the standard steel mill item to be used in the manufacture of the contract
L0:item.
L0:2 Offeror identify the standard steel mill item to be used in the manufacture of the contract item.
L0:3 Offeror insert best estimate of the number of days required for processing the standard steel mill item in the shop
L0:identified under the “labor index” definition.
L0:4 Offeror identify the shop and plant in which the standard steel mill item identified under the “base steel index” definition
L0:will be finally fabricated or processed into the contract item.
L0:5 Offeror insert the same percentage figures for the corresponding blanks in paragraphs (b), (e)(3)(i), and (e)(3)(ii). In
L0:paragraph (e)(3)(iii), insert the percentage representing the difference between the sum of the percentages inserted in
L0:paragraph (b) and 100 percent.
L0:6 In negotiated acquisitions of nonstandard steel items, when there is no “established price” or when it is not desirable to
L0:use this price, this paragraph may refer to another appropriate price basis, e.g., an established interplant price.
L0:(End of clause)

L0:AWARD FEE REDUCTION OR DENIAL FOR JEOPARDIZING THE HEALTH OR SAFETY OF GOVERNMENT
L0:PERSONNEL (SEP 2011)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Covered incident”-

L1:(A) Has been determined in the performance of this contract to have caused serious bodily injury or death of any civilian or

L1:(B) In a civil proceeding, a finding of fault or liability that results in the payment of a monetary fine, penalty,
L0:reimbursement, restitution, or damage of $5,000 or more.
L1:(C) In an administrative proceeding, a finding of fault and liability that results in-
L1:(1) The payment of a monetary fine or penalty of $5,000 or more; or
L1:(2) The payment of a reimbursement, restitution, or damages in excess of $100,000.
L1:(D) In a criminal, civil, or administrative proceeding, a disposition of the matter by consent or compromise with an
L0:acknowledgment of fault by the Contractor if the proceeding could have led to any of the outcomes specified in
L0:subparagraphs (a)(ii)(A), (a) (ii)(B), or (a)(ii)(C).
L1:(E) In a DoD investigation of the Contractor or its subcontractors at any tier not subject to the jurisdiction of the U.S.
L0:courts, a final determination by the Secretary of Defense of Contractor or subcontractor fault (see DFARS 216.405-2 -70).
L0:“Serious bodily injury” means a grievous physical harm that results in a permanent disability.
L1:(b) If, in the performance of this contract, the Contractor’s or its subcontractor’s actions cause serious bodily injury or
L0:death of civilian or military Government personnel, the Government may reduce or deny the award fee for the relevant
L0:award fee period in which the covered incident occurred, including the recovery of all or part of any award fees paid for
L0:any previous period during which the covered incident occurred.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.216-7004 — Award Fee Reduction or Denial for Jeopardizing the Health or Safety of Government Personnel

title: 252.216-7010 Postaward Debriefings for Task Orders and Delivery Orders
content:
L0:252.216-7010 Postaward Debriefings for Task Orders and Delivery Orders.

L0:POSTAWARD DEBRIEFINGS FOR TASK ORDERS AND DELIVERY ORDERS (OCT 2025)

L0:orders valued at $15 million or more to the Contractor, regardless of whether the Contractor’s offer for the task order or
L0:delivery order was successful or unsuccessful, while protecting the confidential and proprietary information of other
L0:contractors. The request is considered timely if received within 3 days of notification of task order or delivery order award.

L1:(iii) The postaward debriefing will not be considered to be concluded until the later of—

L0:response.

L0:task order or delivery order upon notice from the Government Accountability Office of a protest filed within the time
L0:periods listed in paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this clause, whichever is later:
L1:(1) Within 10 days after the date a task order or delivery order is issued, where the value exceeds $25 million (10 U.S.C.

L1:(2) Within 5 days after a debriefing date offered to the protestor under a timely debriefing request in accordance with
L0:Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.506 unless an earlier debriefing date is negotiated as a result.
L1:(3) Within 5 days after a postaward debriefing under FAR 15.506 is concluded in accordance with Defense Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation Supplement 215.506-70 (b).

title: 252.217-7001 Surge Option
content:
L0:252.217-7001 Surge Option.
L0:As prescribed in 217.208-70 (b), use the following clause:
L0:SURGE OPTION (DEC 2018)
L1:(a) General. The Government has the option to—
L1:(1) Increase the quantity of supplies or services called for under this contract by no more than ___ percent or
L0:_______________ [insert quantity and description of services or supplies to be increased]; and/or
L1:(2) Accelerate the rate of delivery called for under this contract, at a price or cost established before contract award or to be
L0:established by negotiation as provided in this clause.
L1:(b) Schedule.
L1:(1) When the Capabilities Analysis Plan (CAP) is included in the contract, the option delivery schedule shall be the
L0:production rate provided with the Plan. If the Plan was negotiated before contract award, then the negotiated schedule shall
L0:be used.
L1:(2) If there is no CAP in the contract, the Contractor shall, within 30 days from the date of award, furnish the Contracting
L0:Officer a delivery schedule showing the maximum sustainable rate of delivery for items in this contract. This delivery
L0:schedule shall provide acceleration by month up to the maximum sustainable rate of delivery achievable within the
L0:Contractor's existing facilities, equipment, and subcontracting structure.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall not revise the option delivery schedule without approval from the Contracting Officer.
L1:(c) Exercise of option.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer may exercise this option at any time before acceptance by the Government of the final
L0:scheduled delivery.
L1:(2) The Contracting Officer will provide a preliminary oral or written notice to the Contractor stating the quantities to be
L0:added or accelerated under the terms of this clause, followed by a contract modification incorporating the transmitted
L0:information and instructions. The notice and modification will establish a not-to-exceed price equal to the highest contract
L0:unit price or cost of the added or accelerated items as of the date of the notice.
L1:(3) The Contractor will not be required to deliver at a rate greater than the maximum sustainable delivery rate under
L0:paragraph (b)(2) of this clause, nor will the exercise of this option extend delivery more than 24 months beyond the
L0:scheduled final delivery.
L1:(d) Price negotiation.
L1:(1) Unless the option cost or price was previously agreed upon, the Contractor shall, within 30 days from the date of option
L0:exercise, submit to the Contracting Officer a cost or price proposal (including a cost breakdown) for the added or
L0:accelerated items.
L1:(2) Failure to agree on a cost or price in negotiations resulting from the exercise of this option shall constitute a dispute
L0:concerning a question of fact within the meaning of the Disputes clause of this contract. However, nothing in this clause
L0:shall excuse the Contractor from proceeding with the performance of the contract, as modified, while any resulting claim is
L0:being settled.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.217-7003 Changes
content:
L0:252.217-7003 Changes.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104 (a), use the following clause:
L0:CHANGES (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Contracting Officer may, at any time and without notice to the sureties, by written change order, make changes
L0:within the general scope of any job order issued under the Master Agreement in—
L1:(1) Drawings, designs, plans, and specifications;
L1:(2) Work itemized;
L1:(3) Place of performance of the work;
L1:(4) Time of commencement or completion of the work; and
L1:(5) Any other requirement of the job order.
L1:(b) If a change causes an increase or decrease in the cost of, or time required for, performance of the job order, whether or
L0:not changed by the order, the Contracting Officer shall make an equitable adjustment in the price or date of completion, or
L0:both, and shall modify the job order in writing.
L1:(1) Within ten days after the Contractor receives notification of the change, the Contractor shall submit to the Contracting
L0:Officer a request for price adjustment, together with a written estimate of the increased cost.
L1:(2) The Contracting Officer may grant an extension of this period if the Contractor requests it within the ten day period.
L1:(3) If the circumstances justify it, the Contracting Officer may accept and grant a request for equitable adjustment at any
L0:later time prior to final payment under the job order, except that the Contractor may not receive profit on a payment under a
L0:late request.
L1:(c) If the Contractor includes in its claim the cost of property made obsolete or excess as a result of a change, the
L0:Contracting Officer shall have the right to prescribe the manner of disposition of that property.
L1:(d) Failure to agree to any adjustment shall be a dispute within the meaning of the Disputes clause.
L1:(e) Nothing in this clause shall excuse the Contractor from proceeding with the job order as changed.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.217-7004 Job Orders and Compensation
content:
L0:252.217-7004 Job Orders and Compensation.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104 (a), use the following clause:
L0:JOB ORDERS AND COMPENSATION (MAY 2006)
L1:(a) The Contracting Officer shall solicit bids or proposals and make award of job orders. The issuance of a job order signed
L0:by the Contracting Officer constitutes award. The job order shall incorporate the terms and conditions of the Master
L0:Agreement.
L1:(b) Whenever the Contracting Officer determines that a vessel, its cargo or stores, would be endangered by delay, or
L0:whenever the Contracting Officer determines that military necessity requires that immediate work on a vessel is necessary,
L0:the Contracting Officer may issue a written order to perform that work and the Contractor hereby agrees to comply with
L0:that order and to perform work on such vessel within its capabilities.
L1:(1) As soon as practicable after the issuance of the order, the Contracting Officer and the Contractor shall negotiate a price
L0:for the work and the Contracting Officer shall issue a job order covering the work.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall, upon request, furnish the Contracting Officer with a breakdown of costs incurred by the
L0:Contractor and an estimate of costs expected to be incurred in the performance of the work. The Contractor shall maintain,
L0:and make available for inspection by the Contracting Officer or the Contracting Officer's representative, records supporting
L0:the cost of performing the work.
L1:(3) Failure of the parties to agree upon the price of the work shall constitute a dispute within the meaning of the Disputes
L0:clause of the Master Agreement. In the meantime, the Contractor shall diligently proceed to perform the work ordered.
L1:(c)(1) If the nature of any repairs is such that their extent and probable cost cannot be ascertained readily, the Contracting
L0:Officer may issue a job order (on a sealed bid or negotiated basis) to determine the nature and extent of required repairs.
L1:(2) Upon determination by the Contracting Officer of what work is necessary, the Contractor, if requested by the
L0:Contracting Officer, shall negotiate prices for performance of that work. The prices agreed upon shall be set forth in a
L0:modification of the job order.
L1:(3) Failure of the parties to agree upon the price shall constitute a dispute under the Disputes clause. In the meantime, the
L0:Contractor shall diligently proceed to perform the work ordered.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.217-7005 Inspection and Manner of Doing Work
content:
L0:252.217-7005 Inspection and Manner of Doing Work.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104 (a), use the following clause:
L0:INSPECTION AND MANNER OF DOING WORK (JUL 2009)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall perform work in accordance with the job order, any drawings and specifications made a part of the
L0:job order, and any change or modification issued under the Changes clause of the Master Agreement.
L1:(b)(1) Except as provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this clause, and unless otherwise specifically provided in the job order, all
L0:operational practices of the Contractor and all workmanship, material, equipment, and articles used in the performance of
L0:work under the Master Agreement shall be in accordance with the best commercial marine practices and the rules and
L0:requirements of the American Bureau of Shipping, the U.S. Coast Guard, and the Institute of Electrical and Electronic
L0:Engineers, in effect at the time of Contractor's submission of bid (or acceptance of the job order, if negotiated).
L1:(2) When Navy specifications are specified in the job order, the Contractor shall follow Navy standards of material and
L0:workmanship. The solicitation shall prescribe the Navy standard whenever applicable.
L1:(c) The Government may inspect and test all material and workmanship at any time during the Contractor's performance of
L0:the work.
L1:(1) If, prior to delivery, the Government finds any material or workmanship is defective or not in accordance with the job
L0:order, in addition to its rights under the Guarantees clause of the Master Agreement, the Government may reject the
L0:defective or nonconforming material or workmanship and require the Contractor to correct or replace it at the Contractor's
L0:expense.
L1:(2) If the Contractor fails to proceed promptly with the replacement or correction of the material or workmanship, the
L0:Government may replace or correct the defective or nonconforming material or workmanship and charge the Contractor the
L0:excess costs incurred.
L1:(3) As specified in the job order, the Contractor shall provide and maintain an inspection system acceptable to the
L0:Government.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall maintain complete records of all inspection work and shall make them available to the
L0:Government during performance of the job order and for 90 days after the completion of all work required.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall not permit any welder to work on a vessel unless the welder is, at the time of the work, qualified to
L0:the standards established by the U.S. Coast Guard, American Bureau of Shipping, or Department of the Navy for the type
L0:of welding being performed. Qualifications of a welder shall be as specified in the job order.
L1:(e) The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Exercise reasonable care to protect the vessel from fire;
L1:(2) Maintain a reasonable system of inspection over activities taking place in the vicinity of the vessel's magazines, fuel oil
L0:tanks, or storerooms containing flammable materials;
L1:(3) Maintain a reasonable number of hose lines ready for immediate use on the vessel at all times while the vessel is
L0:berthed alongside the Contractor's pier or in dry dock or on a marine railway;
L1:(4) Unless otherwise provided in a job order, provide sufficient security patrols to reasonably maintain a fire watch for
L0:protection of the vessel when it is in the Contractor's custody;
L1:(5) To the extent necessary, clean, wash, and steam out or otherwise make safe, all tanks under alteration or repair;
L1:(6) Furnish the Contracting Officer or designated representative with a copy of the “gas-free” or “safe-for-hotwork”
L0:certificate, provided by a Marine Chemist or Coast Guard authorized person in accordance with Occupational Safety and
L0:Health Administration regulations (29 CFR 1915.14) before any hot work is done on a tank;
L1:(7) Treat the contents of any tank as Government property in accordance with the Government Property clause; and
L1:(8) Dispose of the contents of any tank only at the direction, or with the concurrence, of the Contracting Officer.
L1:(f) Except as otherwise provided in the job order, when the vessel is in the custody of the Contractor or in dry dock or on a
L0:marine railway and the temperature is expected to go as low as 35 of, the Contractor shall take all necessary steps to—
L1:(1) Keep all hose pipe lines, fixtures, traps, tanks, and other receptacles on the vessel from freezing; and
L1:(2) Protect the stern tube and propeller hubs from frost damage.
L1:(g) The Contractor shall, whenever practicable—
L1:(1) Perform the required work in a manner that will not interfere with the berthing and messing of Government personnel
L0:attached to the vessel; and
L1:(2) Provide Government personnel attached to the vessel access to the vessel at all times.
L1:(h) Government personnel attached to the vessel shall not interfere with the Contractor's work or workers.
L1:(i)(1) The Government does not guarantee the correctness of the dimensions, sizes, and shapes set forth in any job order,
L0:sketches, drawings, plans, or specifications prepared or furnished by the Government, unless the job order requires that the
L0:Contractor perform the work prior to any opportunity to inspect.
L1:(2) Except as stated in paragraph (i)(1) of this clause, and other than those parts furnished by the Government, the
L0:Contractor shall be responsible for the correctness of the dimensions, sizes, and shapes of parts furnished under this
L0:agreement.
L1:(j) The Contractor shall at all times keep the site of the work on the vessel free from accumulation of waste material or
L0:rubbish caused by its employees or the work. At the completion of the work, unless the job order specifies otherwise, the
L0:Contractor shall remove all rubbish from the site of the work and leave the immediate vicinity of the work area “broom
L0:clean.”
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.217-7005 — Inspection and Manner of Doing Work

title: 252.217-7007 Payments
content:
L0:252.217-7007 Payments.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104 (a), use the following clause:
L0:PAYMENTS (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) “Progress payments,” as used in this clause, means payments made before completion of work in progress under a job
L0:order.
L1:(b) Upon submission by the Contractor of invoices in the form and number of copies directed by the Contracting Officer,
L0:and as approved by the Contracting Officer, the Government will make progress payments as work progresses under the
L0:job order.
L1:(1) Generally, the Contractor may submit invoices on a semi-monthly basis, unless expenditures justify a more frequent
L0:submission.
L1:(2) The Government need not make progress payments for invoices aggregating less than $5,000.
L1:(3) The Contracting Officer shall approve progress payments based on the value, computed on the price of the job order, of
L0:labor and materials incorporated in the work, materials suitably stored at the site of the work, and preparatory work
L0:completed, less the aggregate of any previous payments.
L1:(4) Upon request, the Contractor will furnish the Contracting Officer any reports concerning expenditures on the work to
L0:date that the Contracting Officer may require.
L1:(c) The Government will retain until final completion and acceptance of all work covered by the job order, an amount
L0:estimated or approved by the Contracting Officer under paragraph (b) of this clause. The amount retained will be in
L0:accordance with the rate authorized by Congress for Naval vessel repair contracts at the time of job order award.
L1:(d) The Contracting Officer may direct that progress payments be based on the price of the job order as adjusted as a result
L0:of change orders under the Changes clause of the Master Agreement. If the Contracting Officer does not so direct—
L1:(1) Payments of any increases shall be made from time to time after the amount of the increase is determined under the
L0:Changes clause of the Master Agreement; and
L1:(2) Reductions resulting from decreases shall be made for the purposes of subsequent progress payments as soon as the
L0:amounts are determined under the Changes clause of the Master Agreement.
L1:(e) Upon completion of the work under a job order and final inspection and acceptance, and upon submission of invoices in
L0:such form and with such copies as the Contracting Officer may prescribe, the Contractor shall be paid for the price of the
L0:job order, as adjusted pursuant to the Changes clause of the Master Agreement, less any performance reserves deemed
L0:necessary by the Contracting Officer, and less the amount of any previous payments.
L1:(f) All materials, equipment, or any other property or work in process covered by the progress payments made by the
L0:Government, upon the making of those progress payments, shall become the sole property of the Government, and are
L0:subject to the provisions of the Title clause of the Master Agreement.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.217-7009 Default
content:
L0:252.217-7009 Default.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104 (a), use the following clause:
L0:DEFAULT (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Government may, subject to the provisions of paragraph (b) of this clause, by written notice of default to the
L0:Contractor, terminate the whole or any part of a job order if the Contractor fails to—
L1:(1) Make delivery of the supplies or to perform the services within the time specified in a job order or any extension;
L1:(2) Make progress, so as to endanger performance of the job order; or
L1:(3) Perform any of the other provisions of this agreement or a job order.
L1:(b) Except for defaults of subcontractors, the Contractor shall not be liable for any excess costs if failure to perform the job
L0:order arises from causes beyond the control and without the fault or negligence of the Contractor. Examples of such causes
L0:include acts of God or of the public enemy, acts of the Government in either its sovereign or contractual capacity, fires,
L0:floods, epidemics, quarantine restrictions, strikes, freight embargoes, and unusually severe weather.
L1:(c) If the Contractor's failure to perform is caused by the default of a subcontractor, and if such default arises out of causes
L0:beyond the control of both the Contractor and subcontractor, and without the fault or negligence of either, the Contractor
L0:shall not be liable for any excess costs for failure to perform, unless the supplies or services to be furnished by the
L0:subcontractor were obtainable from other sources in sufficient time to permit the Contractor to perform the job order within
L0:the time specified.
L1:(d) If the Government terminates the job order in whole or in part as provided in paragraph (a) of this clause—
L1:(1) The Government may, upon such terms and in such manner as the Contracting Officer may deem appropriate, arrange
L0:for the completion of the work so terminated, at such plant or plants, including that of the Contractor, as may be designated
L0:by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall continue the performance of the job order to the extent not terminated under the provisions of this
L0:clause.
L1:(ii) If the work is to be completed at the plant, the Government may use all tools, machinery, facilities, and equipment of
L0:the Contractor determined by the Contracting Office to be necessary for that purpose.
L1:(iii) If the cost to the Government of the work procured or completed (after adjusting such cost to exclude the effect of
L0:changes in the plans and specifications made subsequent to the date of termination) exceeds the price fixed for work under
L0:the job order (after adjusting such price on account of changes in the plans and specifications made before the date of
L0:termination), the Contractor, or the Contractor's surety, if any, shall be liable for such excess.
L1:(2) The Government, in addition to any other rights provided in this clause, may require the Contractor to transfer title and
L0:delivery to the Government, in the manner and to the extent directed by the Contracting Officer, any completed supplies
L0:and such partially completed supplies and materials, parts, tools, dies, jigs, fixtures, plans, drawings, information and
L0:contract rights (hereinafter called “manufacturing materials”) as the Contractor has specifically produced or specifically
L0:acquired for the performance of the terminated part of the job order.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall, upon direction of the Contracting Officer, protect and preserve property in possession of the
L0:Contractor in which the Government has an interest.
L1:(ii) The Government shall pay to the Contractor the job order price for completed items of work delivered to and accepted
L0:by the Government, and the amount agreed upon by the Contractor and the Contracting Officer for manufacturing materials
L0:delivered to and accepted by the Government, and for the protection and preservation of property. Failure to agree shall be
L0:a dispute concerning a question of fact within the meaning of the Disputes clause.
L1:(e) If, after notice of termination of the job order, it is determined that the Contractor was not in default, or that the default
L0:was excusable, the rights and obligations of the parties shall be the same as if the notice of termination had been issued for
L0:the convenience of the Government.
L1:(f) If the Contractor fails to complete the performance of a job order within the time specified, or any extension, the actual
L0:damage to the Government for the delay will be difficult or impossible to determine.
L1:(1) In lieu of actual damage, the Contractor shall pay to the Government as fixed, agreed, and liquidated damages for each
L0:calendar day of delay the amount, if any, set forth in the job order (prorated to the nearest hour for fractional days).
L1:(2) If the Government terminates the job order, the Contractor shall be liable, in addition to the excess costs provided in
L0:paragraph (d) of this clause, for liquidated damages accruing until such time as the Government may reasonably obtain
L0:completion of the work.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall not be charged with liquidated damages when the delay arises out of causes beyond the control
L0:and without the fault or negligence of the Contractor. Subject to the provisions of the Disputes clause of the Master
L0:Agreement, the Contracting Officer shall ascertain the facts and the extent of the delay and shall extend the time for
L0:performance when in the judgment of the Contracting Officer, the findings of fact justify an extension.
L1:(g) The rights and remedies of the Government provided in this clause shall not be exclusive and are in addition to any
L0:other rights and remedies provided by law under this agreement.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.217-7010 Performance
content:
L0:252.217-7010 Performance.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104 (a), use the following clause:
L0:PERFORMANCE (JUL 2009)
L1:(a) Upon the award of a job order, the Contractor shall promptly start the work specified and shall diligently prosecute the
L0:work to completion. The Contractor shall not start work until the job order has been awarded except in the case of
L0:emergency work ordered by the Contracting Officer under the Job Orders and Compensation clause of the Master
L0:Agreement.
L1:(b) The Government shall deliver the vessel described in the job order at the time and location specified in the job order.
L0:Upon completion of the work, the Government shall accept delivery of the vessel at the time and location specified in the
L0:job order.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall, without charge and without specific requirement in a job order—
L1:(1) Make available at the plant to personnel of the vessel while in dry dock or on a marine railway, sanitary lavatory and
L0:similar facilities acceptable to the Contracting Officer;
L1:(2) Supply and maintain suitable brows and gangways from the pier, dry dock, or marine railway to the vessel;
L1:(3) Treat salvage, scrap or other ship's material of the Government resulting from performance of the work as items of
L0:Government-furnished property, in accordance with the Government Property clause;
L1:(4) Perform, or pay the cost of, any repair, reconditioning or replacement made necessary as the result of the use by the
L0:Contractor of any of the vessel's machinery, equipment or fittings, including, but not limited to, winches, pumps, rigging,
L0:or pipe lines; and
L1:(5) Furnish suitable offices, office equipment and telephones at or near the site of the work for the Government's use.
L1:(d) The job order will state whether dock and sea trials are required to determine whether or not the Contractor has
L0:satisfactorily performed the work.
L1:(1) If dock and sea trials are required, the vessel shall be under the control of the vessel's commander and crew.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall not conduct dock and sea trials not specified in the job order without advance approval of the
L0:Contracting Officer. Dock and sea trials not specified in the job order shall be at the Contractor's expense and risk.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall provide and install all fittings and appliances necessary for dock and sea trials. The Contractor
L0:shall be responsible for care, installation, and removal of instruments and apparatus furnished by the Government for use in
L0:the trials.
L0:(End of clause)

L0:252.217-7011 Access to Vessel.

L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.217-7012 Liability and Insurance
content:
L0:252.217-7012 Liability and Insurance.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104 (a), use the following clause:
L0:LIABILITY AND INSURANCE (AUG 2003)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall exercise its best efforts to prevent accidents, injury, or damage to all employees, persons, and
L0:property, in and about the work, and to the vessel or part of the vessel upon which work is done.
L1:(b) Loss or damage to the vessel, materials, or equipment.
L1:(1) Unless otherwise directed or approved in writing by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall not carry insurance
L0:against any form of loss or damage to the vessel(s) or to the materials or equipment to which the Government has title or
L0:which have been furnished by the Government for installation by the Contractor. The Government assumes the risks of loss
L0:of and damage to that property.
L1:(2) The Government does not assume any risk with respect to loss or damage compensated for by insurance or otherwise or
L0:resulting from risks with respect to which the Contractor has failed to maintain insurance, if available, as required or
L0:approved by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(3) The Government does not assume risk of and will not pay for any costs of the following:
L1:(i) Inspection, repair, replacement, or renewal of any defects in the vessel(s) or material and equipment due to—
L1:(A) Defective workmanship performed by the Contractor or its subcontractors;
L1:(B) Defective materials or equipment furnished by the Contractor or its subcontracts; or
L1:(C) Workmanship, materials, or equipment which do not conform to the requirements of the contract, whether or not the
L0:defect is latent or whether or not the nonconformance is the result of negligence.
L1:(ii) Loss, damage, liability, or expense caused by, resulting from, or incurred as a consequence of any delay or disruption,
L0:willful misconduct or lack of good faith by the Contractor or any of its representatives that have supervision or direction of
L0:—
L1:(A) All or substantially all of the Contractor's business; or
L1:(B) All or substantially all of the Contractor's operation at any one plant.
L1:(4) As to any risk that is assumed by the Government, the Government shall be subrogated to any claim, demand or cause
L0:of action against third parties that exists in favor of the Contractor. If required by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor
L0:shall execute a formal assignment or transfer of the claim, demand, or cause of action.
L1:(5) No party other than the Contractor shall have any right to proceed directly against the Government or join the
L0:Government as a co-defendant in any action.
L1:(6) Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Contractor shall bear the first $50,000 of loss or damage from each occurrence or
L0:incident, the risk of which the Government would have assumed under the provisions of this paragraph (b).
L1:(c) Indemnification. The Contractor indemnifies the Government and the vessel and its owners against all claims, demands,
L0:or causes of action to which the Government, the vessel or its owner(s) might be subject as a result of damage or injury
L0:(including death) to the property or person of anyone other than the Government or its employees, or the vessel or its
L0:owner, arising in whole or in part from the negligence or other wrongful act of the Contractor or its agents or employees, or
L0:any subcontractor, or its agents or employees.
L1:(1) The Contractor's obligation to indemnify under this paragraph shall not exceed the sum of $300,000 as a consequence
L0:of any single occurrence with respect to any one vessel.
L1:(2) The indemnity includes, without limitation, suits, actions, claims, costs, or demands of any kind, resulting from death,
L0:personal injury, or property damage occurring during the period of performance of work on the vessel or within 90 days
L0:after redelivery of the vessel. For any claim, etc., made after 90 days, the rights of the parties shall be as determined by
L0:other provisions of this agreement and by law. The indemnity does apply to death occurring after 90 days where the injury
L0:was received during the period covered by the indemnity.
L1:(d) Insurance.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall, at its own expense, obtain and maintain the following insurance—
L1:(i) Casualty, accident, and liability insurance, as approved by the Contracting Officer, insuring the performance of its
L0:obligations under paragraph (c) of this clause.
L1:(ii) Workers Compensation Insurance (or its equivalent) covering the employees engaged on the work.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall ensure that all subcontractors engaged on the work obtain and maintain the insurance required in
L0:paragraph (d)(1) of this clause.
L1:(3) Upon request of the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall provide evidence of the insurance required by paragraph
L1:(d) of this clause.
L1:(e) The Contractor shall not make any allowance in the job order price for the inclusion of any premium expense or charge
L0:for any reserve made on account of self-insurance for coverage against any risk assumed by the Government under this
L0:clause.
L1:(f) The Contractor shall give the Contracting Officer written notice as soon as practicable after the occurrence of a loss or
L0:damage for which the Government has assumed the risk.
L1:(1) The notice shall contain full details of the loss or damage.
L1:(2) If a claim or suit is later filed against the Contractor as a result of the event, the Contractor shall immediately deliver to
L0:the Government every demand, notice, summons, or other process received by the Contractor or its employees or
L0:representatives.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall cooperate with the Government and, upon request, shall assist in effecting settlements, securing
L0:and giving evidence, obtaining the attendance of witnesses, and in the conduct of suits. The Government shall reimburse
L0:the Contractor for expenses incurred in this effort, other than the cost of maintaining the Contractor's usual organization.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall not, except at its own expense, voluntarily make any payment, assume any obligation, or incur any
L0:expense other than what would be imperative for the protection of the vessel(s) at the time of the event.
L1:(g) In the event or loss of or damage to any vessel(s), material, or equipment which may result in a claim against the
L0:Government under the insurance provisions of this contract, the Contractor shall promptly notify the Contracting Officer of
L0:the loss or damage. The Contracting Officer may, without prejudice to any other right of the Government, either—
L1:(1) Order the Contractor to proceed with replacement or repair, in which event the Contractor shall effect the replacement
L0:or repair;
L1:(i) The Contractor shall submit to the Contracting Officer a request for reimbursement of the cost of the replacement or
L0:repair together with whatever supporting documentation the Contracting Officer may reasonably require, and shall identify
L0:the request as being submitted under the Insurance clause of the agreement.
L1:(ii) If the Government determines that the risk of the loss or damage is within the scope of the risks assumed by the
L0:Government under this clause, the Government will reimburse the Contractor for the reasonable, allowable cost of the
L0:replacement or repair, plus a reasonable profit (if the work or replacement or repair was performed by the Contractor) less
L0:the deductible amount specified in paragraph (b) of this clause.
L1:(iii) Payments by the Government to the Contractor under this clause are outside the scope of and shall not affect the
L0:pricing structure of the contract, and are additional to the compensation otherwise payable to the Contractor under this
L0:contract; or
L1:(2) In the event the Contracting Officer decides that the loss or damage shall not be replaced or repaired, the Contracting
L0:Officer shall—
L1:(i) Modify the contract appropriately, consistent with the reduced requirements reflected by the unreplaced or unrepaired
L0:loss or damage; or
L1:(ii) Terminate the repair of any part or all of the vessel(s) under the Termination for Convenience of the Government clause
L0:of this agreement.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.217-7013 Guarantees
content:
L0:252.217-7013 Guarantees.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7104 (a), use the following clause:
L0:GUARANTEES (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) In the event any work performed or materials furnished by the contractor under the Master Agreement prove defective
L0:or deficient within 90 days from the date of redelivery of the vessel(s), the Contractor, as directed by the Contracting
L0:Officer and at its own expense, shall correct and repair the deficiency to the satisfaction of the Contracting Officer.
L1:(b) If the Contractor or any subcontractor has a guarantee for work performed or materials furnished that exceeds the 90
L0:day period, the Government shall be entitled to rely upon the longer guarantee until its expiration.
L1:(c) With respect to any individual work item identified as incomplete at the time of redelivery of the vessel(s), the
L0:guarantee period shall run from the date the item is completed.
L1:(d) If practicable, the Government shall give the Contractor an opportunity to correct the deficiency.
L1:(1) If the Contracting Officer determines it is not practicable or is otherwise not advisable to return the vessel(s) to the
L0:Contractor, or the Contractor fails to proceed with the repairs promptly, the Contracting Officer may direct that the repairs
L0:be performed elsewhere, at the Contractor's expense.
L1:(2) If correction and repairs are performed by other than the Contractor, the Contracting Officer may discharge the
L0:Contractor's liability by making an equitable deduction in the price of the job order.
L1:(e) The Contractor's liability shall extend for an additional 90 day guarantee period on those defects or deficiencies that the
L0:Contractor corrected.
L1:(f) At the option of the Contracting Officer, defects and deficiencies may be left uncorrected. In that event, the Contractor
L0:and Contracting Officer shall negotiate an equitable reduction in the job price. Failure to agree upon an equitable reduction
L0:shall constitute a dispute under the Disputes clause of this agreement.
L0:(End of clause)
