title: 252.217-7028 Over and Above Work
content:
L0:252.217-7028 Over and Above Work.
L0:As prescribed in 217.7702 , use a clause substantially as follows:
L0:OVER AND ABOVE WORK (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) “Over and above work” means work discovered during the course of performing overhaul, maintenance, and repair
L0:efforts that is—
L1:(i) Within the general scope of the contract;
L1:(ii) Not covered by the line item(s) for the basic work under the contract; and
L1:(iii) Necessary in order to satisfactorily complete the contract.
L1:(2) “Work request” means a document prepared by the Contractor which describes over and above work being proposed.
L1:(b) The Contractor and Administrative Contracting Officer shall mutually agree to procedures for Government
L0:administration and Contractor performance of over and above work requests. If the parties cannot agree upon the
L0:procedures, the Administrative Contracting Officer has the unilateral right to direct the over and above work procedures to
L0:be followed. These procedures shall, as a minimum, cover—
L1:(1) The format, content, and submission of work requests by the Contractor. Work requests shall contain data on the type of
L0:discrepancy disclosed, the specific location of the discrepancy, and the estimated labor hours and material required to
L0:correct the discrepancy. Data shall be sufficient to satisfy contract requirements and obtain the authorization of the
L0:Contracting Officer to perform the proposed work;
L1:(2) Government review, verification, and authorization of the work; and
L1:(3) Proposal pricing, submission, negotiation, and definitization.
L1:(c) Upon discovery of the need for over and above work, the Contractor shall prepare and furnish to the Government a
L0:work request in accordance with the agreed-to procedures.
L1:(d) The Government shall—
L1:(1) Promptly review the work request;
L1:(2) Verify that the proposed work is required and not covered under the basic contract line item(s);
L1:(3) Verify that the proposed corrective action is appropriate; and
L1:(4) Authorize over and above work as necessary.
L1:(e) The Contractor shall promptly submit to the Contracting Officer, a proposal for the over and above work. The
L0:Government and Contractor will then negotiate a settlement for the over and above work. Contract modifications will be
L0:executed to definitize all over and above work.
L1:(f) Failure to agree on the price of over and above work shall be a dispute within the meaning of the Disputes clause of this
L0:contract.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.219-7004 Small Business Subcontracting Plan (Test Program)
content:

L0:As prescribed in 219.708 (b)(1)(B), use the following clause:
L0:SMALL BUSINESS SUBCONTRACTING PLAN (TEST PROGRAM) (DEC 2022)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—

L0:failure to perform in accordance with the requirements of the Contractor’s approved comprehensive subcontracting plan or
L0:willful or intentional action to frustrate the plan.

L0:Federal Government prime Contractor or subcontractor calling for supplies or services required for performance of the
L0:contract or subcontract.
L1:(b) Test Program. The Contractor’s comprehensive small business subcontracting plan and its successors, which are
L0:authorized by and approved under the Test Program of 15 U.S.C. 637 note, as amended, shall be included in and made a
L0:part of this contract. Upon expulsion from the Test Program or expiration of the Test Program, the Contractor shall
L0:negotiate an individual subcontracting plan for all future contracts that meet the requirements of 15 U.S.C. 637(d).
L1:(c) Eligibility requirements. To become and remain eligible to participate in the Test Program, a business concern is
L0:required to have furnished supplies or services (including construction) under at least three DoD contracts during the
L0:preceding fiscal year, having an aggregate value of at least $100 million.
L1:(d) Reports.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall report semiannually for the 6-month periods ending March 31 and September 30, the information
L0:in paragraphs (d)(1)(i) through (v) of this section within 30 days after the end of the reporting period. Submit the report at
L0:https://www.esrs.gov.
L1:(i) A list of contracts covered under its comprehensive small business subcontracting plan, to include the Commercial and
L0:Government Entity (CAGE) code and unique entity identifier.
L1:(ii) The amount of first-tier subcontract dollars awarded during the 6-month period covered by the report to covered small
L0:business concerns, with the information set forth separately by—
L1:(A) North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code;
L1:(B) Major defense acquisition program, as defined in 10 U.S.C. 4201;
L1:(C) Contract number, if the contract is for maintenance, overhaul, repair, servicing, rehabilitation, salvage, modernization,
L0:or modification of supplies, systems, or equipment, and the total value of the contract, including options, exceeds $100
L0:million; and
L1:(D) Military department.
L1:(iii) Total number of subcontracts active under the Test Program that would have otherwise required a subcontracting plan.
L1:(iv) Costs incurred in negotiating, complying with, and reporting on its comprehensive subcontracting plan.
L1:(v) Costs avoided through the use of a comprehensive subcontracting plan.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall—
L1:(i) Ensure that subcontractors with subcontracting plans agree to submit an Individual Subcontract Report (ISR) and/or
L0:Summary Subcontract Report (SSR) using the Electronic Subcontracting Reporting System (eSRS).
L1:(ii) Provide its contract number, its unique entity identifier, and the email address of the Contractor’s official responsible
L0:for acknowledging or rejecting the ISR to all first-tier subcontractors, who will be required to submit ISRs, so they can
L0:enter this information into the eSRS when submitting their reports.
L1:(iii) Require that each subcontractor with a subcontracting plan provide the prime contract number, its own unique entity
L0:identifier, and the email address of the subcontractor’s official responsible for acknowledging or rejecting the ISRs to its
L0:subcontractors with subcontracting plans who will be required to submit ISRs.
L1:(iv) Acknowledge receipt or reject all ISRs submitted by its subcontractors using eSRS.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall submit SSRs using eSRS at http://www.esrs.gov. The reports shall provide information on
L0:subcontract awards to small business concerns, veteran-owned small business concerns, service-disabled veteran-owned
L0:small business concerns, HUBZone small business concerns, small disadvantaged business concerns, and women-owned
L0:small business concerns. Purchases from a corporation, company, or subdivision that is an affiliate of the prime Contractor
L0:or subcontractor are not included in these reports. Subcontract award data reported by prime contractors and subcontractors
L0:shall be limited to awards made to their immediate next-tier subcontractors. Credit cannot be taken for awards made to
L0:lower-tier subcontractors unless the Contractor or subcontractor has been designated to receive a small business or small
L0:disadvantaged business credit from a member firm of the Alaska Native Corporations or an Indian tribe. Only subcontracts
L0:involving performance in the U.S. or its outlying areas should be included in these reports.
L1:(i) This report may be submitted on a corporate, company, or subdivision (e.g., plant or division operating as a separate
L0:profit center) basis, as negotiated in the comprehensive subcontracting plan with the Defense Contract Management
L0:Agency.
L1:(ii) This report encompasses all subcontracting under prime contracts and subcontracts with the Department of Defense,
L0:regardless of the dollar value of the subcontracts, and is based on the negotiated comprehensive subcontracting plan.
L1:(iii) The report shall be submitted semi-annually for the six months ending March 31 and the twelve months ending
L0:September 30. Reports are due 30 days after the close of each reporting period.
L1:(iv) The authority to acknowledge receipt of or reject the SSR resides with the Defense Contract Management Agency.
L1:(e) Failure to comply. The failure of the Contractor or subcontractor to comply in good faith with the clause of this contract
L0:entitled “Utilization of Small Business Concerns,” or an approved plan required by this clause, shall be a material breach of
L0:the contract.
L1:(f) Liquidated damages. The Contracting Officer designated to manage the comprehensive subcontracting plan will
L0:exercise the functions of the Contracting Officer, as identified in paragraphs (f)(1) through (4) of this clause, on behalf of
L0:all DoD departments and agencies that awarded contracts covered by the Contractor’s comprehensive subcontracting plan.
L1:(1) To determine the need for liquidated damages, the Contracting Officer will conduct a compliance review during the
L0:fiscal year after the close of the fiscal year for which the plan is applicable. The Contracting Officer will compare the
L0:approved percentage or dollar goals to the total, actual subcontracting dollars covered by the plan.
L1:(2) If the Contractor has failed to meet its approved subcontracting goal(s), the Contracting Officer will provide the
L0:Contractor written notice specifying the failure, advising of the potential for assessment of liquidated damages, and
L0:permitting the Contractor to demonstrate what good faith efforts have been made. The Contracting Officer may take the
L0:Contractor’s failure to respond to the notice within 15 working days (or longer period at the Contracting Officer’s
L0:discretion) as an admission that no valid explanation exists.
L1:(3) If, after consideration of all relevant information, the Contracting Officer determines that the Contractor failed to make
L0:a good faith effort to comply with the comprehensive subcontracting plan, the Contracting Officer will issue a final
L0:decision to the Contractor to that effect and require the Contractor to pay liquidated damages to the Government in the
L0:amount identified in the comprehensive subcontracting plan.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall have the right of appeal under the clause in this contract entitled “Disputes” from any final
L0:decision of the Contracting Officer.
L1:(g) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include in subcontracts that offer subcontracting opportunities, are expected to
L0:exceed the applicable threshold specified in FAR 19.702(a) on the date of subcontract award, and are required to include
L0:the clause at FAR 52.219-8, Utilization of Small Business Concerns, the clauses at—
L1:(1) FAR 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan, and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS)

title: 252.223-7002 Safety Precautions for Ammunition and Explosives
content:
L0:252.223-7002 Safety Precautions for Ammunition and Explosives.
L0:As prescribed in 223.370-5 , use the following clause:
L0:SAFETY PRECAUTIONS FOR AMMUNITION AND EXPLOSIVES (NOV 2023)
L1:(a) Definition. “Ammunition and explosives,” as used in this clause—
L1:(1) Means liquid and solid propellants and explosives, pyrotechnics, incendiaries and smokes in the following forms:
L1:(i) Bulk,
L1:(ii) Ammunition;
L1:(iii) Rockets;
L1:(iv) Missiles;
L1:(v) Warheads;
L1:(vi) Devices; and
L1:(vii) Components of (i) through (vi), except for wholly inert items.
L1:(2) This definition does not include the following, unless the Contractor is using or incorporating these materials for
L0:initiation, propulsion, or detonation as an integral or component part of an explosive, an ammunition or explosive end item,
L0:or of a weapon system—
L1:(i) Inert components containing no explosives, propellants, or pyrotechnics;
L1:(ii) Flammable liquids;
L1:(iii) Acids;
L1:(iv) Oxidizers;
L1:(v) Powdered metals; or
L1:(vi) Other materials having fire or explosive characteristics.
L1:(b) Safety requirements.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall comply with the requirements of DoD Manual 4145.26, DoD Contractors’ Safety Manual for
L0:Ammunition and Explosives, hereafter referred to as “the manual,” in effect on the date of the solicitation for this contract.
L0:The Contractor shall also comply with any other additional requirements included in the schedule of this contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall allow the Government access to the Contractor's facilities, personnel, and safety program
L0:documentation. The Contractor shall allow authorized Government representatives to evaluate safety programs,
L0:implementation, and facilities.
L1:(c) Noncompliance with the manual.
L1:(1) If the Contracting Officer notifies the Contractor of any noncompliance with the manual or schedule provisions, the
L0:Contractor shall take immediate steps to correct the noncompliance. The Contractor is not entitled to reimbursement of
L0:costs incurred to correct noncompliances unless such reimbursement is specified elsewhere in the contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor has 30 days from the date of notification by the Contracting Officer to correct the noncompliance and
L0:inform the Contracting Officer of the actions taken. The Contracting Officer may direct a different time period for the
L0:correction of noncompliances.
L1:(3) If the Contractor refuses or fails to correct noncompliances within the time period specified by the Contracting Officer,
L0:the Government has the right to direct the Contractor to cease performance on all or part of this contract. The Contractor
L0:shall not resume performance until the Contracting Officer is satisfied that the corrective action was effective and the
L0:Contracting Officer so informs the Contractor.
L1:(4) The Contracting Officer may remove Government personnel at any time the Contractor is in noncompliance with any
L0:safety requirement of this clause.
L1:(5) If the direction to cease work or the removal of Government personnel results in increased costs to the Contractor, the
L0:Contractor shall not be entitled to an adjustment in the contract price or a change in the delivery or performance schedule
L0:unless the Contracting Officer later determines that the Contractor had in fact complied with the manual or schedule
L0:provisions. If the Contractor is entitled to an equitable adjustment, it shall be made in accordance with the Changes clause
L0:of this contract.
L1:(d) Mishaps. If a mishap involving ammunition or explosives occurs, the Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Notify the Contracting Officer immediately;
L1:(2) Conduct an investigation in accordance with other provisions of this contract or as required by the Contracting Officer;
L0:and
L1:(3) Submit a written report to the Contracting Officer.
L1:(e) Contractor responsibility for safety.
L1:(1) Nothing in this clause, nor any Government action or failure to act in surveillance of this contract, shall relieve the
L0:Contractor of its responsibility for the safety of—
L1:(i) The Contractor's personnel and property;
L1:(ii) The Government's personnel and property; or
L1:(iii) The general public.
L1:(2) Nothing in this clause shall relieve the Contractor of its responsibility for complying with applicable Federal, State, and
L0:local laws, ordinances, codes, and regulations (including those requiring the obtaining of licenses and permits) in
L0:connection with the performance of this contract.
L1:(f) Contractor responsibility for contract performance.
L1:(1) Neither the number or frequency of inspections performed by the Government, nor the degree of surveillance exercised
L0:by the Government, relieve the Contractor of its responsibility for contract performance.
L1:(2) If the Government acts or fails to act in surveillance or enforcement of the safety requirements of this contract, this does
L0:not impose or add to any liability of the Government.
L1:(g) Subcontractors.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall insert this clause, including this paragraph (g), in every subcontract that involves ammunition or
L0:explosives.
L1:(i) The clause shall include a provision allowing authorized Government safety representatives to evaluate subcontractor
L0:safety programs, implementation, and facilities as the Government determines necessary.
L1:(ii) NOTE: The Government Contracting Officer or authorized representative shall notify the prime Contractor of all
L0:findings concerning subcontractor safety and compliance with the manual. The Contracting Officer or authorized
L0:representative may furnish copies to the subcontractor. The Contractor in turn shall communicate directly with the
L0:subcontractor, substituting its name for references to “the Government”. The Contractor and higher tier subcontractors shall
L0:also include provisions to allow direction to cease performance of the subcontract if a serious uncorrected or recurring
L0:safety deficiency potentially causes an imminent hazard to DoD personnel, property, or contract performance.
L1:(2) The Contractor agrees to ensure that the subcontractor complies with all contract safety requirements. The Contractor
L0:will determine the best method for verifying the adequacy of the subcontractor's compliance.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall ensure that the subcontractor understands and agrees to the Government's right to access to the
L0:subcontractor's facilities, personnel, and safety program documentation to perform safety surveys. The Government
L0:performs these safety surveys of subcontractor facilities solely to prevent the occurrence of any mishap which would
L0:endanger the safety of DoD personnel or otherwise adversely impact upon the Government's contractual interests.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer or authorized representative before issuing any subcontract when it
L0:involves ammunition or explosives. If the proposed subcontract represents a change in the place of performance, the
L0:Contractor shall request approval for such change in accordance with the clause of this contract entitled “Change in Place
L0:of Performance—Ammunition and Explosives”.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.223-7006 Prohibition on Storage, Treatment, and Disposal of Toxic or Hazardous Materials
content:
L0:252.223-7006 Prohibition on Storage, Treatment, and Disposal of Toxic or Hazardous Materials.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 223.7106 and 223.7106 (a), use the following clause:
L0:PROHIBITION ON STORAGE, TREATMENT, AND DISPOSAL OF TOXIC OR HAZARDOUS MATERIALS—
L0:BASIC (SEP 2014)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Storage” means a non-transitory, semi-permanent or permanent holding, placement, or leaving of material. It does not
L0:include a temporary accumulation of a limited quantity of a material used in or a waste generated or resulting from
L0:authorized activities, such as servicing, maintenance, or repair of Department of Defense (DoD) items, equipment, or
L0:facilities.
L0:“Toxic or hazardous materials” means—
L1:(i) Materials referred to in section 101(14) of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability
L0:Act (CERCLA) of 1980 (42 U.S.C. 9601(14)) and materials designated under section 102 of CERCLA (42 U.S.C. 9602)
L0:(40 CFR Part 302);
L1:(ii) Materials that are of an explosive, flammable, or pyrotechnic nature; or
L1:(iii) Materials otherwise identified by the Secretary of Defense as specified in DoD regulations.
L1:(b) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2692, the Contractor is prohibited from storing, treating, or disposing of toxic or
L0:hazardous materials not owned by DoD on a DoD installation, except to the extent authorized by a statutory exception to
L0:10 U.S.C. 2692 or as authorized by the Secretary of Defense. A charge may be assessed for any storage or disposal
L0:authorized under any of the exceptions to 10 U.S.C. 2692. If a charge is to be assessed, then such assessment shall be
L0:identified elsewhere in the contract with payment to the Government on a reimbursable cost basis.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (c), in all subcontracts that require,
L0:may require, or permit a subcontractor access to a DoD installation, at any subcontract tier.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Alternate I. As prescribed in 223.7106 and 223.7106 (b), use the following clause, which adds a new paragraph (c) and
L0:revises and redesignates paragraph (c) of the basic clause as paragraph (d):
L0:PROHIBITION ON STORAGE, TREATMENT, AND DISPOSAL OF TOXIC OR HAZARDOUS MATERIALS—
L0:ALTERNATE I (SEP 2014)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Storage” means a non-transitory, semi-permanent or permanent holding, placement, or leaving of material. It does not
L0:include a temporary accumulation of a limited quantity of a material used in or a waste generated or resulting from
L0:authorized activities, such as servicing, maintenance, or repair of Department of Defense (DoD) items, equipment, or
L0:facilities.
L0:“Toxic or hazardous materials” means—
L1:(i) Materials referred to in section 101(14) of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability
L0:Act (CERCLA) of 1980 (42 U.S.C. 9601(14)) and materials designated under section 102 of CERCLA (42 U.S.C. 9602)
L0:(40 CFR Part 302);
L1:(ii) Materials that are of an explosive, flammable, or pyrotechnic nature; or
L1:(iii) Materials otherwise identified by the Secretary of Defense as specified in DoD regulations.
L1:(b) In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2692, the Contractor is prohibited from storing, treating, or disposing of toxic or
L0:hazardous materials not owned by DoD on a DoD installation, except to the extent authorized by a statutory exception to
L0:10 U.S.C. 2692 or as authorized by the Secretary of Defense. A charge may be assessed for any storage or disposal
L0:authorized under any of the exceptions to 10 U.S.C. 2692. If a charge is to be assessed, then such assessment shall be
L0:identified elsewhere in the contract with payment to the Government on a reimbursable cost basis.
L1:(c) With respect to treatment or disposal authorized pursuant to DFARS 223.7104 (10) (10 U.S.C. 2692(b)(10), and
L0:notwithstanding any other provision of the contract, the Contractor assumes all financial and environmental responsibility
L0:and liability resulting from any treatment or disposal of toxic or hazardous materials not owned by DoD on a military
L0:installation. The Contractor shall indemnify, defend, and hold the Government harmless for all costs, liability, or penalties
L0:resulting from the Contractor’s treatment or disposal of toxic or hazardous materials not owned by DoD on a military
L0:installation.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (d), in all subcontracts that require,
L0:may require, or permit a subcontractor access to a DoD installation, at any tier. Inclusion of the substance of this clause in
L0:subcontracts does not relieve the prime Contractor of liability to the Government under paragraph (c).
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.223-7006 — Prohibition on Storage, Treatment, and Disposal of Toxic or Hazardous Materials

title: 252.223-7008 Prohibition of Hexavalent Chromium
content:
L0:252.223-7008 Prohibition of Hexavalent Chromium.
L0:As prescribed in 223.7306 , use the following clause:
L0:PROHIBITION OF HEXAVALENT CHROMIUM (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Homogeneous material” means a material that cannot be mechanically disjointed into different materials and is of uniform
L0:composition throughout.
L1:(1) Examples of homogeneous materials include individual types of plastics, ceramics, glass, metals, alloys, paper, board,
L0:resins, and surface coatings.
L1:(2) Homogeneous material does not include conversion coatings that chemically modify the substrate.
L0:“Mechanically disjointed” means that the materials can, in principle, be separated by mechanical actions such as
L0:unscrewing, cutting, crushing, grinding, and abrasive processes.
L1:(b) Prohibition.
L1:(1) Unless otherwise specified by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall not provide any deliverable or construction
L0:material under this contract that—
L1:(i) Contains hexavalent chromium in a concentration greater than 0.1 percent by weight in any homogenous material; or
L1:(ii) Requires the removal or reapplication of hexavalent chromium materials during subsequent sustainment phases of the
L0:deliverable or construction material.
L1:(2) This prohibition does not apply to hexavalent chromium produced as a by-product of manufacturing processes.
L1:(c) If authorization for incorporation of hexavalent chromium in a deliverable or construction material is required, the
L0:Contractor shall submit a request to the Contracting Officer.
L1:(d) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (d), in all subcontracts,
L0:including subcontracts for commercial products or commercial services, that are for supplies, maintenance and repair
L0:services, or construction materials.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.223-7009 Prohibition of Procurement of Fluorinated Fire-Fighting Agent for Use on Military Installations
content:

L0:AGENT FOR USE ON MILITARY INSTALLATIONS (MAR 2024)

title: 252.225-7001 Buy American and Balance of Payments Program
content:
L0:252.225-7001 Buy American and Balance of Payments Program.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 225.1101 (2)(i) and (2)(ii), use the following clause:
L0:BUY AMERICAN AND BALANCE OF PAYMENTS PROGRAM—BASIC(FEB 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions.As used in this clause—
L0:“Commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item”—
L1:(1) Means any item of supply (including construction material) that is—
L1:(i) A commercial product (as defined in paragraph (1) of the definition of “commercial product” in section 2.101 of the
L0:Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR));
L1:(ii) Sold in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(iii) Offered to the Government, under a contract or subcontract at any tier, without modification, in the same form in
L0:which it is sold in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(2) Does not include bulk cargo, as defined in 46 U.S.C. 40102(4), such as agricultural products and petroleum products.
L0:“Component” means an article, material, or supply incorporated directly into an end product.
L0:“Critical component” means a component that is mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States and deemed
L0:critical to the U.S. supply chain. The list of critical components is at FAR 25.105.
L0:“Critical item” means a domestic construction material or domestic end product that is deemed critical to the U.S. supply
L0:chain. The list of critical items is at FAR 25.105.
L0:“Domestic end product” means—
L1:(1) For an end product that does not consist wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both—
L1:(i) An unmanufactured end product mined or produced in the United States; or
L1:(ii) An end product manufactured in the United States if—
L1:(A) The cost of its qualifying country components and its components that are mined, produced, or manufactured in the
L0:United States exceeds 60 percent of the cost of all its components, except that the percentage will be 65 percent for items
L0:delivered in calendar years 2024 through 2028 and 75 percent for items delivered starting in calendar year 2029, unless an
L0:alternate percentage is established for a contract in accordance with FAR 25.101(d), or award is made before January 1,
L0:2030, for a foreign end product that exceeds 55 percent domestic content (see Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation
L0:Supplement 225.103(b)(ii)). The cost of components includes transportation costs to the place of incorporation into the end
L0:product and U.S. duty (whether or not a duty-free entry certificate is issued). Components of unknown origin are treated as
L0:foreign. Scrap generated, collected, and prepared for processing in the United States is considered domestic. A component
L0:is considered to have been mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States (regardless of its source in fact) if the
L0:end product in which it is incorporated is manufactured in the United States and the component is of a class or kind for
L0:which the Government has determined that—
L1:(1) Sufficient and reasonably available commercial quantities of a satisfactory quality are not mined, produced, or
L0:manufactured in the United States; or
L1:(2) It is inconsistent with the public interest to apply the restrictions of the Buy American statute; or
L1:(B) The end product is a COTS item.
L1:(2) For an end product that consists wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both, an end product
L0:manufactured in the United States, if the cost of iron and steel not produced in the United States or a qualifying country
L0:constitutes less than 5 percent of the cost of all the components used in the end product (produced in the United States or a
L0:qualifying country means that all manufacturing processes of the iron or steel must take place in the United States or a
L0:qualifying country, except metallurgical processes involving refinement of steel additives). The cost of iron and steel not
L0:produced in the United States or a qualifying country includes but is not limited to the cost of iron or steel mill products
L0:(such as bar, billet, slab, wire, plate, or sheet), castings, or forgings, not produced in the United States or a qualifying
L0:country, utilized in the manufacture of the end product and a good faith estimate of the cost of all iron or steel components
L0:not produced in the United States or a qualifying country, excluding COTS fasteners. Iron or steel components of unknown
L0:origin are treated as foreign. If the end product contains multiple components, the cost of all the materials used in such end
L0:product is calculated in accordance with the explanation of cost of components in paragraph (1)(ii)(A) of this definition.
L0:“End product” means those articles, materials, and supplies to be acquired under this contract for public use.
L0:“Foreign end product” means an end product other than a domestic end product.
L0:“Predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both” means that the cost of the iron and steel content exceeds 50
L0:percent of the total cost of all its components. The cost of iron and steel is the cost of the iron or steel mill products (such
L0:as bar, billet, slab, wire, plate, or sheet), castings, or forgings utilized in the manufacture of the product and a good faith
L0:estimate of the cost of iron or steel components excluding COTS fasteners.
L0:“Qualifying country” means a country with a reciprocal defense procurement memorandum of understanding or
L0:international agreement with the United States in which both countries agree to remove barriers to purchases of supplies
L0:produced in the other country or services performed by sources of the other country, and the memorandum or agreement
L0:complies, where applicable, with the requirements of section 36 of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2776) and with
L0:10 U.S.C. 2457. Accordingly, the following are qualifying countries:
L0:Australia
L0:Austria
L0:Belgium
L0:Canada
L0:Czech Republic
L0:Denmark
L0:Egypt
L0:Estonia
L0:Finland
L0:France
L0:Germany
L0:Greece
L0:Israel
L0:Italy
L0:Japan
L0:Latvia
L0:Lithuania
L0:Luxembourg
L0:Netherlands
L0:Norway
L0:Poland
L0:Portugal
L0:Slovenia
L0:Spain
L0:Sweden
L0:Switzerland
L0:Turkey
L0:United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
L0:“Qualifying country component” means a component mined, produced, or manufactured in a qualifying country.
L0:“Qualifying country end product” means—
L1:(1) An unmanufactured end product mined or produced in a qualifying country; or
L1:(2) An end product manufactured in a qualifying country if —
L1:(i) The cost of the following types of components exceeds 60 percent of the cost of all its components, except that the
L0:percentage will be 65 percent for items delivered in calendar years 2024 through 2028 and 75 percent for items delivered
L0:starting in calendar year 2029, unless an alternate percentage is established for a contract:
L1:(A) Components mined, produced, or manufactured in a qualifying country.
L1:(B) Components mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States.
L1:(C) Components of foreign origin of a class or kind for which the Government has determined that sufficient and
L0:reasonably available commercial quantities of a satisfactory quality are not mined, produced, or manufactured in the United
L0:States. Components of unknown origin are treated as foreign; or
L1:(ii) The end product is a COTS item.
L0:“United States” means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and outlying areas.
L0:“Steel” means an alloy that includes at least 50 percent iron, between 0.02 and 2 percent carbon, and may include other
L0:elements.
L1:(b) This clause implements 41 U.S.C. chapter 83, Buy American. In accordance with 41 U.S.C. 1907, the component test
L0:of the Buy American statute is waived for an end product that is a COTS item (see FAR 12.505(a)(1)). Unless otherwise
L0:specified, this clause applies to all line items in the contract.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall deliver only domestic end products unless, in its offer, it specified delivery of other end products in
L0:the Buy American—Balance of Payments Program Certificate provision of the solicitation. If the Contractor certified in its
L0:offer that it will deliver a qualifying country end product, the Contractor shall deliver a qualifying country end product or,
L0:at the Contractor’s option, a domestic end product.
L1:(d) The contract price does not include duty for end products or components for which the Contractor will claim duty-free
L0:entry.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Alternate I. As prescribed in 225.1101 (2)(i) and (2)(iii), use the following clause, which adds “South Caucasus/Central and
L0:South Asian (SC/CASA) state” and “South Caucasus/Central and South Asian (SC/CASA) state end product” to paragraph
L1:(a), and uses different paragraphs (b) and (c) than the basic clause:
L0:BUY AMERICAN AND BALANCE OF PAYMENTS PROGRAM—ALTERNATE I (FEB 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions.As used in this clause—
L0:“Commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item”—
L1:(1) Means any item of supply (including construction material) that is—

title: 252.225-7008 Restriction on Acquisition of Specialty Metals
content:
L0:252.225-7008 Restriction on Acquisition of Specialty Metals.
L0:As prescribed in 225.7003-5 (a)(1), use the following clause:
L0:RESTRICTION ON ACQUISITION OF SPECIALTY METALS (MAR 2013)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Alloy” means a metal consisting of a mixture of a basic metallic element and one or more metallic, or non-metallic,
L0:alloying elements.
L1:(i) For alloys named by a single metallic element (e.g., titanium alloy), it means that the alloy contains 50 percent or more
L0:of the named metal (by mass).
L1:(ii) If two metals are specified in the name (e.g., nickel-iron alloy), those metals are the two predominant elements in the
L0:alloy, and together they constitute 50 percent or more of the alloy (by mass).
L0:“Produce” means—
L1:(i) Atomization;
L1:(ii) Sputtering; or
L1:(iii) Final consolidation of non-melt derived metal powders.
L0:“Specialty metal” means—
L1:(i) Steel—
L1:(A) With a maximum alloy content exceeding one or more of the following limits: manganese, 1.65 percent; silicon, 0.60
L0:percent; or copper, 0.60 percent; or
L1:(B) Containing more than 0.25 percent of any of the following elements: aluminum, chromium, cobalt, molybdenum,
L0:nickel, niobium (columbium), titanium, tungsten, or vanadium;
L1:(ii) Metal alloys consisting of—
L1:(A) Nickel or iron-nickel alloys that contain a total of alloying metals other than nickel and iron in excess of 10 percent; or
L1:(B) Cobalt alloys that contain a total of alloying metals other than cobalt and iron in excess of 10 percent;
L1:(iii) Titanium and titanium alloys; or
L1:(iv) Zirconium and zirconium alloys.
L0:“Steel” means an iron alloy that includes between .02 and 2 percent carbon and may include other elements.
L1:(b) Any specialty metal delivered under this contract shall be melted or produced in the United States or its outlying areas.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.225-7008 — Restriction on Acquisition of Specialty Metals

title: 252.225-7009 Restriction on Acquisition of Certain Articles Containing Specialty Metals
content:
L0:252.225-7009 Restriction on Acquisition of Certain Articles Containing Specialty Metals.
L0:As prescribed in 225.7003-5(a)(2), use the following clause:
L0:Restriction on Acquisition of Certain Articles Containing Specialty Metals (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause “Alloy” means a metal consisting of a mixture of a basic metallic element and one or more metallic, or non-metallic,
L0:alloying elements.
L1:(i) For alloys named by a single metallic element (e.g., titanium alloy), it means that the alloy contains 50 percent or more
L0:of the named metal (by mass).
L1:(ii) If two metals are specified in the name (e.g., nickel-iron alloy), those metals are the two predominant elements in the
L0:alloy, and together they constitute 50 percent or more of the alloy (by mass).
L0:“Assembly” means an item forming a portion of a system or subsystem that—
L1:(i) Can be provisioned and replaced as an entity; and
L1:(ii) Incorporates multiple, replaceable parts.
L0:“Commercial derivative military article” means an item acquired by the Department of Defense that is or will be produced
L0:using the same production facilities, a common supply chain, and the same or similar production processes that are used for
L0:the production of articles predominantly used by the general public or by nongovernmental entities for purposes other than
L0:governmental purposes.
L0:“Commercially available off-the-shelf item”—
L1:(i) Means any item of supply that is (A) A commercial product (as defined in paragraph (1) of the definition of “commercial product” in section 2.101 of the
L0:Federal Acquisition Regulation);
L1:(B) Sold in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(C) Offered to the Government, under this contract or a subcontract at any tier, without modification, in the same form in
L0:which it is sold in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(ii) Does not include bulk cargo, as defined in 46 U.S.C. 40102(4), such as agricultural products and petroleum products.
L0:“Component” means any item supplied to the Government as part of an end item or of another component.
L0:“Electronic component” means an item that operates by controlling the flow of electrons or other electrically charged
L0:particles in circuits, using interconnections of electrical devices such as resistors, inductors, capacitors, diodes, switches,
L0:transistors, or integrated circuits. The term does not include structural or mechanical parts of an assembly containing an
L0:electronic component, and does not include any high performance magnets that may be used in the electronic component.
L0:“End item” means the final production product when assembled or completed and ready for delivery under a line item of
L0:this contract.
L0:“High performance magnet” means a permanent magnet that obtains a majority of its magnetic properties from rare earth
L0:metals (such as samarium).
L0:“Produce” means—
L1:(i) Atomization;
L1:(ii) Sputtering; or
L1:(iii) Final consolidation of non-melt derived metal powders.
L0:“Qualifying country” means any country listed in the definition of “Qualifying country” at 225.003 of the Defense Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS).
L0:“Specialty metal” means—
L1:(i) Steel—
L1:(A) With a maximum alloy content exceeding one or more of the following limits: manganese, 1.65 percent; silicon, 0.60
L0:percent; or copper, 0.60 percent; or
L1:(B) Containing more than 0.25 percent of any of the following elements: aluminum, chromium, cobalt, molybdenum,
L0:nickel, niobium (columbium), titanium, tungsten, or vanadium;
L1:(ii) Metal alloys consisting of—
L1:(A) Nickel or iron-nickel alloys that contain a total of alloying metals other than nickel and iron in excess of 10 percent; or
L1:(B) Cobalt alloys that contain a total of alloying metals other than cobalt and iron in excess of 10 percent;
L1:(iii) Titanium and titanium alloys; or
L1:(iv) Zirconium and zirconium alloys.
L0:“Steel” means an iron alloy that includes between .02 and 2 percent carbon and may include other elements.
L0:“Subsystem” means a functional grouping of items that combine to perform a major function within an end item, such as
L0:electrical power, attitude control, and propulsion.
L1:(b) Restriction.Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this clause, any specialty metals incorporated in items delivered
L0:under this contract shall be melted or produced in the United States, its outlying areas, or a qualifying country.
L1:(c) Exceptions.The restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause does not apply to—
L1:(1) Electronic components.
L1:(2)(i) Commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) items, other than—
L1:(A) Specialty metal mill products, such as bar, billet, slab, wire, plate, or sheet, that have not been incorporated into COTS
L0:end items, subsystems, assemblies, or components;
L1:(B) Forgings or castings of specialty metals, unless the forgings or castings are incorporated into COTS end items,
L0:subsystems, or assemblies;
L1:(C) Commercially available high performance magnets that contain specialty metal, unless such high performance magnets
L0:are incorporated into COTS end items or subsystems; and
L1:(D) COTS fasteners, unless—
L1:(1) The fasteners are incorporated into COTS end items, subsystems, assemblies, or components; or
L1:(2) The fasteners qualify for the commercial item exception in paragraph (c)(3) of this clause.
L1:(ii) A COTS item is considered to be “without modification” if it is not modified prior to contractual acceptance by the next
L0:higher tier in the supply chain.
L1:(A) Specialty metals in a COTS item that was accepted without modification by the next higher tier are excepted from the
L0:restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause, and remain excepted, even if a piece of the COTS item subsequently is removed
L0:(e.g., the end is removed from a COTS screw or an extra hole is drilled in a COTS bracket).
L1:(B) Specialty metals that were not contained in a COTS item upon acceptance, but are added to the COTS item after
L0:acceptance, are subject to the restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause (e.g., a special reinforced handle made of specialty
L0:metal is added to a COTS item).
L1:(C) If two or more COTS items are combined in such a way that the resultant item is not a COTS item, only the specialty
L0:metals involved in joining the COTS items together are subject to the restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause (e.g., a
L0:COTS aircraft is outfitted with a COTS engine that is not the COTS engine normally provided with the aircraft).
L1:(D) For COTS items that are normally sold in the commercial marketplace with various options, items that include such
L0:options are also COTS items. However, if a COTS item is offered to the Government with an option that is not normally
L0:offered in the commercial marketplace, that option is subject to the restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause (e.g. - An
L0:aircraft is normally sold to the public with an option for installation kits. The Department of Defense requests a militaryunique kit. The aircraft is still a COTS item, but the military-unique kit is not a COTS item and must comply with the
L0:restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause unless another exception applies).
L1:(3) Fasteners that are commercial products, if the manufacturer of the fasteners certifies it will purchase, during the
L0:relevant calendar year, an amount of domestically melted or produced specialty metal, in the required form, for use in the
L0:production of fasteners for sale to the Department of Defense and other customers, that is not less than 50 percent of the
L0:total amount of the specialty metal that it will purchase to carry out the production of such fasteners for all customers.
L1:(4) Items manufactured in a qualifying country.
L1:(5) Specialty metals for which the Government has determined in accordance with DFARS 225.7003-3 that specialty metal
L0:melted or produced in the United States, its outlying areas, or a qualifying country cannot be acquired as and when needed
L0:in—
L1:(i) A satisfactory quality;
L1:(ii) A sufficient quantity; and
L1:(iii) The required form. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 4863(m)(4), the term “required form” in this clause refers to the form
L0:of the mill product, such as bar, billet, wire, slab, plate, or sheet, in the grade appropriate for the production of a finished
L0:end item to be delivered to the Government under this contract; or a finished component assembled into an end item to be
L0:delivered to the Government under this contract.
L1:(6) End items containing a minimal amount of otherwise noncompliant specialty metals (i.e., specialty metals not melted or
L0:produced in the United States, an outlying area, or a qualifying country, that are not covered by one of the other exceptions
L0:in this paragraph (c)), if the total weight of such noncompliant metals does not exceed 2 percent of the total weight of all
L0:specialty metals in the end item, as estimated in good faith by the Contractor. This exception does not apply to high
L0:performance magnets containing specialty metals.
L1:(d) Compliance for commercial derivative military articles.
L1:(1) As an alternative to the compliance required in paragraph (b) of this clause, the Contractor may purchase an amount of
L0:domestically melted or produced specialty metals in the required form, for use during the period of contract performance in
L0:the production of the commercial derivative military article and the related commercial article, if—
L1:(i) The Contracting Officer has notified the Contractor of the items to be delivered under this contract that have been
L0:determined by the Government to meet the definition of “commercial derivative military article”; and
L1:(ii) For each item that has been determined by the Government to meet the definition of “commercial derivative military
L0:article,” the Contractor has certified, as specified in the provision of the solicitation entitled “Commercial Derivative
L0:Military Article—Specialty Metals Compliance Certificate” (DFARS 252.225-7010 ), that the Contractor and its
L0:subcontractor(s) will enter into a contractual agreement or agreements to purchase an amount of domestically melted or
L0:produced specialty metal in the required form, for use during the period of contract performance in the production of each
L0:commercial derivative military article and the related commercial article, that is not less than the Contractor’s good faith
L0:estimate of the greater of—
L1:(A) An amount equivalent to 120 percent of the amount of specialty metal that is required to carry out the production of the
L0:commercial derivative military article (including the work performed under each subcontract); or
L1:(B) An amount equivalent to 50 percent of the amount of specialty metal that will be purchased by the Contractor and its
L0:subcontractors for use during such period in the production of the commercial derivative military article and the related
L0:commercial article.
L1:(2) For the purposes of this alternative, the amount of specialty metal that is required to carry out production of the
L0:commercial derivative military article includes specialty metal contained in any item, including COTS items.
L1:(e) Subcontracts.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall exclude and reserve paragraph (d) and this paragraph (e)(1) when flowing down this clause to
L0:subcontracts.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall insert paragraphs (a) through (c) and this paragraph (e)(2) of this clause in subcontracts, including
L0:subcontracts for commercial products, that are for items containing specialty metals to ensure compliance of the end
L0:products that the Contractor will deliver to the Government. When inserting this clause in subcontracts, the Contractor
L0:shall—
L1:(i) Modify paragraph (c)(6) of this clause only as necessary to facilitate management of the minimal content exception at
L0:the prime contract level. The minimal content exception does not apply to specialty metals contained in high-performance
L0:magnets; and
L1:(ii) Not further alter the clause other than to identify the appropriate parties.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.225-7009 — Restriction on Acquisition of Certain Articles Containing Specialty Metals

title: 252.225-7013 Duty-Free Entry
content:
L0:252.225-7013 Duty-Free Entry.
L0:As prescribed in 225.1101 (4), use the following clause:
L0:Duty-Free Entry (AUG 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions.As used in this clause—
L0:“Component,” means any item supplied to the Government as part of an end product or of another component.
L0:“Customs territory of the United States” means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico.
L0:“Eligible product” means—
L1:(1) “Designated country end product,” as defined in the Trade Agreements (either basic or alternate) clause of this contract;
L1:(2) Free Trade Agreement country end product, other than a Bahraini end product, a Moroccan end product, a Panamanian
L0:end product, or a Peruvian end product, as defined in the Buy American—Free Trade Agreements—Balance of Payments
L0:Program (either basic or alternate II) clause of this contract; or
L1:(3) Free Trade Agreement country end product other than a Bahraini end product, Korean end product, Moroccan end
L0:product, Panamanian end product, or Peruvian end product, as defined in the Buy American—Free Trade Agreements—
L0:Balance of Payments Program (either alternate IV or alternate V) clause of this contract.
L0:“Qualifying country” and “qualifying country end product” have the meanings given in the Trade Agreements clause, the
L0:Buy American and Balance of Payments Program clause, or the Buy American—Free Trade Agreements—Balance of
L0:Payments Program clause of this contract, basic or alternate.
L1:(b) Except as provided in paragraph (i) of this clause, or unless supplies were imported into the customs territory of the
L0:United States before the date of this contract or the applicable subcontract, the price of this contract shall not include any
L0:amount for duty on—
L1:(1) End items that are eligible products or qualifying country end products;
L1:(2) Components (including, without limitation, raw materials and intermediate assemblies) produced or made in qualifying
L0:countries, that are to be incorporated in U.S.- made end products to be delivered under this contract; or
L1:(3) Other supplies for which the Contractor estimates that duty will exceed $300 per shipment into the customs territory of
L0:the United States.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Claim duty-free entry only for supplies that the Contractor intends to deliver to the Government under this contract,
L0:either as end items or components of end items; and
L1:(2) Pay duty on supplies, or any portion thereof, that are diverted to nongovernmental use, other than—
L1:(i) Scrap or salvage; or
L1:(ii) Competitive sale made, directed, or authorized by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(d) Except as the Contractor may otherwise agree, the Government will execute duty-free entry certificates and will afford
L0:such assistance as appropriate to obtain the duty-free entry of supplies—
L1:(1) For which no duty is included in the contract price in accordance with paragraph (b) of this clause; and
L1:(2) For which shipping documents bear the notation specified in paragraph (e) of this clause.
L1:(e) For foreign supplies for which the Government will issue duty-free entry certificates in accordance with this clause,
L0:shipping documents submitted to Customs shall—
L1:(1) Consign the shipments to the appropriate—
L1:(i) Military department in care of the Contractor, including the Contractor's delivery address; or
L1:(ii) Military installation; and
L1:(2) Include the following information:
L1:(i) Prime contract number and, if applicable, delivery order number.
L1:(ii) Number of the subcontract for foreign supplies, if applicable.
L1:(iii) Identification of the carrier.
L1:(iv)(A) For direct shipments to a U.S. military installation, the notation: “UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT,
L0:DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE Duty-Free Entry to be claimed pursuant to Section XXII, Chapter 98, Subchapter VIII,
L0:Item 9808.00.30 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States. Upon arrival of shipment at the appropriate port
L0:of entry, District Director of Customs, please release shipment under 19 CFR part 142 and notify Defense Contract
L0:Management Agency (DCMA) St. Louis, St. Louis, MO, ATTN: Duty Free Entry Team, 1222 Spruce Street, Room 9.300,
L0:St. Louis, MO 63103-2812, for execution of Customs Form 7501, 7501A, or 7506 and any required duty-free entry
L0:certificates.”
L1:(B) If the shipment will be consigned to other than a military installation, e.g., a domestic contractor's plant, the shipping
L0:document notation shall be altered to include the name and address of the contractor, agent, or broker who will notify
L0:DCMA St. Louis, Duty Free Entry Team, for execution of the duty-free entry certificate. (If the shipment will be consigned
L0:to a contractor's plant and no duty-free entry certificate is required due to a trade agreement, the Contractor shall claim
L0:duty-free entry under the applicable trade agreement and shall comply with the U.S. Customs Service requirements. No
L0:notification to DCMA St. Louis, Duty Free Entry Team, is required.)
L1:(v) Gross weight in pounds (if freight is based on space tonnage, state cubic feet in addition to gross shipping weight).
L1:(vi) Estimated value in U.S. dollars.
L1:(vii) Activity address number of the contract administration office administering the prime contract, e.g., for DCMA
L0:Dayton, S3605A.
L1:(f) Preparation of customs forms.
L1:(1)(i) Except for shipments consigned to a military installation, the Contractor shall—
L1:(A) Prepare any customs forms required for the entry of foreign supplies into the customs territory of the United States in
L0:connection with this contract; and
L1:(B) Submit the completed customs forms to the District Director of Customs, with a copy to DCMA St. Louis, Duty Free
L0:Entry Team for execution of any required duty-free entry certificates.
L1:(ii) Shipments consigned directly to a military installation will be released in accordance with sections 10.101 and 10.102
L0:of the U.S. Customs regulations.
L1:(2) For shipments containing both supplies that are to be accorded duty-free entry and supplies that are not, the Contractor
L0:shall identify on the customs forms those items that are eligible for duty-free entry.
L1:(g) The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Prepare (if the Contractor is a foreign supplier), or shall instruct the foreign supplier to prepare, a sufficient number of
L0:copies of the bill of lading (or other shipping document) so that at least two of the copies accompanying the shipment will
L0:be available for use by the District Director of Customs at the port of entry;
L1:(2) Consign the shipment as specified in paragraph (e) of this clause; and
L1:(3) Mark on the exterior of all packages—
L1:(i) “UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT, DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE”; and
L1:(ii) The activity address number of the contract administration office administering the prime contract.
L1:(h) The Contractor shall notify the Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO) in writing of any purchase of eligible
L0:products or qualifying country supplies to be accorded duty-free entry, that are to be imported into the customs territory of
L0:the United States for delivery to the Government or for incorporation in end items to be delivered to the Government. The
L0:Contractor shall furnish the notice to the ACO immediately upon award to the supplier and shall include in the notice—
L1:(1) The Contractor’s name, address, and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code;
L1:(2) Prime contract number and, if applicable, delivery order number;
L1:(3) Total dollar value of the prime contract or delivery order;
L1:(4) Date of the last scheduled delivery under the prime contract or delivery order;
L1:(5) Foreign supplier's name and address;
L1:(6) Number of the subcontract for foreign supplies;
L1:(7) Total dollar value of the subcontract for foreign supplies;
L1:(8) Date of the last scheduled delivery under the subcontract for foreign supplies;
L1:(9) List of items purchased;
L1:(10) An agreement that the Contractor will pay duty on supplies, or any portion thereof, that are diverted to
L0:nongovernmental use other than—
L1:(i) Scrap or salvage; or
L1:(ii) Competitive sale made, directed, or authorized by the Contracting Officer;
L1:(11) Country of origin; and
L1:(12) Scheduled delivery date(s).
L1:(i) This clause does not apply to purchases of eligible products or qualifying country supplies in connection with this
L0:contract if—
L1:(1) The supplies are identical in nature to supplies purchased by the Contractor or any subcontractor in connection with its
L0:commercial business; and
L1:(2) It is not economical or feasible to account for such supplies so as to ensure that the amount of the supplies for which
L0:duty-free entry is claimed does not exceed the amount purchased in connection with this contract.
L1:(j) The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Insert the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (j), in all subcontracts for—
L1:(i) Qualifying country components; or
L1:(ii) Nonqualifying country components for which the Contractor estimates that duty will exceed $200 per unit;
L1:(2) Require subcontractors to include the number of this contract on all shipping documents submitted to Customs for
L0:supplies for which duty-free entry is claimed pursuant to this clause; and
L1:(3) Include in applicable subcontracts—
L1:(i) The name and address of the ACO for this contract;
L1:(ii) The name, address, and activity address number of the contract administration office specified in this contract; and
L1:(iii) The information required by paragraphs (h)(1), (2), and (3) of this clause.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.225-7016 Restriction on Acquisition of Ball and Roller Bearings
content:
L0:252.225-7016 Restriction on Acquisition of Ball and Roller Bearings.
L0:As prescribed in 225.7009-5 , use the following clause:
L0:RESTRICTION ON ACQUISITION OF BALL AND ROLLER BEARINGS (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) “Bearing components” means the bearing element, retainer, inner race, or outer race.
L1:(2) “Component,” other than a bearing component, means any item supplied to the Government as part of an end product
L0:or of another component.
L1:(3) “End product” means supplies delivered under a line item of this contract.
L1:(b) Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this clause—
L1:(1) Each ball and roller bearing delivered under this contract shall be manufactured in the United States, its outlying areas,
L0:or Canada; and
L1:(2) For each ball or roller bearing, the cost of the bearing components manufactured in the United States, its outlying areas,
L0:or Canada shall exceed 50 percent of the total cost of the bearing components of that ball or roller bearing.
L1:(c) The restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause does not apply to ball or roller bearings that are acquired as—
L1:(1) Commercial components of an other than commercial; or
L1:(2) Commercial or other than commercial components of an commercial component of a other than commercial end
L0:product.
L1:(d) The restriction in paragraph (b) of this clause may be waived upon request from the Contractor in accordance with
L0:subsection 225.7009-4 of the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement.
L1:(e) If this contract includes DFARS clause 252.225-7009 , Restriction on Acquisition of Certain Articles Containing
L0:Specialty Metals, all bearings that contain specialty metals, as defined in that clause, must meet the requirements of that
L0:clause.
L1:(f) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall insert the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (f), in all subcontracts,
L0:except those for—
L1:(1) Commercial products; or
L1:(2) Items that do not contain ball or roller bearings.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.225-7017 Photovoltaic Devices
content:
L0:252.225-7017 Photovoltaic Devices.
L0:As prescribed in 225.7017-4 (a), use the following clause:
L0:PHOTOVOLTAIC DEVICES (MAR 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions.As used in this clause—
L0:Bahraini photovoltaic device means a photovoltaic device that—

L1:(2) In the case of a photovoltaic device that consists in whole or in part of materials from another country, has been
L0:substantially transformed in Bahrain into a new and different article of commerce with a name, character, or use distinct
L0:from that of the article or articles from which it was transformed, provided that the photovoltaic device is not subsequently
L0:substantially transformed outside of Bahrain.
L0:“Caribbean Basin country photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device that—
L1:(1) Is wholly manufactured in a Caribbean Basin country; or
L1:(2) In the case of a photovoltaic device that consists in whole or in part of materials from another country, has been
L0:substantially transformed in a Caribbean Basin country into a new and different article of commerce with a name,
L0:character, or use distinct from that of the article or articles from which it was transformed, provided that the photovoltaic
L0:device is not subsequently substantially transformed outside of a Caribbean Basin country.
L0:“Designated country” means—
L1:(1) A World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement (WTO GPA) country (Armenia, Aruba, Australia,
L0:Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany,
L0:Greece, Hong Kong, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Korea (Republic of), Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania,
L0:Luxembourg, Malta, Moldova, Montenegro, Netherlands, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal,

L1:(2) A Free Trade Agreement country (Australia, Bahrain, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, El Salvador,

L1:(3) A least developed country (Afghanistan, Angola, Bangladesh, Benin, Bhutan, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia,

L0:Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Haiti, Kiribati, Laos, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania,

L0:“Designated country photovoltaic device” means a WTO GPA country photovoltaic device, a Free Trade Agreement
L0:country photovoltaic device, a least developed country photovoltaic device, or a Caribbean Basin country photovoltaic
L0:device.

L0:“Foreign photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device other than a domestic photovoltaic device.
L0:“Free Trade Agreement country” means Australia, Bahrain, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, El
L0:Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Korea (Republic of), Mexico, Morocco, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, or Singapore.

L0:or use distinct from that of the article or articles from which it was transformed, provided that the photovoltaic device is not

L0:“Moroccan photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device that—

L0:process.

L0:“United States” means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and outlying areas.
L0:“U.S.-made photovoltaic device” means a photovoltaic device that—

title: 252.225-7018 Photovoltaic Devices—Certificate
content:

L0:device,” “photovoltaic device,” “qualifying country,” “qualifying country photovoltaic device,” “United States,” “U.S.made photovoltaic device,” and “WTO GPA country photovoltaic device” have the meanings given in the Photovoltaic

content:
L0:252.225-7036 Buy American—Free Trade Agreements—Balance of Payments Program.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 225.1101 (10)(i) and (10)(i)(A), use the following clause:
L0:BUY AMERICAN—FREE TRADE AGREEMENTS—BALANCE OF PAYMENTS PROGRAM—BASIC (FEB 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions.As used in this clause—
L0:Bahraini end product means an article that—
L1:(1) Is wholly the growth, product, or manufacture of Bahrain; or
L1:(2) In the case of an article that consists in whole or in part of materials from another country, has been substantially
L0:transformed in Bahrain into a new and different article of commerce with a name, character, or use distinct from that of the
L0:article or articles from which it was transformed. The term refers to a product offered for purchase under a supply contract,
L0:but for purposes of calculating the value of the end product includes services (except transportation services) incidental to
L0:its supply, provided that the value of those incidental services does not exceed the value of the product itself.
L0:“Commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item”—
L1:(1) Means any item of supply (including construction material) that is—
L1:(i) A commercial product (as defined in paragraph (1) of the definition of “commercial product” in section 2.101 of the
L0:Federal Acquisition Regulation);
L1:(ii) Sold in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(iii) Offered to the Government, under a contract or subcontract at any tier, without modification, in the same form in
L0:which it is sold in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(2) Does not include bulk cargo, as defined in 46 U.S.C. 40102(4), such as agricultural products and petroleum products.
L0:“Component” means an article, material, or supply incorporated directly into an end product.
L0:“Critical component ” means a component that is mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States and deemed
L0:critical to the U.S. supply chain. The list of critical components is at FAR 25.105.
L0:“Critical item” means domestic construction material or a domestic end product that is deemed critical to the U.S. supply
L0:chain. The list of critical items is at FAR 25.105.
L0:“Domestic end product” means—
L1:(1) For an end product that does not consist wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both—
L1:(i) An unmanufactured end product that has been mined or produced in the United States; or
L1:(ii) An end product manufactured in the United States if—
L1:(A) The cost of its qualifying country components and its components that are mined, produced, or manufactured in the
L0:United States exceeds 60 percent of the cost of all its components, except that the percentage will be 65 percent for items
L0:delivered in calendar years 2024 through 2028 and 75 percent for items delivered starting in calendar year 2029, unless an
L0:alternate percentage is established for a contract in accordance with Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement
L1:(DFARS) 225.101(d); or award is made before January 1, 2030, for a foreign end product that exceeds 55 percent domestic
L0:content (see DFARS 225.103(b)(ii)). The cost of components includes transportation costs to the place of incorporation
L0:into the end product and U.S. duty (whether or not a duty-free entry certificate is issued). Components of unknown origin
L0:are treated as foreign. Scrap generated, collected, and prepared for processing in the United States is considered domestic.
L0:A component is considered to have been mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States (regardless of its source in
L0:fact) if the end product in which it is incorporated is manufactured in the United States and the component is of a class or
L0:kind for which the Government has determined that—
L1:(1) Sufficient and reasonably available commercial quantities of a satisfactory quality are not mined, produced, or
L0:manufactured in the United States; or
L1:(2) It is inconsistent with the public interest to apply the restrictions of the Buy American statute; or
L1:(B) The end product is a COTS item; or
L1:(2) For an end product that consists wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both, an end product
L0:manufactured in the United States, if the cost of iron and steel not produced in the United States or a qualifying country
L0:constitutes less than 5 percent of the cost of all the components used in the end product (produced in the United States or a
L0:qualifying country means that all manufacturing processes of the iron or steel must take place in the United States or a
L0:qualifying country, except metallurgical processes involving refinement of steel additives). The cost of iron and steel not
L0:produced in the United States or a qualifying country includes but is not limited to the cost of iron or steel mill products
L0:(such as bar, billet, slab, wire, plate, or sheet), castings, or forgings, not produced in the United States or a qualifying
L0:country, utilized in the manufacture of the end product and a good faith estimate of the cost of all iron or steel components
L0:not produced in the United States or a qualifying country, excluding COTS fasteners. Iron or steel components of unknown
L0:origin are treated as foreign. If the end product contains multiple components, the cost of all the materials used in such end
L0:product is calculated in accordance with the explanation of cost of components in paragraph (1)(ii)(A) of this definition.
L0:“End product” means those articles, materials, and supplies to be acquired under this contract for public use.
L0:“Foreign end product” means an end product other than a domestic end product.
L0:“Free Trade Agreement country” means Australia, Bahrain, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, El
L0:Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Korea (Republic of), Mexico, Morocco, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, or Singapore.
L0:“Free Trade Agreement country end product” means an article that—
L1:(1) Is wholly the growth, product, or manufacture of a Free Trade Agreement country; or
L1:(2) In the case of an article that consists in whole or in part of materials from another country, has been substantially
L0:transformed in a Free Trade Agreement country into a new and different article of commerce with a name, character, or use
L0:distinct from that of the article or articles from which it was transformed. The term refers to a product offered for purchase
L0:under a supply contract, but for purposes of calculating the value of the end product includes services (except
L0:transportation services) incidental to its supply, provided that the value of those incidental services does not exceed the
L0:value of the product itself.

L0:“Peruvian end product” means an article that—

L0:its supply, provided that the value of those incidental services does not exceed the value of the product itself.
L0:“Predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both” means that the cost of the iron and steel content exceeds 50
L0:percent of the total cost of all its components. The cost of iron and steel is the cost of the iron or steel mill products (such
L0:as bar, billet, slab, wire, plate, or sheet), castings, or forgings utilized in the manufacture of the product and a good faith
L0:estimate of the cost of iron or steel components excluding COTS fasteners.
L0:“Qualifying country” means a country with a reciprocal defense procurement memorandum of understanding or
L0:international agreement with the United States in which both countries agree to remove barriers to purchases of supplies
L0:produced in the other country or services performed by sources of the other country, and the memorandum or agreement
L0:complies, where applicable, with the requirements of section 36 of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2776) and with
L0:10 U.S.C. 2457. Accordingly, the following are qualifying countries:

L0:Denmark

L0:Israel
L0:Italy

L0:Lithuania
L0:Luxembourg
L0:Netherlands

L0:Poland
L0:Portugal
L0:Slovenia
L0:Spain
L0:Sweden
L0:Switzerland
L0:Turkey
L0:United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

L0:“Qualifying country end product” means—

L0:reasonably available commercial quantities of a satisfactory quality are not mined, produced, or manufactured in the United
L0:States; or
L1:(ii) The end product is a COTS item.
L0:“Steel” means an alloy that includes at least 50 percent iron, between 0.02 and 2 percent carbon, and may include other
L0:elements.
L0:“United States” means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and outlying areas.
L1:(b) Unless otherwise specified, this clause applies to all items in the Schedule.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall deliver under this contract only domestic end products unless, in its offer, it specified delivery of
L0:qualifying country end products, Free Trade Agreement country end products other than Bahraini end products, Moroccan
L0:end products, Panamanian end products, or Peruvian end products, or other foreign end products in the Buy American—
L0:Free Trade Agreements—Balance of Payments Program Certificate—Basic provision of the solicitation. If the Contractor
L0:certified in its offer that it will deliver a qualifying country end product or a Free Trade Agreement country end product
L0:other than a Bahraini end product, a Moroccan end product, a Panamanian end product, or a Peruvian end product, the

L0:Bahraini end product, a Moroccan end product, a Panamanian end product, or a Peruvian end product, or, at the
L0:Contractor's option, a domestic end product.
L1:(d) The contract price does not include duty for end products or components for which the Contractor will claim duty-free
L0:entry.
