title: 252.225-7039 Defense Contractors Performing Private Security Functions Outside the United States
content:
L0:252.225-7039 Defense Contractors Performing Private Security Functions Outside the United States.
L0:As prescribed in 225.302-6 , insert the following clause:
L0:DEFENSE CONTRACTORS PERFORMING PRIVATE SECURITY FUNCTIONS OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES
L0:(JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Full cooperation”—
L1:(1) Means disclosure to the Government of the information sufficient to identify the nature and extent of the incident and
L0:the individuals responsible for the conduct. It includes providing timely and complete response to Government auditors'
L0:and investigators' requests for documents and access to employees with information;
L1:(2) Does not foreclose any contractor rights arising in law, the FAR or the terms of the contract. It does not require—
L1:(i) The contractor to waive its attorney-client privilege or the protections afforded by the attorney work product doctrine; or
L1:(ii) Any officer, director, owner, or employee of the contractor, including a sole proprietor, to waive his or her attorneyclient privilege or Fifth Amendment rights; and
L1:(3) Does not restrict the contractor from—
L1:(i) Conducting an internal investigation; or
L1:(ii) Defending a proceeding or dispute arising under the contract or related to a potential or disclosed violation.
L0:“Private security functions” means the following activities engaged in by a contractor:
L1:(1) Guarding of personnel, facilities, designated sites or property of a Federal agency, the contractor or subcontractor, or a
L0:third party.
L1:(2) Any other activity for which personnel are required to carry weapons in the performance of their duties in accordance
L0:with the terms of this contract.
L1:(b) Applicability. If this contract is performed both in a designated area and in an area that is not designated, the clause
L0:only applies to performance in the designated area. Designated areas are areas outside the United States of—
L1:(1) Contingency operations;
L1:(2) Combat operations, as designated by the Secretary of Defense;
L1:(3) Other significant military operations (as defined in 32 CFR part 159), designated by the Secretary of Defense upon
L0:agreement of the Secretary of State;
L1:(4) Peace operations, consistent with Joint Publication 3-07.3; or
L1:(5) Other military operations or military exercises, when designated by the Combatant Commander.
L1:(c) Requirements. The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Ensure that all Contractor personnel who are responsible for performing private security functions under this contract
L0:comply with 32 CFR part 159 and any orders, directives, or instructions to contractors performing private security
L0:functions that are identified in the contract for—
L1:(i) Registering, processing, accounting for, managing, overseeing and keeping appropriate records of personnel performing
L0:private security functions;
L1:(ii) Authorizing, accounting for and registering in Synchronized Predeployment and Operational Tracker (SPOT), weapons
L0:to be carried by or available to be used by personnel performing private security functions;
L1:(iii) Identifying and registering in SPOT armored vehicles, helicopters and other military vehicles operated by Contractors
L0:performing private security functions; and
L1:(iv) In accordance with orders and instructions established by the applicable Combatant Commander, reporting incidents in
L0:which—
L1:(A) A weapon is discharged by personnel performing private security functions;
L1:(B) Personnel performing private security functions are attacked, killed, or injured;
L1:(C) Persons are killed or injured or property is destroyed as a result of conduct by Contractor personnel;
L1:(D) A weapon is discharged against personnel performing private security functions or personnel performing such
L0:functions believe a weapon was so discharged; or
L1:(E) Active, non-lethal countermeasures (other than the discharge of a weapon) are employed by personnel performing
L0:private security functions in response to a perceived immediate threat;
L1:(2) Ensure that Contractor personnel who are responsible for performing private security functions under this contract are
L0:briefed on and understand their obligation to comply with—
L1:(i) Qualification, training, screening (including, if applicable, thorough background checks) and security requirements
L0:established by 32 CFR part 159;
L1:(ii) Applicable laws and regulations of the United States and the host country and applicable treaties and international
L0:agreements regarding performance of private security functions;
L1:(iii) Orders, directives, and instructions issued by the applicable Combatant Commander or relevant Chief of Mission
L0:relating to weapons, equipment, force protection, security, health, safety, or relations and interaction with locals; and
L1:(iv) Rules on the use of force issued by the applicable Combatant Commander or relevant Chief of Mission for personnel
L0:performing private security functions;
L1:(3) Provide full cooperation with any Government-authorized investigation of incidents reported pursuant to paragraph (c)
L1:(1)(iv) of this clause and incidents of alleged misconduct by personnel performing private security functions under this
L0:contract by providing—
L1:(i) Access to employees performing private security functions; and
L1:(ii) Relevant information in the possession of the Contractor regarding the incident concerned; and
L1:(4) Comply with ANSI/ASIS PSC.1-2012, American National Standard, Management System for Quality of Private
L0:Security Company Operations—Requirements with Guidance or the International Standard ISO 18788, Management
L0:System for Private Security Operations—Requirements with Guidance (located at
L0:http://www.acq.osd.mil/log/PS/psc.html).
L1:(d) Remedies. In addition to other remedies available to the Government—
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer may direct the Contractor, at its own expense, to remove and replace any Contractor or
L0:subcontractor personnel performing private security functions who fail to comply with or violate applicable requirements
L0:of this clause or 32 CFR part 159. Such action may be taken at the Government's discretion without prejudice to its rights
L0:under any other provision of this contract;
L1:(2) The Contractor’s failure to comply with the requirements of this clause will be included in appropriate databases of past
L0:performance and considered in any responsibility determination or evaluation of past performance; and
L1:(3) If this is an award-fee contract, the Contractor's failure to comply with the requirements of this clause shall be
L0:considered in the evaluation of the Contractor's performance during the relevant evaluation period, and the Contracting
L0:Officer may treat such failure to comply as a basis for reducing or denying award fees for such period or for recovering all
L0:or part of award fees previously paid for such period.
L1:(e) Rule of construction. The duty of the Contractor to comply with the requirements of this clause shall not be reduced or
L0:diminished by the failure of a higher- or lower-tier Contractor or subcontractor to comply with the clause requirements or
L0:by a failure of the contracting activity to provide required oversight.
L1:(f) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (f), in subcontracts,
L0:including subcontracts for commercial products or commercial services, when private security functions will be performed
L0:outside the United States in areas of—
L1:(1) Contingency operations;
L1:(2) Combat operations, as designated by the Secretary of Defense;
L1:(3) Other significant military operations (as defined in 32 CFR part 159), designated by the Secretary of Defense upon
L0:agreement of the Secretary of State;
L1:(4) Peace operations, consistent with Joint Publication 3-07.3; or
L1:(5) Other military operations or military exercises, when designated by the Combatant Commander.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.225-7040 Contractor Personnel Supporting U.S. Armed Forces Deployed Outside the United States
content:
L0:252.225-7040 Contractor Personnel Supporting U.S. Armed Forces Deployed Outside the United States.
L0:As prescribed in 225.371-5 (a), use the following clause:
L0:CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL SUPPORTING U.S. ARMED FORCES DEPLOYED OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES
L0:(OCT 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Combatant Commander” means the commander of a unified or specified combatant command established in accordance
L0:with 10 U.S.C. 161.
L0:“Contractors authorized to accompany the Force,” or “CAAF,” means contractor personnel, including all tiers of
L0:subcontractor personnel, who are authorized to accompany U.S. Armed Forces in applicable operations and have been
L0:afforded CAAF status through a letter of authorization. CAAF generally include all U.S. citizen n and third-country
L0:national employees not normally residing within the operational area whose area of performance is in the direct vicinity of
L0:U.S. Armed Forces and who routinely are collocated with the U.S. Armed Forces (especially in non-permissive
L0:environments). Personnel collocated with U.S. Armed Forces shall be afforded CAAF status through a letter of
L0:authorization. In some cases, Combatant Commander subordinate commanders may designate mission-essential host nation
L0:or local national contractor employees (e.g., interpreters) as CAAF. CAAF includes contractors previously identified as
L0:contractors deploying with the U.S. Armed Forces. CAAF status does not apply to contractor personnel in support of
L0:applicable operations within the boundaries and territories of the United States.
L0:“Designated operational area” means a geographic area designated by the combatant commander or subordinate joint force
L0:commander for the conduct or support of specified military operations.
L0:“Designated reception site” means the designated place for the reception, staging, integration, and onward movement of
L0:contractors deploying during a contingency. The designated reception site includes assigned joint reception centers and
L0:other Service or private reception sites.
L0:“Law of war” means that part of international law that regulates the conduct of armed hostilities. The law of war
L0:encompasses all international law for the conduct of hostilities binding on the United States or its individual citizens,
L0:including treaties and international agreements to which the United States is a party, and applicable customary international
L0:law.
L0:“Non-CAAF” means personnel who are not designated as CAAF, such as local national (LN) employees and non-LN
L0:employees who are permanent residents in the operational area or third-country nationals not routinely residing with U.S.
L0:Armed Forces (and third-country national expatriates who are permanent residents in the operational area) who perform
L0:support functions away from the close proximity of, and do not reside with, U.S. Armed Forces. Government-furnished
L0:support to non-CAAF is typically limited to force protection, emergency medical care, and basic human needs (e.g., bottled
L0:water, latrine facilities, security, and food when necessary) when performing their jobs in the direct vicinity of U.S. Armed
L0:Forces. Non-CAAF status does not apply to contractor personnel in support of applicable operations within the boundaries
L0:and territories of the United States.
L0:“Subordinate joint force commander” means a sub-unified commander or joint task force commander.
L1:(b) General.
L1:(1) This clause applies to both CAAF and non-CAAF when performing in a designated operational area outside the United
L0:States to support U.S. Armed Forces deployed outside the United States in—
L1:(i) Contingency operations;
L1:(ii) Peace operations, consistent with Joint Publication 3-07.3; or
L1:(iii) Other military operations or military exercises, when designated by the Combatant Commander or as directed by the
L0:Secretary of Defense.
L1:(2) Contract performance in support of U.S. Armed Forces deployed outside the United States may require work in
L0:dangerous or austere conditions. Except as otherwise provided in the contract, the Contractor accepts the risks associated
L0:with required contract performance in such operations.
L1:(3) When authorized in accordance with paragraph (j) of this clause to carry arms for personal protection, Contractor
L0:personnel are only authorized to use force for individual self-defense.
L1:(4) Unless immune from host nation jurisdiction by virtue of an international agreement or international law, inappropriate
L0:use of force by contractor personnel supporting the U.S. Armed Forces can subject such personnel to United States or host
L0:nation prosecution and civil liability (see paragraphs (d) and (j)(3) of this clause).
L1:(5) Service performed by Contractor personnel subject to this clause is not active duty or service under 38 U.S.C. 106 note.
L1:(c) Support.
L1:(1)(i) The Combatant Commander will develop a security plan for protection of Contractor personnel in locations where
L0:there is not sufficient or legitimate civil authority, when the Combatant Commander decides it is in the interests of the
L0:Government to provide security because—
L1:(A) The Contractor cannot obtain effective security services;
L1:(B) Effective security services are unavailable at a reasonable cost; or
L1:(C) Threat conditions necessitate security through military means.
L1:(ii) In appropriate cases, the Combatant Commander may provide security through military means, commensurate with the
L0:level of security provided DoD civilians.
L1:(2)(i) Generally, CAAF will be afforded emergency medical and dental care if injured while supporting applicable
L0:operations. Additionally, non-CAAF employees who are injured while in the vicinity of U. S. Armed Forces will normally
L0:receive emergency medical and dental care. Emergency medical and dental care includes medical care situations in which
L0:life, limb, or eyesight is jeopardized. Examples of emergency medical and dental care include examination and initial
L0:treatment of victims of sexual assault; refills of prescriptions for life-dependent drugs; repair of broken bones, lacerations,
L0:infections; and traumatic injuries to the dentition. Hospitalization will be limited to stabilization and short-term medical
L0:treatment with an emphasis on return to duty or placement in the patient movement system.
L1:(ii) When the Government provides medical treatment or transportation of Contractor personnel to a selected civilian
L0:facility, the Contractor shall ensure that the Government is reimbursed for any costs associated with such treatment or
L0:transportation.
L1:(iii) Medical or dental care beyond this standard is not authorized.
L1:(3) Contractor personnel must have a Synchronized Predeployment and Operational Tracker (SPOT)-generated letter of
L0:authorization signed by the Contracting Officer in order to process through a deployment center or to travel to, from, or
L0:within the designated operational area. The letter of authorization also will identify any additional authorizations,
L0:privileges, or Government support that Contractor personnel are entitled to under this contract. Contractor personnel who
L0:are issued a letter of authorization shall carry it with them at all times while deployed.
L1:(4) Unless specified elsewhere in this contract, the Contractor is responsible for all other support required for its personnel
L0:engaged in the designated operational area under this contract.
L1:(d) Compliance with laws and regulations.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall comply with, and shall ensure that its personnel supporting U.S. Armed Forces deployed outside
L0:the United States as specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this clause are familiar with and comply with, all applicable—
L1:(i) United States, host country, and third country national laws;
L1:(ii) Provisions of the law of war, as well as any other applicable treaties and international agreements;
L1:(iii) United States regulations, directives, instructions, policies, and procedures; and
L1:(iv) Orders, directives, and instructions issued by the Combatant Commander, including those relating to force protection,
L0:security, health, safety, or relations and interaction with local nationals.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall institute and implement an effective program to prevent violations of the law of war by its
L0:employees and subcontractors, including law of war training in accordance with paragraph (e)(1)(vii) of this clause.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall ensure that CAAF and non-CAAF are aware—
L1:(i) Of the DoD definition of “sexual assault” in DoD Directive 6495.01, Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Program;
L1:(ii) That the offenses addressed by the definition are covered under the Uniform Code of Military Justice (see paragraph (e)
L1:(2)(iv) of this clause). Other sexual misconduct may constitute offenses under the Uniform Code of Military Justice,
L0:Federal law, such as the Military Extraterritorial Jurisdiction Act, or host nation laws; and
L1:(iii) That the offenses not covered by the Uniform Code of Military Justice may nevertheless have consequences to the
L0:contractor employees (see paragraph (h)(1) of this clause).
L1:(4) The Contractor shall report to the appropriate investigative authorities, identified in paragraph (d)(6) of this clause, any
L0:alleged offenses under—
L1:(i) The Uniform Code of Military Justice (chapter 47 of title 10, United States Code) (applicable to contractors serving with
L0:or accompanying an armed force in the field during a declared war or contingency operations); or
L1:(ii) The Military Extraterritorial Jurisdiction Act (chapter 212 of title 18, United States Code).
L1:(5) The Contractor shall provide to all contractor personnel who will perform work on a contract in the deployed area,
L0:before beginning such work, information on the following:
L1:(i) How and where to report an alleged crime described in paragraph (d)(4) of this clause.
L1:(ii) Where to seek victim and witness protection and assistance available to contractor personnel in connection with an
L0:alleged offense described in paragraph (d)(4) of this clause.
L1:(iii) That this section does not create any rights or privileges that are not authorized by law or DoD policy.
L1:(6) The appropriate investigative authorities to which suspected crimes shall be reported include the following—
L1:(i) US Army Criminal Investigation Command at http://www.cid.army.mil/reportacrime.html;
L1:(ii) Air Force Office of Special Investigations at http://www.osi.andrews.af.mil/library/factsheets/factsheet.asp?id=14522;
L1:(iii) Navy Criminal Investigative Service at http://www.ncis.navy.mil/Pages/publicdefault.aspx;
L1:(iv) Defense Criminal Investigative Service at http://www.dodig.mil/HOTLINE/index.html;
L1:(v) To any command of any supported military element or the command of any base.
L1:(7) Personnel seeking whistleblower protection from reprisals for reporting criminal acts shall seek guidance through the
L0:DoD Inspector General hotline at 800-424-9098 or www.dodig.mil/HOTLINE/index.html. Personnel seeking other forms
L0:of victim or witness protections should contact the nearest military law enforcement office.
L1:(8)(i) The Contractor shall ensure that Contractor employees supporting the U.S. Armed Forces are aware of their rights to
L0:—
L1:(A) Hold their own identity or immigration documents, such as passport or driver’s license, regardless of the documents’
L0:issuing authority;
L1:(B) Receive agreed upon wages on time;
L1:(C) Take lunch and work-breaks;
L1:(D) Elect to terminate employment at any time;
L1:(E) Identify grievances without fear of reprisal;
L1:(F) Have a copy of their employment contract in a language they understand;
L1:(G) Receive wages that are not below the legal host-country minimum wage;
L1:(H) Be notified of their rights, wages, and prohibited activities prior to signing their employment contract; and
L1:(I) If housing is provided, live in housing that meets host-country housing and safety standards.
L1:(ii) The Contractor shall post these rights in employee work spaces in English and in any foreign language(s) spoken by a
L0:significant portion of the workforce.
L1:(iii) The Contractor shall enforce the rights of Contractor personnel supporting the U.S. Armed Forces.
L1:(e) Preliminary personnel requirements.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall ensure that the following requirements are met prior to deploying CAAF (specific requirements
L0:for each category will be specified in the statement of work or elsewhere in the contract):
L1:(i) All required security and background checks are complete and acceptable.
L1:(ii) All CAAF deploying in support of an applicable operation—
L1:(A) Are medically, dentally, and psychologically fit for deployment and performance of their contracted duties;
L1:(B) Meet the minimum medical screening requirements, including theater-specific medical qualifications as established by
L0:the geographic Combatant Commander (as posted to the Geographic Combatant Commander’s website or other venue);
L0:and
L1:(C) Have received all required immunizations as specified in the contract.
L1:(1) During predeployment processing, the Government will provide, at no cost to the Contractor, any military-specific
L0:immunizations and/or medications not available to the general public.
L1:(2)All other immunizations shall be obtained prior to arrival at the deployment center.
L1:(3)All CAAF and selected non-CAAF, as specified in the statement of work, shall bring to the designated operational area a
L0:copy of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Form 731, International Certificate of Vaccination or
L0:Prophylaxis as Approved by the World Health Organization, (also known as "shot record" or "Yellow Card") that shows
L0:vaccinations are current.
L1:(iii) Deploying personnel have all necessary passports, visas, and other documents required to enter and exit a designated
L0:operational area and have a Geneva Conventions identification card, or other appropriate DoD identity credential, from the
L0:deployment center.
L1:(iv) Special area, country, and theater clearance is obtained for all personnel deploying. Clearance requirements are in DoD
L0:Directive 4500.54E, DoD Foreign Clearance Program. For this purpose, CAAF are considered non-DoD contractor
L0:personnel traveling under DoD sponsorship.
L1:(v) All deploying personnel have received personal security training. At a minimum, the training shall—
L1:(A) Cover safety and security issues facing employees overseas;
L1:(B) Identify safety and security contingency planning activities; and
L1:(C) Identify ways to utilize safety and security personnel and other resources appropriately.
L1:(vi) All personnel have received isolated personnel training, if specified in the contract, in accordance with DoD
L0:Instruction 1300.23, Isolated Personnel Training for DoD Civilian and Contractors.
L1:(vii) Personnel have received law of war training as follows:
L1:(A) Basic training is required for all CAAF. The basic training will be provided through—
L1:(1) A military-run training center; or
L1:(2) A web-based source, if specified in the contract or approved by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(B) Advanced training, commensurate with their duties and responsibilities, may be required for some Contractor
L0:personnel as specified in the contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall notify all personnel who are not a host country national, or who are not ordinarily resident in the
L0:host country, that—
L1:(i) Such employees, and dependents residing with such employees, who engage in conduct outside the United States that
L0:would constitute an offense punishable by imprisonment for more than one year if the conduct had been engaged in within
L0:the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, may potentially be subject to the criminal jurisdiction
L0:of the United States in accordance with the Military Extraterritorial Jurisdiction Act of 2000 (18 U.S.C. 3621, et seq.);
L1:(ii) Pursuant to the War Crimes Act (18 U.S.C. 2441), Federal criminal jurisdiction also extends to conduct that is
L0:determined to constitute a war crime when committed by a civilian national of the United States;
L1:(iii) Other laws may provide for prosecution of U.S. nationals who commit offenses on the premises of U.S. diplomatic,
L0:consular, military or other U.S. Government missions outside the United States (18 U.S.C. 7(9)); and
L1:(iv) In time of declared war or a contingency operation, CAAF are subject to the jurisdiction of the Uniform Code of
L0:Military Justice under 10 U.S.C. 802(a)(10).
L1:(v) Such employees are required to report offenses alleged to have been committed by or against Contractor personnel to
L0:appropriate investigative authorities.
L1:(vi) Such employees will be provided victim and witness protection and assistance.
L1:(f) Processing and departure points. CAAF shall—
L1:(1) Process through the deployment center designated in the contract, or as otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer,
L0:prior to deploying. The deployment center will conduct deployment processing to ensure visibility and accountability of
L0:Contractor personnel and to ensure that all deployment requirements are met, including the requirements specified in
L0:paragraph (e)(1) of this clause;
L1:(2) Use the point of departure and transportation mode directed by the Contracting Officer; and
L1:(3) Process through a designated reception site (DRS) upon arrival at the deployed location. The DRS will validate
L0:personnel accountability, ensure that specific designated operational area entrance requirements are met, and brief
L0:Contractor personnel on theater-specific policies and procedures.
L1:(g) Personnel data.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall use the Synchronized Predeployment and Operational Tracker (SPOT) web-based system, to enter
L0:and maintain the data for all CAAF and, as designated by the Under Secretary of Defense (Acquisition and Sustainment) or
L0:the Combatant Commander, non-CAAF supporting U.S. Armed Forces deployed outside the United States as specified in
L0:paragraph (b)(1) of this clause.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall enter the required information about their contractor personnel prior to deployment and shall
L0:continue to use the SPOT web-based system at https://spot.dmdc.mil to maintain accurate, up-to-date information
L0:throughout the deployment for all Contractor personnel. Changes to status of individual Contractor personnel relating to
L0:their in-theater arrival date and their duty location, to include closing out the deployment with their proper status (e.g.,
L0:mission complete, killed, wounded) shall be annotated within the SPOT database in accordance with the timelines
L0:established in the SPOT Business Rules at https://www.acq.osd.mil/asds/log/cso/ocs/spot.html.
L1:(h) Contractor personnel.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer may direct the Contractor, at its own expense, to remove and replace any Contractor personnel
L0:who jeopardize or interfere with mission accomplishment or who fail to comply with or violate applicable requirements of
L0:this contract. Such action may be taken at the Government’s discretion without prejudice to its rights under any other
L0:provision of this contract, including the Termination for Default clause.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall identify all personnel who occupy a position designated as mission essential and ensure the
L0:continuity of essential Contractor services during designated operations, unless, after consultation with the Contracting
L0:Officer, Contracting Officer’s representative, or local commander, the Contracting Officer directs withdrawal due to
L0:security conditions.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall ensure that Contractor personnel follow the guidance at paragraph (e)(2)(v) of this clause and any
L0:specific Combatant Commander guidance on reporting offenses alleged to have been committed by or against Contractor
L0:personnel to appropriate investigative authorities.
L1:(4) Contractor personnel shall return all U.S. Government-issued identification, to include the Common Access Card, to
L0:appropriate U.S. Government authorities at the end of their deployment (or, for non-CAAF, at the end of their employment
L0:under this contract).
L1:(i) Military clothing and protective equipment.
L1:(1) Contractor personnel are prohibited from wearing military clothing unless specifically authorized in writing by the
L0:Combatant Commander. If authorized to wear military clothing, Contractor personnel must—
L1:(i) Wear distinctive patches, arm bands, nametags, or headgear, in order to be distinguishable from military personnel,
L0:consistent with force protection measures; and
L1:(ii) Carry the written authorization with them at all times.
L1:(2) Contractor personnel may wear military-unique organizational clothing and individual equipment (OCIE) required for
L0:safety and security, such as ballistic, nuclear, biological, or chemical protective equipment.
L1:(3) The deployment center, or the Combatant Commander, shall issue OCIE and shall provide training, if necessary, to
L0:ensure the safety and security of Contractor personnel.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall ensure that all issued OCIE is returned to the point of issue, unless otherwise directed by the
L0:Contracting Officer.
L1:(j) Weapons.
L1:(1) If the Contractor requests that its personnel performing in the designated operational area be authorized to carry
L0:weapons for individual self-defense, the request shall be made through the Contracting Officer to the Combatant
L0:Commander, in accordance with DoD Instruction 3020.41, Operational Contractor Support. The Combatant Commander
L0:will determine whether to authorize in-theater Contractor personnel to carry weapons and what weapons and ammunition
L0:will be allowed.
L1:(2) If Contractor personnel are authorized to carry weapons in accordance with paragraph (j)(1) of this clause, the
L0:Contracting Officer will notify the Contractor what weapons and ammunition are authorized.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall ensure that its personnel who are authorized to carry weapons—
L1:(i) Are adequately trained to carry and use them—
L1:(A) Safely;
L1:(B) With full understanding of, and adherence to, the rules of the use of force issued by the Combatant Commander; and
L1:(C) In compliance with applicable agency policies, agreements, rules, regulations, and other applicable law;
L1:(ii) Are not barred from possession of a firearm by 18 U.S.C. 922;
L1:(iii) Adhere to all guidance and orders issued by the Combatant Commander regarding possession, use, safety, and
L0:accountability of weapons and ammunition;
L1:(iv) Comply with applicable Combatant Commander and local commander force-protection policies; and
L1:(v) Understand that the inappropriate use of force could subject them to U.S. or host-nation prosecution and civil liability.
L1:(4) Whether or not weapons are Government-furnished, all liability for the use of any weapon by Contractor personnel
L0:rests solely with the Contractor and the Contractor employee using such weapon.
L1:(5) Upon redeployment or revocation by the Combatant Commander of the Contractor’s authorization to issue firearms, the
L0:Contractor shall ensure that all Government-issued weapons and unexpended ammunition are returned as directed by the
L0:Contracting Officer.
L1:(k) Vehicle or equipment licenses. Contractor personnel shall possess the required licenses to operate all vehicles or
L0:equipment necessary to perform the contract in the designated operational area.
L1:(l) Purchase of scarce goods and services. If the Combatant Commander has established an organization for the designated
L0:operational area whose function is to determine that certain items are scarce goods or services, the Contractor shall
L0:coordinate with that organization local purchases of goods and services designated as scarce, in accordance with
L0:instructions provided by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(m) Evacuation.
L1:(1) If the Combatant Commander orders a mandatory evacuation of some or all personnel, the Government will provide
L0:assistance, to the extent available, to United States and third country national Contractor personnel.
L1:(2) In the event of a non-mandatory evacuation order, unless authorized in writing by the Contracting Officer, the
L0:Contractor shall maintain personnel on location sufficient to meet obligations under this contract.
L1:(n) Next of kin notification and personnel recovery.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall be responsible for notification of the employee-designated next of kin in the event an employee
L0:dies, requires evacuation due to an injury, or is isolated, missing, detained, captured, or abducted.
L1:(2) In the case of isolated, missing, detained, captured, or abducted Contractor personnel, the Government will assist in
L0:personnel recovery actions in accordance with DoD Directive 3002.01E, Personnel Recovery in the Department of
L0:Defense.
L1:(o) Mortuary affairs. Contractor personnel who die while in support of the U.S. Armed Forces shall be covered by the DoD
L0:mortuary affairs program as described in DoD Directive 1300.22, Mortuary Affairs Policy, and DoD Instruction 3020.41,
L0:Operational Contractor Support.
L1:(p) Changes. In addition to the changes otherwise authorized by the Changes clause of this contract, the Contracting
L0:Officer may, at any time, by written order identified as a change order, make changes in the place of performance or
L0:Government-furnished facilities, equipment, material, services, or site. Any change order issued in accordance with this
L0:paragraph (p) shall be subject to the provisions of the Changes clause of this contract.
L1:(q) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall incorporate the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (q), in all
L0:subcontracts when subcontractor personnel are supporting U.S. Armed Forces deployed outside the United States in—
L1:(1) Contingency operations;
L1:(2) Peace operations consistent with Joint Publication 3-07.3; or
L1:(3) Other military operations or military exercises, when designated by the Combatant Commander or as directed by the
L0:Secretary of Defense.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.225-7040 — Contractor Personnel Supporting U.S. Armed Forces Deployed Outside the United States

title: 252.225-7043 Antiterrorism/Force Protection for Defense Contractors Outside the United States
content:
L0:252.225-7043 Antiterrorism/Force Protection for Defense Contractors Outside the United States.
L0:As prescribed in 225.372-2 , use the following clause:
L0:ANTITERRORISM/FORCE PROTECTION POLICY FOR DEFENSE CONTRACTORS OUTSIDE THE UNITED
L0:STATES (JUN 2015)
L1:(a) Definition. “United States,” as used in this clause, means, the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and outlying areas.
L1:(b) Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this clause, the Contractor and its subcontractors, if performing or traveling
L0:outside the United States under this contract, shall—
L1:(1) Affiliate with the Overseas Security Advisory Council, if the Contractor or subcontractor is a U.S. entity;
L1:(2) Ensure that Contractor and subcontractor personnel who are U.S. nationals and are in-country on a non-transitory basis,
L0:register with the U.S. Embassy, and that Contractor and subcontractor personnel who are third country nationals comply
L0:with any security related requirements of the Embassy of their nationality;
L1:(3) Provide, to Contractor and subcontractor personnel, antiterrorism/force protection awareness information
L0:commensurate with that which the Department of Defense (DoD) provides to its military and civilian personnel and their
L0:families, to the extent such information can be made available prior to travel outside the United States; and
L1:(4) Obtain and comply with the most current antiterrorism/force protection guidance for Contractor and subcontractor
L0:personnel.
L1:(c) The requirements of this clause do not apply to any subcontractor that is—
L1:(1) A foreign government;
L1:(2) A representative of a foreign government; or
L1:(3) A foreign corporation wholly owned by a foreign government.
L1:(d) Information and guidance pertaining to DoD antiterrorism/force protection can be obtained from (Contracting Officer
L0:to insert applicable information cited in PGI 225.372-1 ).
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.225-7043 — Antiterrorism/Force Protection for Defense Contractors Outside the United States

title: 252.225-7044 Balance of Payments Program—Construction Material
content:
L0:252.225-7044 Balance of Payments Program—Construction Material.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 225.7503 (a) and (a)(1), use the following clause:
L0:BALANCE OF PAYMENTS PROGRAM—CONSTRUCTION MATERIAL—BASIC (FEB 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item”—
L1:(1) Means any item of supply (including construction material) that is—
L1:(i) A commercial product (as defined in paragraph (1) of the definition of “commercial product” in section 2.101 of the
L0:Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR));
L1:(ii) Sold in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(iii) Offered to the Government, under a contract or subcontract at any tier, without modification, in the same form in
L0:which it is sold in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(2) Does not include bulk cargo, as defined in 46 U.S.C. 40102(4), such as agricultural products and petroleum products.
L0:“Component” means any article, material, or supply incorporated directly into construction material.
L0:“Construction material” means an article, material, or supply brought to the construction site by the Contractor or a
L0:subcontractor for incorporation into the building or work. The term also includes an item brought to the site preassembled
L0:from articles, materials, or supplies. However, emergency life safety systems, such as emergency lighting, fire alarm, and
L0:audio evacuation systems, that are discrete systems incorporated into a public building or work and that are produced as
L0:complete systems, are evaluated as a single and distinct construction material regardless of when or how the individual
L0:parts or components of those systems are delivered to the construction site. Materials purchased directly by the
L0:Government are supplies, not construction material.
L0:“Cost of components” means—
L1:(1) For components purchased by the Contractor, the acquisition cost, including transportation costs to the place of
L0:incorporation into the end product (whether or not such costs are paid to a domestic firm), and any applicable duty
L0:(whether or not a duty-free entry certificate is issued); or
L1:(2) For components manufactured by the Contractor, all costs associated with the manufacture of the component, including
L0:transportation costs as described in paragraph (1) of this definition, plus allocable overhead costs, but excluding profit.
L0:Cost of components does not include any costs associated with the manufacture of the construction material.
L0:“Critical component” means a component that is mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States and deemed
L0:critical to the U.S. supply chain. The list of critical components is at FAR 25.105.
L0:“Critical item” means domestic construction material or a domestic end product that is deemed critical to the U.S. supply
L0:chain. The list of critical items is at FAR 25.105.
L0:“Domestic construction material” means—
L1:(1) For construction material that does not consist wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both—
L1:(i) An unmanufactured construction material mined or produced in the United States; or
L1:(ii) A construction material manufactured in the United States, if—
L1:(A) The cost of its components mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States exceeds 60 percent of the cost of all
L0:its components, except that the percentage will be 65 percent for items delivered in calendar years 2024 through 2028 and
L0:75 percent for items delivered starting in calendar year 2029, unless an alternate percentage is established for a contract in
L0:accordance with FAR 25.201(c). Components of foreign origin of the same class or kind for which nonavailability
L0:determinations have been made are treated as domestic. Components of unknown origin are treated as foreign; or
L1:(B) The construction material is a COTS item; or
L1:(2) For construction material that consists wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both, a construction
L0:material manufactured in the United States if the cost of iron and steel not produced in the United States (excluding
L0:fasteners) as estimated in good faith by the contractor, constitutes less than 5 percent of the cost of all the components used
L0:in such construction material (produced in the United States means that all manufacturing processes of the iron or steel
L0:must take place in the United States, except metallurgical processes involving refinement of steel additives). The cost of
L0:iron and steel not produced in the United States includes but is not limited to the cost of iron or steel mill products (such as
L0:bar, billet, slab, wire, plate, or sheet), castings, or forgings, not produced in the United States, utilized in the manufacture of
L0:the end product and a good faith estimate of the cost of all iron or steel components not produced in the United States,
L0:excluding COTS fasteners. Iron or steel components of unknown origin are treated as foreign. If the construction material
L0:contains multiple components, the cost of all the materials used in such construction material is calculated in accordance
L0:with the definition of “cost of components” in this clause.
L0:“Predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both” means that the cost of the iron and steel content exceeds 50
L0:percent of the total cost of all its components. The cost of iron and steel is the cost of the iron or steel mill products (such
L0:as bar, billet, slab, wire, plate, or sheet), castings, or forgings utilized in the manufacture of the product and a good faith
L0:estimate of the cost of iron or steel components excluding COTS fasteners.
L0:“Steel” means an alloy that includes at least 50 percent iron, between 0.02 and 2 percent carbon, and may include other
L0:elements.
L0:“United States” means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and outlying areas.
L1:(b) Domestic preference. This clause implements the Balance of Payments Program by providing a preference for domestic
L0:construction material. The Contractor shall use only domestic construction material in performing this contract, except for
L0:—
L1:(1) Construction material valued at or below the simplified acquisition threshold in part 2 of the Federal Acquisition
L0:Regulation;
L1:(2) Information technology that is a commercial product; or
L1:(3) The construction material or components listed by the Government as follows:
L0:___________________________________________________________________________
L0:[Contracting Officer to list applicable excepted materials or indicate “none”]
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Alternate I. As prescribed in 225.7503 (a) and (a)(2), use the following clause, which adds definitions for “South
L0:Caucasus/Central and South Asian (SC/CASA) state” and “SC/CASA state construction material” to paragraph (a), and
L0:uses “domestic construction material or SC/CASA state construction material” instead of “domestic construction material”
L0:in the second sentence of paragraph (b):
L0:BALANCE OF PAYMENTS PROGRAM—CONSTRUCTION MATERIAL—ALTERNATE I (FEB 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item”—
L1:(1) Means any item of supply (including construction material) that is—
L1:(i) A commercial product (as defined in paragraph (1) of the definition of “commercial product” in section 2.101 of the
L0:Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR));
L1:(ii) Sold in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(iii) Offered to the Government, under a contract or subcontract at any tier, without modification, in the same form in
L0:which it is sold in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(2) Does not include bulk cargo, as defined in 46 U.S.C. 40102(4), such as agricultural products and petroleum products.
L0:“Component” means any article, material, or supply incorporated directly into construction material.
L0:“Construction material” means an article, material, or supply brought to the construction site by the Contractor or a
L0:subcontractor for incorporation into the building or work. The term also includes an item brought to the site preassembled
L0:from articles, materials, or supplies. However, emergency life safety systems, such as emergency lighting, fire alarm, and
L0:audio evacuation systems, that are discrete systems incorporated into a public building or work and that are produced as
L0:complete systems, are evaluated as a single and distinct construction material regardless of when or how the individual

title: 252.225-7048 Export-Controlled Items., Export-Controlled Items, clause of this contract
content:
L0:252.225-7048 Export-Controlled Items., Export-Controlled Items, clause of this contract.
L0:“Ineligible transferee” means an individual, an entity, or a country—
L1:(1) Excluded from Federal programs by the General Services Administration as identified in the System for Award
L0:Management Exclusions located at https://sam.gov;
L1:(2) Delinquent on obligations to the U.S. Government under surplus sales contracts;
L1:(3) Designated by the Department of Defense as ineligible, debarred, or suspended from defense contracts; or
L1:(4) Subject to denial, debarment, or other sanctions under export control laws and related laws and regulations, and orders
L0:administered by the Department of State, the Department of Commerce, the Department of Homeland Security, or the
L0:Department of the Treasury.
L0:“Item unique identification” means a system of assigning, reporting, and marking DoD property with unique item
L0:identifiers that have machine-readable data elements to distinguish an item from all other like and unlike items.
L0:“National stock number” means a 13-digit stock number used to identify items of supply. It consists of a four-digit Federal
L0:Supply Code and a nine-digit National Item Identification Number.
L0:“Reparable item” means an item, typically in unserviceable condition, furnished to the contractor for maintenance, repair,
L0:modification, or overhaul.
L0:“Scrap” means property that has no value except for its basic material content. For purposes of demilitarization, scrap is
L0:defined as recyclable waste and discarded materials derived from items that have been rendered useless beyond repair,
L0:rehabilitation, or restoration such that the item’s original identity, utility, form, fit, and function have been destroyed. Items
L0:can be classified as scrap if processed by cutting, tearing, crushing, mangling, shredding, or melting. Intact or recognizable
L0:components and parts are not “scrap.”
L0:“Serially-managed item” means an item designated by DoD to be uniquely tracked, controlled, or managed in maintenance,
L0:repair, and/or supply systems by means of its serial number or unique item identifier.
L0:“Serviceable or usable property” means property with potential for reutilization or sale as is or with minor repairs or
L0:alterations. “Supply condition code” means a classification of materiel in terms of readiness for issue and use or to identify
L0:action underway to change the status of materiel. “Unique item identifier (UII)” means a set of data elements marked on an
L0:item that is globally unique and unambiguous. The term includes a concatenated UII or a DoD recognized unique
L0:identification equivalent.
L1:(b) Reporting Government property.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall use the Government Furnished Property (GFP) module of the Procurement Integrated Enterprise
L0:Environment (PIEE) to—
L1:(i) Report receipt of GFP; (ii) Report the transfer of GFP to another DoD contract;
L1:(iii) Report the shipment of GFP to the Government or to a contractor. The GFP module generates the electronic equivalent
L0:of the DD Form 1149, DD Form 1348-1, or other required shipping documents;
L1:(iv) Report when serially-managed items of GFP are incorporated into a higher-level component, assembly, or end item;
L1:(v) Report the loss of Government property in accordance with paragraph (f)(1)(vii) of the FAR 52.245-1 clause of this
L0:contract;
L1:(vi) Complete the plant clearance inventory schedule in accordance with paragraph (j)(2) of the FAR 52.245-1 clause of
L0:this contract, unless disposition instructions are otherwise included in this contract. The GFP module generates the
L0:electronic equivalent of the Standard Form (SF) 1428, Inventory Disposal Schedule; and (vii) Submit a request to buy back
L0:or to convert to GFP items of Contractor-acquired property.
L1:(2) Information regarding the GFP module is available in the GFP Module Vendor Guide at
L0:https://dodprocurementtoolbox.com/site-pages/gfp-resources. Users may also register for access to the GFP module and
L0:obtain training on the PIEE home page at https://piee.eb.mil.
L1:(3) In complying with paragraphs (b)(1)(i) through (iv) of this clause, the Contractor shall report the updated status of the
L0:property to the GFP module within 7 business days of the date the change in status occurs, unless otherwise specified in the
L0:contract.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall use Wide Area WorkFlow in accordance with DFARS Appendix F, Material Inspection and
L0:Receiving Report, to report the shipment of reparable items after completion of repair, maintenance, modification, or
L0:overhaul.
L1:(5) When Government property is in the possession of subcontractors, the Contractor shall ensure that reporting is
L0:accomplished using the data elements required in paragraph (c) of this clause.
L1:(c) Records of Government property. To facilitate reporting of Government property to the GFP module, the Contractor’s
L0:property records, in addition to the requirements of paragraph (f)(1)(iii) of the FAR 52.245-1 clause of this contract, shall
L0:enable recording of the following data elements:
L1:(1) National stock number (NSN). If an NSN is not available, use either the combination of the manufacturer’s CAGE code
L0:and part number, or model number.
L1:(2) CAGE code on the accountable Government contract.
L1:(3) Received/sent (shipped) date.
L1:(4) Accountable Government contract number.
L1:(5) Serial number (for serially-managed items that do not have a UII); and
L1:(6) Supply condition code (only required for reporting of reparable items). For information on Federal supply condition
L0:codes, see DLM 4000.25, Defense Logistics Management Standards (DLMS), Volume 2, Supply Standards and
L0:Procedures, Appendix 2.5 at https://www.dla.mil/HQ/InformationOperations/DLMS/elibrary/manuals/v2/.
L1:(d) Marking, reporting, and UII registration of GFP requirements. The Contractor—
L1:(1) Shall assign the UII and mark the reparable items identified as serially managed in the GFP attachment to this contract
L0:with an item unique identification (IUID) data matrix, when the technical drawing for the item is accessible to the
L0:Contractor and includes IUID data matrix location and marking method;
L1:(2) Shall report the UII either before or during shipment of the repaired item;
L1:(3) Is not required to mark items that were previously marked with an IUID data matrix and registered in accordance with
L0:DFARS 252.211-7003 Item Unique Identification and Valuation., Item Unique Identification and Valuation; and
L1:(4) Shall assign a new UII, then mark and register the item, when the conditions of paragraph (d)(1) are met, if an item is
L0:found to be marked but not registered in the IUID Registry.
L1:(e) Disposing of Government property.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall complete the plant clearance inventory schedule using the plant clearance capability of the GFP
L0:module of the PIEE to generate an electronic equivalent of the SF 1428, Inventory Disposal Schedule. The plant clearance
L0:inventory schedule requires the following:
L1:(i) If known, the applicable Federal supply code (FSC) for all items, except items in scrap condition.
L1:(ii) If known, the manufacturer name for all aircraft components under Federal supply group 16 or 17 and FSCs 2620,
L0:2810, 2915, 2925, 2935, 2945, 2995, 4920, 5821, 5826, 5841, 6340, and 6615.
L1:(iii) The manufacturer name, make, model number, model year, and serial number for all aircraft under FSCs 1510 and
L0:1520.
L1:(2) If the schedules are acceptable, the plant clearance officer will confirm acceptance in the GFP module plant clearance
L0:capability, which will transmit a notification to the Contractor. The electronic acceptance is equivalent to the DD Form
L0:1637, Notice of Acceptance of Inventory.
L1:(f) Demilitarization, mutilation, and destruction. If demilitarization, mutilation, or destruction of contractor inventory is
L0:required, the Contractor shall demilitarize, mutilate, or destroy contractor inventory, in accordance with the terms and
L0:conditions of the contract and consistent with Defense Demilitarization Manual, DoD Manual (DoDM) 4160.28-M, edition
L0:in effect as of the date of this contract. If the property is available for purchase, the plant clearance officer may authorize
L0:the purchaser to demilitarize, mutilate, or destroy as a condition of sale provided the property is not inherently dangerous to
L0:public health and safety.
L1:(g) Classified Contractor inventory. The Contractor shall dispose of classified contractor inventory in accordance with
L0:applicable security guides and regulations or as directed by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(h) Inherently dangerous Contractor inventory. Contractor inventory that is dangerous to public health or safety shall not
L0:be disposed of unless rendered innocuous or until adequate safeguards are provided.
L1:(i) Contractor inventory located in foreign countries. Consistent with contract terms and conditions, property disposition
L0:shall be in accordance with foreign and U.S. laws and regulations, including laws and regulations involving export
L0:controls, host nation requirements, final governing standards, and government-to-government agreements. The Contractor's
L0:responsibility to comply with all applicable laws and regulations regarding export-controlled items exists independent of,
L0:and is not established or limited by, the information provided by this clause.
L1:(j) Disposal of scrap.
L1:(1) Contractor scrap procedures.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall include, within its property management procedure, a process for the accountability and
L0:management of Government-owned scrap. The process shall, at a minimum, provide for the effective and efficient
L0:disposition of scrap, including sales to scrap dealers, so as to minimize costs, maximize sales proceeds, and contain the
L0:necessary internal controls for mitigating the improper release of non-scrap property.
L1:(ii) The Contractor may commingle Government and contractor-owned scrap and provide routine disposal of scrap, with
L0:plant clearance officer concurrence, when determined to be effective and efficient.
L1:(2) Scrap warranty. The plant clearance officer may require the Contractor to secure from scrap buyers a DD Form 1639,
L0:Scrap Warranty.
L1:(k) Sale of surplus Contractor inventory.
L1:(1) Sales procedures.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall conduct sales of contractor inventory (both useable property and scrap) in accordance with the
L0:requirements of this contract and plant clearance officer direction. The Contractor shall include in its invitation for bids the
L0:sales terms and conditions provided by the plant clearance officer.
L1:(ii) The Contractor may conduct internet-based sales, to include use of a third party.
L1:(iii) If the Contractor wishes to bid on the sale, the Contractor or its employees shall submit bids to the plant clearance
L0:officer prior to soliciting bids from other prospective bidders.
L1:(iv) The Contractor shall solicit bids to obtain adequate competition. Negotiated sales are subject to obtaining such
L0:competition as is feasible under the circumstances of the negotiated sale.
L1:(v) The Contractor shall solicit bids at least 15 calendar days before bid opening to allow adequate opportunity to inspect
L0:the property and prepare bids.
L1:(vi) For large sales, the Contractor may use summary lists of items offered as bid sheets with detailed descriptions attached.
L1:(vii) In addition to providing notice of the proposed sale to prospective bidders, the Contractor may, when the results are
L0:expected to justify the additional expense, display a notice of the proposed sale in appropriate public places, e.g., publish a
L0:sales notice on the internet, in appropriate trade journals or magazines, and in local newspapers.
L1:(viii) The plant clearance officer or designated Government representative will witness the bid opening. The Contractor
L0:shall submit the bid abstract in electronic format to the plant clearance officer within 2 days of bid opening. If the
L0:Contractor is unable to submit the bid abstract electronically, the Contractor may submit 2 copies of the abstract manually
L0:within 2 days of bid opening. The plant clearance officer will not approve award to any bidder who is an ineligible
L0:transferee.
L1:(2) Required terms and conditions for sales contracts. The Contractor shall include the following terms and conditions in
L0:sales contracts:
L1:(i) For sales contracts or other documents transferring title: “The Purchaser certifies that the property covered by this
L0:contract will be used in [insert name of country]. In the event of resale or export by the Purchaser of any of the property,
L0:the Purchaser agrees to obtain the appropriate U.S. and foreign export or re-export license approval.”
L1:(ii) For sales contracts that require demilitarization, mutilation, or destruction of property:
L0:“The following items [insert list provided by plant clearance officer] require demilitarization, mutilation, or destruction by
L0:the Purchaser. Additional instructions are provided in accordance with Defense Demilitarization Manual, DoDM 4160.28M, edition in effect as of the date of this sales contract. A Government representative will certify and verify
L0:demilitarization of items. Prepare demilitarization certificates in accordance with DoDM 4160.28, Volume 2, section 4.5,
L0:DEMIL Certificate (see figure 2, Example DEMIL Certificate).”
L1:(iii) Removal and title transfer:
L0:“Property requiring demilitarization shall not be removed, and title shall not pass to the Purchaser, until demilitarization
L0:has been accomplished and verified by a Government representative.”
L1:(iv) Assumption of cost incident to demilitarization:
L0:“The Purchaser agrees to assume all costs incident to the demilitarization and to restore the working area to its present
L0:condition after removing the demilitarized property.”
L1:(v) Failure to demilitarize:
L0:“If the Purchaser fails to demilitarize, mutilate, or destroy the property as specified in the sales contract, the Contractor
L0:may, upon giving 10 days written notice to the Purchaser—
L1:(A) Repossess, demilitarize, and return the property to the Purchaser, in which case the Purchaser hereby agrees to pay to
L0:the Contractor, prior to the return of the property, all costs incurred by the Contractor in repossessing, demilitarizing, and
L0:returning the property;
L1:(B) Repossess, demilitarize, and resell the property, and charge the defaulting Purchaser with all costs incurred by the
L0:Contractor. The Contractor shall deduct these costs from the purchase price and refund the balance of the purchase price, if
L0:any, to the Purchaser. In the event the costs exceed the purchase price, the defaulting Purchaser hereby agrees to pay these
L0:costs to the Contractor; or
L1:(C) Repossess and resell the property under similar terms and conditions, and charge the defaulting Purchaser with all costs
L0:incurred by the Contractor. The Contractor shall deduct these costs from the original purchase price and refund the balance
L0:of the purchase price, if any, to the defaulting Purchaser. Should the excess costs to the Contractor exceed the purchase
L0:price, the defaulting Purchaser hereby agrees to pay these costs to the Contractor.”
L1:(l) Restrictions on purchase or retention of Contractor inventory. The Contractor may not knowingly sell the inventory to
L0:any person or that person's agent, employee, or household member if that person—
L1:(1) Is a civilian employee of DoD or the U.S. Coast Guard;
L1:(2) Is a member of the Armed Forces of the United States, including the U.S. Coast Guard; or
L1:(3) Has any functional or supervisory responsibilities for or within DoD's property disposal, disposition, or plant clearance
L0:programs or for the disposal of contractor inventory.
L1:(m) Proceeds from sales of surplus property. Unless otherwise provided in the contract, the proceeds of any sale, purchase,
L0:or retention shall be—
L1:(1) Forwarded to the Contracting Officer;
L1:(2) Credited to the Government as part of the settlement agreement pursuant to the termination of the contract;
L1:(3) Credited to the price or cost of the contract; or
L1:(4) Applied as otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.225-7049 Prohibition on Acquisition of Certain Foreign Commercial Satellite Services—Representations
content:
L0:252.225-7049 Prohibition on Acquisition of Certain Foreign Commercial Satellite Services—Representations.
L0:As prescribed in 225.772-5 (a),use the following provision:
L0:PROHIBITION ON ACQUISITION OF CERTAIN FOREIGN COMMERCIAL SATELLITE SERVICES—
L0:REPRESENTATIONS (DEC 2018)
L1:(a) Definitions.As used in this provision—
L0:“Covered foreign country,” “foreign entity,” “government of a covered foreign country,” “launch vehicle,” “satellite
L0:services,” and “state sponsor of terrorism” are defined in the clause at Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement
L1:(DFARS) 252.225-7051 , Prohibition on Acquisition of Certain Commercial Satellite Services.
L0:"Cybersecurity risk" means threats to and vulnerabilities of information or information systems and any related
L0:consequences caused by or resulting from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, degradation, disruption, modification, or
L0:destruction of such information or information systems, including such related consequences caused by an act of terrorism.
L0:(10 U.S.C. 2279)
L1:(b) Prohibition on award. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2279, unless an exception is determined to apply in accordance
L0:with DFARS 225.772-4 , no contract for commercial satellite services may be awarded to—
L1:(1)(i) A foreign entity if the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment or the Under Secretary of
L0:Defense for Policy reasonably believes that—
L1:(A) The foreign entity is an entity in which the government of a covered foreign country has an ownership interest that
L0:enables the government to affect satellite operations;
L1:(B) The foreign entity plans to, or is expected to, provide or use launch or other satellite services under the contract from a
L0:covered foreign country; or
L1:(C) Entering into such contract would create an unacceptable cybersecurity risk for DoD; or
L1:(ii) An offeror that is offering to provide the commercial satellite services of a foreign entity as described in paragraph (b)
L1:(1) of this section; or
L1:(2)(i) Any entity, except as provided in paragraph (b)(2)(ii) of this provision, for a launch that occurs on or after December
L0:31, 2022, if the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment or the Under Secretary of Defense for Policy
L0:reasonably believes that such satellite service will be provided using satellites that will be—
L1:(A) Designed or manufactured—
L1:(1) In a covered foreign country; or
L1:(2) By an entity controlled in whole or in part by, or acting on behalf of, the government of a covered foreign country; or
L1:(B) Launched outside the United States, using a launch vehicle that is—
L1:(1) Designed or manufactured in a covered foreign country; or
L1:(2) Provided by—
L1:(i) The government of a covered foreign country; or
L1:(ii) An entity controlled in whole or in part by, or acting on behalf of, the government of a covered foreign country.
L1:(ii) The prohibition in paragraph (b)(2)(i)(B) of this provision does not apply with respect to launch vehicles for which the
L0:satellite service provider has a contract or other agreement relating to launch services that, prior to June 10, 2018, was
L0:either fully paid for by the satellite service provider or covered by a legally binding commitment of the satellite service
L0:provider to pay for such services.
L1:(c) Representations. The Offeror represents that—
L1:(1) It [ ] is, [ ] is not a foreign entity in which the government of a covered foreign country has an ownership interest that
L0:enables the government to affect satellite operations. If affirmative, identify the covered foreign country:_________;
L1:(2) It [ ] is, [ ] is not a foreign entity that plans to provide satellite services under the contract from a covered foreign
L0:country. If affirmative, identify the covered foreign country:___________;
L1:(3) It [ ] is, [ ] is not offering commercial satellite services provided by a foreign entity in which the government of a
L0:covered foreign country has an ownership interest that enables the government to affect satellite operations. If affirmative,
L0:identify the foreign entity and the covered foreign country:__________;
L1:(4) It [ ] is, [ ] is not offering commercial satellite services provided by a foreign entity that plans to or is expected to
L0:provide satellite services under the contract from a covered foreign country. If affirmative, identify the foreign entity and
L0:the covered foreign country:__________;
L1:(5) It [ ] is, [ ] is not offering commercial satellite services that will use satellites, launched on or after December 31, 2022,
L0:that will be designed or manufactured in a covered foreign country. If affirmative, identify the covered foreign
L0:country:____________;
L1:(6) It [ ] is, [ ] is not offering commercial satellite services that will use satellites, launched on or after December 31, 2022,
L0:that will be designed or manufactured by an entity controlled in whole or in part by, or acting on behalf of, the government
L0:of a covered foreign country. If affirmative, identify the entity, the covered foreign country, and the relationship of the
L0:entity to the government of the covered foreign country:_______________;
L1:(7) It [ ] is, [ ] is not offering commercial satellite services that will use satellites, launched outside the United States on or
L0:after December 31, 2022, using a launch vehicle that is designed or manufactured in a covered foreign country. If
L0:affirmative, identify the covered foreign country:____________;
L1:(8) It [ ] is, [ ] is not offering commercial satellite services that will use satellites, launched outside the United States on or

L0:affirmative, identify the covered foreign country:________________; and

L1:(1) The entity awarded the contract or other agreement:_____________.
L1:(2) The date the contract or other agreement was awarded:___________.
L1:(3) The period of performance for the contract or other agreement:____________.

title: 252.225-7050 Disclosure of Ownership or Control by the Government of a Country that is a State Sponsor of
content:
L0:252.225-7050 Disclosure of Ownership or Control by the Government of a Country that is a State Sponsor of
L0:Terrorism.
L0:As prescribed in 225.771-5, use the following provision:
L0:DISCLOSURE OF OWNERSHIP OR CONTROL BY THE GOVERNMENT OF A COUNTRY THAT IS A STATE
L0:SPONSOR OF TERRORISM (DEC 2022)
L1:(a) Definitions.As used in this provision—
L0:“Government of a country that is a state sponsor of terrorism” includes the state and the government of a country that is a
L0:state sponsor of terrorism, as well as any political subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof.
L0:“Significant interest” means—
L1:(1) Ownership of or beneficial interest in 5 percent or more of the firm’s or subsidiary’s securities. Beneficial interest
L0:includes holding 5 percent or more of any class of the firm’s securities in “nominee shares,” “street names,” or some other
L0:method of holding securities that does not disclose the beneficial owner;
L1:(2) Holding a management position in the firm, such as a director or officer;
L1:(3) Ability to control or influence the election, appointment, or tenure of directors or officers in the firm;
L1:(4) Ownership of 10 percent or more of the assets of a firm such as equipment, buildings, real estate, or other tangible
L0:assets of the firm; or
L1:(5) Holding 50 percent or more of the indebtedness of a firm.
L0:“State sponsor of terrorism” means a country determined by the Secretary of State, under section 1754(c)(1)(A)(i) of the
L0:Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (Title XVII, Subtitle B, of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year
L0:2019, Pub. L. 115-232), to be a country the government of which has repeatedly provided support for acts of international
L0:terrorism. As of the date of this provision, state sponsors of terrorism include Iran, North Korea, Sudan, and Syria.
L1:(b) Prohibition on award. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 4871, unless a waiver is granted by the Secretary of Defense, no
L0:contract may be awarded to a firm if the government of a country that is a state sponsor of terrorism owns or controls a
L0:significant interest in—
L1:(1) The firm;
L1:(2) A subsidiary of the firm; or
L1:(3) Any other firm that owns or controls the firm.
L1:(c) Representation.Unless the Offeror submits with its offer the disclosure required in paragraph (d) of this provision, the
L0:Offeror represents, by submission of its offer, that the government of a country that is a state sponsor of terrorism does not
L0:own or control a significant interest in—
L1:(1) The Offeror;
L1:(2) A subsidiary of the Offeror; or
L1:(3) Any other firm that owns or controls the Offeror.
L1:(d) Disclosure.
L1:(1) The Offeror shall disclose in an attachment to its offer if the government of a country that is a state sponsor of terrorism
L0:owns or controls a significant interest in the Offeror; a subsidiary of the Offeror; or any other firm that owns or controls the
L0:Offeror.
L1:(2) The disclosure shall include—
L1:(i) Identification of each government holding a significant interest; and
L1:(ii) A description of the significant interest held by each government.
L0:(End of provision)

title: 252.225-7051 Prohibition on Acquisition of Certain Foreign Commercial Satellite Services
content:
L0:252.225-7051 Prohibition on Acquisition of Certain Foreign Commercial Satellite Services.
L0:As prescribed in 225.772-5, use the following clause:
L0:PROHIBITION ON ACQUISITION OF CERTAIN FOREIGN COMMERCIAL SATELLITE SERVICES (DEC 2022)
L1:(a) Definitions.As used in this clause—
L0:“Covered foreign country” means—
L1:(1) The People’s Republic of China;
L1:(2) North Korea;
L1:(3) The Russian Federation; or
L1:(4) Any country that is a state sponsor of terrorism. (10 U.S.C. 2279)
L0:“Foreign entity” means—

L0:organization organized under the laws of a foreign state if either its principal place of business is outside the United States
L0:or its equity securities are primarily traded on one or more foreign exchanges.

L0:corporation or division of a corporation, or organization that demonstrates that a majority of the equity interest in such

L0:“Government of a covered foreign country” includes the state and the government of a covered foreign country, as well as
L0:any political subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof.
L0:“Launch vehicle” means a fully integrated space launch vehicle. (10 U.S.C. 2279)
L0:“Satellite services” means communications capabilities that utilize an on-orbit satellite for transmitting the signal from one
L0:location to another.
L0:“State sponsor of terrorism” means a country determined by the Secretary of State, under section 1754(c)(1)(A)(i) of the
L0:Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (Title XVII, Subtitle B, of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year
L0:2019, Pub. L. 115-232)], to be a country the government of which has repeatedly provided support for acts of international
L0:terrorism. As of the date of this provision, state sponsors of terrorism include Iran, North Korea, Sudan, and Syria. (10
L0:U.S.C. 4871)
L1:(b) Limitation. Unless specified in its offer, the Contractor shall not provide satellite services under this contract that—
L1:(1) Are from a covered foreign country; or
L1:(2) Except as provided in paragraph (c), use satellites that will be(i) Designed or manufactured—
L1:(A) In a covered foreign country; or
L1:(B) By an entity controlled in whole or in part by, or acting on behalf of, the government of a covered foreign country; or
L1:(ii) Launched outside the United States using a launch vehicle that is designed or manufactured—
L1:(A) In a covered foreign country; or
L1:(B) Provided by—
