title: 252.225-7052 Restriction on the Acquisition of Certain Magnets, Tantalum, and Tungsten
content:
L0:252.225-7052 Restriction on the Acquisition of Certain Magnets, Tantalum, and Tungsten.
L0:As prescribed in 225.7018-5 , use the following clause:
L0:Restriction on the Acquisition of Certain Magnets, Tantalum, and Tungsten (MAY 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Assembly” means an item forming a portion of a system or subsystem that—
L1:(1) Can be provisioned and replaced as an entity; and
L1:(2) Incorporates multiple, replaceable parts.
L0:“Commercially available off-the-shelf item”—
L1:(1) Means any item of supply that is—
L1:(i) A commercial product (as defined in paragraph (1) of the definition of “commercial product” in section 2.101 of the
L0:Federal Acquisition Regulation);
L1:(ii) Sold in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(iii) Offered to the Government, under this contract or a subcontract at any tier, without modification, in the same form in
L0:which it is sold in the commercial marketplace; and
L1:(2) Does not include bulk cargo, as defined in 46 U.S.C. 40102(4), such as agricultural products and petroleum products.
L0:“Component” means any item supplied to the Government as part of an end item or of another component.
L0:“Covered country” means—
L1:(1) The Democratic People’s Republic of North Korea;
L1:(2) The People’s Republic of China;
L1:(3) The Russian Federation; or
L1:(4) The Islamic Republic of Iran.
L0:“Covered material” means—
L1:(1) Samarium-cobalt magnets;
L1:(2) Neodymium-iron-boron magnets;
L1:(3) Tantalum metals and alloys;
L0:( 4 ) Tungsten metal powder; and
L0:( 5 ) Tungsten heavy alloy or any finished or semi-finished component containing tungsten heavy alloy.
L0:“Electronic device” means an item that operates by controlling the flow of electrons or other electrically charged particles
L0:in circuits, using interconnections such as resistors, inductors, capacitors, diodes, switches, transistors, or integrated
L0:circuits.
L0:“End item” means the final production product when assembled or completed and ready for delivery under a line item of
L0:this contract.
L0:“Subsystem” means a functional grouping of items that combine to perform a major function within an end item, such as
L0:electrical power, attitude control, and propulsion.
L0:“Tungsten heavy alloy” means a tungsten base pseudo alloy that—
L1:(1) Meets the specifications of ASTM B777 or SAE-AMS-T-21014 for a particular class of tungsten heavy alloy; or
L1:(2) Contains at least 90 percent tungsten in a matrix of other metals (such as nickel-iron or nickel-copper) and has density
L0:of at least 16.5 g/cm3).
L1:(b) Restriction.
L1:(1) Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this clause,—
L1:(i) Effective through December 31, 2026, the Contractor shall not deliver under this contract any covered material melted
L0:or produced in any covered country, or any end item, manufactured in any covered country, that contains a covered
L0:material (10 U.S.C. 4872).
L1:(ii) Effective January 1, 2027, the Contractor shall not deliver under this contract any covered material mined, refined,
L0:separated, melted, or produced in any covered country, or any end item, manufactured in any covered country, that contains
L0:a covered material (section 854, Pub. L. 118-31; 10 U.S.C. 4872).
L1:(2)(i)(A) Effective through December 31, 2026, for samarium-cobalt magnets and neodymium-iron-boron magnets, this
L0:restriction includes—
L0:( 1 ) Melting samarium with cobalt to produce the samarium-cobalt alloy or melting neodymium with iron and boron to
L0:produce the neodymium-iron-boron alloy; and
L0:( 2 ) All subsequent phases of production of the magnets, such as powder formation, pressing, sintering or bonding, and
L0:magnetization.
L1:(B) Effective January 1, 2027, for samarium-cobalt magnets this restriction includes the entire supply chain from mining or
L0:production of a cobalt and samarium ore or feedstock, including recycled material, through production of finished magnets.
L1:(ii) The restriction on melting and producing of samarium-cobalt magnets is in addition to any applicable restrictions on
L0:melting of specialty metals if the clause at 252.225-7009 , Restriction on Acquisition of Certain Articles Containing
L0:Specialty Metals, is included in the contract.
L1:(3) Effective January 1, 2027, for neodymium-iron-boron magnets, this restriction includes the entire supply chain from
L0:mining of neodymium, iron, and boron through production of finished magnets.
L1:(4)(i) Effective through December 31, 2026, for production of tantalum metals of any kind and alloys, this restriction
L0:includes the reduction or melting of any form of tantalum to create tantalum metal including unwrought, powder, mill
L0:products, and alloys. The restriction also covers all subsequent phases of production of tantalum metals and alloys.
L1:(ii) Effective January 1, 2027, for production of tantalum metals of any kind and alloys, this restriction includes mining or
L0:production of a tantalum ore or feedstock, including recycled material, through production of metals of any kind and
L0:alloys.
L1:(5)(i) Effective through December 31, 2026, for production of tungsten metal powder and tungsten heavy alloy, this
L0:restriction includes-
L1:(A) Atomization;
L1:(B) Calcination and reduction into powder;
L1:(C) Final consolidation of non-melt derived metal powders; and
L1:(D) All subsequent phases of production of tungsten metal powder, tungsten heavy alloy, or any finished or semi-finished
L0:component containing tungsten heavy alloy.
L1:(ii) Effective January 1, 2027, for production of tungsten metal powder, tungsten heavy alloy, or any finished or semifinished component containing tungsten heavy alloy, this restriction includes mining or production of a tungsten ore or
L0:feedstock, including recycled material, through production of tungsten metal powders, tungsten heavy alloy, or any
L0:finished or semi-finished component containing tungsten heavy alloy.
L1:(c) Exceptions. This clause does not apply—
L1:(1) To an end item containing a covered material that is—
L1:(i) A commercially available off-the-shelf item, other than—
L1:(A) A commercially available off-the-shelf item that is—
L1:(1) 50 percent or more tungsten by weight effective through December 31, 2026; or
L1:(2) 50 percent or more covered material by weight effective January 1, 2027;
L1:(B) Effective through December 31, 2026, a tantalum metal, tantalum alloy, or tungsten heavy alloy, such as bar, billet,
L0:slab, wire, cube, sphere, block, blank, plate, or sheet, that has not been incorporated into an end item, subsystem, assembly,
L0:or component;
L1:(ii) Effective January 1, 2027, a covered material that is a mill product, such as bar, billet, slab, wire, cube, sphere, block,
L0:blank, plate, or sheet, that has not been incorporated into an end item, subsystem, assembly, or component;
L1:(iii)An electronic device, unless otherwise specified in the contract; or
L1:(iv) A neodymium-iron-boron magnet manufactured from recycled material if the milling of the recycled material and
L0:sintering of the final magnet takes place in the United States.
L1:(2) If the authorized agency official concerned has made a nonavailability determination, in accordance with section
L0:225.7018-4 of the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement, that compliant covered materials of satisfactory
L0:quality and quantity, in the required form, cannot be procured as and when needed at a reasonable price.
L1:(i) For tantalum metal, tantalum alloy, or tungsten heavy alloy, the term “required form” refers to the form of the mill
L0:product, such as bar, billet, wire, slab, plate, or sheet, in the grade appropriate for the production of a finished end item to
L0:be delivered to the Government under this contract; or a finished component assembled into an end item to be delivered to
L0:the Government under the contract.(ii) For samarium-cobalt magnets or neodymium-iron-boron magnets, the term
L0:“required form” refers to the form and properties of the magnets.
L1:(d) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall insert the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (d), in subcontracts and
L0:other contractual instruments that are for items containing a covered material, including subcontracts and other contractual
L0:instruments for commercial products, unless an exception in paragraph (c) of this clause applies. The Contractor shall not
L0:alter this clause other than to identify the appropriate parties.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.225-7052 — Restriction on the Acquisition of Certain Magnets, Tantalum, and Tungsten

title: 252.226-7001 Utilization of Indian Organizations, Indian-Owned Economic Enterprises, and Native Hawaiian Small
content:
L0:252.226-7001 Utilization of Indian Organizations, Indian-Owned Economic Enterprises, and Native Hawaiian Small
L0:Business Concerns.
L0:As prescribed in 226.104 , use the following clause:
L0:UTILIZATION OF INDIAN ORGANIZATIONS, INDIAN-OWNED ECONOMIC ENTERPRISES, AND NATIVE
L0:HAWAIIAN SMALL BUSINESS CONCERNS (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Indian” means—
L1:(1) Any person who is a member of any Indian tribe, band, group, pueblo, or community that is recognized by the Federal
L0:Government as eligible for services from the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) in accordance with 25 U.S.C. 1452(c); and
L1:(2) Any “Native” as defined in the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (43 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.).
L0:“Indian organization” means the governing body of any Indian tribe or entity established or recognized by the governing
L0:body of an Indian tribe for the purposes of 25 U.S.C. Chapter 17.
L0:“Indian-owned economic enterprise” means any Indian-owned (as determined by the Secretary of the Interior) commercial,
L0:industrial, or business activity established or organized for the purpose of profit, provided that Indian ownership constitutes
L0:not less than 51 percent of the enterprise.
L0:“Indian tribe” means any Indian tribe, band, group, pueblo, or community, including native villages and native groups
L0:(including corporations organized by Kenai, Juneau, Sitka, and Kodiak) as defined in the Alaska Native Claims Settlement
L0:Act, that is recognized by the Federal Government as eligible for services from BIA in accordance with 25 U.S.C. 1452(c).
L0:“Interested party” means a contractor or an actual or prospective offeror whose direct economic interest would be affected
L0:by the award of a subcontract or by the failure to award a subcontract.
L0:“Native Hawaiian small business concern” means an entity that is—
L1:(1) A small business concern as defined in Section 3 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632) and relevant implementing
L0:regulations; and
L1:(2) Owned and controlled by a Native Hawaiian as defined in 25 U.S.C. 4221(9).
L1:(b) The Contractor shall use its best efforts to give Indian organizations, Indian-owned economic enterprises, and Native
L0:Hawaiian small business concerns the maximum practicable opportunity to participate in the subcontracts it awards, to the
L0:fullest extent consistent with efficient performance of the contract.
L1:(c) The Contracting Officer and the Contractor, acting in good faith, may rely on the representation of an Indian
L0:organization, Indian-owned economic enterprise, or Native Hawaiian small business concern as to its eligibility, unless an
L0:interested party challenges its status or the Contracting Officer has independent reason to question that status.
L1:(d) In the event of a challenge to the representation of a subcontractor, the Contracting Officer will refer the matter to—
L1:(1)(i) For matters relating to Indian organizations or Indian-owned economic enterprises:
L0:U.S. Department of the Interior
L0:Bureau of Indian Affairs
L0:Attn: Bureau Procurement Chief
L0:12220 Sunrise Valley Drive
L0:Reston, VA 20191
L0:Phone: 703-390-6433
L0:Website: https://www.bia.gov/
L1:(ii) The BIA will determine the eligibility and will notify the Contracting Officer.
L1:(2)(i) For matters relating to Native Hawaiian small business concerns:
L0:Department of Hawaiian Home Lands
L0:PO Box 1879
L0:Honolulu, HI 96805
L0:Phone: 808-620-9500
L0:Website: http://dhhl.hawaii.gov/
L1:(ii) The Department of Hawaiian Home Lands will determine the eligibility and will notify the Contracting Officer.
L1:(e) No incentive payment will be made—
L1:(1) While a challenge is pending; or
L1:(2) If a subcontractor is determined to be an ineligible participant.
L1:(f)(1) The Contractor, on its own behalf or on behalf of a subcontractor at any tier, may request an incentive payment in
L0:accordance with this clause.
L1:(2) The incentive amount that may be requested is 5 percent of the estimated cost, target cost, or fixed price included in the
L0:subcontract at the time of award to the Indian organization, Indian-owned economic enterprise, or Native Hawaiian small
L0:business concern.
L1:(3) In the case of a subcontract for commercial products or commercial services, the Contractor may receive an incentive
L0:payment only if the subcontracted items are produced or manufactured in whole or in part by an Indian organization,
L0:Indian-owned economic enterprise, or Native Hawaiian small business concern.
L1:(4) The Contractor has the burden of proving the amount claimed and shall assert its request for an incentive payment prior
L0:to completion of contract performance.
L1:(5) The Contracting Officer, subject to the terms and conditions of the contract and the availability of funds, will authorize
L0:an incentive payment of 5 percent of the estimated cost, target cost, or fixed price included in the subcontract awarded to
L0:the Indian organization, Indian-owned economic enterprise, or Native Hawaiian small business concern.
L1:(6) If the Contractor requests and receives an incentive payment on behalf of a subcontractor, the Contractor is obligated to
L0:pay the subcontractor the incentive amount.
L1:(g) The Contractor shall insert the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (g), in all subcontracts exceeding
L0:$500,000.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.226-7001 — Utilization of Indian Organizations, Indian-Owned Economic Enterprises, and Native Hawaiian Small

title: 252.226-7002 Representation for Demonstration Project for Contractors Employing Persons with Disabilities
content:

title: 252.226-7003 Drug-Free Work Force
content:
L0:252.226-7003 Drug-Free Work Force.
L0:As prescribed in 226.570-2, use the following clause:
L0:DRUG-FREE WORK FORCE (AUG 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:Employee in a sensitive position means an employee who has been granted access to classified information; or employees
L0:in other positions that the Contractor determines involve national security, health or safety, or functions other than the
L0:foregoing requiring a high degree of trust and confidence.
L0:Illegal drugs means controlled substances included in Schedules I and II, as defined by section 802(6) of title 21 of the
L0:United States Code, the possession of which is unlawful under chapter 13 of that title. The term “illegal drugs” does not
L0:mean the use of a controlled substance pursuant to a valid prescription or other uses authorized by law.
L1:(b) The Contractor agrees to institute and maintain a program for achieving the objective of a drug-free work force. While
L0:this clause defines criteria for such a program, contractors are encouraged to implement alternative approaches comparable
L0:to the criteria in paragraph (c) that are designed to achieve the objectives of this clause.
L1:(c) Contractor programs shall include the following, or appropriate alternatives:
L1:(1) Employee assistance programs emphasizing high level direction, education, counseling, rehabilitation, and coordination
L0:with available community resources;
L1:(2) Supervisory training to assist in identifying and addressing illegal drug use by Contractor employees;
L1:(3) Provision for self-referrals as well as supervisory referrals to treatment with maximum respect for individual
L0:confidentiality consistent with safety and security issues;
L1:(4) Provision for identifying illegal drug users, including testing on a controlled and carefully monitored basis. Employee
L0:drug testing programs shall be established taking account of the following:
L1:(i) The Contractor shall establish a program that provides for testing for the use of illegal drugs by employees in sensitive
L0:positions. The extent of and criteria for such testing shall be determined by the Contractor based on considerations that
L0:include the nature of the work being performed under the contract, the employee’s duties, the efficient use of Contractor
L0:resources, and the risks to health, safety, or national security that could result from the failure of an employee adequately to
L0:discharge his or her position.
L1:(ii) In addition, the Contractor may establish a program for employee drug testing—
L1:(A) When there is a reasonable suspicion that an employee uses illegal drugs; or
L1:(B) When an employee has been involved in an accident or unsafe practice;
L1:(C) As part of or as a follow-up to counseling or rehabilitation for illegal drug use;
L1:(D) As part of a voluntary employee drug testing program.
L1:(iii) The Contractor may establish a program to test applicants for employment for illegal drug use.
L1:(iv) For the purpose of administering this clause, testing for illegal drugs may be limited to those substances for which
L0:testing is prescribed by section 2.1 of subpart B of the “Mandatory Guidelines for Federal Workplace Drug Testing
L0:Programs” (53 FR 11980 (April 11 1988)), issued by the Department of Health and Human Services.
L1:(d) Contractors shall adopt appropriate personnel procedures to deal with employees who are found to be using drugs
L0:illegally. Contractors shall not allow any employee to remain on duty or perform in a sensitive position who is found to use
L0:illegal drugs until such times as the Contractor, in accordance with procedures established by the Contractor, determines
L0:that the employee may perform in such a position.
L1:(e) The provisions of this clause pertaining to drug testing program shall not apply to the extent they are inconsistent with
L0:state or local law, or with an existing collective bargaining agreement; provided that with respect to the latter, the
L0:Contractor agrees that those issues that are in conflict will be a subject of negotiation at the next collective bargaining
L0:session.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.227-7018 Rights in Other Than Commercial Technical Data and Computer Software—Small Business
content:
L0:252.227-7018 Rights in Other Than Commercial Technical Data and Computer Software—Small Business
L0:Innovation Research Program and Small Business Technology Transfer Program.
L0:As prescribed in 227.7104-4(a)(1), use the following clause:
L0:RIGHTS IN OTHER THAN COMMERCIAL TECHNICAL DATA AND COMPUTER SOFTWARE—SMALL
L0:BUSINESS INNOVATION RESEARCH PROGRAM AND SMALL BUSINESS TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER
L0:PROGRAM (AUG 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause “Commercial computer software” means software developed or regularly used for nongovernmental purposes which—
L1:(1) Has been sold, leased, or licensed to the public;
L1:(2) Has been offered for sale, lease, or license to the public;
L1:(3) Has not been offered, sold, leased, or licensed to the public but will be available for commercial sale, lease, or license in
L0:time to satisfy the delivery requirements of this contract; or
L1:(4) Satisfies a criterion expressed in paragraph (1), (2), or (3) of this definition and would require only minor modification
L0:to meet the requirements of this contract.
L0:“Computer database” means a collection of recorded data in a form capable of being processed by a computer. The term
L0:does not include computer software.
L0:“Computer program” means a set of instructions, rules, or routines, recorded in a form that is capable of causing a
L0:computer to perform a specific operation or series of operations.
L0:“Computer software” means computer programs, source code, source code listings, object code listings, design details,
L0:algorithms, processes, flow charts, formulae, and related material that would enable the software to be reproduced,
L0:recreated, or recompiled. Computer software does not include computer databases or computer software documentation.
L0:“Computer software documentation” means owner’s manuals, user’s manuals, installation instructions, operating
L0:instructions, and other similar items, regardless of storage medium, that explain the capabilities of the computer software or
L0:provide instructions for using the software.
L0:“Covered Government support contractor” means a contractor (other than a litigation support contractor covered by
L0:252.204-7014) under a contract, the primary purpose of which is to furnish independent and impartial advice or technical
L0:assistance directly to the Government in support of the Government’s management and oversight of a program or effort
L0:(rather than to directly furnish an end item or service to accomplish a program or effort), provided that the contractor—
L1:(1) Is not affiliated with the prime contractor or a first-tier subcontractor on the program or effort, or with any direct
L0:competitor of such prime contractor or any such first-tier subcontractor in furnishing end items or services of the type
L0:developed or produced on the program or effort; and
L1:(2) Receives access to the technical data or computer software for performance of a Government contract that contains the
L0:clause at 252.227-7025, Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with
L0:Restrictive Legends.
L0:“Detailed manufacturing or process data” means technical data that describe the steps, sequences, and conditions of
L0:manufacturing, processing or assembly used by the manufacturer to produce an item or component or to perform a process.
L0:“Developed” means—
L1:(1) (Applicable to technical data other than computer software documentation.) An item, component, or process exists and
L0:is workable. Thus, the item or component must have been constructed or the process practiced. Workability is generally
L0:established when the item, component, or process has been analyzed or tested sufficiently to demonstrate to reasonable
L0:people skilled in the applicable art that there is a high probability that it will operate as intended. Whether, how much, and
L0:what type of analysis or testing is required to establish workability depends on the nature of the item, component, or
L0:process, and the state of the art. To be considered “developed,” the item, component, or process need not be at the stage
L0:where it could be offered for sale or sold on the commercial market, nor must the item, component or process be actually
L0:reduced to practice within the meaning of Title 35 of the United States Code;
L1:(2) A computer program has been successfully operated in a computer and tested to the extent sufficient to demonstrate to
L0:reasonable persons skilled in the art that the program can reasonably be expected to perform its intended purpose;
L1:(3) Computer software, other than computer programs, has been tested or analyzed to the extent sufficient to demonstrate
L0:to reasonable persons skilled in the art that the software can reasonably be expected to perform its intended purpose; or
L1:(4) Computer software documentation required to be delivered under a contract has been written, in any medium, in
L0:sufficient detail to comply with requirements under that contract.
L0:“Developed exclusively at private expense” means development was accomplished entirely with costs charged to indirect
L0:cost pools, costs not allocated to a government contract, or any combination thereof.
L1:(1) Private expense determinations should be made at the lowest practicable level.
L1:(2) Under fixed-price contracts, when total costs are greater than the firm-fixed-price or ceiling price of the contract, the
L0:additional development costs necessary to complete development shall not be considered when determining whether
L0:development was at government, private, or mixed expense.
L0:“Developed exclusively with government funds” means development was not accomplished exclusively or partially at
L0:private expense.
L0:“Developed with mixed funding” means development was accomplished partially with costs charged to indirect cost pools
L0:and/or costs not allocated to a government contract, and partially with costs charged directly to a government contract.
L0:“Form, fit, and function data” means technical data that describe the required overall physical, functional, and performance
L0:characteristics (along with the qualification requirements, if applicable) of an item, component, or process to the extent
L0:necessary to permit identification of physically and functionally interchangeable items.
L0:“Generated” means, with respect to technical data or computer software, first created in the performance of this contract.
L0:“Government purpose” means any activity in which the United States Government is a party, including cooperative
L0:agreements with international or multi-national defense organizations or sales or transfers by the United States Government
L0:to foreign governments or international organizations. Government purposes include competitive procurement, but do not
L0:include the rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical data or computer software for
L0:commercial purposes or authorize others to do so.
L0:“Government purpose rights” means the rights to—
L1:(1) Use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical data or computer software within the
L0:Government without restriction; and
L1:(2) Release or disclose technical data or computer software outside the Government and authorize persons to whom release
L0:or disclosure has been made to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose that data for United States
L0:Government purposes.
L0:“Limited rights” means the rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose technical data, in whole
L0:or in part, within the Government. The Government may not, without the written permission of the party asserting limited
L0:rights, release or disclose the technical data outside the Government, use the technical data for manufacture, or authorize
L0:the technical data to be used by another party, except that the Government may reproduce, release, or disclose such data or
L0:authorize the use or reproduction of the data by persons outside the Government if https://www.acquisition.gov/node/36356/printable/print
L1:(1) The reproduction, release, disclosure, or use is (i) Necessary for emergency repair and overhaul; or
L1:(ii) A release or disclosure to (A) A covered Government support contractor in performance of its covered Government support contracts for use,
L0:modification, reproduction, performance, display, or release or disclosure to a person authorized to receive limited rights
L0:technical data; or
L1:(B) A foreign government, of technical data other than detailed manufacturing or process data, when use of such data by
L0:the foreign government is in the interest of the Government and is required for evaluational or informational purposes;
L1:(2) The recipient of the technical data is subject to a prohibition on the further reproduction, release, disclosure, or use of
L0:the technical data; and
L1:(3) The Contractor or subcontractor asserting the restriction is notified of such reproduction, release, disclosure, or use.
L0:“Minor modification” means a modification that does not significantly alter the nongovernmental function or purpose of
L0:computer software or is of the type customarily provided in the commercial marketplace.
L0:“Other than commercial computer software” means software that does not qualify as commercial computer software under
L0:the definition of “commercial computer software” of this clause.
L0:“Restricted rights” apply only to other than commercial computer software and mean the Government's rights to (1) Use a computer program with one computer at one time. The program may not be accessed by more than one terminal
L0:or central processing unit or time shared unless otherwise permitted by this contract;
L1:(2) Transfer a computer program to another Government agency without the further permission of the Contractor if the
L0:transferor destroys all copies of the program and related computer software documentation in its possession and notifies the

L1:(3) Make a reasonable number of copies of the computer software required for the purposes of safekeeping (archive),
L0:backup, modification, or other activities authorized in paragraphs (1), (2), and (4) through (7) of this definition;
L1:(4) Modify computer software provided that the Government may (i) Use the modified software only as provided in paragraphs (1) and (3) of this definition; and
L1:(ii) Not release or disclose the modified software except as provided in paragraphs (2), ( 5), (6), and (7) of this definition;
L1:(5) Use, and permit contractors or subcontractors performing service contracts (see 37.101 of the Federal Acquisition
L0:Regulation) in support of this or a related contract to use computer software to diagnose and correct deficiencies in a
L0:computer program, to modify computer software to enable a computer program to be combined with, adapted to, or merged
L0:with other computer programs or when necessary to respond to urgent tactical situations, provided that (i) The Government notifies the party which has granted restricted rights that any such release or disclosure to particular
L0:contractors or subcontractors was made;
L1:(ii) Such contractors or subcontractors are subject to the nondisclosure agreement at 227.7103-7 of the Defense Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation Supplement or are Government contractors receiving access to the software for performance of a
L0:Government contract that contains the clause at 252.227-7025, Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of GovernmentFurnished Information Marked with Restrictive Legends;
L1:(iii) The Government shall not permit the recipient to decompile, disassemble, or reverse engineer the software, or use

L0:for any other purpose; and
L1:(iv) Such use is subject to the limitations in paragraphs (1) through (4) of this definition;
L1:(6) Use, and permit contractors or subcontractors performing emergency repairs or overhaul of items or components of
L0:items procured under this or a related contract to use the computer software when necessary to perform the emergency

L0:access to the software for performance of a Government contract that contains the clause at 252.227-7025, Limitations on

L1:(ii) The Government shall not permit the recipient to decompile, disassemble, or reverse engineer the software, or use

L1:(iii) Such use is subject to the limitations in paragraphs (1) through (4) of this definition; and
L1:(7) Use, modify, reproduce, perform, display, or release or disclose computer software to a person authorized to receive
L0:restricted rights computer software for management and oversight of a program or effort, and permit covered Government

L0:Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with Restrictive Legends, to use,

L0:“Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) data” means all technical data or

L0:As prescribed in 227.7104-4(b)(3) or 227.7203-6(c), use the following clause:
L0:VALIDATION OF ASSERTED RESTRICTIONS—COMPUTER SOFTWARE (JAN 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—

L0:Other terms are defined in the 252.227-7014, Rights in Other Than Commercial Computer Software and Other Than
L0:Commercial Computer Software Documentation, clause of this contract.

L0:Contracting Officer a written justification for such asserted restrictions in response to a request for information under
L0:paragraph (d) of this clause or a challenge under paragraph (f) of this clause.
L1:(c) Direct contact with subcontractors or suppliers. The Contractor agrees that the Contracting Officer may transact
L0:matters under this clause directly with subcontractors or suppliers at any tier who assert restrictions on the Government's
L0:right to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose computer software. Neither this clause, nor any action
L0:taken by the Government under this clause, creates or implies privity of contract between the Government and the
L0:Contractor's subcontractors or suppliers.
L1:(d) Requests for information.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer may request the Contractor to provide sufficient information to enable the Contracting Officer
L0:to evaluate the Contractor's asserted restrictions. Such information shall be based upon the records required by this clause
L0:or other information reasonably available to the Contractor.
L1:(2) Based upon the information provided, if the—
L1:(i) Contractor agrees that an asserted restriction is not valid, the Contracting Officer may—
L1:(A) Strike or correct the unjustified marking at the Contractor's expense; or
L1:(B) Return the computer software to the Contractor for correction at the Contractor's expense. If the Contractor fails to
L0:correct or strike the unjustified marking and return the corrected software to the Contracting Officer within 60 days
L0:following receipt of the software, the Contracting Officer may correct or strike the marking at the Contractor's expense;
L1:(ii) Contracting Officer concludes that the asserted restriction is appropriate for this contract, the Contracting Officer shall
L0:so notify the Contractor in writing.
L1:(3) The Contractor's failure to provide a timely response to a Contracting Officer's request for information or failure to
L0:provide sufficient information to enable the Contracting Officer to evaluate an asserted restriction shall constitute
L0:reasonable grounds for questioning the validity of an asserted restriction.
L1:(e) Government right to challenge and validate asserted restrictions.
L1:(1) The Government, when there are reasonable grounds to do so, has the right to review and challenge the validity of any
L0:restrictions asserted by the Contractor on the Government's rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or
L0:disclose computer software delivered, to be delivered under this contract, or otherwise provided to the Government in the
L0:performance of this contract. Except for software that is publicly available, has been furnished to the Government without
L0:restrictions, has been otherwise made available without restrictions, or is the subject of a fraudulently asserted use or
L0:release restriction, the Government may exercise this right only within 6 years after the date(s) the software is delivered or
L0:otherwise furnished to the Government, or 6 years following final payment under this contract, whichever is later.
L1:(2) The absence of a challenge to an asserted restriction shall not constitute validation under this clause. Only a Contracting
L0:Officer's final decision or actions of an agency Board of Contract Appeals or a court of competent jurisdiction that sustain
L0:the validity of an asserted restriction constitute validation of the restriction.
L1:(f) Challenge procedures.
L1:(1) A challenge must be in writing and shall—
L1:(i) State the specific grounds for challenging the asserted restriction;
L1:(ii) Require the Contractor to respond in writing within 60 days;
L1:(iii) Require the Contractor to provide justification for the assertion based upon records kept in accordance with paragraph
L1:(b) of this clause and such other documentation that are reasonably available to the Contractor, in sufficient detail to enable
L0:the Contracting Officer to determine the validity of the asserted restrictions; and
L1:(iv) State that a Contracting Officer's final decision, during the 3-year period preceding this challenge, or action of a court
L0:of competent jurisdiction or Board of Contract Appeals that sustained the validity of an identical assertion made by the
L0:Contractor (or a licensee) shall serve as justification for the asserted restriction.
L1:(2) The Contracting Officer shall extend the time for response if the Contractor submits a written request showing the need
L0:for additional time to prepare a response.
L1:(3) The Contracting Officer may request additional supporting documentation if, in the Contracting Officer’s opinion, the
L0:Contractor's explanation does not provide sufficient evidence to justify the validity of the asserted restrictions. The
L0:Contractor agrees to promptly respond to the Contracting Officer's request for additional supporting documentation.
L1:(4) Notwithstanding challenge by the Contracting Officer, the parties may agree on the disposition of an asserted restriction
L0:at any time prior to a Contracting Officer's final decision or, if the Contractor has appealed that decision, filed suit, or
L0:provided notice of an intent to file suit, at any time prior to a decision by a court of competent jurisdiction or Board of
L0:Contract Appeals.
L1:(5) If the Contractor fails to respond to the Contracting Officer's request for information or additional information under
L0:paragraph (f)(1) of this clause, the Contracting Officer shall issue a final decision, in accordance with the Disputes clause
L0:of this contract, pertaining to the validity of the asserted restriction.
L1:(6) If the Contracting Officer, after reviewing any available information pertaining to the validity of an asserted restriction,
L0:determines that the asserted restriction has—
L1:(i) Not been justified, the Contracting Officer shall issue promptly a final decision, in accordance with the Disputes clause
L0:of this contract, denying the validity of the asserted restriction; or
L1:(ii) Been justified, the Contracting Officer shall issue promptly a final decision, in accordance with the Disputes clause of
L0:this contract, validating the asserted restriction.
L1:(7) A Contractor receiving challenges to the same asserted restriction(s) from more than one Contracting Officer shall
L0:notify each Contracting Officer of the other challenges. The notice shall also state which Contracting Officer initiated the
L0:first in time unanswered challenge. The Contracting Officerwho initiated the first in time unanswered challenge, after
L0:consultation with the other Contracting Officers who have challenged the restrictions and the Contractor, shall formulate
L0:and distribute a schedule that provides the Contractor a reasonable opportunity for responding to each challenge.
L1:(g) Contractor appeal—Government obligation.
L1:(1) The Government agrees that, notwithstanding a Contracting Officer's final decision denying the validity of an asserted
L0:restriction and except as provided in paragraph (g)(3) of this clause, it will honor the asserted restriction—
L1:(i) For a period of 90 days from the date of the Contracting Officer's final decision to allow the Contractor to appeal to the
L0:appropriate Board of Contract Appeals or to file suit in an appropriate court;
L1:(ii) For a period of 1 year from the date of the Contracting Officer's final decision if, within the first 90 days following the
L0:Contracting Officer's final decision, the Contractor has provided notice of an intent to file suit in an appropriate court; or
L1:(iii) Until final disposition by the appropriate Board of Contract Appeals or court of competent jurisdiction, if the
L0:Contractor has—
L1:(A) Appealed to the Board of Contract Appeals or filed suit in an appropriate court within 90 days; or
L1:(B) Submitted, within 90 days, a notice of intent to file suit in an appropriate court and filed suit within 1 year.
L1:(2) The Contractor agrees that the Government may strike, correct, or ignore the restrictive markings if the Contractor fails
L0:to—
L1:(i) Appeal to a Board of Contract Appeals within ninety (90) days from the date of the Contracting Officer's final decision;
L1:(ii) File suit in an appropriate court within ninety (90) days from such date; or
L1:(iii) File suit within 1 year after the date of the Contracting Officer's final decision if the Contractor had provided notice of
L0:intent to file suit within 90 days following the date of the Contracting Officer's final decision.
L1:(3)(i) The agency head, on a nondelegable basis, may determine that urgent or compelling circumstances do not permit
L0:awaiting the filing of suit in an appropriate court, or the rendering of a decision by a court of competent jurisdiction or
L0:Board of Contract Appeals. In that event, the agency head shall notify the Contractor of the urgent or compelling
L0:circumstances. Notwithstanding paragraph (g)(1) of this clause, the Contractor agrees that the agency may use, modify,
L0:reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose computer software marked with—
L1:(A) Government purpose legends for any purpose, and authorize others to do so; or
L1:(B) Restricted or special license rights for Government purposes only.
L1:(ii) The Government agrees not to release or disclose such software unless, prior to release or disclosure, the intended
L0:recipient is subject to the use and nondisclosure agreement at Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement
L1:(DFARS) 227.7103-7 , or is a Government contractor receiving access to the software for performance of a Government
L0:contract that contains the clause at DFARS 252.227-7025, Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished
L0:Information Marked with Restrictive Legends. The agency head’s determination may be made at any time after the date of
L0:the Contracting Officer’s final decision and shall not affect the Contractor’s right to damages against the United States, or
L0:other relief provided by law, if its asserted restrictions are ultimately upheld.
L1:(h) Final disposition of appeal or suit. If the Contractor appeals or files suit and if, upon final disposition of the appeal or
L0:suit, the Contracting Officer's decision is:
L1:(1) Sustained—
L1:(i) Any restrictive marking on such computer software shall be struck or corrected at the Contractor's expense or ignored;
L0:and
L1:(ii) If the asserted restriction is found not to be substantially justified, the Contractor shall be liable to the Government for
L0:payment of the cost to the Government of reviewing the asserted restriction and the fees and other expenses (as defined in
L0:28 U.S.C. 2412(d)(2)(A)) incurred by the Government in challenging the restriction, unless special circumstances would
L0:make such payment unjust.
L1:(2) Not sustained—
L1:(i) The Government shall be bound by the asserted restriction; and
L1:(ii) If the challenge by the Government is found not to have been made in good faith, the Government shall be liable to the
L0:Contractor for payment of fees and other expenses (as defined in 28 U.S.C. 2412(d)(2)(A)) incurred by the Contractor in
L0:defending the restriction.
L1:(i) Flowdown. The Contractor shall insert this clause in all contracts, purchase orders, and other similar instruments with its
L0:subcontractors or suppliers, at any tier, who will be furnishing computer software to the Government in the performance of
L0:this contract. The clause may not be altered other than to identify the appropriate parties.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.227-7019 — Validation of Asserted Restrictions—Computer Software

title: 252.227-7020 Rights in Special Works
content:
L0:252.227-7020 Rights in Special Works.
L0:As prescribed in227.7105-3, 227.7106 (a) or 227.7205 (a), use the following clause:
L0:RIGHTS IN SPECIAL WORKS (JUN 1995)
L1:(a) Applicability. This clause applies to works first created, generated, or produced and required to be delivered under this
L0:contract.
L1:(b) Definitions. As used in this clause:
L1:(1) “Computer data base” means a collection of data recorded in a form capable of being processed by a computer. The
L0:term does not include computer software.
L1:(2) “Computer program” means a set of instructions, rules, or routines recorded in a form that is capable of causing a
L0:computer to perform a specific operation or series of operations.
L1:(3) “Computer software” means computer programs, source code, source code listings, object code listings, design details,
L0:algorithms, processes, flow charts, formulae and related material that would enable the software to be reproduced,
L0:recreated, or recompiled. Computer software does not include computer data bases or computer software documentation.
L1:(4) “Computer software documentation” means owner's manuals, user's manuals, installation instructions, operating
L0:instructions, and other similar items, regardless of storage medium, that explain the capabilities of the computer software or
L0:provide instructions for using the software.
L1:(5) “Unlimited rights” means the rights to use, modify, reproduce, perform, display, release, or disclose a work in whole or
L0:in part, in any manner, and for any purpose whatsoever, and to have or authorize others to do so.
L1:(6) The term “works” includes computer data bases, computer software, or computer software documentation; literary,
L0:musical, choreographic, or dramatic compositions; pantomimes; pictorial, graphic, or sculptural compositions; motion
L0:pictures and other audiovisual compositions; sound recordings in any medium; or, items of similar nature.
L1:(c) License rights.
L1:(1) The Government shall have unlimited rights in works first produced, created, or generated and required to be delivered
L0:under this contract.
L1:(2) When a work is first produced, created, or generated under this contract, and such work is required to be delivered
L0:under this contract, the Contractor shall assign copyright in those works to the Government. The Contractor, unless
L0:directed to the contrary by the Contracting Officer, shall place the following notice on such works:
L0:“© (Year date of delivery) United States Government, as represented by the Secretary of (department). All rights reserved.”
L0:For phonorecords, the “©” marking shall be replaced by a “P”.
L1:(3) The Contractor grants to the Government a royalty-free, world-wide, nonexclusive, irrevocable license to reproduce,
L0:prepare derivative works from, distribute, perform, or display, and to have or authorize others to do so, the Contractor's
L0:copyrighted works not first produced, created, or generated under this contract that have been incorporated into the works
L0:deliverable under this contract.
L1:(d) Third party copyrighted data. The Contractor shall not incorporate, without the written approval of the Contracting
L0:Officer, any copyrighted works in the works to be delivered under this contract unless the Contractor is the copyright
L0:owner or has obtained for the Government the license rights necessary to perfect a license of the scope identified in
L0:paragraph (c)(3) of this clause and, prior to delivery of such works—
L1:(1) Has affixed to the transmittal document a statement of the license rights obtained; or
L1:(2) For computer software, has provided a statement of the license rights obtained in a form acceptable to the Contracting
L0:Officer.
L1:(e) Indemnification. The Contractor shall indemnify and save and hold harmless the Government, and its officers, agents
L0:and employees acting for the Government, against any liability, including costs and expenses, (1) for violation of
L0:proprietary rights, copyrights, or rights of privacy or publicity, arising out of the creation, delivery, use, modification,
L0:reproduction, release, performance, display, or disclosure of any works furnished under this contract, or (2) based upon any
L0:libelous or other unlawful matter contained in such works.
L1:(f) Government-furnished information. Paragraphs (d) and (e) of this clause are not applicable to information furnished to
L0:the Contractor by the Government and incorporated in the works delivered under this contract.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.227-7021 Rights in Data—Existing Works
content:
L0:252.227-7021 Rights in Data—Existing Works.

L1:(a) The term “works” as used herein includes literary, musical, and dramatic works; pantomimes and choreographic works;
L0:pictorial, graphic and sculptural works; motion pictures and other audiovisual works; sound recordings; and works of a

L1:(c) The Contractor shall indemnify and save and hold harmless the Government, and its officers, agents, and employees
L0:acting for the Government, against any liability, including costs and expenses, (1) for violation of proprietary rights,
L0:copyrights, or rights of privacy or publicity arising out of the creation, delivery, or use, of any works furnished under this
L0:contract, or (2) based upon any libelous or other unlawful matter contained in same works.

title: 252.227-7022 Government Rights (Unlimited)
content:
L0:252.227-7022 Government Rights (Unlimited).
L0:As prescribed at 227.7107-1 (a) use the following clause:
L0:GOVERNMENT RIGHTS (UNLIMITED) (MAR 1979)
L0:The Government shall have unlimited rights, in all drawings, designs, specifications, notes and other works developed in
L0:the performance of this contract, including the right to use same on any other Government design or construction without
L0:additional compensation to the Contractor. The Contractor hereby grants to the Government a paid-up license throughout
L0:the world to all such works to which he may assert or establish any claim under design patent or copyright laws. The
L0:Contractor for a period of three (3) years after completion of the project agrees to furnish the original or copies of all such
L0:works on the request of the Contracting Officer.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.227-7023 Drawings and Other Data to Become Property of Government
content:
L0:252.227-7023 Drawings and Other Data to Become Property of Government.
L0:As prescribed at 227.7107-1 (b), use the following clause:
L0:DRAWINGS AND OTHER DATA TO BECOME PROPERTY OF GOVERNMENT (MAR 1979)
L0:All designs, drawings, specifications, notes and other works developed in the performance of this contract shall become the
L0:sole property of the Government and may be used on any other design or construction without additional compensation to
L0:the Contractor. The Government shall be considered the “person for whom the work was prepared” for the purpose of
L0:authorship in any copyrightable work under 17 U.S.C. 201(b). With respect thereto, the Contractor agrees not to assert or
L0:authorize others to assert any rights nor establish any claim under the design patent or copyright laws. The Contractor for a
L0:period of three (3) years after completion of the project agrees to furnish all retained works on the request of the
L0:Contracting Officer. Unless otherwise provided in this contract, the Contractor shall have the right to retain copies of all
L0:works beyond such period.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.227-7023 — Drawings and Other Data to Become Property of Government

title: 252.227-7024 Notice and Approval of Restricted Designs
content:
L0:252.227-7024 Notice and Approval of Restricted Designs.
L0:As prescribed at 227.7107-3 , use the following clause:
L0:NOTICE AND APPROVAL OF RESTRICTED DESIGNS (APR 1984)
L0:In the performance of this contract, the Contractor shall, to the extent practicable, make maximum use of structures,
L0:machines, products, materials, construction methods, and equipment that are readily available through Government or
L0:competitive commercial channels, or through standard or proven production techniques, methods, and processes. Unless
L0:approved by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall not produce a design or specification that requires in this
L0:construction work the use of structures, products, materials, construction equipment, or processes that are known by the
L0:Contractor to be available only from a sole source. The Contractor shall promptly report any such design or specification to
L0:the Contracting Officer and give the reason why it is considered necessary to so restrict the design or specification.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.227-7024 — Notice and Approval of Restricted Designs

title: 252.227-7025 Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with Restrictive
content:
L0:252.227-7025 Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with Restrictive
L0:Legends.
L0:As prescribed in 227.7103-6(c), 227.7104-4(b)(4), or 227.7203-6(d), use the following clause:
L0:LIMITATIONS ON THE USE OR DISCLOSURE OF GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED INFORMATION MARKED
L0:WITH RESTRICTIVE LEGENDS (JAN 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) For contracts in which the Government will furnish the Contractor with technical data, the terms "covered Government
L0:support contractor," "limited rights," and "Government purpose rights" are defined in the clause at 252.227-7013 , Rights in
L0:Technical Data-Other Than Commercial Products and Commercial Services.
L1:(2) For contracts in which the Government will furnish the Contractor with computer software or computer software
L0:documentation, the terms "covered Government support contractor," "government purpose rights," and "restricted rights"
L0:are defined in the clause at 252.227-7014 , Rights in Other Than Commercial Computer Software and Other Than
L0:Commercial Computer Software Documentation.
L1:(3) For Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Program and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Program
L0:contracts, the terms “covered Government support contractor,” “government purpose rights,” “limited rights,” “restricted
L0:rights,” and “SBIR/STTR data rights” are defined in the clause at 252.227-7018, Rights in Other Than Commercial
L0:Technical Data and Computer Software—Small Business Innovation Research Program and Small Business Technology
L0:Transfer Program.
L1:(b) Technical data or computer software provided to the Contractor as Government-furnished information (GFI) under this
L0:contract may be subject to restrictions on use, modification, reproduction, release, performance, display, or further
L0:disclosure.
L1:(1) GFI marked with limited rights, restricted rights, or SBIR/STTR data rights legends.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall use, modify, reproduce, perform, or display technical data received from the Government with
L0:limited rights legends, computer software received with restricted rights legends, or SBIR/STTR technical data or
L0:computer software received with SBIR/STTR data rights legends (during the SBIR/STTR data protection period) only in
L0:the performance of this contract. The Contractor shall not, without the express written permission of the party whose name
L0:appears in the legend, release or disclose such data or software to any unauthorized person.
L1:(ii) If the Contractor is a covered Government support contractor, the Contractor is also subject to the additional terms and
L0:conditions at paragraph (b)(5) of this clause.
L1:(2) GFI marked with government purpose rights legends. The Contractor shall use technical data or computer software
L0:received from the Government with government purpose rights legends for government purposes only. The Contractor
L0:shall not, without the express written permission of the party whose name appears in the restrictive legend, use, modify,
L0:reproduce, release, perform, or display such data or software for any commercial purpose or disclose such data or software
L0:to a person other than its subcontractors, suppliers, or prospective subcontractors or suppliers, who require the data or
L0:software to submit offers for, or perform, contracts under this contract. Prior to disclosing the data or software, the
L0:Contractor shall require the persons to whom disclosure will be made to complete and sign the nondisclosure agreement at
L0:227.7103-7 of the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS).
L1:(3) GFI marked with specially negotiated license rights legends.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, or display technical data or computer software received
L0:from the Government with specially negotiated license legends only as permitted in the license. Such data or software may
L0:not be released or disclosed to other persons unless permitted by the license and, prior to release or disclosure, the intended
L0:recipient has completed the nondisclosure agreement at DFARS 227.7103-7. The Contractor shall modify paragraph (1)(c)
L0:of the nondisclosure agreement to reflect the recipient's obligations regarding use, modification, reproduction, release,
L0:performance, display, and disclosure of the data or software.
L1:(ii) If the Contractor is a covered Government support contractor, the Contractor may also be subject to some or all of the
L0:additional terms and conditions at paragraph (b)(5) of this clause, to the extent such terms and conditions are required by
L0:the specially negotiated license.
L1:(4) GFI technical data marked with commercial restrictive legends.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall use, modify, reproduce, perform, or display technical data that are or pertain to a commercial
L0:product or commercial service and are received from the Government with a commercial restrictive legend (i.e., marked to
L0:indicate that such data are subject to use, modification, reproduction, release, performance, display, or disclosure
L0:restrictions) only in the performance of this contract. The Contractor shall not, without the express written permission of
L0:the party whose name appears in the legend, use the technical data to manufacture additional quantities of the commercial
L0:products or commercial services, or release or disclose such data to any unauthorized person.
L1:(ii) If the Contractor is a covered Government support contractor, the Contractor is also subject to the additional terms and
L0:conditions at paragraph (b)(5) of this clause.
L1:(5) Covered Government support contractors. If the Contractor is a covered Government support contractor receiving
L0:technical data or computer software marked with restrictive legends pursuant to paragraphs (b)(1)(ii), (b)(3)(ii), or (b)(4)
L1:(ii), the Contractor further agrees and acknowledges that—
L1:(i) The technical data or computer software will be accessed and used for the sole purpose of furnishing independent and
L0:impartial advice or technical assistance directly to the Government in support of the Government’s management and
L0:oversight of the program or effort to which such technical data or computer software relates, as stated in this contract, and
L0:shall not be used to compete for any Government or non-Government contract;
L1:(ii) The Contractor will take all reasonable steps to protect the technical data or computer software against any
L0:unauthorized release or disclosure;
L1:(iii) The Contractor will ensure that the party whose name appears in the legend is notified of the access or use within
L0:30days of the Contractor's access or use of such data or software;
L1:(iv) The Contractor will enter into a nondisclosure agreement with the party whose name appears in the legend, if required
L0:to do so by that party, and that any such nondisclosure agreement will implement the restrictions on the Contractor's use of
L0:such data or software as set forth in this clause. The nondisclosure agreement shall not include any additional terms and
L0:conditions unless mutually agreed to by the parties to the nondisclosure agreement; and
L1:(v) That a breach of these obligations or restrictions may subject the Contractor to—
L1:(A) Criminal, civil, administrative, and contractual actions in law and equity for penalties, damages, and other appropriate
L0:remedies by the United States; and
L1:(B) Civil actions for damages and other appropriate remedies by the party whose name appears in the legend.
L1:(c) Indemnification and creation of third party beneficiary rights. The Contractor agrees—
L1:(1) To indemnify and hold harmless the Government, its agents, and employees from every claim or liability, including
L0:attorneys fees, court costs, and expenses, arising out of, or in any way related to, the misuse or unauthorized modification,
L0:reproduction, release, performance, display, or disclosure of technical data or computer software received from the
L0:Government with restrictive legends by the Contractor or any person to whom the Contractor has released or disclosed
L0:such data or software; and
L1:(2) That the party whose name appears on the restrictive legend, in addition to any other rights it may have, is a third-party
L0:beneficiary who has the right of direct action against the Contractor, or any person to whom the Contractor has released or
L0:disclosed such data or software, for the unauthorized duplication, release, or disclosure of technical data or computer
L0:software subject to restrictive legends.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall ensure that its employees are subject to use and nondisclosure obligations consistent with this
L0:clause prior to the employees being provided access to or use of any GFI covered by this clause.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.227-7025 — Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Government-Furnished Information Marked with Restrictive

title: 252.227-7026 Deferred Delivery of Technical Data or Computer Software
content:
L0:252.227-7026 Deferred Delivery of Technical Data or Computer Software.
L0:As prescribed at 227.7103-8 (a), use the following clause:
L0:DEFERRED DELIVERY OF TECHNICAL DATA OR COMPUTER SOFTWARE (APR 1988)
L0:The Government shall have the right to require, at any time during the performance of this contract, within two (2) years
L0:after either acceptance of all items (other than data or computer software) to be delivered under this contract or termination
L0:of this contract, whichever is later, delivery of any technical data or computer software item identified in this contract as
L0:“deferred delivery” data or computer software. The obligation to furnish such technical data required to be prepared by a
L0:subcontractor and pertaining to an item obtained from him shall expire two (2) years after the date Contractor accepts the
L0:last delivery of that item from that subcontractor for use in performing this contract.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.227-7026 — Deferred Delivery of Technical Data or Computer Software

title: 252.227-7027 Deferred Ordering of Technical Data or Computer Software
content:
L0:252.227-7027 Deferred Ordering of Technical Data or Computer Software.
L0:As prescribed at 227.7103-8 (b), use the following clause:
L0:DEFERRED ORDERING OF TECHNICAL DATA OR COMPUTER SOFTWARE (APR 1988)
L0:In addition to technical data or computer software specified elsewhere in this contract to be delivered hereunder, the
L0:Government may, at any time during the performance of this contract or within a period of three (3) years after acceptance
L0:of all items (other than technical data or computer software) to be delivered under this contract or the termination of this
L0:contract, order any technical data or computer software generated in the performance of this contract or any subcontract
L0:hereunder. When the technical data or computer software is ordered, the Contractor shall be compensated for converting
L0:the data or computer software into the prescribed form, for reproduction and delivery. The obligation to deliver the
L0:technical data of a subcontractor and pertaining to an item obtained from him shall expire three (3) years after the date the
L0:Contractor accepts the last delivery of that item from that subcontractor under this contract. The Government's rights to use
L0:said data or computer software shall be pursuant to the “Rights in Technical Data and Computer Software” clause of this
L0:contract.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.227-7027 — Deferred Ordering of Technical Data or Computer Software

title: 252.227-7028 Technical Data or Computer Software Previously Delivered to the Government
content:
L0:252.227-7028 Technical Data or Computer Software Previously Delivered to the Government.
L0:As prescribed in 227.7103-6(d), 227.7104-4(b)(5), or 227.7203-6(e), use the following provision:
L0:TECHNICAL DATA OR COMPUTER SOFTWARE PREVIOUSLY DELIVERED TO THE GOVERNMENT (JUN 1995)

L0:computer software it intends to deliver under this contract with other than unlimited rights that are identical or substantially
L0:similar to documents or other media that the Offeror has produced for, delivered to, or is obligated to deliver to the
L0:Government under any contract or subcontract. The attachment shall identify—
L1:(a) The contract number under which the data or software were produced;
L1:(b) The contract number under which, and the name and address of the organization to whom, the data or software were
L0:most recently delivered or will be delivered; and
L1:(c) Any limitations on the Government's rights to use or disclose the data or software, including, when applicable,
L0:identification of the earliest date the limitations expire.
L0:(End of provision)
