title: 252.227-7037 Validation of Asserted Restrictions on Technical Data
content:
L0:252.227-7037 Validation of Asserted Restrictions on Technical Data.
L0:As prescribed in 227.7102-4(c), 227.7103-6(e)(3), 227.7104-4(b)(7), or 227.7203-6(f), use the following clause:
L0:VALIDATION OF ASSERTED RESTRICTIONS ON TECHNICAL DATA (JAN 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. The terms used in this clause are defined in the Rights in Technical Data—Other Than Commercial
L0:Products and Commercial Services clause of this contract.
L1:(b) Commercial products or commercial services-presumption regarding development exclusively at private expense. The
L0:Contracting Officer will presume that the Contractor’s or a subcontractor’s asserted use or release restrictions with respect
L0:to a commercial product or commercial service are justified on the basis that the item was developed exclusively at private
L0:expense. The Contracting Officer will not issue a challenge unless there are reasonable grounds to question the validity of
L0:the assertion that the commercial product or commercial service was developed exclusively at private expense.
L1:(c) Justification. The Contractor or subcontractor at any tier is responsible for maintaining records sufficient to justify the
L0:validity of its asserted restrictions on the rights of the Government and others to use, duplicate, release, or disclose
L0:technical data delivered, required to be delivered, or otherwise provided to the Government under the contract or
L0:subcontract. Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this clause, the Contractor or subcontractor shall be prepared to furnish
L0:to the Contracting Officer a written justification for such asserted restrictions in response to a challenge under paragraph
L1:(e) of this clause.
L1:(d) Prechallenge request for information.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer may request the Contractor or subcontractor to furnish a written explanation for any asserted
L0:restriction on the right of the United States or others to use, disclose, or release technical data. If, upon review of the
L0:explanation submitted, the Contracting Officer cannot determine the basis of the asserted restriction, the Contracting
L0:Officer may further request the Contractor or subcontractor to furnish additional information in the records of, or otherwise
L0:in the possession of or reasonably available to, the Contractor or subcontractor to justify the validity of any asserted
L0:restriction on technical data delivered,to be delivered, or otherwise provided to the Government under the contract or
L0:subcontract (e.g., a statement of facts accompanied with supporting documentation). The Contractor or subcontractor shall
L0:submit such written data as requested by the Contracting Officer within the time required or such longer period as may be
L0:mutually agreed.
L1:(2) If the Contracting Officer, after reviewing the written data furnished pursuant to paragraph (d)(1) of this clause, or any
L0:other available information pertaining to the validity of an asserted restriction, determines that reasonable grounds exist to
L0:question the current validity of the asserted restriction and that continued adherence to the asserted restriction would make
L0:impracticable the subsequent competitive acquisition of the item or process to which the technical data relates, the
L0:Contracting Officer will follow the procedures in paragraph (e) of this clause.
L1:(3) If the Contractor or subcontractor fails to respond to the Contracting Officer's request for information under paragraph
L1:(d)(1) of this clause, and the Contracting Officer determines that continued adherence to the asserted restriction would
L0:make impracticable the subsequent competitive acquisition of the item or process to which the technical data relates, the
L0:Contracting Officer may challenge the validity of the asserted restriction as described in paragraph (e) of this clause.
L1:(e) Challenge.
L1:(1) Notwithstanding any provision of this contract concerning inspection and acceptance, if the Contracting Officer
L0:determines that a challenge to the asserted restriction is warranted, the Contracting Officer will send a written challenge
L0:notice to the Contractor or subcontractor making the asserted restriction. The challenge notice and all related
L0:correspondence shall be subject to handling procedures for classified information and controlled unclassified information.
L0:Such challenge will—
L1:(i) State the specific grounds for challenging the asserted restriction including, for commercial products or commercial
L0:services, sufficient information to reasonably demonstrate that the commercial product or commercial service was not
L0:developed exclusively at private expense ;
L1:(ii) Require a response within 60 days justifying and providing sufficient evidence as to the current validity of the asserted
L0:restriction;
L1:(iii) State that a DoD Contracting Officer's final decision, issued pursuant to paragraph (g) of this clause, sustaining the
L0:validity of a prior asserted restrictionrestrictive marking identical to the current asserted restriction, within the three3-year
L0:period preceding the current challenge, shall serve as justification for the current asserted restriction if the prior validated
L0:restriction was asserted by the same Contractor or subcontractor (or any licensee of such Contractor or subcontractor) to
L0:which such notice is being provided; and
L1:(iv) State that failure to respond to the challenge notice may result in issuance of a final decision pursuant to paragraph (f)
L0:of this clause.
L1:(2) The Contracting Officer will extend the time for response as appropriate if the Contractor or subcontractor submits a
L0:written request showing the need for additional time to prepare a response.
L1:(3) The Contractor's or subcontractor's written response shall be considered a claim within the meaning of 41 U.S.C. 7101,
L0:Contract Disputes, and shall be certified in the form prescribed at 33.207 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation, regardless
L0:of dollar amount.
L1:(4) A Contractor or subcontractor receiving challenges to the same asserted restrictions from more than one Contracting
L0:Officer shall notify each Contracting Officer of the existence of more than one challenge. The notice shall also state which
L0:Contracting Officer initiated the first in time unanswered challenge. The Contracting Officer initiating the first in time
L0:unanswered challenge after consultation with the Contractor or subcontractor and the other Contracting Officers, will
L0:formulate and distribute a schedule for responding to each of the challenge notices to all interested parties. The schedule
L0:will afford the Contractor or subcontractor an opportunity to respond to each challenge notice. All parties will be bound by
L0:this schedule.
L1:(f) Final decision when Contractor or subcontractor fails to respond.Upon a failure of a Contractor or subcontractor to
L0:submit any response to the challenge notice the Contracting Officer will issue a final decision to the Contractor or
L0:subcontractor in accordance with the Disputes clause of this contract. In order to sustain the challenge for commercial
L0:products or commercial services, the Contracting Officer will provide information demonstrating that the commercial
L0:product or commercial service was not developed exclusively at private expense . This final decision will be issued as soon
L0:as possible after the expiration of the time period of paragraph (e)(1)(ii) or (e)(2) of this clause. Following issuance of the
L0:final decision, the Contracting Officer will comply with the procedures in paragraphs (g)(2)(ii) through (iv) of this clause.
L1:(g) Final decision when Contractor or subcontractor responds.
L1:(1) If the Contracting Officer determines that the Contractor or subcontractor has justified the validity of the asserted
L0:restriction, the Contracting Officer will issue a final decision to the Contractor or subcontractor that sustains the validity of
L0:the asserted restriction, and that states that the Government will continue to be bound by the asserted restriction. The
L0:Contracting Officer will issue this final decision within 60 days after receipt of the Contractor's or subcontractor's response
L0:to the challenge notice, or within such longer period that the Contracting Officer has notified the Contractor or
L0:subcontractor that the Government will require. The Contracting Officer will provide notification of any longer period for
L0:issuance of a final decision within 60 days after receipt of the response to the challenge notice.
L1:(2)(i) If the Contracting Officer determines that the validity of the asserted restriction is not justified, the Contracting
L0:Officer will issue a final decision to the Contractor or subcontractor in accordance with the Disputes clause of this contract.
L0:To sustain the challenge for commercial products or commercial services, the Contracting Officer will provide information
L0:demonstrating that the commercial product or commercial service was not developed exclusively at private expense.
L0:Notwithstanding paragraph (e) of the Disputes clause, the final decision will be issued within 60 days after receipt of the
L0:Contractor’s or subcontractor’s response to the challenge notice, or within such longer period that the Contracting Officer
L0:has notified the Contractor or subcontractor that the Government will require. The notification of a longer period for
L0:issuance of a final decision will be made within 60 days after receipt of the response to the challenge notice.
L1:(ii) The Government agrees that it will continue to be bound by the asserted restriction for a period of 90 days from the
L0:issuance of the Contracting Officer’s final decision under paragraph (g)(2)(i) of this clause. The Contractor or
L0:subcontractor agrees that, if it intends to file suit in the United States Court of Federal Claims, it will provide a notice of
L0:intent to file suit to the Contracting Officer within 90 days from the issuance of the Contracting Officer's final decision
L0:under paragraph (g)(2)(i) of this clause. If the Contractor or subcontractor fails to appeal, file suit, or provide a notice of
L0:intent to file suit to the Contracting Officer within the 90-day period, the Government may cancel or ignore the restrictive
L0:markingsthat are based on the asserted restrictions, and the failure of the Contractor or subcontractor to take the required
L0:action constitutes agreement with such Government action.
L1:(iii) The Government agrees that it will continue to be bound by the asserted restriction where a notice of intent to file suit
L0:in the United States Court of Federal Claims is provided to the Contracting Officer within 90 days from the issuance of the
L0:final decision under paragraph (g)(2)(i) of this clause. The Government will no longer be bound, and the Contractor or
L0:subcontractor agrees that the Government may strike or ignore the restrictive marking that is based on the asserted
L0:restriction, if the Contractor or subcontractor fails to file its suit within 1 year after issuance of the final decision.
L0:Notwithstanding the foregoing, where the head of an agency determines, on a nondelegable basis, that urgent or compelling
L0:circumstances will not permit waiting for the filing of a suit in the United States Court of Federal Claims , the Contractor
L0:or subcontractor agrees that the agency may, following notice to the Contractor or subcontractor, authorize release or
L0:disclosure of the technical data. Such agency determination may be made at any time after issuance of the final decision
L0:and will not affect the Contractor's or subcontractor's right to damages against the United States where its asserted
L0:restrictions are ultimately upheld or to pursue other relief, if any, as may be provided by law.
L1:(iv) The Government agrees that it will be bound by the asserted restrictions where an appeal or suit is filed pursuant to the
L0:Contract Disputes statute until final disposition by an agency Board of Contract Appeals or the United States Court of
L0:Federal Claims. Notwithstanding the foregoing, where the head of an agency determines, on a nondelegable basis,
L0:following notice to the Contractor that urgent or compelling circumstances will not permit awaiting the decision by such
L0:Board of Contract Appeals or the United States Court of Federal Claims, the Contractor or subcontractor agrees that the
L0:agency may authorize release or disclosure of the technical data. Such agency determination may be made at any time after
L0:issuance of the final decision and will not affect the Contractor's or subcontractor's right to damages against the United
L0:States where its asserted restrictions are ultimately upheld or to pursue other relief, if any, as may be provided by law.
L1:(h) Final disposition of appeal or suit.
L1:(1) If the Contractor or subcontractor appeals or files suit and if, upon final disposition of the appeal or suit, the
L0:Contracting Officer's decision is sustained—
L1:(i) The restrictive marking that is based on the asserted restriction on the technical data shall be cancelled, corrected, or
L0:ignored; and
L1:(ii) If the asserted restriction is found not to be substantially justified, the Contractor or subcontractor, as appropriate, shall
L0:be liable to the Government for payment of the cost to the Government of reviewing the asserted restriction and the fees
L0:and other expenses (as defined in 28 U.S.C. 2412(d)(2)(A)) incurred by the Government in challenging the asserted
L0:restriction, unless special circumstances would make such payment unjust.
L1:(2) If the Contractor or subcontractor appeals or files suit and if, upon final disposition of the appeal or suit, the
L0:Contracting Officer's decision is not sustained—
L1:(i) The Government will continue to be bound by the restrictive marking; and
L1:(ii) The Government will be liable to the Contractor or subcontractor for payment of fees and other expenses (as defined in
L0:28 U.S.C. 2412(d)(2)(A)) incurred by the Contractor or subcontractor in defending the marking, if the challenge by the
L0:Government is found not to have been made in good faith.
L1:(i) Duration of right to challenge.
L1:(1) The Government may review the validity of any restriction on technical data, delivered or to be delivered under a
L0:contract, asserted by the Contractor or subcontractor. During the period within 6 years of final payment on a contract or
L0:within 6 years of delivery of the technical data to the Government, whichever is later, the Contracting Officer may review
L0:and make a written determination to challenge the restriction. The Government may, however, challenge a restriction on the
L0:release, disclosure, or use of technical data at any time if such technical data—
L1:(i) Are publicly available;
L1:(ii) Have been furnished to the United States without restriction;
L1:(iii) Have been otherwise made available without restriction; or
L1:(iv) Are the subject of a fraudulently asserted use or release restriction.
L1:(2) Only the Contracting Officer's final decision resolving a formal challenge by sustaining the validity of a restrictive
L0:marking constitutes “validation” as addressed in 10 U.S.C. 3785(c).
L1:(j) Decision not to challenge. A decision by the Government, or a determination by the Contracting Officer, to not
L0:challenge the restrictive marking or asserted restriction shall not constitute “validation.”
L1:(k) Privity of contract. The Contractor or subcontractor agrees that the Contracting Officer may transact matters under this
L0:clause directly with subcontractors at any tier that assert restrictions. However, this clause neither creates nor implies
L0:privity of contract between the Government and subcontractor.
L1:(l) Flowdown. The Contractor or subcontractor agrees to insert this clause in contractual instruments, including
L0:subcontracts and other contractual instruments for commercial products or commercial services, with its subcontractors or
L0:suppliers at any tier requiring the delivery of technical data.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.227-7037 — Validation of Asserted Restrictions on Technical Data

title: 252.227-7038 Patent Rights—Ownership by the Contractor (Large Business)
content:
L0:252.227-7038 Patent Rights—Ownership by the Contractor (Large Business).
L0:As prescribed in 227.303 (2), use the following clause:
L0:PATENT RIGHTS—OWNERSHIP BY THE CONTRACTOR (LARGE BUSINESS) (JUN 2012)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Invention” means—
L1:(1) Any invention or discovery that is or may be patentable or otherwise protectable under Title 35 of the United States
L0:Code; or
L1:(2) Any variety of plant that is or may be protectable under the Plant Variety Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 2321, et seq.).
L0:“Made”—
L1:(1) When used in relation to any invention other than a plant variety, means the conception or first actual reduction to
L0:practice of the invention; or
L1:(2) When used in relation to a plant variety, means that the Contractor has at least tentatively determined that the variety
L0:has been reproduced with recognized characteristics.
L0:“Nonprofit organization” means—
L1:(1) A university or other institution of higher education;
L1:(2) An organization of the type described in the Internal Revenue Code at 26 U.S.C. 501(c)(3) and exempt from taxation
L0:under 26 U.S.C. 501(a); or
L1:(3) Any nonprofit scientific or educational organization qualified under a State nonprofit organization statute.
L0:“Practical application” means—
L1:(1)(i) To manufacture, in the case of a composition or product;
L1:(ii) To practice, in the case of a process or method; or
L1:(iii) To operate, in the case of a machine or system; and
L1:(2) In each case, under such conditions as to establish that—
L1:(i) The invention is being utilized; and
L1:(ii) The benefits of the invention are, to the extent permitted by law or Government regulations, available to the public on
L0:reasonable terms.
L0:“Subject invention” means any invention of the Contractor made in the performance of work under this contract.
L1:(b) Contractor’s rights.
L1:(1) Ownership. The Contractor may elect to retain ownership of each subject invention throughout the world in accordance
L0:with the provisions of this clause.
L1:(2) License.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall retain a nonexclusive royalty-free license throughout the world in each subject invention to which
L0:the Government obtains title, unless the Contractor fails to disclose the invention within the times specified in paragraph
L1:(c) of this clause. The Contractor’s license—
L1:(A) Extends to any domestic subsidiaries and affiliates within the corporate structure of which the Contractor is a part;
L1:(B) Includes the right to grant sublicenses to the extent the Contractor was legally obligated to do so at the time of contract
L0:award; and
L1:(C) Is transferable only with the approval of the agency, except when transferred to the successor of that part of the
L0:Contractor’s business to which the invention pertains.
L1:(ii) The agency—
L1:(A) May revoke or modify the Contractor’s domestic license to the extent necessary to achieve expeditious practical
L0:application of the subject invention pursuant to an application for an exclusive license submitted in accordance with 37
L0:CFR Part 404 and agency licensing regulations;
L1:(B) Will not revoke the license in that field of use or the geographical areas in which the Contractor has achieved practical
L0:application and continues to make the benefits of the invention reasonably accessible to the public; and
L1:(C) May revoke or modify the license in any foreign country to the extent the Contractor, its licensees, or the domestic
L0:subsidiaries or affiliates have failed to achieve practical application in that foreign country.
L1:(iii) Before revoking or modifying the license, the agency—
L1:(A) Will furnish the Contractor a written notice of its intention to revoke or modify the license; and
L1:(B) Will allow the Contractor 30 days (or such other time as the funding agency may authorize for good cause shown by
L0:the Contractor) after the notice to show cause why the license should not be revoked or modified.
L1:(iv) The Contractor has the right to appeal, in accordance with 37 CFR Part 404 and agency regulations, concerning the
L0:licensing of Government-owned inventions, any decision concerning the revocation or modification of the license.
L1:(c) Contractor’s obligations.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall—
L1:(i) Disclose, in writing, each subject invention to the Contracting Officer within 2 months after the inventor discloses it in
L0:writing to Contractor personnel responsible for patent matters, or within 6 months after the Contractor first becomes aware
L0:that a subject invention has been made, whichever is earlier;
L1:(ii) Include in the disclosure—
L1:(A) The inventor(s) and the contract under which the invention was made;
L1:(B) Sufficient technical detail to convey a clear understanding of the invention; and
L1:(C) Any publication, on sale (i.e., sale or offer for sale), or public use of the invention and whether a manuscript describing
L0:the invention has been submitted for publication and, if so, whether it has been accepted for publication; and
L1:(iii) After submission of the disclosure, promptly notify the Contracting Officer of the acceptance of any manuscript
L0:describing the invention for publication and of any on sale or public use.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall elect in writing whether or not to retain ownership of any subject invention by notifying the
L0:Contracting Officer at the time of disclosure or within 8 months of disclosure, as to those countries (including the United
L0:States) in which the Contractor will retain ownership. However, in any case where publication, on sale, or public use has
L0:initiated the 1-year statutory period during which valid patent protection can be obtained in the United States, the agency
L0:may shorten the period of election of title to a date that is no more than 60 days prior to the end of the statutory period.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall—
L1:(i) File either a provisional or a nonprovisional patent application on an elected subject invention within 1 year after
L0:election, provided that in all cases the application is filed prior to the end of any statutory period wherein valid patent
L0:protection can be obtained in the United States after a publication, on sale, or public use;
L1:(ii) File a nonprovisional application within 10 months of the filing of any provisional application; and
L1:(iii) File patent applications in additional countries or international patent offices within either 10 months of the first filed
L0:patent application (whether provisional or nonprovisional) or 6 months from the date the Commissioner of Patents grants
L0:permission to file foreign patent applications where such filing has been prohibited by a Secrecy Order.
L1:(4) The Contractor may request extensions of time for disclosure, election, or filing under paragraphs (c)(1), (2), and (3) of
L0:this clause. The Contracting Officer will normally grant the extension unless there is reason to believe the extension would
L0:prejudice the Government’s interests.
L1:(d) Government’s rights.
L1:(1) Ownership. The Contractor shall assign to the agency, upon written request, title to any subject invention—
L1:(i) If the Contractor elects not to retain title to a subject invention;
L1:(ii) If the Contractor fails to disclose or elect the subject invention within the times specified in paragraph (c) of this clause
L0:and the agency requests title within 60 days after learning of the Contractor’s failure to report or elect within the specified
L0:times;
L1:(iii) In those countries in which the Contractor fails to file patent applications within the times specified in paragraph (c) of
L0:this clause, provided that, if the Contractor has filed a patent application in a country after the times specified in paragraph
L1:(c) of this clause, but prior to its receipt of the written request of the agency, the Contractor shall continue to retain
L0:ownership in that country; and
L1:(iv) In any country in which the Contractor decides not to continue the prosecution of any application for, to pay the
L0:maintenance fees on, or defend in reexamination or opposition proceeding on, a patent on a subject invention.
L1:(2) License. If the Contractor retains ownership of any subject invention, the Government shall have a nonexclusive,
L0:nontransferable, irrevocable, paid-up license to practice, or have practiced for or on behalf of the United States, the subject
L0:invention throughout the world.
L1:(e) Contractor action to protect the Government’s interest.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall execute or have executed and promptly deliver to the agency all instruments necessary to—
L1:(i) Establish or confirm the rights the Government has throughout the world in those subject inventions in which the
L0:Contractor elects to retain ownership; and
L1:(ii) Assign title to the agency when requested under paragraph (d)(1) of this clause and enable the Government to obtain
L0:patent protection for that subject invention in any country.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall—
L1:(i) Require, by written agreement, its employees, other than clerical and nontechnical employees, to—
L1:(A) Disclose each subject invention promptly in writing to personnel identified as responsible for the administration of
L0:patent matters, so that the Contractor can comply with the disclosure provisions in paragraph (c) of this clause; and
L1:(B) Provide the disclosure in the Contractor’s format, which should require, as a minimum, the information required by
L0:paragraph (c)(1) of this clause;
L1:(ii) Instruct its employees, through employee agreements or other suitable educational programs, as to the importance of
L0:reporting inventions in sufficient time to permit the filing of patent applications prior to U.S. or statutory foreign bars; and
L1:(iii) Execute all papers necessary to file patent applications on subject inventions and to establish the Government’s rights
L0:in the subject inventions.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer of any decisions not to file a nonprovisional patent application,
L0:continue the prosecution of a patent application, pay maintenance fees, or defend in a reexamination or opposition
L0:proceeding on a patent, in any country, not less than 30 days before the expiration of the response or filing period required
L0:by the relevant patent office.
L1:(4) The Contractor shall include, within the specification of any United States nonprovisional patent application and any
L0:patent issuing thereon covering a subject invention, the following statement: “This invention was made with Government
L0:support under (identify the contract) awarded by (identify the agency). The Government has certain rights in this
L0:invention.”
L1:(5) The Contractor shall—
L1:(i) Establish and maintain active and effective procedures to ensure that subject inventions are promptly identified and
L0:disclosed to Contractor personnel responsible for patent matters;
L1:(ii) Include in these procedures the maintenance of—
L1:(A) Laboratory notebooks or equivalent records and other records as are reasonably necessary to document the conception
L0:and/or the first actual reduction to practice of subject inventions; and
L1:(B) Records that show that the procedures for identifying and disclosing the inventions are followed; and
L1:(iii) Upon request, furnish the Contracting Officer a description of these procedures for evaluation and for determination as
L0:to their effectiveness.
L1:(6) The Contractor shall, when licensing a subject invention, arrange to—
L1:(i) Avoid royalty charges on acquisitions involving Government funds, including funds derived through the Government’s
L0:Military Assistance Program or otherwise derived through the Government;
L1:(ii) Refund any amounts received as royalty charges on the subject inventions in acquisitions for, or on behalf of, the
L0:Government; and
L1:(iii) Provide for the refund in any instrument transferring rights in the invention to any party.
L1:(7) The Contractor shall furnish to the Contracting Officer the following:
L1:(i) Interim reports every 12 months (or any longer period as may be specified by the Contracting Officer) from the date of
L0:the contract, listing subject inventions during that period and stating that all subject inventions have been disclosed or that
L0:there are no subject inventions.
L1:(ii) A final report, within 3 months after completion of the contracted work, listing all subject inventions or stating that
L0:there were no subject inventions, and listing all subcontracts at any tier containing a patent rights clause or stating that
L0:there were no subcontracts.
L1:(8)(i) The Contractor shall promptly notify the Contracting Officer in writing upon the award of any subcontract at any tier
L0:containing a patent rights clause by identifying—
L1:(A) The subcontractor;
L1:(B) The applicable patent rights clause;
L1:(C) The work to be performed under the subcontract; and
L1:(D) The dates of award and estimated completion.
L1:(ii) The Contractor shall furnish, upon request, a copy of the subcontract, and no more frequently than annually, a listing of
L0:the subcontracts that have been awarded.
L1:(9) In the event of a refusal by a prospective subcontractor to accept one of the clauses specified in paragraph (l)(1) of this
L0:clause, the Contractor—
L1:(i) Shall promptly submit a written notice to the Contracting Officer setting forth the subcontractor’s reasons for the refusal
L0:and other pertinent information that may expedite disposition of the matter; and
L1:(ii) Shall not proceed with that subcontract without the written authorization of the Contracting Officer.
L1:(10) The Contractor shall provide to the Contracting Officer, upon request, the following information for any subject
L0:invention for which the Contractor has retained ownership:
L1:(i) Filing date.
L1:(ii) Serial number and title.
L1:(iii) A copy of any patent application (including an English-language version if filed in a language other than English).
L1:(iv) Patent number and issue date.
L1:(11) The Contractor shall furnish to the Government, upon request, an irrevocable power to inspect and make copies of any
L0:patent application file.
L1:(f) Reporting on utilization of subject inventions.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall—
L1:(i) Submit upon request periodic reports no more frequently than annually on the utilization of a subject invention or on
L0:efforts in obtaining utilization of the subject invention that are being made by the Contractor or its licensees or assignees;
L1:(ii) Include in the reports information regarding the status of development, date of first commercial sale or use, gross
L0:royalties received by the Contractor, and other information as the agency may reasonably specify; and
L1:(iii) Provide additional reports that the agency may request in connection with any march-in proceedings undertaken by the
L0:agency in accordance with paragraph (h) of this clause.
L1:(2) To the extent permitted by law, the agency shall not disclose the information provided under paragraph (f)(1) of this
L0:clause to persons outside the Government without the Contractor’s permission, if the data or information is considered by
L0:the Contractor or its licensee or assignee to be “privileged and confidential” (see 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4)) and is so marked.
L1:(g) Preference for United States industry. Notwithstanding any other provision of this clause, the Contractor agrees that
L0:neither the Contractor nor any assignee shall grant to any person the exclusive right to use or sell any subject invention in
L0:the United States unless the person agrees that any products embodying the subject invention or produced through the use
L0:of the subject invention will be manufactured substantially in the United States. However, in individual cases, the agency
L0:may waive the requirement for an exclusive license agreement upon a showing by the Contractor or its assignee that—
L1:(1) Reasonable but unsuccessful efforts have been made to grant licenses on similar terms to potential licensees that would
L0:be likely to manufacture substantially in the United States; or
L1:(2) Under the circumstances, domestic manufacture is not commercially feasible.
L1:(h) March-in rights. The Contractor acknowledges that, with respect to any subject invention in which it has retained
L0:ownership, the agency has the right to require licensing pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 203 and 210(c), 37 CFR 401.6, and any
L0:supplemental regulations of the agency in effect on the date of contract award.
L1:(i) Other inventions. Nothing contained in this clause shall be deemed to grant to the Government any rights with respect to
L0:any invention other than a subject invention.
L1:(j) Examination of records relating to inventions.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer or any authorized representative shall, until 3 years after final payment under this contract,
L0:have the right to examine any books (including laboratory notebooks), records, and documents of the Contractor relating to
L0:the conception or first reduction to practice of inventions in the same field of technology as the work under this contract to
L0:determine whether—
L1:(i) Any inventions are subject inventions;
L1:(ii) The Contractor has established procedures required by paragraph (e)(5) of this clause; and
L1:(iii) The Contractor and its inventors have complied with the procedures.
L1:(2) If the Contracting Officer learns of an unreported Contractor invention that the Contracting Officer believes may be a
L0:subject invention, the Contractor shall be required to disclose the invention to the agency for a determination of ownership
L0:rights.
L1:(3) Any examination of records under this paragraph (j) shall be subject to appropriate conditions to protect the
L0:confidentiality of the information involved.
L1:(k) Withholding of payment (this paragraph does not apply to subcontracts).
L1:(1) Any time before final payment under this contract, the Contracting Officer may, in the Government’s interest, withhold
L0:payment until a reserve not exceeding $50,000 or 5 percent of the amount of the contract, whichever is less, is set aside if,
L0:in the Contracting Officer’s opinion, the Contractor fails to—
L1:(i) Establish, maintain, and follow effective procedures for identifying and disclosing subject inventions pursuant to
L0:paragraph (e)(5) of this clause;
L1:(ii) Disclose any subject invention pursuant to paragraph (c)(1) of this clause;
L1:(iii) Deliver acceptable interim reports pursuant to paragraph (e)(7)(i) of this clause; or
L1:(iv) Provide the information regarding subcontracts pursuant to paragraph (e)(8) of this clause.
L1:(2) The reserve or balance shall be withheld until the Contracting Officer has determined that the Contractor has rectified
L0:whatever deficiencies exist and has delivered all reports, disclosures, and other information required by this clause.
L1:(3) The Government will not make final payment under this contract before the Contractor delivers to the Contracting
L0:Officer—
L1:(i) All disclosures of subject inventions required by paragraph (c)(1) of this clause;
L1:(ii) An acceptable final report pursuant to paragraph (e)(7)(ii) of this clause; and
L1:(iii) All past due confirmatory instruments.
L1:(4) The Contracting Officer may decrease or increase the sums withheld up to the maximum authorized in paragraph (k)(1)
L0:of this clause. No amount shall be withheld under this paragraph while the amount specified by this paragraph is being
L0:withheld under other provisions of the contract. The withholding of any amount or the subsequent payment thereof shall
L0:not be construed as a waiver of any Government right.
L1:(l) Subcontracts.
L1:(1) The Contractor—
L1:(i) Shall include the substance of the Patent Rights—Ownership by the Contractor clause set forth at 52.227-11 of the
L0:Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), in all subcontracts for experimental, developmental, or research work to be
L0:performed by a small business concern or nonprofit organization; and
L1:(ii) Shall include the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (l), in all other subcontracts for experimental,
L0:developmental, or research work, unless a different patent rights clause is required by FAR 27.303.
L1:(2) For subcontracts at any tier—
L1:(i) The patents rights clause included in the subcontract shall retain all references to the Government and shall provide to
L0:the subcontractor all the rights and obligations provided to the Contractor in the clause. The Contractor shall not, as
L0:consideration for awarding the subcontract, obtain rights in the subcontractor’s subject inventions; and
L1:(ii) The Government, the Contractor, and the subcontractor agree that the mutual obligations of the parties created by this
L0:clause constitute a contract between the subcontractor and the Government with respect to those matters covered by this
L0:clause. However, nothing in this paragraph is intended to confer any jurisdiction under the Contract Disputes statute in
L0:connection with proceedings under paragraph (h) of this clause.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:ALTERNATE I (DEC 2007).
L0:As prescribed in 227.303 (2)(ii), add the following paragraph (b)(2)(v) to the basic clause:
L1:(v) The license shall include the right of the Government to sublicense foreign governments, their nationals, and
L0:international organizations pursuant to the following treaties or international agreements: ______________*.
L0:[* Contracting Officer to complete with the names of applicable existing treaties or international agreements. This
L0:paragraph is not intended to apply to treaties or agreements that are in effect on the date of the award but are not listed.]
L0:ALTERNATE II (DEC 2007).
L0:As prescribed in 227.303 (2)(iii), add the following paragraph (b)(2)(v) to the basic clause:
L1:(v) The agency reserves the right to—
L1:(A) Unilaterally amend this contract to identify specific treaties or international agreements entered into or to be entered
L0:into by the Government after the effective date of this contract; and
L1:(B) Exercise those license or other rights that are necessary for the Government to meet its obligations to foreign
L0:governments, their nationals, and international organizations under any treaties or international agreement with respect to
L0:subject inventions made after the date of the amendment.

title: 252.227-7040 Additional Preaward Requirements for Small Business Technology Transfer Program
content:
L0:252.227-7040 Additional Preaward Requirements for Small Business Technology Transfer Program.
L0:As prescribed in 227.7104-4(c)(1), use the following provision:
L0:ADDITIONAL PREAWARD REQUIREMENTS FOR SMALL BUSINESS TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER PROGRAM
L0:(JAN 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this provision, the terms “research institution” and “United States” have the meaning given in
L0:the 252.227-7041, Additional Postaward Requirements for Small Business Technology Transfer Program,clause of this
L0:solicitation.
L1:(b) Offers submitted in response to this solicitation shall include the following:
L1:(1) The written agreement between the Offeror and a research institution, which shall contain—
L1:(i) A specific allocation of ownership, rights, and responsibilities for intellectual property (including inventions, patents,
L0:technical data, and computer software) resulting from the Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Program award;
L1:(ii) Identification of which party to the written agreement may obtain United States or foreign patents or otherwise protect
L0:any inventions that result from a STTR award; and
L1:(iii) No terms or conditions that conflict with the requirements of the clause at 252.227-7018, Rights in Other Than
L0:Commercial Technical Data and Computer Software-Small Business Innovation Research Program and Small Business
L0:Technology Transfer Program, or this provision, including the rights of the United States, the Offeror, and the research
L0:institution regarding intellectual property, and regarding any right to carry out follow-on research.
L1:(2) The Offeror’s written representation that—
L1:(i) The Offeror is satisfied with its written agreement with the research institution; and
L1:(ii) The written agreement does not conflict with the requirements of this solicitation.
L1:(c) The Offeror shall submit the written representation required by paragraph (b)(2) of this provision as an attachment to its
L0:offer, dated and signed by an official authorized to contractually obligate the Offeror.
L1:(d) The Offeror’s failure to submit the written agreement or written representation required by paragraph (b) of this
L0:provision with its offer may render the offer ineligible for award.
L1:(e) If the Offeror is awarded a contract, the Contracting Officer will include the written agreement and written
L0:representation required by paragraph (b) of this provision in an attachment to that contract.
L0:(End of provision)

title: 252.227-7041 Additional Postaward Requirements for Small Business Technology Transfer Program
content:
L0:252.227-7041 Additional Postaward Requirements for Small Business Technology Transfer Program.
L0:As prescribed in 227.7104-4(c)(2), use the following clause:
L0:ADDITIONAL POSTAWARD REQUIREMENTS FOR SMALL BUSINESS TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER PROGRAM
L0:(JAN 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Research institution” means an institution or entity that—
L1:(1) Has a place of business located in the United States;
L1:(2) Operates primarily within the United States or makes a significant contribution to the U.S. economy through payment
L0:of taxes or use of American products, materials, or labor; and
L1:(3) Is either—
L1:(i) A nonprofit institution that is owned and operated exclusively for scientific or educational purposes, no part of the net
L0:earnings of which inures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual (section 4(3) of the Stevenson-Wydler
L0:Technology Innovation Act of 1980); or
L1:(ii) A federally-funded research or research and development center as identified by the National Science Foundation
L0:(https://www.nsf.gov/statistics/ffrdclist/) in accordance with the guidance atFederal Acquisition Regulation 35.017.
L0:“United States” means the 50 States and the District of Columbia, the territories and possessions of the Government, the
L0:Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, and the Republic
L0:of Palau.
L1:(b) Preaward submissions. Attached to this contract are the following documents, submitted by the Contractor pursuant to
L0:Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 252.227-7040, Additional Preaward Requirements for
L0:Small Business Technology Transfer Program:
L1:(1) The written agreement between the Contractor and a research institution.
L1:(2) The Contractor’s written representation that the Contractor is satisfied with that written agreement, which does not
L0:conflict with the clause at DFARS 252.227-7018, Rights in Other Than Commercial Technical Data and Computer
L0:Software-Small Business Innovation Research Program and Small Business Technology Transfer Program, or this clause.
L1:(c) Postaward updates. The Contractor shall not allow any modification to its written agreement with the research
L0:institution, unless the written agreement, as modified, contains—
L1:(1) A specific allocation of ownership, rights, and responsibilities for intellectual property (including inventions, patents,
L0:technical data, and computer software) resulting from performance of this contract;
L1:(2) Identification of which party to the written agreement may obtain United States or foreign patents or otherwise protect
L0:any inventions that result from a Small Business Technology Transfer Program award;
L1:(3) The Contractor’s written, dated, and signed representation that—
L1:(i) The Contractor is satisfied with its written agreement with the research institution, as modified; and
L1:(ii) The written agreement, as modified, does not conflict with the clause at DFARS 252.227-7018, Rights in Other Than
L0:Commercial Technical Data and Computer Software-Small Business Innovation Research Program and Small Business
L0:Technology Transfer Program, or this clause; and
L1:(4) No terms and conditions that conflict with the clause at DFARS 252.227-7018, Rights in Other Than Commercial
L0:Technical Data and Computer Software-Small Business Innovation Research Program and Small Business Technology
L0:Transfer Program, or this clause, including the rights of the United States, the Contractor, and the research institution
L0:regarding intellectual property, and regarding any right to carry out follow-on research.
L1:(d) Submission of updated agreement. Within 30 days of execution of the modified written agreement described in
L0:paragraph (b)(1) of this clause, the Contractor shall submit a copy of that updated written agreement and the updated
L0:written representation described in paragraph (b)(2) of this clause to the Contracting Officer for review and attachment to
L0:this contract.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.228-7001 Ground and Flight Risk
content:
L0:252.228-7001 Ground and Flight Risk.
L0:As prescribed in 228.371 (b), use the following clause:
L0:GROUND AND FLIGHT RISK (MAR 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Aircraft” means, unless otherwise provided in the contract Schedule, any item, other than a rocket or missile, intended for
L0:flight (e.g., fixed-winged aircraft, blended wing/lifting bodies, helicopters, vertical take-off or landing aircraft, lighter-thanair airships, and unmanned aerial vehicles), including emerging technologies that would commonly be considered aircraft.
L0:New production articles become aircraft at a stage of manufacture or production when a wing, portion of a wing, or engine
L0:is attached to a fuselage. Blended wing/lifting bodies become aircraft at a stage of manufacture or production when the
L0:center portion and a lifting surface become attached.
L0:“Contractor’s managerial personnel” means the Contractor’s directors, officers, managers, superintendents, or equivalent
L0:representatives who have supervision or direction of—
L1:(1) All, or substantially all, of the Contractor’s business;
L1:(2) All, or substantially all, of the Contractor’s operation at any one plant or separate location; or
L1:(3) A separate and complete major industrial operation.
L0:“Contractor's premises” means those premises, including subcontractors’ premises, designated in the Schedule or in writing
L0:by the Contracting Officer, and any other place the aircraft is moved for safeguarding.
L0:“Covered aircraft” means an aircraft owned by or to be delivered to the Government and, when determined by the
L0:contracting officer and specifically identified as such in the contract Schedule, may include contractor-furnished aircraft
L0:that are not intended for induction into the DoD inventory, including—
L1:(1) Aircraft furnished by the Government to the Contractor under this contract while in the Contractor’s possession, care,
L0:custody, or control regardless of their location or state of disassembly or reassembly;
L1:(2) Items removed from a Government-furnished aircraft that are—
L1:(i) Intended for reinstallation on that particular aircraft, which retain their status as covered aircraft while awaiting
L0:installation; and
L1:(ii) Not intended for reinstallation on that particular aircraft, which lose their status as covered aircraft once removal is
L0:complete;
L1:(3) New production aircraft when wholly outside of buildings on the Contractor’s premises or other places described in the
L0:Schedule (e.g., hush houses, run stations, and paint facilities); and
L1:(4) Commercial aircraft, to include commercially available off-the-shelf aircraft, become covered aircraft when the
L0:commercial aircraft arrives at the Contractor’s place of performance for modification under the terms of the contract.
L0:“Crewmember” means, unless otherwise provided in the Schedule, personnel required in the flight manual, assigned for the
L0:purpose of conducting any flight on behalf of the Contractor. It also includes any operator of an unmanned aerial vehicle.
L0:“Flight” means any flight approved in writing by the Government flight representative, to include taxi test made in the
L0:performance of this contract, or flight for the purpose of safeguarding the aircraft. All aircraft off the Contractor's premises
L0:shall be considered to be in flight when on the ground or water for reasonable periods of time following emergency
L0:landings, landings made in performance of the contract, or landings approved in writing by the contracting officer.
L0:“Workmanship error” means damage to the aircraft that is the result of an incorrectly performed skill-based task, operation,
L0:or action that was originally planned or intended.
L1:(b) Combined regulation/instruction. The Contractor shall be bound by the operating procedures contained in the combined
L0:regulation/instruction entitled “Contractor’s Flight and Ground Operations” (Air Force Instruction 10-220, Army
L0:Regulation 95-20, NAVAIR Instruction 3710.1 (Series), Coast Guard Instruction M13020.3 , and Defense Contract
L0:Management Agency Instruction 8210 - 1 (Series)) in effect on the date of contract award. Compliance with the combined
L0:regulation/instruction is required from the time of contract award throughout the period of performance of the contract,
L0:regardless of the Government’s assumption of risk under the contract.
L1:(c) Government as self-insurer. The Government self-insures and assumes the risk of damage to, or loss or destruction of,
L0:covered aircraft subject to the following conditions:
L1:(1) The Contractor’s liability to the Government for damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft is limited to the
L0:Contractor’s share of loss as defined at paragraph (h) of this clause, except when one of the exclusions at paragraph (d)
L0:applies.
L1:(2) The liability provisions of this clause take precedence over the liability provisions of Federal Acquisition Regulation
L1:(FAR) clause 52.245-1, Government Property, with respect to covered aircraft.
L1:(3) The Contractor is not liable for loss, damage, or destruction of covered aircraft as the result of normal wear and tear, or
L0:intentional damage or destruction as required in the Schedule.
L1:(4) Conditions for Government assumption of risk in flight are as follows:
L1:(i) The Contractor’s crewmembers are approved in writing by the Government flight representative(GFR).
L1:(ii) The flight is approved in writing by the GFR.
L1:(d) Exclusions from the Government’s assumption of risk. The Government's assumption of risk under this clause shall not
L0:extend to damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft which—
L1:(1) Is the result of willful misconduct or lack of good faith on the part of the Contractor’s managerial personnel, including
L0:the Contractor’s oversight of subcontractors;
L1:(2) Is sustained during flight if either the flight or the crewmembers have not been approved in advance and writing by the
L0:GFR, who has been authorized in accordance with the combined regulation/instruction entitled “Contractor’s Flight and
L0:Ground Operations”;
L1:(3) Occurs in the course of transportation by rail, or by conveyance on public streets, highways, or waterways, unless the
L0:transportation is limited to the vicinity of the Contractor’s premises, and incidental to work performed under the contract as
L0:described in the Schedule;
L1:(4) Is covered by insurance;
L1:(5) Occurs after the Contracting Officer has, in writing, revoked the Government’s assumption of risk in accordance with
L0:paragraph (e)(3) of this clause; or
L1:(6) Is sustained due to workmanship errors.
L1:(e) Revoking the Government’s assumption of risk .
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer, when finding that the Contractor’s managerial personnel have failed to comply with paragraph
L1:(b) of this clause, will issue a preliminary notice of revocation requiring the Contractor to comply with contract
L0:requirements within a timeframe specified by the Contracting Officer. In determining exposure to unreasonable conditions,
L0:the Contracting Officer will consider factors including, but not limited to, the following: lack of adequate hangar fire
L0:suppression or firefighting vehicles, failure to provide adequate procedures to the GFR, or systemic failure to comply with
L0:approved procedures.
L1:(2) Upon receipt of the preliminary notice of revocation, the Contractor shall promptly correct the noncompliance or cited
L0:conditions, regardless of whether there is agreement that the conditions are unreasonable.
L1:(3) If the Contracting Officer finds that the Contractor failed to correct the cited noncompliance or conditions within the
L0:specified timeframe, the Contracting Officer will issue a notice of revocation of the Government’s assumption of risk for
L0:any covered aircraft.
L1:(4) If the Contracting Officer issues a notice of revocation pursuant to the terms of this clause—
L1:(i) The Contractor shall thereafter assume the entire risk for damage, loss, or destruction of the previously covered aircraft;
L1:(ii) Any costs incurred by the Contractor (including the costs of the Contractor’s self-insurance, insurance premiums paid
L0:to insure the Contractor’s assumption of risk, deductibles associated with such purchased insurance, etc.) to mitigate its risk
L0:are unallowable costs; and
L1:(iii) The liability provisions of the clause at FAR 52.245-1, Government Property, are not applicable to the aircraft
L0:impacted by the notice of revocation.
L1:(5) The Contractor shall promptly notify the Contracting Officer when the noncompliance or cited conditions have been
L0:corrected. Within 3 days of receipt of the Contractor’s notice of correction, the Contracting Officer will notify the
L0:Contractor whether the Government will resume risk of loss. The Contracting Officer will determine that the
L0:noncompliance or cited conditions have been corrected prior to resuming assumption of risk.
L1:(6) The notice of revocation does not relieve the Contractor of its obligation to comply with all other provisions of this
L0:clause, including the combined regulation/instruction entitled “Contractor’s Flight and Ground Operations.”
L1:(7) Any disputes regarding the Contracting Officer’s notice of revocation shall be subject to FAR clause 52.233-1,
L0:Disputes.
L1:(f) Contractor’s exclusion of insurance costs. The Contractor warrants that the contract price does not and will not include,
L0:except as may be authorized in this clause, any charge or contingency reserve for insurance (including the Contractor’s
L0:share of loss) covering damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft when the risk has been assumed by the Government,
L0:even if the assumption may be terminated for covered aircraft.
L1:(g) Procedures in the event of damage, loss, or destruction .
L1:(1) In the event of damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft the Contractor shall take all reasonable steps to protect
L0:the aircraft from further damage, to separate damaged and undamaged aircraft and to put all aircraft in the best possible
L0:order. Except in cases covered by paragraph (h)(2) of this clause, the Contractor shall furnish to the Contracting Officer a
L0:statement of—
L1:(i) The damaged, lost, or destroyed aircraft;
L1:(ii) The time and origin of the damage, loss, or destruction;
L1:(iii) All known interests in commingled property of which aircraft are a part; and
L1:(iv) The insurance, if any, covering the interest in commingled property.
L1:(2) If a new production aircraft is damaged, lost, or destroyed before it has become a covered aircraft, the Government
L0:bears no responsibility for risk of loss.
L1:(3) If a new production aircraft is damaged, lost, or destroyed after it has become a covered aircraft, the Contractor shall
L0:take action in accordance with the Contracting Officer’s written direction that the aircraft shall be—
L1:(i) Replaced;
L1:(ii) Repaired to the condition immediately prior to the damage; or
L1:(iii) Considered beyond economic repair. The Contracting Officer will decide whether further actions are required under
L0:the contract.
L1:(4) If a covered aircraft that has been furnished by the Government to the Contractor is damaged, lost, or destroyed while
L0:covered, the Contractor shall take action in accordance with the Contracting Officer’s written direction that the aircraft
L0:shall be—
L1:(i) Repaired; or
L1:(ii) Considered beyond economic repair. The Contracting Officer will decide further actions required under the contract.
L1:(5) The Contracting Officer will make an equitable adjustment for expenditures made in performing the obligations under
L0:this paragraph (g).
L1:(h) Contractor’s share of loss.
L1:(1) The Contractor’s share of loss or damage to covered aircraft, except for loss or damage caused by negligence of
L0:Government personnel, is the least of—
L1:(i) $200,000;
L1:(ii) 20 percent of the price or estimated acquisition cost of affected aircraft; or
L1:(iii) 20 percent of the price or estimated cost of the contract, task order, or delivery order.
L1:(2) If the Government requires covered aircraft be replaced or repaired by the Contractor, any resulting equitable
L0:adjustment shall not include reimbursement of the Contractor’s share of loss.
L1:(3) In the event the Government does not decide to replace or repair, the Contractor agrees to credit the contract price or
L0:pay the Government, as directed by the Contracting Officer, the least of—
L1:(i) $200,000;
L1:(ii) 20 percent of the price or estimated acquisition cost of affected aircraft; or
L1:(iii) 20 percent of the price or estimated cost of the contract, task order, or delivery order.
L1:(4) The costs incurred by the Contractor for its share of the loss and for insuring against that loss are unallowable costs,
L0:including but not limited to—
L1:(i) The Contractor’s share of loss under the Government’s self-insurance;
L1:(ii) The costs of the Contractor’s self-insurance;
L1:(iii) The deductible for any Contractor-purchased insurance;
L1:(iv) Insurance premiums paid for Contractor-purchased insurance; and
L1:(v) Costs associated with determining, litigating, and defending against the Contractor’s liability.
L1:(i) Reimbursement from a third party. In the event the Contractor is reimbursed or compensated by a third party for
L0:damage, loss, or destruction of covered aircraft and has also been compensated by the Government, the Contractor shall
L0:equitably reimburse the Government. The Contractor shall do nothing to prejudice the Government's right to recover
L0:against third parties for damage, loss, or destruction. Upon the request of the Contracting Officer or authorized
L0:representative, the Contractor shall at Government expense furnish to the Government all reasonable assistance and
L0:cooperation (including the prosecution of suit and the execution of instruments of assignment or subrogation) in obtaining
L0:recovery.
L1:(j) Liability to third parties. Unless the flight and crewmembers have been approved in writing by the GFR, the Contractor
L0:shall not be reimbursed for liability to third parties for loss or damage to property or for death or bodily injury caused by
L0:covered aircraft during flight, even if the Government has accepted such liability under any other provisions of the
L0:contract.
L1:(k) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall incorporate the requirements of this clause, including this paragraph (k), in
L0:subcontracts to include subcontracts for commercial products and commercial services, except—

L0:Administration (FAA) part 145 repair stations performing work pursuant to their FAA license.

title: 252.228-7003 Capture and Detention
content:
L0:252.228-7003 Capture and Detention.
L0:As prescribed in 228.371 (c), use the following clause:
L0:CAPTURE AND DETENTION (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) As used in this clause—
L1:(1) “Captured person” means any employee of the Contractor who is—
L1:(i) Assigned to duty outside the United States for the performance of this contract; and
L1:(ii) Found to be missing from his or her place of employment under circumstances that make it appear probable that the
L0:absence is due to the action of the force of any power not allied with the United States in a common military effort; or
L1:(iii) Known to have been taken prisoner, hostage, or otherwise detained by the force of such power, whether or not actually
L0:engaged in employment at the time of capture; provided, that at the time of capture or detention, the person was either—
L1:(A) Engaged in activity directly arising out of and in the course of employment under this contract; or
L1:(B) Captured in an area where required to be only in order to perform this contract.
L1:(2) A “period of detention” begins with the day of capture and continues until the captured person is returned to the place
L0:of employment, the United States, or is able to be returned to the jurisdiction of the United States, or until the person's
L0:death is established or legally presumed to have occurred by evidence satisfactory to the Contracting Officer, whichever
L0:occurs first.
L1:(3) “United States” comprises geographically the 50 states and the District of Columbia.
L1:(4) “War Hazards Compensation Act” refers to the statute compiled in Chapter 12 of Title 42, U.S. Code (sections 17011717), as amended.
L1:(b) If pursuant to an agreement entered into prior to capture, the Contractor is obligated to pay and has paid detention
L0:benefits to a captured person, or the person's dependents, the Government will reimburse the Contractor up to an amount
L0:equal to the lesser of—
L1:(1) Total wage or salary being paid at the time of capture due from the Contractor to the captured person for the period of
L0:detention; or
L1:(2) That amount which would have been payable if the detention had occurred under circumstances covered by the War
L0:Hazards Compensation Act.
L1:(c) The period of detention shall not be considered as time spent in contract performance, and the Government shall not be
L0:obligated to make payment for that time except as provided in this clause.
L1:(d) The obligation of the Government shall apply to the entire period of detention, except that it is subject to the availability
L0:of funds from which payment can be made. The rights and obligations of the parties under this clause shall survive prior
L0:expiration, completion, or termination of this contract.
L1:(e) The Contractor shall not be reimbursed under this clause for payments made if the employees were entitled to
L0:compensation for capture and detention under the War Hazards Compensation Act, as amended.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.228-7007 Public Aircraft and State Aircraft Operations—Liability
content:
L0:252.228-7007 Public Aircraft and State Aircraft Operations—Liability.
L0:As prescribed in 228.371(f), use the following clause:
L0:PUBLIC AIRCRAFT AND STATE AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS—LIABILITY (MAR 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Civil aircraft” means an aircraft other than a public aircraft or state aircraft.
L0:“Public aircraft” means an aircraft that meets the definition in 49 U.S.C. 40102(a)(41) and the qualifications in 49 U.S.C.
L0:40125. Specifically, a public aircraft means any of the following:
L1:(1) An aircraft used only for the Government, except as provided in paragraphs (5) and (7) of this definition.
L1:(2) An aircraft owned by the Government and operated by any person for purposes related to crew training, equipment
L0:development, or demonstration, except as provided in paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(3) An aircraft owned and operated by the government of a State, the District of Columbia, or a territory or possession of
L0:the United States or a political subdivision of one of these governments, except as provided in paragraph (7) of this
L0:definition.
L1:(4) An aircraft exclusively leased for at least 90 continuous days by the government of a State, the District of Columbia, or
L0:a territory or possession of the United States or a political subdivision of one of these governments, except as provided in
L0:paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(5) An aircraft owned or operated by the armed forces or chartered to provide transportation or other commercial air
L0:service to the armed forces under the conditions specified by 49 U.S.C. 40125(c). In the preceding sentence, the term
L0:“other commercial air service” means an aircraft operation that—
L1:(i) Is within the United States territorial airspace;
L1:(ii) The Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration determines is available for compensation or hire to the
L0:public; and
L1:(iii) Must comply with all applicable civil aircraft rules under title 14, Code of Federal Regulations.
L1:(6) An unmanned aircraft that is owned and operated, or exclusively leased for at least 90 continuous days, by an Indian
L0:Tribal government, as defined in section 102 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42
L0:U.S.C. 5122), except as provided in paragraph (7) of this definition.
L1:(7) As described in 49 U.S.C. 40125(b), an aircraft described in paragraph (1), (2), (3), or (4) of this definition does not
L0:qualify as a public aircraft when the aircraft is used for commercial purposes or to carry an individual other than a
L0:crewmember or a qualified non-crewmember.
L0:“Public aircraft operation” means operation of an aircraft that meets the legal definition of public aircraft established in 49
L0:U.S.C. 40102(a)(41) and the legal qualifications for public aircraft status outlined in 49 U.S.C. 40125.
L0:“State aircraft” means an aircraft operated by the Government for sovereign, noncommercial purposes such as military,
L0:customs, and police services. Military aircraft are afforded status as state aircraft. In very rare circumstances, DoDcontracted aircraft may be designated, in writing, by a responsible Government official pursuant to DoD Directive
L0:4500.54E, DoD Foreign Clearance Program, to be operated in state aircraft status, and such status cannot be deemed
L0:without a written designation by an authorized Government official.
L1:(b) Combined regulation/instruction. Upon award, for contract performance to be conducted as a public aircraft operation,
L0:the Contractor shall be bound by the operating procedures contained in the combined regulation/instruction entitled
L0:“Contractor’s Flight and Ground Operations” (Air Force Instruction 10-220, Army Regulation 95-20, NAVAIR Instruction
L0:3710.1 (Series), Coast Guard Instruction M13020.3 (Series), and Defense Contract Management Agency Instruction 82101 (Series)) in effect on the date of contract award.
L1:(c) Contractor liability for operations for contract performance conducted as public aircraft operations or state aircraft
L0:operations.
L1:(1) The Contractor assumes responsibility for all damage or injury to persons or property, including the Contractor’s
L0:employees and property, and Government personnel and property, occasioned through the use, maintenance, and operation
L0:of the Contractor’s aircraft or other equipment by, or the action of, the Contractor or the Contractor’s employees and
L0:agents.
L1:(2) The Contractor, at the Contractor’s expense, shall maintain adequate public liability and property damage insurance,
L0:including hull insurance for the Contractor’s aircraft, during the duration of this contract, insuring the Contractor against all
L0:claims for injury or damage.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall maintain workers’ compensation and other legally required insurance with respect to the
L0:Contractor’s own employees and agents.
L1:(4) The Government will in no event be liable or responsible for damage or injury to any person or property occasioned
L0:through the use, maintenance, or operation of any aircraft or other equipment by, or the action of, the Contractor or the
L0:Contractor’s employees and agents in performing under this contract, and the Government shall be indemnified and saved
L0:harmless against claims for damage or injury in such cases.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.228-7007 — Public Aircraft and State Aircraft Operations—Liability

L0:articles 11, 14, 15, 17, and 18 of the Agreement on Friendship, Defense and Cooperation between the United States
L0:Government and the Kingdom of Spain, dated July 2, 1982. The Agreement relates to contracts to be performed in whole
L0:or part in Spain, the provisions of which are hereby incorporated into and made a part of this contract by reference.

L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Contract financing payment” means an authorized Government disbursement of monies to a contractor prior to acceptance
L0:of supplies or services by the Government.
L1:(1) Contract financing payments include—
L1:(i) Advance payments;

L1:(ii) Payments for partial deliveries; or
L1:(iii) Lease and rental payments.
L0:“Electronic form” means any automated system that transmits information electronically from the initiating system to
L0:affected systems.
L0:“Invoice payment” means a Government disbursement of monies to a contractor under a contract or other authorization for
L0:supplies or services accepted by the Government.

L0:Prompt Payment, is used.

L0:section of this contract or task or delivery order;

title: 252.232-7010 Levies on Contract Payments
content:
L0:252.232-7010 Levies on Contract Payments.
L0:As prescribed in 232.7102 , use the following clause:
L0:LEVIES ON CONTRACT PAYMENTS (DEC 2006)
L1:(a) 26 U.S.C. 6331(h) authorizes the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to continuously levy up to 100 percent of contract
L0:payments, up to the amount of tax debt.
L1:(b) When a levy is imposed on a payment under this contract and the Contractor believes that the levy may result in an
L0:inability to perform the contract, the Contractor shall promptly notify the Procuring Contracting Officer in writing, with a
L0:copy to the Administrative Contracting Officer, and shall provide—
L1:(1) The total dollar amount of the levy;
L1:(2) A statement that the Contractor believes that the levy may result in an inability to perform the contract, including
L0:rationale and adequate supporting documentation; and
L1:(3) Advice as to whether the inability to perform may adversely affect national security, including rationale and adequate
L0:supporting documentation.
L1:(c) DoD shall promptly review the Contractor’s assessment, and the Procuring Contracting Officer shall provide a written
L0:notification to the Contractor including-
L1:(1) A statement as to whether DoD agrees that the levy may result in an inability to perform the contract; and
L1:(2)(i) If the levy may result in an inability to perform the contract and the lack of performance will adversely affect national
L0:security, the total amount of the monies collected that should be returned to the Contractor; or
L1:(ii) If the levy may result in an inability to perform the contract but will not impact national security, a recommendation
L0:that the Contractor promptly notify the IRS to attempt to resolve the tax situation.
L1:(d) Any DoD determination under this clause is not subject to appeal under the Contract Disputes Act.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.232-7011 Payments in Support of Emergencies and Contingency Operations
content:

L1:(a) Definitions of pertinent terms are set forth in sections 2.101, 32.001, and 32.902 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation.

L1:(v) Shipping and payment terms (e.g., shipment number and date of shipment, discount for prompt payment terms). Bill of

L1:(3) Discounts for prompt payment. The designated payment office will take cost-effective discounts if the payment is made

title: 252.234-7001 Notice of Earned Value Management System
content:

L0:As prescribed in 234.203 (1), use the following provision:
L0:NOTICE OF EARNED VALUE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (APR 2008)
L1:(a) If the offeror submits a proposal in the amount of $50,000,000 or more—
L1:(1) The offeror shall provide documentation that the Cognizant Federal Agency (CFA) has determined that the proposed
L0:Earned Value Management System (EVMS) complies with the EVMS guidelines in the American National Standards
L0:Institute/Electronic Industries Alliance Standard 748, Earned Value Management Systems (ANSI/EIA-748) (current
L0:version at time of solicitation). The Government reserves the right to perform reviews of the EVMS when deemed

L1:(2) If the offeror proposes to use a system that has not been determined to be in compliance with the requirements of
L0:paragraph (a)(1) of this provision, the offeror shall submit a comprehensive plan for compliance with the guidelines in
L0:ANSI/EIA-748.
L1:(i) The plan shall—
L1:(A) Describe the EVMS the offeror intends to use in performance of the contract, and how the proposed EVMS complies
L0:with the EVMS guidelines in ANSI/EIA-748;
L1:(B) Distinguish between the offeror’s existing management system and modifications proposed to meet the EVMS
L0:guidelines;
L1:(C) Describe the management system and its application in terms of the EVMS guidelines;
L1:(D) Describe the proposed procedure for administration of the EVMS guidelines as applied to subcontractors; and
L1:(E) Describe the process the offeror will use to determine subcontractor compliance with ANSI/EIA-748.
L1:(ii) The offeror shall provide information and assistance as required by the Contracting Officer to support review of the
L0:plan.
L1:(iii) The offeror’s EVMS plan must provide milestones that indicate when the offeror anticipates that the EVMS will be
L0:compliant with the guidelines in ANSI/EIA-748.
L1:(b) If the offeror submits a proposal in an amount less than $50,000,000—
L1:(1) The offeror shall submit a written description of the management procedures it will use and maintain in the
L0:performance of any resultant contract to comply with the requirements of the Earned Value Management System clause of
L0:the contract. The description shall include—
L1:(i) A matrix that correlates each guideline in ANSI/EIA-748 (current version at time of solicitation) to the corresponding
L0:process in the offeror’s written management procedures; and
L1:(ii) The process the offeror will use to determine subcontractor compliance with ANSI/EIA-748.
L1:(2) If the offeror proposes to use an EVMS that has been determined by the CFA to be in compliance with the EVMS
L0:guidelines in ANSI/EIA-748, the offeror may submit a copy of the documentation of such determination instead of the
L0:written description required by paragraph (b)(1) of this provision.
L1:(c) The offeror shall identify the subcontractors (or the subcontracted effort if subcontractors have not been selected) to
L0:whom the EVMS requirements will apply. The offeror and the Government shall agree to the subcontractors or the
L0:subcontracted effort selected for application of the EVMS requirements. The offeror shall be responsible for ensuring that
