title: 252.234-7002 Earned Value Management System
content:
L0:252.234-7002 Earned Value Management System.
L0:As prescribed in 234.203 (2), use the following clause:
L0:EARNED VALUE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (JAN 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause——
L0:“Acceptable earned value management system” means an earned value management system that generally complies with
L0:system criteria in paragraph (b) of this clause.
L0:“Earned value management system” means an earned value management system that complies with the earned value
L0:management system guidelines in the ANSI/EIA-748.
L0:“Material weakness” means a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the internal control over information in
L0:contractor business systems, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of such information will
L0:not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A reasonable possibility exists when the likelihood of an
L0:event occurring is—
L1:(1) Probable; or
L1:(2) More than remote but less than likely (section 806 of Pub. L. 116-283).
L1:(b) System criteria. In the performance of this contract, the Contractor shall use—
L1:(1) An Earned Value Management System (EVMS) that complies with the EVMS guidelines in the American National
L0:Standards Institute/Electronic Industries Alliance Standard 748, Earned Value Management Systems (ANSI/EIA-748); and
L1:(2) Management procedures that provide for generation of timely, reliable, and verifiable information for the Contract
L0:Performance Report (CPR) and the Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) required by the CPR and IMS data items of this
L0:contract.
L1:(c) If this contract has a value of $50 million or more, the Contractor shall use an EVMS that has been determined to be
L0:acceptable by the Cognizant Federal Agency (CFA). If, at the time of award, the Contractor’s EVMS has not been
L0:determined by the CFA to be in compliance with the EVMS guidelines as stated in paragraph (b)(1) of this clause, the
L0:Contractor shall apply its current system to the contract and shall take necessary actions to meet the milestones in the
L0:Contractor’s EVMS plan.
L1:(d) If this contract has a value of less than $50 million, the Government will not make a formal determination that the
L0:Contractor’s EVMS complies with the EVMS guidelines in ANSI/EIA-748 with respect to the contract. The use of the
L0:Contractor’s EVMS for this contract does not imply a Government determination of the Contractor’s compliance with the
L0:EVMS guidelines in ANSI/EIA-748 for application to future contracts. The Government will allow the use of a
L0:Contractor’s EVMS that has been formally reviewed and determined by the CFA to be in compliance with the EVMS
L0:guidelines in ANSI/EIA-748.
L1:(e) The Contractor shall submit notification of any proposed substantive changes to the EVMS procedures and the impact
L0:of those changes to the CFA. If this contract has a value of $50 million or more, unless a waiver is granted by the CFA, any
L0:EVMS changes proposed by the Contractor require approval of the CFA prior to implementation. The CFA will advise the
L0:Contractor of the acceptability of such changes as soon as practicable (generally within 30 calendar days) after receipt of
L0:the Contractor’s notice of proposed changes. If the CFA waives the advance approval requirements, the Contractor shall
L0:disclose EVMS changes to the CFA at least 14 calendar days prior to the effective date of implementation.
L1:(f) The Government will schedule integrated baseline reviews as early as practicable, and the review process will be
L0:conducted not later than 180 calendar days after—
L1:(1) Contract award;
L1:(2) The exercise of significant contract options; and
L1:(3) The incorporation of major modifications.
L0:During such reviews, the Government and the Contractor will jointly assess the Contractor’s baseline to be used for
L0:performance measurement to ensure complete coverage of the statement of work, logical scheduling of the work activities,
L0:adequate resourcing, and identification of inherent risks.
L1:(g) The Contractor shall provide access to all pertinent records and data requested by the Contracting Officer or duly
L0:authorized representative as necessary to permit Government surveillance to ensure that the EVMS complies, and
L0:continues to comply, with the performance criteria referenced in paragraph (b) of this clause.
L1:(h) When indicated by contract performance, the Contractor shall submit a request for approval to initiate an over-target
L0:baseline or over-target schedule to the Contracting Officer. The request shall include a top-level projection of cost and/or
L0:schedule growth, a determination of whether or not performance variances will be retained, and a schedule of
L0:implementation for the rebaselining. The Government will acknowledge receipt of the request in a timely manner
L0:(generally within 30 calendar days).
L1:(i) Material weaknesses.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer will provide an initial determination to the Contractor, in writing, of any material weaknesses.
L0:The initial determination will describe the underlying deficiency in sufficient detail to allow the Contractor to understand
L0:the weakness or deficiency.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that
L0:identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor’s EVMS. If the Contractor disagrees with the initial determination, the
L0:Contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.
L1:(3) The Contracting Officer will evaluate the Contractor's response and notify the Contractor, in writing, of the Contracting
L0:Officer’s final determination concerning—
L1:(i) Remaining material weaknesses;
L1:(ii) The adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action;
L1:(iii) System noncompliance, when the Contractor’s existing EVMS fails to comply with the earned value management
L0:system guidelines in the ANSI/EIA-748; and
L1:(iv) System disapproval, if initial EVMS validation is not successfully completed within the timeframe approved by the
L0:Contracting Officer, or if the Contracting Officer determines that the Contractor’s earned value management system
L0:contains one or more material weaknesses in high-risk guidelines in ANSI/EIA-748 standards (guidelines 1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9,
L0:10, 12, 16, 21, 23, 26, 27, 28, 30, or 32). When the Contracting Officer determines that the existing earned value
L0:management system contains one or more material weaknesses in one or more of the remaining 16 guidelines in
L0:ANSI/EIA-748 standards, the Contracting Officer will use discretion to disapprove the system based on input received
L0:from functional specialists and the auditor.
L1:(4) If the Contractor receives the Contracting Officer’s final determination of material weaknesses, the Contractor shall,
L0:within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable
L0:corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the material weaknesses.
L1:(j) Withholding payments. If the Contracting Officer makes a final determination to disapprove the Contractor’s EVMS,
L0:and the contract includes the clause at 252.242-7005 , Contractor Business Systems, the Contracting Officer will withhold
L0:payments in accordance with that clause.
L1:(k) Subcontracts. With the exception of paragraphs (i) and (j) of this clause, the Contractor shall require its subcontractors
L0:to comply with EVMS requirements as follows:
L1:(1) For subcontracts valued at $50 million or more, the following subcontractors shall comply with the requirements of this
L0:clause:
L0:[Contracting Officer to insert names of subcontractors (or subcontracted effort if subcontractors have not been selected)
L0:designated for application of the EVMS requirements of this clause.]
L1:(2) For subcontracts valued at less than $50 million, the following subcontractors shall comply with the requirements of
L0:this clause, excluding the requirements of paragraph (c) of this clause:
L0:[Contracting Officer to insert names of subcontractors (or subcontracted effort if subcontractors have not been selected)
L0:designated for application of the EVMS requirements of this clause.]

title: 252.235-7000 Indemnification Under 10 U.S.C. 3861—Fixed Price
content:
L0:252.235-7000 Indemnification Under 10 U.S.C. 3861—Fixed Price.
L0:As prescribed in 235.070-3 , use the following clause:
L0:INDEMNIFICATION UNDER 10 U.S.C. 3861—FIXED PRICE (DEC 2022)
L1:(a) This clause provides for indemnification under 10 U.S.C. 3861 if the Contractor meets all the terms and conditions of
L0:this clause.
L1:(b) Claims, losses, and damages covered—
L1:(1) Claims by third persons for death, bodily injury, sickness, or disease, or the loss, damage, or lost use of property.
L0:Claims include those for reasonable expenses of litigation or settlement. The term “third persons” includes employees of
L0:the contractor;
L1:(2) The loss, damage, and lost use of the Contractor's property, but excluding lost profit; and
L1:(3) Loss, damage, or lost use of the Government's property.
L1:(c) The claim, loss, or damage—
L1:(1) Must arise from the direct performance of this contract;
L1:(2) Must not be compensated by insurance or other means, or be within deductible amounts of the Contractor's insurance;
L1:(3) Must result from an unusually hazardous risk as specifically defined in the contract;
L1:(4) Must not result from willful misconduct or lack of good faith on the part of any of the Contractor's directors or officers,
L0:managers, superintendents, or other equivalent representatives who have supervision or direction of—
L1:(i) All or substantially all of the Contractor's business;
L1:(ii) All or substantially all of the Contractor's operations at any one plant or separate location where this contract is being
L0:performed; or
L1:(iii) A separate and complete major industrial operation connected with the performance of this contract;
L1:(5) Must not be a liability assumed under any contract or agreement (except for subcontracts covered by paragraph (h) of
L0:this clause), unless the Contracting Officer (or in contracts with the Department of the Navy, the Department) specifically
L0:approved the assumption of liability; and
L1:(6) Must be certified as just and reasonable by the Secretary of the department or designated representative.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall buy and maintain, to the extent available, insurance against unusually hazardous risks in the form,
L0:amount, period(s) of time, at the rate(s), and with such insurers, as the Contracting Officer (or, for Navy contracts, the
L0:Department) may from time to time require and approve. If the cost of this insurance is higher than the cost of the
L0:insurance the Contractor had as of the date of the contract, the Government shall reimburse the Contractor for the
L0:difference in cost, as long as it is properly allocable to this contract and is not included in the contract price. The
L0:Government shall not be liable for claims, loss, or damage if insurance was available and is either required or approved
L0:under this paragraph.
L1:(e) A reduction of the insurance coverage maintained by the Contractor on the date of the execution of this contract shall
L0:not increase the Government's liability under this clause unless the Contracting Officer consents, and the contract price is
L0:equitably adjusted, if appropriate, to reflect the Contractor's consideration for the Government's assumption of increased
L0:liability.
L1:(f) Notice. The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Promptly notify the Contracting Officer of any occurrence, action, or claim that might trigger the Government's liability
L0:under this clause;
L1:(2) Furnish the proof or evidence of any claim, loss, or damage in the form and manner that the Government requires; and
L1:(3) Immediately provide copies of all pertinent papers that the Contractor receives or has received.
L1:(g) The Government may direct, participate in, and supervise the settlement or defense of the claim or action. The
L0:Contractor shall comply with the Government's directions and execute any authorizations required.
L1:(h) Flowdown. The Government shall indemnify the Contractor if the Contractor has an obligation to indemnify a
L0:subcontractor under any subcontract at any tier under this contract for the unusually hazardous risk identified in this
L0:contract only if—
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer gave prior written approval for the Contractor to provide in a subcontract for the Contractor to
L0:indemnify the subcontractor for unusually hazardous risks defined in this contract;
L1:(2) The Contracting Officer approved those indemnification provisions;
L1:(3) The subcontract indemnification provisions entitle the Contractor, or the Government, or both, to direct, participate in,
L0:and supervise the settlement or defense of relevant actions and claims; and
L1:(4) The subcontract provides the same rights and duties, the same provisions for notice, furnishing of papers and the like,
L0:between the Contractor and the subcontractor, as exist between the Government and the Contractor under this clause.
L1:(i) The Government may discharge its obligations under paragraph (h) of this clause by making payments directly to
L0:subcontractors or to persons to whom the subcontractors may be liable.
L1:(j) The rights and obligations of the parties under this clause shall survive the termination, expiration, or completion of this
L0:contract.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.235-7004 Protection of Human Subjects
content:
L0:252.235-7004 Protection of Human Subjects.
L0:As prescribed in 235.072 (e), use the following clause:
L0:PROTECTION OF HUMAN SUBJECTS (JUL 2009)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) “Assurance of compliance” means a written assurance that an institution will comply with requirements of 32 CFR Part
L0:219, as well as the terms of the assurance, which the Human Research Protection Official determines to be appropriate for
L0:the research supported by the Department of Defense (DoD) component (32 CFR 219.103).
L1:(2) “Human Research Protection Official (HRPO)” means the individual designated by the head of the applicable DoD
L0:component and identified in the component’s Human Research Protection Management Plan as the official who is
L0:responsible for the oversight and execution of the requirements of this clause, although some DoD components may use a
L0:different title for this position.
L1:(3) “Human subject” means a living individual about whom an investigator (whether professional or student) conducting
L0:research obtains data through intervention or interaction with the individual, or identifiable private information (32 CFR
L0:219.102(f)). For example, this could include the use of human organs, tissue, and body fluids from individually identifiable
L0:living human subjects as well as graphic, written, or recorded information derived from individually identifiable living
L0:human subjects.
L1:(4) “Institution” means any public or private entity or agency (32 CFR 219.102(b)).
L1:(5) “Institutional Review Board (IRB)” means a board established for the purposes expressed in 32 CFR Part 219 (32 CFR
L0:219.102(g)).
L1:(6) “IRB approval” means the determination of the IRB that the research has been reviewed and may be conducted at an
L0:institution within the constraints set forth by the IRB and by other institutional and Federal requirements (32 CFR
L0:219.102(h)).
L1:(7) “Research” means a systematic investigation, including research, development, testing, and evaluation, designed to
L0:develop or contribute to generalizable knowledge. Activities that meet this definition constitute research for purposes of 32
L0:CFR Part 219, whether or not they are conducted or supported under a program that is considered research for other
L0:purposes. For example, some demonstration and service programs may include research activities (32 CFR 219.102(d)).
L1:(b) The Contractor shall oversee the execution of the research to ensure compliance with this clause. The Contractor shall
L0:comply fully with 32 CFR Part 219 and DoD Directive 3216.02, applicable DoD component policies, 10 U.S.C. 980, and,
L0:when applicable, Food and Drug Administration policies and regulations.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall not commence performance of research involving human subjects that is covered under 32 CFR
L0:Part 219 or that meets exemption criteria under 32 CFR 219.101(b), or expend funding on such effort, until and unless the
L0:conditions of either the following paragraph (c)(1) or (c)(2) have been met:
L1:(1) The Contractor furnishes to the HRPO, with a copy to the Contracting Officer, an assurance of compliance and IRB
L0:approval and receives notification from the Contracting Officer that the HRPO has approved the assurance as appropriate
L0:for the research under the Statement of Work and also that the HRPO has reviewed the protocol and accepted the IRB
L0:approval for compliance with the DoD component policies. The Contractor may furnish evidence of an existing assurance
L0:of compliance for acceptance by the HRPO, if an appropriate assurance has been approved in connection with previous
L0:research. The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer immediately of any suspensions or terminations of the
L0:assurance.
L1:(2) The Contractor furnishes to the HRPO, with a copy to the Contracting Officer, a determination that the human research
L0:proposed meets exemption criteria in 32 CFR 219.101(b) and receives written notification from the Contracting Officer
L0:that the exemption is determined acceptable. The determination shall include citation of the exemption category under 32
L0:CFR 219.101(b) and a rationale statement. In the event of a disagreement regarding the Contractor’s furnished exemption
L0:determination, the HRPO retains final judgment on what research activities or classes of research are covered or are
L0:exempt under the contract.
L1:(d) DoD staff, consultants, and advisory groups may independently review and inspect the Contractor’s research and
L0:research procedures involving human subjects and, based on such findings, DoD may prohibit research that presents
L0:unacceptable hazards or otherwise fails to comply with DoD procedures.
L1:(e) Failure of the Contractor to comply with the requirements of this clause will result in the issuance of a stop-work order
L0:under Federal Acquisition Regulation clause 52.242-15 to immediately suspend, in whole or in part, work and further

title: 252.236-7005 Airfield Safety Precautions
content:
L0:252.236-7005 Airfield Safety Precautions.
L0:As prescribed in 236.570 (b)(3), use the following clause. At some airfields, the width of the primary surface is 1,500 feet
L0:(750 feet on each side of the runway centerline). In such instances, substitute the proper width in the clause.
L0:AIRFIELD SAFETY PRECAUTIONS (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:(1) “Landing areas” means—
L1:(i) The primary surfaces, comprising the surface of the runway, runway shoulders, and lateral safety zones. The length of
L0:each primary surface is the same as the runway length. The width of each primary surface is 2,000 feet (1,000 feet on each
L0:side of the runway centerline);
L1:(ii) The “clear zone” beyond the ends of each runway, i.e., the extension of the primary surface for a distance of 1,000 feet
L0:beyond each end of each runway;
L1:(iii) All taxiways, plus the lateral clearance zones along each side for the length of the taxiways (the outer edge of each
L0:lateral clearance zone is laterally 250 feet from the far or opposite edge of the taxiway, e.g., a 75-foot-wide taxiway would
L0:have a combined width of taxiway and lateral clearance zones of 425 feet); and
L1:(iv) All aircraft parking aprons, plus the area 125 feet in width extending beyond each edge all around the aprons.
L1:(2) “Safety precaution areas” means those portions of approach-departure clearance zones and transitional zones where
L0:placement of objects incident to contract performance might result in vertical projections at or above the approachdeparture clearance, or the transitional surface.
L1:(i) The “approach-departure clearance surface” is an extension of the primary surface and the clear zone at each end of
L0:each runway, for a distance of 50,000 feet, first along an inclined (glide angle) and then along a horizontal plane, both
L0:flaring symmetrically about the runway centerline extended.
L1:(A) The inclined plane (glide angle) begins in the clear zone 200 feet past the end of the runway (and primary surface) at
L0:the same elevation as the end of the runway. It continues upward at a slope of 50:1 (1 foot vertically for each 50 feet
L0:horizontally) to an elevation of 500 feet above the established airfield elevation. At that point the plane becomes horizontal,
L0:continuing at that same uniform elevation to a point 50,000 feet longitudinally from the beginning of the inclined plane
L0:(glide angle) and ending there.
L1:(B) The width of the surface at the beginning of the inclined plane (glide angle) is the same as the width of the clear zone.
L0:It then flares uniformly, reaching the maximum width of 16,000 feet at the end.
L1:(ii) The “approach-departure clearance zone” is the ground area under the approach-departure clearance surface.
L1:(iii) The “transitional surface” is a sideways extension of all primary surfaces, clear zones, and approach-departure
L0:clearance surfaces along inclined planes.
L1:(A) The inclined plane in each case begins at the edge of the surface.
L1:(B) The slope of the incline plane is 7:1 (1 foot vertically for each 7 feet horizontally). It continues to the point of
L0:intersection with the—
L1:(1) Inner horizontal surface (which is the horizontal plane 150 feet above the established airfield elevation); or
L1:(2) Outer horizontal surface (which is the horizontal plane 500 feet above the established airfield elevation), whichever is
L0:applicable.
L1:(iv) The “transitional zone” is the ground area under the transitional surface. (It adjoins the primary surface, clear zone, and
L0:approach-departure clearance zone.)
L1:(b) General.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall comply with the requirements of this clause while—
L1:(i) Operating all ground equipment (mobile or stationary);
L1:(ii) Placing all materials; and
L1:(iii) Performing all work, upon and around all airfields.
L1:(2) The requirements of this clause are in addition to any other safety requirements of this contract.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Report to the Contracting Officer before initiating any work;
L1:(2) Notify the Contracting Officer of proposed changes to locations and operations;
L1:(3) Not permit either its equipment or personnel to use any runway for purposes other than aircraft operation without
L0:permission of the Contracting Officer, unless the runway is—
L1:(i) Closed by order of the Contracting Officer; and
L1:(ii) Marked as provided in paragraph (d)(2) of this clause;
L1:(4) Keep all paved surfaces, such as runways, taxiways, and hardstands, clean at all times and, specifically, free from small
L0:stones which might damage aircraft propellers or jet aircraft;
L1:(5) Operate mobile equipment according to the safety provisions of this clause, while actually performing work on the
L0:airfield. At all other times, the Contractor shall remove all mobile equipment to locations—
L1:(i) Approved by the Contracting Officer;
L1:(ii) At a distance of at least 750 feet from the runway centerline, plus any additional distance; and
L1:(iii) Necessary to ensure compliance with the other provisions of this clause; and
L1:(6) Not open a trench unless material is on hand and ready for placing in the trench. As soon as practicable after material
L0:has been placed and work approved, the Contractor shall backfill and compact trenches as required by the contract.
L0:Meanwhile, all hazardous conditions shall be marked and lighted in accordance with the other provisions of this clause.
L1:(d) Landing areas. The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Place nothing upon the landing areas without the authorization of the Contracting Officer;
L1:(2) Outline those landing areas hazardous to aircraft, using (unless otherwise authorized by the Contracting Officer) red
L0:flags by day, and electric, battery-operated low-intensity red flasher lights by night;
L1:(3) Obtain, at an airfield where flying is controlled, additional permission from the control tower operator every time
L0:before entering any landing area, unless the landing area is marked as hazardous in accordance with paragraph (d)(2) of
L0:this clause;
L1:(4) Identify all vehicles it operates in landing areas by means of a flag on a staff attached to, and flying above, the vehicle.
L0:The flag shall be three feet square, and consist of a checkered pattern of international orange and white squares of 1 foot on
L0:each side (except that the flag may vary up to ten percent from each of these dimensions);
L1:(5) Mark all other equipment and materials in the landing areas, using the same marking devices as in paragraph (d)(2) of
L0:this clause; and
L1:(6) Perform work so as to leave that portion of the landing area which is available to aircraft free from hazards, holes, piles
L0:of material, and projecting shoulders that might damage an airplane tire.
L1:(e) Safety precaution areas. The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Place nothing upon the safety precaution areas without authorization of the Contracting Officer;
L1:(2) Mark all equipment and materials in safety precaution areas, using (unless otherwise authorized by the Contracting
L0:Officer) red flags by day, and electric, battery-operated, low-intensity red flasher lights by night; and
L1:(3) Provide all objects placed in safety precaution areas with a red light or red lantern at night, if the objects project above
L0:the approach-departure clearance surface or above the transitional surface.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.236-7007 Additive or Deductive Items
content:
L0:252.236-7007 Additive or Deductive Items.
L0:As prescribed in 236.570 (b)(5), use the following provision:
L0:ADDITIVE OR DEDUCTIVE ITEMS (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The low offeror and the items to be awarded shall be determined as follows—
L1:(1) Prior to the opening of bids, the Government will determine the amount of funds available for the project.
L1:(2) The low offeror shall be the Offeror that—
L1:(i) Is otherwise eligible for award; and
L1:(ii) Offers the lowest aggregate amount for the first or base bid item, plus or minus (in the order stated in the list of
L0:priorities in the bid schedule) those additive or deductive items that provide the most features within the funds determined
L0:available.
L1:(3) The Contracting Officer shall evaluate all bids on the basis of the same additive or deductive items.
L1:(i) If adding another item from the bid schedule list of priorities would make the award exceed the available funds for all
L0:offerors, the Contracting Officer will skip that item and go to the next item from the bid schedule of priorities; and
L1:(ii) Add that next item if an award may be made that includes that item and is within the available funds.
L1:(b) The Contracting Officer will use the list of priorities in the bid schedule only to determine the low offeror. After
L0:determining the low offeror, an award may be made on any combination of items if—
L1:(1) It is in the best interest of the Government;
L1:(2) Funds are available at the time of award; and
L1:(3) The low offeror's price for the combination to be awarded is less than the price offered by any other responsive,
L0:responsible offeror.
L1:(c) Example. The amount available is $100,000. Offeror A's base bid and four additives (in the order stated in the list of
L0:priorities in the bid Schedule) are $85,000, $10,000, $8,000, $6,000, and $4,000. Offeror B's base bid and four additives
L0:are $80,000, $16,000, $9,000, $7,000, and $4,000. Offeror A is the low offeror. The aggregate amount of offeror A's bid for
L0:purposes of award would be $99,000, which includes a base bid plus the first and fourth additives. The second and third
L0:additives were skipped because each of them would cause the aggregate bid to exceed $100,000.
L0:(End of provision)

title: 252.237-7001 Compliance with Audit Standards
content:
L0:252.237-7001 Compliance with Audit Standards.
L0:As prescribed in 237.270 (e)(2), use the following clause:
L0:COMPLIANCE WITH AUDIT STANDARDS (MAY 2000)
L0:The Contractor, in performance of all audit services under this contract, shall comply with “Government Auditing

L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7003 Requirements
content:
L0:252.237-7003 Requirements.
L0:As prescribed in 237.7003 (a) and (a)(1), use the following clause:
L0:REQUIREMENTS (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Except as provided in paragraphs (c) and (d) of this clause, the Government will order from the Contractor all of its
L0:requirements in the area of performance for the supplies and services listed in the schedule of this contract.
L1:(b) Each order will be issued as a delivery order and will list—
L1:(1) The supplies or services being ordered;
L1:(2) The quantities to be furnished;
L1:(3) Delivery or performance dates;
L1:(4) Place of delivery or performance;
L1:(5) Packing and shipping instructions;
L1:(6) The address to send invoices; and
L1:(7) The funds from which payment will be made.
L1:(c) The Government may elect not to order supplies and services under this contract in instances where the body is
L0:removed from the area for medical, scientific, or other reason.
L1:(d) In an epidemic or other emergency, the contracting activity may obtain services beyond the capacity of the Contractor's
L0:facilities from other sources.
L1:(e) Contracting Officers of the following activities may order services and supplies under this contract—
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7004 Area of Performance
content:
L0:252.237-7004 Area of Performance.
L0:As prescribed in 237.7003 (a) and (a)(2), use the following clause:
L0:AREA OF PERFORMANCE (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The area of performance is as specified in the contract.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall take possession of the remains at the place where they are located, transport them to the
L0:Contractor's place of preparation, and later transport them to a place designated by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(c) The Contractor will not be reimbursed for transportation when both the place where the remains were located and the
L0:delivery point are within the area of performance.
L1:(d) If remains are located outside the area of performance, the Contracting Officer may place an order with the Contractor
L0:under this contract or may obtain the services elsewhere. If the Contracting Officer requires the Contractor to transport the
L0:remains into the area of performance, the Contractor shall be paid the amount per mile in the schedule for the number of
L0:miles required to transport the remains by a reasonable route from the point where located to the boundary of the area of
L0:performance.
L1:(e) The Contracting Officer may require the Contractor to deliver remains to any point within 100 miles of the area of
L0:performance. In this case, the Contractor shall be paid the amount per mile in the schedule for the number of miles required
L0:to transport the remains by a reasonable route from the boundary of the area of performance to the delivery point.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7005 Performance and Delivery
content:
L0:252.237-7005 Performance and Delivery.
L0:As prescribed in 237.7003 (a) and (a)(3), use the following clause:
L0:PERFORMANCE AND DELIVERY (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall furnish the material ordered and perform the services specified as promptly as possible but not
L0:later than 36 hours after receiving notification to remove the remains, excluding the time necessary for the Government to
L0:inspect and check results of preparation.
L1:(b) The Government may, at no additional charge, require the Contractor to hold the remains for an additional period not to
L0:exceed 72 hours from the time the remains are casketed and final inspection completed.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7006 Subcontracting
content:
L0:252.237-7006 Subcontracting.
L0:As prescribed in 237.7003 (a) and (a)(4), use the following clause:
L0:SUBCONTRACTING (DEC 1991)
L0:The Contractor shall not subcontract any work under this contract without the Contracting Officer's written approval. This
L0:clause does not apply to contracts of employment between the Contractor and its personnel.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7007 Termination for Default
content:
L0:252.237-7007 Termination for Default.
L0:As prescribed in 237.7003 (a) and (a)(5), use the following clause:
L0:TERMINATION FOR DEFAULT (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) This clause supplements and is in addition to the Default clause of this contract.
L1:(b) The Contracting Officer may terminate this contract for default by written notice without the ten day notice required by
L0:paragraph (a)(2) of the Default clause if—
L1:(1) The Contractor, through circumstances reasonably within its control or that of its employees, performs any act under or
L0:in connection with this contract, or fails in the performance of any service under this contract and the act or failures may
L0:reasonably be considered to reflect discredit upon the Department of Defense in fulfilling its responsibility for proper care
L0:of remains;
L1:(2) The Contractor, or its employees, solicits relatives or friends of the deceased to purchase supplies or services not under
L0:this contract. (The Contractor may furnish supplies or arrange for services not under this contract, only if representatives of
L0:the deceased voluntarily request, select, and pay for them.);
L1:(3) The services or any part of the services are performed by anyone other than the Contractor or the Contractor's
L0:employees without the written authorization of the Contracting Officer;
L1:(4) The Contractor refuses to perform the services required for any particular remains; or
L1:(5) The Contractor mentions or otherwise uses this contract in its advertising in any way.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7008 Group Interment
content:
L0:252.237-7008 Group Interment.
L0:As prescribed in 237.7003 (a) and (a)(6), use the following clause:
L0:GROUP INTERMENT (DEC 1991)
L0:The Government will pay the Contractor for supplies and services provided for remains interred as a group on the basis of
L0:the number of caskets furnished, rather than on the basis of the number of persons in the group.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7009 Permits
content:
L0:252.237-7009 Permits.
L0:As prescribed in 237.7003 (a) and (a) (7), use the following clause:
L0:PERMITS (DEC 1991)
L0:The Contractor shall meet all State and local licensing requirements and obtain and furnish all necessary health department
L0:and shipping permits at no additional cost to the Government. The Contractor shall ensure that all necessary health
L0:department permits are in order for disposition of the remains.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7010 Prohibition on Interrogation of Detainees by Contractor Personnel
content:
L0:252.237-7010 Prohibition on Interrogation of Detainees by Contractor Personnel.
L0:As prescribed in 237.173-5 , use the following clause:
L0:PROHIBITION ON INTERROGATION OF DETAINEES BY CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Detainee” means any person captured, detained, held, or otherwise under the effective control of DoD personnel (military
L0:or civilian) in connection with hostilities. This includes, but is not limited to, enemy prisoners of war, civilian internees,
L0:and retained personnel. This does not include DoD personnel or DoD contractor personnel being held for law enforcement
L0:purposes.
L0:“Interrogation of detainees” means a systematic process of formally and officially questioning a detainee for the purpose of
L0:obtaining reliable information to satisfy foreign intelligence collection requirements.
L1:(b) Contractor personnel shall not interrogate detainees.
L1:(c) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause,
L0:including this paragraph (c), in all subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial products, that may require
L0:subcontractor personnel to interact with detainees in the course of their duties.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.237-7010 — Prohibition on Interrogation of Detainees by Contractor Personnel

content:
L0:252.237-7011 Preparation History.

title: 252.237-7012 Instruction to Offerors (Count-of-Articles)
content:

title: 252.237-7014 Loss or Damage (Count-of-Articles)
content:
L0:252.237-7014 Loss or Damage (Count-of-Articles).
L0:As prescribed in 237.7101 (c), use the following clause:
L0:LOSS OR DAMAGE (COUNT-OF-ARTICLES) (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The count-of-articles will be—
L1:(1) The count of the Contracting Officer; or
L1:(2) The count agreed upon as a result of a joint count by the Contractor and the Contracting Officer at the time of delivery
L0:to the Contractor.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Be liable for return of the number and kind of articles furnished for service under this contract; and
L1:(2) Shall indemnify the Government for any loss or damage to such articles.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall pay to the Government the value of any lost or damaged property using Federal supply schedule
L0:price lists. If the property is not on these price lists, the Contracting Officer shall determine a fair and reasonable price.
L1:(d) The Contracting Officer will allow credit for any depreciation in the value of the property at the time of loss or damage.
L0:The Contracting Officer and the Contractor shall mutually determine the amount of the allowable credit.
L1:(e) Failure to agree upon the value of the property or on the amount of credit due will be treated as a dispute under the
L0:Disputes clause of this contract.
L1:(f) In case of damage to any property that the Contracting Officer and the Contractor agree can be satisfactorily repaired,
L0:the Contractor may repair the property at its expense in a manner satisfactory to the Contracting Officer, rather than make
L0:payment under paragraph (c) of this clause.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7015 Loss or Damage (Weight of Articles)
content:
L0:252.237-7015 Loss or Damage (Weight of Articles).
L0:As prescribed in 237.7101 (d), use the following clause:
L0:LOSS OR DAMAGE (WEIGHT OF ARTICLES) (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Be liable for return of the articles furnished for service under this contract; and
L1:(2) Indemnify the Government for any articles delivered to the Contractor for servicing under this contract that are lost or

L1:(b) The Contractor shall pay to the Government _________ per pound for lost or damaged articles. The Contractor shall

L0:the Contractor shall repair the articles at its expense in a manner satisfactory to the Contracting Officer.
L1:(e) The maximum weight loss allowable in servicing the laundry is ______ percent of the weight recorded on delivery

L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.237-7015 — Loss or Damage (Weight of Articles)

title: 252.237-7016 Delivery Tickets
content:
L0:252.237-7016 Delivery Tickets.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 237.7101 (e) and (e)(1), use the following clause:
L0:DELIVERY TICKETS—BASIC (NOV 2014)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall complete delivery tickets in the number of copies required and in the form approved by the
L0:Contracting Officer, when it receives the articles to be serviced.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall include one copy of each delivery ticket with its invoice for payment.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Alternate I. As prescribed in 237.7101 (e) and (e)(2), use the following clause, which includes paragraphs (c), (d), and (e)
L0:not included in the basic clause:
L0:DELIVERY TICKETS—ALTERNATE I (NOV 2014)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall complete delivery tickets in the number of copies required and in the form approved by the
L0:Contracting Officer, when it receives the articles to be serviced.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall include one copy of each delivery ticket with its invoice for payment.
L1:(c) Before the Contractor picks up articles for service under this contract, the Contracting Officer will ensure that—
L1:(1) Each bag contains only articles within a single bag type as specified in the schedule; and
L1:(2) Each bag is weighed and the weight and bag type are identified on the bag.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall, at time of pickup—
L1:(1) Verify the weight and bag type and record them on the delivery ticket; and
L1:(2) Provide the Contracting Officer, or representative, a copy of the delivery ticket.
L1:(e) At the time of delivery, the Contractor shall record the weight and bag type of serviced laundry on the delivery ticket.
L0:The Contracting Officer will ensure that this weight and bag type are verified at time of delivery.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Alternate II. As prescribed in 237.7101 (e) and (e)(3), use the following clause, which includes paragraphs (c), (d), and (e)
L0:not included in the basic clause:
L0:DELIVERY TICKETS—ALTERNATE II (NOV 2014)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall complete delivery tickets in the number of copies required and in the form approved by the
L0:Contracting Officer, when it receives the articles to be serviced.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall include one copy of each delivery ticket with its invoice for payment.
L1:(c) Before the Contractor picks up articles for service under this contract, the Contracting Officer will ensure that each bag
L0:is weighed and that the weight is identified on the bag.
L1:(d) The Contractor, at time of pickup, shall verify and record the weight on the delivery ticket and shall provide the
L0:Contracting Officer, or representative, a copy of the delivery ticket.
L1:(e) At the time of delivery, the Contractor shall record the weight of serviced laundry on the delivery ticket. The
L0:Contracting Officer will ensure that this weight is verified at time of delivery.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.237-7017 Individual Laundry
content:

title: 252.237-7019 Training for Contractor Personnel Interacting with Detainees
content:
L0:252.237-7019 Training for Contractor Personnel Interacting with Detainees.
L0:As prescribed in 237.171-4 , use the following clause:
L0:TRAINING FOR CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL INTERACTING WITH DETAINEES (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Combatant Commander” means the commander of a unified or specified combatant command established in accordance
L0:with 10 U.S.C. 161.
L0:“Detainee” means a person in the custody or under the physical control of the Department of Defense on behalf of the
L0:United States Government as a result of armed conflict or other military operation by United States armed forces.
L0:“Personnel interacting with detainees” means personnel who, in the course of their duties, are expected to interact with
L0:detainees.
L1:(b) Training requirement. This clause implements Section 1092 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year
L0:2005 (Pub. L. 108-375).
L1:(1) The Combatant Commander responsible for the area where a detention or interrogation facility is located will arrange
L0:for training to be provided to contractor personnel interacting with detainees. The training will address the international
L0:obligations and laws of the United States applicable to the detention of personnel, including the Geneva Conventions. The
L0:Combatant Commander will arrange for a training receipt document to be provided to personnel who have completed the
L0:training.
L1:(2)(i) The Contractor shall arrange for its personnel interacting with detainees to—
L1:(A) Receive the training specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this clause—
L1:(1) Prior to interacting with detainees, or as soon as possible if, for compelling reasons, the Contracting Officer authorizes
L0:interaction with detainees prior to receipt of such training; and
L1:(2) Annually thereafter; and
L1:(B) Provide a copy of the training receipt document specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this clause to the Contractor for
L0:retention.
L1:(ii) To make these arrangements, the following points of contact apply:
L0:[Contracting Officer to insert applicable point of contact information cited in PGI 237.171-3 (b).]
L1:(3) The Contractor shall retain a copy of the training receipt document(s) provided in accordance with paragraphs (b)(1)
L0:and (2) of this clause until the contract is closed, or 3 years after all work required by the contract has been completed and
L0:accepted by the Government, whichever is sooner.
L1:(c) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (c), in all subcontracts,
L0:including subcontracts for commercial services, that may require subcontractor personnel to interact with detainees in the
L0:course of their duties.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.237-7019 — Training for Contractor Personnel Interacting with Detainees

title: 252.237-7023 , Continuation of Essential Contractor Services, in this solicitation
content:
L0:252.237-7023 , Continuation of Essential Contractor Services, in this solicitation.

L1:(v) The approach for communicating expectations to contractor employees regarding their roles and responsibilities during
L0:a crisis.
L0:(End of provision)
citation: R-DFARS 252.237-7023 — , Continuation of Essential Contractor Services, in this solicitation

title: 252.237-7025 Preaward Transparency Requirements for Firms Offering to Support Department of Defense Audits
content:
L0:252.237-7025 Preaward Transparency Requirements for Firms Offering to Support Department of Defense Audits
L0:—Representation and Disclosure.
L0:As prescribed in 237.270(e)(3), use the following provision:
L0:PREAWARD TRANSPARENCY REQUIREMENTS FOR FIRMS OFFERING TO SUPPORT DEPARTMENT OF
L0:DEFENSE AUDITS—REPRESENTATION AND DISCLOSURE (OCT 2022)
L1:(a) Representation. The Offeror represents that within the 3-year period preceding this offer, the Offeror and/or any of its
L0:principals or employees have [ ] have not [ ] been the subject of disciplinary proceedings before an entity with the authority
L0:to enforce compliance with rules or laws applying to audit services or audit remediation services offered by the Offeror,
L0:that—
L1:(1) Are not yet fully adjudicated or settled; or
L1:(2) Were fully adjudicated or settled against the Offeror and/or its principals or employees.
L1:(b) Disclosure. If the Offeror checked “have” in the representation in paragraph (a) of this provision, the Offeror shall, at a
L0:minimum, disclose for each such proceeding—
L1:(1) The entity hearing the case;
L1:(2) The case or file number; and
L1:(3) The allegation or conduct at issue and, if fully adjudicated or settled, a brief description of the outcome.
L1:(c) Treatment of statements. The Government will safeguard and treat as confidential all statements provided pursuant to
L0:this provision where the statement has been marked “confidential” or “proprietary” by the Offeror. Statements so marked
L0:will not be released by the Government to the public pursuant to a request under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C.
L0:552, without prior notification to the Offeror and opportunity for the Offeror to claim an exemption from release. The
L0:Government will treat any statement provided pursuant to this provision as confidential to the extent required by any other
L0:applicable law.
L0:(End of provision)
citation: R-DFARS 252.237-7025 — Preaward Transparency Requirements for Firms Offering to Support Department of Defense Audits

content:

title: 252.237-7027 Transfer and Adoption of Military Animals
content:
L0:252.237-7027 Transfer and Adoption of Military Animals.

title: 252.239-7000 Protection Against Compromising Emanations
content:
L0:252.239-7000 Protection Against Compromising Emanations.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7103 (a), use the following clause:
L0:PROTECTION AGAINST COMPROMISING EMANATIONS (OCT 2019)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall provide or use only information technology, as specified by the Government, that has been
L0:accredited to meet the appropriate information assurance requirements of—
L1:(1) The National Security Agency National TEMPEST Standards (NSTISSAM TEMPEST 1-92, Compromising
L0:Emanations Laboratory Test Requirements, Electromagnetics (U)); or
L1:(2) Other standards specified by this contract, including the date through which the required accreditation is current or
L0:valid for the contract.
L1:(b) Upon request of the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall provide documentation supporting the accreditation.
L1:(c) The Government may, as part of its inspection and acceptance, conduct additional tests to ensure that information
L0:technology delivered under this contract satisfies the information assurance standards specified. The Government may
L0:conduct additional tests—
L1:(1) At the installation site or contractor's facility; and
L1:(2) Notwithstanding the existence of valid accreditations of information technology prior to the award of this contract.
L1:(d) Unless otherwise provided in this contract under the Warranty of Supplies or Warranty of Systems and Equipment
L0:clause, the Contractor shall correct or replace accepted information technology found to be deficient within 1 year after
L0:proper installations.
L1:(1) The correction or replacement shall be at no cost to the Government.
L1:(2) Should a modification to the delivered information technology be made by the Contractor, the 1-year period applies to
L0:the modification upon its proper installation.
L1:(3) This paragraph (d) applies regardless of f.o.b. point or the point of acceptance of the deficient information technology.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.239-7001 Information Assurance Contractor Training and Certification
content:
L0:252.239-7001 Information Assurance Contractor Training and Certification.

title: 252.239-7002 Access
content:
L0:252.239-7002 Access.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7411 (a), use the following clause:
L0:ACCESS (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Subject to military security regulations, the Government shall permit the Contractor access at all reasonable times to
L0:Contractor furnished facilities. However, if the Government is unable to permit access, the Government at its own risk and
L0:expense shall maintain these facilities and the Contractor shall not be responsible for the service involving any of these
L0:facilities during the period of nonaccess, unless the service failure results from the Contractor's fault or negligence.
L1:(b) During periods when the Government does not permit Contractor access, the Government will reimburse the Contractor
L0:at mutually acceptable rates for the loss of or damage to the equipment due to the fault or negligence of the Government.
L0:Failure to agree shall be a dispute concerning a question of fact within the meaning of the Disputes clause of this contract.

title: 252.239-7004 Orders for Facilities and Services
content:
L0:252.239-7004 Orders for Facilities and Services.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7411 (a), use the following clause:
L0:ORDERS FOR FACILITIES AND SERVICES (SEP 2019)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Governmental regulatory body” means the Federal Communications Commission, any statewide regulatory body, or any
L0:body with less than statewide jurisdiction when operating under the state authority. Regulatory bodies whose decisions are
L0:not subject to judicial appeal and regulatory bodies which regulate a company owned by the same entity that creates the
L0:regulatory body are not governmental regulatory bodies.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall acknowledge a communication service authorization or other type order for supplies and facilities
L0:by—
L1:(1) Commencing performance after receipt of an order; or
L1:(2) Written acceptance by a duly authorized representative.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall furnish the services and facilities under this agreement/contract in accordance with all applicable
L0:tariffs, rates, charges, regulations, requirements, terms, and conditions of—
L1:(1) Service and facilities furnished or offered by the Contractor to the general public or the Contractor's subscribers; or
L1:(2) Service as lawfully established by a governmental regulatory body.
L1:(d) The Government will not prepay for services.
L1:(e) For nontariffed services, the Contractor shall charge the Government at the lowest rate and under the most favorable
L0:terms and conditions for similar service and facilities offered to any other customer.
L1:(f) Recurring charges for services and facilities shall, in each case, start with the satisfactory beginning of service or
L0:provision of facilities or equipment and are payable monthly in arrears.
L1:(g) Expediting charges are costs necessary to get services earlier than normal. Examples are overtime pay or special
L0:shipment. When authorized, expediting charges shall be the additional costs incurred by the Contractor and the
L0:subcontractor. The Government shall pay expediting charges only when—
L1:(1) They are provided for in the tariff established by a governmental regulatory body; or
L1:(2) They are authorized in a communication service authorization or other contractual document.
L1:(h) When services normally provided are technically unacceptable and the development, fabrication, or manufacture of
L0:special equipment is required, the Government may—
L1:(1) Provide the equipment; or
L1:(2) Direct the Contractor to acquire the equipment or facilities. If the Contractor acquires the equipment or facilities, the
L0:acquisition shall be competitive, if practicable.
L1:(i) If at any time the Government defers or changes its orders for any of the services but does not cancel or terminate them,
L0:the amount paid or payable to the Contractor for the services deferred or modified shall be equitably adjusted under
L0:applicable tariffs filed by the Contractor with the regulatory commission in effect at the time of deferral or change. If no
L0:tariffs are in effect, the Government and the Contractor shall equitably adjust the rates by mutual agreement. Failure to
L0:agree on any adjustment shall be a dispute concerning a question of fact within the meaning of the Disputes clause of this
L0:contract.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.239-7004 — Orders for Facilities and Services

title: 252.239-7007 Cancellation or Termination of Orders
content:
L0:252.239-7007 Cancellation or Termination of Orders.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7411 (a), use the following clause:
L0:CANCELLATION OR TERMINATION OF ORDERS (SEP 2019)
L1:(a) Definitions.
L0:“Actual nonrecoverable costs” means the installed costs of the facilities and equipment, less cost of reusable materials, and
L0:less net salvage value.
L0:“Basic cancellation liability” means the actual nonrecoverable cost, which the Government shall reimburse the Contractor
L0:at the time services are cancelled.
L0:“Basic termination liability” means the nonrecoverable cost amortized in equal monthly increments throughout the liability
L0:period.
L0:“Installed costs” means the actual cost of equipment and materials specifically provided or used, plus the actual cost of
L0:installing (including engineering, labor, supervision, transportation, rights-of-way, and any other items which are
L0:chargeable to the capital accounts of the Contractor), less any costs the government may have directly reimbursed the
L0:Contractor under the Special Construction and Equipment Charges clause of this agreement/contract.
L0:“Net salvage value” means the salvage value less the cost of removal.
L1:(b) If the Government cancels any of the services ordered under this agreement/contract, before the services are made
L0:available to the Government, or terminates any of these services after they are made available to the Government, the
L0:Government will reimburse the Contractor for the actual nonrecoverable costs the Contractor has reasonably incurred in
L0:providing facilities and equipment for which the Contractor has no foreseeable reuse. The Government will not reimburse
L0:the Contractor for any actual nonrecoverable costs incurred after notice of award, but prior to execution of the order.
L1:(c) When feasible, the Contractor shall reuse cancelled or terminated facilities or equipment to minimize the charges to the
L0:Government.
L1:(d) If at any time the Government requires that telecommunications facilities or equipment be relocated within the
L0:Contractor's service area, the Government will have the option of paying the costs of relocating the facilities or equipment
L0:in lieu of paying any termination or cancellation charge under this clause. The basic cancellation liability or basic
L0:termination liability applicable to the facilities or equipment in their former location shall continue to apply to the facilities
L0:and equipment in their new location. Monthly recurring charges shall continue to be paid during the period.
L1:(e) When there is another requirement or foreseeable reuse in place of cancelled or terminated facilities or equipment, no
L0:charge shall apply and the basic cancellation liability or basic termination liability shall be appropriately reduced. When
L0:feasible, the Contractor shall promptly reuse discontinued channels or facilities, including equipment for which the
L0:Government is obligated to pay a minimum service charge.
L1:(f) The amount of the Government's liability upon cancellation or termination of any of the services ordered under this
L0:agreement/contract will be determined under applicable tariffs governing cancellation and termination charges which—
L1:(1) Are filed by the Contractor with a governmental regulatory body, as defined in the Rates, Charges, and Services clause
L0:of this agreement/contract;
L1:(2) Are in effect on the date of termination; and
L1:(3) Provide specific cancellation or termination charges for the facilities and equipment involved or show how to determine
L0:the charges.
L1:(g) The amount of the Government's liability upon cancellation or termination of any of the services ordered under this
L0:agreement/contract, which are not subject to a governmental regulatory body, will be determined under a mutually agreed
L0:schedule in the communication services authorization (CSA) or other contractual document.
L1:(h) If no applicable tariffs are in effect on the date of cancellation or termination or set forth in the applicable CSA or other
L0:contractual document, the Government's liability will be determined under the following settlement procedures—
L1:(1) The Contractor agrees to provide the Contracting Officer, in such reasonable detail as the Contracting Officer may
L0:require, inventory schedules covering all items of property or facilities in the Contractor's possession, the cost of which is
L0:included in the Basic Cancellation or Termination Liability for which the Contractor has no foreseeable reuse.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall use its best efforts to sell property or facilities when the Contractor has no foreseeable reuse or
L0:when the Government has not exercised its option to take title under the Title to Telecommunications Facilities and
L0:Equipment clause of this agreement/contract. The Contractor shall apply any proceeds of the sale to reduce any payments
L0:by the Government to the Contractor under a cancellation or termination settlement.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall record actual nonrecoverable costs under established accounting procedures prescribed by the
L0:cognizant governmental regulatory authority or, if no such procedures have been prescribed, under generally accepted
L0:accounting procedures applicable to the provision of telecommunication services for public use.
L1:(4) The net salvage value shall be deducted from the Contractor’s installed cost. In determining net salvage value, the
L0:Contractor shall consider the foreseeable reuse of the facilities and equipment by the Contractor. The Contractor shall make
L0:allowance for the cost of dismantling, removal, reconditioning, and disposal of the facilities and equipment when necessary
L0:either for the sale of facilities or their reuse by the Contractor in another location.
L1:(5) Upon termination of services, the Government will reimburse the Contractor for the nonrecoverable cost less such costs
L0:amortized to the date services are terminated and establish the liability period as mutually agreed to but not to exceed ten
L0:years. In the case of either a cancellation or a termination, the Government’s presumed maximum liability will be capped
L0:by the unpaid non-recurring charges and the monthly recurring charges set out in the contract/agreement. The presumed
L0:maximum liability for monthly recurring charges shall be capped at monthly recurring charges for the minimum service
L0:period and any required notice period.
L1:(6) When the basic cancellation liability or basic termination liability established by the CSA or other contractual document
L0:is based on estimated costs, the Contractor agrees to settle on the basis of actual cost at the time of cancellation or
L0:termination.
L1:(7) The Contractor agrees that, if after settlement but within the termination liability period of the services, should the
L0:Contractor make reuse of equipment or facilities which were treated as nonreusable or nonsalvable in the settlement, the
L0:Contractor shall reimburse the Government for the value of the equipment or facilities.
L1:(8) The Contractor agrees to exclude—
L1:(i) Any costs which are not included in determining cancellation and termination charges under the Contractor's standard
L0:practices or procedures; and
L1:(ii) Charges not ordinarily made by the Contractor for similar facilities or equipment, furnished under similar
L0:circumstances.
L1:(i) The Government may, under such terms and conditions as it may prescribe, make partial payments and payments on
L0:account against costs incurred by the Contractor in connection with the cancelled or terminated portion of this
L0:agreement/contract. The Government may make these payments if the Contracting Officer determines that the total of the
L0:payments is within the amount the Contractor is entitled. If the total of the payments is in excess of the amount finally
L0:agreed or determined to be due under this clause, the Contractor shall pay the excess to the Government upon demand.
L1:(j) Failure to agree shall be a dispute concerning a question of fact within the meaning of the Disputes clause.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.239-7007 — Cancellation or Termination of Orders

title: 252.239-7009 Representation of Use of Cloud Computing
content:
L0:252.239-7009 Representation of Use of Cloud Computing.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7604 (a), use the following provision:
L0:REPRESENTATION OF USE OF CLOUD COMPUTING (SEP 2015)
L1:(a) Definition. “Cloud computing,” as used in this provision, means a model for enabling ubiquitous, convenient, ondemand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources (e.g., networks, servers, storage,
L0:applications, and services) that can be rapidly provisioned and released with minimal management effort or service
L0:provider interaction. This includes other commercial terms, such as on-demand self-service, broad network access,
L0:resource pooling, rapid elasticity, and measured service. It also includes commercial offerings for software-as-a-service,
L0:infrastructure-as-a-service, and platform-as-a-service.
L1:(b) The Offeror shall indicate by checking the appropriate blank in paragraph (c) of this provision whether the use of cloud
L0:computing is anticipated under the resultant contract.
L1:(c) Representation. The Offeror represents that it—
L0:_____ Does anticipate that cloud computing services will be used in the performance of any contract or subcontract
L0:resulting from this solicitation.
L0:_____ Does not anticipate that cloud computing services will be used in the performance of any contract or subcontract
L0:resulting from this solicitation.
L0:(End of provision)
citation: R-DFARS 252.239-7009 — Representation of Use of Cloud Computing

title: 252.239-7010 Cloud Computing Services
content:
L0:252.239-7010 Cloud Computing Services.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7604 (b), use the following clause:
L0:CLOUD COMPUTING SERVICES (JAN 2023)
L1:(a)Definitions.As used in this clause—
L0:“Authorizing official,” as described in DoD Instruction 8510.01, Risk Management Framework (RMF) for DoD
L0:Information Technology (IT), means the senior Federal official or executive with the authority to formally assume
L0:responsibility for operating an information system at an acceptable level of risk to organizational operations (including
L0:mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.
L0:“Cloud computing” means a model for enabling ubiquitous, convenient, on-demand network access to a shared pool of
L0:configurable computing resources (e.g., networks, servers, storage, applications, and services) that can be rapidly
L0:provisioned and released with minimal management effort or service provider interaction. This includes other commercial
L0:terms, such as on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, and measured service. It
L0:also includes commercial offerings for software-as-a-service, infrastructure-as-a-service, and platform-as-a-service.
L0:“Compromise” means disclosure of information to unauthorized persons, or a violation of the security policy of a system,
L0:in which unauthorized intentional or unintentional disclosure, modification, destruction, or loss of an object, or the copying
L0:of information to unauthorized media may have occurred.
L0:“Cyber incident” means actions taken through the use of computer networks that result in a compromise or an actual or
L0:potentially adverse effect on an information system and/or the information residing therein.
L0:“Government data” means any information, document, media, or machine readable material regardless of physical form or
L0:characteristics, that is created or obtained by the Government in the course of official Government business.
L0:“Government-related data” means any information, document, media, or machine readable material regardless of physical
L0:form or characteristics that is created or obtained by a contractor through the storage, processing, or communication of
L0:Government data. This does not include contractor’s business records e.g. financial records, legal records etc. or data such
L0:as operating procedures, software coding or algorithms that are not uniquely applied to the Government data.
L0:“Information system” means a discrete set of information resources organized for the collection, processing, maintenance,
L0:use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition of information.
L0:“Media” means physical devices or writing surfaces including, but not limited to, magnetic tapes, optical disks, magnetic
L0:disks, large-scale integration memory chips, and printouts onto which information is recorded, stored, or printed within an
L0:information system.
L0:“Spillage” security incident that results in the transfer of classified or controlled unclassified information onto an
L0:information system not accredited (i.e., authorized) for the appropriate security level.
L1:(b) Cloud computing security requirements. The requirements of this clause are applicable when using cloud computing to
L0:provide information technology services in the performance of the contract.
L1:(1) If the Contractor indicated in its offer that it “does not anticipate the use of cloud computing services in the
L0:performance of a resultant contract,” in response to provision 252.239-7009 , Representation of Use of Cloud Computing,
L0:and after the award of this contract, the Contractor proposes to use cloud computing services in the performance of the
L0:contract, the Contractor shall obtain approval from the Contracting Officer prior to utilizing cloud computing services in
L0:performance of the contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall implement and maintain administrative, technical, and physical safeguards and controls with the
L0:security level and services required in accordance with the Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide (SRG) (version
L0:in effect at the time the solicitation is issued or as authorized by the Contracting Officer) found at https://public.cyber.mil/
L0:dccs/dccs-documents/ unless notified by the Contracting Officer that this requirement has been waived by the DoD Chief
L0:Information Officer.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall maintain within the United States or outlying areas all Government data that is not physically
L0:located on DoD premises, unless the Contractor receives written notification from the Contracting Officer to use another
L0:location, in accordance with DFARS 239.7602-2 (a).
L1:(c) Limitations on access to, and use and disclosure of Government data and Government-related data.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall not access, use, or disclose Government data unless specifically authorized by the terms of this
L0:contract or a task order or delivery order issued hereunder.
L1:(i) If authorized by the terms of this contract or a task order or delivery order issued hereunder, any access to, or use or
L0:disclosure of, Government data shall only be for purposes specified in this contract or task order or delivery order.
L1:(ii) The Contractor shall ensure that its employees are subject to all such access, use, and disclosure prohibitions and
L0:obligations.
L1:(iii) These access, use, and disclosure prohibitions and obligations shall survive the expiration or termination of this
L0:contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall use Government-related data only to manage the operational environment that supports the
L0:Government data and for no other purpose unless otherwise permitted with the prior written approval of the Contracting
L0:Officer.
L1:(d) Cloud computing services cyber incident reporting. The Contractor shall report all cyber incidents that are related to the
L0:cloud computing service provided under this contract. Reports shall be submitted to DoD via http://dibnet.dod.mil/.
L1:(e) Malicious software. The Contractor or subcontractors that discover and isolate malicious software in connection with a
L0:reported cyber incident shall submit the malicious software in accordance with instructions provided by the Contracting
L0:Officer.
L1:(f) Media preservation and protection. When a Contractor discovers a cyber incident has occurred, the Contractor shall
L0:preserve and protect images of all known affected information systems identified in the cyber incident report (see
L0:paragraph (d) of this clause) and all relevant monitoring/packet capture data for at least 90 days from the submission of the
L0:cyber incident report to allow DoD to request the media or decline interest.
L1:(g) Access to additional information or equipment necessary for forensic analysis.Upon request by DoD, the Contractor
L0:shall provide DoD with access to additional information or equipment that is necessary to conduct a forensic analysis.
L1:(h) Cyber incident damage assessment activities. If DoD elects to conduct a damage assessment, the Contracting Officer
L0:will request that the Contractor provide all of the damage assessment information gathered in accordance with paragraph
L1:(f) of this clause.
L1:(i) Records management and facility access.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall provide the Contracting Officer all Government data and Government-related data in the format
L0:specified in the contract.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall dispose of Government data and Government-related data in accordance with the terms of the
L0:contract and provide the confirmation of disposition to the Contracting Officer in accordance with contract closeout
L0:procedures.
L1:(3) The Contractor shall provide the Government, or its authorized representatives, access to all Government data and
L0:Government-related data, access to contractor personnel involved in performance of the contract, and physical access to
L0:any Contractor facility with Government data, for the purpose of audits, investigations, inspections, or other similar
L0:activities, as authorized by law or regulation.
L1:(j) Notification of third party access requests. The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer promptly of any requests
L0:from a third party for access to Government data or Government-related data, including any warrants, seizures, or
L0:subpoenas it receives, including those from another Federal, State, or local agency.
L0:The Contractor shall cooperate with the Contracting Officer to take all measures to protect Government data and
L0:Government-related data from any unauthorized disclosure.
L1:(k) Spillage.Upon notification by the Government of a spillage, or upon the Contractor’s discovery of a spillage, the
L0:Contractor shall cooperate with the Contracting Officer to address the spillage in compliance with agency procedures.
L1:(l) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include this clause, including this paragraph (l), in all subcontracts that involve or
L0:may involve cloud services, including subcontracts for commercial services.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.239-7011 Special Construction and Equipment Charges
content:
L0:252.239-7011 Special Construction and Equipment Charges.
L0:As prescribed in 239.7411 (b), use the following clause:
L0:SPECIAL CONSTRUCTION AND EQUIPMENT CHARGES (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Government will not directly reimburse the Contractor for the cost of constructing any facilities or providing any
L0:equipment, unless the Contracting Officer authorizes direct reimbursement.
L1:(b) If the Contractor stops using facilities or equipment which the Government has, in whole or part, directly reimbursed,
L0:the Contractor shall allow the Government credit for the value of the facilities or equipment attributable to the
L0:Government's contribution. Determine the value of the facilities and equipment on the basis of their foreseeable reuse by
L0:the Contractor at the time their use is discontinued or on the basis of the net salvage value, whichever is greater. The
L0:Contractor shall promptly pay the Government the amount of any credit.
L1:(c) The amount of the direct special construction charge shall not exceed—
L1:(1) The actual costs to the Contractor; and
L1:(2) An amount properly allocable to the services to be provided to the Government.
L1:(d) The amount of the direct special construction charge shall not include costs incurred by the Contractor which are
L0:covered by—
L1:(1) A cancellation or termination liability; or
L1:(2) The Contractor's recurring or other nonrecurring charges.
L1:(e) The Contractor represents that—
L1:(1) Recurring charges for the services, facilities, and equipment do not include in the rate base any costs that have been
L0:reimbursed by the Government to the Contractor; and
L1:(2) Depreciation charges are based only on the cost of facilities and equipment paid by the Contractor and not reimbursed
L0:by the Government.
L1:(f) If it becomes necessary for the Contractor to incur costs to replace any facilities or equipment, the Government shall
L0:assume those costs or reimburse the Contractor for replacement costs at mutually acceptable rates under the following
L0:circumstances—
L1:(1) The Government paid direct special construction charges; or
L1:(2) The Government reimbursed the Contractor for those facilities or equipment as a part of the recurring charges; and
L1:(3) The need for replacement was due to circumstances beyond the control and without the fault of the Contractor.
L1:(g) Before incurring any costs under paragraph (f) of this clause, the Government shall have the right to terminate the
L0:service under the Cancellation or Termination of Orders clause of this contract.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.239-7011 — Special Construction and Equipment Charges

title: 252.239-7012 Title to Telecommunication Facilities and Equipment
content:
L0:252.239-7012 Title to Telecommunication Facilities and Equipment.

title: 252.239-7013 Term of Agreement and Continuation of Services
content:
L0:252.239-7013 Term of Agreement and Continuation of Services.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 239.7411 (c)(1), use the following clause:
L0:TERM OF AGREEMENT AND CONTINUATION OF SERVICES-BASIC (OCT 2019)
L1:(a) This basic agreement is not a contract. The Government incurs liability only upon issuance of a communication service
L0:authorization, which is a contract that incorporates the terms and conditions of this basic agreement.
L1:(b) This agreement shall continue in force from year to year, unless terminated by either party by 30 days’ written notice.
L0:Termination of this basic agreement does not terminate or cancel any communication service authorizations issued under
L0:this basic agreement prior to the termination.
L1:(c) Communication service authorizations issued under this basic agreement may be modified to incorporate the terms and
L0:conditions of a new basic agreement negotiated with the Contractor.
L0:(End of clause)
L0:Alternate I. As prescribed in 239.7411 (c)(2), use the following clause, which uses a different paragraph (c) than the basic
L0:clause and adds a new paragraph (d).
L0:TERM OF AGREEMENT AND CONTINUATION OF SERVICES-ALTERNATE I (OCT 2019)
L1:(a) This basic agreement is not a contract. The Government incurs liability only upon issuance of a communication service
L0:authorization, which is a contract that incorporates the terms and conditions of this basic agreement.
L1:(b) This agreement shall continue in force from year to year, unless terminated by either party by 30 days’ written notice.
L0:Termination of this basic agreement does not terminate or cancel any communication service authorizations issued under

title: 252.239-7016 Telecommunications Security Equipment, Devices, Techniques, and Services
