title: 252.242-7004 Material Management and Accounting System
content:
L0:252.242-7004 Material Management and Accounting System.
L0:As prescribed in 242.7204 , use the following clause:
L0:MATERIAL MANAGEMENT AND ACCOUNTING SYSTEM (JAN 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions.As used in this clause—
L0:“Acceptable material management and accounting system” means a material management and accounting system that
L0:generally complies with the system criteria in paragraph (d) of this clause.
L0:“Contractor” means a business unit as defined in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 2.101.
L0:“Material management and accounting system (MMAS)” means the Contractor’s system or systems for planning,
L0:controlling, and accounting for the acquisition, use, issuing, and disposition of material. Material management and
L0:accounting systems may be manual or automated. They may be stand-alone systems, or they may be integrated with
L0:planning, engineering, estimating, purchasing, inventory, accounting, or other systems.
L0:“Material weakness” means a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the internal control over information in
L0:contractor business systems, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of such information will
L0:not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A reasonable possibility exists when the likelihood of an
L0:event occurring is—
L1:(1) Probable; or
L1:(2) More than remote but less than likely (section 806 of Pub. L. 116-283).
L0:“Valid time-phased requirements” means material that is—
L1:(1) Needed to fulfill the production plan, including reasonable quantities for scrap, shrinkage, yield, etc.; and
L1:(2) Charged or billed to contracts or other cost objectives in a manner consistent with the need to fulfill the production
L0:plan.
L1:(b) General.The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Maintain an MMAS that—
L1:(i) Reasonably forecasts material requirements;
L1:(ii) Ensures that costs of purchased and fabricated material charged or allocated to a contract are based on valid timephased requirements; and
L1:(iii) Maintains a consistent, equitable, and unbiased logic for costing of material transactions; and
L1:(2) Assess its MMAS and take reasonable action to comply with the MMAS standards in paragraph (e) of this clause.
L1:(c) Disclosure and maintenance requirements.The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Have policies, procedures, and operating instructions that adequately describe its MMAS;
L1:(2) Provide to the Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO), upon request, the results of internal reviews that it has
L0:conducted to ensure compliance with established MMAS policies, procedures, and operating instructions; and
L1:(3) Disclose significant changes in its MMAS to the ACO at least 30 days prior to implementation.
L1:(d) System criteria. The MMAS shall have adequate internal controls to ensure system and data integrity, and shall—
L1:(1) Have an adequate system description including policies, procedures, and operating instructions that comply with the
L0:FAR and Defense FAR Supplement;
L1:(2) Ensure that costs of purchased and fabricated material charged or allocated to a contract are based on valid time-phased
L0:requirements as impacted by minimum/economic order quantity restrictions.
L1:(i) A 98 percent bill of material accuracy and a 95 percent master production schedule accuracy are desirable as a goal in
L0:order to ensure that requirements are both valid and appropriately time-phased.
L1:(ii) If systems have accuracy levels below these, the Contractor shall provide adequate evidence that—
L1:(A) There is no material harm to the Government due to lower accuracy levels; and
L1:(B) The cost to meet the accuracy goals is excessive in relation to the impact on the Government;
L1:(3) Provide a mechanism to identify, report, and resolve system control weaknesses and manual override. Systems should
L0:identify operational exceptions, such as excess/residual inventory, as soon as known;
L1:(4) Provide audit trails and maintain records (manual and those in machine-readable form) necessary to evaluate system
L0:logic and to verify through transaction testing that the system is operating as desired;
L1:(5) Establish and maintain adequate levels of record accuracy, and include reconciliation of recorded inventory quantities to
L0:physical inventory by part number on a periodic basis. A 95 percent accuracy level is desirable. If systems have an
L0:accuracy level below 95 percent, the Contractor shall provide adequate evidence that—
L1:(i) There is no material harm to the Government due to lower accuracy levels; and
L1:(ii) The cost to meet the accuracy goal is excessive in relation to the impact on the Government;
L1:(6) Provide detailed descriptions of circumstances that will result in manual or system generated transfers of parts;
L1:(7) Maintain a consistent, equitable, and unbiased logic for costing of material transactions as follows:
L1:(i) The Contractor shall maintain and disclose written policies describing the transfer methodology and the loan/pay-back
L0:technique.
L1:(ii) The costing methodology may be standard or actual cost, or any of the inventory costing methods in 48 CFR 9904.41150(b). The Contractor shall maintain consistency across all contract and customer types, and from accounting period to
L0:accounting period for initial charging and transfer charging.
L1:(iii) The system should transfer parts and associated costs within the same billing period. In the few instances where this
L0:may not be appropriate, the Contractor may accomplish the material transaction using a loan/pay-back technique. The
L0:“loan/pay-back technique” means that the physical part is moved temporarily from the contract, but the cost of the part
L0:remains on the contract. The procedures for the loan/pay-back technique must be approved by the ACO. When the
L0:technique is used, the Contractor shall have controls to ensure—
L1:(A) Parts are paid back expeditiously;
L1:(B) Procedures and controls are in place to correct any overbilling that might occur;
L1:(C) Monthly, at a minimum, identification of the borrowing contract and the date the part was borrowed; and
L1:(D) The cost of the replacement part is charged to the borrowing contract;
L1:(8) Where allocations from common inventory accounts are used, have controls (in addition to those in paragraphs (d)(2)
L0:and (7) of this clause) to ensure that—
L1:(i) Reallocations and any credit due are processed no less frequently than the routine billing cycle;
L1:(ii) Inventories retained for requirements that are not under contract are not allocated to contracts; and
L1:(iii) Algorithms are maintained based on valid and current data;
L1:(9) Have adequate controls to ensure that physically commingled inventories that may include material for which costs are
L0:charged or allocated to fixed-price, cost-reimbursement, and commercial contracts do not compromise requirements of any
L0:of the standards in paragraphs (d)(1) through (8) of this clause. Government-furnished material shall not be—
L1:(i) Physically commingled with other material; or
L1:(ii) Used on commercial work; and
L1:(10) Be subjected to periodic internal reviews to ensure compliance with established policies and procedures.
L1:(e) Material weaknesses.
L1:(1) The Contracting Officer will provide an initial determination to the Contractor, in writing, of any material weaknesses.
L0:The initial determination will describe the underlying deficiencies in sufficient detail to allow the Contractor to understand
L0:the weaknesses or deficiencies.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that
L0:identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor’s MMAS. If the Contractor disagrees with the initial determination, the
L0:Contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.
L1:(3) The Contracting Officer will evaluate the Contractor's response and notify the Contractor, in writing, of the Contracting
L0:Officer’s final determination concerning—
L1:(i) Remaining material weaknesses;
L1:(ii) The adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action; and
L1:(iii) System disapproval if the Contracting Officer determines that one or more material weaknesses remain.
L1:(f) If the Contractor receives the Contracting Officer’s final determination of material weaknesses, the Contractor shall,
L0:within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable
L0:corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the material weaknesses.
L1:(g) Withholding payments. If the Contracting Officer makes a final determination to disapprove the Contractor’s MMAS,
L0:and the contract includes the clause at 252.242-7005 , Contractor Business Systems, the Contracting Officer will withhold
L0:payments in accordance with that clause.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.242-7004 — Material Management and Accounting System

title: 252.242-7005 Contractor Business Systems
content:
L0:252.242-7005 Contractor Business Systems.
L0:As prescribed in 242.7001 , use the following clause:
L0:CONTRACTOR BUSINESS SYSTEMS (JAN 2025)
L1:(a) This clause only applies to covered contracts that are subject to the Cost Accounting Standards under 41 U.S.C. chapter
L0:15, as implemented in regulations found at 48 CFR 9903.201-1 (see the FAR Appendix).
L1:(b) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Acceptable contractor business systems” means contractor business systems that comply with the terms and conditions of
L0:the applicable business system clauses listed in the definition of "contractor business systems" in this clause.
L0:“Contractor business systems” means—
L1:(1) Accounting system, if this contract includes the clause at 252.242-7006 , Accounting System Administration;
L1:(2) Earned value management system, if this contract includes the clause at 252.234-7002 , Earned Value Management
L0:System;
L1:(3) Estimating system, if this contract includes the clause at 252.215-7002 , Cost Estimating System Requirements;
L1:(4) Material management and accounting system, if this contract includes the clause at 252.242-7004 , Material
L0:Management and Accounting System;
L1:(5) Property management system, if this contract includes the clause at 252.245-7003 , Contractor Property Management
L0:System Administration; and
L1:(6) Purchasing system, if this contract includes the clause at 252.244-7001 , Contractor Purchasing System Administration.
L0:“Material weakness” means a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the internal control over information in
L0:contractor business systems, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of such information will
L0:not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A reasonable possibility exists when the likelihood of an
L0:event occurring is—
L1:(1) Probable; or
L1:(2) More than remote but less than likely (section 806 of Pub. L. 116-283).
L1:(c) General. The Contractor shall establish and maintain acceptable business systems in accordance with the terms and
L0:conditions of this contract.
L1:(d) Material weaknesses.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall respond, in writing, within 30 days to an initial determination that there are one or more material
L0:weaknesses in one or more of the Contractor’s business systems.
L1:(2) The Contracting Officer will evaluate the Contractor’s response and notify the Contractor, in writing, of the final
L0:determination as to whether the Contractor’s business system contains material weaknesses. If the Contracting Officer
L0:determines that the Contractor’s business system contains material weaknesses, the final determination will include a
L0:notice to withhold payments.
L1:(e) Withholding payments.
L1:(1) If the Contracting Officer issues the final determination with a notice to withhold payments for material weaknesses in
L0:a contractor business system required under this contract, the Contracting Officer will withhold 5 percent of amounts due
L0:from progress payments and performance-based payments, and direct the Contractor, in writing, to withhold 5 percent from
L0:its billings on interim cost vouchers on cost-reimbursement, labor-hour, and time-and-materials contracts until the
L0:Contracting Officer has determined that the Contractor has corrected all material weaknesses as directed by the Contracting
L0:Officer’s final determination. The Contractor shall, within 45 days of receipt of the notice, either correct the weaknesses or
L0:submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the weaknesses.
L1:(2) If the Contractor submits an acceptable corrective action plan within 45 days of receipt of a notice of the Contracting
L0:Officer’s intent to withhold payments, and the Contracting Officer, in consultation with the auditor or functional specialist,
L0:determines that the Contractor is effectively implementing such plan, the Contracting Officer will reduce withholding
L0:directly related to the material weaknesses covered under the corrective action plan, to 2 percent from progress payments
L0:and performance-based payments, and direct the Contractor, in writing, to reduce the percentage withheld on interim cost
L0:vouchers to 2 percent until the Contracting Officer determines the Contractor has corrected all material weaknesses as
L0:directed by the Contracting Officer’s final determination. However, if at any time, the Contracting Officer determines that
L0:the Contractor has failed to follow the accepted corrective action plan, the Contracting Officer will increase withholding
L0:from progress payments and performance-based payments, and direct the Contractor, in writing, to increase the percentage
L0:withheld on interim cost vouchers to the percentage initially withheld, until the Contracting Officer determines that the
L0:Contractor has corrected all material weaknesses as directed by the Contracting Officer’s final determination.
L1:(3) Payment withhold percentage limits.
L1:(i) The total percentage of payments withheld on amounts due under each progress payment, performance-based payment,
L0:or interim cost voucher, on this contract shall not exceed—
L1:(A) Five percent for one or more material weaknesses in any single contractor business system; and
L1:(B) Ten percent for material weaknesses in multiple contractor business systems.
L1:(ii) If this contract contains pre-existing withholds, and the application of any subsequent payment withholds will cause
L0:withholding under this clause to exceed the payment withhold percentage limits in paragraph (e)(3)(i) of this clause, the
L0:Contracting Officer will reduce the payment withhold percentage in the final determination to an amount that will not
L0:exceed the payment withhold percentage limits.
L1:(4) For the purpose of this clause, payment means any of the following payments authorized under this contract:
L1:(i) Interim payments under—
L1:(A) Cost-reimbursement contracts;
L1:(B) Incentive type contracts;
L1:(C) Time-and-materials contracts;
L1:(D) Labor-hour contracts.
L1:(ii) Progress payments.
L1:(iii) Performance-based payments.
L1:(5) Payment withholding shall not apply to payments on fixed-price line items where performance is complete and the
L0:items were accepted by the Government.
L1:(6) The withholding of any amount or subsequent payment to the Contractor shall not be construed as a waiver of any
L0:rights or remedies the Government has under this contract.
L1:(7) Notwithstanding the provisions of any clause in this contract providing for interim, partial, or other payment
L0:withholding on any basis, the Contracting Officer may withhold payment in accordance with the provisions of this clause.
L1:(8) The payment withholding authorized in this clause is not subject to the interest-penalty provisions of the Prompt
L0:Payment Act.
L1:(f) Correction of weaknesses .
L1:(1) The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer, in writing, when the Contractor has corrected the business system’s
L0:weaknesses.
L1:(2) Once the Contractor has notified the Contracting Officer that all weaknesses have been corrected, the Contracting
L0:Officer will take one of the following actions:
L1:(i) If the Contracting Officer determines that the Contractor has corrected all material weaknesses as directed by the
L0:Contracting Officer’s final determination, the Contracting Officer will, as appropriate, discontinue the withholding of
L0:progress payments and performance-based payments, and direct the Contractor, in writing, to discontinue the payment
L0:withholding from billings on interim cost vouchers under this contract associated with the Contracting Officer’s final
L0:determination, and authorize the Contractor to bill for any monies previously withheld that are not also being withheld due
L0:to other material weaknesses. Any payment withholding under this contract due to other material weaknesses will remain
L0:in effect until the Contracting Officer determines that those material weaknesses are corrected.
L1:(ii) If the Contracting Officer determines that the Contractor still has material weaknesses, the Contracting Officer will
L0:continue the withholding of progress payments and performance-based payments, and the Contractor shall continue
L0:withholding amounts from its billings on interim cost vouchers in accordance with paragraph (e) of this clause, and not bill
L0:for any monies previously withheld.
L1:(iii) If the Contracting Officer determines, based on the evidence submitted by the Contractor, that there is a reasonable
L0:expectation that the corrective actions have been implemented and are expected to correct the material weaknesses, the
L0:Contracting Officer will discontinue withholding payments, release any payments previously withheld directly related to
L0:the material weaknesses identified in the Contractor notification, direct the Contractor, in writing, to discontinue the
L0:payment withholding from billings on interim cost vouchers associated with the Contracting Officer’s final determination,
L0:and authorize the Contractor to bill for any monies previously withheld.
L1:(iv) If, within 90 days of receipt of the Contractor notification that the Contractor has corrected the material weaknesses,
L0:the Contracting Officer has not made a determination in accordance with paragraph (f)(2)(i), (ii), or (iii) of this clause, the
L0:Contracting Officer will reduce withholding directly related to the material weaknesses identified in the Contractor
L0:notification by at least 50 percent of the amount being withheld from progress payments and performance-based payments,
L0:and direct the Contractor, in writing, to reduce the payment withholding from billings on interim cost vouchers directly
L0:related to the material weaknesses identified in the Contractor notification by a specified percentage that is at least 50
L0:percent, but not authorize the Contractor to bill for any monies previously withheld until the Contracting Officer makes a
L0:determination in accordance with paragraph (f)(2)(i), (ii), or (iii) of this clause.
L1:(v) At any time after the Contracting Officer reduces or discontinues the withholding of progress payments and
L0:performance-based payments, or directs the Contractor to reduce or discontinue the payment withholding from billings on
L0:interim cost vouchers under this contract, if the Contracting Officer determines that the Contractor has failed to correct the
L0:material weaknesses identified in the Contractor’s notification, the Contracting Officer will reinstate or increase
L0:withholding from progress payments and performance-based payments, and direct the Contractor, in writing, to reinstate or
L0:increase the percentage withheld on interim cost vouchers to the percentage initially withheld, until the Contracting Officer
L0:determines that the Contractor has corrected all material weaknesses as directed by the Contracting Officer’s final
L0:determination.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.242-7006 Accounting System Administration
content:
L0:252.242-7006 Accounting System Administration.
L0:As prescribed in 242.7503 , use the following clause:
L0:ACCOUNTING SYSTEM ADMINISTRATION (JAN 2025)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Acceptable accounting system” means a system that complies with the system criteria in paragraph (c) of this clause to
L0:provide reasonable assurance that—
L1:(1) Applicable laws and regulations are complied with;
L1:(2) The accounting system and cost data are reliable;
L1:(3) Risk of misallocations and mischarges are minimized; and
L1:(4) Contract allocations and charges are consistent with billing procedures.
L0:“Accounting system” means the Contractor’s system or systems for accounting methods, procedures, and controls
L0:established to gather, record, classify, analyze, summarize, interpret, and present accurate and timely financial data for
L0:reporting in compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and management decisions, and may include subsystems for
L0:specific areas such as indirect and other direct costs, compensation, billing, labor, and general information technology.
L0:Material weakness means a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the internal control over information in contractor
L0:business systems, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of such information will not be
L0:prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A reasonable possibility exists when the likelihood of an event
L0:occurring is—
L1:(1) Probable; or
L1:(2) More than remote but less than likely (section 806 of Pub. L. 116-283).
L1:(b) General. The Contractor shall establish and maintain an acceptable accounting system. Failure to maintain an
L0:acceptable accounting system, as defined in this clause, shall result in the withholding of payments if the contract includes
L0:the clause at 252.242-7005 , Contractor Business Systems, and also may result in disapproval of the system.
L1:(c) System criteria. The Contractor’s accounting system shall provide for—
L1:(1) A sound internal control environment, accounting framework, and organizational structure;
L1:(2) Proper segregation of direct costs from indirect costs;
L1:(3) Identification and accumulation of direct costs by contract;
L1:(4) A logical and consistent method for the accumulation and allocation of indirect costs to intermediate and final cost
L0:objectives;
L1:(5) Accumulation of costs under general ledger control;
L1:(6) Reconciliation of subsidiary cost ledgers and cost objectives to general ledger;
L1:(7) Approval and documentation of adjusting entries;
L1:(8) Management reviews or internal audits of the system to ensure compliance with the Contractor’s established policies,
L0:procedures, and accounting practices;
L1:(9) A timekeeping system that identifies employees’ labor by intermediate or final cost objectives;
L1:(10) A labor distribution system that charges direct and indirect labor to the appropriate cost objectives;
L1:(11) Interim (at least monthly) determination of costs charged to a contract through routine posting of books of account;
L1:(12) Exclusion from costs charged to Government contracts of amounts which are not allowable in terms of Federal
L0:Acquisition Regulation (FAR) part 31, Contract Cost Principles and Procedures, and other contract provisions;
L1:(13) Identification of costs by contract line item and by units (as if each unit or line item were a separate contract), if

title: 252.244-7001 Contractor Purchasing System Administration
252.246-7007 Contractor Counterfeit Electronic Part Detection and Avoidance System
content:
L0:252.246-7007 Contractor Counterfeit Electronic Part Detection and Avoidance System.
L0:As prescribed in 246.870-3 (a), use the following clause:
L0:CONTRACTOR COUNTERFEIT ELECTRONIC PART DETECTION AND AVOIDANCE SYSTEM (JAN 2023)
L0:The following paragraphs (a) through (e) of this clause do not apply unless the Contractor is subject to the Cost Accounting
L0:Standards under 41 U.S.C. chapter 15, as implemented in regulations found at 48 CFR 9903.201-1.
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Authorized aftermarket manufacturer” means an organization that fabricates a part under a contract with, or with the
L0:express written authority of, the original component manufacturer based on the original component manufacturer’s designs,
L0:formulas, and/or specifications.
L0:“Authorized supplier” means a supplier, distributor, or an aftermarket manufacturer with a contractual arrangement with, or
L0:the express written authority of, the original manufacturer or current design activity to buy, stock, repackage, sell, or
L0:distribute the part.
L0:“Contract manufacturer” means a company that produces goods under contract for another company under the label or
L0:brand name of that company.
L0:“Contractor-approved supplier” means a supplier that does not have a contractual agreement with the original component
L0:manufacturer for a transaction, but has been identified as trustworthy by a contractor or subcontractor.
L0:“Counterfeit electronic part” means an unlawful or unauthorized reproduction, substitution, or alteration that has been
L0:knowingly mismarked, misidentified, or otherwise misrepresented to be an authentic, unmodified electronic part from the
L0:original manufacturer, or a source with the express written authority of the original manufacturer or current design activity,
L0:including an authorized aftermarket manufacturer. Unlawful or unauthorized substitution includes used electronic parts
L0:represented as new, or the false identification of grade, serial number, lot number, date code, or performance
L0:characteristics.
L0:“Electronic part” means an integrated circuit, a discrete electronic component (including, but not limited to, a transistor,
L0:capacitor, resistor, or diode), or a circuit assembly (section 818(f)(2) of Pub. L. 112-81).
L0:“Obsolete electronic part” means an electronic part that is no longer available from the original manufacturer or an
L0:authorized aftermarket manufacturer.
L0:"Original component manufacturer" means an organization that designs and/or engineers a part and is entitled to any
L0:intellectual property rights to that part.
L0:“Original equipment manufacturer” means a company that manufactures products that it has designed from purchased
L0:components and sells those products under the company's brand name.
L0:“Original manufacturer” means the original component manufacturer, the original equipment manufacturer, or the contract
L0:manufacturer.
L0:“Suspect counterfeit electronic part” means an electronic part for which credible evidence (including, but not limited to,
L0:visual inspection or testing) provides reasonable doubt that the electronic part is authentic.
L1:(b) Acceptable counterfeit electronic part detection and avoidance system.The Contractor shall establish and maintain an
L0:acceptable counterfeit electronic part detection and avoidance system. Failure to maintain an acceptable counterfeit
L0:electronic part detection and avoidance system, as defined in this clause, may result in disapproval of the purchasing
L0:system by the Contracting Officer and/or withholding of payments and affect the allowability of costs of counterfeit
L0:electronic parts or suspect counterfeit electronic parts and the cost of rework or corrective action that may be required to
L0:remedy the use or inclusion of such parts (see DFARS 231.205-71 ).
L1:(c) System criteria. A counterfeit electronic part detection and avoidance system shall include risk-based policies and
L0:procedures that address, at a minimum, the following areas:
L1:(1) The training of personnel.
L1:(2) The inspection and testing of electronic parts, including criteria for acceptance and rejection. Tests and inspections shall
L0:be performed in accordance with accepted Government- and industry-recognized techniques. Selection of tests and
L0:inspections shall be based on minimizing risk to the Government. Determination of risk shall be based on the assessed
L0:probability of receiving a counterfeit electronic part; the probability that the inspection or test selected will detect a
L0:counterfeit electronic part; and the potential negative consequences of a counterfeit electronic part being installed (e.g.,
L0:human safety, mission success) where such consequences are made known to the Contractor.
L1:(3) Processes to abolish counterfeit parts proliferation.
L1:(4) Risk-based processes that enable tracking of electronic parts from the original manufacturer to product acceptance by
L0:the Government, whether the electronic parts are supplied as discrete electronic parts or are contained in assemblies, in
L0:accordance with paragraph (c) of the clause at 252.246-7008 , Sources of Electronic Parts (also see paragraph (c)(2) of this
L0:clause).
L1:(5) Use of suppliers in accordance with the clause at 252.246-7008 .
L1:(6) Reporting and quarantining of counterfeit electronic parts and suspect counterfeit electronic parts. Reporting is required
L0:to the Contracting Officer and to the Government-Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP) when the Contractor becomes
L0:aware of, or has reason to suspect that, any electronic part or end item, component, part, or assembly containing electronic
L0:parts purchased by the DoD, or purchased by a Contractor for delivery to, or on behalf of, the DoD, contains counterfeit
L0:electronic parts or suspect counterfeit electronic parts. Counterfeit electronic parts and suspect counterfeit electronic parts
L0:shall not be returned to the seller or otherwise returned to the supply chain until such time that the parts are determined to
L0:be authentic.
L1:(7) Methodologies to identify suspect counterfeit parts and to rapidly determine if a suspect counterfeit part is, in fact,
L0:counterfeit.
L1:(8) Design, operation, and maintenance of systems to detect and avoid counterfeit electronic parts and suspect counterfeit
L0:electronic parts. The Contractor may elect to use current Government- or industry-recognized standards to meet this
L0:requirement.
L1:(9) Flow down of counterfeit detection and avoidance requirements, including applicable system criteria provided herein,
L0:to subcontractors at all levels in the supply chain that are responsible for buying or selling electronic parts or assemblies
L0:containing electronic parts, or for performing authentication testing.
L1:(10) Process for keeping continually informed of current counterfeiting information and trends, including detection and
L0:avoidance techniques contained in appropriate industry standards, and using such information and techniques for
L0:continuously upgrading internal processes.
L1:(11) Process for screening GIDEP reports and other credible sources of counterfeiting information to avoid the purchase or
L0:use of counterfeit electronic parts.
L1:(12) Control of obsolete electronic parts in order to maximize the availability and use of authentic, originally designed, and
L0:qualified electronic parts throughout the product’s life cycle.
L1:(d) Government review and evaluation of the Contractor’s policies and procedures will be accomplished as part of the
L0:evaluation of the Contractor’s purchasing system in accordance with 252.244-7001 , Contractor Purchasing System
L0:Administration—Basic, or Contractor Purchasing System Administration—Alternate I.
L1:(e) Subcontracts. The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, excluding the introductory text and including
L0:only paragraphs (a) through (e), in subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial products, for electronic parts or
L0:assemblies containing electronic parts.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.246-7007 — Contractor Counterfeit Electronic Part Detection and Avoidance System

L1:(ii) Elect a price or fee adjustment instead of correction or replacement.
L1:(3) In addition to the remedies under paragraphs (d)(1) and (2) of this clause, the Contractor shall be liable to the
L0:Government for all damages to the Government as a result of the breach of the warranty.
L1:(i) The additional liability under paragraph (d)(3) of this clause shall not exceed ten percent of the total contract price.
L1:(ii) If the breach of the warranty is with respect to the data supplied by an equipment subcontractor, the limit of the
L0:Contractor's liability shall be—
L1:(A) Ten percent of the total subcontract price in a firm-fixed-price subcontract;
L1:(B) Seventy-five percent of the total subcontract fee in a cost-plus-fixed-fee or cost-plus-award-fee subcontract; or
L1:(C) Seventy-five percent of the total subcontract target profit or fee in a fixed-price-incentive or cost-plus-incentive
L0:subcontract.
L1:(iii) The additional liability specified in paragraph (d)(3) of this clause shall not apply—
L1:(A) With respect to the requirements for product drawings and associated lists, special inspection equipment (SIE)
L0:drawings and associated lists, special tooling drawings and associated lists, SIE operating instructions, SIE descriptive
L0:documentation, and SIE calibration procedures under MIL-T-31000, General Specification for Technical Data Packages,
L0:Amendment 1, or MIL-T-47500, General Specification for Technical Data Packages, Supp 1, or drawings and associated
L0:lists under level 2 or level 3 of MIL-D-1000A, Engineering and Associated Data Drawings, or DoD-D-1000B, Engineering
L0:and Associated Lists Drawings (Inactive for New Design) Amendment 4, Notice 1; or drawings and associated lists under
L0:category E or I of MIL-D-1000, Engineering and Associated Lists Drawings, provided that the data furnished by the
L0:Contractor was current, accurate at time of submission, and did not involve a significant omission of data necessary to
L0:comply with the requirements; or
L1:(B) To defects the Contractor discovers and gives written notice to the Government before the Government discovers the
L0:error.
L1:(e) The provisions of this clause apply anew to that portion of any corrected or replaced technical data furnished to the
L0:Government under paragraph (d)(1)(i) of this clause.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.246-7002 Warranty of Construction (Germany)
content:
L0:252.246-7002 Warranty of Construction (Germany).
L0:As prescribed in 246.710 (2), use the following clause:
L0:WARRANTY OF CONSTRUCTION (GERMANY) (JUN 1997)
L1:(a) In addition to any other representations in this contract, the Contractor warrants, except as provided in paragraph (j) of
L0:this clause, that the work performed under this contract conforms to the contract requirements and is free of any defect of
L0:equipment, material, or design furnished or workmanship performed by the Contractor or any subcontractor or supplier at
L0:any tier.
L1:(b) This warranty shall continue for the period(s) specified in Section 13, VOB, Part B, commencing from the date of final
L0:acceptance of the work under this contract. If the Government takes possession of any part of the work before final
L0:acceptance, this warranty shall continue for the period(s) specified in Section 13, VOB, Part B, from the date the
L0:Government takes possession.
L1:(c) The Contractor shall remedy, at the Contractor’s expense, any failure to conform or any defect. In addition, the
L0:Contractor shall remedy, at the Contractor’s expense, any damage to Government-owned or -controlled real or personal
L0:property when that damage is the result of—
L1:(1) The Contractor’s failure to conform to contract requirements; or
L1:(2) Any defect of equipment, material, or design furnished or workmanship performed.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall restore any work damaged in fulfilling the terms and conditions of this clause.
L1:(e) The Contracting Officer shall notify the Contractor, in writing, within a reasonable period of time after the discovery of
L0:any failure, defect, or damage.
L1:(f) If the Contractor fails to remedy any failure, defect, or damage within a reasonable period of time after receipt of notice,
L0:the Government shall have the right to replace, repair, or otherwise remedy the failure, defect, or damage at the
L0:Contractor’s expense.
L1:(g) With respect to all warranties, express or implied, from subcontractors, manufacturers, or suppliers for work performed
L0:and materials furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Obtain all warranties that would be given in normal commercial practice;
L1:(2) Require all warranties to be executed in writing, for the benefit of the Government, if directed by the Contracting
L0:Officer; and
L1:(3) Enforce all warranties for the benefit of the Government as directed by the Contracting Officer.
L1:(h) In the event the Contractor’s warranty under paragraph (b) of this clause has expired, the Government may bring suit at
L0:its expense to enforce a subcontractor’s, manufacturer’s, or supplier’s warranty.
L1:(i) Unless a defect is caused by the Contractor’s negligence, or the negligence of a subcontractor or supplier at any tier, the
L0:Contractor shall not be liable for the repair of any defects of material or design furnished by the Government or for the
L0:repair of any damage resulting from any defect in Government-furnished material or design.
L1:(j) This warranty shall not limit the Government’s right under the Inspection clause of this contract, with respect to latent
L0:defects, gross mistakes, or fraud.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.246-7003 Notification of Potential Safety Issues
content:
L0:252.246-7003 Notification of Potential Safety Issues.
L0:As prescribed in 246.370 (a), use the following clause:
L0:NOTIFICATION OF POTENTIAL SAFETY ISSUES (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Credible information” means information that, considering its source and the surrounding circumstances, supports a
L0:reasonable belief that an event has occurred or will occur.
L0:“Critical safety item” means a part, subassembly, assembly, subsystem, installation equipment, or support equipment for a
L0:system that contains a characteristic, any failure, malfunction, or absence of which could have a safety impact.
L0:“Safety impact” means the occurrence of death, permanent total disability, permanent partial disability, or injury or
L0:occupational illness requiring hospitalization; loss of a weapon system; or property damage exceeding $1,000,000.
L0:“Subcontractor” means any supplier, distributor, vendor, or firm that furnishes supplies or services to or for the Contractor
L0:or another subcontractor under this contract.
L1:(b) The Contractor shall provide notification, in accordance with paragraph (c) of this clause, of—
L1:(1) All nonconformances for parts identified as critical safety items acquired by the Government under this contract; and
L1:(2) All nonconformances or deficiencies that may result in a safety impact for systems, or subsystems, assemblies,
L0:subassemblies, or parts integral to a system, acquired by or serviced for the Government under this contract.
L1:(c) The Contractor—
L1:(1) Shall notify the Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO) and the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) as soon as
L0:practicable, but not later than 72 hours, after discovering or acquiring credible information concerning nonconformances
L0:and deficiencies described in paragraph (b) of this clause; and
L1:(2) Shall provide a written notification to the ACO and the PCO within 5 working days that includes—
L1:(i) A summary of the defect or nonconformance;
L1:(ii) A chronology of pertinent events;
L1:(iii) The identification of potentially affected items to the extent known at the time of notification;
L1:(iv) A point of contact to coordinate problem analysis and resolution; and
L1:(v) Any other relevant information.
L1:(d) The Contractor—
L1:(1) Is responsible for the notification of potential safety issues occurring with regard to an item furnished by any
L0:subcontractor; and
L1:(2) Shall facilitate direct communication between the Government and the subcontractor as necessary.
L1:(e) Notification of safety issues under this clause shall be considered neither an admission of responsibility nor a release of
L0:liability for the defect or its consequences. This clause does not affect any right of the Government or the Contractor
L0:established elsewhere in this contract.
L1:(f) Subcontracts. (1) The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (f), in subcontracts
L0:for—
L1:(i) Parts identified as critical safety items;
L1:(ii) Systems and subsystems, assemblies, and subassemblies integral to a system; or
L1:(iii) Repair, maintenance, logistics support, or overhaul services for systems and subsystems, assemblies, subassemblies,
L0:and parts integral to a system.
L1:(2) For those subcontracts, including subcontracts for commercial products or commercial services, described in paragraph
L1:(f)(1) of this clause, the Contractor shall require the subcontractor to provide the notification required by paragraph (c) of
L0:this clause to—
L1:(i) The Contractor or higher-tier subcontractor; and
L1:(ii) The ACO and the PCO, if the subcontractor is aware of the ACO and the PCO for the contract.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.246-7003 — Notification of Potential Safety Issues

title: 252.246-7005 Notice of Warranty Tracking of Serialized Items
content:

L0:NOTICE OF WARRANTY TRACKING OF SERIALIZED ITEMS (MAR 2016)
L1:(a) Definitions. “Duration,” “enterprise”, “enterprise identifier,” “fixed expiration,” “item type,” “serialized item,” “starting
L0:event,” “unique item identifier,” “usage,” “warranty administrator,” “warranty guarantor,” and “warranty tracking” are

title: 252.246-7006 Warranty Tracking of Serialized Items
content:
L0:252.246-7006 Warranty Tracking of Serialized Items.
L0:As prescribed in 246.710 (3)(ii), use the following clause:
L0:WARRANTY TRACKING OF SERIALIZED ITEMS (MAR 2016)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Duration” means the warranty period. This period may be a stated period of time, amount of usage, or the occurrence of a
L0:specified event, after formal acceptance of delivery, for the Government to assert a contractual right for the correction of
L0:defects.
L0:“Enterprise” means the entity (e.g., a manufacturer or vendor) responsible for granting the warranty and/or assigning
L0:unique item identifiers to serialized warranty items.
L0:“Enterprise identifier” means a code that is uniquely assigned to an enterprise by an issuing agency.
L0:“First use” means the initial or first-time use of a product by the Government.
L0:“Fixed expiration” means the date the warranty expires and the Contractor’s obligation to provide for a remedy or
L0:corrective action ends.
L0:“Installation” means the date a unit is inserted into a higher level assembly in order to make that assembly operational.
L0:“Issuing agency” means an organization responsible for assigning a globally unique identifier to an enterprise, as indicated
L0:in the Register of Issuing Agency Codes for International Standards Organization/International Electrotechnical
L0:Commission, located at http://www.aimglobal.org/?Reg_Authority15459.
L0:“Item type” means a coded representation of the description of the item being warranted, consisting of the codes C component procured separate from end item, S - subassembly procured separate from end item or subassembly, E -
L0:embedded in component, subassembly or end item parent, and P - parent end item.
L0:“Starting event” means the event or action that initiates the warranty, such as first use or upon installation.
L0:“Serialized item” means each item produced is assigned a serial number that is unique among all the collective tangible
L0:items produced by the enterprise, or each item of a particular part, lot, or batch number is assigned a unique serial number
L0:within that part, lot, or batch number assignment within the enterprise identifier. The enterprise is responsible for ensuring
L0:unique serialization within the enterprise identifier or within the part, lot, or batch numbers, and that serial numbers, once
L0:assigned, are never used again.
L0:“Unique item identifier” means a set of data elements marked on an item that is globally unique and unambiguous.
L0:“Usage” means the quantity and an associated unit of measure that specifies the amount of a characteristic subject to the
L0:contractor’s obligation to provide for remedy or corrective action, such as a number of miles, hours, or cycles.
L0:“Warranty administrator” means the organization specified by the guarantor for managing the warranty.
L0:“Warranty guarantor” means the enterprise that provides the warranty under the terms and conditions of a contract.
L0:“Warranty repair source” means the organization specified by a warranty guarantor for receiving and managing warranty
L0:items that are returned by a customer.
L0:“Warranty tracking” means the ability to trace a warranted item from delivery through completion of the effectivity of the
L0:warranty.
L1:(b) Reporting of data for warranty tracking and administration.
L1:(1) The Contractor shall provide the information required by the attachment entitled “Warranty Tracking Information” on
L0:each contract line item number, subline item number, or exhibit line item number for warranted items no later than the time
L0:of award. Information required in the warranty attachment shall include such information as duration, fixed expiration,
L0:item type, starting event, usage, warranty administrator enterprise identifier, and warranty guarantor enterprise identifier.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall provide the following information no later than when the warranted items are presented for receipt
L0:and/or acceptance—
L1:(A) The unique item identifier for each warranted item required by the attachment entitled “Warranty Tracking
L0:Information;” and
L1:(B) The warranty repair source information and instructions for each warranted item required by the attachment entitled
L0:“Source of Repair Instructions.”
L1:(3) The Contractor shall submit the data for warranty tracking to the Contracting Officer with a copy to the requiring
L0:activity and the Contracting Officer Representative.
L1:(4) For additional information on warranty attachments, see the “Warranty and Source of Repair” training and “Warranty
L0:and Source of Repair Tracking User Guide” accessible on the Product Data Reporting and Evaluation Program (PDREP)
L0:website at https://www.pdrep.csd.disa.mil/pdrep_files/other/wsr.htm.
L1:(c) Reservation of rights. The terms of this clause shall not be construed to limit the Government’s rights or remedies under
L0:any other contract clause.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.246-7006 — Warranty Tracking of Serialized Items

title: 252.246-7008 Sources of Electronic Parts
content:
L0:252.246-7008 Sources of Electronic Parts.
L0:As prescribed in 246.870-3 (b), use the following clause:
L0:SOURCES OF ELECTRONIC PARTS (JAN 2023)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Authorized aftermarket manufacturer” means an organization that fabricates a part under a contract with, or with the
L0:express written authority of, the original component manufacturer based on the original component manufacturer’s designs,
L0:formulas, and/or specifications.
L0:“Authorized supplier” means a supplier, distributor, or an aftermarket manufacturer with a contractual arrangement with, or
L0:the express written authority of, the original manufacturer or current design activity to buy, stock, repackage, sell, or
L0:distribute the part.
L0:“Contract manufacturer” means a company that produces goods under contract for another company under the label or
L0:brand name of that company.
L0:“Contractor-approved supplier” means a supplier that does not have a contractual agreement with the original component
L0:manufacturer for a transaction, but has been identified as trustworthy by a contractor or subcontractor.
L0:“Electronic part” means an integrated circuit, a discrete electronic component (including, but not limited to, a transistor,
L0:capacitor, resistor, or diode), or a circuit assembly (section 818(f)(2) of Pub. L. 112-81).
L0:"Original component manufacturer" means an organization that designs and/or engineers a part and is entitled to any
L0:intellectual property rights to that part.
L0:“Original equipment manufacturer” means a company that manufactures products that it has designed from purchased
L0:components and sells those products under the company's brand name.
L0:“Original manufacturer” means the original component manufacturer, the original equipment manufacturer, or the contract
L0:manufacturer.
L1:(b) Selecting suppliers. In accordance with section 818(c)(3) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year
L0:2012 (Pub. L. 112-81), as amended by section 817 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2015 (Pub. L.
L0:113-291) and section 885 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (Pub. L. 114-92), the Contractor
L0:shall—
L1:(1) First obtain electronic parts that are in production by the original manufacturer or an authorized aftermarket
L0:manufacturer or currently available in stock from—
L1:(i) The original manufacturers of the parts;
L1:(ii) Their authorized suppliers; or
L1:(iii) Suppliers that obtain such parts exclusively from the original manufacturers of the parts or their authorized suppliers;
L1:(2) If electronic parts are not available as provided in paragraph (b)(1) of this clause, obtain electronic parts that are not in
L0:production by the original manufacturer or an authorized aftermarket manufacturer, and that are not currently available in
L0:stock from a source listed in paragraph (b)(1) of this clause, from suppliers identified by the Contractor as contractorapproved suppliers, provided that—
L1:(i) For identifying and approving such contractor-approved suppliers, the Contractor uses established counterfeit
L0:prevention industry standards and processes (including inspection, testing, and authentication), such as the DoD-adopted
L0:standards at https://assist.dla.mil;
L1:(ii) The Contractor assumes responsibility for the authenticity of parts provided by such contractor-approved suppliers; and
L1:(iii) The Contractor’s selection of such contractor-approved suppliers is subject to review, audit, and approval by the
L0:Government, generally in conjunction with a contractor purchasing system review or other surveillance of purchasing
L0:practices by the contract administration office, or if the Government obtains credible evidence that a contractor-approved
L0:supplier has provided counterfeit parts. The Contractor may proceed with the acquisition of electronic parts from a
L0:contractor-approved supplier unless otherwise notified by DoD; or
L1:(3)(i) Take the actions in paragraph (b)(3)(ii) of this clause if the Contractor—
L1:(A) Obtains an electronic part from—
L1:(1) A source other than any of the sources identified in paragraph (b)(1) or (b)(2) of this clause, due to nonavailability from
L0:such sources; or
L1:(2) A subcontractor (other than the original manufacturer) that refuses to accept flowdown of this clause; or
L1:(B) Cannot confirm that an electronic part is new or previously unused and that it has not been comingled in supplier new
L0:production or stock with used, refurbished, reclaimed, or returned parts.
L1:(ii) If the contractor obtains an electronic part or cannot confirm an electronic part pursuant to paragraph (b)(3)(i) of this
L0:clause—
L1:(A) Promptly notify the Contracting Officer in writing. If such notification is required for an electronic part to be used in a
L0:designated lot of assemblies to be acquired under a single contract, the Contractor may submit one notification for the lot,
L0:providing identification of the assemblies containing the parts (e.g., serial numbers);
L1:(B) Be responsible for inspection, testing, and authentication, in accordance with existing applicable industry standards;
L0:and
L1:(C) Make documentation of inspection, testing, and authentication of such electronic parts available to the Government
L0:upon request.
L1:(c) Traceability.If the Contractor is not the original manufacturer of, or authorized supplier for, an electronic part, the
L0:Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Have risk-based processes (taking into consideration the consequences of failure of an electronic part) that enable
L0:tracking of electronic parts from the original manufacturer to product acceptance by the Government, whether the
L0:electronic part is supplied as a discrete electronic part or is contained in an assembly;
L1:(2) If the Contractor cannot establish this traceability from the original manufacturer for a specific electronic part, be
L0:responsible for inspection, testing, and authentication, in accordance with existing applicable industry standards; and
L1:(3)(i) Maintain documentation of traceability (paragraph (c)(1) of this clause) or the inspection, testing, and authentication
L0:required when traceability cannot be established (paragraph (c)(2) of this clause) in accordance with FAR subpart 4.7; and
L1:(ii) Make such documentation available to the Government upon request.
L1:(d) Government sources. Contractors and subcontractors are still required to comply with the requirements of paragraphs
L1:(b) and (c) of this clause, as applicable, if—
L1:(1) Authorized to purchase electronic parts from the Federal Supply Schedule;
L1:(2) Purchasing electronic parts from suppliers accredited by the Defense Microelectronics Activity; or
L1:(3) Requisitioning electronic parts from Government inventory/stock under the authority of 252.251-7000 , Ordering from
L0:Government Supply Sources.
L1:(i) The cost of any required inspection, testing, and authentication of such parts may be charged as a direct cost.
L1:(ii) The Government is responsible for the authenticity of the requisitioned parts. If any such part is subsequently found to
L0:be counterfeit or suspect counterfeit, the Government will—
L1:(A) Promptly replace such part at no charge; and
L1:(B) Consider an adjustment in the contract schedule to the extent that replacement of the counterfeit or suspect counterfeit
L0:electronic parts caused a delay in performance.
L1:(e) Subcontracts.The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause, including this paragraph (e), in subcontracts,
L0:including subcontracts for commercial products, that are for electronic parts or assemblies containing electronic parts,
L0:unless the subcontractor is the original manufacturer.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.247-7000 Hardship Conditions
content:
L0:252.247-7000 Hardship Conditions.
L0:As prescribed in 247.270-4 (a), use the following clause:
L0:HARDSHIP CONDITIONS (AUG 2000)
L1:(a) If the Contractor finds unusual ship, dock, or cargo conditions associated with loading or unloading a particular cargo,
L0:that will work a hardship on the Contractor if loaded or unloaded at the basic commodity rates, the Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Notify the Contracting Officer before performing the work, if feasible, but no later than the vessel sailing time; and
L1:(2) Submit any associated request for price adjustment to the Contracting Officer within 10 working days of the vessel
L0:sailing time.
L1:(b) Unusual conditions include, but are not limited to, inaccessibility of place of stowage to the ship's cargo gear, side port
L0:operations, and small quantities of cargo in any one hatch.
L1:(c) The Contracting Officer will investigate the conditions promptly after receiving the notice. If the Contracting Officer
L0:finds that the conditions are unusual and do materially affect the cost of loading or unloading, the Contracting Officer will
L0:authorize payment at the applicable man-hour rates set forth in the schedule of rates of this contract.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.247-7002 Revision of Prices
content:
L0:252.247-7002 Revision of Prices.
L0:As prescribed in 247.270-4 (b), use the following clause:
L0:REVISION OF PRICES (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Definition. “Wage adjustment,” as used in this clause, means a change in the wages, salaries, or other terms or
L0:conditions of employment which—
L1:(1) Substantially affects the cost of performing this contract;
L1:(2) Is generally applicable to the port where work under this contract is performed; and
L1:(3) Applies to operations by the Contractor on non-Government work as well as to work under this contract.
L1:(b) General. The prices fixed in this contract are based on wages and working conditions established by collective
L0:bargaining agreements, and on other conditions in effect on the date of this contract. The Contracting Officer and the
L0:Contractor may agree to increase or decrease such prices in accordance with this clause.
L1:(c) Demand for negotiation.
L1:(1) At any time, subject to the limitations specified in this clause, either the Contracting Officer or the Contractor may
L0:deliver to the other a written demand that the parties negotiate to revise the prices under this contract.
L1:(2) No such demand shall be made before 90 days after the date of this contract, and thereafter neither party shall make a
L0:demand having an effective date within 90 days of the effective date of any prior demand. However, this limitation does
L0:not apply to a wage adjustment during the 90 day period.
L1:(3) Each demand shall specify a date (the same as or subsequent to the date of the delivery of the demand) as to when the
L0:revised prices shall be effective. This date is the effective date of the price revision.
L1:(i) If the Contractor makes a demand under this clause, the demand shall briefly state the basis of the demand and include
L0:the statements and data referred to in paragraph (d) of this clause.
L1:(ii) If the demand is made by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall furnish the statements and data within 30 days of
L0:the delivery of the demand.
L1:(d) Submission of data. At the times specified in paragraphs (c)(3)(i) and (ii) of this clause, the Contractor shall submit—
L1:(1) A new estimate and breakdown of the unit cost and the proposed prices for the services the Contractor will perform
L0:under this contract after the effective date of the price revision, itemized to be consistent with the original negotiations of
L0:the contract;
L1:(2) An explanation of the difference between the original (or last preceding) estimate and the new estimate;
L1:(3) Such relevant operating data, cost records, overhead absorption reports, and accounting statements as may be of
L0:assistance in determining the accuracy and reliability of the new estimate;
L1:(4) A statement of the actual costs of performance under this contract to the extent that they are available at the time of the
L0:negotiation of the revision of prices under this clause; and
L1:(5) Any other relevant data usually furnished in the case of negotiations of prices under a new contract. The Government
L0:may examine and audit the Contractor's accounts, records, and books as the Contracting Officer considers necessary.
L1:(e) Negotiations.
L1:(1) Upon the filing of the statements and data required by paragraph (d) of this clause, the Contractor and the Contracting
L0:Officer shall negotiate promptly in good faith to agree upon prices for services the Contractor will perform on and after the
L0:effective date of the price revision.
L1:(2) If the prices in this contract were established by competitive negotiation, they shall not be revised upward unless
L0:justified by changes in conditions occurring after the contract was awarded.
L1:(3) The agreement reached after each negotiation will be incorporated into the contract by supplemental agreement.
L1:(f) Disagreements. If, within 30 days after the date on which statements and data are required pursuant to paragraph (c) of
L0:this clause, the Contracting Officer and the Contractor fail to agree to revised prices, the failure to agree shall be resolved
L0:in accordance with the Disputes clause of this contract. The prices fixed by the Contracting Officer will remain in effect for
L0:the balance of the contract, and the Contractor shall continue performance.

L0:shall support its request with—

L0:of this contract shall not affect the Contractor's right under paragraph (g) of this clause.

L0:amount of such adjustment, the disagreement will be resolved in accordance with the Disputes clause of this contract.

title: 252.247-7007 Liability and Insurance
content:
L0:252.247-7007 Liability and Insurance.
L0:As prescribed in 247.270-4 (c), use the following clause:
L0:LIABILITY AND INSURANCE (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) The Contractor shall be—
L1:(1) Liable to the Government for loss or damage to property, real and personal, owned by the Government or for which the
L0:Government is liable;
L1:(2) Responsible for, and hold the Government harmless from, loss of or damage to property not included in paragraph (a)
L1:(1); and
L1:(3) Responsible for, and hold the Government harmless from, bodily injury and death of persons, resulting either in whole
L0:or in part from the negligence or fault of the Contractor, its officers, agents, or employees in the performance of work under
L0:this contract.
L1:(b) For the purpose of this clause, all cargo loaded or unloaded under this contract is agreed to be property owned by the
L0:Government or property for which the Government is liable.
L1:(1) The amount of the loss or damage as determined by the Contracting Officer will be withheld from payments otherwise
L0:due the Contractor.
L1:(2) Determination of liability and responsibility by the Contracting Officer will constitute questions of fact within the
L0:meaning of the Disputes clause of this contract.
L1:(c) The general liability and responsibility of the Contractor under this clause are subject only to the following specific
L0:limitations. The Contractor is not responsible to the Government for, and does not agree to hold the Government harmless
L0:from, loss or damage to property or bodily injury to or death of persons if—
L1:(1) The unseaworthiness of the vessel, or failure or defect of the gear or equipment furnished by the Government,
L0:contributed jointly with the fault or negligence of the Contractor in causing such damage, injury, or death; and
L1:(i) The Contractor, his officers, agents, and employees, by the exercise of due diligence, could not have discovered such
L0:unseaworthiness or defect of gear or equipment; or
L1:(ii) Through the exercise of due diligence could not otherwise have avoided such damage, injury, or death.
L1:(2) The damage, injury, or death resulted solely from an act or omission of the Government or its employees, or resulted
L0:solely from proper compliance by officers, agents, or employees of the Contractor with specific directions of the
L0:Contracting Officer.
L1:(d) The Contractor shall at its own expense acquire and maintain insurance during the term of this contract, as follows—
L1:(1) Standard workmen's compensation and employer's liability insurance and longshoremen's and harbor workers'
L0:compensation insurance, or such of these as may be proper under applicable state or Federal statutes.
L1:(i) The Contractor may, with the prior approval of the Contracting Officer, be a self-insurer against the risk of this
L0:paragraph (d)(1).
L1:(ii) This approval will be given upon receipt of satisfactory evidence that the Contractor has qualified as a self-insurer
L0:under applicable provision of law.
L1:(2) Bodily injury liability insurance in an amount of not less than $300,000 on account of any one occurrence.
L1:(3) Property damage liability insurance (which shall include any and all property, whether or not in the care, custody, or
L0:control of the Contractor) in an amount of not less than $300,000 for any one occurrence.
L1:(e) Each policy shall provide, by appropriate endorsement or otherwise, that cancellation or material change in the policy
L0:shall not be effective until after a 30 day written notice is furnished the Contracting Officer.
L1:(f) The Contractor shall furnish the Contracting Officer with satisfactory evidence of the insurance required in paragraph
L1:(d) before performance of any work under this contract.
L1:(g) The Contractor shall, at its own cost and expense, defend any suits, demands, claims, or actions, in which the United
L0:States might be named as a co-defendant of the Contractor, resulting from the Contractor's performance of work under this
L0:contract. This requirement is without regard to whether such suit, demand, claim, or action was the result of the
L0:Contractor's negligence. The Government shall have the right to appear in such suit, participate in defense, and take such
L0:actions as may be necessary to protect the interest of the United States.
L1:(h) It is expressly agreed that the provisions in paragraphs (d) through (g) of this clause shall not in any manner limit the
L0:liability or extend the liability of the Contractor as provided in paragraphs (a) through (c) of this clause.
L1:(i) The Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Equitably reimburse the Government if the Contractor is indemnified, reimbursed, or relieved of any loss or damage to
L0:Government property;
L1:(2) Do nothing to prevent the Government's right to recover against third parties for any such loss or damage; and
L1:(3) Furnish the Government, upon the request of the Contracting Officer, at the Government's expense, all reasonable
L0:assistance and cooperation in obtaining recovery, including the prosecution of suit and the execution of instruments of
L0:assignment in favor of the Government.
L0:(End of clause)

title: 252.247-7016 Contractor Liability for Loss or Damage
content:
L0:252.247-7016 Contractor Liability for Loss or Damage.
L0:As prescribed in 247.271-3 (d), use the following clause:
L0:CONTRACTOR LIABILITY FOR LOSS OR DAMAGE (DEC 1991)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:“Article” means any shipping piece or package and its contents.
L0:“Schedule” means the level of service for which specific types of traffic apply as described in DoD 4500.34-R, Personal
L0:Property Traffic Management Regulation.
L1:(b) For shipments picked up under Schedule I, Outbound Services, or delivered under Schedule II, Inbound Services—
L1:(1) If notified within one year after delivery that the owner has discovered loss or damage to the owner's property, the
L0:Contractor agrees to indemnify the Government for loss or damage to the property which arises from any cause while it is
L0:in the Contractor's possession. The Contractor's liability is—
L1:(i) Non-negligent damage. For any cause, other than the Contractor's negligence, indemnification shall be at a rate not to
L0:exceed sixty cents per pound per article.
L1:(ii) Negligent damage. When loss or damage is caused by the negligence of the Contractor, the liability is for the full cost
L0:of satisfactory repair or for the current replacement value of the article.
L1:(2) The Contractor shall make prompt payment to the owner of the property for any loss or damage for which the
L0:Contractor is liable.
L1:(3) In the absence of evidence or supporting documentation which places liability on a carrier or another contractor, the
L0:destination contractor shall be presumed to be liable for the loss or damage, if timely notified.
L1:(c) For shipments picked up or delivered under Schedule III, Intra-City and Intra-Area—
L1:(1) If notified of loss or damage within 75 days following delivery, the Contractor agrees to indemnify the Government for
L0:loss or damage to the owner's property.
L1:(2) The Contractor's liability shall be for the full cost of satisfactory repair, or for the current replacement value of the
L0:article less depreciation, up to a maximum liability of $1.25 per pound times the net weight of the shipment.
L1:(3) The Contractor has full salvage rights to damaged items which are not repairable and for which the Government has
L0:received compensation at replacement value.
L0:(End of clause)
citation: R-DFARS 252.247-7016 — Contractor Liability for Loss or Damage

title: 252.247-7023 Transportation of Supplies by Sea
content:
L0:252.247-7023 Transportation of Supplies by Sea.
L0:Basic. As prescribed in 247.574 (a) and (a)(1), use the following clause:
L0:TRANSPORTATION OF SUPPLIES BY SEA—BASIC (Oct 2024)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L0:"Foreign-flag vessel" means any vessel that is not a U.S.-flag vessel.
L0:"Ocean transportation" means any water-borne transportation aboard a ship, vessel, boat, barge, ferry, or the like outside
L0:the internal waters of the United States as defined in 33 CFR 2.24.
L0:"Subcontractor" means a supplier, materialman, distributor, or vendor at any level below the prime contractor whose
L0:contractual obligation to perform results from, or is conditioned upon, award of the prime contract and who is performing
L0:any part of the work or other requirement of the prime contract.
L0:"Supplies" means supplies that are clearly identifiable for eventual use by or owned by DoD at the time of transportation
L0:by sea, or are otherwise transported by DoD, regardless of ownership or use by DoD. An item is clearly identifiable for
L0:eventual use by DoD if, for example, the contract documentation contains a reference to a DoD contract number or a
L0:military destination.
L0:"U.S.-flag vessel" means either a vessel belonging to the United States or a vessel of the United States as that term is
L0:defined in 46 U.S.C. 116.
L1:(b) If the transportation of supplies by sea is anticipated under this contract, the Contractor shall—
L1:(1) Notify the Contracting Officer and Maritime Administration (MARAD) at Cargo.Marad@dot.gov —
L1:(i) Within 3 business days after contract award; or
L1:(ii) Immediately prior to the shipment departure date necessary to meet delivery schedules, whichever is earlier; and
L1:(2) Include in the notification—
L1:(i) A statement of the Contractor's intent to transport supplies by sea;
L1:(ii) The contract number; and
L1:(iii) The task-order or delivery-order number, when applicable.
L1:(c)(1) The Contractor shall use U.S.-flag vessels when transporting any supplies by sea under this contract.
L1:(2) A subcontractor transporting supplies by sea under this contract shall use U.S.-flag vessels if—
L1:(i) This contract is a construction contract; or
L1:(ii) The supplies being transported are—
L1:(A) Other than commercial products; or
L1:(B) Commercial products that—
L1:(1)The Contractor is reselling or distributing to the Government without adding value (generally, the Contractor does not
L0:add value to items that it subcontracts for f.o.b. destination shipment);
L1:(2)Are shipped in direct support of U.S. military contingency operations, exercises, or forces deployed in humanitarian or
L0:peacekeeping operations; or
L1:(3)Are commissary or exchange cargoes transported outside of the Defense Transportation System in accordance with 10
L0:U.S.C. 2643.
L1:(d) The Contractor and its subcontractors may request, via the Contracting Officer, a waiver of the requirement to use a
L0:U.S.-flag vessel, or identification of any available U.S.-flag vessels, if the Contractor or a subcontractor sufficiently
L0:explains that—
L1:(1) U.S.-flag vessels are not available at a fair and reasonable rate for commercial vessels of the United States; or
L1:(2) U.S.-flag vessels are otherwise not available.
L1:(e) The Contractor must submit any request for use of foreign-flag vessels in writing to the Contracting Officer at least 45
L0:days prior to the sailing date necessary to meet its delivery schedules. The Contracting Officer will process requests
L0:submitted after such date(s) as expeditiously as possible, however, if a DoD waiver is not approved prior to the shipper's
L0:sailing date, this will not of itself constitute a compensable delay under this or any other clause of this contract. Requests
L0:shall contain at a minimum—
L1:(1) Type, weight, and cube of cargo;
L1:(2) Required shipping date(s) and required delivery date(s);
L1:(3) Special handling and discharge requirements;
L1:(4) Loading and discharge points;
L1:(5) Name of shipper and consignee;
L1:(6) Prime contract number; and
L1:(7) A documented description of current, diligent efforts made to secure U.S.-flag vessels, including points of contact (with
L0:names and telephone numbers) with at least two U.S.-flag carriers contacted. Copies of quotes will suffice for this purpose.
L0:Copies of telephone notes, emails, and other relevant communications will otherwise be considered for this purpose.
L1:(f) The Contractor shall, within 30 days after each shipment covered by this clause, provide the Contracting Officer and
L0:MARAD at Cargo.Marad@dot.gov, Attention: Military Team, one copy of the rated on board vessel operating carrier's
L0:ocean bill of lading, which shall contain the following information:
L1:(1) Prime contract number;
L1:(2) Name of vessel;
L1:(3) Vessel flag of registry;
L1:(4) Date of loading;
L1:(5) Port of loading;
L1:(6) Port of final discharge;
L1:(7) Description of commodity;
L1:(8) Gross weight in pounds and cubic feet if available;
L1:(9) Total ocean freight in U.S. dollars; and
L1:(10) Name of the carrier.
L1:(g) If this contract exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold, the Contractor shall provide with its final invoice under this
L0:contract a representation that to the best of its knowledge and belief—
L1:(1) No ocean transportation was used in the performance of this contract;
L1:(2) Ocean transportation was used and only U.S.-flag vessels were used for all ocean shipments under the contract;
L1:(3) Ocean transportation was used, and the Contractor had received a prior-approved waiver for U.S.-flag vessels for all
L0:foreign-flag ocean transportation; or
L1:(4) Ocean transportation was used and some or all of the shipments were made on foreign-flag vessels without the written
L0:consent of DoD. The Contractor shall describe these shipments in the following format:
L0:ITEM DESCRIPTION
L0:QUANTITY
L0:CONTRACT LINE ITEMS
L0:TOTAL

title: Part 1 - Overview
content:
Overview
Overview
3

A Smarter Approach to Federal Acquisition
The Vision
This guide offers a foundational framework to navigate part of the acquisition planning process
aligned with the core principles of the Federal Acquisition Regulations System (FAR 1.102). The
aim isn’t to create more red tape but to help you to be a more effective, strategic buyer.
This Guide Promotes
● Commercial Utilization. Use the private sector’s competitive marketplace and
innovations whenever possible to deliver better, more cost-effective, and vendor-
agnostic solutions for the taxpayer.
● Prioritization of Existing Government-wide Contracts and Blanket Purchase
Agreements (BPAs). As prescribed in FAR 8.104, leverage the federal marketplace
where existing government-wide contracts and BPAs can meet agency needs.
● Simplicity and Efficiency. Streamline processes to reduce complexity and speed up
delivery. Our focus is on prioritizing rapid deployment and eliminating unnecessary
delays to accelerate mission success.
● Adaptability. Embrace change and be prepared to adjust your strategy based on new
information, user feedback, and evolving mission needs.
This Guide is Not
● A Compliance Checklist. This isn’t a rigid list of rules to be checked off. Instead, it’s a
resource to inform your decisions, encouraging you to apply its principles thoughtfully to
your unique situation.
● Limiting. We encourage you to use sound business judgement and critical thinking. Be
flexible and creative to achieve mission success, even if it means finding a better way of
doing business within this framework.
● Process Over Outcomes. The ultimate goal is always to achieve tangible results and
deliver value to the mission, not simply to follow a procedure for its own sake.
4

Navigating the Buying Process
Know your lane
Understanding the Continuum
The “simple” to “other-than-simple” continuum is a useful framework that helps you, a federal
buyer, categorize your procurement needs. Understanding where your requirement falls on this
spectrum helps you determine which regulatory FAR parts to follow, informs your market
research, and shapes your overall acquisition strategy.
