Part 4 - Administrative and Information Matters
## Compass guidance
Empowering Acquisition Through Efficient Administration

## Compass guidance (2)
PLEASE NOTE, CYBERSECURITY MATURITY MODEL CERTIFICATION ( CMMC) AND NATIONAL INDUSTRIAL SECURITY PROGRAM CONTRACT CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NCCS) HAVE MOVED FROM PART 4 TO PART 40

## Compass guidance (3)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! (DAF Requirement)

## Compass guidance (4)
Contracting officers are required to sign all contract actions (either via wet signature, signature as produced by CON-IT, or digital signature produced with a DoD Public Key Infrastructure certificate using a Common Access Card), ensure contractor signatures are obtained, if required or desired, and maintain signed contractual documents within the official contract file.

## Compass guidance (5)
Exchangeable repair contracts with provisions for modifications require specific CLIN structures when there are multiple output national stock numbers permitted. Whenever a family of part numbers may be input under a specific repair and modification CLIN and the output parts may have different NSNs, then each output NSN should have a separate subCLIN. This will permit assigning a completion date to specific reparable for delivery schedule tracking purposes.
Exchangeable repair contracts – refers to a contract that allows for the exchange of a defective product for a replacement.

## Compass guidance (6)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! (DAF Requirement)

## Compass guidance (7)
The chief of the contracting office may approve use of an early effective date (i.e., effective date prior to the contract award date) subject to the following conditions:
The negotiating parties have reached agreement on all terms and conditions, including price;
Funding is currently available; and
For early effective dates established more than 30 days prior to the projected contract award date, legal review has been obtained. An early effective date shall not be used if the government intends to direct a prospective contractor, to accept benefits of the contractor’s efforts, or to make payments before the contract award date.
After receiving approval to use an early effective date, the contracting officer shall notify the contractor of the early effective date in writing and include all of the following:
Agreed upon terms and conditions, including price;
A statement that any costs recognized in the resulting contract must be limited to those allowable, allocable, and reasonable costs that would be recognized if incurred after contract award;
A statement that if a contract is not awarded all incurred costs shall be at the contractor’s own risk;
A statement that costs cannot not be invoiced or paid until after contract award
And a statement that prior to contract award the government may not direct the contractor or accept benefits of the contractor’s efforts. The contracting officer should also advise the program office or requirements owner that the government cannot direct the contractor or accept benefits of the contractor’s efforts until after contract award.

## Compass guidance (8)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! (DAF Requirement)

## Compass guidance (9)
Electronic Retention of Contract Files
Contracting offices listed in KT Fileshare (KTFS) shall use it as both the working and official file, per RFO 4.309 . It shall be used to create, modify, store, access, and route documents necessary to manage the acquisition process for review and approval, over the life of the entire acquisition lifecycle, (e.g., requirements development to contract closeout.) Contracting Officers shall ensure that KTFS contains all appropriate contract documents required for the official contract file. If a contract document is maintained within the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE, https://wawf.eb.mil/ ), within Electronic Document Access (EDA), the Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS), or the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act Subaward Reporting System (FSRS), then that system is the official system of record; contracting officers are not required to duplicate the document in KTFS, unless the contracting office determines an exception applies to ensure ready accessibility to principal users (e.g., clearance reviewers, auditors). All contract files are required to include copies of Award Documents, copies of Government-Furnished Property (GFP) attachments, and PDS Validation. Contracting officers shall add screenshots of system of record documents (Reps/Certs, SAM/FAPIIS, etc.) that are dynamic/overwritten to reflect status at time of contract action. In addition, KTFS shall not be used to store documents that are not required to be part of the contract file such as CDRL submittals and annual CPARS reports.

## Compass guidance (10)
Contents of Contract Files
For contract offices not listed in KTFS and that maintain hard copy official contract files, SCOs may use the Air Force contract file content index templates below, or their own specific contract file content checklist or index to maintain contract files:
Operational Services and Construction
Research and Development
Systems and Logistics

## Compass guidance (11)
Storage, Handling, and Contract Files
As part of the Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) program, contract files shall be retained for a period of 10 years after the final invoice in accordance with DoD 7000.14-R, Volume 1, Chapter 9.
Prior to disposing of contract and other procurement files under Series 63, Acquisition, or Series 64, Contracting, of the Air Force Records Disposition Schedule, contracting officers shall ensure that all records necessary to support intellectual property rights are transferred to an appropriate Air Force organization with an appropriate system of records, such as research and development (R&D) case files. These records may include, but are not limited to: contracts, especially the solicitation/contract forms, the description/statement of work, and any attached licenses or data rights assertions; the solicitation; market research; the awardee’s proposal; preliminary and critical design review slides; the integrated master schedule; and data deliverables such as technical reports or software development plans and other procurement records that may grant the Government licenses to technical data, computer software, and other intellectual property or may be necessary to establish that a given technology was developed with Government funding, . To protect the Government’s intellectual property interests, records that support the intellectual property rights may need to be retained for multiple decades following contract closeout. Certain documents evidencing the Government’s rights and interests in intellectual property might also need to be recorded with other government entities, such as the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. Consult with legal counsel and records managers as necessary.

## SBIR/STTR
For a small business concern that is an offeror submitting a proposal under the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) program or the Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) program, the contracting officer is authorized to provide an opportunity to correct the offeror’s SAM.gov registration prior to award of an SBIR or STTR contract where:
the SBIR or STTR solicitation required registration in SAM.gov for contracts;
at the time of submission of the proposal, the offeror was registered in SAM.gov for grants;
the offeror is able to register in SAM.gov for contracts prior to award;
the corrective registration is ministerial in nature, i.e., the offeror is not changing its ownership, place of business or organization, small business size or status, or the substance of other representations and certifications; and
the contracting officer determines that the correction of the SAM.gov registration from grants to contracts is in the government’s best interest and furthers the statutory policy of 15 U.S.C. 638(a) to assist small business concerns’ participation in Federal research and development.

## Compass guidance (12)
Certification for Non-SAM Registered Vendors
- THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! (Section 889)
Contracting Officers shall ensure 889 certifications from non-SAM registered vendors, being uploaded to the AFCC Knowledge Center SharePoint Site , do not exceed a 12-month period. As required by SAM.gov, all vendors shall revalidate their certifications on an annual basis.
See RFO 4.203-1(b) Policy for exemptions to SAM registration.

## Compass guidance (13)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! ( R-DFARS PGI 204.201 )

## Compass guidance (14)
Contracting officers should refer to the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Internal Use Software (IUS) Accountability found in DAFMAN 17-1203 INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) ASSET MANAGEMENT (ITAM) when an IUS is identified by the requiring activity.
The contracting officer shall use the letter "K" in the second position of the supplementary PII number for Provisioned Item Orders (PIOs)* unless separately identified below:
L
- - AFSC/Tinker
M
- - AFSC/Hill OL
Q
- - AFSC/Robins OL
*Provisioned Item Order (PIO) – an order that is issued under a contract but does not have a firm price. It is used to acquire the items the government needs for provisioning.
Procurements which are completely administered by the purchasing office should use normal modification numbering procedures for amended shipping instructions (ASIs). All other procurements should use the letter "T" in the second position of the supplementary PII number for ASIs unless separately identified below:
U-- AFSC/Tinker V-- AFSC/Hill Ol
Y-- AFSC/Robins OL

THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! ( R-DFARS 204.7600 )

## Compass guidance (17)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! ( RFO 4.301 )

## Compass guidance (18)
Subsequent to each contract action, the contracting officer must reference the CAR in the official contract file.
In order to comply with the DoD annual certification and data validation requirement, the DAF, on a quarterly basis, SAF/AQCI will provide procurement data information to the Modernization Board (MODBOD) who shall verify and validate the information with the appropriate contracting officer. Upon completion, the contracting officer shall post the results using the V&V tool. SAF/AQCI will collect the data from the V&V tool once the data is gathered from the MODBOD members.
For additional questions: ( SAF.AQ.SAF-AQCI.Workflow@us.af.mil )
Additional guidance can be found at the V&V website: AF-FPDS-NG Data Validation

## Compass guidance (19)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! (DoW)

## Compass guidance (20)
Maintaining DoD Activity Address Codes (DoDAAC)
The contracting officer administering the contract must obtain a contractor DoDAAC (see DAFMAN 23-230 , Maintaining Air Force DoD Activity Address Codes (DoDAAC)) for contracts that furnish Government property or authorize requisition from a Government supply source. The contracting officer administering the contract must provide the DoDAAC to the program management office/requiring activity to facilitate the shipment of government furnished property.
The Purpose Code Management module contained within Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) must be used to:
Obtain the existing DoDAAC or submit a new DoDAAC request for all contracts awarded;
Initiate contractor DoDAAC account changes, including extensions of contract completion dates and contract terminations;
Initiate contractor DoDAAC deletion when the contract is physically complete, unless the DoDAAC covers other active contracts; and,
Validate contractor DoDAACs in accordance with DAFMAN 23-230 , paragraph 4.2.

Part 5 - Publicizing Contract Actions
## Compass guidance
Promoting Fair Competition through Transparent Contracting

## Compass guidance (2)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! ( RFO 5.101(b) )

## Compass guidance (3)
Exceptions
The Contracting Officer shall document the exception to presolicitation in the contract file.
If advance notice is not appropriate or reasonable ( RFO 5.101(b)(3) ), t he request must state why the notice is not appropriate or reasonable and identify alternative actions to optimize opportunities for small business participation.

## Compass guidance (4)
Presolicitation Notices
In accordance with DAFMAN 16-201 , the contracting officer must identify if there are any restrictions on foreign participation.

## Compass guidance (5)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! ( RFO 5.302 )

## Compass guidance (6)
Public Announcement of Contract Awards
- When
The 1279 Report is used for Congressional notification AND public announcement of contract awards that exceed the DoD threshold, and must be submitted to SAF/LLP no later than 3 duty days prior to the award date. The Contracting Officer may request to shorten the three duty day advance notification requirement.
Information on awards must not be released and awards shall not be made until after the agency announces the award on https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/ . Contract announcements are posted at 1700 Eastern Time daily.
For actions valued at $50M and above, email a courtesy copy of the 1279 report to the cognizant SCO

## Compass guidance (7)
Public Announcement of Contract Awards
- How To
Use the 1279 Report Format in the following tabs
Alternate 1279 reporting for the announcement of source selection contract awards.
If the awardee information cannot be provided three duty days in advance, the report does not need to identify the offeror that has been selected for award. Insert “Source Selection Information
- Will Advise” for “Contractor Data” and either "$50 million or above" or "below $50 million" for “Face Value” and “Funding Data”. When using these procedures, provide the successful offeror, face value of the award, and funding data to SAF/LLP no later than 1300 hours Eastern the day before the anticipated award date. If SAF/LLP is not notified by 1300 hours Eastern the day before the anticipated award date, announcement of the award may need to be delayed.
After a 1279 Report has been submitted, report any changes in plans promptly to SAF/LLP
When immediate award is required and advance notification under paragraph (a) above was not accomplished, prepare the 1279 Report as usual and send it to SAF/LLP . Include the justification for immediate award.
If the Congressional and public announcement cannot be made the same day as the award, the contracting officer must obtain the contractor’s agreement to withhold public announcement of the award until the award is posted on https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/ .
Include in the report a statement that this non-disclosure agreement has been made. The contracting officer will notify the contractor of the agreed upon date of public announcement.
The award may then be made without the three duty day coordination.

## Compass guidance (8)

- 1279 Report Format (For New Awards)

Do not use any abbreviations and use full names of all contractors, including all subsidiary and division designations as appropriate

## Compass guidance (11)
Public Announcement of Contract Awards
- Reports of Intent to Award Multiyear Contracts
Contact your cognizant HCA action officer to confirm receipt
Use the format for Contract Award
state the face value for the total multiyear period and, separately, the value of any options
include the estimated cancellation ceilings for each program year of the proposed contract and the estimated savings over annual procurement methods
If award is an Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC) with a cancellation ceiling, also state the maximum cancellation ceiling amount [see 42 U.S.C. 8287(a)(2)(D) ]. (This paragraph does not apply to 1279 Reports under R-DFARS 205.303 .)
Do not list fund cites

## Compass guidance (12)
Public Announcement of Contract Awards
- Examples
For examples of contract and modification announcements, please see https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/
Examples of explanatory statements for description of scope of contract:
This modification adds the (# of increment, i.e., second, third, etc.) increment of the (length of multi-year contract, i.e., three, four, etc.) year multi-year basic contract.
This modification provides for the purchase of an additional quantity of (quantity and item, e.g., 500 widgets) being produced under the basic contract. (If appropriate, indicate that the contracting action is the result of a competitive negotiated procurement)

title: Part 6 - Competition Requirements
content:
Part 6 - Competition Requirements
## Compass guidance
Promoting Fair Competition, Empowering Strategic Decisions

## Compass guidance (2)
J&A Template Guidance
The following template guidance is provided to help acquisition personnel complete the Justification & Approval template (March 2026 Revision).
Section I. Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)): Self-explanatory
Section II. Nature and/or Description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)): The following language is approved for mandatory use in all Justifications and Approval (J&A) documents. The text in brackets is to be updated for each specific acquisition. If class, the CO must ensure that each contract action taken pursuant to the authority of the class J&A is within scope and shall document the contract file for each contract action accordingly.
This document approves the award of a [Insert Action Type e.g., contract, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), modification, Delivery/Task Order] on a [Insert sole source or limited source] basis to [Insert Contractor Name(s)] for [Provide a brief, high-level description of the supply/service] in support of the [Program/System Name]. This justification is made on [an Individual or a Class] basis.
Section III. Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3). Provide a clear and concise description of the supplies or services to be acquired (including the necessary IP required to meet the program and mission needs), the estimated value (including all options), appropriation and funding amounts planned, anticipated contract type, major items and associated quantities.
Section IV. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)). Self-explanatory
- The following table describes the required documentation.
Authority permitting other than full and open competition
Required Documentation
6.103-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements
Justification & Approval Required by 6.104
6.103-2 Unusual and compelling urgency
6.103-3 Industrial mobilization; engineering, developmental, or research capability; or expert services
6.103-4 International agreement
Justification & Approval is not required for DoD. Use of an International Agreement Competitive Restriction (IACR) approved by the CO is required.
6.103-5 Authorized or required by statute

Section VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition Guidance (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)): This integrated section combines three required content elements (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)). The goal is not less work, but more focused, high-impact work that directly supports a defensible sole source or limited sources acquisition.
Streamlined and Efficient: Eliminates redundant sections, reducing administrative burden.
Stronger Justification: Tells a more compelling and logical story from initial research to final conclusion.
Enhances Compliance: Creates a clear, defensible audit trail by explicitly mapping research activities to market responses.
Focus on Outcomes: Demonstrates a genuine, outcome-based effort to seek competition, shifting the focus from "checking a box" to building a solid business case.
Provide a concise summary of market intelligence, sources sought synopsis and other industry engagement efforts, a list of sources that expressed interest in writing, and a summary of the results. This section must clearly demonstrate why competition is not viable. Consider the following:
Market Intelligence (if a Market Research Report was accomplished reference & summarize)
Describe the results of reviewing historical acquisitions and patent/data rights.
Identify the primary suspected barrier to competition (e.g., "Initial research indicated that Company XYZ held the proprietary data rights...").
Efforts to Solicit Competition
Describe the specific action(s) taken, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by part 5 and, if not, which exception under part 5 applies.
State the Sources Sought Notice/RFI number and the posting dates on the Government Point of Entry (GPE). IAW DFARS CD 2026-O0017 PGI 206.103-170(d) include the results of any Request for Information (RFI) or Sources Sought notice.
Summarize the key capabilities vendors were required to prove to be considered viable (e.g., "...vendors were required to provide evidence of existing production facilities and access to the proprietary TDP.").
Address specific industry engagement efforts, if any. For example, if an industry day was conducted “To further explore the market, a virtual Industry Day was held on [Date]. The event, announced via [Announcement Method, e.g., GPE Notice #], provided a forum to discuss the program's minimum requirements and receive direct feedback from industry.”
Results/Conclusion
Detail the results of the synopsis.
Explicitly list all sources that expressed interest in writing.
For each source, state factually and objectively why they were deemed technically unacceptable by linking back to the requirements listed in Paragraph 2.
Conclude with a definitive statement that the market analysis confirms only one source can meet the government's minimum requirements without unacceptable cost or schedule impacts.
Reminder: Include the results of the request for information or sources sought notice posted in accordance with R-DFARS PGI 206.103-170 (unless the requirement to post has been waived)

## Compass guidance (4)
Additional Approval Guidance
Solicitation Release Prior to Approval . Solicitations for other than full and open competition may be released prior to justification approval, except as set forth in RFO 6.301(b)(2). However, the Contracting Officer should minimize this practice due to risks of justification not being approved. When SPE approval is required, the SCO may authorize solicitation release after the justification is reviewed for adequacy and forwarded to the cognizant HCA for coordination to SAF/AQ or SAF/SQ for approval.
Approval by SPE . J&As for actions exceeding $500M must be coordinated with the cognizant HCA prior to SPE approval. Contracting officers are encouraged to obtain DAF IP Cadre (SAF/AQCK) feedback on draft J&As before submission. Submit J&As for SPE approval using the J&A Submission Form located on the DAF J&A/Limited Sources Acquisition Team Portal. Changes recommended during the staffing process for SPE approval must be adjudicated by the contracting officer in coordination with the cognizant HCA prior to submitting the final package for approval.
Changes after J&A Approval . Regardless of dollar value, if a proposed change is for new work outside the scope of the original J&A, submit a new J&A to the appropriate approving official based on the value of the new work. Negotiations should not commence for the new work until the J&A is approved unless the new work will be authorized in accordance with J&A authority RFO 6.10.3-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.
Before contract award, if the dollar value is expected to exceed the authority of the original J&A approving official, submit an amended J&A to the appropriate approving official. Clearly identify the dollar increase from the approved J&A.
After contract award, if the dollar value of an in-scope change exceeds the authority of the original J&A approving official, submit an amended J&A to the appropriate approving official. Clearly identify the dollar increase from the approved J&A.
A new or amended J&A is not required for an increase in the estimated dollar value of in-scope work that does not exceed the authority of the original J&A approving official. Provide e-mail notification to the J&A approval authority of the revised J&A value if increase of the in-scope work exceeds 25% of the approved J&A value.

## Compass guidance (10)
Purpose
This mandatory section implements, in part, AFPD 64-1 , The Contracting System, 41 USC 1705, and provides guidance and procedures for personnel implementing the Department of the Air Force (DAF) Competition and Commercial Advocacy Program. This MP applies to all Procuring Activity Competition and Commercial Advocates (CCAs), appointed by SAF/AQC and Subordinate Procuring Activity CCAs. Space Force CCAs are appointed IAW with local procedures and will provide space-focused input to SAF/AQ (DAF Lead) as needed to establish DAF competition goals and plans to eliminate barriers and to prepare the annual report, IAW HAF Mission Directive 1-17 .

## Compass guidance (11)
Objectives
The objective of the DAF Competition and Commercial Advocacy Program is to promote and support full and open competition and commercial practices to the maximum extent possible.
The DAF is committed to providing maximum practical opportunities for competition, both for the initial contract award and for orders placed against multiple award contracts. The program emphasizes competition strategies for creating and maintaining competitive environments as outlined in the DoD Competition Guide, dated December 2014 “Guidelines for Creating and Maintaining a Competitive Environment for Supplies and Services in the Department of Defense.”
A guiding principle of DAF acquisition is to apply effective commercial practices to obtain the best technical solutions, quality, schedule, and price for our customers. DAF activities will conduct market research to determine whether commercial items are available to meet agency requirements addressed throughout the acquisition planning process.

## Compass guidance (12)
Competition Advocate General
The DAS(C) is the designated DAF Competition Advocate General (CAG). The CAG shall:
Be responsible for the overall Competition and Commercial Advocacy program. Ensure policies and procedures encourage effective competition and promote the use of commercial procedures.
Challenge the barriers to and promote full and open competition and the acquisition of commercial items and service.
Advise the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Acquisition (SAF/AQ) as the DAF Senior Procurement Executive (SPE) on program acquisition strategies.
Establish competition goals for the DAF no later than 1 December of each year.
Review and coordinate on all acquisition plans and justifications for Other than Full & Open Competition requiring approval by SAF/AQ.
Act as the Air Force Competition Ombudsman, addressing issues and questions from industry and other sources on the competitive and commercial aspects of DAF acquisitions.
Submit the DAF Annual Competition Report to the SPE, January of each year.

## Compass guidance (14)
CCA Duties & Responsibilities
In addition to the duties and responsibilities identified at RFO 6.003 , CCAs are responsible for the following:
Support the DAF CAG in formulating, managing, and providing oversight of the DAF Competition and Commercial Advocacy Program.
For acquisition programs managed by their commander or an associated Program Executive Officer (PEO), seek to improve the overall competitive performance and increase use of commercial practices.
Ensure the organization's policies and procedures encourage full and open competition whenever possible and promote the use of commercial practices.
Review acquisition planning documents and ensure market research demonstrates that competitive and commercial opportunities were considered. As required by RFO 7.1 04(b)(4), coordinate on plans proposing to use other than full and open competition.
Ensure that requirements are stated in the least restrictive manner to maximize competition and the use of commercial practices.
Participate in acquisition strategy planning through forums such as the Acquisition Strategy Panel process.
Identify the potential for full and open competition and effective competition and commercial opportunities.
Review and provide appropriate comments on determinations made in accordance with RFO 9.202(b) that it would be unreasonable to specify the standards for qualifications that a prospective offeror (or its product) must satisfy in order to meet established qualification requirements.
Review and approve sole source/limited source Justification and Approval (J&A), Limited Sources Justifications (LSJ), and Exception to Fair Opportunity (EFO) justifications.
Work with Government and industry to eliminate barriers to competition and the acquisition of commercial products and commercial services.
Ensure operational contracting Squadrons/Flights have access to an Installation/Center CCA.
Establish a competition and commercial advocacy program for activities within the procuring activity. The activities’ Competition and Commercial Advocacy Program must meet the oversight, management, and reporting requirements identified throughout this mandatory section.
Provide support as required for the preparation of the annual competition and commercial report in accordance with RFO 6.003(b) .

title: Part 7 - Acquisition Planning
content:
Part 7 - Acquisition Planning
## Compass guidance
Planning Today for Stronger, Smarter Acquisitions Tomorrow

## Compass guidance (2)
COs! Please note there are items requiring notification to SAF/AQC when used.
Approval Authority Matrix Acronyms

## Compass guidance (3)
MANDATORY (Required by RFO 7.102)
Quick Rule: All acquisitions require planning. Not all acquisitions require a written acquisition plan.

## Compass guidance (4)
Formal Written Acquisition Plans
A written Acquisition Plan (AP) is required in accordance with RFO 7.103 and the dollar thresholds identified at R-DFARS 207.103-70 .
A written AP may take any format that addresses the planning considerations in RFO 7.104 and R-DFARS 207.104-70 , and an ASP briefing may serve as the written AP when it meets those considerations, consistent with the RFO framework's allowance for scalable, judgement-based planning.
Notwithstanding the requirements at R-DFARS 207.103(e) , acquisition plans may be written on a program basis when the requiring activity chooses to write a single plan for all known program actions or on an individual contract basis when there is only one contract, task or delivery order to be covered by the plan. An acquisition plan is not required for individual orders when the contract-level acquisition plan adequately covers all anticipated orders and the order is issued IAW the terms of the basic contract.

## Compass guidance (5)
When a Formal Acquisition Plan Isn't Required
Contracting officers shall maintain decision support information in the contract file for acquisitions that do not require written acquisition plans as well as those that do. Where a written plan is not required, contract documentation such as memoranda for record, market research reports (e.g., Streamlined Market Acquisition Approach Document (SMRAA) ), and Streamlined Acquisition Strategy Summary (SASS) may be used to record acquisition pre-award decisions and risk assessment information. The acquisition team shall ensure consistency among requirements, acquisition planning, market research, and solicitation documents and, to the extent practicable, avoid duplication of information between documents (e.g., by referencing content).
If a Written AP Is Not Required, Use One or More of the Following:
Streamlined Acquisition Strategy Summary (SASS)
Streamlined Market Research Acquisition Approach (SMRAA)
Market research report
Memorandum for record
Briefing slides

## Compass guidance (6)
Acquisition Strategy Panels (ASPs). An ASP is a cross‑functional forum convened by the acquisition approving authority to review and discuss the proposed acquisition strategy prior to approval. The panel typically includes the planner (e.g., PM/SAL or requiring activity lead) along with contracting, legal, fiscal, technical, and small business stakeholders whose equities are central to the acquisition. The purpose of the ASP is to ensure the strategy is informed, integrated, and aligned with program objectives before the plan is approved.
Under the RFO Part 7 framework, ASPs are no longer mandatory, but they remain an available planning tool that approval authorities may use when:
The acquisition is high‑risk, high‑visibility, or complex
Cross‑functional alignment is needed
The approval authority prefers a structured review
The team needs a forum to resolve issues before approval
Stakeholder Role in the ASP Planner Unless otherwise designated by the acquisition approving authority, the planner for acquisitions is the program manager/Services Acquisition Lead (SAL), or other official responsible for the program (i.e., requiring activity). Develops the proposed acquisition strategy, integrates functional inputs, and presents the strategy to the ASP. Ensures alignment with mission needs and program objectives. Contracting Advises on acquisition approach, competition strategy, contract type, business clearance requirements, and regulatory compliance. Ensures the strategy is executable and aligned with R‑DFARS PGI 207.104‑70(b)(2) . Legal Reviews the strategy for legal sufficiency and identifies statutory, regulatory, fiscal law, and protest‑related risks. Ensures the approach complies with applicable laws and policy. Financial Management / Comptroller Validates funding strategy, confirms proper use of appropriations, ensures obligation timing and color‑of‑money compliance, and identifies financial risks or constraints. Technical / Engineering Provides technical requirements insight, assesses feasibility and technical risk, validates performance parameters, and ensures alignment with technical baselines and lifecycle considerations. Small Business Advises on small business opportunities, subcontracting strategies, and compliance with small business coordination requirements. Identifies potential consolidation or bundling concerns. Program Security / Cyber / Intel (as applicable) Identifies security, cybersecurity, supply chain, and threat considerations that may affect acquisition approach, evaluation criteria, or contract structure. Cost/Price Analysts (as applicable) Provides cost realism, price analysis, and independent cost estimate insights to ensure the strategy is affordable, reasonable, and aligned with cost‑risk considerations. Logistics / Sustainment (as applicable) Ensures sustainment planning is integrated early, identifies lifecycle support risks, and validates that the strategy accounts for long‑term readiness and supportability. Acquisition Approving Authority Convenes and chairs the ASP when used, reviews the proposed strategy, and determines whether the strategy is ready for approval. Decides whether an ASP is needed and whether ASP materials may serve as the written AP.

## Compass guidance (7)
Key Point: RFO Part 7 does not assign approval authorities. Approval authority comes from the program's governing directive or, if not applies, organizational governance.
Air Force Approval Authority Rules
1. Default Rule
The Senior Contracting Official (SCO) is the acquisition approving authority unless a governing DAFI designates someone else.
2. Check Applicable DAFIs
If DAFI 63‑138 (Acquisition of Services) applies → use the approval authority designated in 63‑138 .
If DAFI 63‑101/20‑101 (Integrated Life Cycle Management) applies → use the approval authority designated in 63‑101/20‑101 .
If neither applies → the SCO is the approval authority.
Delegation Options (Unless prohibited by regulation or policy)
Firm‑Fixed‑Price (FFP) acquisitions: → Approval may be delegated to the Contracting Officer.
Other‑than‑FFP acquisitions: → Approval may be delegated to one level above the Contracting Officer.

## Compass guidance (8)
(DAF Requirement
- applies regardless of approval authority)

## Compass guidance (9)
$1B+ and HCA Business Clearance Actions
The following actions must be reviewed and coordinated by:
The local Small Business Professional
The cognizant MAJCOM/FLDCOM/DRU and Center Small Business Directors
SAF/SB
Triggers:
All actions $1B and greater
All actions requiring Head of Contracting Agency (HCA) business clearance approval
SAF/SB may provide recommendations and/or coordination at its discretion.

## Compass guidance (10)
Consolidation and Bundling
The following actions must be reviewed and coordinated by SAF/SB before final approval , regardless of who the acquisition approving authority is:
All consolidations of $2M or greater
All bundling actions of any dollar value
This includes review of:
The acquisition plan or strategy
The consolidation or bundling Determination & Findings (D&F)
Supporting documentation required by 13 C.F.R. 125.2(c)(4) and (5)
Note: For detailed definitions, examples, and documentation requirements, see the DAF Consolidation & Bundling page .

## Compass guidance (11)
SAF/SB Coordination & Submission Requirements
(Applies to all actions requiring SAF/SB review, including consolidation/bundling and $1B+/HCA actions)
1. Required Pre‑Coordination
Before submitting a package to SAF/SB, the following reviews must already be completed:
Local Small Business Professional (SBP)
MAJCOM/FLDCOM/DRU Small Business Director
Center Small Business Director
2. What to Submit to SAF/SB
Send the full coordination package to SAF.SB.Workflow@us.af.mil , including:
Acquisition strategy or acquisition plan
ESIS and/or ASP briefing materials
Consolidation or bundling D&F (if applicable)
Summary of pending issues
Any additional documentation prescribed by SAF/SB
Planning Tip: Allow at least 15 business days for SAF/SB review, depending on complexity.
Ensure the local SBP, MAJCOM/FLDCOM/DRU and Center SB Directors, and SAF/SB are invited to ESIS and ASP sessions.
3. Small Business Program Considerations
Acquisition planners must consider all applicable small business programs early in planning, including:
Small Business set‑aside opportunities
Subcontracting strategies
SBIR/STTR programs
Impacts to small business participation (especially for consolidations/bundling)

Part 9 - Contractor Qualifications
## Compass guidance
Promoting Accountability and Competence in Contractor Selection

## Compass guidance (2)
COs! Please note an item requires notification to SAF/AQC when used.
Approval Authority Matrix Acronyms

## Compass guidance (3)
How to make contractor responsibility determination

## Compass guidance (4)
Where to go to make contractor responsibility determination

## Compass guidance (5)
MANDATORY!
- The contracting Officer shall document the contract file with a determination of responsibility.

## Compass guidance (6)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! ( R-DFARS PGI 209.105-1(2) )
Contracting Officers shall document the contract file that the Supplier Performance Risk System has been checked for supplier risk assessment when determining responsibility for actions above the Micro-Purchase Threshold.

## Compass guidance (7)
Section 1612 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2018 (P.L. 115-91) requires Space Systems Command (SSC) to establish and maintain a Space Contractor Responsibility Watch List (CRWL). SSC Instruction (SSCI) 64-101, Space Contractor Responsibility Watch List (CRWL), establishes the CRWL and its applicability to space program solicitations or contracts.

## Compass guidance (8)
Procedures for Suspension and Debarment
Step 1: Investigation and referral .
The contracting officer or the referring person must promptly notify SAF/GCR , their SCO, and their designated legal counsel with all known information relating to the following:
Any non-responsibility determination.
Any indictment, conviction, or civil judgment (including those listed on required certifications, or those disclosed in accordance with RFO 3.1003 or RFO 52.203-13 relating to an offeror’s or contractor’s lack of integrity or business honesty, regardless of whether the indictment, conviction, or civil judgment related to a government contract.
Any recommended or final termination for default or for cause.
Any recommendation for debarment or suspension.
Any debarred or suspended contractor who bids on a Government contract (including those who indicate debarment or suspension on required certifications).
The contracting officer must provide additional information as requested by SAF/GCR.
Step 2: Decision-making process .
If SAF/GCR determines that a hearing is required, the contracting activity must provide witnesses and other support as requested.
Step 3: Documentation
Provide a copy of request to SAF/GCR . The request must include a description of efforts taken to establish alternate sources and the impact if the exception is not granted. The cognizant HCA will forward the approved exceptions to GSA.

## Compass guidance (9)
THIS SECTION HAS MANDATORY ELEMENTS! ( RFO 9.5 )

## What's an unfair advantage?
An unfair advantage occurs if a contractor seeking a federal contract has access to proprietary information from a government official without proper authorization or possesses source selection details that are not available to all competitors but could help secure the contract. (WarU)

## Compass guidance (10)
Click the tabs below to access the information

## Compass guidance (11)
Potential OCI verbiage
- Mandatory!
As prescribed in RFO 9.507-1 , insert in Section L Potential Organizational Conflict of Interest verbiage, substantially as written.

## Compass guidance (12)
OCI verbiage
- Mandatory!
In accordance with RFO 9.507-2 , insert Organizational Conflict of Interest verbiage, substantially as written, in the award/attachments when the contractor's eligibility for future prime contract or subcontract awards shall be restricted because of services being provided as stated in RFO 9.505-1 through
- 4 .

## Compass guidance (13)
As prescribed in RFO 9.507-1 , insert in the solicitation/award (SOW/PWS/Section L/attachment) Potential Organizational Conflict of Interest verbiage, substantially as written.
POTENTIAL ORGANIZATIONAL CONFLICT OF INTEREST
(a) There is potential organizational conflict of interest (see RFO Subpart 9.5, Organizational and Consultant Conflicts of Interest) due to (state the nature of the proposed conflict). Accordingly:
(1) Restrictions are needed to ensure that (state the nature of the proposed restraint and the applicable time period).
(2) As a part of the proposal, the offeror shall provide the contracting officer with complete information of previous or ongoing work that is in any way associated with the contemplated acquisition.
(b) If award is made to the offeror, the resulting contract may include an organizational conflict of interest limitation applicable to subsequent Government work, at either a prime contract level, at any subcontract tier, or both. During evaluation of proposals, the Government may, after discussions with the offeror and consideration of ways to avoid the conflict of interest, insert a special provision in the resulting contract which shall disqualify the offeror from further consideration for award of future contracts.
(c) The organizational conflict of interest clause included in this solicitation may be modified or deleted during negotiations.
ALTERNATE VERBIAGE . At the discretion of the contracting officer, substitute the following paragraph (b) for paragraphs (b) and (c) in the basic provision:
(b) The organizational conflict of interest clause in this solicitation may not be modified or deleted.

## Compass guidance (14)
In accordance with RFO 9.507-2 , insert Organizational Conflict of Interest verbiage, substantially as written, in the award (SOW/PWS/attachment) when the contractor's eligibility for future prime contract or subcontract awards shall be restricted because of services being provided as stated in RFO 9.505-1 through
- 4 .
Insert the basic verbiage when the contractor will be providing systems engineering and/or technical direction. See RFO 9.505-1 .
Alternate I verbiage
When the contractor will be preparing specifications or work statements. See RFO 9.505-2 .
Alternate II verbiage
When the contractor will be providing technical evaluation or advisory and assistance services. See RFO 9.505-3 .
Alternate III verbiage
When the contractor will be obtaining access to proprietary information. See RFO 9.505-4 .
Alternate IV verbiage
When the contract is a task ordering contract and when more than one system is supported. The contracting officer may modify Alternate IV to include a list of systems for which task orders may be issued and indicate which organizational conflict of interest shall apply.
Alternate V verbiage
When the contract provides for delivery orders. The contracting officer shall indicate in each delivery order which organizational conflict of interest shall apply.
Alternate VI verbiage
When it is necessary to have the restrictions of this clause included in all or some subcontracts, teaming arrangements, and other agencies calling for performance of work related to the contract.
Verbiage
ORGANIZATIONAL CONFLICT OF INTEREST
(a) The following restrictions and definitions apply to prevent conflicting roles which may bias the Contractor's judgment or objectivity, or to preclude the Contractor from obtaining an unfair competitive advantage in concurrent or future acquisitions.
(1) Descriptions or definitions:
"Contractor" means the business entity receiving the award of this contract, its parents, affiliates, divisions and subsidiaries.
"Development" means all efforts towards solution of broadly-defined problems. This may encompass research, evaluating technical feasibility, proof of design and test, or engineering of programs not yet approved for acquisition or operation.
"Proprietary Information" means all information designated as proprietary in accordance with law and regulation, and held in confidence or disclosed under restriction to prevent uncontrolled distribution. Examples include limited or restricted data, trade secrets, sensitive financial information, and computer software; and may appear in cost and pricing data or involve classified information.
"System" means the system that is the subject of this contract.
"System Life" means all phases of the system's development, production, or support.
"Systems Engineering" means preparing specifications, identifying and resolving interface problems, developing test requirements, evaluating test data, and supervising design.
"Technical Direction" means developing work statements, determining parameters, directing other Contractors' operations, or resolving technical controversies.
(2) Restrictions: The Contractor shall perform systems engineering and/or technical direction, but will not have overall contractual responsibility for the system's development, integration, assembly and checkout, or production. The parties recognize that the Contractor shall occupy a highly influential and responsible position in determining the system's basic concepts and supervising their execution by other Contractors. The Contractor's judgment and recommendations must be objective, impartial, and independent. To avoid the prospect of the Contractor's judgment or recommendations being influenced by its own products or capabilities, it is agreed that the Contractor is precluded for the life of the system from award of a DoD contract to supply the system or any of its major components, and from acting as a subcontractor or consultant to a DoD supplier for the system or any of its major components.
ALTERNATE I verbiage. Either substitute paragraph (a)(2) of the basic verbiage with one or both of the following paragraphs, or use one or both in addition to the basic paragraph (a)(2). Use these paragraphs substantially as written.
(a)(2)(i) The Contractor shall prepare and submit complete specifications for non-developmental items to be used in a competitive acquisition. The Contractor shall not furnish these items to the DoD, either as a prime or subcontractor, for the duration of the initial production contract plus (insert a specific period of time or an expiration date).
(a)(2)(ii) The Contractor shall either prepare or assist in preparing a work statement for use in competitively acquiring the (identify the system or services), or provide material leading directly, predictably, and without delay to such a work statement. The Contractor may not supply (identify the services, the system, or the major components of the system) for a period (state the duration of the constraint, however, the duration of the initial production contract shall be the minimum), as either the prime or subcontractor unless it becomes the sole source, has participated in the design or development work, or more than one Contractor has participated in preparing the work statement.
ALTERNATE II verbiage. Either substitute paragraph (a)(2) of the basic verbiage with the following paragraph, or add the following in addition to the basic restriction. Renumber the paragraphs as needed if more than one restriction applies. Use this paragraph, substantially as written.
(a)(2) The Contractor shall participate in the technical evaluation of other Contractors' proposals or products. To ensure objectivity, the Contractor is precluded from award of any supply or service contract or subcontract for the system or its major components. This restriction shall be effective for (insert a definite period of time). This does not apply to other technical evaluations concerning the system.
ALTERNATE III verbiage. Add the following paragraph (b) to the basic verbiage substantially as written:
(b) The Contractor may gain access to proprietary information of other companies during contract performance. The Contractor agrees to enter into company-to-company agreements to: (1) protect another company's information from unauthorized use or disclosure for as long as it is considered proprietary by the other company; and, (2) to refrain from using the information for any purpose other than that for which it was furnished. For information purposes, the Contractor shall furnish copies of these agreements to the contracting officer. These agreements are not intended to protect information which is available to the Government or to the Contractor from other sources and furnished voluntarily without restriction.
ALTERNATE IV verbiage. Add the following paragraph (b) to the basic verbiage. If Alternate III is also used, renumber this to paragraph (c).
(b) The Contractor agrees to accept and to complete all issued task orders, and not to contract with Government prime Contractors or first-tier subcontractors in such a way as to create an organizational conflict of interest.
ALTERNATE V verbiage. Add the following paragraph (b) to the basic verbiage substantially as written. If more than one Alternate is used, renumber this paragraph accordingly.
(b) The Contractor agrees to accept and to complete issued delivery orders, provided that no new organizational conflicts of interest are created by the acceptance of that order. The contracting officer shall identify the organizational conflict of interest in each order. The Contractor shall not contract with Government prime Contractors or first-tier subcontractors in such a way as to create an organizational conflict of interest.
ALTERNATE VI verbiage. Add the following paragraph (b) to the basic verbiage substantially as written. If either Alternate III or IV or both are used, renumber this paragraph accordingly.
(b) The above restrictions shall be included in all subcontracts, teaming arrangements, and other agreements calling for performance of work which is subject to the organizational conflict of interest restrictions identified in this clause, unless excused in writing by the contracting officer.

title: Part 10 - Market Research
content:
Part 10 - Market Research
## Tactical market research
• Tactical market research is conducted at specific points during the acquisition process
• designed to provide in-depth information to answer specific questions about the capabilities, products, or services available in the market

## Strategic market research
• conducted continuously throughout the acquisition process (before an acquisition program exists and continue after it ends)
• overall market developments, trends, and capabilities

## Market Research is mandatory! Why is it important? How do we do it?
Decode RFO Part 10. Execute with precision. Empower your buys.

## WHO IS RESPONSIBLE FOR MARKET RESEARCH?
EVERYONE ON THE MULTI-FUNCTIONAL TEAM!!!
MISSION OWNERS, PROGRAM MANAGERS, ENGINEERS, CONTRACTING OFFICERS, CONTRACTING SPECIALISTS, SMALL BUSINESS SPECIALISTS

## Compass guidance
RFO 2.101 collecting and analyzing information about capabilities within the market to satisfy agency needs
DAU Market research is a continuous process for gathering data on product characteristics, suppliers’ capabilities, and the business practices/trends that surround them
- - plus the analysis of that data to make smart acquisition decisions
DoD Instruction 5000.74, “Defense Acquisition of Services” collect information to maximize reliance on the commercial marketplace and to benefit from its capabilities, technologies, and competitive forces to fulfill DoD needs

## Compass guidance (2)
- Find solutions that satisfy agency requirements
- Identify market trends that affect the requirement
- Understand commercial markets, competitive forces, and potential sources
- Identify opportunities for using commercial items or services to meet agency needs
- Determine how other activities are acquiring services similar to the requirement
- Determine whether commercial products or services can be modified or adapted to meet the special needs of an agency
- Determine the availability of other nondevelopmental items to meet agency requirements
- Understand product cycles and the way new technology is introduced into commercial products
- Develop product descriptions, statements of work, and statements of objectives that allow companies to offer their commercial products and services in consonance with commercial practices
- Shape acquisition strategies, requirements, and tradeoffs
- Determine if consolidation or bundling is in the best interest of the Government
- Understand the costs of various alternatives
- Develop support and test plans that accommodate commercial practices
- Determine the extent to which the market can support other federal government objectives, such as providing opportunities for small businesses, meeting environmental goals, and using domestic sources
- Craft solicitation and contract terms, conditions, and evaluation factors
- Identify the leverage the Government may have in the market

## WHEN DO WE DO IT?
• Before developing new requirements documents for an acquisition
• On an ongoing basis, and to take advantage to the maximum extent practicable of commercially available market research methods, to identify the capabilities, including the capabilities of small businesses and new entrants into federal contracting, that are available in the marketplace for meeting agency requirements in furtherance of a contingency operation or defense against or recovery from a nuclear, biological, chemical, or radiological attack or for disaster relief

## WHEN DO WE DO IT? (2)
• Before soliciting offers for acquisitions with an estimated value in excess of the simplified acquisition threshold
• Before soliciting offers for acquisitions with an estimated value less than the simplified acquisition threshold when adequate information is not available and the circumstances justify its cost
• Before soliciting offers for acquisitions that could lead to a bundled contract
• Before awarding a task or delivery order under an indefinite-delivery/indefinite quantity contract for a noncommercial item in excess of the simplified acquisition threshold
• Before soliciting offers for acquisitions that could lead to a consolidation of contract requirements as defined in DFARS 207.170-2
• Before issuing a solicitation with tiered evaluation of offers (Section 816 of Public Law 109-163)

## Compass guidance (3)
Early market research is particularly significant because it could have a major effect on how the acquisition strategy unfolds

## Compass guidance (4)
Strategic market research is particularly significant because it could have a major effect on how the program unfolds

## Compass guidance (5)
Submit a Request for Information (RFI) or Sources Sought to SAM.gov and/or GSA

## HOW TO PERFORM MARKET RESEARCH
- DOCUMENTATION

title: Part 14 - Sealed Bidding
content:
Part 14 - Sealed Bidding
## Compass guidance
Sealed Bidding: A Pathway to Competitive and Transparent Contracts

## Compass guidance (2)
A competitive procurement method where bidders submit confidential offers (bids) in sealed envelopes or through a secure electronic system by a specific deadline. All bids are opened simultaneously, and the contract is typically awarded to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder.

## Compass guidance (3)
Did you know you can do two-step sealed bids?!
A variation of the process, used when specifications are not clear initially. Step one involves submitting technical proposals (without pricing), which are evaluated. In step two, only those with acceptable technical proposals are invited to submit sealed priced bids.
STEP 1: In step one, firms are allowed to submit technical (not price) proposals to satisfy a requirement
STEP 2: In step two, each firm with a satisfactory technical approach is allowed to submit a sealed bid (price), which uses that firm's approach as the contract specification.
Award goes to the low responsive and responsible bidder

## Compass guidance (4)
The contracting officer shall maintain the records required by RFO 14.304-3(h) in the contract file.

## Compass guidance (5)
Currently, there are no SAF/AQC Part 14 templates

title: Part 15 - Contracting by Negotiation
