title: Part 46 - Quality Assurance
content:
Part 46 - Quality Assurance
## Compass guidance
Fostering Long-Term Success with Unwavering Commitment to Quality. Delivering Results You Can Trust: Quality Assurance from Start to Finish.

## Compass guidance (2)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! (see RFO 46.202-4 )

## Compass guidance (3)
Contracting Officers shall establish procedures for determining when higher-level contract quality requirements are necessary for determining the risk (both the likelihood and the impact) of nonconformance, and for advising the contracting officer about which higher-level standards should be applied and included in the solicitation and contract. Requiring compliance with higher-level quality standards is necessary in solicitations and contracts for complex or critical items (see RFO 46.202-4 ) or when the technical requirements of the contract require
- Control of such things as design, work operations, in-process controls, testing and inspection; or
Attention to such factors as organization, planning, work instructions, documentation control, and advanced metrology; or
Any subcontract for complex and critical items (see RFO 46.203 (b) and (c)).

## Compass guidance (4)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! (unless the three conditions at R-DFARS PGI 201.404-70(e)(1) are met.)

## Compass guidance (5)
R-DFARS PGI 201.404-70(e)(1)
Contracting officers may exempt service contracts from this requirement when the following three conditions are met:
( 1 ) The contract will be awarded using simplified acquisition procedures;
( 2 ) The requirement is not complex; and
( 3 ) The contracting officer documents the file, in writing, with the specific reasons why the appointment of a COR is unnecessary.

## Compass guidance (6)
If those conditions are NOT met, follow the below
(Click on the tabs for the responsibilities of each role)

## Compass guidance (7)
COCO/Chiefs of Performance Management Offices
The COCO/Chiefs of Performance Management Offices must ensure that a Quality Assurance Program Coordinator (QAPC) is appointed and properly trained to integrate the quality contract requirements into the quality assurance program, act as the liaison between the contracting and functional organizations, and provide training and record keeping in accordance with the DAF Part 1 QAPC section.

## Compass guidance (8)
Contracting Officer
The CO must:
Advise the acquisition team on Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan development.
Designate Contracting Officer’s Representatives (COR) in accordance with the DAF Part 1 COR section

## Compass guidance (9)
Quality Assurance Program Coordinator (QAPC)
The QAPC must:
Successfully complete the QAPC course conducted by AETC prior to conducting any training
Support the acquisition team in the development of contract quality assurance requirements specifically ensuring that requirements are clearly stated and enforceable Assist the acquisition team during market research efforts in determining commercial quality assurance practices
Assist, as required, with the evaluation of contractor Quality Control Plans

## Compass guidance (10)
Contracting Officer Representatives (CORs)
All Contracting personnel (1102 or 64p) who are appointed as CORs and any non-1102 or 64p CORs who are responsible for monitoring subcontractor compliance must successfully complete the Management of Subcontracting Compliance (CLC 059) course offered by the Warfighting Acquisition University, when contracts include a subcontracting plan.

## Are you a COR/QAPC?
Request access to the Team below to ask questions to your peers, receive lessons learned, discuss performance plans, and dispel urban legends.
Also, to receive specific emails, become a member of the QAPC Network distro list by emailing kelly.ashworth@us.af.mil

## Compass guidance (11)
Please check the Approval Authority Matrix item at the top of the page when R-DFARS 246.703-11(2) applies

title: Part 49 - Termination of Contracts
content:
Part 49 - Termination of Contracts
## Compass guidance
Minimizing Disruptions with Transparent and Efficient Terminations

## Compass guidance (2)
The SCO (or designee) must approve a termination for default or cause prior to a contracting officer taking the action, unless there is a command-appointed termination contracting officer (TCO). When requesting approval, the contracting officer must provide all relevant documents to include a chronology of key events, cure/show cause notices and responses thereto.

## Compass guidance (3)
THIS SECTION IS MANDATORY! ( RFO 49.4 )

## Compass guidance (4)
Procedure for Termination for Default
Prior to making a final decision concerning termination for default (including a termination for cause under RFO Part 12), the contracting officer must forward the termination notice and the complete contract file to AF/JACQ’s Contract Law Field Support Team with a copy of the termination notice to SAF/GCR and follow the procedures in the Claims and Termination for Default tab of the Disputes and Appeals and Contracting Officer's Decision section of the DAF Part 33 page. The supporting documentation for AF/JACQ coordination shall include a legal memorandum by local legal office. At a minimum, the required legal memorandum should include:
(1) an analysis and evaluation of the specific ground(s) for termination for default/cause;
(2) an analysis and evaluation of the presence and adequacy of facts supporting the specific ground(s) for termination for default/cause;
(3) an analysis and evaluation of the applicability and adequacy of any defenses or excuses the Contractor may have (including the Contractor’s response to any delinquency notices); and
(4) legal determination whether termination for default/cause is legally sufficient.

## Compass guidance (5)
Repurchase Against Contractor’s Account
The contracting officer must provide copies of assessments of excess re-procurement costs through the SCO to AF/JACQ

## Compass guidance (6)
Special Termination Costs ( R-DFARS 249.501-70 )
Please check the Approval Authority Matrix item at the top of the page for special termination costs in incrementally funded contracts
Submit requests to include R-DFARS clause 252.249-7000 , Special Termination Costs through the cognizant HCA to SAF/FMB for approval and OSD Comptroller concurrence.
In accordance with Volume 2A, Chapter 1, paragraph 2.14.3.2.1 of DoD 7000.14-R, DoD Financial Management Regulation , the use of a Special Termination Cost Clause (STCC) requires SAF/FMB approval, OSD Comptroller concurrence, and Congressional notification.
Because approval to include an STCC entails a long approval process over which DAF has little control, the contracting officer should allow sufficient time to process requests to use R- DFARS 252.249-7000 , Special Termination Costs (i.e., not less than 90 days prior to contract award). The cognizant HCA request to SAF/FMB must include the following:
A detailed breakdown of applicable cost categories in the clause at R- DFARS 252.249-7000, (a)(1) through (5) , which includes the reasons for the anticipated incurrence of the costs in each category;
Information on the financial and program need for the clause including an assessment of the contractor's financial position and the impact of a failure to receive authority to use the clause; and
Clear evidence that only costs that arise directly from a termination would be compensated under the clause. Costs that would be incurred by the Government, regardless of whether a termination occurs, must not be covered by a STCC.
SAF/FMB will obtain OSD Comptroller concurrence. Upon receipt of OSD Comptroller concurrence, SAF/AQ or SAF/SQ will complete the required congressional notifications (See STCC Congressional Notification Template).

## Compass guidance (7)
Congressional Notification on Significant Contract Terminations ( R-DFARS 249.7001 )
The contracting officer must submit the proposed Congressional notification through the SCO to cognizant HCA workflow at least five workdays before the proposed termination date. The cognizant HCA action officer will forward the information to SAF/LLP . The contracting officer must not release the termination notice until Congress has been notified.
“Contract price of the items terminated” means the contract price of the supplies or services not yet accepted that are being terminated. The contracting officer must not adjust this amount downward for progress or advance payments, accepted vouchered costs, or less than full funding and should use estimates when un-priced contract actions are being terminated, or when otherwise necessary.

## Compass guidance (8)
Notification of Anticipated Terminations or Reductions ( R-DFARS 249-7003 )
The contracting officer must submit the draft notification through the SCO to the cognizant HCA Workflow as soon as the proposed termination/reduction is known. The cognizant HCA will forward the notification to SAF/AQ or SAF/SQ for signature.
Address the notification to:
Administrator
Office of National Response
U. S. Department of Labor
Employment and Training Administration 200 Constitution Avenue NW
Room N5422 Washington DC 20210
The notice must address the following key elements:
1. Contract number, date, and type of contract
2. Name of the Company
3. Nature of contract or end item
4. The reason for the termination
5. Contract price of the items terminated
6. Total number of contractor employees involved, including the Government’s estimate of the number who may be discharged
7. Statement of anticipated impact on the company and the community
8. The area labor category, whether the contractor is a large or small business, and any known impact on hardcore disadvantaged employment programs
9. Total number of subcontractors involved and the impact in this area, and
10. An unclassified draft of a suggested press release

title: Part 50 - Extraordinary Contractual Actions and the Safety Act
content:
Part 50 - Extraordinary Contractual Actions and the Safety Act
## Compass guidance
Flexibility in Action: Managing Contract Changes and Extraordinary Needs. Handling the Unexpected with Agile and Effective Contract Adjustments.

## Compass guidance (2)
DAF RFO Part 50 Authority
The authorities, policies, and procedures established for Part 50 are based on the authority of HAF MD 1-10 , Assistant Secretary of the Air Force (Acquisition) .

## Compass guidance (3)
Following are the mandatory approval authorities for the DAF and are the only ones authorized approve requests to obligate the Government for actions under Pub. L. 85-804.
Pub. L. 85-804 – Approval Authority
Obligation Amount
DAS(C), on a non-delegable basis
$90,000 or less
DAF Contract Adjustment Board, on a non-delegable basis
In excess of $90,000
The Senior Contracting Official (SCO) has the authority to deny a request for adjustment and document their denial in a Memorandum of Decision (See RFO Part 50 for documentation requirements). The SCO shall provide a copy of the denial to the cognizant HCA. If the SCO recommends approval after making the determination of essentiality and loss, submit the required preliminary record to the SAF/AQC Workflow for adjudication by the appropriate authority above. See below for additional guidance pertaining to r equests for adjustment due to inflationary conditions as a result of the 2020 COVID Pandemic.

## Compass guidance (4)
The section provides additional guidance related to r equests for adjustment due to inflationary conditions as a result of the 2020 COVID Pandemic
NOTE: Sec. 822 of the FY23 NDAA/Sec. 824 of the FY24 NDAA is NOT AUTHORIZED. Per DPCAP, Pub. L. 85-804, as implemented by FAR and DFARS Part 50, is currently the only authority available for Contracting Officers to afford Extraordinary Contractual Relief when contractors have sought or may seek an upward adjustment to the price of an existing firm-fixed-price contract to account for current economic conditions. See Essentiality Considerations below.
Communication & Collaboration between the Gov't Team and Contractor is key to ensure Preliminary Records are complete for adjudication.

## Compass guidance (5)
Click the tabs below for resources

## Compass guidance (6)
Upon completion of all buying activity coordination, the contracting officer must forward the indemnification request through the SCO to the cognizant HCA Workflow to for staffing to the SECAF.

## Compass guidance (7)
Currently, there are no SAF/AQC templates for Part 50
